articles.title: What Kentucky’s Will Stein said after humbling blowout loss to Tennessee
articles.summary: The Kentucky football team suffered a tough defeat to Tennessee on Saturday. Following the game, Kentucky head coach Will Stein stressed his team’s need to move on quickly. “We have a great locker room….we have really good people in there,” Stein said, per KSR. “Nobo
articles._body: The Kentucky football team suffered a tough defeat to Tennessee on Saturday. Following the game, Kentucky head coach Will Stein stressed his team’s need to move on quickly . “We have a great locker room….we have really good people in there,” Stein said, per KSR. “Nobody’s negative. Nobody is going to sulk, nobody is going to complain……..it’s about responding.” Will Stein praised Kenny Minchey's leadership following Kentucky's loss to Tennessee. According to Stein, Minchey stood up in front of the locker room and told his teammates there would be no negativity, complaining, or blaming others after the loss. Stein says it's now about… pic.twitter.com/MlsIleLxTc — KSR (@KSRonX) November 8, 2026 Tennessee thumped Kentucky Saturday, 34-6. It was a very tough loss for the Wildcats, who have seen a resurgence under Stein as head coach. Against Tennessee, the Wildcats struggled to protect the football . “Seven penalties for 50 yards,” Stein said, per the Associated Press. “We had three turnovers. That was the story of the game — the turnovers.” Kentucky saw a six-game win streak snapped. It was a tough loss, as the team hopes to make the College Football Playoff this year. A third loss would decimate the team’s chances. This is Stein’s first season as head coach at Kentucky. He previously worked at Oregon, where he served as offensive coordinator. He helped lead the Ducks to the CFP the last few seasons. The Wildcats just couldn’t overcome turnovers in this game against the Volunteers. “You can’t turn the ball over and expect to win football games,” Kentucky quarterback Kenny Minchey said. “There were multiple drives where we shot ourselves in the foot.” Following the win, Tennessee is also 7-2 on the season. The Volunteers kept their hopes alive for earning a CFP bid. “The defense had an elite performance,” Tennessee coach Josh Heupel said. “It was a tremendous effort, especially the red zone defense (Kentucky reached the red zone twice and settled for two field goals).” Kentucky next plays Florida on Saturday. articles.title: Myles Garrett’s first sack with Rams comes in style vs. Jayden Daniels
articles.summary: Myles Garrett is playing in just his second career game with the Los Angeles Rams after missing the past seven games due to a left knee injury. However, in his first game back in action since the club’s season opener, Garrett finally recorded his first sack as a Ram after bringing down Wash
articles._body: Myles Garrett is playing in just his second career game with the Los Angeles Rams after missing the past seven games due to a left knee injury. However, in his first game back in action since the club’s season opener, Garrett finally recorded his first sack as a Ram after bringing down Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels on Sunday. It was a brilliant play by the 30-year-old edge rusher. Not only did he sack Daniels, but Garrett also managed to knock the ball loose , resulting in a fumble. The fumble was picked up by teammate Omar Speights, giving the Rams’ offense excellent field position on the next drive. Myles Garrett has his first sack as a Ram pic.twitter.com/ZAclU2ucdB — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 8, 2026 The Week 9 matchup against the Commanders is also the first game Garrett is finally recording any stats in general, as he was ineffective in the 27-7 Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. But now that he’s back on the field and healthy, the Rams are hopeful the five-time First-Team All-Pro can play at his superstar level for the rest of the campaign. This story is currently developing, and more information will be available soon. The post Myles Garrett’s first sack with Rams comes in style vs. Jayden Daniels appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Michael Jackson’s ‘Thriller’ Scares Up Highest Rank on Billboard 200 Albums Chart in More Than 40 Years
articles.summary: The classic, which spent 37 weeks at No. 1 in 1983-84, surged sparked by Halloween.
articles._body: Michael Jackson ’s Thriller vaults 13-2 on the Billboard 200 (dated Nov. 14), scoring its highest rank on the list since the spring of 1984, when it logged its 37th and final week at No. 1 on the April 14-dated list. Thriller continues to hold the record for the most weeks atop the list for an album by a singular artist. (Only the film soundtrack to West Side Story spent more weeks at No. 1: 54, in 1962-63.) Related Olivia Rodrigo’s ‘you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love’ Notches Fourth Week Atop Billboard 200 Simple Plan Are Meeting a Whole New Generation of Fans, 25 Years In Deep Purple's Ian Gillan Shares Encouraging News After Undergoing Surgery The Billboard 200 chart ranks the most popular albums of the week in the U.S. based on multi-metric consumption as measured in equivalent album units, compiled by Luminate. Units comprise album sales, track equivalent albums (TEA) and streaming equivalent albums (SEA). Each unit equals one album sale, or 10 individual tracks sold from an album, or 2,500 ad-supported or 1,000 paid/subscription on-demand official audio and video streams generated by songs from an album. The new Nov. 14, 2026-dated chart will be posted in full on Billboard ‘s website on Nov. 10. For all chart news, follow @billboard and @billboardcharts on both X and Instagram. In the tracking week of Oct. 30 through Nov. 5 — thus, including Halloween — Thriller earned 55,000 equivalent album units (up 89%), boosted by seasonal spooky streams of the set’s title track, as well as new physical versions of the album that were released. Of that unit total, SEA units comprise 32,000 (up 37%, equaling 34.34 million on-demand official streams of the set’s songs; it moves 14-5 on Top Streaming Albums), album sales comprise 22,000 (up 335%; it rises 14-3 on Top Album Sales) and TEA units comprise 1,000 (up 30%). On Oct. 30, Thriller was reissued across three new vinyl variants (two color editions and a liquid-filled version) and a cassette tape. The album’s 22,000 sales for the week mark its largest single-week sales sum in nearly four years, since it shifted 23,000 (Dec. 31, 2022-dated list). Notably, of Thriller ’s 22,000 sold in the latest tracking week, vinyl purchases account for 19,000 — the album’s largest sales week on vinyl since Luminate began electronically tracking sales in 1991. With Thriller ’s jump to No. 2, Jackson has his highest rank on the Billboard 200 in more than a decade, since the posthumous album Xscape debuted and peaked at No. 2 on the May 31, 2014-dated chart. Notably, Thriller has appeared on the Billboard 200 each year since 2009, following Jackson’s death that June. It has resided in the top 20 each week since early May, with 15 consecutive weeks in the top 10 through August, spurred by the record-setting biopic Michael .

Rodrigo’s unit total is the smallest for the week’s No. 1 album in more than a year, since SZA’s SOS was tops on the May 3, 2025-dated chart with 52,000. Michael Jackson’s Thriller vaults 13-2 on the Billboard 200, scoring its highest rank on the list since the spring of 1984, when it logged its 37th and final week at No. 1 on the April 14-dated list. The remainder of the top five on the latest Billboard 200 comprises former No. 1s and non-movers, as Morgan Wallen’s I’m the Problem is No. 3 (49,000 equivalent album units earned, down 7%), followed by Ella Langley’s Dandelion (45,000, down 4%) and Noah Kahan’s The Great Divide (40,000, up 1%). ILLIT captures its first top 10 on the Billboard 200 as BREAK EVEN bows at No. 6 with 37,000 equivalent album units earned (the group’s best week by units). Of that sum, album sales comprise 32,500 (ILLIT’s best sales week; it debuts at No. 1 on Top Album Sales — the act’s first leader), SEA units total 4,500 (equaling 4.87 million on-demand official streams of the set’s tracks) and TEA units account for a negligible sum. BREAK EVEN ’s album sales were largely driven by its availability across more than 24 CD (all containing collectible items such as photocards, stickers and posters, with some items randomized). BREAK EVEN is the pop group’s fifth charted entry on the Billboard 200, and first top reach the top 20. The act had previously gone as high as No. 26 with its last title, Mamihlapinatapai , in May. BigXthaPlug scores his third top 10 on the Billboard 200 as Better Over Time enters at No. 7 — tying for his highest-charting album. He previously hit No. 7 with I Hope You’re Happy in 2025 and No. 8 with Take Care in 2024. The new album launches with 35,000 equivalent album units earned. Of that sum, SEA units comprise 29,000 (equaling 29.06 million on-demand official streams of the set’s tracks; it debuts at No. 7 on Top Streaming Albums), album sales total 6,000 (it debuts at No. 12 on Top Album Sales) and TEA units comprise a negligible sum. articles.title: Vans’ Waterproof Skate Shoe Stays Fresh When Wet
articles.summary: Vans releases a clean light grey version of its Half Cab GORE-TEX sneaker, just in time for the cold weather.
articles._body: We saw the vision when Vans transformed the Half Cab into a stylish Vibram-soled boot . Now, the model's back, living out its rugged dreams as a rain boot. To be clear, Vans didn't exactly turn the Half Cab into a rain boot (although that would be pretty cool). But the brand's treating the skate shoe like one, adding GORE-TEX waterproofing to keep out precipitation. What's more, the Half Cab looks good in its GORE-TEX coat. The latest version comes in a nice tonal light grey color scheme, which, by the way, will look just as fresh on inclement weather days. The Half Cab badges are posted throughout, alongside plentiful GORE-TEX logos, which admittedly makes the model look more rugged and ultimately cooler than others. It also features a suede-and-canvas upper, paired with thick All-Trac soles that provide reliable grip across different surfaces. Vans has dished out other nice waterproof Half Cabs this season, alongside winterized Crosspath XC and SK8 Hi models . And the other colorways were nice, but this light grey pair is the cleanest in the lineup. It's now available on Premier's website for $180. articles.title: Lane Kiffin taken to woodshed by angry LSU Tigers fans after Alabama embarrassment
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin is getting intense criticism from the LSU Tigers fanbase following their 31-13 loss to the Alabama Crimson Tide on Saturday evening. Kiffin is going through his first season as the Tigers’ head coach following a controversial exit from Ole Miss. He looks to achieve the objective
articles._body: Lane Kiffin is getting intense criticism from the LSU Tigers fanbase following their 31-13 loss to the Alabama Crimson Tide on Saturday evening. Kiffin is going through his first season as the Tigers’ head coach following a controversial exit from Ole Miss. He looks to achieve the objective of leading LSU to the College Football Playoffs, one that seems to be harder than he initially anticipated. Losing to Alabama ramped up the frustration among fans. Even Barstool personality T-Bob Hebert blasted him and LSU on social media, with some fans expressing their thoughts on Reddit . “Absolutely f**king embarrassing, there is ONE THING that the best f**king state in the country cares about and you f**king BLEW IT You didn’t get unlucky YOU GOT F**KING DOMINATED this is the most pathetic loss that LSU has ever experienced,” Hebert wrote. “That first half was awful awful game management by Kiffin. LSU gets the ball to start the 2nd half. Why did kiffin go for it so many times on 4th down instead of taking the points? At worst your down 10-9 with the ball back to start the 2nd half. The difference that game was bama had a calm collected coach who didn’t make emotional decisions it felt like lane was pressing that entire game. All those yards gained means nothing if you walk away empty. Womack called that defense Almost as if he knew Kiffin and Leavitt wouldn’t execute and malfunction in the redzone when the pressure got tight,” one fan wrote on Reddit. How Lane Kiffin, LSU performed against Alabama Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers have some self-reflecting to do after losing to Alabama. Falling to 6-3 this season, they will need to win out to have an outside chance of being in CFP contention. Both teams traded blows throughout the contest, seeing Alabama up 17-13 after three quarters. It wasn’t until the fourth period when the Crimson Tide took full control, outscoring LSU 14-0 in the last 15 minutes of regulation. Sam Leavitt failed to record any type of touchdown in the game, frequently throwing the ball to receivers for potential scoring opportunities but to no avail. He completed 35 out of 47 passes for 380 yards and an interception. Dilin Jones led the run game with 17 carries for 56 yards and a touchdown while catching seven passes for 36 yards. Jackson Harris commanded receivers with 11 catches for 166 yards, while Trey’Dez Green caught 10 passes for 85 yards. LSU fell to a 6-3 overall record this season, including a 3-3 display in SEC action. They sit at sixth place in the conference standings, being above the Missouri Tigers and the Tennessee Volunteers while trailing the Texas Longhorns and the Ole Miss Rebels. The No. 14 Tigers will look to bounce back in their next matchup, remaining at home. They host the No. 7 Texas Longhorns in Week 11 as kickoff commences on Nov. 14. articles.title: Giants’ Malik Nabers throws helmet on bench during frustrating first half vs. Eagles
articles.summary: On Sunday afternoon, the New York Giants hit the field on the road for a game against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Giants entered this one coming off a bye week, looking to pick up their fourth win of the season against the spiraling Eagles. New York didn’t exactly have a great offensive fi
articles._body: On Sunday afternoon, the New York Giants hit the field on the road for a game against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Giants entered this one coming off a bye week, looking to pick up their fourth win of the season against the spiraling Eagles. New York didn’t exactly have a great offensive first half in this one, putting just six points on the board and trailing by a bizarre score of 8-6 heading into the locker room for halftime. At one point, star Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers vented his frustration on the bench amid the rough first half. “Malik Nabers just threw his helmet down on the bench and it bounced onto the ground. Giants’ top receiver is frustrated as NY punts again. He has 2 catches on 2 targets for 25 yards as we near half,” reported Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News on X, formerly Twitter. Quarterback JJ McCarthy was under constant pressure in the first half, finding himself sacked five times by the Eagles defense, although he did throw for 101 yards in the half. Meanwhile, as Leonard mentioned, Nabers was only targeted twice, so it’s understandable that the team’s top offensive weapon would want to see the ball thrown his way a little more often than that. Although the Giants are in first place in the NFC East, they’ll still need to take care of business as often as possible, especially when faced with weaker competition like the spiraling Eagles. At the conclusion of this game, the Giants will next hit the field on Thursday vs the Washington Commanders. articles.title: Holiday fares hit a 10-year high. A Black Friday deal may only get you back to last year’s price
articles.summary: Hopper says Thanksgiving airfare averages $402, up 31%. A travel agent explains why Travel Tuesday bundles beat Black Friday flash sales.
articles._body: A 15% Black Friday discount on a Christmas hotel room this year comes to about $167 a night. That is roughly what the average Christmas room cost a year ago. Black Friday falls on Nov. 27 this year, followed by Cyber Monday on Nov. 30 and Travel Tuesday on Dec. 1, and airlines, hotels and cruise lines are expected to compete for bookings across all three. For budget-conscious travelers, the question is whether a markdown matters when starting prices have already jumped. Fuel costs are keeping fares high According to Hopper’s 2026 Holiday Travel Index , domestic round-trip Thanksgiving flights are averaging $402, up 31% from 2025. Christmas fares are up 23%, with round trips averaging $452. Hopper projects this will be the most expensive holiday travel season in a decade. Elevated jet fuel prices are behind the climb, making deep holiday discounts less likely. For most carriers, fuel is the second-largest cost after labor. Delta said after its third-quarter results that its jet fuel costs rose 60%, an increase of $1.6 billion from a year earlier. Travelers have absorbed most of that. CEO Ed Bastian said in July that he expected Delta to pass close to 100% of its higher fuel costs on to customers in the third quarter, and the airline’s revenue per seat mile rose 15%. On the earnings call, Bastian said the market “has accepted these price points.” He also said, “Hopefully, we will see fuel recede into the next year at some point, and that’s when I think you’ll see the real earnings power of this franchise be amplified.” As Fortune reported , that suggests higher fares could stick even if fuel prices ease, as long as demand holds up. Other carriers, including American, United and Southwest, have cut less profitable routes , tightening supply as demand peaks. U.S. airfares were up 22.4% in September from a year earlier, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, as airlines chose higher fares over fuller planes . Hotels are steady at Thanksgiving and pricier at Christmas Domestic hotel prices are splitting. Hopper reports that Thanksgiving rates are running about $170 a night, comparable to 2025, while Christmas rates average $197 a night, up 18% from a year ago. Hopper expects rates to rise and availability to fall as the holidays near, which changes the math on any sale. A promotional price may only bring a surge-priced room back to last year’s rate. The best travel deals come bundled With capacity tight and costs elevated, there is little room left for deep discounts. DaShawna Carpenter, owner of Skyy Travel Mavens, says the shopping holiday has lost some of its punch in travel. “Black Friday is definitely becoming weaker,” she says. “While I think you can genuinely find legitimate savings, I have found that prices are sometimes inflated to appear cheaper during the sale periods. So it’s more of a marketing campaign than anything, especially for travel.” She says Travel Tuesday tends to offer the best deals of the three days but cautions that most of them are bundled. “Most of the deals are attached to packages rather than flights alone, so it’s hard to say whether there are huge fare deals or not.” That distinction matters for anyone hoping to save on airfare alone. A package price blends airfare, lodging and extras, which makes it difficult to see what the flight itself costs. Even when a discount does apply to airfare, Carpenter says, the savings may be narrower than they look. “Some airlines apply discounts to airfare but leave fuel pricing, taxes, and other fees the same.” Her advice is to arrive with a reference point rather than be swayed by a lower sticker price. “A traveler has to be knowledgeable in what the fare normally costs to really understand the discounts and what they are comparing it to.” Travel sales fill a slow booking window November and December have historically been slow booking months, and Carpenter notes that the discount-day “marketing campaigns have helped fill that gap.” The sales are less about generosity than about smoothing demand in a quiet window for trips later in the year. That is also why missing them is not a big deal. “If you don’t buy on any of these marketed ‘discount days,’ there will definitely be other chances to catch a discount,” she says. Carpenter’s read on traveler spending is consistent with carriers’ decision to hold prices high. “We found out during COVID that travel is somewhat recession- and virus-proof,” she says. “Travelers are going to remain committed to their vacations and I’ve found they cut back on other things in order to keep their travel plans up.” She also credits buy now, pay later services such as Klarna, Afterpay and Affirm with making travel more attainable and consistent, even for price-sensitive travelers. What to do before you book For travelers eyeing next year, Carpenter’s advice centers on comparison shopping rather than chasing a single flash fare. Compare against the normal price, not the crossed-out one. Watch a route or hotel for weeks before the sale and check its price history. Read what the discount covers. Taxes, fuel-related charges and fees may not change, and a sale that applies only to a nonrefundable fare is not the same as a cheaper trip. Look at packages, but price the parts. The strongest bundled offers tend to appear on Travel Tuesday, but a bundle can hide a weak airfare. Don’t panic if you miss the window. Other sales will come. For this holiday season, timing matters more than coupons. Hopper had advised booking holiday flights and hotels before Halloween and expects prices to keep rising as the dates approach, so waiting for a sale works against the trend. Fares on the Sunday after Thanksgiving can top $600, Hopper notes, while flying on Thanksgiving Day, Black Friday or Cyber Monday is cheaper. This year, the best Black Friday travel deal may be a seat on a plane that day. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles._body: On Sunday, the Kansas City Chiefs hit the field at home for a game against the New York Jets. This game was surprisingly back and forth throughout the first half, with Kansas City holding onto a two-point lead heading into the locker room. The Chiefs had a chance to increase that lead to five, but Harrison Butker missed a field goal attempt from 56 yards out. However, he got another chance after the Jets were called for an offsides penalty, moving him five yards closer… and he missed yet again. The fans in Arrowhead Stadium were not shy about letting Butker hear it following the two straight misses. Chiefs fans boo their team heading into halftime after Harrison Butker missed back-to-back FG attempts following a penalty Kansas City leads the Jets, 14-12. pic.twitter.com/pnksvZq3iY — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 8, 2026 It’s been a tough season for Butker, who for several years was among the most reliable legs in the league, but has seen a steep decline in his accuracy this season. The Chiefs made headlines, not many of them positive, last week when they signed kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad, and it remains to be seen if he will get a call up to the main team in the wake of Butker’s continued struggles. Meanwhile, the Chiefs had another scary moment toward the end of the first half when quarterback Patrick Mahomes went down with an apparent arm injury after getting blasted by David Bailey and fumbling the ball. However, thankfully, the play appeared to be just a stinger and Mahomes was able to return for the next series. In any case, the Chiefs will next hit the field next Sunday for a road game vs the Atlanta Falcons. articles.title: Former ESPN star calls out NFL WAGs Brittany Mahomes, Kelly Stafford over recent comments
articles.summary: Linda Cohn isn’t holding back about her feelings toward NFL WAGs Brittany Mahomes and Kelly Stafford after their recent comments about the league. “Are you kidding me, Brittany? Brittany, have you heard the conversations happening constantly outside Kansas City for the last few years? You m
articles._body: Linda Cohn isn’t holding back about her feelings toward NFL WAGs Brittany Mahomes and Kelly Stafford after their recent comments about the league. “Are you kidding me, Brittany? Brittany, have you heard the conversations happening constantly outside Kansas City for the last few years? You may need to expand your group chat,” Cohn, who used to work at ESPN as an anchor on SportsCenter from 1992 until her contract expired in June, said on her self-titled podcast. Brittany is married to Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, and she came to the defense of her three-time Super Bowl champion husband last week following their game against the Denver Broncos. She aimed her frustration at the referees who gave Chiefs offensive tackle Jaylon Moore a false-start penalty on what could have been a go-ahead touchdown pass from Patrick to Rashee Rice in the final seconds of the game. The Chiefs ended up getting their second loss of the season as the final score read 28-24. “You can’t tell me you call that on a game winning TD, oh wait yeah I can cause it’s us,” Brittany wrote on her Instagram Story at the time. Cohn called out Brittany’s “us” comment revealing how other NFL fans have interpreted the referees calls in favor of the Chiefs. “So you can understand why people hear ‘because it’s us’ and think, ‘Are we remembering the same football games, Brittany?’ You saw those,” Cohn said. The former ESPN anchor then called out Kelly who is married to Matthew Stafford, the quarterback for the Los Angeles Rams. Kelly complained about the Rams’ bye week that happens for them in Week 11. She was frustrated with the NFL because the players only get 10 days off rather than the standard two-week period because they will be on Thanksgiving Eve against the Green Bay Packers. She even said that she was tired and can only imagine how the players might feel. “Kelly makes the case for player recovery that’s a conversation worth having. Just understand why your own game day exhaustion might not generate the sympathy you expect,” Cohn said. “Marriage to a quarterback doesn’t disqualify you from commentary, from having an opinion. It also doesn’t exempt your commentary from criticism,” she continued. “Kelly and Brittany are two people making public statements.” Cohn concluded her statement on the WAGs’ comments, saying that they should look to see how others might view their remarks. “Sometimes before you hit post, the most useful question is, how is this going to sound to somebody whose life looks very, very different from my own? Three words, know the room,” Cohn said. At this time, neither Kelly nor Brittany has reacted to Cohn’s statements. The NFL stars also haven’t shared their feelings about their wives’ original comments or Cohn’s rebuttal. articles._body: With the Tennessee football team handing the Kentucky Wildcats a loss on Saturday, 34-6, it was a massive bounce back after the 27-24 loss last weekend to the South Carolina Gamecocks. As the Tennessee football program rocked their Dark Mode jerseys for the contest, head coach Josh Heupel would shout out a specific unit during his post-game press conference. In his introduction before taking questions from the media, Heupel would shout out the “phenomenal environment” inside Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tennessee. Heupel would then commend the Volunteers’ defense for holding Kentucky to six points, calling the effort “elite.” “Phenomenal environment. Knew it would be. Dark Mode, Homecoming. Our fans were tremendous tonight. And a great environment that they create for us. Proud of the way that we competed,” Heupel said, according to The Next Round on X, formerly Twitter. “Turnovers were going to be big. Defensively, we forced couple and didn’t give it up offensively. That’s been a huge part of our opponent’s success this year. And I thought defensively, elite performance ultimately, what you end up giving up on the scoreboard. Tremendous effort. There was a huge part of the game early was just red-zone defense. Did a great job of forcing a couple of kicks.” "Defensively, elite performance." – Josh Heupel after Tennessee's 34-6 throttling of #6 Kentucky in Knoxville pic.twitter.com/3Xn3iP4Yf7 — The Next Round (@NextRoundLive) November 8, 2026 Tennessee football’s Josh Heupel continues on win over Kentucky Heupel would continue talking about the Tennessee football’s performance, as the offense scored in every quarter of the contest, including a 21-point fourth quarter. As for the defense, the Volunteers only allowed six points in the second quarter, stifling the Wildcats in every other aspect, and even with the productive performance, Heupel still thought there was room for improvement, like the six penalties against them, costing them 60 yards. “We got to continue to grow in that way,” Heupel continued. “But I thought we missed some things offensively in the first half. But the second-half performance as a football team, I love the way that they went out there and competed in the second half…Enjoy it tonight and move on.” Heupel and the Tennessee football team look to keep the momentum going into Saturday against Texas A&M. articles._body: On Sunday afternoon, the Kansas City Chiefs hit the field for a home game against the lowly New York Jets. The Chiefs suffered a huge injury scare when quarterback Patrick Mahomes went down with an apparent arm injury. The play occurred after Mahomes took a big hit from Jets pass rusher David Bailey. The injury to Mahomes here. pic.twitter.com/cyAwqHbIaP — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) November 8, 2026 The play caused a fumble, which the Jets were able to recover. Kansas City has already been hit with the injury bug in other areas of the roster, and one could feel the collective sigh of relief in Arrowhead Stadium when he trotted back out onto the field on Sunday. articles.title: Bills’ Week 9 injury report vs. Vikings: Can Buffalo survive O-Line injuries vs. Brian Flores?
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills (6-1) are on a mission this year to get the job done in the regular season and regain the AFC East title after losing it last year to the New England Patriots. That’s just the regular-season goal. The full-year goal is to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl and win it [
articles._body: The Buffalo Bills (6-1) are on a mission this year to get the job done in the regular season and regain the AFC East title after losing it last year to the New England Patriots. That’s just the regular-season goal. The full-year goal is to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl and win it for the first time in team history. Bills Saturday injury report pic.twitter.com/FRC4zXinhq — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 7, 2026 This week’s game against the Minnesota Vikings (6-1) represents the dramatic positioning of the Bills as the best offensive team in the NFL meeting the best defense in the league. The Monday night setting at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis means the whole world — at least from the NFL’s perspective — will be watching. In addition to the best vs. best aspect, the game also features the Bills’ struggling defense against the Vikings moribund offense. If either one of those units can step up in this game, it could go a long way towards determining the winner of this matchup. Both sides have significant injuries. The homestanding Vikings have benched starting QB Kyler Murray because he has a hamstring injury and backup Carson Wentz has been tapped on the shoulder by head coach Kevin O’Connell to start the game. Offensive line issues have hit the Bills The Bills have a slew of injuries , primarily on the offensive line. Three of the Bills starters on the offensive line are listed on the team’s substantial injury report. They include left tackle Dion Dawkins , left guard Alec Anderson and right tackle Spencer Brown. Dawkins missed practice throughout the week, and sat out the last three days, including Saturday with a rib injury. He is listed as doubtful on the injury report. Anderson has an ankle issue. While he did not practice Thursday or Friday, he was on the field in a limited fashion Saturday with his teammates. The Bills also list him as questionable. Brown seems to be in a much better position than either of the other two offensive linemen. He has a back injury, but he was a limited participant on Thursday and Friday. He jumped up to a full participant Saturday. Josh Allen needs solid OL performance against Vikings’ relentless D The Bills have not seen a defense like the one the Vikings present on an every-game basis. Their blitzing ways is a challenge for every opposing quarterback and offensive coordinator, and that means it should be somewhat difficult for Allen and Pete Carmichael Jr. However, Allen is capable of delivering big plays even when he is under pressure. If the Vikings pass rush that consists of key sackers Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel get their hands on Allen, they must put him on the ground. It is much tougher to finish a sack on Allen than nearly any quarterback in the league because of his size and strength. The Vikings will undoubtedly try to target the left side of the Buffalo line where Dawkins and Anderson are playing. Even if both are in the lineup for the Bills, neither one is likely to be at their best. Their backups are likely to be Tylan Grable and Jude Bowry, and both have played quite well to this point. They may be able to hold up based on their recent improvement. In addition to the offensive line issues that the Bills are going to try to overcome, nose tackle Greg Gaines is questionable with a calf injury and wide receiver Josh Palmer is out with a hamstring issue. Bills will feature TE Dalton Kincaid, but star tight end is not 100 percent Mandatory Credit: Christopher Trim-Imagn Images Dalton Kincaid is regularly Allen’s favorite receiver, but it seems even more likely that he will take on a key role against the blitzing Vikings. Kincaid leads the Bills with 27 receptions for 401 yards and 2 touchdowns. He is dangerous after the catch, as 148 yards have come after he makes the reception. Additionally, he has 8 plays of 20 yards or more. TE Dawson Knox is Kincaid’s partner in crime. Kincaid is clearly the primary pass catcher of the duo, but Knox could be active in Monday night in the passing game. He has 9-42-1 to this point, but Allen may be looking his way if he needs to get rid of the ball quickly. The Vikings were vulnerable against the run in their Week 8 loss to the Detroit Lions. In that game, the Vikings offense could not stay on the field and the Lions were able to unleash Jahmyr Gibbs for 153 yards and backup Sione Vaki for 65 yards. The Bills will undoubtedly attempt to do the same thing with James Cook, who has rushed for 707 yards while averaging 5.1 yards per carry. The one fear that head coach Joe Brady has with Cook is his tendency to fumble. He has been charged with 4 fumbles this season, and opponents have recovered two of them.       The post Bills’ Week 9 injury report vs. Vikings: Can Buffalo survive O-Line injuries vs. Brian Flores? appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Falcons most to blame for getting carved up by Joe Burrow in NFL Madrid Game loss to Bengals
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons took a tough 34-17 loss in Week 9 to the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid. The Falcons came into this game after losing to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, where they weren’t able to put any points on the board, and Michael Penix Jr. finished that game with four interceptions. He s
articles._body: The Atlanta Falcons took a tough 34-17 loss in Week 9 t o the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid. The Falcons came into this game after losing to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, where they weren’t able to put any points on the board, and Michael Penix Jr. finished that game with four interceptions. He said that he would be better moving forward, and though he was, it still wasn’t good enough to keep up with the Bengals. As far as the Falcons’ defense, they had a tall task going up against a red-hot Bengals’ offense, and Joe Burrow had himself a day, as well as Ja’Marr Chase. There are a few reasons why the Falcons fell in this one, and here they are. Falcons’ secondary couldn’t keep up with the Bengals’ receivers It was the Burrow and Chase show for the Bengals in the first half, and the Falcons didn’t have an answer for anything they threw at them. If the Falcons played man, AJ Terrell didn’t have the speed or elusiveness to keep up with Chase, which is how he got beat for the Bengals’ first touchdown of the game. If they went zone, Chase just found the sweet spot and made a play there. If it wasn’t Chase, it was Tee Higgins who was catching almost any pass that Burrow threw. Terrell and CJ Henderson had a long day as the outside cornerbacks, and it felt like there wasn’t much they could do to stop them. No discipline on offense The Falcons had a clean drive to start the game, but after that, it was hard for them to score the rest of their points because of undisciplined play. There were too many times throughout the game when the Falcons were getting called for penalties such as false starts and holding. That would take them out of position to pick up a first down, or even take them out of scoring position. The Falcons finished the game with 12 penalties, compared to just six by the Bengals. Michael Penix Jr. bounces back, but it still wasn’t good Penix didn’t lie when he said he would be better than in his last game against the Buccaneers, but it’s really hard to do worse than throw four interceptions. He finished this game with 162 yards for one touchdown and one interception, but that wasn’t good enough for the Falcons. He still missed some key throws, and he looked rattled in the pocket when the Bengals put pressure on him. If Penix continues to perform at this level, it’ll be interesting to see if they make a change. articles._body: The Memphis Tigers have began the 2026-27 season at 2-0, including an upset win over the No. 18 ranked Iowa State Cyclones. Memphis head coach Penny Hardaway’s future with the program has been a subject of conversation in recent seasons, but after the team’s win against Iowa State, the former NBA star was quick to remind the doubters that he has a proven track record with the Tigers, as per The Field of 68. “Last year was an anomaly. To me that’s a one-off … my teams don’t play like that. I’ve done great in the past seven years of winning 20+ games a season with a schedule just like this. So it’s not my first time winning,” Hardaway said. “We’ve always won. Last year was the one year that we didn’t. I know it’s behind us, and I was looking forward to this season. But, the Ws are what we do here. It’s been in the history of Memphis, we win games like this. I’m just thankful to win another one.” Memphis is now in the program’s ninth season with Penny Hardaway at the helm as head coach. And he’s right in the sense that the Tigers have never won fewer than 20 games, aside from last season, under his leadership since he took over in 2018. The Tigers are coming off a disappointing year in which they finished 13-19 and only 8-10 in the American Conference standings. But prior to that, Memphis had posted its best regular season finish in Hardaway’s tenure at 29-6 and 16-2 in conference play. However, Memphis has only reached the NCAA Tournament in three of his eight previous seasons, and they’ve never advanced past the round of 32 under his watch. The Tigers have another big matchup coming up against the No. 24 ranked Vanderbilt Commodores. The post Penny Hardaway fires back at haters after Memphis’ 2-0 start appeared first on ClutchPoints .

Miami enjoyed an incredible start to the 2026 season, rolling off eight consecutive victories throughout
articles._body: Mario Cristobal and the Miami Hurricanes’ reign over the top spot in the AP Top 25 football poll is no more following their 31-24 loss to the Notre Dame Fighting Irish on Saturday night. Miami enjoyed an incredible start to the 2026 season, rolling off eight consecutive victories throughout the campaign. This allowed them to take over the top spot in the AP Top 25 rankings following losses from previous squads that boasted the No. 1 spot. The Hurricanes held onto the throne for a few weeks, shining as one of the top squads in the country. However, their loss to the Fighting Irish ended their perfect start to the season and unseated their place at No. 1. The AP revealed its latest Top 25 rankings on Sunday. Miami fell down four spots, going from No. 1 to No. 5. Instead, the Georgia Bulldogs make their way back to the top spot of the poll. Other teams that jumped over Miami are Utah, Notre Dame and UCLA. How Mario Cristobal, Miami performed against Notre Dame Mario Cristobal and Miami will still be firm in CFP bracket given their remarkable start to the 2026 season. However, the Notre Dame loss poses some holes they need to address before closing out the campaign and gearing up for the postseason. Notre Dame landed the first big punched, taking a 17-3 lead at halftime. Miami tried to fight back in the second half, but the Fighting Irish made enough big plays down the stretch to secure their most pivotal win of the season. Darian Mensah sorely missed star teammate Malachi Toney due to injury, but he did his best to keep Miami competitive on the road against Notre Dame. He completed 24 out of 43 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns and one interception. Elija Lofton led receivers with 113 yards and a touchdown on seven catches, while Cooper Barkate caught 10 passes for 92 yards and two touchdowns. The No. 5 Hurricanes will look to bounce back in their next matchup, being at home. They host the Duke Blue Devils in Week 11 as kickoff commences on Nov. 14 at 12 p.m. ET. articles.title: Michael Vick’s Norfolk State team loses after stunning victory formation debacle
articles.summary: Michael Vick and Norfolk State lost in bizarre fashion on Saturday, falling 29-28 to North Carolina Central. The loss moved the Spartans down to 4-6 on the year. What was crazy? Well, Norfolk State led 28-23 with 1:34 to go in the game and NC Central had no timeouts remaining. On 2nd and five, the [
articles._body: Michael Vick and Norfolk State lost in bizarre fashion on Saturday, falling 29-28 to North Carolina Central . The loss moved the Spartans down to 4-6 on the year. What was crazy? Well, Norfolk State led 28-23 with 1:34 to go in the game and NC Central had no timeouts remaining. On 2nd and five, the assumption was “victory formation” called by Vick. The second-year head coach and former quarterback said he had taken his headset off, signaling they were ready to wrap up a win. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage However, they lined up in shotgun and quarterback Deljay Bailey ran with the football, fumbling in the process. NC Central recovered it, went on to score a go=ahead touchdown and held on for a 29-28 victory, even after Norfolk State got the ball back. “I don’t know what happened at the end of the game,” Vick said postgame. “I put my headset down. I called victory formation. All we had to do was take a knee, kneel the clock out. That’s just situational football. I don’t know what happened in regards to that. I looked up and we was running the ball, and then I seen the fumble. But my final instructions was victory formation. That’s when you kneel it out. And they had, I think, zero timeouts left and the game was over practically.” Take note that Vick said “practically,” meaning there would’ve been about 15 seconds left to play during a would-be Norfolk State punt. From there, it would’ve taken quite the effort for NC Central to win, barring disaster. What’s even crazier is the Spartans got the ball, starting the drive at their own 38. Penalties and 33 yards off two completed passes gave Norfolk State a 37-yard field goal to win the game. However, Marco Peery missed it and NC Central came away with the win. “Well, I put my headset down, and I took my headset off because all we had to do was just run it three times, or two times, or kneel it out,” Vick said. “That’s called victory. I don’t know what happened. A run play was called. I looked up, I seen us running the ball. I don’t know what happened. I really don’t. I don’t know what the play call was. I don’t know why we even ran that play. “People will look at that, and that’ll go on as a teaching tape for a lot of teams across the country for years to come. I hate it had to be us. But I called victory formation. Just letting everybody know that. I called victory.” Norfolk State is 0-3 in MEAC play this year and have lost three straight games. Vick and the Spartans will play Morgan State and Howard to conclude the year over the next two weeks. In nearly two seasons, Norfolk State is 5-17 under Vick following a 1-11 campaign in 2025.

articles._body: On Sunday afternoon, the Denver Broncos hit the road for a game against the Carolina Panthers. The Broncos entered this game coming off a big home win vs the Kansas City Chiefs last week, but unfortunately, they got a big injury scare early in this one. The scare occurred when star wide receiver Jaylen Waddle took a big hit while attempting to make a catch. Jaylen Waddle being evaluated for a concussion in the locker room after this hit. We will see updates on return pic.twitter.com/kXbSoNwlEg — Maddox McCloud, PT, DPT (@MaddoxMcCloudPT) November 8, 2026 He was then taken back into the locker room to be evaluated for a concussion. Later, cornerback Riley Moss was also evaluated for a concussion, and it has since been revealed that both players were indeed diagnosed with concussions, per NFL insider Mike Garafolo of the NFL Network on X, formerly Twitter. The hit itself was not penalized, although a pass interference was called, as was a taunting penalty on cornerback Marco Wilson for standing over Waddle after the play. Meanwhile, Waddle has given Bo Nix and the offense a big lift this season, adding playmaking and a vertical threat down the field to help Denver expand its offensive attack. The Broncos will certainly hope that the former Miami Dolphins star isn’t forced to miss extensive time with the injury. In any case, after the conclusion of the Panthers game, the Broncos will have a much-needed bye week and then next hit the field on November 22 for a home game vs the Las Vegas Raiders. articles.title: How CJ Carr went from a boy to a man between Miami starts
articles.summary: A dominant quarterback performance helped the Notre Dame Fighting Irish secure a statement 31-24 victory over previously unbeaten and No. 1-ranked Miami Hurricanes. CJ Carr showcased tremendous poise under pressure, strengthening his Heisman Trophy candidacy while keeping Notre Dame’s Colle
articles._body: A dominant quarterback performance helped the Notre Dame Fighting Irish secure a statement 31-24 victory over previously unbeaten and No. 1-ranked Miami Hurricanes . CJ Carr showcased tremendous poise under pressure, strengthening his Heisman Trophy candidacy while keeping Notre Dame’s College Football Playoff hopes alive . His latest outing also highlighted just how much he has matured since making his first career start against the Hurricanes. According to ESPN’s November 7 report and Brandon Marcello’s November 8 article for CBS Sports, CJ Carr’s growth was evident throughout the matchup, particularly after his father, Jason, reminded him of the difference between his first Miami start in 2025 and his current form. “A huge difference,” Carr said when reflecting on his development. He also recalled his father’s assessment of that first appearance: “It was a boy playing at Miami for my first start.” This time, Carr looked like a completely different quarterback, leading Notre Dame with 319 passing yards, three touchdowns, and zero interceptions. The Michigan native completed 29 of his 40 attempts, consistently making smart decisions and delivering accurate passes against Miami’s defense. His connection with Micah Gilbert was particularly effective, as the receiver caught two touchdown passes during the victory. Carr also showed his composure when Miami threatened to erase Notre Dame’s advantage. Rather than allowing the momentum shift to affect him, he continued making important plays, including a crucial 36-yard completion to Nolan James Jr. on fourth down. Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman praised Carr’s preparation and consistency, emphasizing that the quarterback’s work ethic has remained impressive since his early days with the program. With a signature victory over the nation’s top-ranked team, Carr has taken another significant step forward in his development. articles.title: What Oklahoma HC Brent Venables said about Jason Witten’s triumphant debut as new OC
articles.summary: Brent Venables and the Oklahoma Sooners pulled off a strong 23-7 win over the Florida Gators on Saturday evening. It also featured the debut of offensive coordinator Jason Witten, earning praise from the Sooners head coach. The Sooners recently made the decision to fire offensive coordinator Ben
articles._body: Brent Venables and the Oklahoma Sooners pulled off a strong 23-7 win over the Florida Gators on Saturday evening. It also featured the debut of offensive coordinator Jason Witten, earning praise from the Sooners head coach. The Sooners recently made the decision to fire offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle. Witten, the Dallas Cowboys’ former tight end who was coaching high school in suburban Texas last year, took over on an interim basis for the remiander of the season. Under Witten, the Sooners didn’t dazzle; they had only one play longer than 20 yards. But they were efficient, particularly on the clinching drive that took 12:45 off the clock. They converted five third-down plays on the drive. “Bragging on his ambition, and his excitement for the opportunity, you can’t fabricate that,” Sooners coach Brent Venables said of Witten after the game , via ESPN. “And I certainly didn’t want someone to put a toe in the water, when willing to do it. I wanted someone who saw how good we could be.” “Really complete performance. Just really clean football game, with complementary football. Thought we really dominated the line of scrimmage.” How Brent Venables, Oklahoma performed against Florida Brent Venables and Oklahoma controlled the game from start to finish. They did an excellent job containing Florida’s attack, only conceding a touchdown in the second quarter. John Mateer shined with a big performance on the road. He completed 21 out of 33 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns while rushing 14 times for 56 yards. Rocky Beers led receivers with four catches for 72 yards. Isaiah Sategna III came next with four receptions for 34 yards and a touchdown, while Hayden Hansen caught a three-yard touchdown pass. Oklahoma improved to a 5-4 record this season, going 3-3 in SEC action so far. They sit at sixth place in the conference standings, being above Florida and Auburn while trailing Missouri and LSU. The Sooners will look forward to their next matchup, being at home. They host the Ole Miss Rebels in Week 11 as kickoff commences on Nov. 14. articles.summary: On Sunday morning, the Atlanta Falcons took their second straight loss with a blowout defeat in Madrid against the Cincinnati Bengals. It was the second straight tough game for quarterback Michael Penix Jr., who threw for just 162 yards and one touchdown, against one interception. Now, a new stat
articles._body: On Sunday morning, the Atlanta Falcons took their second straight loss with a blowout defeat in Madrid against the Cincinnati Bengals. It was the second straight tough game for quarterback Michael Penix Jr., who threw for just 162 yards and one touchdown, against one interception. Now, a new stat has been unearthed showing just how much Penix Jr. struggles when opposing defenses turn up the heat. “Per ESPN Research: Michael Penix Jr. went 1-of-9 for -3 yards and an interception when pressured Sunday. Penix has completed a league-low 18% of his passes when pressured on the season. That would be the lowest mark by a qualified passer since ESPN began tracking pressures in 2009,” reported NFL insider Marc Raimondi of ESPN on X, formerly Twitter. Last week, Penix Jr. had the worst game of his career in a rainstorm against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, tossing four interceptions in a blowout road loss. Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski kept it honest on Penix Jr.’s performance after the loss in Madrid. “Can he play better and are there things we can get corrected? Yes. But we expected him to play well,” he said. “We know that’s not who we want to be this season. We have to put that on display if we want to win football games,” said Penix Jr. Overall, Penix Jr. has been quite up and down so far this season, at times showing the tools to be a very solid starter at the NFL level, and at others struggling to make basic reads and completions on seemingly easier throws. The Falcons now sit at 3-6 on the season, and although they are still alive in the playoff race thanks to their division, it’s hard to imagine the team making a big turnaround at this point. articles.title: Ohio State football won national title last time they were ranked so low in AP Top 25 Poll
articles.summary: On Saturday, the Ohio State football program took its third loss of the season with a blowout home defeat at the hands of the Oregon Ducks. It was an embarrassing performance for the Buckeyes, one that had fans wondering how far the team would tumble in the AP Poll, which was released on Sunday.
articles._body: On Saturday, the Ohio State football program took its third loss of the season with a blowout home defeat at the hands of the Oregon Ducks . It was an embarrassing performance for the Buckeyes, one that had fans wondering how far the team would tumble in the AP Poll, which was released on Sunday. “Ohio State dropped to No. 21, its lowest AP ranking since Sept. 21, 2014 (No. 22). The Buckeyes won the national title that year. It is also the Buckeyes’ first November outside the AP Top 20 since 2011, when they were unranked,” reported college football insider Brett McMurphy of On3 Sports on X, formerly Twitter. It’s highly unlikely that the Buckeyes will get a chance to make it 2-2 on national titles when being ranked this low, as the team is now effectively eliminated from the college football playoff race after suffering its third loss of the year. While Ryan Day and company will likely pine for their team to still make it and point to their strength of schedule outside the conference, including most notably a loss to the Texas Longhorns earlier this year, the committee’s precedent from last year would not seem to bode well for the Buckeyes. Meanwhile, Ohio State has largely fallen apart since quarterback Julian Sayin went down with an injury, with the offense going completely dormant in the second half vs Oregon and the defense also falling well short of expectations. In any case, Ohio State will next hit the field on Saturday for a home game against Northwestern. Kickoff for that game is set for 12:00 pm ET. articles.title: Mario Cristobal criticizes officials for negating potential game-tying Miami touchdown: 'It's bulls**t'

The Hurricanes were one of three remaining FBS teams with an unblemished record, but that is no longer the case. Miami now has one loss on its resume, while […]
articles._body: No. 1 Miami ‘s perfect season came to an end Saturday night at the hands of the No. 11 ranked Notre Dame Fighting Irish in South Bend. The Hurricanes were one of three remaining FBS teams with an unblemished record, but that is no longer the case. Miami now has one loss on its resume, while Notre Dame snagged its signature victory en route to a potential CFP appearance. Following the loss, head coach Mario Cristobal blasted the officiating for negating what might have been a potential game-tying touchdown with 3:36 remaining in the fourth quarter. Receiver Elija Lofton appeared to haul in the score, before it was broken up at the last second by Notre Dame safety Luke Talich . After a review, it was determined Lofton did not have full possession of the catch, which turned the ball over on downs. TD OR NO?!?!?!! pic.twitter.com/gOEHWVUDDd — Grant Reacts (@GrantReacts1) November 8, 2026 $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage “Really, really disappointed that they negated Elija Lofton ‘s touchdown with two hands on the ball and two feet in bounds,” Cristobal said in his postgame news conference. “But, like we told our team before we left Miami , do not leave it in the hands of the officials because that’s what you’re going to get out here. “ I’m pissed off. It’s bulls**t, and I’ll leave it at that . That’s the way it was seen by them. So I got to live with it and respect it, and our players got to live with it, and we got to do better. Again, don’t leave it in the hands of the officials.” Notre Dame snagged signature victory with win over Miami While Miami is no longer undefeated, Notre Dame now has its signature victory. Just last week, CFP Chair Hunter Yuracheck claimed the Irish were ranked at No. 11 in the inaugural Rankings due to just that very thing . Notre Dame , now sitting at 8-1 on the season with games against Boston College , SMU , and Syracuse remaining, looks to be in good shape to return to the College Football Playoff. “A special moment for them,” Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman said postgame. “I’m so happy for our players because they put a lot of work in to achieve this. They’re a dang good football team, and they beat a dang good football team.” “When it mattered the most, we executed. It got a little ugly in that second half, and we talked about this moment before the game. I said at some point in the game, there’s going to be a struggle. I don’t know when it’s going to be, but they battle through it and they execute it when it matters the most.”

Lofton had two hands on the ball and two feet down in what looked like the game-tying touchdown late, but he lost control of the ball and did not complete the process of the catch. Controversial or not, Miami still controls its own destiny. 6. Indiana After two stressful wins, Indiana had a much needed bye week and are 8-1 on the season. It seems like them, and fellow AP Poll top 10 team UCLA, are going to be the two teams playing for the Big Ten. Still, there are three weeks to go and the Hoosiers will play host to USC this coming weekend. That’ll be the game to watch to see which squad is actually for real in 2026 and can make the CFP. 7. Alabama (+2) Talk about statement games. Alabama moved up the AP Poll with an impressive win over LSU in Baton Rouge, in a game where many thought LSU could hit their stride. Not this time as the Crimson Tide won 31-13. Alabama outscored LSU 21-10 in the second half to run away with this one. Keelon Russell threw for 206 yards and three touchdowns in the win for Kalen DeBoer’s crew. 8. Texas (+2) It was a slow start for Texas, but the Longhorns hit their groove to stay in the top 10 of the AP Poll this week. The Longhorns went on the road and beat Missouri 34-20 to improve to 7-2 on the season. Arch Manning threw for 297 yards and three touchdowns despite no Cam Coleman. Raleek Brown ran for 85 yards and a score on the ground. Texas also outscored Missouri 24-10 in the second half. 9. Tennessee (+7) So much for Tennessee not being legit right? They moved up the AP Poll with a 34-6 thrashing of Kentucky in Knoxville and improved to 7-2 on the season. The ground game dominated in this one. DeSean Bishop had 25 carries for 109 yards and two touchdowns while Duane Morris had 85 yards and a score. Tennessee seems poised to win out at this point too with Texas A&M, LSU and Vanderbilt left on the schedule. 10. Texas Tech (+3) Texas Tech is alive folks! A lot of people left them for dead but the Red Raiders are now 8-1 on the season following a 53-48 shootout win over West Virginia. The QB switch to Thomas Castellanos has now paid off. Castellanos helped Texas Tech move up the AP Poll by throwing for 362 yards and five touchdowns! Not only that, he ran for 102 yards on the ground. Imagine if he can keep that pace up! 11. Wake Forest (+3) There’s not much to say about Wake Forest this week except that they scored 77 points against Merrimack and shut them out. It wasn’t beating an AP Poll ranked team, but the Demon Deacons took care of business. Steele Pizzella threw for 432 yards and three touchdowns and also ran for 63 yards and a touchdown. Now the important stretch: at SMU, at Georgia Tech and home against Duke in an ACC that’s there for the taking. 12. BYU (-5) BYU fell in the AP Poll and the Cougars suffered their second loss of the season, losing 28-20 to rival Utah on the road. Bear Bachmeier was picked off four times in this one and the Cougars still blew a 20-14 halftime lead. BYU has to win out to have any shot at the Big 12 championship, likely a rematch against Utah. At that point, they might need that in order to have a shot at the College Football Playoff in a few weeks. 13. Kentucky (-5) Kentucky was everyone’s darling this year and with three games left, that 7-2 record suddenly looks suspect. Well, we don’t want to get ahead of ourselve

articles.title: Celine Dion Goes Backstage With Metallica After Rocking Out at Sphere: ‘Loved the Show’
articles.summary: The Grammy-winning singer was spotted enjoying the show alongside Jack Black.
articles._body: Celine Dion embraced her inner metalhead at Metallica ‘s Sphere show in Las Vegas. After going viral for playing air bass during Metallica’s Nov. 5 performance at Sphere in Las Vegas, the superstar singer returned for the band’s Life Burns Faster residency show on Saturday (Nov. 7), where she was spotted enjoying the concert alongside Jack Black before meeting the heavy metal legends backstage. Related Céline Dion Plays Air Bass at Metallica’s Sphere Show Metallica Sphere Setlist: Every Song From Night 1 of ‘Life Burns Faster’ Las Vegas Residency Simple Plan Are Meeting a Whole New Generation of Fans, 25 Years In In video obtained by TMZ from Saturday’s show, Dion threw her arms in the air and headbanged along as Metallica performed its iconic 1991 hit “Enter Sandman” while also showing off her air-guitar skills. Black stood alongside Dion, clapping over his head during a guitar solo and enthusiastically taking in the show. Following the concert, Dion went backstage to meet Metallica members James Hetfield, Lars Ulrich, Kirk Hammett and Robert Trujillo. She shared a series of behind-the-scenes photos from the encounter on Instagram , including moments with her sons Eddy and Nelson Angélil, whom she shares with her late husband, René Angélil. “Thank you James, Lars, Kirk and Rob and everyone from the @Metallica organization for the warm welcome!” Dion captioned the gallery. “We had such a wonderful time seeing you at the Sphere. We absolutely loved the show.🤘” The carousel features a group photo of Dion posing with her sons and the band, along with playful shots of the singer alongside bassist Trujillo and a black-and-white snapshot of her chatting with frontman Hetfield. While Dion’s enthusiasm might come as a surprise to fans more familiar with her soaring ballads, her appreciation for Metallica is hardly new. Earlier this year, she shared a selection of songs from her personal playlist that included the band’s 1996 song “Until It Sleeps.” Dion is also no stranger to Las Vegas residencies. The Grammy-winning singer headlined two celebrated runs at the Colosseum at Caesars Palace from 2011 to 2019. The two residencies grossed a combined $681.3 million , according to Billboard Boxscore. Her recent Metallica appearances come during a milestone year for the singer. On Sept. 12, Dion returned to the stage for her first full-length concert in more than six years, opening a 26-show residency in Paris. The performances marked a significant step in her return to live music after she revealed in December 2022 that she had been diagnosed with stiff-person syndrome , a rare neurological disorder that causes muscle stiffness and spasms and forced her to step away from touring. Metallica launched its Life Burns Faster residency at Sphere on Oct. 1. The band’s fall 2026 run wrapped Saturday (Nov. 7), but the residency is scheduled to return to the Las Vegas venue for additional performances beginning in January 2027, with dates currently extending through March.

articles.title: Philip Rivers Expected to be Hired As NC State Coach
articles.summary: USA TODAY Network
articles._body: Philip Rivers, the longtime Chargers quarterback who postponed his Pro Football Hall of Fame candidacy to make an NFL return last season with the Colts, is expected to be hired as the next head coach at North Carolina State, a source confirmed Sunday to Front Office Sports . Rivers, 44, has been a high school coach in Alabama. He interviewed in January for the Bills’ head coaching job but was not hired. He moves to the college coaching ranks in a return to his alma mater. Another prominent former NFL quarterback who previously played at NC State, Russell Wilson, also interviewed for the job. But Rivers emerged in recent days as the focus of the school’s search and is expected to finish an agreement to be its coach, barring any last-minute snags. On3 first reported that the school was working to finalize a deal with Rivers. School officials did not immediately respond to requests for comment Sunday by FOS . Rivers was not available to comment. His son, Gunner Rivers, plays quarterback for his father at St. Michael Catholic High School and has verbally committed to play for the Wolfpack. St. Michael was eliminated from the Alabama state playoffs on Friday. Rivers played in three games for the Colts last season after retiring as a player following the 2020 season. His return pushed back his Hall of Fame eligibility by five years. He was an eight-time Pro Bowl selection in 18 NFL seasons for the Chargers, both in San Diego and Los Angeles, and Colts. Rivers ranks eighth in NFL history with his 63,984 career passing yards and seventh with his 425 touchdown passes. He had an estimated $244.2 million in career NFL earnings, according to Spotrac. He succeeds Dave Doeren, who was fired last month after 14 seasons. The school owes Doeren more than $9 million. Todd Goebbel was named the interim head coach for the remainder of this season. Stocks will tumble much further as AI investment will slow next year then fall in 2028 and drag GDP down too, economist predicts
articles.summary: Capital Economics expects the S&P 500 will be 12% below its current level by the end of 2027, putting it 17% off its early-October peak.
articles._body: Investors have already taken a severe beating recently, but there’s much more stock market carnage in store as the AI investment boom wanes, according to Capital Economics. In a note on Friday, Chief Economic Adviser Vicky Redwood said AI still has potential to boost productivity but is bearish about the amount of revenue that can be generated to sustain the rate of investment. A handful of hyperscalers are expected to spend $800 billion this year, double from a year ago, and invest an estimated $1 trillion or more in 2027. Many forecasts assume annual capital expenditures will remain above $1 trillion for several years. But Redwood calculated that annual AI-related revenues earned from external customers would have to explode by 10-fold by 2030 to justify all that spending. While that’s possible, it implies a much more severe and rapid disruption to the economy than currently seen, such major displacement of existing businesses and labor. As a result, she thinks investment will continue to rise next year but at a slower pace—then fall outright in 2028 by around 10%. Given that higher AI investment added 0.3 percentage point to U.S. GDP growth last year, a capex slowdown should trim that much from its recent growth rate, Redwood estimated, and a 10% capex drop might take 0.1% off GDP. That’s actually just a slight haircut, especially compared to more AI-dependent economies in Asia. Taiwan’s real GDP growth next year should be around 3 percentage points lower, and South Korea’s should be 1 point lower, with a further drag in 2028. Meanwhile, the stock market will price in the looming AI capex drop even sooner. Redwood expects the S&P 500 will be 12% below its current level by the end of 2027, putting it 17% off its early-October peak. “We expect considerably larger falls in tech-heavy indices,” she added. “A tightening of financial conditions driven by factors such as higher energy prices or term premia could also make financing investment hard.” Lower stock prices will also feed into the economy via the wealth effect, which fuels consumer spending. The market’s rally over the past year lifted GDP by around 0.4%, according to Redwood, so a stock selloff should produce an economic drag of similar scale. Despite the warnings about capex, GDP and stocks, AI will continue to work its way into the economy and improve productivity, helped by the infrastructure that’s already been built and the new investment that’s on the way, albeit at a slower rate. In fact, capex could remain relatively high even after declining, Redwood pointed out, as hyperscalers keep spending to replace depreciating equipment, exploit economies of scale, and stay ahead in the “winner-takes-most” AI race. They could also spread out any investment declines over several years instead of all at once. “The bottom line for the U.S. economy is that we expect slower GDP growth in 2028, but not a major downturn,” Redwood wrote. “Admittedly, recessions have sometimes followed previous capex booms and busts, including in the early 2000s after the dotcom bust. However, a fall in capital spending alone has generally not been sufficient to cause a recession.” At the same time, AI adoption should continue to expand, boosting productivity and supporting output growth. Redwood estimated that AI will increase U.S. productivity by about 1% per year for several years. She does not expect an abrupt collapse in AI investment or a severe economic downturn when the boom ends. “Rather, we expect investment to adjust to a more sustainable pace, with sufficient capacity still being added to support further growth in AI usage,” she concluded. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

AntiFind indexes filesystems, not folders.

It maintains a live view of storage by reading filesystem metadata directly. Because it understands the underlying filesyst
articles._body: I've made AntiFind, to allow you to search everywhere at once, vastly increasing the efficiency of LLMs and your own searches: AntiFind indexes filesystems, not folders. It maintains a live view of storage by reading filesystem metadata directly. Because it understands the underlying filesystems, it can search across storage that the operating system is not currently exposing, including unmounted partitions. Allowing you to search for and play media from Linux in your Windows and the other way around. Without mounting the drives. This works on Linux, Windows and MacOS. The underlying idea is simple: instead of walking directories, read the filesystem's file tables directly. Most tools discover the filesystem again every time you search. AntiFind reads the drive's metadata in one pass and then follows changes as they happen. AntiFind supports Windows, Linux and macOS. It includes both a GUI and a command line. The CLI supports JSON output (--json) and was designed to integrate cleanly with automation and LLM workflows. There's a lot more to it, and you can find timings on my site, but that's the core idea. Both teams have important frontcourt players dealing with injuries ahead of their second meeting in less than a week. Philadelphia enters Sunday’s contest looking to build on its 126-107 victory over Chicago on Monday. However, the Bulls kept the game competitive before the Sixers pulled away late. Chicago has since fallen to 1-7 and is riding a six-game losing streak. The Sixers also have other frontcourt concerns. Adem Bona is out with a cervical spine sprain, while Dominick Barlow remains sidelined because of a lower back stress reaction. Embiid’s availability is especially important with Philadelphia short on healthy big men. His probable designation offers some optimism, although his foot condition remains something to monitor. Chicago has its own questions beyond Claxton. Jalen Smith is probable despite a left finger sprain, while Tobe Awaka is questionable with an MCL sprain. Zach Collins and Dailyn Swain are ruled out. The Bulls enter with a rest advantage after last playing Wednesday. Still, Joel Embiid and Nic Claxton’s return could be the biggest factors in Sunday’s matchup. articles._body: In an article published early last month, controversial former Michigan football staffer Connor Stalions delivered a scathing critique on X, targeting first-year Wolverines head coach Kyle Whittingham amid the team’s rocky 3-2 start. articles._body: The Missouri football team suffered a tough defeat on Saturday to Texas. Missouri was defeated, 34-20. Tigers head coach Eli Drinkwitz wasn’t happy after the game. “If I say what I want to say, I’m going to get fined until I don’t have any retirement, and I’m not going to do that. I’m not going to blame the officials. That would be disrespectful to Coach Sarkisian and his team,” Drinkwitz said, per On3. Missouri dropped to 6-3 on the season. The Tigers finished the game allowing 401 total yards of offense to the Longhorns. The Tigers struggled to move the chains. Missouri finished the game going just 3-for-16 on third-down conversions. The team also couldn’t take advantage when Texas made mistakes. “I could hear the talk getting on the plane yesterday. I could hear the talk when we got here. Nobody believed we’d win the game,” Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said, per ESPN. “Nobody thought we were going to come here and win the game. Nobody thought we were tough enough at the line of scrimmage.” Texas improved to 7-2 on the year. There were some questionable calls during Missouri-Texas game At least one college football analyst feels Drinkwitz’s pain. That is Jesse Palmer from ESPN. Palmer felt that a play that was called a fumble on Texas should have instead been ruled an incomplete pass. Because the play was ruled a fumble, Texas was actually able to gain yards on the play. The ball moved downfield . “If you’re a Missouri fan, if you’re Eli Drinkwitz, you are livid because it does feel like a lot of these calls are going against Missouri today,” Palmer said, per Awful Announcing, regarding the officiating in the game. Missouri’s loss effectively ends their chances at making the College Football Playoff this season. The Tigers are now 3-3 in SEC play. The team’s losses this season are to Texas, Ole Miss and Mississippi State. Missouri next plays Georgia on Saturday. Show HN: FELF – AppImage-like single binaries without FUSE, root, or a runtime
articles.summary:
Hello HN!

I've always had a bad time redistributing programs that use shared libraries, AppImage in my opinion does too much, and a container is an overkill - not always integrates smoothly.

I've moved to nix since long ago, but redistributing between nix and other distros or vice versa it's
articles._body: Hello HN! I've always had a bad time redistributing programs that use shared libraries, AppImage in my opinion does too much, and a container is an overkill - not always integrates smoothly. I've moved to nix since long ago, but redistributing between nix and other distros or vice versa it's still a pain in the ass, more so if you want to run an alien app in nix or a nix app without the package manger in any other distro. For that, with the help of Claude, I've implemented a format that deduces at pack-time all the shared libraries a program needs, puts them, together with its own glibc and a patched dynamic linker into a single executable. This means that you don't actually need a runtime nor any special capability, it can run inside a FROM SCRATCH docker, alpine linux etc... And it also supports coreutils-like multiple programs accessible via symlinks, so it is a good fit for that purpose. You can just use: > felf pack $(which git) --output git.felf and you'll have already a git binary that works everywhere, no matter which distro you are building this from. This only packs the binary and their dependencies. Essentially, the effect is similar as if you LD_PRELOAD's all the libraries that it requires. In the end, we have been fighting these demons since long long ago, chroots/docker/appimage/flatpack/nix etc... So this xkcd applies: https://xkcd.com/927/ I'm happy to share the project, I hope it inspires new discoveries/tools in this regard! articles._body: Texas football greatly strengthened its College Football Playoff resume and kept its SEC title aspirations alive by securing a dominant 34-20 road victory over No. 18 Missouri. This victory marked a fourth significant win against a top-20 opponent in a stellar postseason-building campaign led by head coach Steve Sarkisian and quarterback Arch Manning. The crucial win reinforced the Longhorns’ standing among the nation’s elite. After the game, Sarkisian delivered a passionate address that addressed external doubts about his team’s capabilities. Reports shared on X by Tyler Horka highlighted Sarkisian’s defiant stance: “Nobody believed Texas would win today, and the Longhorns proved the doubters wrong,” he stated, adding , “We’re big-game hunters, and we showed up again today.” Horka also captured Sarkisian’s emphasis on team grit, noting that the coach believes Texas is one of the toughest teams in America because “there is a toughness in our organization that is undeniable. Right when people want to count us out, we refuse to go away.” Concluding his message, Sarkisian explained the ultimate purpose behind their efforts: “We don’t recruit really well; we don’t recruit really hard for fun. It’s for moments like today.” This unyielding culture continues to fuel the Longhorns as they navigate a challenging schedule, proving that Sarkisian’s squad thrives when the stakes are highest.
