articles.title: The Strokes Get a Surprise Visit From Walton Goggins During ‘SNL’ Performance: Watch
articles.summary: The NYC band performed “Lonely in the Future” and “Going Shopping” during its Nov. 7 appearance on the show.
articles._body: The Strokes rocked Saturday Night Live with two new songs and a surprise appearance by Walton Goggins. The New York City rock band appeared during the Druski-hosted episode on Nov. 7, performing “Lonely in the Future” and “Going Shopping,” both featured on its seventh studio album, Reality Awaits , which arrived in July. Related The Strokes Better Look Out: Druski Is Coming for Their Musical Guest Gig in New ‘SNL’ Promos Simple Plan Are Meeting a Whole New Generation of Fans, 25 Years In Deep Purple's Ian Gillan Shares Encouraging News After Undergoing Surgery For their first performance, the Julian Casablancas -led quintet delivered “Lonely in the Future” against a backdrop of psychedelic visuals and elaborate lighting. Following the performance, the band released the song’s official music video , which features a cast of handcrafted puppets created in collaboration with the team behind the British satirical series Spitting Image . The group closed its SNL musical guest appearance with “Going Shopping,” which featured a surprise appearance by actor Goggins. Dressed in an all-black suit and sunglasses, the Fallout star joined the band on bongos, reprising his role in the song’s music video. Saturday’s appearance marked The Strokes’ fourth time as musical guests on SNL . The band made its debut on the NBC sketch comedy show in January 2002, followed by performances in 2006 and 2011. The Strokes are currently promoting Reality Awaits , which debuted at No. 13 on the all-genre Billboard 200 and No. 5 on the Top Rock & Alternative Albums chart. The nine-track set was recorded in Costa Rica with legendary producer Rick Rubin, who previously worked with the act on its 2020 album, The New Abnormal . SNL is back Nov. 14 with fan favorite John Mulaney returning to host and Phoebe Bridgers taking the stage as musical guest. articles.title: Cowboys’ George Pickens, Joey Porter Jr., DeMarvion Overshown all out vs. Colts
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys are scheduled to take on the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday for a pivotal Week 9 matchup. However, the club will be without several key players, including George Pickens, Joey Porter Jr., and DeMarvion Overshown. Reports indicate that Pickens, Porter, and Overshown have all been
articles._body: The Dallas Cowboys are scheduled to take on the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday for a pivotal Week 9 matchup. However, the club will be without several key players, including George Pickens, Joey Porter Jr., and DeMarvion Overshown. Reports indicate that Pickens, Porter, and Overshown have all been officially ruled out for Sunday’s contest against the Colts, according to Todd Archer of ESPN. The 25-year-old wide receiver is dealing with shoulder and hamstring injuries, while Porter is dealing with an ankle issue, and Overshown has back and hamstring injuries. “The Cowboys will be without wide receiver George Pickens (shoulder, hamstring), cornerback Joey Porter Jr. (ankle), and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (back, hamstring) today against the Colts, according to multiple sources,” Archer reported. This will be Pickens’ first missed game of the 2026-27 campaign. While it’s been a down year compared to last season, the five-year veteran has still put up decent numbers in his second season with the Cowboys . He’ll sit out Week 9 with 39 receptions, 533 yards, and two touchdowns. As for Porter, injuries have been the story for the 26-year-old cornerback this year. He didn’t play a single snap with the Pittsburgh Steelers before being traded to the Cowboys in early October. Since the trade, Porter has only appeared in four games, accumulating eight combined tackles (six solo) and three pass deflections. Similar to Porter, Overshown has also missed a majority of the season due to injuries. He’s been limited to just three appearances (two starts) and is now missing yet another contest with the Cowboys. However, the 26-year-old has been productive when on the field this year, recording 20 combined tackles (eight solo), one interception, and one forced fumble. articles.title: Positive Jalen Duren Pistons injury update comes with buzzkill
articles.summary: With the Detroit Pistons dealing with injury concerns as center Jalen Duren is dealing with a hamstring issue, the latest update comes with good and bad news. As it was understood that Duren’s injury with the Pistons would force him out for weeks, the team would make an announcement showing
articles._body: With the Detroit Pistons dealing with injury concerns as center Jalen Duren is dealing with a hamstring issue, the latest update comes with good and bad news. As it was understood that Duren’s injury with the Pistons would force him out for weeks, the team would make an announcement showing his progress. According to ClutchPoints’ NBA insider Brett Siegel, Detroit would announce that Duren is making progress when it comes to his rehab for his hamstring injury and has “begun on-court activities.” However, the team would make sure to say that his “status will be updated again in two weeks.” “Jalen Duren is making progress in his rehab for a right hamstring strain and has begun on-court activities,” Siegel wrote on X, formerly Twitter. “His status will be updated again in two weeks.” Duren suffered the injury in the Pistons’ 128-111 win over the Miami Heat on Oct. 23 in the second quarter as he attempted a spin move on Giannis Antetokounmpo. The pain was immediate, as he grabbed his leg during the play, went to the locker room, and didn’t return to the contest. More on the injury to Pistons’ Jalen Duren According to Coty M. Davis of The Detroit News, the Pistons center did an on-court workout on Thursday after the team’s practice, as he was doing dribbling drills “while catching a tennis ball with his left.” Also working with Detroit’s player development staff and taking some shots, and while he’s critical to the team’s success, the team is 6-2 ahead of Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Lakers. Speaking earlier in the week, Pistons head coach J.B. Bickerstaff would applaud how “the guys have stepped up,” such as big men Peyton Reed, John Collins, and Tolu Smith, though it’s obvious that the team misses Duren, according to The Athletic. Only playing two games this season for Detroit, Duren looks to replicate or exceed what he produced last season, averaging 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds per game while shooting 65 percent from the field. At any rate, it remains to be seen when Duren returns to the court in game action with the Pistons. articles._body: The Sacramento Kings received a potential boost ahead of Sunday’s matchup against the Miami Heat , as Keegan Murray has been upgraded to questionable. The forward had previously been listed as out while dealing with a left ankle issue . According to the Sacramento Kings’ latest injury report, Murray is questionable because of left ankle capsulitis . His status will depend on how he responds before tipoff, and his playing time could be monitored if he is cleared. Meanwhile, Jonathan Mogbo and Sean Pedulla are out on G League two-way assignments. Maxime Raynaud is also sidelined with a right patella subluxation, while Ben Simmons remains out following right Achilles tendon surgery. The absence of Keegan Murray and Ben Simmons leaves the Sacramento Kings without two valuable contributors, as both players offer important skills in scoring, playmaking, and defensive versatility. Murray’s potential return would be a welcome development for a Sacramento team looking to turn around its difficult start. The Kings enter the contest with a 1-7 record and have lost three consecutive games at home. Having another offensive option available could help them challenge Miami. The Heat, meanwhile, are coming off a 120-100 loss to the Golden State Warriors. Bam Adebayo finished with 18 points and 10 rebounds, but Miami struggled to contain Golden State’s offense, particularly in the third quarter. Miami holds a 3-6 record and will look to take advantage of Sacramento’s injury concerns. The Heat have no players listed on their injury report, giving them a healthier roster heading into the matchup. Sunday’s game presents an opportunity for both teams to regain momentum. Murray’s availability could be an important factor, especially if the Kings hope to end their home losing streak. Tipoff is scheduled for 9 p.m. ET in Sacramento. articles._body: The New York Giants will be facing the Philadelphia Eagles this week, and they could be without one of their running backs in the matchup. Cam Skattebo suffered a hamstring injury against the Houston Texans in their last game, and he’s still trying to recover from it. According to ESPN’s Jordan Raanan, he won’t be available for the game. “RB Cam Skattebo (hamstring) out on the field in sneakers. Not going through a workout. He’s not going to play Sunday vs. Eagles. Skattebo was doubtful for the contest,” Raanan wrote on X, formerly Twitter. That’s not the best news for the Giants, and it’ll have to be the next man up for the rest of their running backs. Watch Giants vs. Eagles LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Cam Skattebo’s injury status vs. Eagles Skattebo was listed as doubtful on the injury report, so there was a good chance he was never going to play unless a miracle happened. He also didn’t practice on Friday, which was another indicator that he wasn’t going to be available. That means Devin Singletary will get a load of the snaps for the Giants in the backfield, and he also had a good game against the Texans. The hope is that Skattebo’s injury doesn’t keep him out for any longer, but hamstring issues are always tricky. That may be one of the reasons the Giants are looking to improve their running back room, as they’ve been one of the teams that have shown interest in Jonathan Taylor . According to Jay Glazer, the Giants offered the Indianapolis Colts a 2nd- and 5th-round pick for Taylor, but the offer has since been pulled. They don’t have long until the trade deadline, and it’ll be interesting to see if they make the Colts another offer. articles.title: ‘On par with what the DoD pursued during the Cold War’: Pentagon’s war stockpile plan hits a minerals wall
articles.summary: FORTRESS America calls for reserves of critical minerals, fuel, and munitions inside the U.S. A $2 billion tungsten deal shows why filling them will take years.
articles._body: The Pentagon wants to stockpile enough critical minerals, fuel, and munitions on American soil to keep fighting a major war even if cyberattacks and sabotage knock out factories and power grids at home. One defense expert says the scale of the planned effort is “on par with what the DoD pursued during the Cold War.” The minerals may be the hardest part. The U.S. produces less than 1% of the most common type of rare-earth magnet it uses, and China, which dominates the processing of many critical minerals, has kept American companies short even in peacetime. The initiative, known as FORTRESS America, short for Federal Operations for Resilience, Troop Resources, Energy, Supply, and Survivability, was formally established on Sept. 30 . It is designed to keep U.S. forces operating if a conflict disrupts domestic power grids and manufacturing supply chains, and it is the same program behind the Pentagon’s push for major bases to plan for 90 days without the grid . Stockpiling materials isn’t unusual for the U.S. military, Bryan Clark, a senior fellow at the Hudson Institute, told Fortune . What distinguishes FORTRESS is its planned scale and its shift toward domestic reserves rather than overseas stockpiles. During the Cold War, the Pentagon stored as much or more war matériel overseas, near anticipated battlefields in Eastern Europe or Northeast Asia, Clark said. FORTRESS instead focuses on protecting supplies inside the United States, reflecting growing concern that American factories could themselves become targets. China could disrupt U.S. industrial production through cyber operations, drones, electromagnetic warfare, or attacks carried out by people inside the country, Clark warned. U.S. agencies have already warned that Chinese state-sponsored hackers had positioned themselves inside American critical infrastructure . That concern has a recent precedent in Europe. On Dec. 29, 2025, cyberattacks hit about 30 renewable energy sites, a manufacturing company, and a heat and power plant serving nearly 500,000 customers in Poland. Polish officials linked the attacks to Russia’s Federal Security Service and said the attackers tried to destroy industrial systems, but the country avoided a major outage. America makes less than 1% of its most common rare-earth magnet Building stockpiles on the scale Clark described runs into a stark industrial reality: America’s defense industry remains deeply reliant on foreign supply chains for its raw materials. In 2025, the U.S. imported about $60 billion worth of critical minerals other than rare earths, including nickel, lithium, cobalt, graphite, and tungsten, according to the Peterson Institute for International Economics. The gap is most acute in rare-earth magnets. U.S. demand for the most common type reached roughly 48,000 metric tons in 2025, while domestic sources supplied just 300 metric tons, according to Arthur D. Little data reported by Reuters . U.S. companies are on track to have capacity for about 5,000 metric tons by the end of this year, roughly a tenth of last year’s demand. The shortage has already reached factory floors. Ford, No. 22 on the 2026 Fortune 500 , idled its Chicago Explorer plant for a week in May 2025 when rare-earth supplies ran short. China has repeatedly tightened rare-earth export controls , and American companies are still struggling to secure enough supply, Reuters reported on Nov. 6, citing U.S. officials. That day, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer pressed Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng to fully carry out Beijing’s commitments on rare earths and other critical minerals. A major war could further disrupt overseas production and shipping routes, making it harder for the Pentagon to replenish its stockpiles. To reduce foreign dependence, Clark said, the Pentagon is pursuing a dual approach: building raw-material reserves while funding domestic mining and processing capacity. Why a $2 billion tungsten deal won’t fill the stockpile soon Tungsten, a stockpiling priority Clark identified, illustrates why building reserves takes more than government spending. The U.S. hasn’t commercially mined tungsten since 2015, when cheaper imports undercut domestic production, according to Scientific American . Its net import reliance for the metal exceeded 50% in 2025 , according to the U.S. Geological Survey. In September, tungsten manufacturer The Elmet Group won a Defense Logistics Agency contract worth up to $2 billion to supply tungsten ores, concentrates, and sodium tungstate to the National Defense Stockpile. Only $150 million of that is guaranteed. The Pentagon also committed $450 million to Elmet, including about $150 million earmarked to restart the Springer tungsten complex in Nevada . Yet Elmet said it won’t begin deliveries to the stockpile until additional supply becomes available. To avoid diverting existing tungsten from American manufacturers, the company plans to wait until new production comes online from investments in Nevada, Australia, and Spain. The deal illustrates a problem FORTRESS could face across the board: signing supply contracts doesn’t immediately put minerals into government vaults. A price tag that could reach hundreds of billions The cost of FORTRESS also remains uncertain. A senior defense official told reporters on Oct. 20 that officials are still assessing costs, Air & Space Forces Magazine reported . The magazine estimated the broader initiative could cost “scores of billions of dollars, if not hundreds of billions.” To help cover the bill, the Pentagon is exploring public-private partnerships, Dale Marks, assistant secretary of defense for energy, installations, and environment, told Breaking Defense . Even with capital flowing, analysts warn that supply chain independence can’t be rushed. “The Pentagon is unlikely to meet the goals in the near term,” Clark said, pointing to the structural difficulty of rapidly stockpiling both finished weapons and raw minerals. Chris Berry, a minerals

articles.title: Trinidad Chambliss left ’embarrassed’ by Georgia after failing to tie Ole Miss record
articles.summary: Ahead of a crucial matchup against Georgia, Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss received high praise from former NFL signal-caller Chase Daniel on SEC Nation, who called him one of the best and most versatile players in the entire country. Georgia head coach Kirby Smart also expressed respect
articles._body: Ahead of a crucial matchup against Georgia, Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss received high praise from former NFL signal-caller Chase Daniel on SEC Nation, who called him one of the best and most versatile players in the entire country. Georgia head coach Kirby Smart also expressed respect for Chambliss, labeling him an elite player who is extremely difficult to defend, as the 6-2 Rebels sought a vital resume-building win. Chambliss entered the game with 2,189 passing yards and 18 touchdowns on the season. However, Georgia’s elite defense effectively shut down Ole Miss’s high-powered offense in a dominant 42-7 victory in Oxford. Following the blowout, a series of reports shared on X by Brad Logan, Yahoo Sports, and The Next Round highlighted the harsh reality of the loss. Logan captured Chambliss’s candid postgame assessment, where the quarterback admitted , “It’s embarrassing,” adding that “It’s unacceptable. It’s not Ole Miss football. It’s tough,” while maintaining resilience by stating , “I don’t think our season is over.” Furthermore, Yahoo Sports pointed out that Chambliss was held without a touchdown pass for the first time as Ole Miss’s starter, falling just one game shy of tying Chad Kelly’s school record for consecutive games with a scoring pass. Acknowledging the effective game plan, Kirby Smart told The Next Round postgame, “There’s really only one way to play this guy. You either give him a lot of time, and he gets you, or you give him less time, and you try to get him.” Despite the crushing defeat that significantly impacts their College Football Playoff aspirations, Chambliss and the Rebels must quickly regroup to salvage their campaign as the season progresses. articles._body: NC State football is going through a disappointing 2026 season, one that saw head coach Dave Doeren get fired in October. Now, as the Wolfpack play out the string on the rest of the year, it has already settled on its next head coach. Legendary NFL quarterback Philip Rivers, an NC State alum, is expected to be the next head coach in Raleigh. The two sides are working to finalize a deal , and Rivers has already started contacting potential front office and staff candidates, per On3 Sports. Rivers is one of the program legends at NC State. He played there from 2000-03 and threw for more than 13,000 yards and 95 touchdowns in his career there. He went on to play 18 NFL seasons and will have an argument to make the Pro Football Hall of Fame when he is eligible in a few years. After retiring from the NFL, Rivers became a high school football coach at St. Michael Catholic in Alabama. He had a 44-16 record as the head coach there in five seasons before returning to the NFL as a player briefly in 2025. NC State came into this season with some fairly high expectations, with star quarterback CJ Bailey returning. But instead, the Wolfpack have had a season defined by missed opportunities, namely in a loss to Vanderbilt on the last play of the game. Rivers should have a decent number of pieces to work with in his first year in 2027. There is a good chance Bailey opts to come back to school, though the possibility of him entering the transfer portal remains. While he has been inconsistent this season, he has shown signs of growth that are the major reason why he is one of the most talented passers in the nation. Wolfpack fans will be hoping that, under the tutelage of one of the best quarterbacks in NFL history, Bailey can unlock his full potential in 2027. If he does, this NC State team will be a factor in the ACC title race right away. The post NC State football finalizing deal to make Philip Rivers next head coach appeared first on ClutchPoints .

It should be no surprise that Ja’Marr Chase was a big part of the Bengals’ hot start. Chase joined legendary wide re
articles._body: The Cincinnati Bengals did whatever they wanted in the first half in Madrid . Cincinnati entered halftime up 24-10 over Atlanta after a special start from their offense. It should be no surprise that Ja’Marr Chase was a big part of the Bengals’ hot start . Chase joined legendary wide receiver Randy Moss as the only receivers in NFL history with seven or more touchdowns in each of their first six seasons in the league, per Ari Meirov. Ja’Marr had some truly explosive production during the first half. He hauled in eight receptions for 142 receiving yards and a touchdown. That is the most by any Bengals player in the first half since 1988 , per ESPN Insights. Chase showed a little bit of everything in the first half. On top of his great stats, he logged 55 yards after the catch and two broken tackles. The actual catches themselves were quite impressive, with one toe-tapping catch and another wild one-handed grab. The Bengals needed their passing game to power their offense in the first half. Cincinnati finished the first half with just over 40 rushing yards on nine attempts. Chase Brown was not finding much room to operate on a consistent basis. That put a lot more pressure on Burrow, Chase, and Tee Higgins to move the sticks. Cincinnati started off strong with a 47-yard touchdown pass between Burrow and Chase on the team’s opening drive. Chase continued hauling in impressive catches after that, nearly scoring on a few different occasions. Higgins also caught a touchdown pass and Burrow sneaked the ball in for a one-yard rushing touchdown. Finally, kicker Evan McPherson drilled a 57-yard field goal just before halftime. Hopefully the Bengals can continue leaning on their offense throughout the second half. If they can keep up this pace, they should prevail with a victory. Cincinnati is up 31-17 with just two minutes left in the third quarter. articles.title: Notre Dame HC Marcus Freeman’s message to CFP committee after Miami win cold takes initial ranking snub
articles.summary: One of the biggest surprises of the initial College Football Playoff rankings last Tuesday was the placement of Notre Dame. The Irish, despite a 7-1 record and a sterling history of laying waste to inferior opponents, came in at No. 11 in the rankings, right on the projected cut line. The selecti
articles._body: One of the biggest surprises of the initial College Football Playoff rankings last Tuesday was the placement of Notre Dame. The Irish, despite a 7-1 record and a sterling history of laying waste to inferior opponents, came in at No. 11 in the rankings , right on the projected cut line. The selection committee sent Notre Dame a message: win against No. 1 Miami on Saturday night, or you are likely out. Marcus Freeman and company answered the bell , getting a 31-24 win over the top-ranked team in the country in South Bend and sending a message that they are national title contenders in the process. After the game, Freeman talked about using that initial ranking, which came as a shock to many, as motivation coming into this game. “We learned that last year, it doesn’t matter what you’re ranked until the last week, and that’s the truth,” Freeman said, via Adam Rittenberg of ESPN. “We don’t need to focus on it. We don’t need to talk about it. Our job was to leave no doubt today, and they [did not].” A loss would have put Notre Dame in a very similar situation as it was in last season, when the Irish blew out 10 inferior teams but lost to both Miami and Texas A&M, a pair of playoff teams. The committee judged that since Notre Dame didn’t have quality wins, it was less deserving of a spot than Alabama or Miami, and the Irish were the first team on the outside looking in. The Hurricanes made good on that decision with their run all the way to the national championship game. Now, Notre Dame doesn’t have to worry about a similar scenario playing out this season. The Irish have three games remaining in the regular season, and if Freeman and company can take care of business in those games, they will be securely in the CFP. Notre Dame will be back in action next Saturday against Boston College, and a marquee matchup with an explosive SMU team looms in Week 12 as the final big test of the regular season. articles.title: NC State working to finalize deal with school legend, former NFL QB Philip Rivers
articles.summary: NC State is working to finalize a deal to hire Wolfpack legend and former NFL quarterback Philip Rivers, sources tell On3’s Chris Low and Pete Nakos and The Wolfpacker’s Noah Fleischman. Rivers was the head coach at St. Michael Catholic High School in Fairhope, Alabama, for the past six seasons. He
articles._body: NC State is working to finalize a deal to hire Wolfpack legend and former NFL quarterback Philip Rivers , sources tell On3’s Chris Low and Pete Nakos and The Wolfpacker’s Noah Fleischman. Rivers was the head coach at St. Michael Catholic High School in Fairhope, Alabama, for the past six seasons. He coached his son, Gunner , who is committed to play quarterback for NC State. St. Michael Catholic’s season ended with a playoff loss on Friday night. A previously scheduled NC State Board of Trustees meeting is set for later this week, where the board could approve Rivers’ contract. Rivers has begun reaching out to potential front office and coaching staff candidates. His name had been mentioned heavily behind the scenes in recent weeks, as rumors began to circulate that NC State was moving on from Dave Doeren . Rivers has the support of NC State boosters, which would be critical for securing NIL dollars. Doeren was fired following an embarrassing loss at Stanford. Doeren was the fourth-longest-tenured coach in the FBS, taking over the Wolfpack in 2013 and becoming the school’s winningest coach, posting a 95-70 record. Despite Doeren’s success at NC State, the program never reached the ACC Championship Game or won more than nine games in a season. The 44-year-old Rivers interviewed for the Buffalo Bills job this past offseason. As a quarterback at NC State, he set numerous records, started 51 straight games and completed an ACC-record 1,147 passes on 1,710 attempts, with 95 touchdowns. His No. 17 was retired before his final college game with the Wolfpack. One of NC State’s top boosters recently told On3 that “Rivers is NC State,” giving his stamp of approval to the potential hire. Questions will arise about whether Rivers is ready to step in and run a college program after six seasons coaching high school football. But sources have said confidence is high that he can come in and raise unprecedented dollars for the football program’s roster. Athletic director Boo Corrigan brought on former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach and NC State linebacker Bill Cowher to assist with the Wolfpack’s coaching search. Dewayne Washington also assisted in the search.

articles.title: Nets’ Jordi Fernandez explains why Mikel Brown Jr. remains unavailable for back-to-backs
articles.summary: The Brooklyn Nets will be without rookie Mikel Brown Jr. during Sunday’s back-to-back against the Dallas Mavericks. Despite being healthy, Brown has not yet been cleared for back-to-backs. Jordi Fernandez explained why on Saturday. “It’s not my thinking. It’s like a plan t
articles._body: The Brooklyn Nets will be without rookie Mikel Brown Jr. during Sunday’s back-to-back against the Dallas Mavericks. Despite being healthy, Brown has not yet been cleared for back-to-backs. Jordi Fernandez explained why on Saturday. “It’s not my thinking. It’s like a plan that we have with professionals that know exactly about how your body is, how you feel after,” Fernandez said following the Nets’ 124-121 loss to the Atlanta Hawks. “Then we assess the player. And then once we assess the player, then we keep building him up. So right now he’s not going to play back-to-backs, and obviously we’ll let you know when he does. There’s no reason why we want to disclose that information right now. We’re happy with where he is. He’s playing well. He’s doing great things. His body is where we want it to be, and we want him to keep getting better. If we play him in a back-to-back, the risk is going to be that, you know, his condition will probably decrease and there’s going to be more risk. So we’re not willing to take that risk.” Brown missed the second half of his freshman season at Louisville due to a back injury. He then missed most of training camp and the preseason due to an ankle injury. Nets’ Mikel Brown Jr. trusting process amid minutes restriction to start season Brad Penner-Imagn Images The No. 6 pick has been on a minutes restriction to start the season, averaging 23.1 per game across his first seven NBA appearances. While he’s looked good physically and appears capable of playing more minutes, he’s trusting Brooklyn’s medical staff. “It’s all about getting stronger,” Brown told The New York Post’s Brian Lewis on Saturday. “This is my first year playing against this type of high level of athletes. You’ve got to be at an elite performance level body-wise. But that’s just the everyday process when it comes to that stuff. I’m constantly in the weight room every day just strengthening the parts of my body I need to strengthen. But yeah, that’s us going along with the plan. I’m all aboard with it. As long as we’re winning games, that’s all I care about. I’ve just been leaning on my performance staff. My body feels great. Just take it slow. It’s an 82-game season. We want to be in a position to make the playoffs, so every game matters, but they’re just like, ‘the long run, the long run.’ So taking it a game at a time, a day at a time, and attacking it. Everything’s fine. I don’t look at (social) media like that, but yes, everything’s fine. My body’s great, just continuing to build.” Brown delivered his best performances of the season in the Nets’ last two games. The rookie posted 18 points and four assists on 6-of-11 shooting during Wednesday’s 114-104 win over the Charlotte Hornets. He missed his first seven shots vs. the Hawks on Saturday before scoring 13 fourth-quarter points on 5-of-9 shooting from the field and 3-of-4 from three. For the season, Brown has averaged 12.9 points, 3.9 assists and 2.1 turnovers per game on 34.6 percent shooting from the field and 31.1 percent from three. The Nets will also be without Egor Demin during Sunday’s matchup with the Mavericks. Demin has missed Brooklyn’s last five games due to a right leg bone bruise. articles.title: What Ryan Day told Ohio State about ‘storm’ as CFP dreams go up in smoke
articles.summary: The Ohio State football team suffered a brutal defeat on Saturday to Oregon. The Buckeyes are now 6-3 on the season, and the team’s chances of making the College Football Playoff are likely up in smoke. Ohio State head coach Ryan Day had a message to his team following the loss to the Ducks
articles._body: The Ohio State football team suffered a brutal defeat on Saturday to Oregon. The Buckeyes are now 6-3 on the season, and the team’s chances of making the College Football Playoff are likely up in smoke. Ohio State head coach Ryan Day had a message to his team following the loss to the Ducks. “I just told the team in the locker room that now we’ve got to weather this storm,” Day said, per ESPN. “And it’ll be a storm here, something that none of us are used to at Ohio State.” The Buckeyes lost to Oregon, 41-28. It was a historic defeat for Day. This is the first time in his Ohio State tenure where he has suffered three losses in a season, per ESPN. “We were able to get no rhythm on offense,” Day said. “That put the defense in some tough situations. “So I’ve got to evaluate everything. … It all starts with the staff and then it goes to the players. There needs to be accountability for all of it.” Ohio State is playing without regular starting quarterback Julian Sayin . Sayin is down with an injury. Without Sayin, the Buckeyes have gone with Luke Fahey at quarterback. He is a true freshman. Fahey finished the Oregon game with 360 yards passing. “The kid is trying his tail off,” Day said of Fahey. “It’s a tough spot to be in for a true freshman, but the expectation is to come in and play and win.” The Buckeyes are now 6-3 on the season, and 4-2 in the Big Ten. Ohio State still has conference games left this season with Michigan, Northwestern and Nebraska. The Buckeyes next play Northwestern on Saturday in Columbus. articles.summary:

I spent some time trying to see if I could modify SkyLight and Window Manager to tweak Stage Manager behaviors, but t
articles._body: I am one of the (dozens!) of users of Stage Manager, but I don't like some of its UX choices. For example, it moves newly opened windows into a new stage, which breaks my focus. I spent some time trying to see if I could modify SkyLight and Window Manager to tweak Stage Manager behaviors, but this required me to turn off SIP and the experience was janky. So I built a full replacement that still feels great to use. You can make as many stages as you want, reorder them, and drag windows and apps between them. IMO all the drag-and-drop behaviors work the way you’d expect. Like several recent window managers, emcee hides windows in an invisible Space (I learned this from yabai), and it works with SIP on. There were lots of little edge cases to get right, e.g: - Keeping the strip’s previews fresh without hammering Screen Recording - Cmd-Tab switching to the right stage and putting focus somewhere sensible. - "Save dialogs", listening for app quit events, etc. Happy to answer any questions! articles._body: The Indianapolis Colts have a few decisions to make over the next few days with the trade deadline approaching, as teams have become interested in several of their players. One of those players is Jonathan Taylor, and the New York Giants seem to be at the top of the list of teams that want to add him to their team. Though the Giants have been active in their efforts, there wasn’t much communication between them and the Colts this week, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. “The Giants and Colts didn’t have much contact this week. It feels like the Colts are sitting on their offers, and they’re going to have a decision to make. Do they want to trade one of the best young players in the game, or do they want to sit tight with him after they’ve had all these trade talks out there?” Schefter said. Some trade talk on ESPN’s Sunday NFL Countdown: pic.twitter.com/C7yHaLsInz — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 8, 2026 The Giants reportedly have already put out an offer for Taylor, according to Jay Glazer. “The Giants offered the Colts a 2nd- and 5th-round pick for RB Jonathan Taylor, but that offer has since been pulled, per Jay Glazer,” Ari Meirov of The33rdTeamFB wrote on X, formerly Twitter. Maybe the Giants decide to put another offer on the table, but they don’t have very long until the deadline. As of now, the feeling around the Colts is that Taylor will still be on the Colts, according to NFL insider Tom Pelissero. “After weeks of speculation, the most likely outcome for Taylor is … staying in Indianapolis,” Pelissero wrote. “As we reported last week at The Sweep, the Colts quickly rejected an offer of a 2027 second-round pick plus another pick for Taylor. And while there were more inquiries made to the Colts this week, no team has come close to offering the type of premium capital that would persuade Indianapolis to deal him.” The post NFL rumors: Giants’ lucrative Jonathan Taylor trade offer to Colts yanked off table appeared first on ClutchPoints .

If there’s a chance for the Pac-12 to get back into the national spotlight, since they’re outside the Power Four conference
articles._body: ESPN’s College GameDay will head to Boise State for their matchup with Oregon State in Week 11, per On3’s Pete Nakos. ESPN later confirmed with an official announcement Sunday. If there’s a chance for the Pac-12 to get back into the national spotlight, since they’re outside the Power Four conferences these days, this is it. Boise State was No. 25 in the initial CFP top 25 rankings last week and dominated this past weekend. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage While Oregon State wasn’t ranked and are coming off a loss, this is big for the conference. Boise State is 8-1 and 5-0 in Pac-12 play while the Beavers are 5-4 and 3-2 in conference play. The video announcement can be seen below. GET READY BOISE, WE'RE COMING TO YOUR CITY‼️ We're heading west for a Pac-12 showdown that could have CFP implications between Oregon State and Boise State 🍿 pic.twitter.com/o9XzuwoKyv — College GameDay (@CollegeGameDay) November 8, 2026 In Boise State’s 64-38 win over Colorado State on Saturday, the Broncos led 29-10 at halftime and never looked back. Max Cutforth was 16-of-19 passing for 317 yards and four touchdowns. On the ground, Dylan Riley had 19 carries for 192 yards and two touchdowns. “Our guys were rolling tonight, I was really proud of them,” Boise State head coach Spencer Danielson said postgame. “They came out and executed. We talked all week about execution and playing our best ball, and our guys did that pretty much the entire night.” While the team has made plays all season long, especially amid the eight-game winning streak, Boise State will need to tighten things up on defense, especially having to face a WR like Jesse Legree next week. “We’ve got to execute better,” Danielson said. “And that’s the reality of playing defense; you can’t take anything off the board. We’ll play good defense, but then we’ll play bad defense. We’ve looked at it and we’ve got to grow it, we’ve got improve it. We had some good stops, but there’s a lot of things on film that we’ve got to be better at defensively. That’s just the facts of it, and I know we will.” In nine games this season, Legree has 61 catches (Pac-12 leading), 1,209 yards (NCAA-leading), 14 touchdowns (NCAA-leading) and 19.8 yards per catch. Sure, Boise State can win shootouts, but Legree is a game changer that could lead to an upset next week. Hence why College GameDay was interested in spotlighting those two squads. articles.title: Paul Finebaum after LSU loss to Alabama: 'Lane Kiffin got punked'
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin did it again folks. Well, that’s probably what Paul Finebaum was thinking as LSU fell 31-13 at home to Alabama on Saturday afternoon into the evening. Kiffin’s Tigers are now 6-3 and more than likely out of the running for the College Football Playoff in Year 1 of his regime. Funny enoug
articles._body: Lane Kiffin did it again folks. Well, that’s probably what Paul Finebaum was thinking as LSU fell 31-13 at home to Alabama on Saturday afternoon into the evening. Kiffin’s Tigers are now 6-3 and more than likely out of the running for the College Football Playoff in Year 1 of his regime. Funny enough, it was 13-10 late third quarter, so it looked like LSU and Kiffin might actually pull it off and keep their good fortune rolling. Not so fast my friend. Simply put, Kiffin “hasn’t figured it out,” per Finebaum, despite seemingly turning the corner to be amongst the elites of the elites. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage “Yeah, I mean the simple headline is Lane Kiffin got punked,” Finebaum said on The Mat Barrie Show . “And it wasn’t even close. I mean, he just looked foolish, and it was two years ago on this weekend when a similar event happened down there. That was really the beginning of the end for Brian Kelly. He wasn’t around at this point last year for the for the Alabama game in Tuscaloosa … I just don’t think I’ve seen anything quite like that. “And the easy answer is it’s the same old ‘Lane Kiffin can’t beat Alabama, can’t win big games.’ What’s so remarkable is that every one of us bought into Kiffin beating Clemson, Kiffin beating Mississippi State, Auburn, all bad teams. Okay, against the good teams that hasn’t happened, and I just kept wanting to believe that he had figured it out, but he hasn’t.” All things considered, LSU and Kiffin could win out to finish 9-3 and they might actually have a CFP case. With games against Texas and Tennessee the next weeks, it could be a compelling argument. Arkansas is their final game, but going into the Alabama game, Kiffin’s crew was one of the few teams that might’ve been able to afford a third loss. Still, they are now in the hands of the committee and that’s not always the best sign. “The only good thing that happened to Lane Kiffin yesterday was that Ole Miss lost by a pretty similar amount to an even a slightly better team, at least for the moment, than Alabama,” Finebaum said. “I have said to you and others that I thought Kiffin would get it turned around at some point and win a national championship. But you have to wonder if Lane Kiffin isn’t just all sizzle and no substance. “I mean, I didn’t see anything last night that impressed me. They had so many opportunities, and when it came down to a call from the sidelines, Kiffin whiffed … That’s that’s what we get from Lane Kiffin in these situations, and all the work, all the great profiles that have been offered books, magazines, specials on on how great this guy is. What’s so great about him, Matt?”

articles.title: What Notre Dame’s Luke Talich said about controversial game-saving pass breakup vs. Miami’s Elija Lofton
articles.summary: After a spirited second-half comeback by Miami, Notre Dame football held on to bring down the No. 1-ranked Hurricanes, 31-24. However, the win was not without controversy. Miami’s Elija Lofton looked to have scored a potential game-tying touchdown on fourth down with under four minutes left
articles._body: After a spirited second-half comeback by Miami, Notre Dame football held on to bring down the No. 1-ranked Hurricanes , 31-24. However, the win was not without controversy. Miami’s Elija Lofton looked to have scored a potential game-tying touchdown on fourth down with under four minutes left in the game. But the referees ruled it as an incomplete pass after Irish safety Luke Talich’s intervention, and Miami turned the ball over on downs. When asked about his game-saving pass breakup, Talich didn’t think there was much controversial about it . “I felt like I got the ball out. I felt like he didn’t have control of it,” Talich said, per The Athletic’s Pete Sampson. Based on the replay, while it was close, it didn’t look like Lofton had full control of the football before Talich was able to break up the pass. As such, an incompletion was the correct call. It was a great play by Talich, who was the big defensive star for the Irish. Aside from his pass breakup, Talich also recorded six tackles and one interception against Miami. The senior safety has been coming through all season long for Notre Dame. He is second on the team with 41 tackles and leads the team with three picks. While Talich deserves credit for his late-game heroics, CJ Carr deserves credit for putting Notre Dame in that position in the first place. The Irish quarterback was sensation from start to finish with 319 yards and three touchdowns, two of which going to Micah Gilbert. It’s that top-tier quarterback play that has the Irish fans dreaming of a national championship. articles.title: Miami HC Mario Cristobal goes off on unruly Notre Dame fans rushing field after upset
articles.summary: Three teams entered Week 10 of the college football season with an unbeaten record, and only two remain. No. 1 Miami (FL) was beaten on the road at Notre Dame 31-24 to suffer its first defeat of 2026. Miami trailed 24-3 in its first game without Malachi Toney, who is out due to an ankle […]
articles._body: Three teams entered Week 10 of the college football season with an unbeaten record, and only two remain. No. 1 Miami (FL) was beaten on the road at Notre Dame 31-24 to suffer its first defeat of 2026. Miami trailed 24-3 in its first game without Malachi Toney, who is out due to an ankle injury that will likely cost him the rest of the regular season . It took the Hurricanes a little over a half to figure out life without their superstar receiver, but Darian Mensah eventually settled in and nearly led the comeback. After the game, Notre Dame fans immediately stormed the field and swarmed the players and coaches on both sides. After the game, Miami head coach Mario Cristobal made it clear that he wasn’t a fan of the way some Irish fans handled themselves during the celebration. Mario Cristobal is a fan of Field Storming, just stay out of his and his players way, and go have fun #GoCanes #TheU #CollegeFootball #MiamiHurricanes #notredame pic.twitter.com/3X0nkjAUwQ — Eye of the Hurricanes (@CanesCentralSI) November 8, 2026 “It’s player safety, my sons are out there as well,” Cristobal said. “I’m all for fun and everything else, but when you start to infringe on (safety), brother you better get back. It ain’t gonna be pretty for you. Something has to be done about that kind of stuff. Let the fans have a good time and if the field is involved, that’s great, but do not antagonize people.” Of course, some college football fans were stunned that the Irish fans rushed the field in the first place. Even though Miami entered this game as the No. 1 team in the country, Notre Dame is still one of the premier programs in the sport and entered the game as a touchdown favorite, and many fans and pundits were expecting an Irish victory in this game. Miami should be just fine in the College Football Playoff race despite this loss, even with Toney slated to miss more time with his ankle injury. The Hurricanes are still a virtual lock to make the ACC Championship Game, where they will be a favorite over any opponent across from them. If they handle their business there, Cristobal and company will have a chance to make another run at a national title. ’13 years of trust’ – Why Steve Kerr sat Stephen Curry, Draymond Green to start OT in Warriors’ win over Magic
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO – When Stephen Curry and Draymond Green saw that Steve Kerr didn’t have their names on the whiteboard as the Golden State Warriors gathered around in the huddle to see the five who would be on the floor to start overtime, it took all 13 years of the trio’s time together – ever
articles._body: SAN FRANCISCO – When Stephen Curry and Draymond Green saw that Steve Kerr didn’t have their names on the whiteboard as the Golden State Warriors gathered around in the huddle to see the five who would be on the floor to start overtime , it took all 13 years of the trio’s time together – every minute and every second of the trio’s 13 golden years of winning and battling together – to trust in what their revered coach was asking them to do. “Steve said to me and Steph, like, ‘Yo, we sitting y’all the first minute,’” Green said after the Dubs’ 126-119 overtime win over the Orlando Magic. “We’re like, ‘Nah, we’re good. Like, yo, we all right. That ain’t changing nothing. That one minute’s not changing anything.’ And he looked at us, and he was like, ‘Ah… we think it’s the right thing to do.’ And so, you know, I was telling (Kerr) on the bench. I said (at the) start of overtime, ‘So that’s 13 years of trust.’” Kerr’s thought process was simple: Curry and Green, 38 and 36, respectively, had already played extended minutes up to that point. And as his assistant coach Seth Cooper would point out to Kerr, if the game was tied with five minutes left in regulation, they would give their veteran duo a small break to catch their breath. Perhaps in the old days they would have pushed it no problem, Kerr explained, but they’re not in their heyday anymore. Thus, in weighing the bigger picture of preserving Curry and Green’s stamina and health over the course of 82 games, Kerr leaned on the currency of trust he has accumulated with his guys, his two future Hall of Famers, to quell their competitive fire for a moment and accept that taking a quick breather was in everyone’s best interest. And even more so, trust that their depth and their reserves could hold down the fort in the meantime. Which they did, and even went a little beyond. “‘All right, cool, come on, fellas, y’all got it. We believe in y’all,’” Green continued, intimating the sentiment he and Curry poured into Charles Bassey, Brandon Williams, and the rest of the unit that kicked off overtime after they got over their own initial frustrations about not starting in the extra period. “We want to play, but we believe in y’all. And that group got us a four-point advantage starting overtime. (Charles) Bass wins the tip. We get a bucket. Bass gets a bucket. So they were really good to start that overtime. But I think what it shows is the depth that this team has. Start us on the bench in overtime, and we come up four points. That’s what we’ve been leaning into, and that’s what’s been good for this team: leaning on the depth and everybody doing what they have to do, taking pride in their role. That’s been big for this team.” And once that unit got Curry and Green the four-point lead, the duo landed the daggers. His first possession back in the game, Green navigated a broken half-court set with the shot clock winding down to relocate the play to rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, getting him the ball and setting him a screen to free him up for a big 3-pointer. Two possessions later, trailing by one, Curry iso’d a mismatch with Wendell Carter Jr., yanked the ball back for a reverse between the legs to avoid the double team coming, and scooped the ball high above Jamal Cain for the and-1 finish in traffic. And then the icing on the cake: Curry scooping another layup to the moon and back over Carter in the lane, plus a sideways shimmy shuffle as he danced away from the wreckage, to complete a 41-point outing and give Golden State the overtime victory , their seventh in a row. Stephen Curry’s conversations with the reserves postgame D. Ross Cameron-Imagn Images After a win like that, in which the reserves collected 44 points off the bench and their young core, Lendeborg and Brandin Podziemski, came up big with 23 points and 15 points, respectively, Curry made sure to highlight their contributions to victory. “The conversation and the energy (were) more frustration for us, not doubt in the unit that was going out there,” Curry said, not wanting the team to mistake him and Green’s fire as an indictment on them after explaining that it was a weird situation for him to not start overtime as a competitor who wants to play every single minute of crunch time. “We wanted to make sure they knew that, because they’ve been playing well all year, and those 90 seconds they got us a lead, and me and Draymond got to take a quick break. It matters in the big picture of the season. I wanted to echo that after the game because that’s a big deal. They can see our body language on the bench, and you can kind of confuse that as, ‘We can go out there and do it.’ But it was more, ‘No, we just want to play.’ But it was confidence in their ability to go take care of business.” That’s the kind of leadership that ignites a locker room. It’s the kind of gesture that invigorates a spunk and a confidence, which Curry knows the Warriors are going to need from top to bottom given that they’re back to a kind of strength-in-numbers formula that they have to lean on if Curry and Green are to last the gauntlet that is the 82-game regular season. “It all matters, and it all helps,” Curry said of the reserves being able to buy him and Green minutes this season without much drop-off, also referencing he didn’t have to play the final seven minutes of their 120-100 over the Miami Heat a game ago. “Over the course of 82, you’d hope that we could keep that pattern going while we still win.” But more than anything, speeches like Curry’s, on nights like these and wins like these, help coalesce an identity. Curry’s conversation to the team was notable in Steve Kerr’s eyes, who emphasized the “grit” and “togetherness” the Warriors displayed top to bottom. “(Curry) mentioned how much trust that he and the vets have in the young guys, and so we’ve got a good th

articles.title: NFL rumors: Commanders not totally out of Brandon Aiyuk business as 49ers status hangs in air
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL trade deadline is already living up to expectations. There have already been some massive trades ahead of the deadline, including a blockbuster deal involving Jeffery Simmons. Could one of the league’s most controversial veteran players finally be on the move after more than a
articles._body: The 2026 NFL trade deadline is already living up to expectations. There have already been some massive trades ahead of the deadline, including a blockbuster deal involving Jeffery Simmons . Could one of the league’s most controversial veteran players finally be on the move after more than a year of off-the-field drama? NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport shared intel from around the league ahead of the trade deadline. They explained that the Commanders are still not completely out of Brandon Aiyuk. “The Commanders haven’t completely abandoned the idea of adding wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk, who was rumored during the summer to end up in Washington, according to sources,” Schefter and Rapoport wrote on Sunday. “Before an Aiyuk deal could happen — if it were to happen — the organization would have to have discussions with multiple people. It’s not a no, but it’s also not a yes just yet.” Aiyuk has not suited up in the NFL since the 2024 season. He suffered a serious knee injury and missed multiple team meetings. As a result, the 49ers voided roughly $27 million of guarantees on Aiyuk’s contract. Understandably, the relationship between both sides is now quite contentious. Aiyuk is attempting to get reinstated to play in the NFL this season. But some experts like ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler are skeptical that Aiyuk will be reinstated anytime soon. “Aiyuk wants to get reinstated to play in the NFL. His prospects in the short term are not promising, assuming he becomes a free agent eventually,” Fowler said. As for the Commanders, they are 2-4-1 and still technically alive in the NFC East. Wide receiver is still a position of need, especially with Terry McLaurin on injured reserve . Aiyuk could be the solution Washington is looking for, so long as he is locked in on reviving his NFL career. It will be interesting to see what happens next in the Aiyuk saga. The NFL trade deadline is 4 p.m. ET on November 10th. Any potential Aiyuk move must come before that deadline. articles.title: Colorado football’s Deion Sanders drops defiant take on hot seat after latest ugly loss
articles.summary: The Colorado football team suffered yet another loss on Saturday. This time the Buffaloes bowed to Arizona State, 20-10. Colorado head coach Deion Sanders dropped a defiant take after suffering yet another Big 12 conference defeat. “I don’t think about that, man. I’m not here fo
articles._body: The Colorado football team suffered yet another loss on Saturday. This time the Buffaloes bowed to Arizona State, 20-10. Colorado head coach Deion Sanders dropped a defiant take after suffering yet another Big 12 conference defeat. “I don’t think about that, man. I’m not here for my job. I’m here for these young men. I’m not, I’m not built like that. Like, like, I’m really not. I’m really, really, really not,” Sanders said postgame when asked about his job security, per ESPN. Colorado is now 3-6 on the season, following this loss. One more loss will assure Sanders of his third losing season in four years as Colorado’s head coach. Sanders understands the frustration, but wants to focus on helping his team perform better. “This is not how it’s supposed to be, and we could apologize a thousand times to the fanbase, to you all,” Sanders said of the loss. “But unless we get it together, it’s gonna be the same ol’, same ol’. And that’s pathetic because … the fanbase deserves better.” The Colorado football program is struggling in the Big 12 The Buffaloes are now just 1-5 in Big 12 play. Colorado has just two conference wins since the start of the 2025 season. Sanders is seen as coaching on the hot seat , by the national news media. Sanders is still standing by this team. “Didn’t see quit, didn’t see anybody being lethargic, didn’t see them giving up by any means, but it was way too late,” Sanders said. “I wish we had started off like that instead of end up like that.” Colorado has Big 12 games left this season against Houston, Cincinnati and UCF. Colorado must win out in order to finish the season with a .500 record, and make a bowl game. Time will tell if Sanders’ days are numbered at Colorado. The Buffaloes next play Houston on Friday. articles._body: The San Francisco 49ers will be facing the Las Vegas Raiders this week, and the injuries have continued to pile up for them. This week, it’s the wide receiver room that’s taken a hit, with Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. out for another game . Later in the week, Christian Kirk was placed on injured reserve after hurting his meniscus. It’s uncertain how serious the injury is, but the 49ers are hoping that it’s not too bad when looking at their current situation. For the time being, it has to be next man up for the 49ers, and if you’re looking for someone who could help your fantasy team, the pickings may be slim. At the same time, there are some players who may have a productive day against the Raiders. The top player who should expect to have a big day on the 49ers is George Kittle, who has always been one of Brock Purdy’s top targets. Kittle should be looked at as the security blanket, and he’s there when Purdy needs him. It wouldn’t be a surprise if he had the most targets, and he could even get into the end zone. Another player that could be a good fantasy option is Demarcus Robinson, and he’ll most likely be the WR1 for Purdy. In two games this season, Robinson has totaled five receptions for 84 yards and a touchdown. That could end up being his stat line just against the Raiders, and Purdy could be looking for him a lot. Brandin Cooks could find some more time on the field for the 49ers this week as well, and he still has the speed to take the top off of a defense. He may not see as many targets as Kittle and Robinson, but he is a sneaky fantasy option if you’re looking for someone on the 49ers. articles.title: Paul Finebaum: 'There warning signs from Day 1' about Ohio State

articles._body: Paul Finebaum isn’t quite surprised about what happened to Ohio State and Ryan Day on Saturday as the Buckeyes fell 41-28 to Oregon . The loss dropped Ohio State to 6-3 on the season and virtually out of College Football Playoff contention. Finebaum claimed this was evident from the start of the season, despite a lot of hype surrounding the Buckeyes, now-injured QB Julian Sayin and Heisman contender Jeremiah Smith . What’s next for Ohio State? It’s tough to say, at least for this season. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage “I think there were warning signs from Day 1, but they were still preseason No. 1 because we just are accustomed to thinking that Ryan Day will actually do the job,” Finebaum said on The Matt Barrie Show . “And you know, the one thing Ryan Day is consistent on is is buying black dye for his beard. But other than that, really, it’s been all over the place. I mean, Buckeye fans can scream and holler. They won the national championship on a year when he laid a massive egg. Last year was just inexcusable the way that season ended, but it portended the future.” Funny enough, Oregon had similar hype as in, this was the year for the Ducks. But both have similar records, injuries and struggles. But Ohio State and Day have to look at themselves in the mirror with three games remaining. Coming into the year, losing a lot of talent to the NFL and being two years from a title, hindsight tells us this was going to be a 50-50 season for the boys in Columbus. “After asking questions about probably the best constructed football program in America, what’s in front of them? I’m not saying that they’re going off a map,” Finebaum said. “They recruit at the top shelf, but it just always seems to be chaotic, Matt, for a program that that really nothing should go wrong on that massive a scale. And the irony, losing to another team that started this season, I think No. 2, that was (left for) dead.” After the game, head coach Day acknowledged that the team is coming up short. Day went on to say that there needs to be accountability with what’s going wrong, and it starts with the staff. The loss is the Buckeyes’ second in a row and third of the season. “I’ve got to evaluate everything and try to come in tomorrow and figure out, with the staff, the things we’re coming up short on and figure out how to adjust those things,” Day said in his postgame press conference . “It all starts with the staff, and then it goes to the players. There needs to be accountability for all of it, and then we go from there.”

articles._body: PHOENIX– Eight games in, and Dillon Brooks and Jalen Green got their retribution. That was after the Phoenix Suns took down the Houston Rockets, 102-99, on Saturday. Leading up to the game, Brooks was involved in a social media feud with Kevin Durant. Some thought that story would be a costly distraction. Safe to say it wasn’t, as both Brooks and Green had other plans. The latter was barking at the Houston bench through the first quarter. His teammate did so, but in a rather unconventional way that was different from his usual self. Nonetheless, it prompted Brooks to cautiously walk the fine line of using his intensity in a fruitful manner. “I was whispering, s**t-talking to other guys, trying to communicate and let the refs know that I’m a passionate player, even though it’s year 10,” he joked in the locker room postgame. I’m a passionate player. I apologize for yelling. When I’m alone with a player, I just say what I need to say, play with that physicality, and use it against them as well.” Dillon Brooks on how he made sure not to cross the line against Kevin Durant and his former team: “I was whispering, shit-talking to other guys, trying to communicate and let the refs know that I'm a passionate player, even though it's year 10. I'm a passionate player. I… pic.twitter.com/ySnWj9ImnQ — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 8, 2026 The adjective, passion, is an important one. For all the dap ups and laughs before the game, as soon as that ball was tipped in the air, it was go-time for both Suns players. Green was matched up on a few different players, such as Fred VanVleet and Amen Thompson for stints. His athleticism proved to be too much once he got to the second level. Plenty of straight line drives to the basket and using his bounce truly helped. Then going back to Brooks, his physicality against Durant played a role in limiting him to 21 points, and only one shot attempt in the first half. Jalen Green and Dillon Brooks wanted this Suns win Mandatory Credit: Allan Henry-Imagn Images Every win in the NBA matters, but there was some extra juice for both men. They didn’t have a win against Houston last season, and Brooks himself had four consecutive losses while Green has two. It felt as if the Rockets overmatched the Suns during that time, but Saturday didn’t look to be that way. This looked like the 2025-26 rendition of “Suns basketball” people are accustomed to seeing. Unlike his counterpart, Green was an open door to trash talking. He invited it, but simmered down as the game progressed. Much like Brooks, he stood on that line of intensity and cautious walked across. “Obviously, it’s a balance. You want to come out and play hard regardless, especially with all the emotions out there,” Green shared postgame. “Our crowd always shows up, but you felt the energy a little bit more tonight. We just stay locked in and engaged. That’s the biggest part. The end goal is to come out with a win, so you try to push that limit a little bit just to see what we can get away with, but still be smarter about it.” Jalen Green spoke to me about managing the emotions and intensity of tonight's game, but not going over the edge. "Obviously, it's a balance. You want to come out and play hard regardless, especially with all the emotions out there. Our crowd always shows up, but you felt the… pic.twitter.com/QvcefseqBv — Hayden Cilley (@HaydenCilley) November 8, 2026 This is one of those marquee wins Phoenix has sought after this season.They built a 19-point lead in the second quarter and nearly squandered it all away. Still, it was enough for them to come up with right now, would be an upset win. A sweet concotion of 48 minutes of defense, tough shot-making, and that gritty nastiness the Suns have was ever present. The box score might not show it, but that emotion Brooks and Green had coming into the arena was a significant boost. articles._body: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will take on the Chicago Bears on Sunday Night Football in Week 9, and they’re set to get Emeka Egbuka back. The Buccaneers wide receiver is listed as questionable, but he returned to practice this week and is ready to return after a two-game absence. Egbuka has missed the Bucs’ last two games due to the injury. His last appearance came in their 26-19 overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. He had seven catches on a whopping 16 targets for 48 yards and one touchdown in that game. Despite missing two games, Egbuka still leads the team with 28 catches on the season. He’s also got 240 receiving yards, just three yards behind team leader Chris Godwin. However, these are still far below his numbers from his rookie campaign last season, where he finished with 63 catches for 938 yards and six touchdowns. The Bucs’ passing game as a whole has been quite anemic this season. They are dead-last in the league with just 1,180 passing yards. They took it to the extreme last time out as they didn’t complete a single pass against Atlanta Falcons . But they were still able to win 16-0 on the strength of 324 rushing yards and three touchdowns. Hopefully, Egbuka’s return will help give Baker Mayfield a completion this time around in Chicago. articles.title: Nebraska football fans about done with Matt Rhule, but there’s a $60 million problem
articles.summary: The Nebraska football team is reeling right now. The Cornhuskers lost on Saturday to Illinois, 24-13, to drop to 5-4. Nebraska fans are getting very frustrated with Cornhuskers head coach Matt Rhule. If Rhule does get the boot at Nebraska though, he would be owed an absolutely massive buyout. 
articles._body: The Nebraska football team is reeling right now . The Cornhuskers lost on Saturday to Illinois, 24-13, to drop to 5-4. Nebraska fans are getting very frustrated with Cornhuskers head coach Matt Rhule. If Rhule does get the boot at Nebraska though, he would be owed an absolutely massive buyout. “After Penn State fired James Franklin a year ago, Nebraska chose to extend Rhule through 2032, saddling the school with a buyout in the $60 million range,” Yahoo Sports reported. Nebraska fired offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen in recent days, after offensive struggles in Big Ten play this year. Nebraska started out the season with a promising 5-0 record, but has dropped four straight. “Holgorsen, who came from the Mike Leach offensive tree at Texas Tech, was never going to be a great fit in the Big Ten. Rhule hired him anyway. He was also going to be a square peg in a round hole building an offense around Dylan Raiola, a quarterback with limited mobility. Rhule hired him anyway,” Yahoo reported. The Cornhuskers have had an up and down tenure under Rhule’s leadership. He is in his fourth season at the school. He has posted back-to-back winning seasons, but the team is in danger this year of missing a bowl. That is certainly not acceptable to Nebraska fans . The Cornhuskers of course were a national power under the legendary head coach Tom Osborne. Nebraska fans expect Rhule to win and compete for Big Ten titles. Things get no easier for Nebraska moving forward. The Cornhuskers still have Big Ten games remaining this season with Iowa and Ohio State. Time will tell if the Nebraska program moves on from Rhule any time soon. Nebraska is next in action against Rutgers on Saturday. articles.title: Jordi Fernandez explains controversial decision during Nets’ late-game collapse vs. Hawks
articles.summary: Nolan Traore was the Brooklyn Nets’ most efficient offensive player through three quarters of Saturday’s matchup with the Atlanta Hawks. Then, he was benched for the fourth. After scoring 19 points on 8-of-10 shooting, Traore did not play during the final period of the Nets’ 124
articles._body: Nolan Traore was the Brooklyn Nets’ most efficient offensive player through three quarters of Saturday’s matchup with the Atlanta Hawks. Then, he was benched for the fourth. After scoring 19 points on 8-of-10 shooting, Traore did not play during the final period of the Nets’ 124-121 loss at State Farm Arena. Head coach Jordi Fernandez opted to roll with rookie point guard Mikel Brown Jr., who scored 13 points on 5-of-9 shooting in the fourth. The Nets led 114-110 with two minutes remaining but struggled to execute on both ends in the clutch, allowing the Hawks to close on a 14-7 run to win the game. Fernandez explained his reasoning behind benching Traore following the loss. “Mikel had those five straight points, and I just let him roll. Because you cannot just keep taking them in and out,” the coach said. “I think that when I was about to sub Nolan in, Mikel made two or three threes and a mid-range pull-up. So I thought that was the right thing to do. Was it right? I don’t know. Obviously, Nolan did very well. They scored 18 and 19 [points]. So that’s a very good contribution from your two point guards.” Traore was asked if Fernandez said anything to him about the benching during or after the game. “No, he didn’t say anything,” the Nets sophomore replied. Traore and Brown have emerged as two of the Nets’ most dynamic offensive threats in recent games. However, Fernandez has been unwilling to play the pair of 6-foot-4 guards together, likely because of defensive concerns. Nets fall apart in final minutes during loss to Hawks with Nolan Traore on bench Jordan Godfree-Imagn Images While Brown did his best to keep the Nets afloat down the stretch, Traore’s absence hurt the team offensively. Brooklyn scored 26 points on 10-of-26 shooting with six assists and five turnovers in the fourth quarter. Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle combined for eight points on 3-of-10 shooting with two assists and two turnovers during the decisive period. The Nets couldn’t get stops or hold up on the defensive boards late, as the Hawks scored 36 fourth-quarter points on 11-of-24 shooting while attempting 16 free throws. “We were not consistent enough to do the right things. And it’s not about making shots; it’s about trying to do the right things. Obviously, the points off turnovers [were an issue]. This is a team that will pressure you, and we had 22 turnovers for 28 points. That’s not acceptable. That’s where you lose the game,” Fernandez said. Traore criticized the Nets’ effort down the stretch. “Our effort was not great. We didn’t do a lot of things. We didn’t pay attention to details. Offensively, a lot of random stuff. So I guess we were just not really focused anymore,” he said. “We had great looks in the first half, but in the second half, we played more random stuff, so we didn’t have the same quality shots. So that might be the main thing. I don’t think Atlanta did something that disturbed us. It was more just us doing random stuff.” The Nets will need Porter and Randle to be better if they hope to snap out of their early-season struggles. While Brooklyn’s lead duo combined for 44 points on 16-of-31 shooting, they committed nine turnovers. Brooklyn turned the ball over 22 times during the loss, leading to 28 Hawks points. Randle and Porter have combined for 57 turnovers and 56 assists this season. The duo was involved in a critical late-game sequence. With the Nets trailing 115-114 with 1:15 remaining, Porter missed an open three. The rebound deflected out to Randle. However, instead of grabbing it, he slapped the ball out toward half court. The ball was deflected, and although Randle wound up closest to it, Nikeil Alexander-Walker outhustled him to recover it and went the other way for a layup. Day’Ron Sharpe tallied the first triple-double of his career during the loss, posting 12 points, 10 rebounds and 13 assists. However, the Nets big man also had a critical late-game gaffe. After Brown hit a three to give Brooklyn a 114-110 lead, Alexander-Walker missed a three on the other end. Sharpe grabbed the rebound, but Dyson Daniels stripped him, leading to an Onyeka Okongwu three. If the Nets lose this game, these two plays will be why. Day'Ron and Julius need to secure these rebounds. pic.twitter.com/p9MXnzFhXu — Erik Slater (@ErikSlater_) November 8, 2026 The loss drops Brooklyn to 2-7. They’ll travel to face the Dallas Mavericks during a back-to-back on Sunday. The Nets will be without Egor Demin (right leg bone bruise) and Mikel Brown Jr. (back injury management) during the road matchup. If the Rams can get a win against the Commanders, their season will officially be back on track. Fortunately, the Rams may be getting some
articles._body: The Los Angeles Rams are ready to make their push back to the playoffs. LA is just 4-4 but riding a two-game winning streak entering the middle of the season. If the Rams can get a win against the Commanders , their season will officially be back on track. Fortunately, the Rams may be getting some huge reinforcements back in Week 9. Myles Garrett is finally off injured reserve and could play against Washington this week. LA just got a positive injury update on Garrett that fans will want to hear about before Sunday’s matchup with the Commanders. Myles Garrett’s injury status vs. Commanders Kirby Lee-Imagn Images All signs point to Garrett making his triumphant return for the Rams in Week 9, per NFL insider Ian Rapoport. “Myles Garrett makes his dramatic return for the Los Angeles Rams today, finally. Remember Myles Garrett, who was the subject of that blockbuster trade this offseason going from the Browns to the Rams. Creating this superteam and all the hype around the Rams,” Rapoport said on Sunday via NFL GameDay Morning. “Well he hasn’t played since Week 1, kind of hobbled through that Australia game and had surgery to clean out his knee… It’s been about eight weeks for Myles Garrett, but he was at practice this week.” Garrett did not log a single stat in Week 1 and has not played since. That means Sunday’s game will be the first time he can make an impact for LA. Rapoport expects Garrett to primarily get pass rush duties in his first game back. “I expect a lot of Myles Garrett, mostly on passing downs,” Rapoport added. “This is someone I know the Rams are excited to see.” In other Rams injury news, Jaylen Watson and Terrance Ferguson have both been ruled out . Long snapper Joe Cardona is also doubtful with an ankle injury. Rams at Commanders kicks off at 1 p.m. ET from Northwest Stadium in Summerfield, Maryland. Monangai has only played in four games thus far due to injuries and hasn’t featured since last month’s game against the New York Jets. Roschon Johnson, the team’s third running back, hasn’t really stepped up in Monangai’s absence. He’s scored an incredible seven touchdowns over the last four games, including three in the second half of their 34-17 beatdown of the Seattle Seahawks. While Monangai remains out, defensive backs Malik Muhammad II (toe) and Tyrique Stevenson Sr. (thumb) are both expected to play against the Bucs. Stevenson will play with a splint. articles._body: The Houston Rockets got beat by the Phoenix Suns on Saturday. Rockets star Kevin Durant admitted it was tough to lose to his former team. He even admitted he misses living in Phoenix, Arizona. “It’s a normal, regular game. I played here for 2.5 years bro. It’s not that deep. I loved living in Phoenix. I miss it everyday, to be honest with you,” Durant said, per ClutchPoints. "It's a normal, regular game. I played here for 2.5 years bro. It's not that deep. I loved living in Phoenix. I miss it everyday, to be honest with you. Kevin Durant on being back in Phoenix (via @HoustonRockets ) pic.twitter.com/TcGzvJ1cli — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 8, 2026 Houston lost on Saturday, 102-99. Durant finished the game with 21 points and 10 rebounds. The veteran finished 10-for-11 from the free throw line in the contest. Durant played for the Suns from 2023-2025. He still has a lot of friends in Phoenix, including Suns guard Devin Booker. “I’m always going to embrace that friendship, that brotherhood, no matter what. Before he even came here, I was always a fan. So, it’s going to continue to grow. Obviously, it was going to be a high-intensity game every time we play them for Dillon (Brooks) and Jalen (Green) too, so I’m glad we got a win for them,” Booker said after the game Saturday, per ClutchPoints. Durant has played for several teams in his long NBA career. This season, he is averaging 20.8 points per game. He also is averaging 5.7 rebounds and three assists per contest. Kevin Durant wants the Rockets to play better late in games Against Phoenix on Saturday, Durant led Houston in scoring. He struggled from three-point range, making just one three pointer on seven attempts. Durant wants his team to execute better down the stretch. “It’s the most important thing,” Durant said of late-game execution, per The Athletic. “Fourth-quarter games and winning tight games is what the NBA is about. As much as you can get the reps and as much as you can get that on film and, as a coach, see what lineups work and, as a player, see what moves and angles work. It’s good early in the season that we’ve got a few of those games under our belt.” The Rockets are now 7-3 on the season , following the loss. Houston next plays the Denver Nuggets on Monday.
