articles.title: The 1 trade Eagles must make in final week before 2026 NFL trade deadline
articles.summary: It’s (almost) here, Philadelphia Eagles fans: the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Soon, fans around the NFL will get to see who ends up playing where, how many stars have to find new homes, and which teams are willing to go all in on 2026, or punt on the campaign in favor of the future. In […
articles._body: It’s (almost) here, Philadelphia Eagles fans: the 2026 NFL trade deadline . Soon, fans around the NFL will get to see who ends up playing where, how many stars have to find new homes, and which teams are willing to go all in on 2026, or punt on the campaign in favor of the future. In the past, for the vast majority of the 21st century, in fact, the Eagles have firmly been buyers, using the shrewd dealings of Howie Roseman to cash out future picks for present contributors. If it worked, like with Jay Ajayi, great, the Eagles’ ceiling elevated considerably and Roseman paid up with a new, long-term contract. And if it didn’t, that’s cool too; acquiring Jaelan Phillips didn’t really help the Eagles’ Super Bowl chances in 2025, but when he left in free agency, he effectively got the team back the pick they surrendered to bring him into the program, even if it comes in 2027 instead of 2026. In 2026, the Eagles are firmly sellers, with teams around the NFL trying to pry away a few members of the Super Bowl LIX roster in the hopes of getting them to Super Bowl LXI. Some players, like Saquon Barkley, have been publicly removed from the trade block, while others, like Moro Ojomo, have noted that the Eagles want to keep them long-term instead of pulling off a trade, but as the sharks circle and the time ticks down, more deals will arrive that Roseman has to navigate, some of which could change the franchise forever. With very few players truly untradeable – Jordan Mailata, Quinyon Mitchell, Jalen Hurts, as he deals with blood clots – there is one player who is almost certainly not going to be traded at the deadline, but could garner a massive return from a team like the Jacksonville Jaguars, who are reportedly looking for a defensive tackle desperately: Jalen Carter. From a talent standpoint, Carter is maybe the Eagles’ best defensive player when he’s firing on all cylinders, but considering how infrequently that happens, it might be the perfect time to cash out while his value is at an all-time high. Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Eagles have a perfect chance to exit the Jalen Carter rollercoaster When the Eagles landed Carter in the first round of the 2022 NFL Draft, it looked like the steal of the century. Using a draft pick originally owned by the New Orleans Saints, which the Eagles artificially improved by allowing the Washington Commanders to beat them in the regular season finale, fans watched in awe as a player widely considered the most talented in the entire class slid down the board, with a minor trade of a fourth-round pick the only requirement to move from nine to eight in order to get a deal done. From the point where Carter took the field as a rookie, he instantly impressed, turning in snaps, drives, quarters, and even games where he looked like the best player on the field regardless of uniform. Standing 6-foot-3, 314 pounds, Carter’s unique combination of bend and power has routinely wrecked interior offensive lines with ease, collapsing pockets and ruining whatever plan a quarterback had at the snap. The problem: Carter simply doesn’t do it often enough. Now in 2026, Carter has an excuse. The 25-year-old suffered a hairline fracture in his wrist early in the season and, as a result, has been playing with a cast on his hand. And yet, there have been games where Carter caused havoc all the same, recording five tackles, three tackles for a loss, and two sacks against the Jaguars in Week 5 after doing very little in the two games before and after. This trend of a dominant game followed by unremarkable performance has unfortunately been a trend for Carter as a pro. Unlike, say, Jeffery Simmons, who was traded for a massive package back in October , the Eagles never quite know what they will get from Carter every time he takes the field, and as a result, if he’s off, the entire defense tends to be as well. Sure, every player has a down game from time to time, but for the most part, when Zack Baun, Quinyon Mitchell, or even Jalyx Hunt takes the field, Vic Fangio knows what he’s going to get, and that just hasn’t been the case for Carter. Could Carter put it all together and become the next Fletcher Cox, or even surpass him, which he has the talent to do? Sure, he could theoretically play another decade and will only get better as he enters Year 5, 6, and beyond. But it’s also possible Carter remains a very expensive question mark on a team with a lot of questions surrounding their future. Trade proposal Eagles: 2027 second-round pick, 2027 third-round pick, 2028 first-round pick, Brian Thomas Jr. Jaguars: Jalen Carter, 2027 fifth-round pick Mandatory Credit: Travis Register-Imagn Images The Eagles can reset their roster with Brian Thomas Jr., Moro Ojomo If the Eagles are going to trade Carter – which they probably won’t, but should at least consider – the conversation doesn’t even start unless at least one first-round pick is on the table. Sure, some fans will want a second first-round pick or at least an additional Day 2 selection, but at the bare minimum, the Eagles need to add another one, especially in 2028, when they will have three at their disposal, and Hurts could theoretically no longer be on the team. But what if they could also add a depreciated asset who has produced at the NFL level but is currently struggling to consistently reach the top end of his ceiling? Fortunately, the Jaguars have that on their roster too in Brian Thomas Jr., who looked like a legit WR1 as a rookie before becoming an afterthought in Liam Coen’s scheme. Initially drafted in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of LSU, Thomas was one of the more controversial players in his class, a deep threat who ran a limited scheme in college, but quickly proved doubters wrong right out of the gate, where he recorded 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns on his way to a Pro Bowl appearance. articles.title: FEMA’s maps undercount the U.S. flooding risk by about 6 million homes — and some of those maps are two decades old
articles.summary: Most homeowner’s policies don’t cover flood damage.
articles._body: If your home isn’t in a federally designated flood zone, flooding might seem like someone else’s problem. No one requires you to buy flood insurance, and the map suggests you’re in the clear. But reality may be very different. Mounting evidence reveals that significantly more homes are at risk of flooding than is indicated by FEMA’s 100-year flood maps – about 6 million more , and 14.6 million properties in all, by one estimate. The official maps are commonly outdated , and some are two decades old . Even when updated, they typically rely on historical flood data rather than future risk projections. But there’s another problem that redrawing the lines won’t solve. FEMA’s flood maps answer only one question: Is the water likely to reach my neighborhood? They don’t assess an individual home’s risks or what the impacts are likely to be when the water rises. To understand the impact, more comprehensive data is needed , including the probable flood depth at the home, the building’s age and construction quality, and insurance coverage. Same street, different risks When these other factors are considered, your home’s true flood risk is far more complex than the map might seem to indicate. The data shows how two houses on the same street can face radically different risks from flooding , even when located in the same flood zone – and where local governments can help. One home may be newer, well maintained and covered by flood insurance. Another may be decades older, at the low end of the same street where water runs deeper during a flood, and is in poor repair and uninsured. The same storm would leave them in very different predicaments, with very different paths to recovery. Neighborhood averages can make it hard to tell which homes are likely to be hit hardest. But understanding an individual property’s risks matters for residents figuring out how to protect a home, and for local officials deciding where limited flood-protection money should go. We study how flooding affects homes and the people who live in them. To see how much these house-by-house differences matter, we and colleagues Aaron Flores of Arizona State University and Sara Meerow of the University of Colorado Boulder built a detailed flood risk score for nearly 1 million homes in Houston. We describe the results in a new study published in the journal Applied Geography. Our past research in Houston found that more than half of 100,000 documented flood-prone buildings in the city currently lie outside official flood boundaries, and that these overlooked buildings are more likely to be in poor condition and uninsured, leaving them especially exposed when the floodwaters do come. The new research helps communities locate those homes. 4 things that make a home vulnerable To get a better understanding of each household’s vulnerability, we combined four types of information about each home. Water : How deep would floodwaters likely get at the home in a 100-year flood event, defined as having a 1% chance of occurrence in any given year? Here, we took a national flood model’s map of estimated parcel-level flood depths across Harris County and recorded the estimated depth at each residence. Building : How old is the home, and how well has it been constructed and maintained? Older, lower-quality homes in poor repair tend to suffer more damage when floodwater enters the structure. County appraisal records collected by expert assessors can provide critical pieces of information for making such judgments. Mobility : How busy are the roads nearby? For each home, we measured typical traffic within about a half-mile and within 3 miles. The busier those surrounding roads, the more a flood disrupts trips to work, school and hospitals, and the harder it is for first responders to get in and trapped residents to get out. Finances : How much would it cost to repair the home, and what share of nearby homes have flood insurance? Neither keeps water out of a home, but both reflect what it costs to recover. We chose these four criteria because flood research consistently highlights their importance for how hard a flood hits a community: how much water arrives , how well the building holds up , whether people can still get around and how big the repair bill is for the owner . They aren’t the only possible measures; a city could use others within each category, depending on available data. What we found Homes in the same neighborhood can have very different flood vulnerability scores. In fact, we found the scores differed more from house to house within a neighborhood than from one neighborhood to the next. In practice, this means that knowing a neighborhood’s flood risk doesn’t necessarily tell you how hard a flood could hit any individual home. A neighborhood could look safe on average while containing some of the county’s riskiest homes , and there may be many well-protected homes in an otherwise risky neighborhood. Much of the problem, we show, lies at the scale of buildings, not neighborhoods or ZIP codes. What residents and communities can do Homeowners can check several of these risks themselves. Ask longtime neighbors or your city’s flood plain office whether your home or the street has been flooded before. Look up the home’s age in local property records and have an inspector assess its condition. Find out whether the routes to work and school flood easily. And check whether you have a flood insurance policy , and what it covers: Most homeowner’s policies don’t cover flood damage. Communities can apply our approach with their own data to locate particularly vulnerable housing where neighborhood averages may disguise the need for help. They can start with existing address-level flood scores, such as First Street’s , and add local records on buildings, roads and insurance. articles.title: Referee jokingly offers Jacob Fowler an apple during Maple Leafs clash
articles.summary: The Montreal Canadiens goaltender Jacob Fowler experienced an unusual interruption during Saturday’s matchup against the Toronto Maple Leafs when a fake green apple appeared on the ice. The bizarre incident caught the attention of both players and fans, with referee T.J. Luxmore adding to t
articles._body: The Montreal Canadiens goaltender Jacob Fowler experienced an unusual interruption during Saturday’s matchup against the Toronto Maple Leafs when a fake green apple appeared on the ice . The bizarre incident caught the attention of both players and fans, with referee T.J. Luxmore adding to the moment by briefly showing the object to the rookie netminder. According to Sportsnet, Fowler noticed the apple while focused on tracking the puck during the second period. After Luxmore picked it up, the official showed it to Fowler during a stoppage in play. “I’m used to tracking a black puck, not a green apple,” Fowler joked after the game. The goaltender also revealed that he had never experienced anything like it before. The incident was also shared by Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman on X. Can I offer you an apple in this trying time? : @Sportsnet or stream on Sportsnet+ https://t.co/qAjIlD26Mn pic.twitter.com/UFu7ltqXq8 — NHL (@NHL) November 8, 2026 The object had been thrown onto the ice with approximately 8:30 remaining in the second period. Fowler initially questioned what it was, while Luxmore jokingly identified it as a tennis ball before revealing its apple-like appearance. The referee also suggested he might have stopped play if the Maple Leafs had entered the offensive zone while the object was on the ice. Fowler admitted that the incident caught him off guard but did not disrupt his performance. The 21-year-old finished with 26 saves as Montreal secured a 4-2 victory at Scotiabank Arena. Despite Toronto’s attempts to mount a comeback in the third period, Fowler helped the Canadiens preserve their lead before Zachary Bolduc added an insurance goal on the power play. The rookie improved his season record to 8-1-1 through 10 starts, with a 2.15 goals-against average and .925 save percentage. articles.title: You won’t be able to return a Christmas gift you bought on Amazon purchased before Nov. 1
articles.summary: Estimates for spending on holiday gifts, decor and the like between late 2026 and January 2027 range from about $1 trillion to $1.7 trillion in the U.S.
articles._body: Amazon , Costco, Target , Walmart and other retailers begin their holiday sales as early as October . But there’s no need to rush to buy wool scarves, fuzzy throw blankets and the other holiday gifts on your list the second you spot some tinsel while shopping. As a finance professor who studies how people and companies make financial decisions , I can explain why the holiday shopping season starts so early: It can help retailers attract more customers while allowing cash-strapped shoppers to stretch purchases out across multiple paychecks. And, for people with deeper pockets, buying gifts early can help them avoid the stress that goes with last-minute shopping. Why retailers get such an early start Estimates for spending on holiday gifts, decor and the like between late 2026 and January 2027 range from about US$1 trillion to $1.7 trillion in the U.S. Some 29% of Americans plan to shell out their share of those large sums in early to mid-December this holiday season, while 17% will shop on Black Friday, the day after Thanksgiving, according to the Bank of America Holiday Spending survey . But many people like to shop for holiday gifts early – meaning before Halloween . Some do this out of necessity : They can’t afford to buy all the gifts they want to give unless they spread the cost over multiple paychecks. For others, it’s more of a preference. In a 2025 survey, about 54% of early shoppers said they want to manage their budgets gradually . In addition, 41% said they buy gifts early to avoid the stress associated with last-minute shopping. Retailers are adjusting by getting an early start on holiday sales and promoting seasonal items. By offering customers deals months before gift-giving commences, they can encourage even more people to join the early birds . And by launching promotions in October, they might secure sales that otherwise would go to their competitors later in the season. A longer selling season offers other advantages to retailers. It may ease pressure on their supply chain and logistics , since they can receive seasonal orders over three months instead of one or two. This minimizes shipping difficulties and lowers warehouse overhead costs. Building more time into the calendar to move seasonal inventory gives retailers more opportunities to sell those items. However, an earlier shopping season does not necessarily increase consumer spending overall. Some purchases may simply shift from December to October. Beware of some early-shopping pitfalls To make sure that buying gifts long before the holidays occur is a wise move, early shoppers should read vendors’ fine print and research their return policies . Many big retailers are making their return policies more restrictive by shortening the length of time you can return purchases and adding return/restocking fees. In some cases, the deadline you face for returning an item could fall before the holidays. For example, Best Buy’s extended policy takes effect in 2026 only for purchases made on or after Oct. 30. Target similarly restricts its holiday-season returns window to items bought on or after Nov. 1. Amazon extended its holiday return policy in 2026. If you buy an item from Nov. 1 to Dec. 31, it can be returned until Jan. 31, 2027, except for Apple products, which can be returned until Jan. 15. Anyone who bought gifts beforehand will likely be subject to a standard 30-day return policy, which will expire long before Christmas. When buying early makes financial sense Shopping early is smart when the costs of waiting could outweigh the potential benefits of spending your money earlier than otherwise necessary. For example, if a popular wool scarf that was priced at $100 in October is out of stock on Amazon by November, the supply is gone, but demand remains high. If you want to buy it for your mom and ensure it arrives in time, you may need to get it from other retailers. Maybe you can find the scarf on a website but is selling for $150. If time has run out, you might have to pay, say, $30 more for expedited shipping, bringing the total to $180. Clearly, you would have been better off buying it early on at a lower price. But that doesn’t mean you necessarily need to rush to buy a gift weeks or months ahead of when you’ll be placing it under a tree. First make sure that the price is in line with your expectations and what you’re willing to shell out. And you should do some comparison shopping to make sure other retailers aren’t charging less for the same or similar items. Remember, waiting to do your holiday shopping until the last minute can lead to unnecessary costs, like rush shipping fees. The key is to have a budget , recognize when the price is right, and know when to stop shopping. James Malm , Professor of Finance and Director of the Global Business Resource Center, College of Charleston This article is republished from The Conversation under a Creative Commons license. articles.title: JP Morgan Athlete Center of Excellence: athletes need a financial playbook now more than ever
articles.summary: These aren’t professional athlete questions.
articles._body: For years, the playbook was simple: athletes focused on their sport first, and financial planning came later. Only after signing a professional contract did they typically hire advisors, accountants and attorneys — and start thinking seriously about managing their wealth. That timeline often no longer reflects reality. The sports industry has made tremendous strides in creating new ways for athletes to earn money. The next challenge is ensuring they have the knowledge and support to manage it. Today, many athletes start earning meaningful income long before they turn professional. The College Sports Commission estimates that student-athletes received $1.77 billion in revenue-sharing pay in 2025-2026. Name, Image and Likeness (NIL) opportunities have accelerated that shift, giving student-athletes access to sponsorships and business opportunities while they’re still in school. At the same time, the demand for financial guidance is growing. The 2022 NCAA Student-Athlete Well-Being Study found that many have a strong desire for more resources on financial literacy and taxes. There is a big focus on creating more earning opportunities for athletes. We now need to put the same energy into helping athletes prepare for the financial responsibilities that come with them. Decisions are coming earlier Too often, financial education starts after the money arrives. By then, habits have already formed and important decisions may have already been made. The reality is that some of the most important financial choices for athletes happen before they sign a major contract. How do taxes work? How much should I save? How do I navigate money conversations with friends and family? Who should I trust? These aren’t professional athlete questions. They’re life questions. And athletes are encountering them earlier than ever before. One thing I’ve learned from conversations with athletes in my role at J.P. Morgan’s Athlete Center of Excellence is that they’re eager for this guidance. I’ve spoken with current players who — when they were earning NIL income — budgeted for spending and invested the rest, only to find themselves short on cash when tax payments were due. They had the right pieces in place but only became fully engaged when there was a need to be. I’ve seen a lot of players learn to bring in their financial advisor this way — relying on the advisor to then quarterback communication among their agent, attorney and accountant. Athletes need to think like CEOs Athletes should not be expected to be financial experts. Just as athletes rely on coaches, trainers, nutritionists and medical professionals, they should be able to rely on trusted specialists for financial guidance. But athletes should also have basic financial knowledge so they can ask thoughtful questions, evaluate advice and make informed decisions. I often encourage athletes to think of themselves as the CEO of their own business. You don’t have to master every function of the organization, but you should understand how the pieces fit together and remain engaged in the decisions that affect your future. That mindset has become increasingly important as athletes build personal brands and create new income streams earlier in their careers. Today’s athletes aren’t just managing contracts. Many are navigating partnerships, content opportunities, business ventures and NIL deals at a young age. The financial complexity has increased, and adequate preparation needs to increase with it. What happens next? The answer isn’t limiting opportunity for athletes. It’s building a stronger foundation of education and support around it. First, we need to start earlier. Financial fundamentals should be introduced in high school, before athletes encounter significant earnings. By the time money arrives, the framework for managing it should already be in place. Second, financial education cannot be a one-time conversation. Athletes’ needs evolve as they move from high school to college, turn professional and transition out of sports. The guidance they receive should evolve alongside them. One of the reasons the JPMorganChase Athlete Council was created was to hear directly from athletes. This way, we can better understand the financial questions they’re facing and develop resources that reflect their real-world experiences, not our assumptions. Athletic careers are unlike almost any other profession. Most people earn income over several decades. Athletes often earn a huge portion of their career income over a much shorter period of time. Opportunities can arrive unexpectedly, and they can disappear just as quickly. If we want athletes to thrive not only during their playing careers but throughout the rest of their lives, we need to start with financial education long before the first major paycheck arrives. articles.summary: The New England Patriots Hall of Fame induction of tight end Rob Gronkowski celebrated not only his on-field achievements but also the personality and lasting impact that made him a beloved figure throughout the organization. In a video message shared by the Patriots, former teammate Julian Edelm
articles._body: The New England Patriots Hall of Fame induction of tight end Rob Gronkowski celebrated not only his on-field achievements but also the personality and lasting impact that made him a beloved figure throughout the organization. In a video message shared by the Patriots, former teammate Julian Edelman described Gronkowski as “the most dominant player I ever played with,” highlighting his impact in both the running and passing games. Edelman also praised his former teammate’s positive outlook and ability to bring happiness to those around him. “You were the best teammate, a joy to be around, and made everyone have fun,” Edelman said. Gronkowski officially entered the Patriots Hall of Fame on Saturday, November 7, during a ceremony at Gillette Stadium. More than 60 former players and several Hall of Famers returned to celebrate the former tight end, who spent nine seasons in New England and captured three Super Bowl championships. The induction also reunites three key members of New England’s championship era in the Patriots Hall of Fame, with Gronkowski joining former teammates Julian Edelman and Tom Brady. The ceremony also featured tributes from former teammates and the Kraft family. Although unable to attend while recovering from back surgery, owner Robert Kraft sent a video message praising Gronkowski’s impact on the organization. Jonathan Kraft also highlighted his ability to bring happiness to those around him. Beyond his football career, Gronkowski’s impact extended into the community through his charitable initiatives. His Gronk Nation Youth Foundation has supported children, youth programs, and charitable organizations across New England, reflecting his commitment to making a difference beyond the football field. A CEO gave his employees Fridays off. Three years later, revenue is up about 160%
articles.summary: Brick Media caps workloads and hires instead of piling on. Resignations fell from six in 2022 to none so far in 2026, though profit margins have held flat.
articles._body: In late 2022, Jake Kurtz, founder and CEO of Tampa-based social media agency Brick Media, wanted a better work-life balance. He had a wild idea: What if everyone worked just four days a week? After seeing European companies experiment with shorter workweeks on social media, he launched a 90-day pilot in January 2023 , giving employees Fridays off without cutting their salaries. By April, he had made the schedule permanent . Nearly four years later, Brick’s revenue has grown dramatically. According to figures the company provided, revenue jumped 73% in 2023, another 39% in 2024, and 8% in 2025. Compounded, that’s roughly 160% growth in three years. Kurtz believes some of that success traces back to the four-day workweek, though he doesn’t claim the schedule alone explains it. He bets that giving employees a reason to stay makes the company more efficient and more competitive, even as workplace researchers say the four-day week has faded from the hybrid-work conversation and some leaders who tried it have dialed it back . How Brick’s four-day week works At Brick, employees work four nine-hour days, Monday through Thursday. That’s a 36-hour week, four hours short of the traditional 40, with paid lunch breaks included. Employees are still considered full-time and eligible for benefits. That puts Brick between a compressed 40-hour week and the 32-hour model some researchers advocate. At Fortune ‘s Workplace Innovation Summit in May, University of Georgia psychology professor Malissa Clark argued that the point of a four-day week is to cut eight hours, not cram 40 hours into four days. Brick’s schedule also contrasts with the long hours common in the related public relations field. Muck Rack’s State of PR 2026 report found that 55% of PR professionals surveyed had worked more than 40 hours the previous week. Social media doesn’t exactly take weekends off, but Kurtz said clients have been surprisingly understanding of the arrangement, and most content shoots, meetings and other work can be planned ahead of time. Employees still occasionally handle small tasks on Fridays or weekends, which he described as taking “five minutes here and there.” He estimated that more serious emergencies requiring several hours of work happen roughly once or twice a quarter. In those cases, nonexempt employees are eligible for overtime if they work more than 40 hours in a week, and the company brings in freelance contractors when needed. The rule he goes by: Don’t bury employees in work. Brick served 56 clients in all of 2022, compared with 85 in just the first half of 2026, according to Kurtz. A social media manager typically handles six or seven clients, with seven the upper limit. Once employees approach that threshold, Brick hires more people instead of piling more work on existing staff. That’s one reason revenue has grown so quickly. It’s also why profit margins have stayed roughly unchanged since 2022, Kurtz said, as payroll has risen alongside revenue. Employees also work from home most of the time. Only one of the four working days requires a trip to the office. Why Kurtz treats retention as a growth strategy For Kurtz, keeping employees happy is as much a business strategy as a cultural one. “If I can keep people here longer, and they like their job, and they’re communicating with similar people all the time, it just makes the business a lot more efficient,” he told Fortune . Experienced employees don’t need everything spelled out. Kurtz said colleagues who have worked together for years can sometimes resolve something in a two-minute hallway conversation that might otherwise take 30 minutes. He believes that efficiency translates into better client relationships and, ultimately, more business. Of the 20 new leads Brick received in October, 16 came from referrals, according to Kurtz. The company’s resignation numbers suggest employees are increasingly willing to stay. Brick recorded six voluntary departures in 2022, before the schedule change, compared with two in 2023, two in 2024, three in 2025, and none so far in 2026, according to figures provided to Fortune . Its workforce has grown from 15 employees at the end of 2022 to 25 today. Asked whether Brick could have achieved the same success with employees onsite five days a week and working frequent overtime, Kurtz said, “No, I really don’t… I think people would leave Brick Media for like a $5,000 raise.” He said he knows some employees have had better offers and chosen to stay. “People have a hard time leaving the four-day schedule once they experience it, because they start to realize that life is way more than just the salary,” he said. It’s the same case ThredUp CEO James Reinhart made on Clark’s panel at the Fortune summit, where he warned that companies sticking with five-day weeks will lose the competition for top talent. An employee’s view: same work, fewer days For Andrea Echeverry, Brick’s director of client experience, who has been with the company since before the schedule change, switching to four days hasn’t meant doing less work. “I think we have just found more ways to be more efficient with our time,” she told Fortune . She doesn’t mind squeezing the same workload into four longer days. In fact, she prefers it. Echeverry said “hustle culture has played a role,” explaining that people her age are still willing to work long hours but take a different approach to the traditional “work hard, play hard” mentality. She is a working mother whose husband also works full-time, and Fridays are now for spending time with her child and running personal errands. To Echeverry, it’s part of a generational shift in attitudes toward work. Rather than accept traditional workplace arrangements simply because previous generations di

I mean, data engineers like to work on these platforms but since some time I really have ethical concerns about it - like: - vendor lock-in - high costs (because of cloud costs - and in most cases you are not able to connect your own metal if you have one) - non-EU vendors... - other open-source solutions have high license costs for LDAP etc. pp. That's why is started to build my own opinionated data lakehouse platform in my spare time (tbh I also started learning agentic engineering and what harnesses are..), only curated from open source projects already available. The building blocks are pretty straightforward imo: - Iceberg tables on whatever S3 storage you already have - Trino for SQL and Spark Connect for jobs - Airflow for schedules, plus notebooks, Kafka streams and dashboards - One web UI and one API over all of it - stuff around like OIDC, secrets management etc. It's fully pre-alpha. But I want to use it as an internal pitch project at my current employer to push agentic engineering & the idea of creating our own data platform for our non-hyperscaler customers. articles.title: Unrest in France looks like a ‘pretty big foreshadowing’ to economists nervously eyeing national debt at 126% of GDP
articles.summary: "To me, the biggest warning sign from France is really not just the K-shaped economy effect, but the generational effect that's going on and to see young people really driving this latest protest."
articles._body: When U.S. markets watched as Paris metaphorically imploded just weeks ago, the consensus reaction was: “Let’s not do that.” Unrest ripped through the French capital after protesters initially highlighted failings in the public school system. The action snowballed into widespread expressions of dissatisfaction with the cost of living and job prospects. The macroeconomic health of the European nation is not in great shape: unemployment was 8.3% in Q2, real GDP growth was 0.4%, and wage growth was 1.7% at the national level. And underpinning it all is public debt, currently at 116% of GDP, with 30-year bonds topping 5.4% at the time of writing. And the U.S. bond market, flirting with a wrap on the wrist for its own policymakers presiding over mounting debt , stalled. In fact, 10- and 30-year Treasury yields even declined. “There’s a reason that the U.S. has pulled back a little bit in the last few weeks [and] why France has not,” Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, told a Bipartisan Policy Center (BPC) event last week. “It’s a couple of key indicators that differentiate us from France and suggest … that we still have a little bit of room to have these debates now, in the context of a K-shaped economy. “We’re at about 100% debt-to-GDP; they’re at 120% debt-to-GDP. They are further along that crisis curve, and they are growing at about 0.5%. We’re growing at just over 2%. That’s a pretty big difference. ” While economists largely agree that policymakers are perhaps naive in their hopes to simply grow the U.S. out of a debt crisis, starting from a point of strength rather than stagnation gives the economy a better chance of rebalancing its debt-to-GDP ratio. But Long added that France also differs from the U.S. in that the former has exhausted much of its revenue-generating capacity through taxes. Per the OECD, the “tax wedge” (the difference between labor costs to the employer and the corresponding net take-home pay of the employee) for French workers is 47.2%, according to its most recent data. The U.S., on the other hand, is down at 30%. “It’s certainly not easy to raise taxation in the U.S., but from a financial world perspective and the bond market perspective, there’s a lot more room to experiment and to grow in the United States than there is in France,” Long added. “To me, the biggest warning sign from France is really not just the K-shaped economy effect, but the generational effect that’s going on and to see young people really driving this latest protest … from the disparities that they’re seeing generationally, and that seems like a pretty big foreshadowing [of] what we could see here as we creep towards 120% debt to GDP.” The generation question As with any debt, the question of repayment isn’t if but when—and that’s the question budget experts are asking the public and politicians to think about. Phil Swagel, the director of the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office , said policymakers have a series of choices to make: How they might prepare for growth to slow if spending is cut, which forms of tax to explore, and so on. “The other set of choices that you can think about with the deficit is about which generation is paying, so the longer we wait to make changes, that means some generations are … missing out on their share of the burden of the adjustment,” Swagel told the BPC event, “and then who within each generation will pay a tax.”   He explained: “The longer we wait means some generations, in some sense, don’t share in the burden of the adjustment. Then, who within each generation is affected? I think there’s a societal consensus it will be progressive, not in the political sense, but in the sense that households with relatively high lifetime incomes will have more of a share of the adjustment. But that’s a societal preference, and there’s lots of room for disagreement in there.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles._body: Michigan finally broke Dave Portnoy. The Barstool Sports founder unloaded a four-plus-minute NSFW rant after watching his alma mater fall 15-6 at home to the Michigan State Spartans on Saturday. He did not direct his ire at the players, however. No, the colorful sports media personality decided to focus all his wrath on the Wolverines’ coaching staff . “Kyle Whittingham — fire him, gone, get him out of here,” Portnoy said in a video he posted on X. “{Michigan offensive coordinator} Jason Beck — gone, fire him, get him out of here. They’re both absolute football terrorists. They don’t belong here. They never fit in here. Kyle Whittingham is the most lifeless old man. “This guy, the game has passed him by. He just sits on the sidelines with that hangdog glare…. He’s just not our guy. I wanted to give you the benefit of the doubt, but this is so pathetic. I’m watching this team, and I just want to puke… This is the worst coaching staff. Sherrone Moore looks like a f*****g genius compared to these guys… This Michigan football team is the worst Michigan football team I’ve pretty much ever seen.” Portnoy can lay it on pretty thick, but many fans likely share his outrage . The Wolverines are a controversial win versus Western Michigan away from being sub-.500 right now. With surging Oregon, undefeated UCLA and declining yet generally dangerous Ohio State all on the final stretch of the schedule, it is hard to see this squad becoming bowl-game eligible. Michigan football is a joke Dave wants everybody FIRED pic.twitter.com/vxxjbs38AR — Barstool Sports (@barstoolsports) November 8, 2026 The Bryce Underwood investment has failed catastrophically, and the Whittingham hire has not brought the program back to its roots like Ann Arbor hoped. The play-calling is too often uninspiring, and there is no offensive identity. Stumbling in The Big House versus a lowly Spartans team sent a startling message to Dave Portnoy and the rest of the alumni/fan base. Michigan is in disaster mode. Making huge changes one year after hiring a head coach is uncommon, but these are obviously unacceptable outcomes. El Presidente is not shy about expressing his opinion, even though he has interviewed Whittingham and enjoyed cordial interactions with him. “At some point, you have to be like ‘you’re the worst football coach in football right now,'” Portnoy opined. “I don’t know what you did in Utah, but you are 100 years old. You’re a fossil, you cannot coach this football team. If you had an ounce of dignity, you wouldn’t ask for a paycheck or a buyout, because all you’ve done is torpedo this program. Go sailing, go catch fish, go do whatever old people do in an old person home. “You belong in a nursing home. And Jason Beck, you belong on the terrorist watch list.” Dave Portnoy has been able to keep up the Michigan bravado for a while, riding high after the 2023-24 national championship, but he is utterly disgusted by this version of the Wolverines. Despite only allowing 16.4 points per game, this group ranks 97th with 138.0 rushing yards per game and is outside the top-200 with 178.4 passing yards per game. If Michigan can find success against their three ranked opponents to end the year, then perhaps Whittingham and Beck will be granted a stay of execution from the angry Ann Arbor mob. Or is it already too late? The post Michigan alum Dave Portnoy wants everybody fired after loss to Michigan State appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: ‘No vote, no warning, just plain math’: Social Security is six years from an automatic 22% cut—and most Americans have no idea
articles.summary: The retirement trust fund runs dry in late 2032, triggering an automatic cut for current and future retirees. Every year Congress waits makes the fix bigger.
articles._body: More than one in five Americans don’t know that their Social Security checks could be cut by roughly 20% in about six years, according to a recent TIAA survey on Social Security . The program’s retirement trust fund, which pays benefits to retirees and survivors, is projected to run out of reserves in the fourth quarter of 2032, according to the 2026 Social Security Trustees Report . After that, incoming payroll taxes would cover only 78% of scheduled benefits. The resulting 22% cut would apply across the board, including to people already collecting. “Insolvency is a slightly misleading word for what the Trustees are projecting,” says Martin Mulyadi, YHB Endowed Chair in Accounting and Professor of Accounting at Shenandoah University. Payroll taxes keep flowing after 2032, he notes: “Social Security is not running out of money in 2032. It is running out of savings.” The stakes are large. Social Security pays monthly benefits to more than 71 million people , and it provides the majority of income for 43% of seniors, according to AARP . The Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget (CRFB) estimates that a 22% cut would cost a typical dual-income couple retiring in 2033 about $16,900 a year. CRFB has warned that the program is “on a collision course toward insolvency,” and Fortune has reported that its finances haven’t looked this bad since 1983. The alarm grew louder after the trustees confirmed the 22% cut in June . “America has a 25 trillion dollar problem,” says Michael Liner, a disability attorney and founder of Liner Legal, a law firm that specializes in Social Security disability benefits. “The gap between what Social Security has promised and what it can actually afford to pay.” The trustees now put that 75-year gap even higher, at $29.3 trillion in present value, up from $25.1 trillion in last year’s report. If nothing changes, Liner says, the cut arrives automatically: “No vote, no warning, just plain math.” For many retirees, he adds, it will be “the difference between getting by or not.” Why the retirement fund is running dry Social Security is funded mainly by payroll taxes. For decades, those taxes exceeded what the program paid out, and the surplus built up reserves in two trust funds: the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance (OASI) fund for retirees and survivors, and the Disability Insurance (DI) fund. That changed in 2021, when the retirement fund’s costs began exceeding its total income, according to the Congressional Research Service . Reserves have been covering the difference ever since. “In 2025, Social Security took in about $1.45 trillion and paid out about $1.61 trillion, and reserves covered the gap,” Mulyadi says. The disability fund is in better shape; the trustees don’t project it running dry at any point in the next 75 years. If Congress legally merged the two funds, combined reserves would last until 2034 and then cover 83% of benefits, according to CRFB . That would require a change in law, and it wouldn’t close the underlying shortfall. The public has noticed. In a June 2025 survey, just 36% of Americans told AARP they were confident in Social Security’s future, the lowest level since 2010 . Much of the pressure is demographic. Social Security now serves roughly twice as many beneficiaries as it did in 1980, when about 35.5 million people collected. Lower birth rates mean fewer workers paying in, retirees are collecting for longer, and declining immigration has shrunk the pool of workers paying payroll taxes. Inequality plays a role, too. Payroll taxes apply only to earnings up to a cap, $184,500 this year, and high earners’ pay has grown faster than everyone else’s. The share of total wages subject to the tax fell from almost 87% in 1984 to roughly 83% today, according to Roosevelt Institute research reported by CBS News . “The Social Security trust fund is under strain because Congress has failed to update the program for the economy we actually have,” said Elizabeth Wilkins, CEO of the Roosevelt Institute, a progressive think tank. “Too much income now flows to the top, where it escapes Social Security taxation.” Congress fixed a similar crisis in 1983 The last time Social Security came this close, Congress acted. The 1983 amendments gradually raised the full retirement age from 65 to 67 and, for the first time, subjected some benefits to federal income tax. “We’ve had two instances in our history where it was suggested Social Security was going to go insolvent,” says Ernie Wingard, an advisor at Capital Choice Financial Group, “and in both of those instances, at the last minute, Congress was able to come to an agreement that saved it.” That 1983 fix was designed to keep the program solvent for 75 years. If the retirement fund runs dry in 2032 as projected, it will have lasted about 50. The fixes on the table, and their trade-offs Lawmakers have plenty of levers. Options modeled in the American Academy of Actuaries’ Social Security Challenge tool and in Social Security Administration analyses include: Raising the full retirement age from 67 to 69. Raising the payroll tax rate from 6.2% to 7.2% each for workers and employers. Lifting the cap on taxable earnings, set at $192,300 for 2027 , to a higher level such as $250,000 or $400,000. Using a different inflation measure to calculate the annual cost-of-living adjustment (COLA), which would slow benefit growth. “Any fix has to close that gap through some mix of more revenue, such as a higher payroll tax rate or a higher cap on taxable earnings, and slower benefit growth, such as a later full retirement age or changes to the benefit formula,” Mulyadi says. “Each option has trade-offs, and the longer Congress waits, the larger each adjustment has to be.” The fight is over the mix. In a debate covered by Fortune , two economists who disagreed on whether to phase out Social Security still agreed that wealthy Americans would have to pay more. articles._body: John Mateer expressed a unity message about the Oklahoma Sooners’ chemistry and bond following their 23-7 win over the Florida Gators on Saturday evening. Mateer is going through the senior campaign of his collegiate career with the Sooners. While the team has gone through mixed results, the quarterback has persevered to be productive on the field. For this game, Mateer shined with a big performance on the road. He completed 21 out of 33 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns while rushing 14 times for 56 yards. The quarterback reflected on the victory after the game, having firm praise on how the team came together to pull off this win over Florida, who were ranked in the AP Top 25. “W e just believed s omething like this can happen, and kids like us can make a decision . But everybody in the building decided to fight and play for each other, and we started off with a good flow. N eed to score more touchdowns. Field goals are cool, but we want touchdowns. But it was good, man. And we have each other’s back, and that matters, ” Mateer said on the ESPN broadcast. “W e knew coming in here it’s a great environment. We were saying in the locker, this is what you dream of. A s a kid, so many great players have played here, and we love each other like we’re not going to give up on each other. S ome people might quit. Some people might want us to quit because the trials are hard, and they are. But we give it to God, and we do it for each other.” ❝We’re not gonna give up on each other❞ pic.twitter.com/7n4PP74RGz — Oklahoma Football (@OU_Football) November 8, 2026 Mateer and Oklahoma controlled the game from start to finish. They did an excellent job containing Florida’s attack, only conceding a touchdown in the second quarter. Rocky Beers led receivers with four catches for 72 yards. And right now, we don’t have that identity clear enough offensively, which is frustrating,” Sumrall said, per reporter Chandler Dantzler. articles.title: Notre Dame’s Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa breaks ‘The U’ after sacking Darian Mensah
articles.summary: There are multiple developments coming out of Notre Dame’s 31-24 home victory over No. 1 Miami on Saturday night. The Fighting Irish are a genuine national title contender now ensconced in the College Football Playoff, and quarterback CJ Carr secured his spot in the Heisman Trophy ceremony
articles._body: There are multiple developments coming out of Notre Dame’s 31-24 home victory over No. 1 Miami on Saturday night. The Fighting Irish are a genuine national title contender now ensconced in the College Football Playoff, and quarterback CJ Carr secured his spot in the Heisman Trophy ceremony after completing 72.5 percent of his passes for 319 yards and three touchdowns. But fans cannot overlook another consequence of this signature win in South Bend . Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa just formally established himself as one of the most impactful linebackers in the country. One specific moment best accentuated his game-changing performance. Less than a minute into the third quarter, and with his team leading 17-3, the 20-year-old American Samoan reinforced Notre Dame’s momentum by recording a huge sack on Miami star QB Darian Mensah. This third-and-7 stop kept the Hurricanes on their back. Actually, according to Viliamu-Asa, it broke their back. The 6-foot-3, 234-pound junior used his hands to form “The U” symbol before pretending to break it over his knee . This game meant a lot to him, especially given his recent thumb injury, but it also meant the world to the program. Notre Dame's Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa sacks Darian Mensah and breaks "The U" over his knee to celebrate. pic.twitter.com/1YVYZe4nIM — Underdog CFB (@UnderdogCFB) November 8, 2026 The CFP selection committee essentially told the Fighting Irish that they would need to beat Miami in order to have a realistic shot at making the final 12-team bracket. Pressure was rising, and even though electric Canes wide receiver Malachi Toney was sidelined with an ankle injury, Notre Dame could have still tripped on the big stage. It certainly has before. Not on this night, though. Despite allowing Miami to cut the deficit to one possession, Marcus Freeman’s squad answered the committee’s challenge. CJ Carr, WR Micah Gilbert (nine receptions for 98 yards and two touchdowns) and safety Luke Talich (clutch interception around midfield late in the third) all produced highlight-reel plays that will have a lasting impression on fans. But so too will the Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa sack. And the ensuing celebration. The Fighting Irish (8-1) will have to prove themselves all over again in the CFP, as will the other competitors, but they aced the eye and result tests on Saturday. What more will be asked of Notre Dame football? Fans will find out when the newest rankings are unveiled on Tuesday. articles.title: Skip Bayless drops ‘refund’ claim after Alabama takes down Lane Kiffin’s LSU
articles.summary: No. 14 LSU suffered a 31-13 home loss to No. 5 Alabama on Saturday at Tiger Stadium, dropping to 6-3 overall and 3-3 in SEC play. Following the defeat, popular sports analyst Skip Bayless took to social media with a pointed remark about Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin’s seven-year, $91 millio
articles._body: No. 14 LSU suffered a 31-13 home loss to No. 5 Alabama on Saturday at Tiger Stadium, dropping to 6-3 overall and 3-3 in SEC play. Following the defeat, popular sports analyst Skip Bayless took to social media with a pointed remark about Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin’s seven-year, $91 million contract. “LSU is going to want a refund,” he wrote on X (formerly Twitter). The result brought another setback for Kiffin, who arrived in Baton Rouge after leaving Ole Miss. The Tigers entered the contest with expectations of competing for a national championship, but their third defeat of the season has left their College Football Playoff hopes in serious jeopardy. LSU’s chances of reaching the postseason dropped from 51% to 25% after Saturday’s loss, according to the Allstate Playoff Predictor. While the Tigers outgained the Crimson Tide 457-285, they repeatedly came up empty when it mattered the most. Quarterback Sam Leavitt completed 35 of 47 passes for 380 yards but failed to throw a touchdown and was intercepted once. He also took four sacks. Running back Jackson Harris contributed 166 receiving yards on 11 catches, while tight end Trey’Dez Green added 10 receptions for 85 yards. However, LSU’s inability to finish drives came back to ultimately haunt the team. The Tigers converted none of their four fourth-down attempts, resulting in the most fourth-down failures of Kiffin’s coaching career. LSU also reached the red zone four times but managed only one touchdown and one field goal. Moreover, the Tigers missed a 56-yard field goal attempt. LSU moved ahead 13-10 late in the third quarter through Dilin Jones’ five-yard touchdown run, but that advantage lasted less than three minutes before the Crimson Tide responded with a touchdown pass from quarterback Keelon Russell to tight end Josh Ford. Alabama then added two more touchdowns to complete a 21-point unanswered run. Russell finished with 206 passing yards and three touchdowns on 17-of-24 passing. Ryan Coleman-Williams also played a major role, returning a punt 32 yards to set up the Crimson Tide’s fourth-quarter touchdown drive. The defeat extended the Tigers’ disappointing run against Alabama. LSU has now lost four consecutive meetings to the Crimson Tide, all by double-digit margins, and seven of their last eight games against them at home. Kiffin also remains winless versus Alabama as a head coach , falling to 0-6 in his career against the program. Speaking after the game, Kiffin described the performance as “really disappointing” and acknowledged that the offensive production should have resulted in considerably more points. He also admitted he did not expect his team to be 6-3 at this stage of the season. The Tigers now face another big challenge, with a home game against a top-10 Texas team scheduled for next week. LSU will need to win its remaining games and receive considerable help elsewhere to have a realistic opportunity to reach the College Football Playoff. articles.title: Why Hawks’ Jalen Johnson was feeling his shot in huge win over Nets
articles.summary: ATLANTA – The Atlanta Hawks just came off a game against the Washington Wizards the night before, where their defense wasn’t the best, but they still walked away with the win. In the first quarter against the Brooklyn Nets, that trend may have continued, and it led them into a 17-poin
articles._body: ATLANTA – The Atlanta Hawks just came off a game against the Washington Wizards the night before, where their defense wasn’t the best, but they still walked away with the win. In the first quarter against the Brooklyn Nets, that trend may have continued, and it led them into a 17-point deficit early. It didn’t last for long, as they were able to tighten up in the second half and get their first lead of the game late in the fourth quarter, ultimately defeating the Nets 124-121. It was Jalen Johnson, who returned from a three-game absence due to injury, and Aaron Wiggins who willed the Hawks to victory in the fourth. Though Johnson went 0-for-5 from the 3-point line, he continued to put pressure on the rim and get to his mid-range shot, finishing the game with a game-high 30 points. “I was just trusting my shots,” Johnson said after the game. “Obviously the 3s didn’t go in, but my teammates made it easy for me, and I was just trying to find easy ways to operate more. Just trusting the spots I know I can get to at any point.” Head coach Quin Snyder has praised Johnson since last year for his willingness to take catch-and-shoot 3s. They didn’t go in tonight, but Snyder still wants him to stay aggressive, while also finding other ways to affect the game. “The way he started, he was really running. He was active without the ball,” Snyder said. “When you can learn to play without the ball, it takes your game to another level. At certain times, he was able to have the ball, and we wanted him to have the ball and make good reads, which I thought was important. “I want him to shoot. I think that’s really important for him to catch and shoot and make those reads before he gets the ball. That’s what he did. I don’t think JJ went away from anything. I thought he did additional things, and then obviously at the end of the game he was really good.” Wiggins continues to come off the bench and provide instant offense for the Hawks, and that’s what he did at the start of the fourth to cut down the Hawks’ deficit. He finished with 12 points in the quarter, and 20 overall for the night. “Just being aggressive,” Wiggins said. “Coming in and trying to provide any bit of energy or spark that I can for the team off the bench. You don’t want to have a drop-off in production, so I’m trying to go in there and make sure I’m contributing in a positive way and also being aggressive to help the team.” After allowing 70 points in the first half, the Hawks held the Nets to 51 in the second half. They were their most dominant down the stretch of the fourth, where several players were able to make big plays. Dyson Daniels got a steal, Onyeka Okongwu and Kingston Flemings had blocks, and Nickeil Alexander-Walker turned a loose ball into two points on the other end of the floor to extend the Hawks’ lead. Hustle plays pic.twitter.com/WCSgcrIW4R — Atlanta Hawks (@ATLHawks) November 8, 2026 “Our identity offensively is where we can run and move the ball, but defending, that’s the foundation,” Snyder said. “When we do that, it gives us an opportunity to do those other things across the board. Last night wasn’t our best defensive effort. We talked about that a little before the game, and I don’t think we started at the level we wanted to. Some of that was Brooklyn making shots, but as the game progressed, I thought we got better and better defensively.” After winning a game against the Wizards where they had the lead for most of the game, the Hawks had to fight back until the final minutes in this one to get their first lead and win. “You want to win games by as much as you can, but it’s good for us. Those experiences are good for us because it’s a long season. The NBA is full of good teams, and you’re not going to be able to avoid close games all the time. You can learn a lot from your team in those situations,” Wiggins said. The post Why Hawks’ Jalen Johnson was feeling his shot in huge win over Nets appeared first on ClutchPoints .

While Jared McCain led the Thunder’s bench in scoring in Saturday’s win at the Paycom Center, Mara stuffed the stat sheet in his second-career start, going 8-for-10, including his first NBA 3-pointer, and finishing with eight rebounds, three assists, and three blocks. articles._body: There were a ton of really juicy matchups in the Top 25 on Saturday, and with several ranked-on-ranked matchups there was sure to be movement in the polls. On3 stops to project the updated rankings coming out of the day’s events. Our projections are based on results posted over the weekend, as well as historical moves in the AP Poll. Keep in mind these are projections of what the AP Poll will look like on Sunday afternoon, not an On3 ballot or ranking of the Top 25. [ $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] There was a ton of action to dissect on Saturday, including a plethora of losses in the bottom half of last week’s ranking. Let’s dig into the updated projection of the AP Top 25. *** AP Top 25 Projections *** 25. SMU Mustangs (7-2) RESULT: 51-28 win vs. Virginia Tech PREVIOUS RANKING: NR SMU played on Friday night, against a Virginia Tech team that has been pretty good and sniffing around the bottom of the Top 25 rankings in recent weeks. It was no sweat for the Mustangs, who scored 23 points in the first half to take the lead and set the tone. Quarterback Kevin Jennings threw for 350 yards and four touchdowns in the contest. He was picked off once, but it wasn’t enough to impact the outcome. SMU spread the ball on the ground, racking up 219 yards rushing in the contest. Now comes a major ACC showdown. NEXT UP: Wake Forest 24. Ohio State Buckeyes (6-3) RESULT: 41-28 loss vs. Oregon PREVIOUS RANKING: 11 Ohio State knew it needed to play better after falling to USC. Things started off well enough, with running back Bo Jackson notching two early touchdown runs to put the team up 14-0. It all fell apart from there, following a flurry by Oregon to close the first half. Quarterback Luke Fahey was picked off once and couldn’t fully take advantage of the weapon that Jeremiah Smith was until the game was essentially over. Dan Lanning had Ryan Day ‘s number throughout the game, and Ohio State was stunned at home for a third loss this season. NEXT UP: Northwestern 23. LSU Tigers (6-3) RESULT: 31-13 loss vs. Alabama PREVIOUS RANKING: 15 LSU had the upper hand at various points in the game. It simply couldn’t finish. Several drives into Alabama territory produced only 13 points early, and eventually the Crimson Tide busted through on the other end to take charge of the contest. For the Tigers, the loss was a costly one. The program already trailed Alabama by nine spots in the CFP rankings, to the point that a third loss might have proven fatal. We’ll see, but this was a big opportunity missed for Lane Kiffin ‘s bunch. NEXT UP: Texas 22. Ole Miss Rebels (6-3) RESULT: 42-7 loss vs. Georgia PREVIOUS RANKING: 12 Ole Miss joins the list of three-loss SEC teams, and at this point it’s looking like it might be difficult for any of them to be within range of the Top 12 by year’s end. At the very least, it will likely take some help given where they’re expected to shake out in this week’s Top 25. The Rebels were never really competitive against the Bulldogs, having no answers for Gunner Stockton in the loss. Trinidad Chambliss was kept completely in check, throwing for just 170 yards, with one interception. He carried it nine times for a loss of 12 yards, with lost yardage from sacks included. NEXT UP: @ Oklahoma 21. Oregon Ducks (6-3) RESULT: 41-28 win at Ohio State PREVIOUS RANKING: NR Oregon fell behind 14-0 in the first quarter and might have been written off by some. Instead, the Ducks quickly turned things around late in the first half, scoring 17 points in the second quarter to take a 17-14 lead into the halftime break. It was all Ducks from there. They confounded Buckeyes quarterback Luke Fahey and made his day a mess. Quarterback Dylan Raiola got hot, aided by a remarkable touchdown catch by Dakorien Moore . Dierre Hill Jr. tacked on two touchdowns on the ground in the road rout. What a win. NEXT UP: Michigan 20. Arizona Wildcats (7-2) RESULT: 29-28 win vs. TCU PREVIOUS RANKING: 24 TCU has played just about everyone hard this season and Arizona was pushed to the absolute brink. It took some late theatrics for the Wildcats to pull out the win, but it’ll count as a ‘W’ all the same. And, boy, what a win it was on Friday night. Arizona could have tied the game with 1:45 remaining but failed a two-point conversion attempt. From there, it successfully executed a pooch onside kick to get itself a shot at the game-winning field goal. Michael Salgado-Medina connected from 37 for the win. NEXT UP: Utah 19. New Mexico Lobos (8-1) RESULT: 31-3 win at Nevada PREVIOUS RANKING: 22 New Mexico had no real problems in its Friday night tilt against Nevada. That was actually the program’s first game playing with an AP Top 25 ranking next to its name, so it was impressive that the team handled the hype so well. The Lobos took a 14-0 lead in the first quarter and never really looked back. Scottre Humphrey ran for 107 yards and two scores, while Kiefer Sibley added 54 yards and a rushing touchdown. The Lobos have a tricky next game coming up. NEXT UP: UNLV 18. South Carolina Gamecocks (6-3) RESULT: 17-9 win vs. Texas A&M PREVIOUS RANKING: 23 It was a defensive slugfest on Saturday, and for much of the day Texas A&M controlled the tempo of the game. The Aggies were able to run the ball fairly effectively, but the Gamecocks defense was good in its own end of the field. That resulted in a low-scoring affair, one in which starting quarterback LaNorris Sellers was banged up early. He sealed the deal late when he burst around the right side of the line for a 41-yard rushing touchdown with less than two minutes left to play, to the delight of a fired-up Williams-Brice Stadium. NEXT UP: @ Arkansas 17. Iowa Hawkeyes (7-2) RESULT: 24-10 win at Northwestern PREVIOUS RANKING: 21 Iowa had the luxury of facing Northwestern without its starting quarterback, Aidan Chiles . And his absence was certainly felt in the contest, even though backup Nicco Marchiol had some previous playing experience at West V

articles.title: Ole Miss’ Pete Golding takes responsibility for not overlooking Oklahoma amid CFP pursuit
articles.summary: Coach Pete Golding’s Ole Miss Rebels ran out of gas in a 42-7 blowout loss to Kirby Smart’s Georgia Bulldogs that was a huge Trinidad Chambliss letdown for one former NFL QB. Golding made a lifelong Ole Miss coaching declaration that had fans embracing him ahead of the game, but now t
articles._body: Coach Pete Golding’s Ole Miss Rebels ran out of gas in a 42-7 blowout loss to Kirby Smart’s Georgia Bulldogs that was a huge Trinidad Chambliss letdown for one former NFL QB . Golding made a lifelong Ole Miss coaching declaration that had fans embracing him ahead of the game, but now the Rebels are officially a downtrodden team with Oklahoma next on the docket. Golding addressed the Oklahoma game after the Georgia loss, warning his team ahead of Week 11’s forthcoming game, in comments shared by Brad Logan of Champions Network. “(Players) come here to compete for a National Championship. We worry too much about things we can’t control. It starts with me. It starts with Oklahoma. We have to get some things fixed.” The Rebels appeared tired after a long series of high profile games. Chambliss didn’t live up to the considerable hype surrounding him as he failed to pass for over 200 yards and he was intercepted once by Smart’s defense. Horatio Fields had eight catches for 96 yards to pace the passing game while Ole Miss was outrushed by a final tally of 295 yards to 66. The Rebels have a lot to fix before hitting the road and taking on Brent Venables’ Oklahoma Sooners in Norman. The Sooners started the year as a CFP contender but have run into several different buzzsaws in the SEC Conference and have fallen out of contention. The Rebels were mathematically eliminated from SEC title contention, and will now play for pride, and perhaps an outside shot at a CFP game. Golding’s time as Rebels head coach has been a positive one so far, but Week 10’s loss put a huge dark cloud over it heading into Week 11. articles.title: Michigan HC Kyle Whittingham admits to being ‘pretty disappointed’ in offense after loss to Michigan State
articles.summary: Michigan football’s offensive struggles played a significant role in its disappointing 15-6 loss against Michigan State, as Kyle Whittingham’s team failed to generate any consistent production throughout the rivalry matchup. Michigan’s head coach also expressed considerable frus
articles._body: Michigan football’s offensive struggles played a significant role in its disappointing 15-6 loss against Michigan State , as Kyle Whittingham’s team failed to generate any consistent production throughout the rivalry matchup. Michigan’s head coach also expressed considerable frustration with the team’s offensive performance. During his postgame press conference, Whittingham openly addressed the offense’s shortcomings and admitted that the Wolverines had plenty of problems to resolve. “Now the time to panic about the offense seems to be what it was,” Whittingham said. “It was very disappointing after we had played pretty effectively last week on offense. We had some production, some good production in a lot of areas last week. And there’s nothing productive about this game. “Really, I can’t come up with one positive offensively in this game. So we’re right back to the drawing board. And obviously gotta figure out our issues. Falls on me without, I’m not hiding from that at all. Anything that happens has got my name on it.” The Wolverines came into the rivalry game hoping to gain momentum, but their offensive shortcomings ultimately proved costly throughout the game. Michigan State’s defense created four turnovers and registered five sacks while limiting Michigan to only 54 rushing yards on 26 carries. Quarterback Tommy Carr struggled to get the offense going, completing 14 of 26 passes for 138 yards while throwing two interceptions. Meanwhile, Michigan State quarterback Alessio Milivojevic played a key role in helping his team maintain control despite entering the game with a questionable status . He finished with 188 passing yards on 21-of-32 attempts without committing a turnover. The loss marks another frustrating setback for the first-year head coach, as the Wolverines continue to struggle with consistency during the 2026 season. Michigan began the season with hopes of competing among the Big Ten’s top teams, but persistent offensive issues have repeatedly kept the program from capitalizing on its defensive performances. The Wolverines now face another challenging test next Saturday when they travel to Oregon. Kiffin is going through his first season as the Tigers’ head coach following a controversial exit from Ole Miss. He looks to achieve
articles._body: Lane Kiffin’s hardships against Alabama continue to live on as the No. 14 LSU Tigers suffered a 31-13 loss to the No. 5 Crimson Tide on Saturday night. Kiffin is going through his first season as the Tigers’ head coach following a controversial exit from Ole Miss. He looks to achieve the objective of leading LSU to the College Football Playoffs, one that seems to be harder than he initially anticipated. Going into the matchup, Kiffin had an 0-5 all-time record in his duels with Alabama. Unfortunately, that record fell to 0-6 as LSU had no answer for Alabama’s balanced attack throughout the course of the game. Lane Kiffin's struggles vs. Alabama continue pic.twitter.com/Y4o2rHc26G — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) November 8, 2026 How Lane Kiffin, LSU performed against Alabama Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers have some self-reflecting to do after losing to Alabama. Falling to 6-3 this season, they will need to win out to have an outside chance of being in CFP contention. Both teams traded blows throughout the contest, seeing Alabama up 17-13 after three quarters. It wasn’t until the fourth period when the Crimson Tide took full control, outscoring LSU 14-0 in the last 15 minutes of regulation. Sam Leavitt failed to record any type of touchdown in the game, frequently throwing the ball to receivers for potential scoring opportunities but to no avail. He completed 35 out of 47 passes for 380 yards and an interception. Dilin Jones led the run game with 17 carries for 56 yards and a touchdown while catching seven passes for 36 yards. Jackson Harris commanded receivers with 11 catches for 166 yards, while Trey’Dez Green caught 10 passes for 85 yards. LSU fell to a 6-3 overall record this season, including a 3-3 display in SEC action. They sit at sixth place in the conference standings, being above the Missouri Tigers and the Tennessee Volunteers while trailing the Texas Longhorns and the Ole Miss Rebels. The No. 14 Tigers will look to bounce back in their next matchup, remaining at home. They host the No. 7 Texas Longhorns in Week 11 as kickoff commences on Nov. 14. The highly regarded shortstop, who previously emerged as a potential centerpiece in blockbuster trade discussions, continues to attract attention as one of baseball’s brightest young talents. Walcott enters the event after overcoming a significant injury setback earlier this year. The Bahamas native underwent elbow surgery but returned to competitive action during the fall season. His powerful swing and impressive athleticism have helped establish him among baseball’s elite prospects. Texas continues monitoring his development as he gains experience against advanced competition. The Rangers have also evaluated other promising prospects as potential trade assets, highlighting the importance of their developing farm system. For Walcott, Sunday’s showcase provides another opportunity to demonstrate his abilities against highly regarded players from other organizations. The event also offers fans an early look at prospects who could eventually become major league contributors. Strong performances can generate excitement, although one exhibition cannot determine a player’s readiness. But in NFL great Jason Witten’s first game as offensive play-caller, the Sooners bounced back to beat Florida, 23-7. Sooners head coach Brent Vena
articles._body: The Oklahoma football team suffered a scathing 42-25 loss to South Carolina , which resulted in the firing of offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle. But in NFL great Jason Witten’s first game as offensive play-caller, the Sooners bounced back to beat Florida, 23-7. Sooners head coach Brent Venables appreciated that his team showed some pride by responding after such a tough loss, particularly on the defensive end. “After the blistering we took last week, to see our guys respond… I value that more than anything,” Venables said, per Brandon Drumm. Oklahoma had a tough time against South Carolina star LaNorris Sellers as he led the Gamecocks to 521 total yards of offense. However, they had a much easier time against Florida quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. The Sooners defense limited the Gators to just 203 total yards on offense and picked off Jones twice. Meanwhile, the Oklahoma offense performed reasonably well in Witten’s play-calling debut . Quarterback John Mateer had 207 yards and two touchdowns, and he also rushed for a season-high 56 yards. Florida has been having some major offensive issues over the last few weeks, so it’s important to take the Oklahoma defense’s success against them with a grain of salt. Nevertheless, Venables can take heart in the fact that he has not lost the locker room yet. Venables will be hoping the Florida defensive performance doesn’t turn out to be a fluke when the Sooners take on Ole Miss next week. The Rebels are coming off their own disastrous offensive performance in their crushing 42-7 loss to Georgia.
