articles.title: Nets’ Egor Demin remains out for back-to-back following leg injury evaluation
articles.summary: Egor Demin will remain out for the Brooklyn Nets’ matchup against the Dallas Mavericks on Sunday, according to head coach Jordi Fernandez. Demin has missed the Nets’ last five games due to a right leg bone bruise, including a 124-121 loss to the Atlanta Hawks on Saturday. Demin suffer
articles._body: Egor Demin will remain out for the Brooklyn Nets’ matchup against the Dallas Mavericks on Sunday, according to head coach Jordi Fernandez. Demin has missed the Nets’ last five games due to a right leg bone bruise, including a 124-121 loss to the Atlanta Hawks on Saturday. Demin suffered the injury during an Oct. 27 loss to the Boston Celtics at TD Garden. The Nets announced on Oct. 29 that Demin would be reevaluated in one week . Fernandez said on Saturday that the Brooklyn sophomore will be reevaluated during the team’s off days following Sunday’s Mavericks tilt. “[Egor is] progressing well. He’s on the court. He’s not going to play today or tomorrow, and then we’ll go from there,” Fernandez told the New York Post’s Brian Lewis. Demin was one of the Nets’ few bright spots during last year’s tanking season. The 2025 No. 8 pick was one of three rookies last season to average over 10.0 points and 3.0 assists with a true shooting percentage above 56.0, alongside Charlotte Hornets guard Kon Knueppel and San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper. However, he got off to an underwhelming start to his rookie campaign. Egor Demin remains out for Nets vs. Mavericks due to right leg bone bruise Rob Gray-Imagn Images Demin averaged 9.7 points, 2.7 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 2.3 turnovers on 8-of-26 (30.8 percent) shooting from the field and 6-of-19 (31.6 percent) from three across Brooklyn’s first three games. He played 10 minutes during the Celtics matchup before injuring his leg, posting two points, one rebound, two assists and one turnover on 1-of-3 shooting from the field and 0-of-2 from three. Demin entered the season with relatively high expectations following a standout Summer League. The Russian guard posted the NBA’s worst two-point percentage among all players 6-foot-8 or taller last season. However, after adding significant muscle during the offseason, Demin showed dramatic improvement as a driver at Summer League. The 20-year-old converted 22 of 29 two-point attempts across five outings. Yet, Demin’s start to the 2026-27 season looked more like a return to the three-point-dependent scoring repertoire of his rookie season. The BYU product has converted just 3 of 8 two-point attempts with seven free-throw attempts across his first four games. Still, Demin’s return should provide an offensive boost for a Nets team that ranks 25th on that end of the floor. The Brooklyn guard will have two more days to recover following the Mavericks matchup. His next chance to suit up will come when the Nets continue a four-game road trip against the New Orleans Pelicans on Wednesday. Rookie point guard Mikel Brown Jr. will also miss Sunday’s matchup vs. the Mavericks. The No. 6 pick remains on a minutes restriction to start the year and has not yet been cleared for back-to-backs, per Fernandez. Brown played 25 minutes during the Nets’ loss to the Hawks on Saturday. The 20-year-old scored 13 fourth-quarter points on 5-of-9 shooting from the field and 3-of-4 from three. That came after he missed his first seven shots to start the game. Brown has averaged 12.9 points on 34.6 percent shooting from the field and 31.1 percent from three, with 3.9 assists and 2.1 turnovers per game across seven appearances to start the year. He’s played 23.2 minutes per game, the lowest of any of the top six picks from the 2026 draft. Brown could return alongside Demin when the Nets travel to New Orleans to face the Pelicans on Wednesday at Smoothie King Center. articles.title: Michigan fans demand Kyle Whittingham’s job after shocking loss to Michigan State
articles.summary: Coach Kyle Whittingham’s odyssey with the Michigan Wolverines looks in serious jeopardy after a bland, borderline embarrassing rivalry game loss to Pat Fitzgerald’s Michigan State Spartans that came after injury concerns dogged MSU’s starting quarterback Alessio Milivojevic. Sta
articles._body: Coach Kyle Whittingham’s odyssey with the Michigan Wolverines looks in serious jeopardy after a bland, borderline embarrassing rivalry game loss to Pat Fitzgerald’s Michigan State Spartans that came after injury concerns dogged MSU’s starting quarterback Alessio Milivojevic . Starting QB Tommy Carr lit up Rutgers and got an endorsement from Whittingham , then proceeded to play some of the worst football of his young career in a 15-6 loss. After the game, fans demanded Whittingham’s ouster as they also debated whether or not high priced offensive coordinator Jason Beck should be fired immediately. “Kyle Whittingham should do the right thing and resign tomorrow, if not, fire him on Monday,” one fan said . “I have nothing to say but ‘Fire Kyle Whittingham,’ and do it NOW, not later,” another said . Fans were in a disgusted mood as they continued to vent their frustrations. “U of M shouldn’t even have to fire Kyle Whittingham. He should resign. He is incompetent. You can listen to his press conference and infer that he is not mentally equipped to do the job. Nice guy. Also a buffoon,” another said . Whittingham was asked about potentially firing Beck , and gave a direct answer. “Not right now. Not as I’m sitting here at this podium, no. But at some point you’ve got to have results. It’s a result-driven business, and it’s a bottom line business. I’ll evaluate everything after the season and determine what the best course of action is. But not right here, right now.” Fans were not amused as they continued their common refrain after a humiliating loss to a Spartans team that was just 2-6 coming in. “Fire Whittingham. Fire Beck,” one said . Another mentioned that the Wolverines lost to Minnesota for the first time since 1977, went 0-2 to start the Big Ten for the first time since 1967, and were shut out in the first half of three straight home games for the first time since 1934. “Kyle Whittingham is single-handedly ruining Michigan. FIRE HIM,” they wrote . Carr finished with 138 yards passing and two interceptions while five-star freshman running back Savion Hiter added a virtually meaningless touchdown at the end of the game to make it 15-6. Michigan’s offense is historically bad, and the team isn’t much better. Whittingham must win a few more games to save face before the end of the season or risk getting the axe, perhaps sooner rather than later. articles._body: OKLAHOMA CITY — Head coach Mark Daigneault and the Oklahoma City Thunder captured their fourth straight win in a 114-75 victory over the Washington Wizards, with Jared McCain leading the bench in scoring. After Ajay Mitchell scored a career-high 35 points against the Memphis Grizzlies as part of the first leg of a road/home back-to-back, McCain finished with 19 points on 8-for-10 shooting, including a perfect 6-of-6 from inside the 3-point arc. McCain also finished with five rebounds, two assists, one steal, and one block on Saturday, which didn’t go unnoticed as Daigneault highlighted the third-year guard’s performance during his postgame press conference. “A lot of it is what’s your identity if you took shooting off the table. What are you left with as a player? And I think we got a lot of guys on the team that model that well. I think Caruso, obviously, is in the Hall of Fame for that. Hartenstein, in the last two nights, he’s scored four points in two games — two points last night/two points tonight. Last night, we won his minutes by 31 points. Tonight, he had 14 rebounds. We won his minutes by 25. “That’s a great example of an impactful winning player that can do it in all the other ways outside of the counting stats with points. And Jared, younger player, relatively new, you got guys like them, Kenrich; these guys that do all the invisible stuff. It’s very contagious. And it brings value to those things. A guy like Jared has done a great job, despite the fact that he is great scorer and a great shooter, of focusing on those things. It’s a shoutout to him, but it’s a shoutout to the environment we have in our locker room,” Daigneault concluded. “A lot of it is what’s your identity if you took shooting off the table. What are you left with as a player? And I think we have a lot of guys on the team that model that well. I think Caruso, obviously, is in the Hall of Fame for that. Hartenstein, in the last two nights, he’s… pic.twitter.com/8vGsf8vB5D — Josue Pavón (@Joe_Sway) November 8, 2026 In his first full season with the Thunder, Jared McCain, who was traded by the Philadelphia 76ers mid-season in 2025-26, is finding his stride in Oklahoma City. Embracing the Thunder’s culture, McCain spent parts of his offseason training with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander in Canada, Chet Holmgren in Los Angeles, and Kenrich Williams in Fort Worth, Texas. Amid a 0-for-18 shooting slump, which ended in the Thunder’s 124-116 win against the Cleveland Cavs on Wednesday, Jared McCain has found other ways to make his presence felt on both ends of the floor. For McCain, Isaiah Joe, who the Thunder traded to the Detroit Pistons over the summer, set an example early in his tenure with Oklahoma City. “Isaiah, he helped me a lot. Any questions I had, defensively/offensively, we talked a lot about being a shooter, and how that works in this league,” McCain said after Saturday’s win. “There’s going to be times when you missed shots. It happened. It might happen again. It’s something that you have to just work through. I think staying confident is huge, but being able to affect the game defensively, rebounding, something; you gotta find something to affect the game. “That usually gets yourself going on the other end, anyways. So, for me, I just try to rebounds, and play super hard on defense. Now I can continue that, and use both. I think I’m getting better on the defensive end as well. So, being able to contribute on both side is huge, especially if you’re not making shots because you gotta find a way to stay on the floor.” Head coach Mark Daigneault is seeing his Thunder team fight through the adversity of a team that’s competing without three members of its starting lineup continue to find a way to win. They improved to 8-2 on the regular season, and 5-2 since losing Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace, and Holmgren to their respective long-term injuries. The Thunder will embark on a four-game road trip that starts with a back-to-back against the Portland Blazers on Tuesday. articles.title: Miami HC Mario Cristobal ‘very disappointed’ with Elija Lofton incomplete pass call
articles.summary: Notre Dame defeated No. 1 Miami, handing the Hurricanes their first loss of the season and strengthening its College Football Playoff case with a statement-making 31-24 win at home. Miami became the fourth AP No. 1-ranked team to suffer a defeat this season. However, beyond the disappointing resu
articles._body: Notre Dame defeated No. 1 Miami, handing the Hurricanes their first loss of the season and strengthening its College Football Playoff case with a statement-making 31-24 win at home. Miami became the fourth AP No. 1-ranked team to suffer a defeat this season. However, beyond the disappointing result, head coach Mario Cristobal was particularly frustrated with the officiating decision that overturned Elijah Lofton’s apparent touchdown reception. During his postgame press conference, Cristobal expressed his disappointment with the officials’ ruling. “Really, really disappointed that they negated Elijah Lofton’s touchdown with two hands on the ball, two feet in the mouse,” Cristobal said. “So, like we told our team before we left Miami, do not leave it in the hands of the officials, and that’s what you’re going to get out of you. “So, aside from that, a very hard-fought game. Congratulations to Notre Dame for winning the game, and very disappointed in the way that was called, winning the game on the line and clear possession of a football inbounds.” Lofton came close to making a game-tying touchdown reception that would have brought Miami within one point at 31-30 with 3:36 remaining. He appeared to secure a fourth-down pass in the end zone and get both feet down, but Notre Dame’s Luke Talich managed to knock the ball loose. Officials subsequently ruled that Lofton had not completed the catch. The victory moved Notre Dame to an 8-1 record , while Miami also dropped to 8-1 after suffering its first defeat of the season. The loss does not eliminate Miami from College Football Playoff contention, but it leaves the Hurricanes with little margin for error during the remainder of the regular season. Miami will aim to bounce back when it hosts Duke next Saturday, while Notre Dame prepares to welcome Boston College as it looks to build on one of its most significant wins of the season. articles._body: Robert Griffin III has seen enough from the Utah Utes. After Utah held off BYU 28-20 in the Holy War on Saturday at Rice-Eccles Stadium , the former Heisman Trophy winner made a bold case for the Utes. “Utah should be the #1 team in the country,” Griffin wrote on X, formerly Twitter . The Utes certainly have the résumé to back it up. Saturday’s win improved Utah to 9-0, marking the program’s first 9-0 start since 2008. The Utes also extended their winning streak to 15 games, the longest active run in the country. Griffin’s take came on a chaotic night at the top of the College Football Playoff rankings. Top-ranked Miami suffered its first loss of the season , falling 31-24 to Notre Dame in South Bend. Georgia, the other team ranked ahead of the Utes, took care of business with a 42-7 rout of Ole Miss , but Utah, which entered the weekend at No. 3, still has an unblemished record to point to. The Utes did not make it easy on themselves against their rivals, though. Utah jumped out to a 14-0 lead before BYU clawed its way back into the game. Quarterback Devon Dampier steadied the ship, completing 14 of 26 passes for 177 yards and two touchdowns, both to Braden Pegan. He was just as dangerous with his legs, rushing 20 times for 89 yards and two more scores. Utah’s defense came up big as well. The Utes did not record a sack, but they kept BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier under pressure and picked him off four times. Nate Ritchie sealed the win with an interception in the end zone with two seconds left. The victory carried extra weight for Utah, which had dropped three straight games to BYU in the rivalry. It also came in the first Holy War in which both teams were ranked in the top 10, with BYU entering at No. 7. Morgan Scalley has made quite the impression in his first season as head coach since taking over for Kyle Whittingham. Utah now sits firmly in control of its path to a first College Football Playoff berth. Whether the selection committee agrees with Griffin remains to be seen. The Utes will look to stay perfect when they visit the Arizona Wildcats next Saturday. articles._body: In his first game serving as Oklahoma ‘s interim offensive coordinator following Ben Arbuckle ‘s firing earlier this week, elevated tight ends coach Jason Witten helped lead the Sooners to a 23-7 road victory over No. 24 Florida Saturday night. Following the win, Witten called the game ‘maybe the greatest moment’ he’s ever had in his illustrious football career. “Tonight was pretty special. In all the years I’ve been around football, maybe the greatest moment I’ve had,” Witten said, via SoonerScoop . Certainly some strong words from Witten, who has gone down in history as one of the best tight ends to ever step foot in the NFL. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Oklahoma ‘s disappointing 2026 campaign hit a breaking point in last week’s 42-25 home loss to South Carolina , which led to head coach Brent Venables shaking up his coaching staff. The Sooners fell to 4-4 on the season, with their less-than-stellar offense being one of the major factors. “I have decided to make a change at offensive coordinator,” Venables said in a statement last Monday. “My responsibility is to the whole team and what I believe is best for us right now. We need a change. I believe we still have meaningful opportunities ahead and a responsibility to maximize them. Our expectations remain high and our commitment to meeting them is unwavering.” Witten, who was hired in Jan. as OU’s tight ends coach, was elevated to the vacant OC position following Arbuckle’s firing. Witten had previously never held any position on any college football coaching staff. Just 11 months later, however, his first game as an offensive coordinator in the SEC led to a road win over Florida in ‘The Swamp’. Oklahoma improves to 5-4 following its win over No. 24 Florida Oklahoma took an early 3-0 lead Saturday night, and increased that lead to 10 thanks to a three-yard touchdown pass from John Mateer to Hayden Hansen six minutes into the second quarter. Florida pulled within three following a Jadan Baugh 15-yard touchdown run, but was ultimately unable to ever take the lead. The Sooners used a Tate Sandell 48-yard field goal to pad the lead back to six points heading into the half, and a six-yard passing touchdown from Mateer to Isaiah Sategna to cement the win late in the fourth quarter. That score, which gave Oklahoma a 20-7 lead, capped off an impressive 20-play, 89-yard, 12:45 drive. “Super proud of our team. Really complete performance for us,” Venables said postgame. “Very clean football. Complimentary football. I thought we really dominated the line of scrimmage, and it was just an incredible efficient football game. That was our best four quarters of football as a football team.” Oklahoma improved to 5-4 (3-3) on the season with the win. It will close out the regular season with games against No. 10 Ole Miss , Texas A&M , and Missouri . It takes just one win for the Sooners in that span to clinch bowl eligibility for the 27th consecutive season.

articles.summary: Notre Dame fans had every reason to celebrate on Saturday night, and the Fighting Irish made sure to add a little extra salt to Miami’s wounds in the process. After Notre Dame knocked off No. 1 Miami 31-24 at Notre Dame Stadium, fans poured onto the field to celebrate the massive upset. As the cr
articles._body: Notre Dame fans had every reason to celebrate on Saturday night , and the Fighting Irish made sure to add a little extra salt to Miami’s wounds in the process. After Notre Dame knocked off No. 1 Miami 31-24 at Notre Dame Stadium, fans poured onto the field to celebrate the massive upset. As the crowd stormed the turf, the stadium blasted the Scorpions’ 1984 classic “Rock You Like A Hurricane,” a not-so-subtle jab at the defeated Hurricanes, according to Ross Dellenger of Yahoo Sports . They’re storming the field and playing “Rock You Like A Hurricane” in South Bend pic.twitter.com/kO2sm5hGgq — Ross Dellenger (@RossDellenger) November 8, 2026 It was a fitting soundtrack for one of the biggest wins of the season in South Bend, and at least one famous fan saw it coming. Actor Jason Sudeikis, the celebrity guest picker on ESPN’s “College GameDay” that morning, guaranteed an Irish upset . Marcus Freeman’s squad controlled most of the night despite missing several key defenders . Spencer Porath opened the scoring with a 44-yard field goal, and Jordan Faison hauled in a touchdown from quarterback CJ Carr early in the second quarter . Micah Gilbert then capped a two-minute drill with an 18-yard scoring grab before halftime, as the Irish built a 17-3 lead at the break. Gilbert’s 20-yard touchdown grab in the third quarter pushed the lead to 24-3, but Miami did not go away quietly. Heisman Trophy contender Darian Mensah led a comeback charge, throwing a pair of touchdown passes, including a 12-yard strike to Elija Lofton that capped a 75-yard drive, to cut the deficit to 24-17. Luke Talich then came up with a key interception of Mensah near midfield , and Nolan James Jr. punched in a 1-yard touchdown run to make it 31-17. Miami added a late score, but Notre Dame held on as time expired to seal the upset . The win was especially sweet given what happened last season. Miami beat Notre Dame 27-24 in the 2025 season opener, a loss that ultimately cost the Irish in the College Football Playoff picture. With the victory, Notre Dame improved to 8-1 on the season. The Irish now have nine all-time wins over the AP’s No. 1 team. Miami, meanwhile, suffered its first loss of the season and fell to 8-1. Notre Dame will look to keep the momentum going when it hosts Boston College next Saturday. articles.summary: Coach Marcus Freeman’s Notre Dame Fighting Irish took the fight to the No. 1-ranked Miami Hurricanes in Week 10 action in South Bend, getting a huge game from QB CJ Carr en route to the win. Miami Heisman candidate Darian Mensah got blasted and stuffed on a goal line run that helped give ND
articles._body: Coach Marcus Freeman’s Notre Dame Fighting Irish took the fight to the No. 1-ranked Miami Hurricanes in Week 10 action in South Bend, getting a huge game from QB CJ Carr en route to the win . Miami Heisman candidate Darian Mensah got blasted and stuffed on a goal line run that helped give ND the win and improved Carr’s own Heisman standing. After the game, Freeman spoke with NBC Sports’ Kathyrn Tappen in front of a sea of green and gold Irish backers, revealing his good mood . “I’m happy for this university, I’m happy for our players, you know, there’s a lot of support from Notre Dame nation and this is a special moment for them. I’m so happy for our players, because they put in a lot of work to achieve this. They’re a dang good football team and they beat a dang good football team. When it mattered the most we executed, it got a little ugly in that second half…They battle through (the struggle), and they executed when it mattered most.” Carr and Mensah both went over the 300-yard mark but Mensah threw an interception and failed to lead his team to the win. The Irish made celebrity guest picker Jason Sudeikis look good after he guaranteed victory against the top team in the country, and are sure to pick up more fans nationwide after a huge performance. Micah Gilbert was Carr’s top target in the passing game, finishing with 98 yards and two touchdowns on a magical night in South Bend, Indiana. The Fighting Irish redeemed themselves after a tough early season loss to the BYU Cougars, and now have a chance to march toward the College Football Playoff as one of the nation’s undisputed best teams. articles.title: Bill Simmons boldly declares Warriors star Stephen Curry is ‘so so back’ after OT win over Magic
articles.summary: Bill Simmons has seen enough. After Stephen Curry torched the Orlando Magic in the Golden State Warriors’ 126-119 overtime victory on Saturday night, the longtime NBA commentator and founder of The Ringer made his feelings known in all caps. “STEPH NEVER LEFT BUT REGARDLESS STEPH IS SO SO SO BACK
articles._body: Bill Simmons has seen enough. After Stephen Curry torched the Orlando Magic in the Golden State Warriors’ 126-119 overtime victory on Saturday night , the longtime NBA commentator and founder of The Ringer made his feelings known in all caps. “STEPH NEVER LEFT BUT REGARDLESS STEPH IS SO SO SO BACK,” Simmons posted on X . Simmons made sure to cover his bases. Curry, now 38, has never really fallen off, and there is plenty of evidence to back that up. Last season, he passed Michael Jordan for the most 40-point games by a player after turning 30 . On Saturday, he added another milestone to his resume, setting the NBA record for the most 40-point games by a player 35 years or older . Still, it is easy to see why Simmons felt the need to shout about it. Curry poured in 41 points against Orlando while missing just six of his 19 shots. He hit half of his 10 attempts from beyond the arc and did not miss any of his 10 free throws, chipping in six rebounds and six assists for good measure. The two-time MVP also delivered in the clutch. With the game going to an extra period, Curry helped the Warriors take control late in overtime to fend off a pesky Magic team led by Franz Wagner, who finished with 30 points and 11 assists. Saturday’s outburst was no one-off, either. Curry has been on a heater during Golden State’s winning streak, which now sits at seven games. He scored 34 points in a win over the Phoenix Suns earlier in the week, then needed only 28 minutes to rack up 29 points against the Miami Heat on Thursday . That surge has completely flipped the Warriors’ season. Golden State dropped its first three games of the year , and the slow start raised plenty of questions about the group. Since then, Steve Kerr’s group has not lost, climbing to 7-3. Curry is not doing it alone, of course. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has been a revelation , and he backed up his star teammate with 23 points against the Magic. The Warriors will look for their eighth straight win on Monday against the New Orleans Pelicans. Based on how Curry is playing, Simmons might want to keep the caps lock on. Warriors make record history not seen since 1951

articles._body: Another spectacular performance from Steph Curry and another thrilling finish for the Golden State Warriors. Golden State has plenty of reasons to believe in its chances of making a deep playoff run after defeating the Orlando Magic 126-119 in overtime on Saturday. The victory marks another positive result for the Warriors, who have turned their disappointing start to the season into an impressive winning streak while also making NBA history. According to Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints, the Warriors have become the first team in NBA history since the 1950-51 Boston Celtics to open a season with an 0-3 record before winning their next seven consecutive games. The Warriors appeared to have the game firmly under control in the first half, establishing a 12-point lead after putting up 31 points in the opening quarter. However, Orlando refused to back down and slowly fought its way back into the game before eventually forcing overtime. Though Golden State let its comfortable advantage slip away, the team stepped up when it mattered most. The win moved the Warriors to a 7-3 record. Curry led the way with 41 points, six rebounds and six assists, shooting an impressive 13-of-19 from the field. Beyond Curry’s scoring efforts, Golden State also benefited from several important contributions from its supporting cast. Yaxel Lendeborg recorded 23 points, eight rebounds and three assists, going 9-of-15 from the field while knocking down two three-pointers. Brandin Podziemski also made a significant impact, contributing 15 points and seven rebounds while connecting on 4-of-5 attempts from beyond the arc. Meanwhile, Draymond Green directed the Warriors’ offense effectively, recording 13 assists and six rebounds while adding two points. Golden State will aim to maintain its impressive momentum in its upcoming games as the team continues to strengthen its position as a competitive force in the Western Conference. articles.title: Georgia’s Kirby Smart reveals the most impressive aspect of win over Ole Miss
articles.summary: Kirby Smart’s Georgia football team made their top-10 clash against Ole Miss look like an absolute mismatch as the No. 2 Bulldogs put a 42-7 beatdown on the No. 10 Rebels. The Bulldogs defense was pitching a shutout against Ole Miss until the fourth quarter, when Shekai Mills-Knight scored
articles._body: Kirby Smart’s Georgia football team made their top-10 clash against Ole Miss look like an absolute mismatch as the No. 2 Bulldogs put a 42-7 beatdown on the No. 10 Rebels. The Bulldogs defense was pitching a shutout against Ole Miss until the fourth quarter, when Shekai Mills-Knight scored a consolation touchdown. However, Smart wasn’t disappointed despite the defense losing the shutout. Instead, he gave them props for sticking to the gameplan . “Great job by the defensive staff. Kids bought into the plan. We talked about sticking to the plan. They stuck to the plan. Did a great job,” Smart said in his post-game interview. The Georgia defense completely shut down the explosive Ole Miss offense, limiting them to just 252 total yards. Trinidad Chambliss had arguably the toughest night of his career, completing just 18 of 34 attempts for only 170 yards with one interception and four sacks. He was also held without a touchdown pass for the first time as Ole Miss’ starting quarterback. On the other side, the Bulldogs offense also delivered a major beatdown. The Georgia ground game ran all over the Rebels, finishing with 295 yards and two touchdowns. And quarterback Gunner Stockton threw four touchdown passes, three of which going to wide receiver Talyn Taylor. After Miami’s loss to Notre Dame , Georgia looks poised to reclaim the No. 1 spot in the AP Poll. And with back-to-back dominant performances against Florida and Ole Miss (15 total points, 504 total yards allowed), the Bulldogs defense is rounding into shape at the right time. The Bulldogs will look to put on another impressive performance when they host Missouri in Athens next week. articles._body: Alabama running back Daniel Hill celebrated the Crimson Tide’s 31-13 road win over LSU in Death Valley on Saturday by bringing out the belt and striking a Tigers sideline pad. The celebration came after No. 5 Alabama pulled away from No. 14 LSU to claim a much-needed victory and improve its College Football Playoff outlook. Bama brought out the belt after blowing out LSU in Death Valley pic.twitter.com/JzNwx1Gige — ESPN College Football (@ESPNCFB) November 8, 2026 The Crimson Tide found themselves trailing 13-10 with 2:20 remaining in the third quarter after Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt helped his team take the lead with an 11-play, 90-yard drive capped by running back Dilin Jones’ 5-yard touchdown run. However, Alabama responded quickly, needing just 2:08 to regain control. Quarterback Keelon Russell connected with tight end Josh Ford for a touchdown after wide receiver Rico Scott produced a 57-yard reception and run to set up the score. Russell tossed three touchdown passes despite playing through an ankle injury. He finished with 206 passing yards, finding Ford for a 7-yard score, wideout Cederian Morgan for a 25-yard touchdown and wide receiver Kaleb Edwards for a 4-yard reception. All three scoring passes came after LSU had moved ahead. The Crimson Tide entered the fourth quarter with a 17-13 advantage before extending their lead. After forcing the Tigers to punt from their own 16-yard line, Russell connected with Morgan on the following play for another touchdown. He later found Edwards for his third scoring pass, completing the 21-point unanswered stretch that put the game beyond LSU’s reach. The Tigers failed to capitalize on their opportunities, going 0-for-4 on fourth-down attempts and scoring only one touchdown on four trips inside the red zone. Leavitt completed 35 of 47 passes for 380 yards but threw an interception to linebacker Luke Metz and couldn’t record a passing touchdown. LSU also managed just 77 rushing yards on 33 attempts. The triumph improved Alabama’s record to 7-2 overall and 5-2 in SEC play, keeping the Crimson Tide squarely in the playoff conversation. The Tigers, meanwhile, fell to 6-3 and 3-3, leaving Lane Kiffin’s team with considerably slimmer postseason hopes. The Crimson Tide have now won 16 of their last 20 meetings with LSU and seven of their previous eight visits to Tiger Stadium. Alabama will next travel to face Vanderbilt on Saturday, with kickoff scheduled for 12:45 p.m. ET on the SEC Network. articles.title: Warriors star Stephen Curry leads Golden State to dominant OT win over Magic
articles.summary: Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors just keep finding ways to win. The Warriors outlasted the Orlando Magic 126-119 in overtime on Saturday night at Chase Center, as Curry delivered yet another vintage performance to extend the team’s winning streak to seven games. The two-time MVP was si
articles._body: Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors just keep finding ways to win. The Warriors outlasted the Orlando Magic 126-119 in overtime on Saturday night at Chase Center, as Curry delivered yet another vintage performance to extend the team’s winning streak to seven games . The two-time MVP was simply unstoppable , finishing with 41 points on a blistering 13-of-19 shooting from the field. He knocked down five of his 10 3-point attempts and went a perfect 10-of-10 from the free-throw line, while also adding six rebounds and six assists. The performance also put Curry in the record books . He now has the most 40-point games by a player 35 years or older in NBA history. The superstar guard came through when the Warriors needed him most. With Golden State clinging to a 120-118 lead in the final minute of overtime, Curry was still going at the Magic defense, having already reached the 41-point mark, as Golden State pulled away for the win. It was the latest in a string of big nights for Curry during the streak. He dropped 34 points against the Phoenix Suns last Monday and followed that up with 29 points in just 28 minutes in Thursday’s blowout win over the Miami Heat . Curry had plenty of help against Orlando, too. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg continued his impressive start with 23 points on 9-of-15 shooting, along with eight rebounds and three blocks. Brandin Podziemski chipped in 15 points and seven rebounds, knocking down four of his five 3-point attempts, while Draymond Green orchestrated the offense with 13 assists. As a team, the Warriors shot 53.8% from the field and 46.9% from deep, and they dished out 32 assists. The Magic made the Warriors work for it. Franz Wagner led Orlando with 30 points and 11 assists, while Wendell Carter Jr. posted 19 points and 11 rebounds . Tristan da Silva added 19 points, and Anthony Black and Jamal Cain each scored 18. Orlando also dominated the offensive glass with 24 offensive rebounds, but its 38.1% shooting from the field proved costly. The win improved Golden State to 7-3 on the season, a remarkable turnaround after the team opened the year with three straight losses . Since then, the Warriors have not lost a game. Curry and the Warriors will look to make it eight in a row when they close out their homestand against the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday. articles._body: Georgia football entered Oxford with a chance to snap Ole Miss’s 16-game home winning streak . Coach Kirby Smart and the Bulldogs obliterated it. And in the process catapulted back into the No. 1 conversation. The No. 2 Bulldogs rolled to the 42-7 trouncing at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium Saturday. And put together that dominating performance on an evening No. 1 Miami went down against Notre Dame. That means the Bulldogs will reignite theories of claiming the top once again. Georgia previously lost its top spot after taking the stunning 27-20 home loss to Auburn back on Oct. 17. The Bulldogs didn’t even need quarterback Gunner Stockton to overwhelm the Rebels through the air. He threw only 15 passes total, completing nine of it. But Stockton tossed four touchdown throws; three landing into the hands of wide receiver Talyn Taylor including the 58-yarder to spark the rout. 58-yard TD strike to Talyn Taylor : ABC pic.twitter.com/4PIjBnfYCb — Georgia Football (@GeorgiaFootball) November 8, 2026 Stockton ended his night tallying 186 yards. Taylor finished with four receptions for 140 yards and scored three times. Ethan Barbour caught the fourth touchdown throw from Stockton, which was a short three-yard connection. Meanwhile, Smart leaned into the familiar run-first identity that’s been a staple of past Bulldog teams. Running back Nate Frazier wore down Ole Miss with 107 yards on 16 carries. Finally, Smart’s area of expertise defense delivered a brilliant game plan that frustrated Ole Miss star quarterback Trinidad Chambliss , who entered this game overhearing NFL Draft buzz. But Chambliss finished 18-of-34 passing for 170 yards and never tossed one touchdown, while getting picked off once. Running back Shekai Mills-Knight prevented the shutout by scoring from eight yards out in the fourth quarter. But Georgia has potentially ended the Rebels’ pursuit of making it back to the CFP. All while Georgia faces moving back to No. 1. The post Georgia dominates Ole Miss in massive SEC win appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles._body: Coach Marcus Freeman’s Notre Dame Fighting Irish welcomed Mario Cristobal’s Miami Hurricanes to Notre Dame Stadium in South Bend, Indiana and rode 14 second-quarter points to a 31-24 win on a day when Darian Mensah was demolished in a goal-line stand . Irish QB CJ Carr connected with Jordan Faison on a spectacular play that gave the home team a 10-0 lead they wouldn’t look back on. Notre Dame was ranked 11th in the CFP Selection Committee’s latest poll, but knocked off the Committee’s top team after staving off a wild second-half comeback. The Irish win capped a day of upsets among Top 25 teams with the lower-ranked team winning four of seven matchups. Carr staked his claim for the Heisman Trophy with 319 passing yards and three touchdowns while Micah Gilbert added 98 receiving yards and two scores through the air, showing the improved depth of Freeman’s team. The Fighting Irish might have made the CFP with a loss, but they didn’t want to leave anything to chance, as they showed in their huge win over the top team in all the land on Saturday, November 7. The Irish made Jason Sudeikis look good as they fulfilled his pre-game prediction . Notre Dame slightly outgained Miami by a tally of 412 yards to 403 while also winning the time of possession war by a slight margin. Everything came together swimmingly for Freeman’s team as they staked their claim as one of the nation’s best teams, avenging their earlier season upset loss at the hands of the BYU Cougars in Utah. articles._body: It was a week full of big rivalry games in college football , and Air Force pulled off a big 24-21 victory over Army. Air Force quarterback Evan Medders connected with Simon Kibbee early in the fourth quarter to score the game-winning touchdown. As Brett McMurphy of On3 noted on X, formerly Twitter, the win means Air Force has claimed the Commander-in-Chief’s Trophy for the first time since 2022 . It was also their record 22nd CIC Trophy. After a scoreless first quarter, Air Force struck with two quick scores to start the second quarter. Running back Kemper Hodgers scored a three-yard touchdown to put the Falcons up 10-0. Army hit back with a touchdown of their own, but Medders ran for another score with seconds left in the half to reestablish the Falcons’ 10-point lead at the half. The Black Knights stormed back in the second half with back-to-back touchdowns to take a 21-17 lead. However, the Falcons hit back in the fourth to reclaim the lead and held on for the victory. Hodges had 119 yards to lead the Falcons rushing attack that went for 260 yards. Medders threw for 84 yards and rushed for 59 yards as he had a passing and rushing score of his own. On the other side, Godspower Nwawuihe and Bryson Luter paced the Black Knights with 82 and 81 rushing yards, respectively. At 7-2, the Falcons are still on course to get their first double-digit win season since 2022 under long-time Air Force football coach Troy Calhoun . They have home games left against San Jose State and UTEP before finishing the regular season at New Mexico. Interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten played a significant role in the Sooners’ victory, e
articles._body: Oklahoma football pulled off an impressive 23-7 road win in their game against Florida , ending its losing streak in their Week 10 college football matchup on Saturday at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. Interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten played a significant role in the Sooners’ victory, earning recognition from popular sports analyst Skip Bayless. Witten, who joined Oklahoma’s coaching staff in this year as the tight ends coach , received his first opportunity to call plays at the college level against Florida. Following the Sooners’ impressive performance, Bayless took to X to suggested that Oklahoma should consider making his position permanent. “JASON WITTEN STRIKES AGAIN (AND AGAIN): OU, 20-play TD drive, Mateer to Sategna, 20-7. No more “interim.” Give Witten a long-term deal,” Bayless wrote. The victory gives Oklahoma a much-needed lift following a challenging stretch of the season. The Sooners had struggled to find consistency, alternating between victories and defeats during their first eight games. The coaching change followed Oklahoma’s growing offensive concerns, particularly after its disappointing 42-25 loss to South Carolina. Head coach Brent Venables believed that bringing in a new offensive leader could help the Sooners make the most of their remaining opportunities this season. Witten faced a challenging first assignment as Oklahoma traveled to Gainesville to take on a ranked Florida team. However, the Sooners came away with an impressive victory, providing their interim offensive play-caller with a promising start to his new role. Oklahoma’s offense also showed noticeable improvement under Witten’s leadership. The Sooners also claimed their first win in Gainesville during the first on-campus meeting between the two programs. Their previous encounters took place in the 2009 BCS National Championship Game and the 2020 Cotton Bowl. articles.title: Matthew Schaefer, Luke Hughes throwdown during Islanders-Devils NHL clash
articles.summary: The New York Islanders and New Jersey Devils served up one of the more surprising scraps of the NHL season on Saturday night, as Islanders phenom Matthew Schaefer and Devils defenseman Luke Hughes got into it at UBS Arena. The unexpected throwdown came in the second period, with the Islanders lea
articles._body: The New York Islanders and New Jersey Devils served up one of the more surprising scraps of the NHL season on Saturday night, as Islanders phenom Matthew Schaefer and Devils defenseman Luke Hughes got into it at UBS Arena. The unexpected throwdown came in the second period, with the Islanders leading 4-2. Schaefer had taken Hughes down earlier in the game, and tempers eventually boiled over between two of the league’s brightest young blueliners. SportsCenter summed up the reaction perfectly on X , calling it “not the matchup we expected to see.” MATTHEW SCHAEFER VS. LUKE HUGHES Not the matchup we expected to see pic.twitter.com/WUGVXgxzKR — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) November 8, 2026 It was a rare sight for both players. Neither Schaefer nor Hughes has a fight on his NHL record, making the heated exchange between the two skilled, puck-moving defensemen all the more stunning. Schaefer, the first overall pick in the 2025 NHL Draft , had already made his presence felt on the scoresheet, scoring his fifth goal of the season in the first period to give the Islanders a 2-1 lead. But it was Hughes who got the last laugh. The Devils stormed back in the third period, as Luke Evangelista cut the deficit to one at 6:08 and Dougie Hamilton tied the game on a power play with 6:18 left in regulation. Luke Hughes was flying in overtime, with Schaefer struggling to match him stride for stride, according to Pucks and Pitchforks. Eventually, his brother Jack Hughes finished off a two-on-one rush with a shot past Ilya Sorokin’s blocker with 3:42 remaining to give New Jersey a 5-4 win. It was Jack’s third overtime goal of the season. Sorokin was outstanding in the loss, turning aside 45 shots, but the Islanders could not hold on. Anthony Duclair, Simon Holmstrom and Victor Eklund also scored for New York, while Bo Horvat chipped in two assists. Evan Rodrigues and Declan Chisholm had the other goals for New Jersey, and Jake Allen made 19 saves. The win extended the Devils’ winning streak to four games, while the Islanders dropped their third straight. It was a far cry from the teams’ first meeting of the season, when New York blew out New Jersey 6-0 on Oct. 3. With the rivalry clearly heating up, the next Islanders-Devils clash could bring even more fireworks. U2 Weigh In on Ed Sheeran and Macklemore Tour Controversy
articles.summary: The Edge and Larry Mullen Jr. defended the rapper’s right to speak out, while the Edge said Sheeran “should not be vilified”.
articles._body: U2 have weighed in on Macklemore ’s removal from Ed Sheeran ’s U.S. tour, backing the rapper’s right to speak out while cautioning against blaming Sheeran. “We totally support Macklemore’s right as an artist to say what he wanted to say,” the Edge said in an interview with BBC News. “I don’t think Ed should be vilified,” he added, acknowledging the difficult position Sheeran had been in. The guitarist also praised the artists who left Sheeran’s tour in solidarity, framing the dispute as a matter of free expression. Drummer Larry Mullen Jr. went further. “Artists can choose whether they want to be politically active or not. It’s a human right,” he said. “But we as a band will fight for the right to speak your mind as long as it doesn’t incite violence. And even if we disagree with it or don’t like it, nobody has a right – no billionaire, no promoter, no owner has the right to censor anybody. They will definitely not be censoring us ever.” Macklemore was dropped from the North American leg of Sheeran’s Loop Tour in September after two opening sets at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, where he said “Free Palestine,” spoke about Gaza and the West Bank, and performed his protest song “Hind’s Hall.” Promoter Messina Touring Group said venues on the remaining dates would not allow the shows to go ahead with him on the bill. New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft confirmed he barred the rapper from Gillette Stadium, citing his comments and what Kraft called “a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery.” Sheeran said the decision belonged to the promoter. Several acts left the tour in response, including Finneas, Lukas Graham and Irish folk band Beoga, which had been performing with Sheeran each night. Sheeran later opened a show in Philadelphia by apologizing for “mistakes” in his handling of the situation. Macklemore has since played three sold-out Free Palestine benefit concerts in Dublin, Paris and London, with guests including Hozier, Kneecap and Beoga, raising money for organizations supporting Palestinians. U2 release Carnaval De Luz , their 16th studio album and first full-length of new material in nine years, on Nov. 13. The album closes with “Torn,” a duet with the late Dolly Parton that the band says was her last recorded vocal performance.

articles._body: Coach Dan Lanning trolled the Ohio State Buckeyes as his Oregon Ducks scored one of their most satisfying wins in recent memory, winning 41-28 in Columbus behind 257 passing yards and two touchdowns from Dylan Raiola. Lanning gave coach Ryan Day his flowers after the Buckeyes loss as fans began wondering what the future holds. Lanning’s team’s schedule looks highly manageable the rest of the way as the Ducks continue to look more and more like their old selves. New offensive coordinator Jay Johnson has Dylan Raiola firing on all cylinders at quarterback while the Ducks have shuffled star players including Evan Stewart (in this week) and Jordon Davison (out this week) in and out of the lineup. The Ducks have a path to a Big Ten title, and it’s looking clearer each week. They do need some “carnage,” as Johnson put it, but there is hope, and that matters quite a bit in Eugene. articles.title: Kentucky HC Will Stein gets 100% real on ‘no moral victories’ after loss to Tennessee
articles.summary: Kentucky football watched Tennessee fans troll the Wildcats following Saturday’s 34-6 trouncing. This loss surely alters both the SEC title game and College Football Playoff picture. But it also got UK coach Will Stein dropping 100% honesty after the game. Stein takes his biggest loss of hi
articles._body: Kentucky football watched Tennessee fans troll the Wildcats following Saturday’s 34-6 trouncing. This loss surely alters both the SEC title game and College Football Playoff picture. But it also got UK coach Will Stein dropping 100% honesty after the game. Stein takes his biggest loss of his young head coaching career. Such a win would’ve increased UK’s chances of making a long-awaited trip to the conference championship. Plus impress the CFP committee in the process. But Stein dropped this eight-word admission after the defeat. “There really aren’t a lot of moral victories,” Stein told reporters after the game . He also described how “uncharacteristic plays” did the Wildcats in during the drubbing. Will Stein’s opening statement following the loss at #16 Tennessee pic.twitter.com/BLaQJyfQuk — Cats Coverage (@Cats_Coverage) November 8, 2026 Kentucky now helps create quite the logjam in the SEC. So UK joins the Volunteers , Alabama and Texas at 7-2 teams all vying for a spot in Atlanta on Dec. 5 with the conference title on the line. Except now the Vols and the Crimson Tide own the tiebreaker edge over the Wildcats, by virtue of their victories over UK. So Stein and Kentucky must win out, then have lots of outside factors play into UK’s favor. Certainly one more loss by the aforementioned three 7-2 teams can boost Kentucky’s case. But the Wildcats face a daunting road. Kentucky hosts No. 24 Florida in Lexington next, with the loser potentially facing elimination from the SEC title game and CFP race. No. 18 Missouri then follows and surely, the Tigers will want to redeem themselves from their own letdown loss Saturday to Texas. Finally, Stein gets his taste of the Bluegrass State rivalry in facing Louisville to close out the season. articles.title: Simple Plan Are Meeting a Whole New Generation of Fans, 25 Years In
articles.summary: Drummer Chuck Comeau talks TikTok, Good Things Festival, and why a farewell tour is “not in the cards”
articles._body: Simple Plan have been playing the same songs for 25 years. Lately, they’re playing them to a lot of people hearing them live for the first time. “Every night we ask people, ‘Hey, how many people are here for the first time?’” drummer Chuck Comeau tells Billboard. “Sometimes it’s like 85% have never seen the band.” The Montreal pop-punk band is drawing fans who weren’t born when “I’m Just a Kid” arrived in 2002, alongside the original listeners who are now bringing their own kids to shows. Some of the younger crowd have even started calling Simple Plan “classic rock.” “And you’re like, ‘What are you talking about?’” Comeau says. “There’s nothing cooler than what’s happening to our band right now,” he adds. Much of that can be traced to “I’m Just a Kid” going viral on TikTok, where it soundtracked a challenge encouraging users to recreate their childhood photos. Comeau calls the trend a “gigantic gift,” but says meeting fans online has always come naturally to the band, which was filming backstage antics and sharing them through its website and DVDs long before TikTok existed. “It’s the same thing,” he says. “It’s just a new platform.” The renewed attention builds on a strong early run. The band’s 2004 album Still Not Getting Any… debuted at No. 3 on the Billboard 200, while “Perfect” and “Welcome to My Life” reached Nos. 24 and 40, respectively, on the Billboard Hot 100. Next up is a return to Australia for Good Things Festival, where Simple Plan join a bill led by Limp Bizkit and featuring Spiritbox , the All-American Rejects , Bad Religion and MxPx. The festival hits Melbourne’s Flemington Racecourse on Dec. 4, Sydney Showground on Dec. 5 and Brisbane Showgrounds on Dec. 6, marking the band’s third trip Down Under in three years. “We love Australia. What can I say?” Comeau says. “Any excuse, we come back.” The lineup mixes pop-punk with nu-metal, hardcore and heavier rock, the kind of bill Comeau admits might once have made him nervous. “Being on this lineup would have been a bit more intimidating 25 years ago,” he says. He credits streaming with breaking down the scene boundaries that once divided fans, making it easier for younger listeners to move between genres. The band has seen it firsthand at European festivals, sharing stages with acts like Slipknot . “At first, you’re a little terrified,” he says. “You’re like, ‘How’s that gonna go?’ And then you actually realize that people are stoked.” He has his own Good Things wish list. Bad Religion, whom he calls his favorite band, are near the top, along with Swedish punks Millencolin, who are playing Pennybridge Pioneers in full. He’s also keen to finally see Limp Bizkit live. “I’ve seen a lot of crazy videos right now that are popping up everywhere,” he says. Meanwhile, Simple Plan have started writing their seventh studio album, with work set to continue into 2027. There’s no release date, but Comeau says the band has a batch of songs it’s excited about, and no intention of rushing. “We’ve been around for 25 years and we only have six albums,” he says. “So we take our time.” The record will follow 2022’s Harder Than It Looks , and Comeau says the aim is to refine the band’s sound rather than overhaul it. “We know who we are,” he says. “We’re not going to turn around and make a black metal record.” The harder challenge is competing with the band’s own past. Songs that soundtracked fans’ teenage years carry a weight that new material has to earn. “When you get to this stage of your career, you’re almost playing against yourself,” Comeau says. “You’re playing against your history.” “You’re not the new shiny young band anymore,” he adds. “So you’ve got to work harder to have people pay attention.” That’s why he won’t put a deadline on it. “There’s never a good time for a bad record, and there’s never a bad time for a good record,” he says. Next year also marks 25 years since the band’s debut album, No Pads, No Helmets…Just Balls . Comeau says a special-edition vinyl and a few anniversary performances are on the table, but not a full album tour. “I think we’re bigger than just one album,” he says. “But that album was really consequential for us. It’s the one that started it all.” Another milestone arrives March 9, 2027, when the band releases its first children’s picture book, I’m Just a Kid: The Story of Simple Plan , illustrated by Jomike Tejido. Comeau says it grew out of watching the band’s original fans grow up and start families of their own. “We were with them throughout their difficult moments,” he says, recalling how songs about breakups, school and friendships became part of listeners’ teenage years. “Fast-forward 20 years, 25 years, now they’re starting families, they’re having kids. We want to be there with them in this new chapter of their lives.” The book explores friendship and perseverance and includes nods for longtime fans. “It’s as much for the parents as it is for the kids,” Comeau says. For all the anniversaries and nostalgia, Simple Plan have never broken up, gone on hiatus or staged a reunion, which is rare among their peers. Comeau believes the years since the pandemic have been some of the band’s best, with bigger crowds and a sharper focus on the live show. “When we were young, you were going out and you were partying,” he says. “Now it’s like, no, we don’t do that anymore. We’re all doing yoga and stretching.” “We’ve always just kept going,” he says. “I feel like there’s a lot of work to be done.” So, a farewell tour? “There’s no talk about a farewell tour,” Comeau says. “Not in the cards for now.”

articles.title: Angels rumors: Infielder joins Zach Neto as potential offseason trade candidate
articles.summary: Zach Neto has already been floated as a potential trade chip for the Los Angeles Angels this offseason, and now another young infielder is being mentioned alongside him. With the franchise at a crossroads, first baseman Nolan Schanuel could also be on the move if the club decides to rebuild. MLB.
articles._body: Zach Neto has already been floated as a potential trade chip for the Los Angeles Angels this offseason, and now another young infielder is being mentioned alongside him. With the franchise at a crossroads, first baseman Nolan Schanuel could also be on the move if the club decides to rebuild. MLB.com’s Rhett Bollinger noted that both players are firmly entrenched in the Angels’ infield, but their futures could depend on which direction the team takes. “The Angels have Zach Neto entrenched at shortstop and Nolan Schanuel at first base, but either could be a trade candidate if they decide to rebuild,” Bollinger wrote. The Angels are coming off a brutal 2026 season in which they lost 100 games. On top of that, the organization is in the middle of a major transition. Arte Moreno agreed to sell the team to Kroenke Sports & Entertainment for a reported $4 billion, and the Angels are not expected to hire a new general manager or manager until the sale is approved. Interim GM John Mozeliak is set to depart when his contract expires in December. Neto has been at the center of trade speculation for months. The Boston Red Sox reportedly had strong interest in the 25-year-old shortstop ahead of the trade deadline, and MLB Network’s Jon Morosi recently suggested the Angels should explore the market . “This is the time to gauge interest in Zach Neto and Reid Detmers,” Morosi said on MLB Network’s “Hot Stove.” “It’s not about winning a World Series in 2027.” It is easy to see why teams would be interested. Neto slugged 27 home runs and drove in 77 runs in 157 games in 2026, and he has three years of team control remaining. Schanuel, meanwhile, is 24 years old and coming off a solid campaign in which he hit .276 with seven home runs, 49 RBIs and a .736 OPS in 107 games. The former first-round pick has been a steady presence at first base since debuting just weeks after being drafted in 2023. For now, any major moves will likely have to wait until the ownership change is finalized. But if the new regime chooses to tear things down, Neto and Schanuel could be two of the most intriguing names on the trade market. articles.title: How Patriots legend Rob Gronkowski truly felt about Tom Brady’s presence at his New England Hall of Fame ceremony
articles.summary: Rob Gronkowski had plenty of familiar faces in his corner for his New England Patriots Hall of Fame induction on Saturday, but one presence clearly stood out above the rest. The former tight end opened up about what it meant to have Tom Brady by his side for the big day. “It meant everything̷
articles._body: Rob Gronkowski had plenty of familiar faces in his corner for his New England Patriots Hall of Fame induction on Saturday , but one presence clearly stood out above the rest. The former tight end opened up about what it meant to have Tom Brady by his side for the big day. “It meant everything… He wanted to be here. It just meant a lot, man. Tom can be anywhere else. He’s the greatest player of all time. It just meant a lot to myself, my family, and to the fans, I’m sure as well,” Gronkowski said, via Justin Turpin . Rob Gronkowski on having Tom Brady at his Patriots Hall of Fame induction: “It meant everything… He wanted to be here. It just meant a lot, man. Tom can be anywhere else. He’s the greatest player of all time. It just meant a lot to myself, my family, and to the fans, I’m sure… pic.twitter.com/JF8oYLQLTv — Justin Turpin (@JustinmTurpin) November 7, 2026 Brady received a loud ovation from the crowd at Patriot Place Plaza, where many of Gronkowski’s former teammates and coaches gathered for the ceremony. The legendary quarterback also showed his former tight end some love on social media , reposting a video of the two embracing with a simple message. “That’s my ,” Brady wrote. The mutual admiration makes sense. Brady and Gronkowski formed one of the most dominant quarterback-tight end duos in NFL history, winning three Super Bowls together in New England before reuniting with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to capture a fourth title in the 2020 season. Gronkowski was voted into the Patriots Hall of Fame by fans in April, in his first year of eligibility. He joined Brady, who was inducted in 2024. The honor caps a remarkable career in New England . Gronkowski spent nine seasons with the Patriots after being selected in the second round of the 2010 NFL Draft out of Arizona. He racked up 521 receptions for 7,861 yards and 79 touchdowns in the regular season, and his 80 total touchdowns rank first in franchise history. He was also a five-time Pro Bowler and four-time First-Team All-Pro. Patriots owner Robert Kraft was unable to attend the ceremony while recovering from back surgery, but he had high praise for Gronkowski when the honor was announced. “Rob became a fan favorite almost immediately and remained the standard at tight end for nearly a decade,” Kraft said. The celebration continues on Sunday, when Gronkowski will be honored at halftime of the Patriots’ game against the Green Bay Packers. Brady will be on hand for that one as well, calling the game from the FOX broadcast booth. CJ Carr had gotten the better of his high-profile matchup with Mensah with two first-half touchdowns, including a beautiful throw to Jordan Faison. But Mensah and No. 1 Miami have stormed back with two touchdown passes in a row. First he found Elija Lofton to cap off an 11-play drive. Then, a 31-yard pass to Lofton helped set up the touchdown for Barkate in their following drive. Barkate entered the game as the team’s second-leading receiver behind Malachi Toney. He had 28 catches for 372 yards and four touchdowns, which were far behind Toney’s otherworldly numbers. But with Toney out, the senior has done his best to step up to the plate for the Hurricanes. articles._body: Kenny Minchey and the No. 8 Kentucky Wildcats were the latest victims of the Tennessee Volunteers’ suffocating defense. The Kentucky football quarterback, who could potentially land in the first round of the NFL draft next year, had a rough game as his offense was limited to a season-low six points in the Vols’ decisive 34-6 victory over the Wildcats. As the game was winding down in the fourth quarter with Tennessee up big, Vols fans were spotted b ringing out their belts , signifying the beatdown they just handed to the Wildcats. Tennessee fans brought the belts out for Kentucky pic.twitter.com/pytpTV8jf8 — YEET Sportsbook (@yeetsportsbook) November 8, 2026 Minchey completed an impressive 26 of 34 pass attempts (76.5%) for 224 yards. But he was held without a touchdown and threw just his second interception of the season. The Wildcats didn’t help themselves as they also lost two fumbles, one of which resulted in a Tennessee touchdown. Kentucky didn’t trail the Vols by that much in terms of total yards as it finished 389-361 to Tennessee. The Wildcats also dominated the time of possession battle, 35-25. However, those costly turnovers and the inability to convert those drives into points doomed them against the Vols. It was always going to be tough for Kentucky to get the win in Knoxville, though. Other top quarterbacks in Texas’ Arch Manning and Alabama’s Keelon Russell found it tough to play at Neyland Stadium given the atmosphere and the Vols’ impressive defense this season. With their six-game win streak snapped, the Wildcats will need to bounce back to finish what has been a promising first season under Will Stein strong. articles.title: Oregon HC Dan Lanning hilariously trolls Ohio State during huge upset win
articles.summary: Oregon head coach Dan Lanning had the last laugh against Ohio State, cheekily taunting the Buckeyes during Saturday’s stunning 41-28 road win. The Ducks overcame an early 14-point deficit before putting together a remarkable scoring run that left the home crowd heading for the exits. Ranked
articles._body: Oregon head coach Dan Lanning had the last laugh against Ohio State, cheekily taunting the Buckeyes during Saturday’s stunning 41-28 road win . The Ducks overcame an early 14-point deficit before putting together a remarkable scoring run that left the home crowd heading for the exits. Ranked No. 23 in the College Football Playoff rankings, Oregon (6-3, 4-2 Big Ten) scored 38 unanswered points versus No. 12 Ohio State (6-3, 4-2), turning a difficult afternoon into one of the most consequential results of the Buckeyes’ season. The defeat not only ended Ohio State’s 12-game home winning streak but also gave the program its first consecutive losses since 2011. Lanning’s aggressive approach played a huge role in the turnaround. Trailing 14-3 late in the second quarter, the Ducks faced fourth-and-9 at its own 31-yard line. Instead of punting, Oregon executed a fake that saw linebacker Teitum Tuioti find fellow linebacker Matayo Uiagalelei for a 30-yard gain. The conversion helped set up a 70-yard touchdown drive, which ended with running back Dierre Hill Jr.’s 9-yard scoring run. The Ducks then received another opportunity after defensive back Devin Jackson intercepted Buckeyes freshman quarterback Luke Fahey near the sideline. With two seconds remaining before halftime, Lanning declined to settle for a field goal. Oregon used an unusual formation, with tight end Jamari Johnson taking a direct snap and powering into the end zone for a 2-yard touchdown. That gave the Ducks a 17-14 lead heading into the break. Oregon carried that momentum into the second half. Hill broke through Ohio State’s defense for a 48-yard touchdown run on the opening possession, extending the advantage to 24-14. Ducks quarterback Dylan Raiola later connected with Dakorien Moore for an impressive one-handed, 11-yard touchdown reception before Brandon Smith added another score on a 15-yard screen pass. As Oregon continued to pull away, frustration became increasingly visible on the Buckeyes’ sideline. Wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, who finished with seven receptions for 133 yards and a touchdown, was seen shouting toward coaches and teammates early in the fourth quarter. Ohio State’s frustrations eventually spilled over near the Ducks’ sideline, where players from both teams exchanged words after an Oregon scoring play. Lanning responded by pointing the opposing players toward the scoreboard , letting the numbers do all the talking. By that stage, the Ducks had already scored 38 consecutive points, and many Buckeyes supporters had left the stadium with more than 10 minutes remaining. Dan Lanning pointing at the scoreboard pic.twitter.com/y8DTbQygRK — CBS Sports College Football (@CBSSportsCFB) November 8, 2026 Oregon’s explosive stretch left Ohio State with little chance of recovering. Fahey finished with 360 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception on 36-of-50 passing, while the Buckeyes were unable to generate meaningful offense during the Ducks scoring surge. They eventually added two late touchdowns, but those scores could not change the outcome. For Ohio State, the setback marked its first three-loss season since 2011 and severely damaged its College Football Playoff hopes. The Buckeyes also suffered their first back-to-back defeats against unranked opponents since October 1992. Meanwhile, Oregon has won consecutive games despite losing starting quarterback Dante Moore to a season-ending concussion. Raiola completed 25 of 40 passes for 257 yards and two touchdowns, while Hill contributed 75 rushing yards and two scores. The Ducks will now turn their attention to a home game versus Michigan next Saturday. The post Oregon HC Dan Lanning hilariously trolls Ohio State during huge upset win appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Curtis Samuel breaks three-year social media silence to critique 'unacceptable' Ohio State loss
articles.summary: Former Ohio State national champion and All-American receiver Curtis Samuel spoke out on social media following the program’s 41-28 loss to Oregon on Saturday. More specifically, he posted his first tweets since 2023. He seemed to feel it was that important to make his thoughts clear on the state of
articles._body: Former Ohio State national champion and All-American receiver Curtis Samuel spoke out on social media following the program’s 41-28 loss to Oregon on Saturday. More specifically, he posted his first tweets since 2023. He seemed to feel it was that important to make his thoughts clear on the state of the program following the third loss of the season — one that got away from the Buckeyes quickly. [ $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] “Can’t allow a team to come in the shoe and be the bully that’s unacceptable and for sure not the culture,” Samuel wrote at 6:49 p.m. ET on Saturday . Samuel had also posted “This is horrible smh” during the game, then followed it up with a final thought after the above commentary on the state of the program. “Last thing you telling me Legend Bey isn’t good enough to get offensive snaps in meaningful parts of the game?” Samuel wrote . “I think the kid is super talented.” The former Ohio State star demanding some accountability also fits with the postgame message of coach Ryan Day . But what that accountability might look like remains to be seen. The Buckeyes are certainly in unfamiliar territory during Day’s tenure. Ryan Day demanding accountability Ohio State started off reasonably well against Oregon on Saturday afternoon, taking a 14-0 lead in the first quarter. But it went downhill quickly from there. Day went on to say that there needs to be accountability with what’s going wrong, and it starts with the staff. The loss is the Buckeyes’ second in a row and third of the season. “I’ve got to evaluate everything and try to come in tomorrow and figure out, with the staff, the things we’re coming up short on and figure out how to adjust those things,” Day said in his postgame press conference. “It all starts with the staff, and then it goes to the players. There needs to be accountability for all of it, and then we go from there.” Day went on to say that the team didn’t expect any of this to happen. But once Oregon took the momentum in the second quarter, there was no getting it back. Ohio State led 14-0 in the first quarter, but Oregon answered with a 17-0 second quarter to make it 17-14 at halftime. The Ducks then won the third quarter 14-0, and that proved to be too much for the Buckeyes to come back from. “We didn’t expect any of this to happen,” said Day. “I thought the way that we came out was how we thought we would play in this game. Once the momentum swung, we just weren’t able to stop that and then swing it.” Momentum now is swinging against Day and his staff pretty hard. The fanbase is upset and even former players are speaking out on what they see as wrong with the program right now. It’ll take a big effort to halt the skid in its tracks, before any further damage can be done. Ohio State returns to action next weekend with a game against Northwestern . On3’s Jonathan Wagner also contributed to this report.

articles.title: South Carolina QB LaNorris Sellers talks gutting out win over Texas A&M with ankle injury
articles.summary: LaNorris Sellers left South Carolina football fans cringing before halftime against Texas A&M. Yet broke off a 41-yard touchdown on a bad ankle. Sellers gutting it out inspired the crucial 17-9 victory to officially become bowl eligible. Injury and all, Sellers has officially lifted the Gamec
articles._body: LaNorris Sellers left South Carolina football fans cringing before halftime against Texas A&M . Yet broke off a 41-yard touchdown on a bad ankle. Sellers gutting it out inspired the crucial 17-9 victory to officially become bowl eligible. Injury and all, Sellers has officially lifted the Gamecocks back into the postseason picture. “My ankle just bothered me pretty much. It got better as the game went on. But then the last one, I couldn’t stop and it started hurting. So that’s bad on me. But we found a way to finish,” Sellers said postgame to ESPN. Even his head coach Shane Beamer was overcome with emotions in seeing his own QB battle through the ailment. “I had flashbacks of the LSU game two years ago. It was the same spot where he got hurt. But the grit that he showed, I told the team at halftime that we’re gritty as hell. We’re physically and mentally tough. It was a gritty win,” Beamer said afterward. Postgame with Shane Beamer & LaNorris Sellers after a gritty win over Texas A&M! 4-straight dubs for the Gamecocks! Sellers gutted this thing out tonight. pic.twitter.com/culTUyz0FJ — Stormy (Buonantony) Normandt (@StormBuonantony) November 8, 2026 South Carolina managed to sneak inside the College Football Playoff ranking on Tuesday even with three losses. Oregon and Florida were the other three-loss teams that made it into that top 25 list. Now the Gamecocks likely will move up in the CFP poll. The race to the SEC title game is becoming tighter with South Carolina still not mathematically out of it. Plus Kentucky’s lopsided loss to Tennessee has sent the picture into a new tailspin. Sellers ended the evening with 251 passing yards , one touchdown and 34 rushing yards with the 41-yard score there. articles.title: Warriors star Stephen Curry joins elusive club with Kobe Bryant, LeBron James
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors superstar may be nearing the final chapter of his illustrious career, but the veteran sharpshooter continues to prove that he remains a dominant force in the NBA this season. Stephen Curry has already reached several significant milestones during the season, and he added
articles._body: The Golden State Warriors superstar may be nearing the final chapter of his illustrious career, but the veteran sharpshooter continues to prove that he remains a dominant force in the NBA this season . Stephen Curry has already reached several significant milestones during the season, and he added another remarkable achievement during Saturday’s matchup against the Orlando Magic. Curry joined an exclusive group featuring Kobe Bryant, James Harden, John Havlicek, LeBron James, Oscar Robertson and Russell Westbrook, becoming just the seventh player in NBA history to record at least 26,000 points, 5,000 rebounds and 6,000 assists. Additionally, the 38-year-old became the fastest point guard since the NBA-ABA merger to reach 25,000 points, 5,000 rebounds and 5,000 assists. Curry made a strong impact in the first half alone, finishing with 14 points, four rebounds and four assists. He was highly efficient from the floor, converting five of his six field-goal attempts, including two of three from beyond the arc, while going a perfect 2-of-2 from the free-throw line. The Warriors entered halftime holding a commanding 16-point advantage, with Curry delivering an unbelievable shot to close out the first half. The Warriors superstar has now knocked down at least one three-pointer in 100 consecutive regular-season games. It marks the seventh-longest streak in NBA history and the third-longest of his career. Curry continues to serve as the focal point of Golden State’s offense, relying on his elite shooting, and playmaking skills to keep the team competitive. Despite the NBA’s emergence of a new generation of stars, the Warriors superstar’s impact remains irreplaceable. Golden State has also demonstrated that it has enough offensive firepower to compete with established Western Conference contenders. However, improving its defensive consistency and maintaining a high level of performance throughout games will be equally important. Curry’s leadership and experience will remain essential to the Warriors’ ambitions. While the veteran guard is approaching the final chapter of his illustrious career, his performances early this season continue to show that he has plenty left in the tank. articles._body: As of publication, the Golden State Warriors held a double digit lead over the Orlando Magic late in the second quarter on Saturday evening, but the game had a little bit of fireworks to start off. Instead of playing for a national championship this season, Ohio State appears to be out of contention and playing for mere respectability. Ryan Day on Oregon’s offensive creat
articles._body: The Ohio State Buckeyes are in big trouble. After consecutive losses to USC and Oregon, the Buckeyes are simply reeling. Instead of playing for a national championship this season, Ohio State appears to be out of contention and playing for mere respectability. Ryan Day on Oregon’s offensive creativity (and Ohio State’s lack thereof): pic.twitter.com/vPTIhcRUh3 — Stefan Krajisnik (@skrajisnik3) November 8, 2026 Ohio State may have gotten off to a sharp start against the visiting Ducks by scoring 14 points in the first quarter. However, all that did was wake the visitors, who would score the next 38 points as they registered a stunning 41-28 triumph. Ohio State has struggled badly since losing starting QB Julian Sayin to a fractured elbow in a victory over Indiana. The offense has lost its momentum, and the defense has failed to do its job. In the loss to Oregon, the Ducks showed off their creativity behind quarterback Dylan Raiola. The Buckeyes could not match that aspect of the game, and head coach Ryan Day admitted his team was not able to keep up with Oregon in that area and it cost his team in the matchup. “I give them credit because they did some good things there,” Day said after the game. “It’s our job. We have to figure some things out. We have to figure out a way to put our guys in a position to be successful. Creativity is one of those things and I can’t sit here and say we’ve done a good enough job the last two games.” Ohio State will try to bounce back next week at home against Northwestern before playing at Nebraska and at home against Michigan in the final two weeks of the regular season. articles._body: The Utah Jazz come into their matchup againsT the Minnesota Timberwolves on Sunday looking to get back in the win column and snap a seven-game losing streak. The team has begun the 2026-27 season at 1-8, with their sole win coming against the New Orleans Pelicans in only the second game of the year. And the Jazz might be short-handed as big man Lauri Markkanen popped up on the team’s injury report against the Timberwolves. Laurie Markkanen listed as questionable for the Jazz’s game against the Timberwolves as he’s dealing with a right wrist sprain . Markkanen has played in eight of the Jazz’s nine games to start the season, missing only the team’s loss to the San Antonio Spurs on Oct. 28 due to said wrist injury. He’s coming off a 24-point performance in a loss to the Dallas Mavericks. He also added eight rebounds and one assist in the loss. The former Arizona star has dealt with various injury issues during his career, and has been limited to an average of only 44 games the past two seasons. This season, he’s been playing a little over 30 minutes per game for the Jazz while averaging 18.0 points. He’s also averaging 6.8 rebounds and 2.0 assists with splits of 38.9 percent shooting from the field, 39.7 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 84.4 percent shooting from the free-throw line. The No. 7 overall pick in the 2017 NBA Draft, Markkanen is in his fifth season with the Jazz. He was acquired ahead of the 2022-23 season in the blockbuster trade that brought Donovan Mitchell to the Cleveland Cavaliers.
