articles.title: Elvis Presley Rights Owners Sue Suno Over AI Voice Cloning: ‘Elvis’ Identity Was Stolen’
articles.summary: The singer's legendary voice is at the center of a cutting-edge lawsuit that aims to hold the AI firm legally liable for allowing users to create knockoff vocals.
articles._body: The owners of Elvis Presley ’s intellectual property are suing Suno in a new lawsuit that claims the artificial intelligence music company violated the King of Rock ‘n’ Roll’s likeness rights by stealing his voice. Weeks after suing AI giant Anthropic for training Claude on Elvis songs, the new case filed Friday (Nov. 6) by Elvis Presley Enterprises levels similar copyright accusations against Suno, the leading AI music firm. But it also includes legally-novel allegations that Suno broke the law by letting users clone Presley’s “unmistakable and iconic voice.” Related Anthropic Sued For Stealing Elvis Presley Music to Train AI: ‘Deeply Protective of These Iconic Songs’ Suno Says Jason Isbell Lawsuit Over Artist ‘Identities’ Must Be Dismissed: ‘Nothing Unlawful About That’ Reservoir Sues Suno & Anthropic in Latest Lawsuits Over AI Music: ‘Meant to Replace the Artists’ “All of the humanity, history, despair, and triumph that constitutes Elvis’ identity was stolen and is stored on servers and harnessed by Suno to make massive amounts of money,” writes Richard Busch, a veteran music litigator at the firm Adams & Reese who filed the case. “Suno did so intentionally, maliciously, and fraudulently to financially benefit itself and artificially compete with Elvis’ likeness and copyrights, and continues to do so to this day.” The new lawsuit marks one of the first major cases under a new Tennessee law, coincidentally called the ELVIS Act, that was recently enacted to address problems caused by AI. The first-in-the-nation statute was touted as a weapon against people who create illegal deepfakes, but it also allows for lawsuits against tech firms that enable such voice and image cloning in the first place. Taken together with the Anthropic case, the suits over Elvis represent easily most significant action filed on behalf of an individual musician over AI — in this case, arguably the most famous recording artist of all time. Suno and Anthropic were already facing cases from music labels accusing them of infringing millions of copyrighted songs to train their models, as well as a class action by smaller artists who similarly say Suno stole their likenesses. Friday’s lawsuit was filed by Elvis Presley Enterprises, a unit of the licensing giant Authentic Brands Group that controls the intellectual property tied to Elvis, including much of his song catalog and the rights to his name, image and likeness. In a statement to Billboard on Saturday, ABG spokeswoman Lark-Marie Antón said the new lawsuit and its evidence “speak for themselves.” “The name, image, likeness, and music of Elvis Presley are among the most valuable intellectual property assets in the world,” Antón said. “We protect those rights vigorously.” In statement Saturday responding to the lawsuit, a Suno spokeswoman told Billboard : “Suno exists to help people create new, original music, not to trade on anyone’s name or likeness, and we prohibit any unauthorized use of an artist’s work. To protect against this, we do not allow prompts for specific artists’ names and songs and work with third party providers to screen uploaded audio files and lyrics for potential misuse. We are always working to strengthen our guardrails and we will continue to add new safeguards that protect artists and our users.” The looming battle with Suno will raise untested legal questions about the extent to which AI companies can be sued for allegedly ripping off a musical artist’s identity. The use of AI to convincingly mimic real people has been one of the booming technology’s most controversial applications, and no where less so than an industry largely built on famous singing voices. “Elvis’ voice possessed a distinctively rich vocal timbre, with a warm velvety resonance and perfectly employed vibrato, coupled with his ability to vary his technique and delivery within the same song as well as across several different styles of music, which became his immediately recognizable musical signature across the world,” the lawsuit says. Suno has argued in other lawsuits that its current models do not allow users to include the names of specific artists in prompts, nor produce outputs that mimic specific real voices. But in Friday’s complaint, the Elvis owners say those claims are “unequivocally false.” They included links to videos capturing the use of Suno’s platform to play songs that sound remarkably similar to Presley. “Those … are NOT examples of Elvis Presley singing. They are synthetic and unlicensed uses of Elvis’ voice and likeness,” Busch writes. “There are hundreds to thousands more like it.” The new case will test the power and limits of the ELVIS (Ensuring Likeness Voice and Image Security) Act, a law enacted in 2024 in Presley’s adopted home state to make it easier for musicians to bring such cases. Existing laws typically only applied to commercial exploitation of someone’s likeness, like an unauthorized advertisement; the new statute removed those restrictions. ELVIS also specifically imposed liability on companies that provide tools allowing for unauthorized use of a person’s likeness. “Suno is the embodiment of why the ELVIS Act was so essentially required,” the lawsuit reads. “Suno has stolen Elvis’ voice, his image, and likeness, as well as his copyrighted works on, literally, a breathtaking scale, and must now be called to answer for its theft.” Suno’s lawyers have argued such claims won’t hold up in court. In an earlier likeness case filed by Jason Isbell and other artists, the AI firm’s lawyers argued it merely uses artist names as “shorthand for the genre they perform in” and does not allow for direct theft of t

articles._body: The Miami football program has suffered a devastating blow to its national title hopes with the news that star wide receiver and Heisman hopeful Malachi Toney will undergo ankle surgery . However, while the surgery hurts Miami as they head into a massive Notre Dame matchup , getting Toney’s ankle fixed now could have the wideout back in time for the College Football Playoff. “The early feel on the recovery timetable for Miami star receiver Malachi Toney was in the range of 4-6 weeks, sources tell @CBSSports,” per Matt Zenit. “Gives him a shot to be back as early as possibly the ACC title game. At the very least, in position to be back for the College Football Playoff.” After the Miami-Notre Dame tilt on Saturday night, the Hurricanes have winnable games against Duke, Virginia Tech, and Boston College, followed by the ACC Championship. So, even if Toney’s absence costs them the Notre Dame game, chances are good that Miami makes the CFP. Toney has been one of the most dangerous players in college football this season, racking up 73 catches, 1,027 yards, and 13 touchdowns in eight games. The other silver lining for the Miami football program is that Toney is a true sophomore, meaning he cannot enter the 2027 NFL Draft and should be back in Coral Gables next season. The question is, though, who will his quarterback be? Toney’s teammate and fellow Heisman contender, Darian Mensah, does have another year of college eligibility, but with names like Arch Manning, Drew Mestemaker, CJ Carr, and others leaning toward staying in school, Mensah may leave for the pros as the potential No. 1 overall pick. articles._body: The Detroit Red Wings could receive a timely boost to their lineup as two injured forwards near their returns. Marco Kasper and Mason Appleton are both expected to rejoin the team at some point during its upcoming four-game road trip, giving head coach Todd McLellan additional options as Detroit continues its season. The team has also seen encouraging signs from rookie Michael Brandsegg-Nygård adding another reason for optimism in Detroit. McLellan provided an encouraging update on both players , telling reporters that he anticipates their availability before the road trip concludes. According to The Athletic’s Max Bultman, McLellan said he expects Kasper and Appleton to play during the trip, while defenseman Albert Johansson could need more time before returning. Kasper missed Detroit’s season opener with an upper-body injury. The 22-year-old center could strengthen the team’s lineup when he returns. His comeback would also give McLellan another option at center. Appleton left the lineup after Detroit’s second game and landed on injured reserve. The 30-year-old winger recorded six hits in his first two appearances. He could also add valuable depth to the team’s bottom six once he returns. Detroit’s upcoming schedule gives both players an opportunity to make their comebacks on the road. The four-game stretch begins Saturday against the Colorado Avalanche and runs through November 14, when the Red Wings visit the Tampa Bay Lightning. Getting Kasper and Appleton back would give head coach Todd McLellan more options as he looks to stabilize the lineup and build momentum. Their returns could also provide a timely boost amid questions surrounding Dylan Larkin’s uncertain future in Detroit , while Johansson’s recovery timeline remains unclear. articles.title: Illinois football HC hits SEC with perfect dig after impressive win over Nebraska
articles.summary: Illinois football clinched bowl eligibility for the third consecutive season after taking down Nebraska 24-13 at Gies Memorial Stadium on Friday night. The win extended the Fighting Illini’s winning streak to four games, improved their overall record to 6-3 and moved them to 4-2 in Big Ten
articles._body: Illinois football clinched bowl eligibility for the third consecutive season after taking down Nebraska 24-13 at Gies Memorial Stadium on Friday night. The win extended the Fighting Illini’s winning streak to four games, improved their overall record to 6-3 and moved them to 4-2 in Big Ten play. However, head coach Bret Bielema had another reason to celebrate after the win, using the opportunity to take a subtle shot at the SEC and the College Football Playoff rankings. Speaking to reporters after the game, Bielema pointed out how difficult it is to reach postseason play in three consecutive seasons, particularly while building a program. He further alluded to Illinois’ demolition of another team boasting a 5–3 record, suggesting that the Fighting Illini would receive considerably more recognition if they competed in the SEC. “I think about as we’re building things here at Illinois, now we’re three seasons in a row that we’ll have postseason play, which is absolutely awesome and really hard for anybody,” said Bielema. “But to be in this job, where we’re at right now, 6-3, we beat another 5-3 team. If we were in the SEC, we’d probably be a top-15 team. We’ve just got to continue to stay on track where we’re at and do a really good job of holding the moment and putting ourselves in a position to be successful.” The victory over the Huskers was largely powered by quarterback Katin Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon. Houser completed 22 of 36 attempts for 292 yards and three touchdowns, while Dixon recorded eight receptions for 129 yards and two scores. Dixon also set a new program single-season record for touchdown receptions. His 12th touchdown catch of the campaign surpassed the previous program record by two. His first scoring reception, a three-yard catch late in the second quarter, brought Illinois level at 7-7 heading into halftime. The Fighting Illini took control early in the third quarter through an unexpected special-teams play. Facing fourth-and-12, Illinois executed a fake field goal, with punter and holder Lars Rau running 29 yards to move the offense inside the five-yard line. Jordan Anderson subsequently caught a five-yard touchdown pass from Houser to give the Fighting Illini a 14-7 advantage. Dixon added another touchdown early in the fourth quarter, and Ethan Moczulski converted a 21-yard field goal to complete the win. Defensively, Matthew Bailey led Illinois with 11 tackles, a forced fumble and half a sack. James Kreutz contributed 10 tackles, while Mason Muragin came away with a sack on Nebraska’s final possession. The Fighting Illini have now allowed no more than 17 points in each of their last three games following a 37-point outing against Michigan State. Illinois has also surrendered an average of 20.2 points per game across its five contests since defensive coordinator Bobby Hauck’s departure. With bowl eligibility secured, the Fighting Illini now face a challenging stretch versus No. 5 UCLA, No. 21 Iowa and Northwestern. Illinois will next travel to Los Angeles on November 13 to face the Bruins, who remain unbeaten in Big Ten play. articles._body: The BYU football team have been waiting to get star running back LJ Martin back from injury. And they will finally get him back for the Holy War against fierce rivals Utah. ESPN’s Pete Thamel confirmed the big news during College GameDay. NEWS: BYU star tailback LJ Martin will play today. From @CollegeGameDay . pic.twitter.com/ttoVsvJwTb — Pete Thamel (@PeteThamel) November 7, 2026 In addition to that, ESPN’s Taylor McGregor has reported that Martin will start for the Cougars if he clears his pre-game health checks. The BYU running back has been on course to play after missing the last month with an ankle injury. The expectation is that he might play a limited part in the game, although the extent of his role will be determined when he’s evaluated before the game. Nevertheless, the Cougars will still be happy to have the senior running back available for the Holy War. Martin rushed for 1,305 yards with 12 touchdowns last season as he was named the Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year. Unfortunately, Martin has missed the Cougars’ last four games after getting hurt against TCU. But even though he has missed half the season, he is still BYU’s leading rusher with 344 yards on an impressive 7.8 yards per carry. In his absence, Preston Rex and Sione Moa have carried the load in the Cougars’ backfield. Rex has rushed for 223 yards, including a season-high 66 yards in BYU’s big win over then-No. 2 Notre Dame . Meanwhile, Moa has three rushing touchdowns in his last two games. Rex did not feature in BYU’s 27-20 win over Arizona State, though, and it remains to be seen if he will be back against Utah. With both Rex and Martin missing, the Cougars could only get 47 yards on 1.6 yards per carry against the Sun Devils. BYU will be hoping Martin’s return can help improve the running game. articles.summary:

Whenever XMPP or Matrix threads pop up on HN, several commenters casually mention their "friends and family XMPP (or Matrix) server."

H
articles._body: I love open-source software and open protocols, but my family and friends primarily communicate through SMS for exactly the reasons in https://xkcd.com/2365/ Whenever XMPP or Matrix threads pop up on HN, several commenters casually mention their "friends and family XMPP (or Matrix) server." How did you convince friends and family to move away from SMS/WhatsApp and replace it with a niche messaging app? My family and friends aren't hardcore nerdy, but they're more tech-savvy than average. Their needs in messaging are mainly pragmatic: they want ease of use, reliability, and fun features. They don't care that much about privacy, decentralization, or extensibility (though I care about those things a lot). I've been experimenting with self-hosting XMPP and Matrix servers and clients in the past week, and the UX is even worse than I expected. It seems like all the clients either imitate Slack, imitate Discord, or imitate hot garbage. I haven't seen any that try to be a simple, friendly replacement for SMS. I'm a software developer who uses computers all day, and I find the UX for most of the clients incredibly hard to use. The only angle I could see to pitch XMPP/Matrix to people for non-philosophical reasons are that there's a more consistent experience across iOS/Android. The biggest shortcoming I think is visible to regular users is that there's feature degradation and missing information when iOS users have SMS conversations with Android users, especially in group chats. For people who have successfully won family and friends to XMPP or Matrix, what was your pitch? What do you recommend others do to make XMPP or Matrix an attractive experience for a regular person? articles._body: The Oklahoma State football team has surprised a lot of people this season, under first-year head coach Eric Morris. The Cowboys have quarterback Drew Mestemaker leading the way. A glaring stat though is showing why Mestemaker may not be selected as the top quarterback in the 2027 NFL Draft. “Through Week 9 of 2026, Mestemaker has seven turnover-worthy plays on 54 dropbacks when he was pressured, according to PFF. That’s a 13.0% rate, more than double the 5.8% median for the first-round quarterbacks in our historical comparison,” CBS Sports reported. Mestemaker is playing in the Big 12 this season after previously playing at North Texas. He followed his head coach Morris from North Texas to Stillwater. Even at his previous stop, the quarterback struggled under pressure. “Mestemaker’s struggles have followed him from North Texas to Oklahoma State. His turnover-worthy-play rate was 8.3% under pressure in 2025 before climbing to 13% so far this season. Over that span, he’s put the ball in harm’s way 13 times in 126 such situations. That’s a 10.3% rate, and it’s something NFL evaluators will have to consider,” CBS added. This season Mestemaker has passed for 2,649 yards. He has 25 touchdown passes and seven interceptions. He has helped Oklahoma State completely turn around from where they were a year ago, when they didn’t win a single conference game. However, last week’s 19-15 loss to the Detroit Lions revealed issues that could become increasingly challenging to address against stronger opponents. There is considerable concern surrounding the quarterback position, especially with Kyler Murray dealing with a hamstring injury and Carson Wentz preparing to face the Buffalo Bills. Additionally, the Vikings face another significant issue to resolve before the November 10 trade deadline: a major injury has forced the offensive line to make adjustments. Early on, the results were promising, as the Vikings showed improvement in managing pressure and maintaining a more consistent pocket, but their progress took a major hit when left guard Donovan Jackson suffered a torn meniscus during Minnesota’s victory over Miami in early October. The injury required surgery, and head coach Kevin O’Connell said Jackson will likely miss the rest of the regular season. Jackson had been developing into a key contributor, giving Minnesota a young offensive lineman capable of handling increasingly demanding responsibilities. His absence forced the Vikings to make adjustments at a position where continuity is particularly crucial. His recent injury has introduced further uncertainty, with Wentz preparing to lead the offense against Buffalo on Monday night. The Vikings have enough talent to withstand individual mistakes, but consistently relying on their quarterbacks to compensate for breakdowns in protection makes operating the offense much more challenging. Adding Dickerson could help solve this problem with his experience and physicality, giving Minnesota a reliable interior blocker capable of making an immediate impact. At 28 years old, Dickerson is still young enough to contribute beyond the current season, which is an important consideration for the Minnesota Vikings as they aim to compete now without jeopardizing their long-term development. Dickerson’s experience would also enhance the Vikings’ running game. The team has faced challenges in consistently generating explosive offensive plays, making it increasingly important to establish manageable situations on early downs, and a powerful interior blocker like Dickerson could help create more favorable running lanes and reduce the number of obvious passing situations that allow opposing defenses to mount aggressive attacks. articles.title: Predators’ Steven Stamkos’ immediate reaction to scoring overtime winner vs. Avalanche
articles.summary: The Nashville Predators‘ decision to sign Steven Stamkos continues to pay dividends as the veteran forward delivered another clutch performance, scoring the overtime winner in a 3-2 victory over the Colorado Avalanche on Thursday at Ball Arena. Reflecting on his game-winning goal, Stamkos h
articles._body: The Nashville Predators ‘ decision to sign Steven Stamkos continues to pay dividends as the veteran forward delivered another clutch performance, scoring the overtime winner in a 3-2 victory over the Colorado Avalanche on Thursday at Ball Arena. Reflecting on his game-winning goal , Stamkos highlighted the importance of capitalizing on Nashville’s power-play opportunity, particularly after failing to convert on his earlier chances. “You get a power play in overtime, it’s, obviously, a great opportunity,” Stamkos said. “I had a few chances earlier on the power plays, and didn’t get quite the shot that I wanted to, and that one felt really good coming off the stick.” Stamkos earned the opportunity by drawing a hooking penalty against Colorado defenseman Devon Toews late in overtime. Roman Josi then set him up at the left face-off circle, where the veteran forward unleashed a one-timer past Mackenzie Blackwood at 2:18 to secure Nashville’s victory. The goal was also a milestone for the 36-year-old. His 247th career power-play goal moved him past Phil Esposito and tied Luc Robitaille for fifth place on the NHL’s all-time list. Nashville also received goals from Ross Colton and rookie Vitali Pinchuk, who recorded his first NHL goal. Ryan O’Reilly contributed two assists, while Justus Annunen stopped 30 shots. The victory extended the Predators’ winning streak to three games and gave them four wins in their last six outings. Nashville improved to 7-4-5 with 19 points, moving within one point of Colorado, which fell to 9-6-2 following its second consecutive loss. For Stamkos, the overtime finish capped an important team effort and another valuable step forward for Nashville. But the delay in a Downs deal is apparently due to the Colts looking for a team that can meet their asking price. As reported by ESPN’s Ian Rapoport a
articles._body: The Indianapolis Colts have yet to trade Josh Downs despite his trade reques t, coupled with interest in the wide receiver around the league . But the delay in a Downs deal is apparently due to the Colts looking for a team that can meet their asking price. As reported by ESPN’s Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter, the Colts have been telling teams they already have an offer of a fourth-round pick for Downs. That’s lower than the Colts’ original asking price of a third-rounder for the wide receiver. It remains to be seen whether the Colts are being truthful about that fourth-round offer being on the table as they look to bump up the price for Downs. If they are, then Downs is as good as gone before the trade deadline. He’s on the last year of his contract, and the logical move would be for the Colts to get what they can for him (in this case, a fourth-rounder) instead of losing him for nothing. But if the deadline passes and Downs is still on the team, then that would raise some questions about there actually being an offer on the table. Choosing not to trade him just because they could only get a fourth instead of a third that they wanted wouldn’t make much sense. Either way, it won’t be long before the resolution to the Downs trade sage is finally known. At this point, it would be a surprise if he does not get dealt away regardless of whether it’s for a third or fourth-rounder. When we write it is one of our emotions writing it. We want to talk to ourselves between these debating ideas and emotions. We are solo but also there are persons inside us. That's where the name is from solo-us. In Solous, you can reply to your own message anytime. It supports normal stuff like tag and search. I try to make it as secure as possible with e2ee as an option. I am the sole builder of the app. I built this app mostly for myself in my free time with Claude. Yes I vibed 100% but I am familiar with aws and python, I am a decent programmer. It is true that these days, everyone can do that. But it still takes time and effort to make it run smoothly and polish features and make it easy to use. I don't believe the future of software is everyone vibe their own stuff. The most efficient way is still to use several good apps. I think there may be more diversity instead of everyone use app store or play store. Because it is made for myself, it has no reminder emails, sometimes, I even don't journal for days, but I feel good when I write one. I think it is good to record what happened in life. Especially when I feel bad. And it is private, it has two factor login, security keys such as face id or whatever you use to unlock your phone, and it has optional end to end encryption. At first I want to make it default, but then I realized it takes some time to setup and maybe it will reduce conversion. so I leave it for whoever care about privacy. The app is free for now. articles.title: Portugal names Real Madrid star new captain after Cristiano Ronaldo retirement
articles.summary: Portugal has named Real Madrid midfielder Bernardo Silva as its new national team captain following Cristiano Ronaldo’s international retirement. The 32-year-old, who ended his trophy-filled spell at Manchester City this summer, will inherit the armband after Ronaldo concluded his remarkabl
articles._body: Portugal has named Real Madrid midfielder Bernardo Silva as its new national team captain following Cristiano Ronaldo’s international retirement. The 32-year-old, who ended his trophy-filled spell at Manchester City this summer, will inherit the armband after Ronaldo concluded his remarkable 23-year international career. Portugal manager Jorge Jesus confirmed the leadership change during Friday’s squad announcement ahead of the upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures. Transfer insider Fabrizio Romano reported Silva’s new captaincy role on Saturday, signaling the beginning of a new chapter for Portuguese soccer. Silva has earned 115 international appearances, making him the most experienced player in Portugal’s leadership group. Jesus also identified Ruben Dias, Joao Cancelo, Ruben Neves and Bruno Fernandes as other potential captains. The Portuguese manager praised Silva’s experience and current performances at Real Madrid. He highlighted the midfielder’s ability to compete regularly at one of Europe’s biggest clubs. Silva joined Madrid during the summer after leaving Manchester City, where he enjoyed considerable domestic and European success. His growing influence at club level now coincides with greater responsibility for his country. Meanwhile, Ronaldo’s departure closes an extraordinary chapter in Portugal’s history. The 41-year-old retired with 234 international appearances and 146 goals, both men’s international records. Ronaldo had previously opened up about his eventual retirement plans , emphasizing the importance of maintaining his motivation to continue playing. He also helped Portugal win the 2016 European Championship and two UEFA Nations League titles. Portugal will begin its post-Ronaldo era with Nations League fixtures against Denmark on November 14 and Wales on November 17. For Silva, replacing one of soccer’s most influential captains brings significant expectations. Portugal will now look to its experienced midfielder to guide the national team into a new era. articles.title: Billionaire Brian Chesky’s social-worker parents told him to pick a high-paying career. He went to art school—and started Airbnb with 3 air beds
articles.summary: Chesky’s mother, herself a social worker, was worried when he became an art student. He started Airbnb when he was barely making rent.
articles._body: Before Airbnb had over 9 million listings worldwide, there was one sole lodging: three inflatable air beds at CEO Brian Chesky’s San Francisco home. He had quit his job and packed up all his belongings in a Honda Civic to make a cross-country move, and couldn’t pay his rent. That’s when he noticed all the local hotels were booked because of the Industrial Designers Society of America’s International Design Conference in San Francisco, and a business was born. “We called it the air-bed-and-breakfast,” he told Fortune in 2017 at a World’s Greatest Leaders event. Chesky and Airbnb cofounder Joe Gebbia were hooked on the idea of making money and meeting new friends through their makeshift accommodations, so they opened their home to three guests: “What if you could book someone’s home the way you could book a hotel anywhere in the world?” Chesky said about their inspiration. They launched Airbnb with Gebbia’s former roommate Nathan Blecharczyk in 2008. Chesky’s social-worker parents in upstate New York (he was born in Albany) told him to pursue a high-paying career, but much to their chagrin he went to art school instead, at the famous Rhode Island School of Design. “I’m going to become an artist,” Chesky recalls telling his mom, to which she responded: “You somehow managed to pick the only job in the world that pays less than a social worker. You’ll get paid nothing.” Today, Chesky doesn’t have to worry as much. Airbnb has a market capitalization of $112 billion, above its level from before the pandemic, which threatened its very survival as a business. The company lost 80% of its business in the first months of the pandemic, and Chesky reorganized it in a scramble for survival. View this post on Instagram A post shared by FORTUNE (@fortunemag) How was Chesky’s business ethos shaped by his creative background ? Though Chesky’s creativity is what birthed (and saved) Airbnb, it also meant business veterans did not initially take him seriously. Chesky’s design background was at first a hindrance to a budding Airbnb. While looking for $150,000 to fund an estimated 10% of the company, Chesky met with over 20 potential investors, all of whom turned him down. “Joe and I were designers, and as far as they were concerned, designers didn’t start companies,” Chesky said. “We didn’t look like a tech founder, which is ridiculous because I don’t think you should ever hire somebody because they look like something else. You want a new thing.” Investors didn’t take an interest in Airbnb until it began designing presidential-candidate-themed cereal boxes , which eventually got the attention of Paul Graham, founder of startup accelerator Y Combinator. “Creative companies are companies that tap into a sense of imagination,” Chesky told Time . “That they might come up with new breakthrough ideas, that people that were only beholden to near-term measurable outcomes won’t ever have.” How has Airbnb navigated challenges? Success at Airbnb has been a double-edged sword. Explosive growth has forced the company to refocus at times.  During the pandemic, Chesky told Fortune in 2023, he even opened his own home as an Airbnb to better understand the host experience and lived in various Airbnbs across the country for six months, where he discovered inconsistent and unnecessary practices across hosts, including complicated rent agreements. Airbnb still faces challenges as waves of short-term rental regulations in New York and across Europe, where cities are implementing phase-outs, prohibiting rentals for less than 30 days, or no longer renewing tourist apartment licenses, for example. In the U.S., housing advocates have fought against Airbnb, according to the AP , claiming short-term rentals have essentially become hotels.  Airbnb has pushed back against regulations, saying that short-term rental bans would limit affordable accommodations for travelers. Last month, Airbnb implemented a new “reasonable house rules and requests” policy , where the company has stopped asking guests to “complete tasks that require significant effort or time, or would typically be performed by a cleaner,” such as stripping the bed, washing and putting away dishes, or taking trash offsite. The new policy, which will go into effect on rentals booked on or after Nov. 20, has drawn pushback as hosts threaten to boycott or hike cleaning fees, and been a pleasant surprise to customers. A version of this story was published on Fortune.com on Jan. 24, 2024. Furious hosts are threatening to boycott and raise cleaning fees Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky warns two types of people won’t survive the AI era : ‘pure people managers’ and workers who resist change This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Starter homes cost $1 million in a record 242 U.S. cities—proof the affordability crisis has hit the homes meant for first-time buyers
articles.summary: The first rung on the property ladder now costs seven figures in a record 242 cities, a new Zillow report shows.
articles._body: They waited out the pandemic boom. They saved longer, rented longer, delayed longer, and watched the typical first-time homebuyer age climb to a record 40 . Now, the buyers who did everything right are running into a new problem: The Northeast just became the fastest-growing region for million-dollar starter homes in the country. It’s especially imperfectly timed for millennials entering their peak household spending years and beginning to form their own families (or at least try to). A Zillow report published in June counts a record 242 U.S. cities where starter homes cost $1 million or more—triple the 80 cities that cleared that mark before the pandemic, and up from 226 a year ago. The share of first-time buyers has fallen to half the historical norm. For millennial parents in the Northeast—now in their late thirties and early forties, often with kids, hunting for more space—the numbers have a specific shape. New Jersey had just one million-dollar starter city before the pandemic. Now it has 26. New York used to have 12; now it has 41. The two states added 15 cities to the list in the past year alone—faster growth than anywhere else in the country. The New York City metro area now leads all with 63 cities where a starter home runs $1 million or more. That growth didn’t happen in a vacuum. Six of the 10 most competitive housing markets in the country are in the Northeast, per Zillow’s 2026 analysis, a region where new construction has chronically lagged and inventory deficits run deepest. California still leads the raw count with 105 cities, but the Northeast is where the crisis is actively spreading. “A housing shortage a decade in the making ran headlong into intense demand with mortgage rates at historic lows, driving up home values at a record pace,” Zillow senior economist Kara Ng wrote. For Northeast buyers, those forces have compounded. The new typical first-time homebuyer is 40 First-time homebuyers are historically younger, although the typical age of first-time buyers climbed to an all-time high of 40 , according to a National Association of Realtors report released in November 2025. In fact, the housing market has gotten so unaffordable that the number of first-time homebuyers fell to half the historical norm last July.  A rising price floor on starter homes only pushes that first home purchase further out of reach. And it’s a problem that’s worsened, especially during the past couple of years. “For homebuyers, the prevalence of million-dollar cities significantly—greatly—strains what is already the worst housing affordability since at least the 1980s ,” Christopher M. Naghibi, executive vice president and chief operating officer at First Foundation Bank , told Fortune in 2024 when Zillow released a report about the number of U.S. cities with $1 million median-priced homes. “Prospective buyers in these markets face higher barriers to entry, needing ridiculously large down payments and higher incomes to afford homes.” That still holds true today. Zillow defines a starter home as one in the lowest third of home values in a given region. As of June, the typical starter home nationwide was worth $198,649, up 1.7% from a year earlier. But in well over 200 U.S. cities, starter home prices are a whopping five times as high as that. It’s a phenomenon that keeps spreading, and into places it never used to touch. Zillow chalks it up to the effects of the pandemic housing boom. It’s not just a California problem anymore Before 2020, the list of cities with $1 million starter homes was almost all coastal. Colorado was the only non-coastal state with a million-dollar starter-home city. Now 26 states have at least one, up from nine before the pandemic. Texas, Wyoming, and Illinois each have multiple examples. California still leads with 105 cities, but the fastest growth is in the Northeast. New York and New Jersey added 15 cities combined over the past year. New York is now up to 41, from just 12 before the pandemic. New Jersey is at 26, up from one. The New York City metro area tops all metros with 63 cities where a starter home runs $1 million or more. San Francisco follows with 37, then Los Angeles with 33, San Jose with 13, and Miami and Seattle with eight each. The trend aligns with Zillow’s 2026 hottest markets analysis , which found six of the 10 most competitive housing markets are in the Northeast, where new construction has lagged and inventory deficits run deep. The pandemic reset the cost of buying a home. A housing shortage a decade in the making collided with surging demand and historically low mortgage rates, pushing values up at a record pace. Those effects have stuck. Baby boomers edge younger buyers out of the housing market The squeeze on millennials and Gen Z has been building for years. Baby boomers, sitting on paid-off homes or cheap pandemic-era mortgages, have edged younger buyers out of the market in record numbers. The cost has pushed some Americans to delay milestones like marriage and kids, and others to co-buy homes with friends or partners just to split the bill. Others have done the opposite—had kids first, rented longer, and are now hunting for space in a market that moved against them.  “We’re seeing a reshaping of the housing ladder,” Alexandra Gupta, a real-estate broker with the Corcoran Group, previously told Fortune . “Some first-time buyers are turning to long-term renting or even co-living models because the idea of owning a home has become so out of reach.” There are modest signs of relief. Conditions are slowly turning friendlier for buyers. Zillow found the typical buyer now breaks even versus renting after about six years, down from more than eight in late 2023. More inventory and slower price growth mean buyers who are financially prepared are in better shape than they had been. One of the least penalized teams in the league. Playing really smart in all three phases, so it’ll be a great test. And we are looking forward to it,” Heupel said, per On3. Heupel says his defense must play a near-perfect game to defeat the Wildcats. “Defensively, we got to control the line of scrimmage. You got to get them into third ball situations. You got to get them off the field. There’s a lot of eye candy shift-trade motion before the snap. So communication at all three levels of the defense, playing in sync will be critical in this one too,” Heupel said. Heupel has been the head coach at Tennessee since 2021. His Volunteers have had some very successful seasons, but are still looking for the school’s first national championship in his tenure there. Tennessee is currently 3-2 in the SEC. articles.title: This CEO lived on canned soup and took just two days off for his daughter’s birth. Now, he admits he lost sight of proper work-life balance
articles.summary: Ron Schneidermann, CEO of test prep company Acely, is urging Gen Z to do it differently.
articles._body: The grind to success can be long, punishing, and it can quietly take more than it gives.  Ron Schneidermann knows that better than most.  After scaling his first company, Liftopia, into a business with more than $60 million in annual revenue, he went on to become CEO of AllTrails, the popular hiking map app. Today, he leads test-prep startup Acely . But looking back across his career, he says he had to learn the hard way what real work-life balance actually costs—and what it’s worth. While building Liftopia, a digital marketplace for ski resorts, that mindset came at a personal price. Schneidermann worked out of a cramped San Francisco apartment, turned spending less than $15 a day into a kind of endurance test, and went two years without taking a salary, surviving largely on canned soup. The tradeoffs even extended into his family life. When his first daughter was born four years into Liftopia, he took just two days off work. Three years later, he allowed himself just a week for his son’s birth—and thought that was progress. “I look back, I was just able to justify it as ‘that’s just part of the grind’… but you never get that time back,” Schneidermann told Fortune . “That was a mistake.” It’s not an easy admission in startup culture, where sacrifice is often worn as a badge of honor and overwork is normalized as the price of ambition. But Schneidermann, now in his late 40s, has since reframed the experience entirely. “For everything that was frustrating, that went wrong, that I regretted about Liftopia, I was able to take the inverse and turn it into a strength,” he said. By the time he joined AllTrails in 2015, that mindset shift was already underway. He eventually became CEO in 2019 and instituted a company-wide ritual: the first Friday of every month, AllTrails shut down and employees were encouraged to go outside. In August 2025, he took on the new challenge of becoming CEO of Acely. This time, he’s bringing those hard-won lessons with him from the start. Instead of monthly trail days, the company now runs a monthly “hackathon,” where its less than a dozen employees pause routine work for the whole day and experiment with AI tools and new ideas—no meetings, no KPIs, no deliverables. Ron Schneidermann says he’ll never take a job for its salary ever again Even before Schneidermann had his eyes on entrepreneurship, he was learning career lessons the hard way. In the late 1990s, he was a student at UCLA studying mass communication and business while also working at Abercrombie & Fitch to help pay for his studies. However, he ended up getting fired three separate times because he “never liked it” enough to muster the proper decorum. Similarly, after graduating in 2000, he landed a job at Accenture working as a business process consultant. Once again, though, he found it not aligning with the life he wanted to have. And despite the lucrative salary of working at a Fortune 500 consulting firm, he quit. “It was a great experience. I’m grateful for it, but I hated it,” he said. “I hated it, and I told myself, I am never going to take a job for money again. Life is too short.” That realization eventually pushed him toward startups.  Through a friend of a friend, he landed a role at Hotwire, then a travel startup that was later acquired by Expedia , and it became his entry point into the tech world. Looking back, Schneidermann said that early career path offers a lesson he wishes more young workers would take seriously: relationships matter as much as résumés, especially in a job market where traditional entry-level pipelines are narrowing. “Really invest in your network,” he said. “There’s a small pond at the end of the day. If you stay in it long enough, you are going to know everyone, and everyone you know are going to be leaders somewhere.” Digital-native Gen Zers can boost their careers by working to build real relationships Schneidermann’s point may resonate with Gen Z at a time when employers say early-career workers are struggling with basic professional norms. A 2024 survey found that six in 10 bosses admitted they had already fired Gen Z employees hired straight out of college, citing poor communication, lack of professionalism, and disorganization. For Schneidermann, the issue isn’t just skills—it’s mindset. Too many young workers treat networking as transactional, when in reality it’s built on consistency, reputation, and how you show up over time. That starts with small, often overlooked behaviors. “There’s a human on the other end. Don’t ghost people and just show up,” he said. The same principle applies more broadly to career growth. Rather than chasing the perfect role or obsessing over credentials, Schneidermann emphasized curiosity as the real differentiator. “Just approach everything with a curious mindset,” he added. “Just constantly try to be learning and exploring.” That philosophy has carried through multiple career pivots, including his most recent move to Acely, a startup with no obvious connection to his background. After being approached by an executive search firm, he took the job in part because his high school–aged daughter had recently used the product for SAT prep. She was among its over 50,000 active users. For Schneidermann, the challenge was one he was eager to take on. From his perspective, he didn’t need to be an expert in the industry—he just needed to be willing to learn it.  A version of this story was published on  Fortune.com  on April 25, 2026. articles.title: Broncos rumors: Denver ‘outrageously’ checks in on potential Trey McBride trade
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos have explored the tight end market ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, including an inquiry about Arizona Cardinals star Trey McBride, as they seek more production from the position. Denver sits alone atop the AFC West at 6-2, but starting tight end Evan Engram has just 13 c
articles._body: The Denver Broncos have explored the tight end market ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, including an inquiry about Arizona Cardinals star Trey McBride, as they seek more production from the position. Denver sits alone atop the AFC West at 6-2, but starting tight end Evan Engram has just 13 catches for 136 yards and one touchdown through eight games. He went without a reception on three targets in last week’s 28-24 win over the Kansas City Chiefs. ESPN’s Adam Schefter detailed the Broncos’ interest Saturday on X, formerly Twitter, sharing an update from a trade-deadline report he co-wrote with Ian Rapoport. The Denver Broncos have checked in around the league on tight ends, going so far as to ambitiously — and some would say outrageously — check on Cardinals star Trey McBride, who is from Fort Morgan, Colorado, and played at Colorado State. The Cardinals made it very clear they… https://t.co/fz5M8XuzSF pic.twitter.com/7M5uZb4uKo — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 7, 2026 McBride leads the NFL with 66 receptions on 86 targets this season after earning first-team All-Pro honors in 2025. That total includes 10 catches for 111 yards and a touchdown against the Broncos in Week 7, when Denver won 30-16 in Glendale. The star tight end’s Colorado roots add another layer to Denver’s interest. He grew up a Broncos fan in Fort Morgan and played at Colorado State, so a trade would bring him home to the team he supported as a child. Arizona’s stance on McBride comes despite its willingness to move other players. The Cardinals have already sent quarterback Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens, showing that their deadline activity depends on the player involved. The full report indicates the Broncos turned their attention elsewhere after the Cardinals rejected the inquiry. It does not establish that the teams discussed compensation or that Denver submitted an offer for McBride. Engram’s contract expires after this season, adding a longer-term consideration at the position beyond Denver’s immediate needs. With Tuesday’s November 10 NFL trade deadline approaching, the Broncos continue searching for tight end help while the Cardinals remain unwilling to move McBride. articles._body: The New York Giants have been linked with the Indianapolis Colts’ Jonathan Taylor as they search for another running back ahead of the trade deadline. They have also asked about a certain Baltimore Ravens running back, but it’s not Derrick Henry. As ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported, the Ravens are not expected to trade Henry before the deadline. Patricia Traina quote tweeted that report and added that the Giants asked about Henry’s teammate Justice Hill. Hill, 28, has spent seven seasons with the Ravens, and this season is shaping up to be his best one yet. Through nine games, he already has 240 rushing yards, putting him on pace for 453 yards. That would shatter his previous career-high of 387 yards he set in 2023. He’s also averaging 7.3 yards per carry, which is far and away a career best. Hill exploded for 85 yards on just nine carries against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night. That includes a 65-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. The Giants currently have Cam Skateboo as their starting RB. The second-year player has a team-leading 418 yards with two touchdowns through seven games. However, he has had injury concerns as well as fumble issues this season. Hill is not a workhorse like Taylor or Henry but is more of a change-of-pace back who could provide the Giants backfield a different look. With the Giants in a great position to win the NFC East, Hill would be a potential running back upgrade at a cheaper price compared to what it would cost to get Taylor. The battle for megawatts: why restricting data centers is a strategic mistake
articles.summary: Power must reach new computing capacity in time.
articles._body: In Ireland, data centers consume nearly a quarter of the country’s electricity. New grid connections around Dublin were effectively frozen for three years. Under revised rules , new projects must provide generation or storage capacity onsite or nearby. Amsterdam previously imposed a moratorium on new facilities, while Frankfurt regulates their location through zoning. In July 2026, New York State introduced a moratorium of up to one year on certain environmental permits for new large data centers. State officials said the pause would allow them to assess the facilities’ impact on the power grid and the environment. As of May 2026, data center projects representing nearly 12 GW of potential demand were in the state’s grid interconnection queue. Should governments restrict data centers when power grids cannot keep pace? I believe they should expand power supply and grid capacity instead. As co-founder and general partner of Roosh Investment Group, I have been investing in technology companies for over five years. Our portfolio includes AI infrastructure, and energy is now a key focus. This experience has shown me how access to energy infrastructure influences investment decisions. Reliable power is increasingly becoming a decisive factor in a company’s ability to scale and attract capital. As businesses rely more on AI, control over its models and infrastructure matters more. A foreign provider’s decision to change terms, raise prices, or restrict access could affect entire industries. Domestic computing capacity gives countries more control over the infrastructure their businesses depend on. Control over AI is becoming a source of economic power This helps explain the intensity of U.S.–China competition in AI. American companies hold leading positions across the AI stack, from advanced models and chips to major cloud platforms. Washington views the power supply for data center infrastructure as a national security issue. Beijing is pursuing a state-led strategy. Its “Eastern Data, Western Computing” program directs the development of computing capacity toward western China, where energy and land resources are more readily available. At the same time, the country is expanding power generation at scale. According to the International Energy Agency , China added nearly 500 GW of renewable capacity in 2025—more than 60% of the global increase. Europe, meanwhile, risks falling further behind. Brussels plans up to seven AI gigafactories and at least a tripling of EU data center capacity within five to seven years. Yet some countries are slowing construction, while European businesses still rely primarily on American cloud providers. Restrictions do not remove demand for AI; they risk pushing investment abroad and reinforcing that dependence. The bottleneck is local Data centers’ hunger for power should be understood in the context of wider electricity demand. According to the International Energy Agency, they accounted for only around 70 TWh of the 800 TWh increase in global electricity consumption in 2025. Industry, air conditioning, heat pumps, and electric vehicles contributed far more. The challenge is rapidly growing demand concentrated in a handful of locations. Power must reach new computing capacity in time. What is holding up connections? In the U.S., lead times for large transformers now exceed two years, compared with roughly 50 weeks before the pandemic. Morgan Stanley estimates that U.S. data centers could face a power shortfall of around 49 GW by 2028. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has acknowledged that power has become the company’s binding constraint. Some of its GPUs are sitting in inventory with nowhere to plug them in. Dedicated gas-fired plants offer no quick fix. GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, and Mitsubishi Power produce around two-thirds of the world’s gas turbines, and their factories are booked years ahead. GE Vernova reported 116 GW in gas power equipment orders and slot reservations, while targeting annual turbine output of 20 GW in the third quarter of 2026. The hardware itself adds another challenge. A server rack once required 7–12 kW. Systems built around NVIDIA’s GB200 consume 120–132 kW per rack. Conventional air cooling is no longer sufficient at that power density, so new facilities must be designed for liquid cooling from the outset. Tech giants are securing power themselves. Microsoft agreed to buy electricity from the 835 MW Three Mile Island reactor, which is being restarted to serve its needs. Google’s agreement with Kairos Power calls for small modular reactors, with the first expected online by 2030. Governments cannot rely on corporate initiative alone. They must plan energy and digital infrastructure together: expand grids, accelerate transformer production, streamline connections, and encourage long-term power purchase agreements, generation near data centers, and storage. How war accelerated distributed generation in Ukraine Ukraine’s experience shows how a crisis can accelerate the deployment of local generation. War and repeated attacks forced the country to rapidly deploy local power sources where the centralized grid could no longer guarantee a reliable supply. My experience investing in technology companies has shown me that reliable infrastructure is essential for business growth. In Ukraine, companies have long had to manage energy risks. They need reliable electricity, backup power, and plans for potential outages. This also matters to investors. A company’s ability to operate during power outages affects how they assess its potential for growth. Ukraine already has around 1.8 GW of distributed gas-fired generation, with more than 500 MW under construction. It is also streamlining grid connection and permitting procedures. Ukraine’s experience cannot be directly applied to large AI data centers. But it illustrates how making energy resilience a priority can accelerate investment in additional generation and changes to connection procedures,

articles.title: Bret Bielema after Illinois' 6th win: 'If we were in the SEC, we'd probably be a top-15 team'
articles.summary: With a Friday night victory over Nebraska, Illinois is bowl-eligible once again. The Fighting Illini will play in a bowl game for the third straight season, and Bret Bielema tossed some shade at the SEC while celebrating the achievement. Illinois got three passing touchdowns from Katin Houser to get
articles._body: With a Friday night victory over Nebraska , Illinois is bowl-eligible once again. The Fighting Illini will play in a bowl game for the third straight season, and Bret Bielema tossed some shade at the SEC while celebrating the achievement. Illinois got three passing touchdowns from Katin Houser to get the 24-13 victory over Nebraska at Gies Memorial Stadium on Saturday. It’s the Fighting Illini’s fourth straight win after their change at defensive coordinator and sent them to a third consecutive bowl game for the first time since the early 1990s. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Speaking with reporters postgame, Bielema made clear how proud he was of the program’s run. He then noted Illinois beat another 5-3 team to get there, which is why he the SEC wound up in the crosshairs as he shaded the College Football Playoff rankings. “I think about as we’re building things here at Illinois, now we’re three seasons in a row that we’ll have postseason play, which is absolutely awesome and really hard for anybody,” Bielema said during his press conference . Watch on Fubo (Try for Free) “But to be in this job, where we’re at right now, 6-3, we beat another 5-3 team. If we were in the SEC, we’d probably be a top-15 team. We’ve just got to continue to stay on track where we’re at and do a really good job of holding the moment and putting ourselves in a position to be successful.” Collin Dixon made some big plays for Illinois to help lead the Fighting Illini offense. He hauled in eight receptions for 129 yards and three touchdowns as the top target for Houser, who had 292 passing yards along with the three touchdowns. Since allowing 37 points to Michigan State , Illinois has not allowed more than 17 points in its last three matchups. In fact, in the five games since defensive coordinator Bobby Hauck’s departure, the Illini have allowed 20.2 points per game. It’s been quite the turnaround for the Fighting Illini, who are now tied with USC for fourth in the Big Ten standings entering Saturday’s action. Illinois started the year 2-3 before heating up in October and will look to keep the momentum going into October. Next week, Illinois will head to the Rose Bowl to take on UCLA in Week 11. The Bruins enter Saturday as the Big Ten’s last remaining unbeaten team, and next week’s game will be part of the stretch run as the regular season begins to wind down.

articles.title: Insider confirms Colts getting ‘multiple’ Daniel Jones trade calls
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts have been busy fielding calls ahead of the NFL trade deadline, with running back Jonathan Taylor and wide receiver Josh Downs gaining most of the attention. As it turns out, they are even getting interest for quarterback Daniel Jones. In a report by NFL insider Ian Rapoport
articles._body: The Indianapolis Colts have been busy fielding calls ahead of the NFL trade deadline , with running back Jonathan Taylor and wide receiver Josh Downs gaining most of the attention. As it turns out, they are even getting interest for quarterback Daniel Jones . In a report by NFL insider Ian Rapoport with Adam Schefter, the Colts have engaged in trade talks with multiple teams for the former No. 6 overall pick. One such team was the Baltimore Ravens, who recently traded for Arizona Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett instead. The Vikings, whom Jones was a member of in 2024, have also been linked amid the injury to Kyler Murray. As Albert Breer explained in a post on X, formerly Twitter, Jones’ contract is quite an easy one to move given its structure. “Daniel Jones’ contract is tradeable—he’s on a base salary of $5.49 million, with $510K in per-game roster bonuses ($30K/game). Trading him for the Colts would mean his $44 million signing bonus would be a sunk cost. No fully guaranteed money after this year. Easy to move,” Breer wrote. After going an impressive 8-5 as a starter last season, Jones has had a disappointing sophomore campaign in Indy. He has completed just 60.4% of his passes (a career-low) for 1,542 yards, with only five touchdowns and nine interceptions, one more than his total in 13 games last year. The Colts have gone only 2-6 in his eight starts. However, it doesn’t look like this has deterred teams from trying to trade for Jones. Perhaps they think a change of scenery is all he needs in order to rediscover his form of 2025. articles._body: I made a 2 player browser game based on Pentago and janispritzkau's Loopover game ( https://github.com/janispritzkau/loopover ). Each turn you place a marble, then slide a row or column of the board. The first player to get five in a line (diagonal, vertical, or horizontal) wins. You can play the computer, someone you know with a shared link, or a random opponent online. It’s free with no sign-in required. Online play and play vs the computer are new, so please let me know about any bugs you find. It is built with TypeScript and Vue and uses Supabase for the online play. articles.title: Big Tech’s AI race will save small business owners time. It won’t find them customers
articles.summary: The next customer is one introduction away.
articles._body: Meta , Google, OpenAI and Anthropic are racing to become the small business owner’s AI assistant. Meta brought its Muse agent to small businesses in September. Anthropic and OpenAI now package tools aimed squarely at owners, and Google is building the same features into tools millions of them already use. That competition is good for Main Street. But it’s a race to save owners time, and time isn’t what keeps them up at night. What keeps them up is where the next customer will come from. A word on where I sit. I run Alignable, a network of 10 million small business owners, so I have a stake in this argument. Alignable also co-hosts small business AI training with Anthropic, one of the companies named here. Read what follows with that in mind. But I also have something the assistants don’t: 13 years of data on how small businesses actually find work. Fifty beats 500 Start with where customers come from. In our surveys, members say about 85% of their customers come through referrals. Not ads, not search, not cold email. People who already trust them. Across 35,000 local communities, our members have formed 226 million business connections. Most of them never become a relationship that sends work either way. The owners who grow through their networks aren’t the ones with the most connections. I’ve told owners for years that 50 warm relationships beat 500 cold contacts. That’s a rule of thumb from experience, not a number we’ve measured. But the owners who win do keep a small set of relationships active and leave the rest alone. And most owners are sitting on more opportunity than they know. When members tell us what their ideal customer looks like, we can count how many of those businesses sit one introduction away: connected to someone the owner already knows. Among members whose ideal customers show up in their extended network, the typical one has about 190 of them a single introduction away. For one in four, it’s more than 600. The next customer is rarely a stranger. They’re one relationship away, through someone the owner hasn’t talked to in months. Those relationships aren’t random, either. In my experience, three kinds do most of the work: customers who talk you up, businesses that serve the same customer without competing with you, and a handful of people who open doors. The best referral partner usually isn’t a peer in your own industry. It’s the business your customer calls right before or right after they call you: the realtor and the home inspector, the accountant and the financial planner. What a general assistant can’t see Ask any of the big assistants how to get more referrals and you’ll get a solid list of best practices. Ask an assistant that sits on a map of business relationships and it can tell you something specific: three nearby businesses serve your ideal customer, one of them already knows two of your clients, and you haven’t spoken to your best referral partner in four months. That’s the difference between advice and action. A general assistant can’t answer that question, because the answer lives in data it doesn’t have. The early numbers bear this out. In Bluehost’s 2026 study of 350 U.S. owners, 78% said AI saves them time every week. But 43% have seen no change in revenue. Time saved only matters if it goes somewhere that pays. Too often it goes into volume. Forbes recently told the story of Paul Birrell, a New Jersey owner whose automation loop sent roughly 400,000 emails in three days. His reaction: “I don’t have 400,000 customers.” Everything we see says growth comes from the opposite: judgment about the few people who matter. Three kinds of AI, not one AI will reach small business owners in three forms. The first is the personal assistant the giants are fighting over. It delivers time, and the assistants are converging fast. The second is AI built into the systems that already hold the business’s own data. Intuit knows the books. Shopify knows the store. That AI delivers control: it can flag a cash crunch six weeks out or spot the product quietly losing money. The third is AI built on the relationships between businesses: who knows whom, who serves the same customers, who sends work to whom. That’s the one that delivers growth, and it’s the one almost nobody is talking about. At Alignable, ours is called Allie. The giants have real advantages, and they’ll connect to the other two kinds. Meta’s Muse already plugs into QuickBooks, Shopify and Stripe , and the others are adding similar connections. The open question is who the intelligence works for. Meta makes nearly all of its money selling ads, and an assistant built by an ad company will tend to find that the answer involves more advertising. The data that actually works for the owner describes how their business runs and who in their community can help it grow. What owners should do now Use a personal assistant every day. The time savings are real. Then decide, in advance, where the reclaimed hours go. Put them on the calendar against the work that generates revenue, and the most neglected item on that list is relationships. Write down the 50 people most likely to send you business. Most owners can name 10 without trying. Those 10 are where AI should be pointing you. There are about 36 million small businesses in the U.S. , and more than 80% of them have no employees. For those owners, AI isn’t a department upgrade. It’s a capability they never had. Owners should take the better tools the giants’ race produces. But the biggest gains won’t come from saving an hour. They’ll come from knowing which 50 relationships to spend it on. articles.title: Eagles’ Nick Sirianni clears air about Tanner McKee, Joe Milton starter confusion with media truthbomb
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are turning to Joe Milton as their new starting quarterback in Week 9 against the New York Giants, replacing Tanner McKee. Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni had said McKee would be the starter earlier in the week, but he later changed his mind and went with Milton. Sirianni
articles._body: The Philadelphia Eagles are turning to Joe Milton as their new starting quarterback in Week 9 against the New York Giants, replacing Tanner McKee. Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni had said McKee would be the starter earlier in the week, but he later changed his mind and went with Milton. Sirianni addressed the media about his QB U-turn, which he claims was a strategic move to try and unsettle the Giants. “I’m gonna tell you what I want to tell you, guys. I respect the job that you all have to do. But I’m gonna tell you what I want to tell you, guys, because I’m always gonna protect the team, first and foremost. Every second that goes by in a situation like that, that you can hold on to the information as long as you possibly can, is a little less time for the opponent to prepare for the game,” Sirianni said. Sirianni also gave props to Tanner McKee for his performance after being called upon to replace Jalen Hurts, but he felt the change was for the good of the team . “I felt Tanner played solid … but is what I felt I needed to do,” Sirianni said, per Jeff McLane. A sixth round pick by the Eagles in 2023, McKee got three starts after Hurts got shut down for the season due to blood clots . He completed 63% of his passes for 638 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions. Sirianni will now turn to Joe Milton, who will be making his first career start. Milton brings more of the dynamism and mobility that Hurts has, which may have played a part in why he was chosen over McKee. articles.title: Last-minute fantasy football streaming options for NFL Week 9: Kicker
articles.summary: Finding the right kicker can make a meaningful difference in close fantasy football matchups. The best streaming options often come down to a combination of offensive production, scoring opportunities, and a kicker’s ability to convert when called upon. Week 9 features several interesting c
articles._body: Finding the right kicker can make a meaningful difference in close fantasy football matchups. The best streaming options often come down to a combination of offensive production, scoring opportunities, and a kicker’s ability to convert when called upon. Week 9 features several interesting candidates , including a reliable veteran coming off a perfect performance and a San Francisco option whose recent accuracy issues are becoming difficult to ignore. If you’re still searching for a last-minute upgrade, these four kickers deserve a closer look before kickoff. Eddy Pineiro, SF (vs. LV) Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Eddy Pineiro has the benefit of playing behind one of the more potent offenses in football. That said, his recent performances have made him a less dependable fantasy option than his situation might suggest. In San Francisco’s Week 8 loss to the Atlanta Falcons, Pineiro did not attempt a field goal. He converted just two of his three extra-point attempts. Missing another PAT is particularly concerning because it adds to an increasingly frustrating trend for the 49ers kicker. Pineiro is now 21-for-25 on extra-point attempts this season. He has converted only six of his nine field-goal tries. Pineiro certainly needs to become more reliable when those chances arrive. The Week 9 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders could offer a chance to get back on track. The 49ers have enough offensive firepower to create multiple scoring opportunities. However, managers should be cautious about treating him as a sure thing. His environment is appealing, but his recent accuracy issues make him a relatively risky option. Cairo Santos, CHI (vs. TB) Cairo Santos is coming off exactly the kind of performance fantasy football managers want. He converted all four of his extra-point attempts and both field-goal tries in Week 8. Santos rewarded managers who trusted him in a favorable offensive environment. Even better, Santos has been producing consistently well lately. Chicago’s offense has demonstrated an ability to put points on the board. Santos should benefit from the scoring opportunities generated by the offense. His Week 9 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers should keep him firmly on the streaming radar. There is little reason to overthink this one. Santos should be started in most fantasy football leagues. He is one of the more appealing options available heading into Week 9. Wil Lutz, DEN (@ CAR) Wil Lutz is another kicker worth targeting. That is especially true with the Denver Broncos’ offense generating plenty of scoring opportunities. Lutz converted both of his field-goal attempts and both extra-point tries in Week 8. He connected from 39 and 45 yards, continuing a productive stretch. The bigger picture is even more encouraging. Lutz has made five field goals over his last two games. Denver’s offense has scored also 58 points during that span. Denver now faces the Carolina Panthers in Week 9. That should give Lutz another opportunity to capitalize on the offense’s recent momentum. The Broncos’ scoring potential makes Lutz an appealing option regardless of whether they finish every drive in the end zone. For fantasy managers looking for a reliable streamer, Lutz checks several important boxes. He deserves consideration as a strong starting option this week. Chase McLaughlin, TB (@ CHI) Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Chase McLaughlin continues to establish himself as one of the most dependable kickers in fantasy football. He connected on all three of his field-goal attempts and converted his lone extra-point opportunity in Sunday’s game. What made the performance particularly impressive was McLaughlin’s ability to remain accurate from distance. He connected on field goals of 46, 34, and 42 yards, all in the first half. The unfavorable conditions did little to disrupt his rhythm. McLaughlin’s consistency makes him more than just a streaming consideration. He has been one of the top kickers in fantasy football this season. His ability to convert from multiple distances gives him a strong weekly ceiling. The Buccaneers face the Chicago Bears in Week 9, a matchup that should provide another opportunity for McLaughlin to contribute. Managers who already have him rostered should feel comfortable keeping him in their starting lineups. Those searching for a kicker should also consider making him a priority if he is somehow available. Final Takeaway McLaughlin and Santos are the strongest options heading into Week 9. Lutz offers plenty of upside behind Denver’s productive offense. Pineiro has a favorable environment but carries accuracy concerns. When in doubt, trust consistency and scoring opportunities.
