articles.summary: With the Golden State Warriors beating the Miami Heat on Thursday on the second night of a back-to-back, 120-100, the latter is still looking to find its groove with all its new faces such as Giannis Antetokounmpo, Klay Thompson, and others. As the Heat now fall to 3-6 on the season after the los
articles._body: With the Golden State Warriors beating the Miami Heat on Thursday on the second night of a back-to-back, 120-100, the latter is still looking to find its groove with all its new faces such as Giannis Antetokounmpo, Klay Thompson, and others. As the Heat now fall to 3-6 on the season after the loss to the Warriors, one newcomer who has been struggling recently is Tim Hardaway Jr., as head coach Erik Spoelstra speaks on the matter. Hardaway was signed this offseason to bring dynamic shooting to the team and be an energizer off the bench, especially coming off a season with the Denver Nuggets where he received Sixth Man of the Year consideration, shooting 40.7 percent from deep. Through nine games in familiar territory in Miami, as he grew up in the city while his father played with the Heat for six years, Hardaway Jr. has averaged 5.1 points while shooting 28.6 percent from the field and 24.3 percent from three-point range. The minutes have been eye-opening, as while his role was a sure-fire to record double-digit minutes, the last two games say otherwise. Heat’s Erik Spoelstra: “I feel for Tim right now” Playing seven minutes in Wednesday’s win over the Los Angeles Clippers and four minutes in the aforementioned loss to the Warriors, as rookie Ryan Conwell has been getting extended play recently. Hardaway is looking to get himself back in the rotation, as Spoelstra explains why it isn’t solely the guard’s fault. “I feel for Tim right now because it’s not really about him,” Spoelstra said, via The Miami Herald. “It’s not necessarily anybody in that second unit right now. We’re just facing some teams that have multiple ball handlers and point-of-attack guys. That was a good lineup for us yesterday when we had D. Mitch and Ryan out there together. It wasn’t really moving the needle for us tonight, so that’s just the way it goes sometimes.” At any rate, it remains to be seen what Hardaway’s role looks like with Miami as the next game comes on Sunday against the Sacramento Kings. Margaret Howell's Simple Trick to Surviving 50 Years of Fashion
articles.summary: That Margaret Howell has made it 50 years in fashion is no accident. The British designer's success comes down to one simple little thing, as she tells us.
articles._body: The genius of Margaret Howell is not that she was the first designers to create, simply, clothes. No, Howell envisioned clothes with all the beauty of "fashion" that met the necessities of daily life. For a long time, fashion was fashion and clothes were clothes. Howell dared to do both simultaneously. This is why, across her label's half-century of life, Margaret Howell's beautiful but approachable garments came to define the very notion of good clothing. They're as lovely now as they were back then and they'll be just as lovely in another 50 years. Turns out, by ignoring trend in favor of quality make and material, you end up with timeless stuff. "I have always wanted to design and make things that are truly lasting," the designer tells us. And indeed, much of it has lasted long enough to be documented in a new book dedicated to Howell's life and work, appropriately titled Margaret Howell Life and Work — and a follow-up to the much-loved Japan-only Margaret Howell Houses published over two decades ago and currently on its 10th edition — which provides a necessary opportunity to slow down and reflect on one of the industry's all-time greats. Much praise has been deservingly lavished upon Howell's work over the years — including during multiple conversations with this very outlet — and given its indifference to trend, it's sometimes difficult to find more to say about it. Her clothes really do speak for themselves, both the Margaret Howell mainline and the militaria-inclined MHL. sub-label. They're nice, they're considered, they're not going anywhere, even as they inspire wave after wave of new-gen adherents who venerate Howell like a deity (and if you worship quality clothes, she kinda is). But Margaret Howell Life and Work , published in English and Japanese by Tokyo publisher Shueisha, provides a neat look back at it all, tracing five decades of output, ideas, spaces, photographs, and people who've informed both Margaret Howell the brand and Margaret Howell the woman. It's a reflection of how her line's permanence, a longevity guaranteed by one simple trick: make nice things. This conversation has been condensed and edited. Your relationship with Japan is a crucial part of your label's legacy. [Howell's label has maintained a Japanese licensee for over 30 years] Can you speak to how Japan has shaped your approach to working, living, thinking? Margaret Howell: My strong connection with Japan comes from the great team we have in Tokyo, who I’ve always enjoyed working with, and the Japanese appreciation of natural materials, their attention to detail and respect for craftsmanship. Do you think that informs the lasting appeal of Margaret Howell Houses ? It’s obviously nice that people continue to respond positively to Margaret Howell Houses. The book showed real places that I liked. The houses were lived-in and comfortable, perhaps in the same way that our clothes are relaxed and designed to be worn. That has proven to be very lasting. It all feels very holistic, how your approach to living informs your label's oeuvre. Would you recommend that young creatives practice something similar? I would never tell someone else how to think. My approach to working and living isn’t a conscious decision. The way I choose to live and the things I respond to feed naturally into my work. How did you refine your perspective to what it is today? I have always wanted to design and make things that are truly lasting. I grew up in a time of postwar recovery, so we looked after the things we owned. A sense of quality was instilled in me at a young age and this has stayed with me. It feels like a very forward-looking way to consider clothing. Thinking about the future doesn’t change my approach to creative work. To me, design demands care and thought, and I apply these values to both my work and the way that I live. articles.title: Show HN: AJX – Find out where AI agents get stuck using your product
articles.summary: Hi HN. I made AJX (Agent Journey Experience). It is a CLI and skill bundle that you run to test what your product feels like to use from the point of view of an agent, and you get back a list of "asks" that would improve your product from an agentic usability perspective: so that agents spend les
articles._body: Hi HN. I made AJX (Agent Journey Experience). It is a CLI and skill bundle that you run to test what your product feels like to use from the point of view of an agent, and you get back a list of "asks" that would improve your product from an agentic usability perspective: so that agents spend less time, tokens and retries to accomplish tasks with it. How? It works by having an outer loop (AJX harness skill + CLI) that controls an "inner loop": the agent that actually tries out your product. The outer loop investigates the inner loop once it finishes. To try it, copy the prompt from the main page into your favorite agent and it will install the skill and CLI and you can then trigger /ajx skill, give it a prompt and some simple configuration as text, and it helps you with the rest. The outer loop starts loading the configured harness of your choice (claude, codex, kiro-cli etc..) in an environment and configuration of your choice (docker, VM, local, with or without specific skills, specific model, amount of runs, and more), and provides the harness (inner loop) with your input prompt and links, and "definition of done" - what does it mean to succeed with this product? For example with vercel cli you could say "build and deploy a simple hello world with vercel CLI [link]" as the prompt for the AJX test. Once the inner loop harness runs its course, the outer harness loop examines the run, logs and details, and outputs and extract the needed information from that run: retries, tokens, mistakes, assumptions and more, and created a very detailed report, as well as a list of asks that if applied to the product, would improve the agentic journey given the same prompt in the future. I call this "Agent Journey eXperience" it's the agentic equivalent of "User Experience" - if we were to document the journey an agent does when trying your product for the first time in a specific scenario. - Where does it go astray and makes mistakes? - How many retries does it take to succeed with the task? - How much time? - How many tokens? List of ASKS as an output: What features/fixes would the agent want the product to have to save it from making these mistakes or costing extra time and token in the future? here are some examples: - CLI missing a --JSON, which cost lots of parsing of unneeded code - CLI missing commands like doctor, help aliases - DOCS disagree with behavior of the product - Skills pull the agent in the wrong direction - lack of feedback while product is executing - Human friendly CLIs outputs break the agent loop - and much more. Why? I'm a startups solutions architect @ AWS, and previously wrote the art of unit testing and did lots of work on code quality, engineering practiced and continuous delivery) I built AJX (ajx.dev) when I was tasked with giving feedback on an internal upcoming AWS product that is meant to be used by agents. The team wanted feedback from potential users, and I figured that agents are the new potential users. I figured that if I was a product owner, I'd love to know what it feels like to work with my product (CLI, SDK, Website, Docs etc), and that the harder the agents work to use my product, the less people would point their agent at it, or the less the agent would tend to recommend it. Also I think it's useful to have "brag points" that your product is "agent-friendly". I even tested AJX with AJX and it found great of issues with the CLI (for example ajx status was returning the wrong status sometimes, ajx init --task behaved differently than expected, and other cool stuff like that. I envision this being used as part of a CI/CD cycle with a loop until AJX returns "all green" and no ASKS. AJX is still very new - so probably lots of rough edges but in an agent first world, I think it's a step in the right direction: see the world from an agent's POV. articles.title: 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan ‘couldn’t care less’ about Brandon Aiyuk visit with Drew Rosenhaus
articles.summary: Disgruntled San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is reportedly visiting the facilities on Friday with his agent Drew Rosenhaus. While more details are yet to come regarding that situation, head coach Kyle Shanahan didn’t appear to care about Aiyuk finally arriving at the organiza
articles._body: Disgruntled San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is reportedly visiting the facilities on Friday with his agent Drew Rosenhaus. While more details are yet to come regarding that situation, head coach Kyle Shanahan didn’t appear to care about Aiyuk finally arriving at the organization. Media members asked the 46-year-old what he expects to happen when Aiyuk and Rosenhaus visit the 49ers. Shanahan didn’t mince words and claimed he has no idea how it will play out, according to Mike Garafolo of the NFL Network. Shanahan also admitted that he doesn’t even care how it goes, and didn’t have an opinion on what he would like to see come to fruition with the visit. “49ers HC Kyle Shanahan on what to expect today with Brandon Aiyuk and Drew Rosenhaus heading to the facility: ‘No clue. Your guess is as good as mine.’ Asked what he would like to see happen, Shanahan replied, ‘I (couldn’t) care less,'” Garafolo reported. The drama between the 49ers and Aiyuk all began when the 28-year-old failed to follow through with mandatory team activities, meetings, and post-surgery checkups after suffering a severe knee injury in the 2024-25 campaign. Missing those events led to the organization voiding about $27 million in guaranteed money. Aiyuk has gone viral numerous times on social media, voicing his displeasure with the 49ers, along with trolling the franchise for even giving him a four-year, $120 million contract extension in August 2024. He’s also posted numerous times about demanding a trade to the Washington Commanders. The five-year veteran currently remains under contract with San Francisco. Brandon Aiyuk has not played since the 2024-25 season. In 69 career games, the former first-round pick has accumulated 294 receptions, 4,305 yards, and 25 touchdowns. articles.title: Kirby Smart calls for mental heath support for athletes in NIL era: 'They deal with a lot of outside pressure'
articles.summary: While looking at the modern era of college football, Georgia coach Kirby Smart said athletes are facing “an all-time high of mental stress” amid mounting outside pressure. With that, he called on schools to provide more support on that front. Smart cited the amount of pressure that comes with the NI
articles._body: While looking at the modern era of college football, Georgia coach Kirby Smart said athletes are facing “an all-time high of mental stress” amid mounting outside pressure. With that, he called on schools to provide more support on that front. Smart cited the amount of pressure that comes with the NIL era, in particular. As athletes earn money, he said they then sometimes hear from family members about the amount they’re making while some put those dollars toward supporting their families. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage While evaluating what athletes deal with in 2026, whether it’s NIL or noise on social media, Smart said schools should be able to give them more support to deal with their mental health. He added pressures they currently face are different than those he and others had during their careers. “I think these kids are at an all-time high of mental stress,” Smart said Thursday on his radio show . “They have stressors at home. A lot of them make NIL money that’s large money for a college athlete. And they get pressure from home, people reach out. … People you don’t even know come out of the woodworks because they find out what they make and they want to tap in. There’s no greater pressure than to feel like you have to support not your immediate family, you’ve got to support your outside family. SUBSCRIBE to the On3 NIL and Sports Business Newsletter “They carry a heavy burden. I don’t think anybody in the country does enough to support them mentally and just making sure that they’re where they need to be, in a good headspace. They deal with a lot of outside pressure – pressure that we didn’t deal with.” Athletes in the NIL era have also grown up with social media. Many of them have used their followings to cash in off the field by entering into deals and create more value away from the playing field. But on the flip side, Kirby Smart noted they can also hear more of the criticism that previous generations were able to avoid. That could also have an impact on an athlete’s headspace and add to what they’re dealing with off the field. “They’re comparing themselves to others,” Smart said. “They’re looking at what people say about them. They’re hearing things we never had to hear. They were said, but we didn’t hear them because nobody could write them. Now, you see everything.” The NCAA has taken steps to provide support for athletes dealing with any threats or harassing behavior on social media. It announced the Bad Actor Program late last month, which is an initiative aimed at helping identify such behavior online.

articles.summary: Coach Dan Quinn’s Washington Commanders are 2-4-1 on the season with a crucial game up next against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 9 that will come without injured, star receiver Terry McLaurin. Quinn fielded an awkward Davante Adams question and then focused on two of his own playmakers, wid
articles._body: Coach Dan Quinn’s Washington Commanders are 2-4-1 on the season with a crucial game up next against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 9 that will come without injured, star receiver Terry McLaurin . Quinn fielded an awkward Davante Adams question and then focused on two of his own playmakers, wide receivers Dyami Brown and Treylon Burks. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler commented on the situation with November 8’s game scheduled for 1 p.m. ET at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Maryland. “Commanders rule out WRs Dyami Brown and Treylon Burks. Should see plenty of Antonio Williams and Stefon Diggs vs. Rams.” Brown is a former playoff hero with the Commanders who lit up the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Detroit Lions during 2025’s playoff run, before wilting with 42 yards in the NFC Title Game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Brown has played in seven games this season and has contributed, albiet at a reduced rate, with nine receptions for 94 yards and no touchdowns. He has been dealing with a calf injury. Burks has been ramping up his production this season with 12 catches for 233 yards and two touchdowns, including 81 yards against the Eagles on November 1. He is dealing with a left foot injury. The Commanders were previously linked to 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk in trade rumors. Aiyuk is expected to be back soon ahead of November 10’s trade deadline. Trades looked like a longshot for the Commanders, but Quinn’s team may need to push a few buttons and try a few things in hopes of turning themselves into a contender with time ticking down on the NFL season. articles.title: The killer mistake Eagles must avoid at 2026 NFL trade deadline
articles.summary: With just one game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the 2026 NFL trade deadline, it’s safe to say Howie Roseman has a little more than the New York Giants on his mind heading into Week 9. One of the most consistently good teams in the NFL this century, with Nick Sirianni leading his team
articles._body: With just one game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the 2026 NFL trade deadline , it’s safe to say Howie Roseman has a little more than the New York Giants on his mind heading into Week 9. One of the most consistently good teams in the NFL this century, with Nick Sirianni leading his team to the playoffs in every season he’s been a head coach, losing isn’t exactly a novelty in the City of Brotherly Love, but prolonged losing certainly is, with just three losing seasons on the Birds’ resume since 2000. Would it be cool to see new starting quarterback Joe Milton put it all together, shock the world, and turn a collection of youngsters like Makai Lemon, Eli Stowers, and Markel Bell into a certified unit, one made all the more impressive when veterans like Saquon Barkley, Dontayvion Wicks, and DeVonta Smith are back to full strength ? Sure, and from a purely entertainment standpoint, giving Milton half a season to let it loose can only lead to impressive highlights and dazzling feats of athleticism, regardless of the final score. But unless pretty much everyone across the board, including Sirianni, Sean Mannion, and Vic Fangio, can hit at the very top of their expectation curve, it’s probably not going to result in much more than worse draft positioning and, at best, an embarrassing playoff loss. No, while it may not feel great in the moment, the Eagles simply aren’t a good enough team to justify even staying the course at the deadline, and must instead shed talent now to pick up more in the future, knowing that it could cost them plays, drives, or even games down the stretch. That means saying goodbye to players they would probably lose in free agency come March anyway, players like Riq Woolen, Hollywood Brown, and maybe even Moro Ojomo too , if a team is willing to give up compensation on par with, or greater than, what would come back in the compensatory formula, but what if opposing general managers come calling about more foundational pieces? Saquon Barkley has already been told he won’t be traded despite being a very attractive option for teams unwilling to give up the Indianapolis Colts’ asking price for Jonathan Taylor, and other established veterans like Landon Dickerson have come up in conversation too, especially after Cam Jurgens was already shipped down I-95 to the Baltimore Ravens before their season was also derailed by injuries. When Week 9 comes to an end, players like Barkley, Dickerson, Jalen Carter, Cooper DeJean, and Zack Baun will almost certainly drive back to their respective homes and rest easy, knowing they likely won’t be looking for sublets a few weeks before Thanksgiving, but should they feel so comfortable? Because at this point, the biggest mistake the Eagles could make would be trusting that they will be back to contending in 2027 and thus should hold onto veterans who are highly valued now but could see their value diminish by the time they are actually ready to go for another Super Bowl, especially with so much uncertainty just over the horizon. Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Eagles have to be ruthless when determining what their future looks like Who will be the Eagles’ head coach when Week 1 of the 2027 NFL season opens up? Who will have crafted the playbook the team will be running on offense? Who will be calling the defense? And who will be under center playing quarterback? Things could look relatively familiar, with Nick Sirianni surviving a doomed season, Sean Mannion showing enough to maintain his job as offensive coordinator, Vic Fangio holding off on retiring for another year, and Jalen Hurts agreeing to sign a long-term contract extension. Or Sirianni could get fired, Mannion could get fired, Fangio could retire – or all three – or Hurts, after everything he just went through, is gone as well, be it via trade or maybe even a medical retirement if disaster strikes and he can’t overcome his blood clot issues. If Sirianni sticks around but his coordinators don’t – a disaster scenario in the mind of many fans – could he convince the front office that the combination of, say, Shane Steichien and Jim Schwartz is good enough to shoot for another Super Bowl, with a few high-profile draft picks helping to fortify their roster? Or could this be the year where Philadelphia steals away one of the hot-shot young offensive minds they’ve been after for years, someone like Declan Doyle or last year’s dark-horse OC option, Charlie Weis Jr. , and suddenly Fangio’s experience is more important than ever, forcing some major changes all over the Jefferson Health Training Complex to accommodate a new offensive regime and a bolstered defensive one? Needless to say, 2027 is one of the least certain years in recent memory at this point in the Eagles’ season, and as a result, planning one way or another would be foolish. As tough as it may be to admit, the Eagles really don’t have that many untouchable players on their roster at this point, especially if a team is willing to give up an above-market package that’s too good to be true, like the Chicago Bears surrendered for Jeffery Simmons. Hurts unquestionably falls into that category, as a team would be foolish to give up a pick for his services while dealing with blood clots, but who else falls into that category? Quinyon Mitchell comes to mind, as does Jordan Mailata, but outside of that trio, who is an elite player now who will also be in five years? Smith probably falls into that category, and from a pure talent standpoint, Carter does too, but in 2026, DeJean, Jordan Davis, Jalyx Hunt, Nolan Smith, and seemingly every other blue-chip player has shown flaws in their games that could only get worse, leading some to wonder if moving them now could result in steals like the picks Roseman got for AJ Brown and Jurgens. articles.title: Bruins star rookie James Hagens suffers injury in win vs. Penguins
articles.summary: The Boston Bruins steamrolled the Pittsburgh Penguins 6-2 on Thursday night, but the convincing win came at a cost as rookie forward James Hagens exited the contest with an apparent lower-back injury. Hagens left the game early in the third period after Penguins defenseman Samuel Girard landed a
articles._body: The Boston Bruins steamrolled the Pittsburgh Penguins 6-2 on Thursday night, but the convincing win came at a cost as rookie forward James Hagens exited the contest with an apparent lower-back injury. Hagens left the game early in the third period after Penguins defenseman Samuel Girard landed a cross-check to his lower back. The 20-year-old immediately appeared uncomfortable, holding his back before making his way to the bench to receive medical attention. He subsequently headed down the tunnel and did not return for the remainder of the contest. James Hagens exited tonight's game after taking this cross-check from Samuel Girard… pic.twitter.com/Bo5w3E5lc8 — NESN (@NESN) November 6, 2026 Before his departure, Hagens had logged 11:57 of ice time across 15 shifts and recorded four shot attempts. The Bruins did not provide an update on his condition after the game. The injury is a concerning one given the impact Hagens has made during his rookie campaign. He has accumulated six goals and six assists for 12 points in 17 appearances, placing him among the NHL’s most productive first-year players. His 12 points lead all rookies, while his six goals are tied for second behind Roman Kantserov, who has scored eight. Beyond his offensive contributions, Hagens has demonstrated a willingness to contribute defensively. He has amassed 19 blocked shots, ranking fourth among rookies in that category. Five of his six goals have also come from opportunities around the net, showing his effectiveness in high-danger scoring situations. Boston has benefited from his contributions on a line alongside Casey Mittelstadt and Elias Lindholm. The trio has produced a plus-five goal differential across 13 games together, making it the Bruins’ most effective line during that stretch. Hagens was selected seventh overall by Boston in the 2025 NHL Draft and is in the second year of his three-year entry-level contract . The Bruins have two days off before hosting the Florida Panthers at TD Garden on Sunday. With Matthew Poitras also dealing with a nose injury this week , Hagens’ condition could become another concern for Boston. articles.summary: With Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs requesting a trade from the team, there has been a myriad of speculation on which teams could go after the 25-year-old. As rumors around the Colts will continue ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, this NFL insider goes into the two teams that
articles._body: With Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs requesting a trade from the team, there has been a myriad of speculation on which teams could go after the 25-year-old. As rumors around the Colts will continue ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline , this NFL insider goes into the two teams that have been checking in on Downs. According to ESPN league insider Jeremy Fowler, the Kansas City Chiefs and Pittsburgh Steelers have “checked in” on Indianapolis regarding Downs. So far this season, Downs has caught 30 passes for 330 yards and one touchdown. “There probably will be some wink-wink deals that ‘Hey, let’s get through the week and see if what we need still stands.’ Or ‘Here’s the pick I’m willing to give up. Will you take it?’ I think at wide receiver some of that will shake out a little bit,” Fowler said on “The Rich Eisen Show.” “Josh Downs in Indianapolis has made clear he wants out; there are teams involved there,” Fowler continued. “Teams like Kansas City, Pittsburgh that have checked in on it, do they put that over the top after the game is something that’s on my radar.” @JFowlerESPN believes more teams will make moves after this weekend's games He shares why Brian Thomas Jr. is on his radar ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline (via @RichEisenShow ) pic.twitter.com/Jmqml0xXDD — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) November 6, 2026 The Colts have been active regarding trading away key players, as they have done so with star offensive lineman Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers. With Downs and star running back Jonathan Taylor being rumored to be next on the trade block for Indianapolis, it remains to be seen if that will be the case. When it comes to Downs, he could be finding himself a new home by the trade deadline, as Kansas City and Pittsburgh seem to be likely options. articles.title: Nets rookie Mikel Brown Jr. has critical reaction to season-best performance
articles.summary: Mikel Brown Jr. delivered his best NBA performance to date during the Brooklyn Nets’ 114-104 win over the Charlotte Hornets on Wednesday. The No. 6 pick scored a career-high 18 points on 6-of-11 shooting with two rebounds and four assists in 20 minutes. “[Mikel] was a big part of the win,&#
articles._body: Mikel Brown Jr. delivered his best NBA performance to date during the Brooklyn Nets’ 114-104 win over the Charlotte Hornets on Wednesday. The No. 6 pick scored a career-high 18 points on 6-of-11 shooting with two rebounds and four assists in 20 minutes. “[Mikel] was a big part of the win,” said head coach Jordi Fernandez. “Every time that they took a little bit of a lead, we responded. He was helping us push back, and he played composed. I know [he had] a couple of [late] turnovers, but I’m not concerned because I want him to go out there, play free, and be aggressive… I’m very happy with Mikel. Him [playing] in pick-and-roll, how fast he is, how shifty he is. He can shoot the three, get to the rim. Very, very happy with his performance.” Brown scored from all three levels during the Nets win. The 20-year-old drained three of his five three-point attempts, all off the dribble. He also converted a pair of acrobatic and-one layups and a mid-range jumper. good hoops from the rook https://t.co/qlYBb9z4RT pic.twitter.com/axoiPF2OY5 — Brooklyn Nets (@BrooklynNets) November 5, 2026 His top highlight was an impressive no-look pass to Moe Wagner off a baseline drive. still in awe of this. pic.twitter.com/1iUzC9hOrN — Brooklyn Nets (@BrooklynNets) November 5, 2026 However, Fernandez took Brown out of the game after he turned the ball over twice early in the fourth quarter. While Brown said this was his most well-rounded performance thus far, he feels he has plenty of room to improve. “You could say [this was my best game so far]. I mean, it’s just the expectation that I hold myself to,” Brown said. “I should be [playing] like this. Obviously, down the stretch I had a couple of turnovers that I [need to] clean up. A miscommunication, me and Julius [Randle] talked about it. But I mean, this is the expectation. This is my standard that I’m supposed to be playing at. And I could do better than this.” Asked Mikel Brown Jr. if he felt last night was his most complete game thus far: “It’s just the expectation I hold myself to. Down the stretch, I had a couple of turnovers I can clean up… But this is my standard I’m supposed to be playing at, and I can do better than this." pic.twitter.com/nHYmpUpm5h — Erik Slater (@ErikSlater_) November 5, 2026 The Nets rookie has averaged 12.0 points on .338/.297/.833 shooting splits with 4.0 assists and 2.2 turnovers per game across his first six NBA appearances. Nets rookie Mikel Brown Jr. shows improvement with season-best performance vs. Hornets Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images However, Brown has played only 22.8 minutes per game while on a restriction. His latest performance came after he posted 13 points and three assists during the Nets’ 103-90 loss to the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden on Monday Brown has seen a heavy dose of pick-and-roll ball-handling opportunities during Brooklyn’s last two games. He’s been effective, averaging 1.06 points per possession and posting a 66.7 effective field goal percentage across 16 possessions as a pick-and-roll ball handler, per Synergy. “It’s just understanding time and position when it comes to that stuff, who’s got it going. Where the spots are that we can get to or where I can get to make a play, not just for myself, but for others,” Brown said of his pick-and-roll success. “It’s starting to just click, and I’m just being patient, moving on to the next play. This game is an imperfect game, so I’m just having that next-play mentality. I have great vets. They’re just telling me to just keep that positive energy, keep that positive vibe.” The Nets’ win over the Hornets brought them to 2-6. They’ll return to action when they kick off a four-game road trip on Saturday vs. the Atlanta Hawks. Brown is active vs. the Hawks. However, he’ll likely sit during Brooklyn’s back-to-back against the Dallas Mavericks on Sunday, as he’s not yet cleared for back-to-backs. articles.title: Teddy Swims’ ‘Mr. Know It All’ Hits No. 1 on Billboard Pop Airplay Chart
articles.summary: The singer-songwriter scores his second leader at the format, after “Lose Control” in 2024.
articles._body: Teddy Swims earns his second No. 1 on Billboard ’s Pop Airplay chart as “Mr. Know It All” ascends two spots to the top of the Nov. 14-dated ranking. Released on SWIMS Int./Warner Records, the song becomes the singer-songwriter’s second leader at the format, after “Lose Control” reigned for two weeks in April 2024. Related Teddy Swims Wishes He Wasn’t ‘Mr. Know It All’: Stream It Now Teddy Swims Gets Real About Fatherhood, Fame & His Next Chapter | Billboard News Teddy Swims Talks Fatherhood, Performing For Mariah Carey & More | GRAMMYs 2026 The Pop Airplay chart measures songs’ weekly plays, as tabulated by Mediabase and provided to Billboard by Luminate, on nearly 150 U.S. mainstream top 40 radio stations. Swims has also hit the Pop Airplay top 10 with “Bad Dreams,” which reached No. 8 in April 2025, and “The Door” (No. 9, November 2024). On the all-genre, multimetric Billboard Hot 100 , “Mr. Know It All,” which Swims cowrote, has hit a No. 26 high, likewise becoming Swims’ fourth top 40 hit, after “Bad Dreams” (No. 30), “The Door” (No. 24) and “Lose Control” (No. 1 for one week). “Lose Control” went on to rule as the No. 1 song on the 2024 year-end Hot 100 . “I feel like every time I meet one, I’m grateful, but I’m never satisfied,” Swims told Billboard News ’ Tetris Kelly earlier this year of how he assesses goals. “The human eye sees, like, 20 miles ahead, right? So soon as you get that 20 miles, you’re seeing 20 more miles and you’re, like, there’s still much further to go. So I always try to celebrate the wins, but I want to be the best. I try to just be where my feet are and know that this is where I’m supposed to be.” Added the father of a now-16-month-old, “I just also want my son to think I’m cool.” All charts dated Nov. 14 will update Tuesday, Nov. 10, on Billboard.com.

articles.title: Mets bring pitcher back early in offseason
articles.summary: New York Mets president of baseball operations David Stearns devastated and enraged many fans by removing a large portion of the team’s soul last offseason. People used his reluctance to invest long term in beloved first baseman Pete Alonso as an indictment of the executive’s analytic
articles._body: New York Mets president of baseball operations David Stearns devastated and enraged many fans by removing a large portion of the team’s soul last offseason. People used his reluctance to invest long term in beloved first baseman Pete Alonso as an indictment of the executive’s analytics-driven strategy, but he helped plant a significant part of the Milwaukee Brewers’ foundation — the one that just lifted the franchise to its first-ever World Series title . The Flushing Faithful can only hope he makes a similar impact on the Mets. He is beginning his fourth offseason at the helm with a minor move that is unlikely to shift public opinion. But perhaps it can still yield positive results. New York is re-signing right-handed pitcher Robert Stock to a one-year split contract, per USA Today’s Bob Nightengale. The veteran hurler, who will turn 37 years old later this month, posted a 5.93 ERA with 29 strikeouts and a .297 batting average against in 30 1/3 innings last season. The Mets dismantled their bullpen ahead of the trade deadline and could struggle to repair the unit before the new campaign begins. Though, Stack actually occupied a place in their staring rotation during the final stretch of the year. Expecting an aging and struggling pitcher to join a turnaround effort may be wishful thinking, but this specific one did exhibit flashes of impressive form. The 2009 second-round draft pick pitched 5 1/3 shutout innings versus the Tampa Bay Rays on Aug. 31, recorded another quality start against the Miami Marlins and tossed an adequate 4 1/3 innings each versus the San Diego Padres and Washington Nationals. Unfortunately, he also surrendered a combined 15 runs to the Brewers and Pittsburgh Pirates in the same month. Robert Stock struggled with control, walking 10.2 percent of the batters he faced in 2026. Stearns wants a little more time with him, though. The Mets are highly dependent on homegrown arms like Nolan McLean, Christian Scott, Zac Thornton and Jonah Tong, but they must stumble on a hidden gem or two as well. Does Stock fulfill that criteria? Fans now have some more time to find out. The post Mets bring pitcher back early in offseason appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Guardians bring infielder back who they traded away in 2024
articles.summary: MLB free agency is underway, and the Cleveland Guardians are already making moves to improve the roster for next season. On Friday, the club managed to acquire an infielder who was previously traded away from the organization in 2024. Reports indicate that the Guardians claimed infielder Jose Ten
articles._body: MLB free agency is underway, and the Cleveland Guardians are already making moves to improve the roster for next season. On Friday, the club managed to acquire an infielder who was previously traded away from the organization in 2024. Reports indicate that the Guardians claimed infielder Jose Tena off waivers from the Washington Nationals, according to Zack Meisel of The Athletic. The Nationals designated the 25-year-old for assignment on November 2. He now heads back to Cleveland after playing the past two and a half seasons with the Nationals. “The Guardians claimed infielder and old friend Jose Tena from the Nationals. They traded him to the Nationals in 2024 for Lane Thomas.” Tena appeared in a career-high 114 games for the Nationals last season, mainly playing as a designated hitter (58 appearances). Washington spread the four-year veteran around the field defensively, as he played two or more games at second base, third base, and in the outfield. Offensively, Tena finished the campaign with 57 hits, seven home runs, and 25 RBIs through 257 at-bats, giving him a .222 batting average and .302 OBP. The Dominican Republic native heads back to Cleveland with a chance to serve as a depth piece in the infield. The Guardians already have star-caliber talent in key areas, with Jose Ramirez at third base and Travis Bazzana at second. Additionally, shortstop Brayan Rocchio was a solid contributor, along with first baseman David Fry. The Guardians are coming off a 2026 campaign that ended in a 4-2 series loss to the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALCS. We’ll see how the front office navigates the rest of the offseason in preparation for 2027. The post Guardians bring infielder back who they traded away in 2024 appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Elon Musk once said the Cybertruck would be Tesla’s ‘best product ever.’ Now he’s winding down production
articles.summary: Cybertruck sales fell 48% between 2024 and 2025, according to an estimate by Cox Automotive’s Kelley Blue Book.
articles._body: Elon Musk said Friday Tesla would be phasing out the production of the Cybertruck, the boxy-looking electric pickup he once pitched as the future of his EV maker. In a post on X, Musk said: “Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production.”  The changes to Cybertruck production come seven years after Musk introduced the vehicle at a splashy Sci-Fi-themed event at Tesla’s design studio in Hawthorne, Calif., complete with pyrotechnics and a live demonstration of the car’s “armor glass” in which Tesla’s lead designer shattered two Cybertruck windows with a steel ball. Just a month before the launch event, Musk had touted the vehicle as Tesla’s “best product ever” during Tesla’s third quarter earnings call in 2019. “This could be totally wrong. I could be totally out to lunch here, but I think the Tesla Cyber Truck is our best product ever. That’s my opinion,” he said at the time. Yet, the Cybertruck, which starts at a whopping $92,490, has been popular, but it has struggled to find the mass appeal of other Tesla vehicles like the Model Y and Model 3. After production delays pushed the vehicle’s launch date to 2023 from a previously promised 2021 launch, production still fell short of the between 250,000 and 500,000 Cybertrucks Musk predicted Tesla would eventually produce annually.  Tesla sold 38,965 Cybertrucks in the U.S. in 2024 and then just 20,237 in 2025 , a decline of 48%, according to estimates by Kelley Blue Book. In the first half of the year, Kelley Blue Book’s parent company Cox Automotive also estimated Tesla sold a total of 7,263 Cybertrucks , which would put them on track for yet another year-over-year sales decline this year. Tesla does not break out its Cybertruck sales in its public filings. Musk has now pivoted the company’s future prospects to the autonomous Cybercab, which he announced to fanfare at an event in 2024. The first Cybercabs hit roads in Austin, Texas, in September. Tesla also has Robotaxi operations , using the Model Y, in Houston, Dallas, and Fort Worth in Texas as well as Miami, Orlando, and Tampa in Florida, with plans for more U.S. cities to be included later. Tesla did not immediately respond to Fortune ’s request for comment. New ambitions The shift away from Cybertruck production comes as Tesla seeks to convince investors autonomous technology can drive growth in the future by surpassing traditional EV sales, which have fallen since President Donald Trump ended the EV tax credit last year. Tesla sells the most EVs of any company in the U.S. The EV maker has positioned its Cybercab, a two-seater without a steering wheel or pedals, as key to its expansion into autonomous transportation and robotics. But the new vehicle also faces hurdles. Federal auto safety regulators in September opened an investigation into whether Tesla properly certified that the Cybercab complies with federal vehicle safety standards. At the end of October, Tesla submitted its answers to questions from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), but requested its responses remain sealed because they are “confidential business information.” The NHTSA has not yet ruled on Tesla’s confidentiality request, according to Electrek . In the autonomous robotaxi market, Tesla is entering late. Alphabet’s Waymo already operates in 15 U.S. cities and reportedly provides 500,000 rides per week , it said in an X post earlier this year.  For its part, the Cybertruck has been hit with 11 recalls since customer deliveries began in November 2023, according to Reuters . Price changes that made it significantly more expensive than Musk’s original vision have also stood in the way of mass adoption. Tesla advertised a starting price of $39,900 when it introduced the truck in 2019—but by the time deliveries began in 2023, Tesla was advertising a version of the vehicle expected to cost $60,990 . Tesla raised the price of several models of the Cybertruck this month and discontinued orders for the cheapest model, the Dual Motor AWD. That means the cheapest Cybertruck model still available starts at $92,490, up from the $84,990 price the same model reached in August after previous price hikes, according to Electrek . Tesla has previously tried introducing less expensive versions of the Cybertruck to attract buyers. The company launched a rear-wheel-drive Cybertruck in 2025 but pulled it from the lineup months later. Musk’s Friday post also leaves existing Cybertruck owners in limbo. Tesla has not said how long it will continue selling remaining inventory or supplying replacement parts, though winding down the vehicle’s production does not mean it will end support for existing vehicles. Musk, for his part, still appeared enthusiastic about the truck Friday.  In response to a user highlighting Musk’s Cybertruck announcement as the end of an era, the CEO replied : “True, but the Cybertruck fleet will be around for a long time.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles._body: On Thursday, Rory McIlroy endured a difficult start to the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship. McIlroy — who is currently playing in the DP World Tour — initially shot a 68. However, his final score ended up being a 70 for the round after he was awarded a two-stroke penalty for attempting to improve his lie on hole 12. McIlroy acknowledged his mistake but also explained that it was an accident . The 37-year-old did not let the controversial moment impact his performance on Friday, as he shot a 63 and finished the round with 11 birdies. According to Golf Channel, McIlroy accomplished an impressive feat as well. His 11 birdies represent his career-high mark on the DP World Tour. Rory McIlroy bounced back from a Thursday penalty with a DP World Tour career-best 11 birdies on Friday Excellent round of 63 powers him to T-4 position entering the weekend in Abu Dhabi pic.twitter.com/MZ6hy44tpq — Golf Channel (@GolfChannel) November 6, 2026 McIlroy is now tied for fourth overall in the tournament at -11 after surging up the leaderboard. He is certainly in a quality position heading into the weekend without question. It has been a memorable year for Rory McIlroy so far. Of course, McIlroy earned his second consecutive Masters championship in April. He is currently second overall in the world golf rankings, trailing only Scottie Scheffler. McIlroy would love to add another win this year on the DP World Tour. He still has work to do over the weekend, but it seems as if McIlroy found his rhythm on Friday. If he can keep things going, it would not be surprising to see him end up winning the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship. He’s difficult to beat when he’s on top of his game. articles._body: With the New York Giants coming off the 27-21 win over the Houston Texans on Oct. 25, the team has been using the bye week to get ready for this Sunday as they take on the Philadelphia Eagles. However, Giants running back Cam Skattebo finds himself on the team’s injury report after missing another practice on Friday, but what does that say about his status for Sunday against the Eagles? According to Jordan Raanan at ESPN, Skattebo didn’t practice on Friday, and while that usually means that a player is on track to miss the game on Sunday, head coach John Harbaugh didn’t go that far during his press conference. “Cam Skattebo did not practice again on Friday, per John Harbaugh. But the Giants coach wasn’t ready to rule him out for Sunday against the Eagles,” Raanan wrote on X, formerly Twitter. So far this season, Skattebo has recorded 418 yards with two touchdowns with New York, and while Harbaugh left a sliver of hope that he could be available on Sunday, his injury listing says otherwise. Raanan later reported that Skattebo is listed as “doubtful,” and with Tyron Tracy Jr. on the injured reserve, fans should expect Devin Singletary to be the lead back for the Giants against the Eagles. “Cam Skattebo is doubtful for Sunday vs. Eagles,” Raanan wrote on X. “It’s likely going to be Devin Singletary’s show as the primary running back. Greg Desrosiers and Phil Mafah the other likely options.” At any rate, it remains to be seen if Skattebo will somehow be active for the contest and if not, his next chance comes on Nov. 12 against the Washington Commanders. The award celebrates her ever-evolving artistic journey and her ability to leave a lasting mark on the Italian music landscape. With the announcement of the Woman of the Year, the full lineup of honorees is now complete: Icon – Loredana Bertè Powerhouse – Ditonellapiaga Impact – Elisa Songwriter of the Year – Francesca Michielin DJ of the Year – Adiel Group of the Year powered by Morellato – Bambole di Pezza Rising Star – Angelica Bove Executive of the Year – Eleonora Rubini Among this year’s new highlights, Spotify’s EQUAL Award will be presented to the collective Canta Fino a 10 in recognition of its tangible and creative commitment to championing female talent, challenging gender stereotypes in Italian music and fostering collaboration. The 2026 edition aims to tell the story of music from multiple perspectives, shining a light not only on those who take the stage, but also on the people who write, produce, lead and work behind the scenes every day. It is an opportunity to offer a fuller picture of the many professions that make up the industry and help drive its evolution. Partners for the 2026 edition include the collecting society SIAE (Società Italiana degli Autori ed Editori), which renews its support for creativity and women working in the music industry. articles.title: The midterms didn’t stop the AI buildout. They simply repriced it—and OpenAI is already promising to pay up
articles.summary: Two days after voters rejected data centers almost everywhere, OpenAI pledged to cover its own power bills and post financial guarantees.
articles._body: Two days after what appears to be voters rejecting data centers in town after town, OpenAI went shopping for something it can’t build: permission. On Thursday, the company published a National Community Compact, in which the company pledged to pay for the electricity and grid infrastructure of the data center campuses it owns and operates. It also pledged to post financial guarantees before major spending begins, so other utility customers aren’t stuck with the bill if a project is delayed or canceled. The company told Fortune this has been months in the making and is something they’ve been pledging in their data center campuses already—the compact is simply the first time OpenAI put in writing a number of pledges it has already undertaken. Mining and energy companies have a name for what OpenAI is after: a social license. (If you’re interested, you can read my grad school capstone about social license in Peru, which has since been enacted into law). These are a type of Community Partnership Agreements (CPAs) that entails getting a community’s ongoing consent to operate: No zoning board grants it, and no tax abatement buys it. Instead, companies earn it by showing the people next door that a project leaves them better off—or at least no worse off. Lose it, and permits stall, lawsuits pile up, and local officials find reasons to say no. So following the Democratic wave on Tuesday, the AI industry found out how little of that license it had left. And distinctly, the midterm turnout wasn’t a cry from voters to stop the buildout, but simply to put a new price tag on it, and OpenAI is the first major AI company to agree to pay it since the votes were counted. Limits, not bans, on data centers Data centers were on the ballot in roughly 40 localities across the country. By Wednesday morning, about 28 measures had passed in 25 localities, all of them opposing data centers. Chief among them were the 18 municipalities in Ohio, which already has 125 data center moratoriums. Sunbury, Ohio, banned data centers over 25 megawatts, 79% to 21%, after Amazon proposed a $2 billion campus there. In Trenton, Ohio, where Amazon Web Services is already building a 250-megawatt data center, a ban passed 80% to 20%. In Hubbard, Ohio, a ban won 76% to 24%, and the mayor has since said a proposed 300-megawatt project is dead. But voters weren’t saying no to data centers: The ballot measures were to place limits on data centers, rather than full-out bans. In Perry, Ohio, 87% of voters required hyperscale developers seeking tax breaks to post financial guarantees and meet noise limits, the same safeguard OpenAI offered two days later. Grove City, Ohio, banned nothing. By 55% to 45%, it required a public vote on any project over 50 acres, 20 megawatts or 500,000 gallons of water a day. Most of the bans set a size threshold, meaning a modest server farm can still come to town, but a gigawatt campus can’t. This wasn’t limited just to the Democratic party: Former Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy pledged a moratorium on construction until the legislature acted, and Texas Gov. Greg Abbott had already paused new grid connections for data centers in August. The common complaint was the electric bill: More than 70% of Americans polled said they’d oppose a data center planned near them, with rising power prices the top reason. Swapping tax breaks for training programs Corporations largely have benefitted from local/municipal/state/federal praxis: Get a tax credit for coming here to my jurisdiction. The examples are endless: Think of the $33 billion taxpayers have spent on getting a sports stadium built, of which they rarely see the full amount brought back into the community. Perhaps the most famous example of tax incentives proving futile is none other than Amazon’s HQ2 debacle, in which Newark, NJ, offered $7 billion in tax incentives to Amazon to locate their second headquarters there, and New York City offered “only” $3 billion. Amazon was always going to pick Queens, but the company was smart enough to play more than two dozen jurisdictions across the country against each other to gain the biggest tax reward. So the AI buildout is no different. For most of the boom, the industry’s offer to communities was simple: We bring tax revenue and construction jobs, you bring the tax breaks. But Tuesday showed that offer was no longer on the table. Now, hyperscalers are making a new offer, which looks a lot like a social license agreement. In January, Microsoft launched a “Community-First AI Infrastructure” plan, pledging to pay its own way on electricity, pay full local property taxes without asking for tax breaks , replenish more water than it uses, and offer free AI training in local schools and community colleges. A week later, OpenAI said every Stargate campus would get its own community plan. By this fall, Google, Microsoft, Meta , Oracle , xAI, OpenAI, and Amazon had signed a non-binding White House pledge to build or buy the power their facilities need. That’s repricing in action. Instead of asking towns for discounts, the industry now offers to cover the grid upgrades, the water, the training and, in OpenAI’s case, a guarantee against walking away. Previously, every one of those costs used to fall on the community. Bans don’t make demand for computing power disappear. They move it. Harwood, the lone town that voted the industry’s way, sits near a data center that Applied Digital is already building. The projects pushed out of Sunbury and Hubbard will look for counties that still say yes, at whatever price those counties set. While it is absurd to think of some newly-elected members of the Democratic wave advocating to put “a pause on advanced AI development, regulation of this out of control industry, and a ban on artificial superintelligence,” as Congresswoman Yassamin Ansari (D-Ariz.) posted on Election Day, it isn’t all that obscene to think t

That means the Hurricanes will be without their top target after he underwent tightrope ankle surgery , as On3’s Pete Nakos reported. But to ESPN’s Kirk Herbstreit , Miami might be able to turn Toney’s absence into a rallying cry. But in his absence, Herbstreit noted other playmakers such as Cooper Barkate who will need to step up and fill the void. “One thing I know from being around Mario Cristobal and this Miami program, kind of the culture, they’re going to use this in a way that the players are going to get fired up,” Herbstreit said Friday on Get Up . “They’re going to feel like, ‘Hey, we’ve got something to prove.’ They’ve got plenty of athletes on the outside. Cooper Barkate, who transferred over from Duke with Mensah, the quarterback, he’ll have to take up a little bit more slack. There’s so much anticipation, hype for this game that I think Miami is going to use this as a motivator. … When I heard Malachi Toney was out, I was like, ‘Oh, well.’ I think Miami’s going to use that as a rally-the-troops, ‘We’re more than just one guy,’ kind of things.” Miami heads into Saturday as one of the only undefeated teams left in the FBS and sits atop the initial College Football Playoff rankings. Charlie Woods, who signed with Team TaylorMade recently , hails from The Benjamin School in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida and will be taking his talents over 400 miles away to the in-state Division-I university. That posture alone says the gym work is still there,” one fan said . “He’s too old (50) to compete with these youngsters, but he can hang in the Champions tour,” another added . “I mean, fitness has never been the problem,” another added . “Man is about to outdrive the entire FSU roster just to prove a point. Let him cook,” another said . “Looks can be deceiving,” another said , doubting Woods’ aptitude for a comeback. Charlie Woods is 17 years old and a member of the American Junior Golf Association. articles.title: There's No Moomin Merch Like Bottega Veneta Moomin Merch
articles.summary: The Finnish cartoon is getting immortalized in Bottega Veneta leathercraft. This is how you do franchise-luxury collabs.
articles._body: The world’s favorite Finnish animated character has become the latest face of the franchised-character-to-luxury pipeline, and we love to see it. That’s right, illustrator Tove Jansson’s Moomin got the Bottega Veneta leather treatment — and it’s actually good? I’m not too shocked because it’s Bottega, a luxury brand known for leathercraft, but the most pleasant surprise lies in how organic Moomin Bottega actually feels, something that doesn’t always happen with character-luxury crossovers. The capsule feels a little left-field coming from Bottega, not a luxury brand you expect to link up with cartoon-y franchises. But, the Bottega-taste of it all comes from a balance between items literally stamped with Moomin comics and more clever pieces like the red-and-white striped Intrecciato-woven Andiamo and Campana handbags, which mimic Moomin’s striped apron. There are also artisanally crafted Intrecciato Moomin character charms, a delicious method of making what would otherwise feel like a cutesy Daiso find into a mini luxury item. (It’s all available November 11 in Japan, where Moomin is a bonafide celebrity, and November 18 rest of world.) Other luxury houses have previously run franchise-first plays to great success. LOEWE did Studio Ghibli in 2021, Balenciaga did Hello Kitty in 2020 (and they’re actually doing another Japan-exclusive collab …) Collaborations like these and Bottega Veneta’s Moomin collection are essentially fanboy grails that tap into a different demographic than a Richard Prince Louis Vuitton while still activating the human urge to collect. These leather Moomins demonstrate that there’s not so much separating an art-world aficionado and an action-figure collector, at least in the world of luxury. Everyone loves a specialty product that speaks to them! I bet my bottom dollar that there are people — probably with very deep pockets — who bought Studio Ghibli Puzzle bags though they still pronounce LOEWE like “low.” And you can bet Bottega Moomin will do similar numbers. That’s the power of a good franchise crossover, especially when the star is as cute as Moomin . articles.title: It's High Time You Invested in a Better Beanie
articles.summary: Beanies for men don't have to be boring. From classic wool knits to more offbeat takes on the winter staple, these are the styles worth getting your hands on.
articles._body: You don't have to be doomscrolling for very long to realize that beanies are one of the most important parts of any man's winter wardrobe. Particularly if you consider your taste a cut above. Because, let's be honest, a good beanie can do a lot of heavy lifting. It can rescue a questionable hair day (if you're lucky enough to still have any), pull an otherwise bog-standard fit together, or even serve as a not-so-subtle indicator of your sartorial standing. Of course, finding the right beanie isn't quite as straightforward as it might seem. There's the question of fit, for starters. Do you like yours pulled right down over your ears, or are you more of a short, above-the-ear watch-cap type? Are you after something with a bit of slouch, or do you prefer a closer fit? These might sound like minor details, but anyone who's spent a winter looking a bit daft in the wrong beanie will know they matter. Beanies have always had a more seasonal thing going on. More of a cold-weather companion than an everyday fixture, they tend to be fished out just as the temperature starts to dip. Still, most of us have our preferences. Some are fiercely loyal to the same style year after year, while others are happy to experiment with a different shape, knit, or fit. The question is, which one will you be wearing this winter? The Scruffy One The poor beanie can only really go so far. Its ability to wow is limited by the nature of the very thing. This one, though? This one is cool. Norlha has given the humble beanie a bit of a shake-up with its laddered knit, which makes it look like it's been through the wars in the best possible way. It's made from 100% yak wool, too, so it's not exactly your run-of-the-mill head warmer. A little rough around the edges, and all the better for it. The Sk8r One Speaking of comebacks, Supreme has been having a pretty good run lately. The once-untouchable skate label has found its way back into the wardrobes of fashion's more clued-in crowd, and collaborations like this one are part of the reason why. Teaming up with Polartec, Supreme has given the humble beanie a fleece upgrade, making it a nice departure from the usual ribbed wool affair. The Dimensional One mfpen is usually good for taking familiar wardrobe staples and giving them a little twist. This beanie is no exception. The ribbed wool construction is nothing out of the ordinary, but the mix of brown and beige gives it a bit more going on than your standard one-color affair. Sometimes that's all you need. The Cheap(er) One Not every beanie needs to cost an arm and a leg. In fact, unless you're particularly precious about what's going on your head, there's a pretty good argument for keeping things simple. This Zara number is a straightforward rib-knit style in a dark khaki shade. No bells and whistles, just a decent beanie and plenty of change left over for something else. The Short King One At some point along the way, beanies got shorter and our ears got colder. The short watch cap is a bit of a throwback to that era, although Universal Works makes a pretty good case for bringing it back. Made from British wool, this one has a close-fitting shape and folded cuff that leaves your ears to fend for themselves. Not exactly the one to reach for when the temperature really drops, but if you like your beanies on the stingier side, this is the one. The Technical One Not every good beanie needs to reinvent the wheel. Sometimes a decent color combination and a logo in the right place will do just fine. This Arc'teryx number ticks both boxes, with its two-tone knit and familiar bird embroidery. It's the sort of thing that’ll work just as well with a technical jacket as it will your everyday winter get-up. The Hand-Me-Down One This is the traditional one. Cable knit and a shade of green that feels like it should come with a pint of Guinness. It's got a distinctly old-school feel to it, the kind of beanie you'd expect to find in a family photo from 40 years ago, only a little less moth-eaten. Made in Scotland, too, so it's not messing around when it comes to its knitting credentials . The Niche One Japanese design outdoes itself once again. If you know RoToTo, chances are you know it for its socks. The label has built a pretty serious reputation for its knitwear, too, and this waffle-knit watch cap is a good example of why. Made in Japan, it takes the familiar watch cap shape and gives it a waffle-knit construction that feels a bit more considered than your average beanie. Hey, sometimes it really is the little things. Some Strong Contenders: How We Test and Choose Products Style means different things to different people, but knowing what's worth your money shouldn't be a guessing game. At Highsnobiety, we’ve spent more than two decades covering fashion, keeping tabs on the brands worth knowing, and figuring out which products deserve your time. We test products firsthand when possible, digging into everything from quality and construction to comfort and wearability. With more brands competing for your attention than ever, we also consider what sets a product apart. For the rest, we lean on our product knowledge, editorial research, and the taste that’s made us a trusted voice in fashion. The full narrative arc peels back his many layers as an artist, giving fans a visual feast packed with genuine emotional resonance. This also showcases the vast potential of this young artist — who possesses both vocal prowess and creative talent — on the international stage. articles.title: U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions. Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission warned the same month that the platform was marketing to local investors without a licence. Seychelles’ Financial Services Authority said in May 2026 it took action against MX Global Ltd for unlicensed virtual-asset operations — footnoted in FinCEN’s order. Those compliance gaps matter because the illicit-flow thesis is specific, not guilt by association. Beyond Russia, FinCEN cites about $1 billion in direct traffic with more than 40 Iranian crypto exchangers, nearly $26 million with the OFAC-sanctioned A7 sanctions-evasion network, and almost $200 million tied to the A7A5 stablecoin. DPRK facilitators and cybercrime flows are also alleged. MEXC has not issued a public response to the Friday order; its main X account kept posting marketing content through the afternoon. Why it matters for bitcoin markets Practically, once the order bites, U.S. banks, money transmitters and other covered firms cannot move dollars or crypto to MEXC wallets or accounts. Offshore users may keep trading peer-to-peer, but dollar on-ramps and any bank that still clears for MEXC become legal risk. The template tracks earlier 9714 cut-offs of venues such as Bitzlato , and it lands beside a busy sanctions week that has already seen North Korea crypto designations, an Iranian exchange action, and Russia’s push to put bitcoin trading on the Moscow Exchange . Whether MEXC contests the finding, seeks an exemption, or quietly reroutes liquidity is the open question. For now the paper trail is clear: a final FinCEN order under 9714(a), a 30-day fuse after Federal Register publication, and Treasury’s claim of at least $16 billion in illicit volume sitting behind the cut-off. This post U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .

articles._body: Chris Brown and Usher are bringing the R&B Tour to Atlanta’s Mercedes-Benz Stadium for a record-breaking five nights, but the mini-residency got off to a rocky start with their first show on Thursday night (Nov. 5). Related Chris Brown & Usher Cancel 4 Shows Ahead of Brown’s Sentencing Court Date in London Usher & Chris Brown’s Raymond & Brown Tour 2026 Setlist: Every Song Played at the First Show Ye Makes Surprise Appearance at Chris Brown & Usher’s L.A. Show With Hit-Filled Medley Per The Atlanta Journal-Constitution , the concert started over two hours late. Brown and Usher never hit the stage together and their sets were cut short as the show was pressed against the midnight curfew. T.I. and Young Dro were the lone special guests for the night. Breezy attempted to calm the storm and defend himself from the backlash. “Internet [cap],” Brown wrote on his IG Story early Friday (Nov. 6). “Don’t fall for it.” When Usher made it on stage, he told fans, “Welcome to my show,” which only enflamed rumors of a rift with CB. “After this tour Chris need to stay far away from Usher. Dead ass,” one fan wrote on X. “Throw that my ‘big bro’ shit in the 🚮.” Another added: “They need to go ahead and wrap this tour up.” There will be four more shows to get back on track in Atlanta for Usher and Brown. The duo’s next chance comes on Friday (Nov. 6), which will be followed by shows on Sunday (Nov. 8), Tuesday (Nov. 10) and Wednesday (Nov. 11) before the trek heads to Los Angeles. The co-headlining tour has been a cash cow thus far, as the run was the highest-grossing and best-selling trek of September. According to Billboard Boxscore , the R&B Tour grossed $77.4 million and sold 423,000 tickets across 10 shows in the month. articles.title: Show HN: Realtime sync engine without any new infra
articles.summary:
Tandem is an open-source sync engine and client-side database that plugs into your existing infrastructure. Add the Tandem library to sync data in real time across your clients and server, without deploying any new services.

I started work on Tandem 6 years ago as a side project. I was frustrat
articles._body: Tandem is an open-source sync engine and client-side database that plugs into your existing infrastructure. Add the Tandem library to sync data in real time across your clients and server, without deploying any new services. I started work on Tandem 6 years ago as a side project. I was frustrated by the sync engine landscape at the time, thinking I could build a better DX and require less lock-in. Even now, sync engine companies and “full-stack databases” need you to migrate to their database or provision a separate service with auth, networking, etc. This makes them annoying to maintain and also harder to adopt incrementally. Tandem is designed to just be embedded into your existing frontend and backend code. You define a schema, set up a database adapter (any SQL-like database is supported), add the new sync endpoint to your existing API, and then you're good to go. Tandem uses DST (Deterministic Simulation Testing) on every PR and nightly to ensure correctness. Our DST system Gatekeeper lets us model not only storage and network failures, but also race conditions, by gating each call between client/server/other services independently. Tandem currently supports any React-based frontend, any serverful backend (like Cloudflare Durable Objects), and any SQL-like database. New adapters are easy to build, and PRs and issues are appreciated! articles.title: ESPN Warns Talent About Insider Betting on Prediction Markets
articles.summary: REUTERS/Mike Segar
articles._body: ESPN has added prediction markets to its existing guidelines about TV talents being prohibited from insider betting, Front Office Sports has learned. Last week, the network’s talent department circulated a memo, reviewed by FOS , to on-air employees containing general guidelines for social media posting, political commentary, and sports betting. The timing of the memo lined up with several days before the midterm elections, with political tensions expected to be high. Much of what was in the memo was not different from past years. But the memo also specified that talents are not allowed to bet on sports news where they have non-public information as a result of their jobs at ESPN, including on prediction markets, “including Polymarket.” While Polymarket is named in the memo, Kalshi is not. Examples in the memo of such bets include awards votes, player personnel decisions, and sports media deals—bets you might see listed as options on prediction markets. An ESPN spokesperson declined to comment. The prediction-market language is an update from a policy originally distributed to ESPN talents in 2023, ahead of the launch of the now-defunct ESPNBet. As first covered by The Action Network at the time , ESPN’s policy prohibits reporters from utilizing, disclosing, and providing access to “non-public information … for any betting-related purposes, including influencing others to place bets or disclosing such information to any sportsbook operator.” Talents are also not permitted to bet on games where they’re assigned to be covering, and insider reporters are banned entirely from wagering on the sports they cover. articles.summary: The Portland Trail Blazers sit atop the Western Conference with a 6-1 record going into Friday’s NBA Cup matchup against the second-placed Los Angeles Lakers. Hours before the 10 p.m. EST tip-off, a Hall of Fame point guard revealed that he’s a true believer in what Portland is doing
articles._body: The Portland Trail Blazers sit atop the Western Conference with a 6-1 record going into Friday’s NBA Cup matchup against the second-placed Los Angeles Lakers. Hours before the 10 p.m. EST tip-off, a Hall of Fame point guard revealed that he’s a true believer in what Portland is doing this year. During the latest segment of “NBA on ESPN,” Jason Kidd shares his two cents about the Blazers’ early success. Kidd claims he saw the high caliber of play coming all along, and credits Damian Lillard for ensuring that Deni Avdija takes over as the team’s leader. Overall, the former point guard, head coach, and now analyst likes the Blazers’ chances to make noise in the Western Conference. “I think when you talk about Dame and just his leadership and understanding,” Kidd said. “I thought he said something incredible the other day about Avdija, like, ‘He’s our horse. We’re here to support him. You go, we will follow.’ And so, as a leader, [Lillard’s] taking a step back, but he understands that the leader on the court is Avdija.” https://x.com/ESPNNBA/status/2118802047818461509 Lillard and Avdija have given the Blazers a solid one-two punch that’s been difficult for opponents to stop. The team is playing a unique brand of basketball that runs through Avdija, as the 25-year-old has emerged as Portland’s top player. His style of play opens up the floor for the shooters, which makes Lillard a perfect fit for Avdija’s game. Damian Lillard’s first year back with the Blazers has been stellar so far. While giving up the leadership role to Deni Avdija, the 14-year veteran is still averaging 20.1 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 4.1 assists per game while shooting 42.0% from the floor and 31.7% from beyond the three-point line. As for Avdija, the Israeli native is proving to be one of the most prolific forwards in the NBA. He enters Friday’s contest against the Lakers averaging 23.4 points, 6.4 rebounds, and 6.4 assists per game. He’s recording those numbers while owning a 47.8% field goal percentage and hitting 31.6% of his three-point attempts.
