Stewart helped the Grizzlies to a 5-0 start this season. As the team’s new defensive enforcer, he’s adapted well a
articles._body: Veteran center Isaiah Stewart thought he was heading to the Washington Wizards or the Los Angeles Lakers when the Detroit Pistons traded him to the Memphis Grizzlies over the summer. Stewart helped the Grizzlies to a 5-0 start this season. As the team’s new defensive enforcer, he’s adapted well after leaving the only NBA team he’s ever played for. Upon entering his seventh season, Stewart revealed how he first learned he was traded to the Grizzlies, per Andscape’s Marc Spears. “I got a call from my agent, and he’s thinking it’s maybe the Wizards or the Lakers, and called me back a couple minutes later and said Trajan called, and he got a deal from Memphis that he can’t turn down,” Stewart said. Grizzlies’ Isaiah Stewart reflected on his NBA career , as his reputation precedes him as an aggressive center who’s ready to fight at any notice. However, that’s just how he is as a competitor. Off the court, he’s much more tamed, as he revealed in his interview with Spears. “A lot of people judge me off of my perception as a basketball player, and an enforcer,” Stewart said. “To me, I think of it as I’m going to war. But I’m so competitive — that’s just who I am.” While joining the Grizzlies has been an ideal fresh start for the veteran, it’s not where he initially thought he was heading during the offseason. However, he’s happy it’s where he ended up. The Grizzlies are now 6-2 after their perfect start. Stewart is averaging 11.9 points on 66.7% shooting, including 57.1% from beyond the 3-point arc, and 3.4 rebounds per game. articles.title: Chainalysis says hackers stole credentials and tokens for all of its customers
articles.summary: Company said a "multifront cyberattack" included AI agents and an on-path data snatch.
articles._body: Blockchain analysis firm Chainalysis said that hackers have obtained sensitive personal information—including names, usernames, password hashes, and live tokens—for all of its users following a breach of its network security. The accomplishment could be a major coup for the attackers. Both Chainalysis and public sources have revealed a long list of high-profile customers, including government agencies such as the FBI, US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency, and the US Air Force, as well as private companies such as Microsoft, Coinbase, and Barclays. It's unclear if the data theft exposed customers to additional threats. We regret to inform you... Last Friday, Chainalysis said it had been the target of a cybersecurity incident in October that was similar to the hacks of other platforms during the same month. The external actor used AI agent-assisted offensive techniques to gain unauthorized access to Chainalysis systems and internal tools. An email the company sent to affected customers said some “non-sensitive customer data, such as user IDs, full names, email addresses, and organization role labels for users provisioned on our platform were accessed.” It's not clear why the company considered such information "non-sensitive." articles._body: Since former NBA insider Adrian Wojnarowski joined St. Bonaventure as the team’s general manager, the goal has been to mold the Bonnies into a perennial contender in the Atlantic 10 Conference whether that’s via the transfer portal or through high school recruiting. And when it comes to high school recruits, St. Bonaventure recently landed a commitment from class of 2027 forward Isaiah Carpenter, as per Dushawn London of 247Sports. Isaiah Carpenter’s commitment to St. Bonaventure gives the program their second commitment in the class of 2027, following Victor Aborowa’s decision back in September. Aborowa is the highest ranked recruit that the Bonnies have pulled in since the modern recruiting rankings. Carpenter will finish up his senior year of high school at St. James Performance Academy this season. He will join St. Bonaventure for the 2027-28 season. In the meantime, the Bonnies tipped off the 2026-27 season with a 79-71 loss to Youngstown State on Nov. 2. The Bonnies were led by guard Zach Philipkoski’s 28 points, three rebounds, four assists, two steals and one blocked shot. Center Benjamin Bill finished with 15 points and guard Taj Au-Duke added 12 points. Wojnarowski is in his third season as the program’s general manager. After his second year, he opted to part ways with former head coach Mike Schmidt. He was replaced with Mike MacDonald as the Bonnie’s new head coach. MacDonald had previously coached at the Division II and Division III levels, while also having a stint at Division I Canisius. The Bonnies are coming off a 17-17 finish last year, and a fifth consecutive season of missing the NCAA Tournament. articles.title: Exclusive: No, I Play Rocky didn’t use this filmmaking trick to recreate iconic scenes, with 1 exception
articles.summary: There’s no doubt that I Play Rocky perfectly depicts some of the original movie’s iconic scenes, especially due to Anthony Ippolito’s performance as Sylvester Stallone. Sometimes, the scenes are almost too perfectly recreated. Did director Peter Berg and Co. use any tricks, such
articles._body: There’s no doubt that I Play Rocky perfectly depicts some of the original movie’s iconic scenes, especially due to Anthony Ippolito’s performance as Sylvester Stallone . Sometimes, the scenes are almost too perfectly recreated. Did director Peter Berg and Co. use any tricks, such as superimposing Ippolito into scenes from Rocky, to accomplish these recreations? Surprisingly, they didn’t, with one exception. Ippolito, 27, might be too young to have used this trick on any of his other projects, looking to Farrelly while asked by ClutchPoints about being superimposed into scenes at the I Play Rocky roundtable. “One time,” Farrelly proudly said. “The orange.” The “orange” in question is the one thrown to Rocky while he’s running through the streets of Philadelphia. It makes sense, as recreating this shot would’ve been timely and expensive. “We didn’t wanna do visual effects,” Farrelly said. “In [Rocky’s] apartment, when his hands are up on the bar, we built that apartment. We put the shadow across his face. We did everything. “But the one scene was when he was running through Market Street, and the guy throws him an orange. We looked at that—we didn’t have a huge budget—and we’re looking, like, ‘This is gonna cost us a million bucks to do this.’ There’s hundreds of people we have to match, and you got fires, you gotta shut down the street, and we didn’t have enough,” he added. Why the scene was still “hard” to film A behind-the-scenes still from I Play Rocky courtesy of Amazon MGM Studios. While it was the only scene they used a green screen for, it was “hard.” Farrelly credited “genius” cinematographer Sean Porter for helping them pull it off. “We had him running along, and we had the green screen behind him,” Farrelly said, setting the scene, “And then we had one of our guys flip the orange. He [Ippolito] has to turn the exact same way.” Farrelly then remembered one more instance of using a green screen. When Rocky runs along the harbor, the ships in the background aren’t there anymore. It’s still Ippolito running—yes, he ran that fast —but the ships had to be placed in the background. They still shot it on location, though. “We had to put the ships in the background, but that’s him running, and that’s us on the harbor,” the director explained. “And, in fact, people have asked me [if] we sped up his running ’cause he’s so fast, and we did not. This kid is the fastest runner I’ve ever seen in my life. It’s insane. He outran the camera car — we had to speed the camera car up because he was going so fast.” Ippolito also praised Porter for his work. The whole crew “did such an excellent job on the film.” He was “very specific about what he wanted” when shooting scenes. Production designer Anthony Gasparro also got a shoutout from Ippolito, as he designed and constructed the sets, which he felt were “so nuanced and detail-oriented.” Ippolito felt he was “in a time capsule” filming some scenes in I Play Rocky. Did Peter Farrelly prefer the actors looked or acted more like their characters in I Play Rocky? A still from I Play Rocky courtesy of Amazon MGM Studios. I Play Rocky faces a familiar challenge to biopics in that its actors have to look and sound the part of who they’re playing. In this instance, the movie benefits from amazing casting, which was done by Rick Montgomery. Everyone in Rocky, from Ippolito to Scot Teller, who played Burt Young (who played Paulie in the Rocky franchise), looked and sounded exactly like who they were portraying. Kiki Seto, Stephan James, and Robert Morgan also did remarkable jobs in smaller roles as Talia Shire (who played Adrian), Carl Weathers (who played Apollo Creed), and Burgess Meredith (who played Mickey). Many were looked at, but only a few could talk the talk. Looking and sounding the part were important to Farrelly, though he made one exception. Rocky producers Irwin Winkler and Robert Chartoff are played by P. J. Byrne and Toby Kebbell, respectively. Farrelly didn’t feel it was as necessary to cast actors who looked just like them since the general public wouldn’t pick Winkler or Chartoff or even Rocky director John G. Avildsen out of a crowd. “They had to look and sound the part. First of all, it was going for looks,” Farrelly recalled. “You had to match it, and Rick Montgomery did a stellar job finding Micky, Paulie, and Adrian, and especially this guy [points at Ippolito]. But I only cared what the people in Rocky looked like. “We kinda matched Winkler and Chartoff, but I didn’t care. Nobody knows what they look like. I happen to know, and we came close, but I wasn’t gonna waste time,” he continued. I Play Rocky is playing in select theaters. The post Exclusive: No, I Play Rocky didn’t use this filmmaking trick to recreate iconic scenes, with 1 exception appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Madison Square Garden Responds to Macklemore: ‘He’s Not an Arena Level Act’
articles.summary: The rapper also accused eight other arenas of blocking his Free Palestine tour from visiting.
articles._body: A spokesperson for Madison Square Garden has responded after Macklemore called out the arena for allegedly blocking him from performing there on his Free Palestine Tour. Related Macklemore Calls Out MSG, Kia Forum & More U.S. Arenas for Allegedly Refusing to Host His Free Palestine Tour A Timeline of the Ed Sheeran & Macklemore ‘Free Palestine’ Tour Controversy Macklemore Says His Free Palestine Tour ‘Sold Out Immediately,’ Teases ‘Lineups Coming Soon’ In a statement shared with Billboard , the spokesperson simply said Friday (Nov. 6), “We have some of the busiest venues in the world with extremely limited availability and he’s not an arena level act.” Billboard has reached out to Macklemore’s reps for comment. Earlier in the day, the rapper had named MSG and eight other arenas — Prudential Center, Barclays Center, UBS Arena, Intuit Dome, Kia Forum, Crypto.com Arena, Chase Center and Climate Pledge Arena — in a statement claiming he was not welcome at the venues due to his tour’s message and purpose. “From the beginning, our plan was to bring this tour home to the U.S,” he wrote following his Free Palestine shows in Dublin, Paris and London. “But after weeks of reaching out, nine major American arenas have turned us down.” “By mid-September, we received available dates at these arenas through the end of the year,” he continued. “But once they found out these were my benefit shows for Palestine, those dates were suddenly off the table. The doors were closed. The conversations were all different, but the result was the same. The shows were not going to be allowed to happen in these venues.” He added that he’d “rather lose every opportunity in this industry than spend another day protecting people who value their business relationships with Israel more than they value Palestinian human life.” Despite the MSG spokesperson’s claim, Macklemore’s previous three Free Palestine shows all took place in arenas: 3Arena in Dublin, Accor Arena in Paris and the OVO Arena Wembley in London. Each performance sold out immediately , according to the musician, and each drew thousands of fans and featured guest performances from Hozier, Kneecap and AURORA. On Nov. 14, 2013, Macklemore & Ryan Lewis headlined a show at Madison Square Garden at the height of the duo’s commercial powers. This latest development follows Macklemore’s previous conflict with Robert Kraft — whose Kraft Group owns Gillette Stadium — and other American stadium owners who allegedly banded together to pressure Ed Sheeran’s promoter into dropping the rapper from the Loop Tour supporting lineup. During his first two performances opening for Sheeran, Macklemore had incorporated “Free Palestine” demonstrations into his act. In the aftermath of his dismissal from the Loop trek, the “Thrift Shop” artist announced his Free Palestine trek as well as donated $1 million to humanitarian aid for Gaza.

articles.title: Weezer, Hilary Duff and More Set for Billboard Live Music Summit 2026: WHAT TO EXPECT
articles.summary: Billboard Live Music Summit to feature star-studded panels, awards, and luncheon sponsored by AEG Presents.
articles._body: This article was created in partnership with AEG Presents.   Billboard’s Live Music Summit returns to Los Angeles on Nov. 10, bringing together some of the biggest names and influential voices in live entertainment for a day of industry conversations, networking and celebration. Among this year’s honorees are Weezer, receiving the Legends of Live Award, and Hilary Duff, recognized with Outstanding Pop Tour of the Year. With more than three decades of touring under their belt, Weezer has built a devoted, multigenerational fanbase, bringing their catalog of alternative rock anthems to stages around the world. Currently on their 32-city arena, The Gathering World Tour, the band continues to demonstrate the enduring appeal that has made them a force in live music.  At the summit, Weezer will reflect on their touring career and lasting impact on the industry in a conversation with Billboard co-chief content officer Jason Lipshutz. The band joins past Legends of Live recipients including Usher and John Mayer.     Beyond the stage, the summit offers opportunities for the people behind live music to connect. Returning as a sponsor, AEG Presents will host this year’s luncheon, bringing artists, executives and industry leaders together for an afternoon of conversation and networking. As a leading global live entertainment company behind major tours, festivals and live experiences, AEG Presents shares the summit’s commitment to celebrating the people and partnerships that keep the industry moving.   Hilary Duff will also take the spotlight, receiving the Outstanding Pop Tour of the Year honor for her Lucky Me Tour and joining Billboard correspondent Lyndsey Havens for an exclusive conversation. After more than a decade away from touring, Duff made her highly anticipated return with the intimate Small Room, Big Nerves shows, reconnecting with fans who grew up alongside her. What began as a limited four-show run quickly evolved into a full-scale Lucky Me world tour, fueled by overwhelming demand and an expanding schedule of dates through 2027. With 32 new extension dates, the tour now spans 91 shows worldwide, kicking off in Madrid in May 2027 and wrapping in Anaheim, California in November.    Beyond the honorees, the summit will bring together executives and industry leaders for discussions exploring the evolving live entertainment landscape.  MSG Entertainment’s Josephine Vaccerello will join Billboard’s senior correspondent Kristin Robinson for a live taping of Billboard’s On The Record, while representatives from leading talent agencies UTA (Jbeau Lewis), The TEAM (Kevin Shivers), WME (Robby Fraser), IAG (Jarred Arfa), TBA (Josh Mulder), and CAA (Shirin Nury) will discuss the business of touring on the agency sector panel. The conversation will be followed by a discussion on the festival market, featuring Dreamshop Management’s Heather Kolker, ROAM’s Jeremy Shpinzer, C3 Presents’ Huston Powell, Goldenvoice’s Melissa Ormond, and Another Planet’s Allen Scott, moderated by TK. Rounding out the programming, Billboard’s co-chief content officer Leila Cobo will moderate a conversation on international touring with OCESA’s Guillermo “Memo” Parra, Live Nation’s Nidhish Varughese, Oak View Group’s Steve Collins, and AEG Presents’ Angie Rho. The Tigers tied with three other teams for fifth place in the SEC, a half-game behind the Ole Miss Rebels and Alabama Crimson Tide for fourth place. Quarterback Austin Simmons h
articles._body: Coach Eli Drinkwitz’s Missouri Tigers are 6-2 on the season and slight underdogs against Texas in Week 10 action . The Tigers tied with three other teams for fifth place in the SEC, a half-game behind the Ole Miss Rebels and Alabama Crimson Tide for fourth place. Quarterback Austin Simmons has wowed fans with insane throws this season and now has a chance to announce himself on the national stage against Arch Manning and the Longhorns. On November 6, ESPN writer Pete Thamel shared a Simmons announcement that will keep him in Columbia, Missouri for the foreseeable future . “Sources: Missouri has re-signed quarterback Austin Simmons for the 2027 season, which would bring back a player who projects as one of the faces of the sport. By signing now, Simmons’ return allows the staff at Missouri to retain and recruit a top roster.” Simmons is a 6-foot-4, 220-pound senior from Miami, Florida who has passed for nearly 2,000 yards (1,952) this season. He has 16 touchdown passes against just two interceptions, although his completion percentage (63.3%) needs plenty of improvement. The Tigers are making noise about getting the gang back together for next season as Drinkwitz recently shot down Florida State coaching rumors . Getting Simmons back in the fold gives the Tigers plenty of leverage on the recruiting trail and in the transfer portal, as he is a veteran with a high level of production and commitment to winning a championship in Columbia. Whether or not it comes true is anyone’s guess, but for now, the Tigers have tons of momentum heading into their clash with the Longhorns. Beating Arch Manning and the ‘Horns could launch not only Simmons as a national star, but the entire Tigers program as one to watch in the coming weeks and months on a national scale. articles.title: Yoshitomo Nara’s Big-Headed Girls Have Found Their Forever Designer
articles.summary: The British designer and Japanese artist's third collection proves why this is a match made in heaven, fueled by mutual respect and artisanal craftsmanship.
articles._body: Seeing a major artist collaborate with fashion brands is nothing new. We’ve lost count of the capsule collections pumped out with work by Takashi Murakami and Damien Hirst, Keith Haring and KAWS . Once you reach a certain level of fame in the art world, brands will come calling . What’s rare isn’t the crossover; it’s seeing one artist stick almost exclusively to one fashion brand, like Yoshitomo Nara and Stella McCartney . On one side is Nara, famed for his punkish series of cartoonish children with oversized heads and oversized eyes, expressive and often almost comically disdainful; on the other, the British designer known for her countercultural, nonconformist vibe. The pairing is built on a kind of sympatico energy that slapping Basquiat’s Neo-Expressionist art onto a T-shirt could never do. Each comes from different worlds, but their matchup makes perfect sense. Both McCartney and Nara champion youth-led activist causes, including climate change. This translates into collections that are more than just cute, wide-eyed girls and animals printed and embroidered onto clothes; the capsules are made with “100 percent responsible” materials like deadstock yarn and vegan leather, according to McCartney. It adds up to a pretty clear argument for why Nara rarely strays from the McCartney coop. The artist’s other collabs are one-off, small endeavors, like last year’s FireAid benefit concert merch after the LA wildfires and bottle designs for the Y by Yoshiki winemaker. With the announcement of a third McCartney x Nara collection, releasing November 11, this dynamic duo couldn't have better timing. Nara-mania is in full swing lately: the David Zwirner gallery just opened its first-ever show of the artist, which also marks Nara’s first solo New York exhibition in nearly a decade. And on November 19, auction house Fair Warning will sell In the Milky Lake / Thinking One — the largest of his works to ever sell at auction, with an estimate of $10-$15 million. That is likely a far higher price tag than most can afford, but that’s what makes the Stella McCartney collab so genius. Nara’s signature “big-headed girls,” as they’re commonly called, don’t just look great on a canvas, hung in a gallery. They look mighty fine grafted onto McCartney’s eco-friendly hoodies and sweaters, or a surprise adidas SPW64 sneaker — a triple-collab take on the shoemaker’s Tokyo 64 track silhouette, quietly tucked into the drop. In the first collection, which marked Nara’s first-ever fashion collab, McCartney picked the works she wanted to use; in the second, they switched it up, with Nara picking and the designer placing them as she saw fit. With the third, they moved into the atelier together for made-to-order pieces like a grail-worthy knitted sweater embroidered with Cutie in the Puddle — a 60-hour undertaking per piece. That kind of creative dialogue is what separates this from the gift-shop fare that usually trails a big art star. What you’re buying into here is something no amount of money can touch: mutual respect. Highsnobiety has affiliate marketing partnerships, which means we may receive a commission from your purchase. A former WWE and TNA tag team champion, Hardy recently formed a partnership with Moose on TNA Impact to take on The Syx. However, ahead of that, Hardy answe
articles._body: Regarded as one of the greatest pro-wrestlers of all time, WWE legend and current TNA star Matt Hardy is still going strong at 52 years old. A former WWE and TNA tag team champion , Hardy recently formed a partnership with Moose on TNA Impact to take on The Syx. However, ahead of that, Hardy answered a few exclusive questions from ClutchPoints, where he opened up about his retirement plans. Over the age of 50 and nearing his career’s dusk, Hardy was asked what his retirement might look like. While not ready to hang up his boots anytime soon, Hardy claimed that the retirement question at this stage of his career is understandable. “We have not talked about that. We get that question quite a bit now, which is understandable. But we’ve never really thought about what our retirement match would be, or how to get to it, or what to do,” he said. Hardy further added that he would like his last match to be him and Jeff Hardy taking on Edge and Christian Cage in a ladder match. “Kind of end things that way. Because it started for us there, as I said earlier. That’s the match where it changed. We all became stars that night. I don’t know, man. I’m just feeling good, and I’m just trying to give back, trying to help the next generation, trying to make pro wrestling as prevalent and as good as it can be right now,” he added. As a WWE veteran, it would only be justified for him to earn a WWE Hall of Fame induction like many of his colleagues. When asked about getting another WrestleMania moment and a Hall of Fame induction, he said, “I would love for it to happen. It would be great. It would be cool, especially if the circumstances were right and all the stars and the planets were aligned. It would be very cool.” However, as of now, Hardy is a regular on TNA and wrestles almost on a weekly basis on the Impact episodes. Currently in a feud with Syx, Hardy did not share anything concrete about making a jump to WWE. WWE veteran Matt Hardy addresses the online negativity about TNA PPV numbers Answering ClutchPoints’ questions via Casino.org US , Hardy was asked about the ongoing social media negativity about TNA’s PPV numbers. Earlier this year, in Jan. 2026, TNA premiered on the AMC Network and has been a regular on the channel. However, despite their weekly shows and extremely good PPVs, there has been recurring negative social media banter about the promotion’s PPV numbers and gate attendance. “It’s natural. People criticise everything, now more than ever, especially if you’re someone who is actively online. I almost feel bad for people to get into wrestling now and have to read what people say to them after they perform, especially if they’re a younger guy and they haven’t gotten used to it, or they haven’t learned how to [handle it]. “Social media is so interesting, because when people are posting their opinions, that often does not reflect reality. And sometimes it’s hard for people to look past that and understand that. And even with TNA, our ratings have been so much further up than they were on AXS TV. The highest show that we had done, we did 307,000, 309,000 viewers live, and it was the one that featured the Righteous Deletion, us vs. the Righteous. “That was a very story-driven, character-based programme altogether, and it was our blow-off. So it just showed that people cared about that programme. So with that being said, I think TNA is doing good. We’re holding the path. We go against football, and our numbers are still coming up on Thursday night, even going against the NFL, which does massive numbers,” he finished. Matt Hardy is very positive about Zilla Fatu’s addition to WWE’s John Cena Classic Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports. Earlier this week, on the Nov. 4, 2026 episode of WWE NXT, John Cena appeared and announced Zilla Fatu as the second addition to the upcoming John Cena Classic . When asked Matt Hardy about his thoughts on Fatu’s addition, he shared an extremely positive feeling about it. “Zilla is certainly gonna benefit from entering that. We’re big Zilla guys. We were obviously real close with his dad. I remember when he was a little baby, man. And it’s so cool that we’ve got to work with him and against him a couple times recently, and I’m so happy he ended up going to WWE. I certainly think he’ll benefit. I think someone like Ethan Page, who I’m a big fan of as well, would benefit from being in it also,” he finished. The John Cena Classic is scheduled to take place on Dec. 14, 2026. The John Cena Classic will be taking place at the ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex at Walt Disney World in Kissimmee, Florida. articles.title: Five games that could impact ESPN College GameDay's Week 11 location
articles.summary: The calendar has flipped to November, and a jam-packed slate of games awaits in Week 10. Some of them could have implications for ESPN’s College GameDay and its next location in Week 11 on Nov. 14. Saturday morning, College GameDay will be in South Bend for the highly anticipated matchup between Mia
articles._body: The calendar has flipped to November, and a jam-packed slate of games awaits in Week 10. Some of them could have implications for ESPN’s College GameDay and its next location in Week 11 on Nov. 14. Saturday morning, College GameDay will be in South Bend for the highly anticipated matchup between Miami and Notre Dame . The program has drawn strong TV ratings throughout the 2026 season and is coming off 2.5 million viewers on average for Week 9 at Indiana . $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage As for where College GameDay could go next, there are a few options, and Rece Davis hinted at a potential Group of 6 trip, as well. Here are some of the Week 10 games that might have implications for next week. #7 Texas vs. #18 Missouri Date/Time: Nov. 7, 12 p.m. ET Channel: ESPN Week 11 Games to Watch: Texas vs. LSU; Missouri vs. Georgia ESPN’s early game between Texas and Missouri could have plenty of College GameDay implications. Based on the Week 11 schedule, both teams could be playing in games that could put them in the spotlight. Texas is coming off a resounding win over Mississippi State , its second straight as part of a rebound from the loss to Florida . Missouri, meanwhile, cruised past Arkansas on the road last time out to stay squarely in a crowded SEC race. #5 Alabama vs. #14 LSU Date/Time: Nov. 7, 3:30 p.m. ET Channel: ABC Week 11 Game to Watch: Texas vs. LSU Saturday’s matchup between Alabama and LSU is already one of the biggest games of Week 10. But the Tigers could have an impact on ESPN’s College GameDay ahead of next week’s matchup against Texas . LSU is fresh off a bye as Alabama comes to town for a highly anticipated matchup. The Tigers enter Saturday with two straight wins, including a victory over Auburn prior to the week off, to set the stage for a Top-15 battle. #25 Boise State vs. Colorado State Date/Time: Nov. 7, 6 p.m. ET Channel: USA Week 11 Game to Watch: Oregon State vs. Boise State As the highest-ranked Group of 6 team in the initial College Football Playoff rankings, Boise State is in the driver’s seat for the G6 bid. Another big Pac-12 game awaits on Saturday against Colorado State , which Rece Davis has already hinted has College GameDay implications. Boise State survived a furious charge by Texas State in last week’s game to stay undefeated in Pac-12 play. The Broncos sit atop the new-look conference standings, and a win over Colorado State would add to the magnitude around the matchup with Oregon State in Week 11. #6 Kentucky vs. #14 Tennessee Date/Time: Nov. 7, 6:15 p.m. ET Channel: ESPN Week 11 Game to Watch: Florida vs. Kentucky Will Stein will continue his debut season at Kentucky with a road trip to Tennessee on Saturday evening. UK’s Week 11 game against Florida was another game Rece Davis indicated could be in the mix for College GameDay , as well. Kentucky is tied with Georgia atop the SEC standings and debuted at No. 6 in the initial College Football Playoff rankings. It’s been quite the first season in Lexington for Stein as the Wildcats get ready for a key road showdown at Tennessee on Saturday. Texas State vs. Oregon State Date/Time: Nov. 7, 10:30 p.m. ET Channel: The CW Week 11 Game to Watch: Oregon State vs. Boise State JaMarcus Shephard and Oregon State have become one of the stories in college football heading into November. The Beavers are 5-3 overall and 3-1 in Pac-12 play heading into Week 10, but a win over Texas State could put them in the College GameDay spotlight in Week 11. Oregon State is fresh off its first Pac-12 loss of the season, falling to Fresno State last time out. All the while, Texas State put up quite the fight against Boise State before the Broncos came away with a thrilling late-night victory in Week 9. More games to watch for College GameDay Week 11 Georgia vs. Ole Miss (Week 11 Game to Watch: Missouri vs. Georgia) Saturday’s primetime game between Georgia and Ole Miss is one of the top games on the Week 10 slate. The Bulldogs could also be in the mix for College GameDay in Week 11, though, if Missouri can take down Texas and bring CFP implications to next week’s matchup. Oklahoma vs. Florida (Week 11 Game to Watch: Florida vs. Kentucky) This week, Florida will take on Oklahoma to kick off the final stretch of the season. But the Gators will head to Lexington next week in Jon Sumrall’s return to Kentucky, and they could wind up in the College GameDay spotlight in the process. West Virginia vs. Texas Tech (Week 11 Game to Watch: Texas Tech vs. Oklahoma State) Fresh off a thrilling victory over Arizona , Texas Tech will now welcome West Virginia to continue Big 12 play. Depending on how some key results shake out on Saturday, though, it’s worth wondering if the Red Raiders could wind up in the mix to host College GameDay in Week 11. Oklahoma State vs. Kansas State (Week 11 Game to Watch: Texas Tech vs. Oklahoma State) Through Eric Morris’ first season at Oklahoma State, the Cowboys have shown one of the best offenses in the country, led by quarterback Drew Mestemaker . There could be an opportunity for another Big 12 feature on College GameDay in Week 11, though, when they head to Texas Tech. It looks like ESPN could have some strong options for College GameDay’s Week 11 location, given the buzz around the Week 10 slate of games. We likely won’t know where the show is going until Saturday night or Sunday, though.

Coach Nori’s unique approach to his first year with the Blazers included instructing his coaching
articles._body: After the Portland Blazers parted ways with head coach Tiago Splitter in favor of Micah Nori, many wondered how it would affect the team’s young players, including fourth-year guard Scoot Henderson. Coach Nori’s unique approach to his first year with the Blazers included instructing his coaching staff to read “The Old Man and the Sea,” by Ernest Hemingway. For the players, it’s Nori’s attention to detail that stands out most, Henderson said, per The Athletic’s Jason Quick. “We lacked small details,” Henderson said. “Great teams are big on that, from what I can see, just playing against them. Going back to last year, we lacked some of the small details. Nori is helping us with that.” Scoot Henderson and the Blazers have the best record (6-1) in the Western Conference standings. Two weeks into the regular season, head coach Micah Nori has his team fully committed to success, led by All-Star Deni Avdija and veterans Damian Lillard, Ja Morant, and Jrue Holiday. “I’m getting way too much credit, I really am; I’m not just saying that,” Nori said. “I’m not trying to be overly humble, but I’m getting way too much credit for putting really good players in good positions. It’s playing to their strengths; that’s all.” Portland is leading the league in scoring (121.9). Last year, the Blazers averaged the most turnovers in the NBA, more than 17 a game. This season, they rank 14th out of 30, averaging nearly two fewer. The vast improvements, along with early returns this season, have them positioned to become one of the better teams in the association. articles.title: Earth's churning mantle may have created the Great Unconformity
articles.summary: Explaining the Great Unconformity, where Cambrian deposits sit on top of older rocks.
articles._body: In the Grand Canyon, there is a line in the rock where time seems to have gone missing. Ancient crystalline rocks mark its bottom, while sandstones laid down as life started to diversify during the Cambrian explosion mark the top. “It’s called the Great Unconformity, and it’s a gap in the geologic record,” says Nicolas Flament, a geoscientist at the University of Wollongong, Australia. "This gap can be anywhere between 200 million years, which is not that impressive, to more than a billion years.” In a recent Nature study, Flament and his colleague Santosh Dhungana argue that this gap was carved with help from deep within the planet. According to their models, slow currents of hot rock in Earth's mantle pushed entire continents up for hundreds of millions of years, letting glaciers grind them down and then let them sink, allowing fresh sediments to bury the scar. The largest hole in the rock record might be a fingerprint of processes happening deep in the planet's interior. Ice and sea The oldest sediments resting on the Great Unconformity in North America are between 635 and 482 million years old. Geologists have traced it across most of North America and parts of northern Europe and northern China. “Something seems to have happened, in particular in North America,” Flament says. articles.title: Bears’ Kyle Monangai gets huge injury update for Buccaneers clash
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears have won three straight games, scoring 30 or more points in each of those victories. Here is the scary thing, though. Ben Johnson’s offense is operating well below its peak, at least on the ground. Although running back D’Andre Swift has six rushing touchdowns during
articles._body: The Chicago Bears have won three straight games, scoring 30 or more points in each of those victories. Here is the scary thing, though. Ben Johnson’s offense is operating well below its peak, at least on the ground. Although running back D’Andre Swift has six rushing touchdowns during the current winning streak, he averaged less than 3.0 yards per carry twice in the same span. Few veteran RBs can carry a backfield against physical defenses for an extend period of time. Fortunately, help is coming . Kyle Monangai returned to practice in limited fashion on Friday, making him questionable for Sunday night’s prime-time collision with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , per The 33rd Team’s Ari Meirov. The 2025 seventh-round draft pick has not played since Oct. 4 due to toe and thumb injuries. Even if Monangai cannot take the field in Week 9, it is deeply encouraging to see him clear this roadblock. The 5-foot-8, 207-pounder boasts 324 rushing yards and three TDs in four games played, averaging an excellent 5.4 yards per attempt. The Bears (6-2) lead the NFL with 281 rushes and rank second with 150.8 rushing yards per game (Bucs are No. 1). Heavy run volume is a major part of Johnson’s game plan, and Swift can only endure so many hits on his own. Simply put, the 24-year-old Kyle Monangai is arguably the biggest X-factor on this offense. It will be important to see how he responds after the layoff. Those type of injuries can certainly linger throughout the campaign. The Bears still trust D’Andre Swift, though, and do not have to hasten Monangai’s return. The Bears go on their bye in Week 10, so there is potential benefit to giving the former Rutgers star a little more time off. articles.title: Democrats just won control of Georgia Power’s regulator for the first time in 30 years — and its OpenAI data center contract was entirely redacted
articles.summary: Beginning in January, three of the five officials on the Georgia Public Service Commission will be Democrats.
articles._body: “This story was originally published by Grist . Sign up for Grist’s weekly newsletter here .” Beginning in January, three of the five officials on the Georgia Public Service Commission will be Democrats. It will be the first time the party has controlled the powerful energy regulation board in 30 years. The commission, which regulates utilities including the state’s largest electric provider, Georgia Power, has come under more scrutiny in recent years due to rising power bills and the high energy demands of data centers.  Now, Democrats plan to focus on affordability, clean energy, and closer scrutiny of Georgia Power.  “There’s a long laundry list of things that need to be looked into,” said Democratic commissioner Peter Hubbard, who won his reelection bid this week. “And so we’ll have to triage, in fact, and decide how best to move forward.” One of his first priorities will be launching an affordability docket, he said — a series of hearings that would delve into the reasons for high power bills and ways to save customers money. Hubbard said he and his fellow Democrats also plan to bring close scrutiny to upcoming Georgia Power requests around making more energy and adjusting customer rates. Shelia Edwards and Alicia Johnson are the other two Democrats on the PSC. But any changes, especially to power bills, will likely take time.  “We may not be able to expect immediate effects on our wallets,” said Emory University associate professor Kristin Phillips, who studies energy burden and the PSC. “But I think we can expect immediate change in the types of decisions that are made.” Affordability and high energy bills were driving issues in the campaigns both this year and last year, the two elections that together resulted in the new Democratic majority on the commission. “We knew that we had to connect the dots between energy and affordability,” said Brionté McCorkle of Georgia Conservation Voters, a group that campaigned for the Democratic candidates and worked to draw attention to the PSC elections. “It’s not just this obscure regulatory body like it used to be treated. Its decisions directly affect household budgets, communities, health, and our energy future.” Chris Womack, the CEO of Southern Company, Georgia Power’s parent company, also acknowledged the central importance of affordability during the company’s third-quarter earnings call on Thursday. But Womack said he’s confident the utility can address those concerns with the new commissioners. “If you look at what we have been doing with rate freezes, with benefits, with how we are providing benefits from growth to customers — existing customers — as well as to the communities, we think that’s a strong platform to stand on,” he said. Read Next How the midterms could unleash a new era for clean energy in these 3 states Jake Bittle Since the data center boom in Georgia began, Georgia Power has maintained that the increased revenue would more than pay for the new infrastructure to serve them, which the utility argues would keep rates lower for residential and small business customers. The utility calls this “downward pressure.” It doesn’t mean rates will go down, but rather that any increases would be offset by the influx of revenue from data centers.  The utility recently doubled down on that promise as part of its deal to serve a massive new OpenAI data center. The deal, Georgia Power said, would bring $15 of not savings but downward pressure per month for what Georgia Power calls the “typical” residential customer.  Separately, Georgia Power also credited the increased revenue from data centers for the temporary rate freeze approved last year. But the rate freeze received criticism from some advocacy groups. Instead of first holding a PSC hearing to give advocates a chance to verify the utility’s financial claims, Georgia Power announced the temporary rate freeze. Advocates feel that the backward process left them unable to confirm whether the company was delivering on its promises and fully shielding ordinary customers from data center costs.  It’s part of a broader criticism often leveled at the PSC and Georgia Power: lack of transparency. The OpenAI contract was entirely redacted, and only a summary provided to the public after it was approved. Specific details involved in service contracts, deals to buy energy, and construction costs are often redacted from the utility’s public filings under the auspices of trade secrecy. “I absolutely think transparency is potentially one of the biggest impacts here,” said Phillips of the election results. “It has been often on advocates to push on the way that the PSC communicates about the decisions that it’s making, and I’m hoping that there will be more clarity and transparency.” The Democrats on the commission have promised to bring increased scrutiny to the next rate-setting process, due in 2028, along with Georgia Power’s long-term plans to make and deliver energy, its forecasts about rising demand, and other issues. Hubbard has also proposed conducting a rate case for the state’s natural gas utilities, which he said hasn’t been done in over a decade. And he said they’ll push for other changes going forward. “We’ll continue with an agenda next year and the year after that to take advantage of this four-year period when we have the majority and can push for long-lasting reforms and shifting the direction of the state in terms of energy,” Hubbard said. This article originally appeared in Grist at https://grist.org/georgia-psc/democrats-take-control-of-georgias-powerful-utility-regulator/ . Grist is a nonprofit, independent media organization dedicated to reporting on climate change. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: ‘Everyone knows why we lost,’ JD Vance points to the Iran war — which has already cost at least $38 billion and 19 American lives
articles.summary: During the summer, the U.S. and Iran agreed to an initial 14-point memorandum of understanding that, if finalized, could have brought a permanent end to the hostilities.
articles._body: While votes were still being counted in the U.S. midterm elections , administration figures in Washington were already inviting speculation over how the results might be connected to the conflict with Iran . On the morning after the election, Vice President JD Vance wrote on X that the major reason for the dramatic loss for Republicans was the American public’s opposition to the war. “Everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there,” he wrote, in reference to the ongoing conflict that began with U.S.-Israeli airstrikes against Iran in late February 2026. While it is rare for a vice president to make such a critical proclamation about their own administration’s policy, President Donald Trump later stated that he did not disagree with Vance’s appraisal of the role that frustration with the Iran war played in voters’ minds. But whether this changes Trump’s view on next steps in the ongoing conflict remains unclear. Reporting over the past few weeks has indicated that the U.S. military has been actively preparing options and increasing capabilities in the Persian Gulf region in the event the president directs a resumption of hostilities. As an expert on Middle East affairs and a former senior official at the National Security Council during the first Trump administration, I’m aware that months of conflict have failed to bring Iran to its knees, force regime change or militarily defeat a perceived threat to U.S. assets and allies. Escalating now is unlikely to change those realities – and it carries the additional risk of further damaging Republicans in the eyes of Americans voters as they turn toward the 2028 presidential race. Even if Trump were to ratchet up the conflict, moreover, it’s unclear how much wiggle room he’ll have come January facing a Democratic Congress almost uniformly opposed to the war . Sunk costs Part of the issue facing Iran war hawks in Washington now is that the conflict has caused serious setbacks for the regime in Tehran without satisfying the officially stated strategic reasons for going to war. They argue that pulling back now – as welcome as that might be for Americans struggling with the associated rising cost of fuel – may allow Iran to rebuild before the conflict is “won.” Moreover, it would render the military and reputational costs already sunk by Washington as wasted. Among the achievements of this war touted by the Trump administration has been the death of former Supreme Leader Ali Khameini , along with the killing of scores of senior leaders within the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps – including individuals like the former head of Iran’s National Security Council Ali Larijani . Significant elements of Iran’s air defense and radar network, ballistic missile and drone production, and storage and launch sites have also been destroyed. And Iran’s already outdated navy and air force has been further degraded. Meanwhile, the U.S.-imposed naval blockade against Iranian-linked shipping in the Persian Gulf cut off a crucial lifeline for Iran’s economy. And additional sanctions and economic penalties imposed by Washington have served to further devalue Iran’s currency and deprive Iran of additional financial links to the international banking system. Down but not out Yet for all the U.S. successes in degrading the Iranian military by limitless aerial bombardment and the significant financial pressure against the Iranian economy, an obvious endgame remains elusive. Despite weakening the Iranian government – now led by Ali Khameinei’s son, Mojtaba, and a new echelon of senior IRGC commanders – the Islamic Republic remains intact. Moreover, it still possesses enough ballistic missiles and drones to hold the region at risk, while continuing to impose significant control over its population . Meanwhile, U.S. military spending continues to rise. In September, the U.S. Congressional Budget Office assessed that the military costs of the Iran War had already totaled US$38 billion . Since then, that number has only increased . And that is to say nothing of the associated global economic costs that have resulted from Iran’s de facto closure of the Strait of Hormuz – a key shipping route for oil and gas. Should Trump decide to change course on Iran, he – and others – may think that the money, effort and lives of 19 American servicemen killed in the conflict would have been spent with no obvious objective achieved. Yet continued military expenditure with no strategic endgame could only magnify those same costs. To Iran, the midterm results have not changed its public position. Mojtaba Khameini has issued statements directing the IRGC to widen the conflict in the region and perhaps beyond should the U.S. and Israel attack again. At the same time, a statement attributed to him indicates that hostilities between the United States and Iran will persist regardless of the balance of party political power in Washington. This raises questions about the prospects for diplomacy . During the summer, the U.S. and Iran agreed to an initial 14-point memorandum of understanding that, if finalized, could have brought a permanent end to the hostilities. But since the 60-day clock on that agreement lapsed , no parallel diplomatic agreement has emerged. No practical solution Even with the major shift in the U.S. political landscape, it remains unclear whether Trump will resume operations against Iran before the new Congress is sworn in. The messy election result in Israel – which has left the pro-war, and potentially outgoing, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyanu with potentially more reason to double-down in Iran – only complicates matters. articles.title: Gen Z voters broke for Democrats 66% to 31% in the midterms — and the Iran war cracked their top three issues
articles.summary: Overall, 27% of young people – meaning people ages 18 to 29 – went to the polls during the midterms, our Nov. 5 analysis shows.
articles._body: The economy was the top issue for voters in the November 2026 midterm elections, which saw Democrats win decisive majorities in both houses of Congress. And for young voters, whether in college or not, the economy and jobs, as well as healthcare, were their top concerns, our research at CIRCLE , a nonpartisan, research organization focused on youth civic engagement at Tufts University, shows. Overall, 27% of young people – meaning people ages 18 to 29 – went to the polls during the midterms, our Nov. 5 analysis shows. This marks the second-highest midterm youth voter turnout in the past 30 years, behind only the 2018 election cycle. As a scholar at CIRCLE who studies young people and their voting behavior, I think it’s helpful to understand some of the factors that motivated so many young people to vote – and to cast their lot with the Democrats. Understanding young voters Among youth, being enrolled as a college student or not did not make a big difference in who they voted for during these midterms. But there are some voting trend differences based on young people’s educational attainment, especially in the gap between young people with an education level of high school or less, and those with at least some college experience and more. Those with only a high school degree or less voted Democratic by a 24-point margin, compared with a 42-point margin among those with at least some college education. College students who are young men also voted Democrat by a 24-point margin . Female college students, meanwhile, voted Democrat at a 45-point margin. A similar gender gap appears among young voters who aren’t in college. Overall, this gender gap has persisted at least since 2024, as young women then were also voting more Democratic than men were. Latest youth voter trends About 66% of young people ages 18-29 voted for a Democratic candidate for the U.S. House of Representatives, compared with 31% for a Republican candidate, our data shows. This marks the highest percentage of support for Democratic candidates among all age groups. Within this group, 70% of young women voted for a Democratic U.S. House candidate in the midterms, as opposed to 59% of young men. Partisan trends among young voters have fluctuated over the past few decades – in 2000, for example, 49% of young people voted Democratic, while 48% voted Republican. In 2026, Asian American and Pacific Islander, Black and Latino young people gave Democrat candidates the strongest support, at 81%, 79% and 71%, respectively. By comparison, 61% of white young people voted for Democratic House candidates, with 36% voting Republican. Young people are focused on the economy Across race, education, income and geographic location, young people overwhelmingly indicated that the economy and jobs was their top issue in this election. Healthcare and the Iran war also showed up as areas of importance for young voters. All three of these issues are connected to young people’s concerns about the cost of living. We found that voting preferences did vary according to how young people viewed their own financial circumstances, a pattern that held among college students. Low-income students were more likely than their affluent peers to vote for Democrats . The issues that matter most to young people have shifted considerably over the past several years. In 2020, we were seeing different groups of young people prioritize social issues like racism , climate change and gun control. In 2022, we began to see young people prioritize the economy – their concern about inflation was the second-most important issue to them after abortion. Now, after the economy , healthcare was ranked second for young voters. The third-most important issue was the war in Iran. This is striking, because in the past, we’ve polled young voters about foreign policy issues like the war between Israel and Palestinians and the war between Russia and Ukraine. Young people have never really ranked these other foreign policy issues as a top area of concern. On the sidelines Youth voter turnout generally tends to be much weaker in midterm elections than in presidential elections. In 2018, there was 28% turnout for young people – a midterm turnout that was considerably higher than 2014, when only 13% of young people turned out to vote. Campaigns seem to recognize that young voters tend to be less politically engaged. For example, our research shows that during the 2024 presidential election cycle, more than 1 in 3 young people were never contacted about the election. Among those without college experience, 48% were never contacted. Our research still shows that college students face logistical barriers to voting. Young people are frequent movers, which means they might need to reregister whenever they change addresses. The fact that college students may be living on campus while they’re registered to vote from their parents’ address can also create complications. College students still have more voting information than young people who are not in college. But compared with other age groups, young people receive less voting information – making their turnout in the 2026 midterms all the more remarkable. Sara Suzuki , Senior Researcher and Research Assistant Professor at CIRCLE, Tufts University This article is republished from The Conversation under a Creative Commons license. Read the original article . This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Gas was pricier on this Election Day than any before it — up almost 40% to $4.15 a gallon since the Iran war began
articles.summary: Right before 1974's midterm election, Gerald Ford launched the “Whip Inflation Now,” campaign. But Republicans lost 48 House seats and five Senate seats.
articles._body: As Democrats and Republicans look at the overwhelming results of the 2026 midterm election, it’s worth remembering what has become a political axiom in America: “ It’s the economy, stupid .” Democratic strategist James Carville famously said that to presidential candidate Bill Clinton in 1992, but he might have said “it’s energy prices” instead. The cost of energy underlies much of the economy , making energy and politics inseparable, especially when gasoline prices rise. Midterm elections have historically been difficult for incumbent presidents and often shift the balance of power in Washington, D.C. Many factors affecting gasoline prices are beyond a president’s or Congress’s control. Prices for crude oil and petroleum products such as gasoline are set on global markets as the results of economic forces of supply and demand. Even the companies that produce oil don’t have as much influence as people might think , because of how that oil gets to refineries: Over 60% of the world’s crude oil is transported by ocean tankers , with 20% of global supplies traveling through the Strait of Hormuz , which has been closed, or nearly so, for much of 2026 as the conflict with Iran drags on. When energy prices rise, other prices, such as food , follow. Sudden spikes in gasoline prices can contribute to higher inflation, both regionally and nationally . Voters pay attention to those changes, and incumbents are less likely to win reelection . For the 2026 midterm election, gasoline prices were the highest of any previous election. That put Republicans in the precarious position of defending their record . Four American presidents – Gerald Ford, Jimmy Carter, Ronald Reagan and Joe Biden – confronted the consequences of severe inflation and high fuel prices during midterm elections. Oil embargo, Nixon and Ford Richard Nixon was the first modern president to truly face an energy crisis that became political. In retaliation for U.S. support for Israel during the October 1973 Yom Kippur War, Arab members of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries cut oil production and imposed an oil embargo on the United States. OPEC oil production fell by 5% a month , and crude oil prices rocketed 184% from prewar levels of $4.31 to $10.31 per barrel in March 1974. Nixon’s federal price controls on petroleum didn’t prevent U.S. gasoline prices from increasing 32% . When Nixon resigned over the Watergate scandal in August 1974, Gerald Ford took office. Inflation was 12.3% , and gas prices were still high . Right before that year’s midterm election, Ford launched the “ Whip Inflation Now ,” or WIN, campaign. But Republicans lost 48 House seats and five Senate seats. “WIN” didn’t work, and by the 1976 presidential election, gas prices were over 60 cents a gallon – adjusted for inflation to late 2026, that’s $3.49. Ford lost his reelection bid to Jimmy Carter. Carter’s struggles In Carter’s first two years in office, starting in 1977, the monthly average price of unleaded gasoline in the U.S. stayed high and even climbed slightly . Inflation hit 9% in 1978 . In the 1978 midterm election, Democrats lost 15 House and three Senate seats . Inflation continued to climb , and by the 1980 presidential election, gas prices were twice what they had been in 1976 . Plagued by those figures and the Iranian hostage crisis, Carter lost the 1980 election to Ronald Reagan. Reagan enters the picture Reagan implemented “ Reaganomics ” by cutting taxes and regulations, reducing government spending, tightening monetary policy and removing the remaining price controls on petroleum . By the mid-1980s, increased oil production from U.S. and non-OPEC nations led to an oil glut , lowering the average price of crude oil and U.S. gasoline price from previous highs . In the 1982 midterms, Republicans lost 26 seats in the House and gained one in the Senate. Reagan won reelection to the presidency in a landslide in 1984, but the challenges for incumbents remained in the 1986 midterms. Though crude oil prices were $15 a barrel and gas had dropped to 82 cents a gallon, Republicans lost five seats in the House and eight in the Senate. Trump’s first round In the lead-up to the midterms during Donald Trump’s first term as president, crude prices had risen about 24% from when he took office in January 2017 to October 2018. And gas prices were up 22% . In the 2018 midterms, Republicans lost 41 House seats but gained two in the Senate . Biden years Over the course of 2020, COVID-19 restrictions slowed the U.S. economy. U.S. crude oil production fell as gasoline demand plummeted by 40% . Prices rose because of pandemic-related supply chain backups. And from Election Day in November 2020 to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, the average price of unleaded gasoline in the U.S. rose by 66%, from $2.11 to $3.52 per gallon . Also, as pandemic restrictions lifted and the economy began recovering, demand for gasoline rebounded, straining supplies. Upon taking office in 2021, Biden took steps to curb rising energy costs, including releasing oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve in March 2022, which the Treasury Department suggested helped prevent gasoline price increases of $0.17 to $0.42 per gallon . But other Biden policy moves made it harder to increase energy supplies. He canceled the Keystone XL pipeline project that would have brought more petroleum into the U.S. and suspended new oil and gas leases in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge and the Gulf of Mexico. He also recommitted the U.S. to the Paris climate accord , under which countries have promised to cut their greenhouse gas emissions, generally meaning moving away from fossil fuels as an energy source. In June 2022, inflation reached 9.1% , a 40-year high. And U.S. gasoline prices reached an all-time high of $4.929 per gallon ; adjusted for inflation, that’s $5.60 a gallon today. articles.title: Knicks rush to Taylor Swift’s defense after Tyler Kolek’s ‘fakest fan’ callout
articles.summary: After being called out by New York Knicks star Tyler Kolek for being the team’s “fakest celebrity fan,” the organization has defended Taylor Swift, who attended Game 4 of the NBA Finals. The Knicks issued a statement, defending Swift’s longtime fandom and her “long h
articles._body: After being called out by New York Knicks star Tyler Kolek for being the team’s “fakest celebrity fan,” the organization has defended Taylor Swift, who attended Game 4 of the NBA Finals. The Knicks issued a statement, defending Swift’s longtime fandom and her “long history with Madison Square Garden.” They are grateful for her support. “Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization,” the statement read. Knicks star Tyler Kolek’s comments about Taylor Swift’s fandom Brad Penner-Imagn Images. Kolek and his teammate, Mile McBride, did a video for Deflected. They were asked who the “fakest celebrity fan” of the Knicks is: Kolek said there are several “performative” fans who clout-chase by going to games. Among those celebrities was Swift. “At the Knicks games, I would say it’s very performative ’cause they just want to be seen at the game; they’re not necessarily fans,” said Kolek. “Maybe Taylor Swift. I don’t know if I’ve seen her at any other games.” McBride knew Kolek might have made a mistake, saying, “Swifties not gonna like that answer,” before shouting out other celebrity fans like Ben Stiller and Tracy Morgan. Kolek tried to save himself, conceding that Swift may have “a lot going on so she can’t come all the time.” Still, he finds it “a little performative.” Swift attended Game 4 of the NBA Finals when the Knicks played the San Antonio Spurs. They famously erased a 29-point deficit to gain a 3-1 lead in the series. She was decked out in a Knicks-themed shirt that read, “Stevie Knicks.” Swift sat alongside Mariska Hargitay and Este and Alana Haim. They stayed enthusiastic despite the Knicks trailing almost the entire game. However, a few weeks earlier, she attended one of the Knicks’ games against the Cleveland Cavaliers in the Eastern Conference Finals. She was with her husband and Ohio native Travis Kelce. articles.title: Florida voters nearly tripled the homeowner tax break — blowing an $11.8 billion hole in county budgets
articles.summary: This translates to a 30% reduction in revenue for Florida counties and a 13% cut for smaller municipal governments.
articles._body: Many Florida homeowners cheered on Nov. 3, 2026, when more than 60% of voters approved a constitutional amendment to significantly reduce property taxes. Under the measure, Amendment 3 , a homeowner’s tax break known as a homestead exemption would go from the current US$51,400 to $150,000 in 2027 and increase again to $250,000 in 2028. By shielding more of a home’s assessed value from taxation, this exemption effectively lowers homeowners’ tax bills. New Florida residents who buy a home would also reportedly be eligible for a property tax break, but on a more phased-in basis. But the measure comes with a hefty price tag. The Florida Legislature’s research arm estimated the measure would reduce annual revenue from property taxes by $11.8 billion . This translates to a 30% reduction in revenue for Florida counties and a 13% cut for smaller municipal governments. While homeowners will get some relief, the budget crunch due to the lower tax revenue will affect other Floridians in more adverse ways. As economists who have been following the debates over Amendment 3, we argue that local governments will struggle to fund basic services with less money. And we expect more sweeping economic consequences as well – including less affordable residential housing and a broader shift of the tax burden away from relatively wealthier homeowners to those who are less well off. How Amendment 3 would work Much of the political momentum for Amendment 3 came from a rise in the cost of living and frustration over rising property taxes . These now average just over $3,000 annually but can run much higher for Floridians with more expensive homes . In addition to raising the homestead tax exemption, Amendment 3 lowers the cap on annual assessments on rental and commercial properties from a 10% increase to a 5% increase . Since property taxes are based on an asset’s assessed value, this language effectively limits but doesn’t rule out tax hikes for businesses. So landlords, for example, could still see meaningful annual tax increases as their properties go up in value – costs that would likely be passed on to renters. Amendment 3 makes clear that school-related property taxes are exempt from these tax cuts. It also lists some theoretical limits on how local governments should use tax dollars, as a way to ensure continued funding for essential services such as public safety, infrastructure or obligations for employee retirement benefits. But it also states that funds may be used for “ expenditures approved ” by local and county governments – ambiguous wording that suggests these stipulations can be breached. Who pays the bill? Florida property taxes are levied and collected by some 640 local government entities. There’s no state income tax , so any reductions in property tax revenue directly affect local and county governments. With tax revenue slashed, businesses, landlords and owners of other non-homestead properties like second homes would almost certainly see their taxes go up. This is a typical pattern: When governments cut property taxes for some groups, taxes shift to other groups. This dynamic is likely to play out with local governments as they try to keep revenue stable: Amendment 3 would force them to hike taxes in other areas to make up for the shortfall. This could include increases in state and local sales taxes, an expansion of the list of goods subject to sales taxes , or a hike in “ documentary stamp taxes ,” which are required on documents such as deeds, bonds and mortgages. State and local governments could also impose higher fees for specific services, such as solid waste treatment and stormwater utilities . Another option is to hike permits and inspection fees , fuel taxes or other service charges such as vehicle registration fees. Finally, local governments could raise tourism-related taxes , such as on food, beverages and hotels. But this recourse wouldn’t help counties with limited tourism, and such revenues fluctuate in any event. In the end, though, essential services would still almost certainly be affected. Funding for police, fire and emergency medical services is primarily the responsibility of local governments, and, for most counties, they make up the largest line item in their annual expenditures. Reducing property taxes would amount to a direct hit, especially in smaller, less-populated counties. And if local governments do raise sales tax rates to the extent they can, lower-income Floridians will bear a disproportionate burden as they spend much more of their income on consumption. They’re also far more likely to rent than own a home, so any increased rents would take a bigger toll. A looming affordable housing crunch? Less noticed in the debate over Amendment 3 was how it would affect the state’s affordable housing shortage . We argue that the structure of the property tax cut will likely create more incentives for counties and developers to build commercial structures instead of more residential housing. When developers build residential homes, they require a basic level of public services to support residents and the local infrastructure. In fact, property taxes in much of Florida effectively subsidize residential home development: For every dollar that a homeowner pays in property taxes, it costs county governments around $1.20 to provide those services. This gap will only grow when property tax revenues fall. From the standpoint of local and county governments, then, it may make more sense to focus on commercial or industrial construction as a way to keep tax revenues stable. But with fewer homes built at the expense of business construction – from manufacturing to data centers – the supply squeeze will only drive up prices and rents for the workers who are needed for those jobs. Now that Amendment 3 is on the books, Florida’s county and local governments will confront major trade-offs. We believe that state officials will come to realize how much of a change has been made –

articles.summary: With the Florida State football program firing head coach Mike Norvell, speculation has been swirling in the sports world about who should replace him and lead the Seminoles in the foreseeable future. As Jimbo Fisher has been a popular name linked to the Florida State football team, the former he
articles._body: With the Florida State football program firing head coach Mike Norvell , speculation has been swirling in the sports world about who should replace him and lead the Seminoles in the foreseeable future. As Jimbo Fisher has been a popular name linked to the Florida State football team , the former head coach would reflect on leaving Tallahassee, Florida, back in 2017. Speaking on the “Trials to Triumph” podcast, Fisher would speak about his time as head coach with the Seminoles from 2010 to 2017, and how leaving was the “most difficult thing I’ve ever done,” further saying that he “never wanted to go.” “We had great success,” Fisher said, via Josh Chambers. “The last couple years we didn’t, but that run we had there, I did not ever want to leave. I don’t want to get into this the wrong way. I just knew, kind of, the situation the ACC is in now. I saw those things and tried to get us ahead of that a little bit.” “I wanted more stuff for our staff and players, and some more facilities, because I knew where the game was going and where we were putting our money,” Fisher continued. “It just never worked out. I’m not going to throw anybody under the bus. Sometimes you have to do it.” Jimbo Fisher says he never wanted to leave Florida State, and says leaving Tallahassee was the most difficult thing he’s ever done “Most difficult thing I’ve ever done. I never wanted to go. We had great success. The last couple years we didn’t, but that run we had there, I did… pic.twitter.com/He9nH4MJaq — Josh Chambers (@JoshChambers) November 5, 2026 Jimbo Fisher continues on painful Florida State football exit Fisher’s name has come up in connection with the Florida State football team now that Norvell has been fired, as no one can tell if the program would be interested in a reunion. If there’s one thing for certain, Fisher loves the school. “But listen, I grew up a Florida State fan; I love Florida State, I grew up loving Florida State,” Fisher said. “The Bowdens were like family to me, and I was like family to them. It was one of the most difficult things I’ve ever done…I remember I cried. You remember me? I cried. It killed me. But life takes turns sometimes.” It remains to be seen who the Seminoles get as their next head coach and if Fisher would be considered. articles.title: Your Winter Wardrobe Could Use a Few Quiet Overachievers
articles.summary: Discover Vuori’s winter wardrobe staples, from premium jackets and versatile pants to comfortable tops that nail the balance between style and comfort.
articles._body: Some clothes just get it right. No loud logos, no unnecessary bells and whistles, just good cuts, nice fabrics, and the kind of details that make you wonder why more brands don’t keep things this simple. We know by now that the best wardrobe staples aren’t necessarily the ones that grab your attention first, but the ones you keep reaching for long after the novelty of everything else has worn off. And when a piece looks as good as it feels, even better. The sweet spot is finding clothes that can pass for something from a fancy fashion label but still feel like things you’d actually want to wear on a regular ol’ Tuesday. Think less gym uniform, more genuinely good clothes that happen to be comfortable enough to spend all day in. A pretty good deal, if you ask us. Vuori has plenty of pieces that fit the bill. From the kind of pants that make you question why you ever put up with stiff ones to layers that look considerably more expensive than your average staples, the lineup has a few surprises up its sleeve. We’ve pulled together the standouts worth a closer look. Tops A good T-shirt is a good T-shirt, but finding one that gets the fit and finer details right is another story. Vuori makes a pretty convincing case for the everyday top, with Henleys, long sleeves, and ever-dependable sweatshirts that keep things simple without feeling like an afterthought. Not every top needs to reinvent the wheel. Sometimes you just need a really good wheel. Jackets Outerwear is where a wardrobe can get pretty expensive pretty quickly, so finding ones that earn their keep is always a win. You want something that can pull a fit together without making you feel like you need to plan the rest of your look around it. Vuori has a range of layers that keep things simple in the best way, with enough personality to hold their own. Basically, the sort of purchase that makes you feel very sensible, which is always a nice bonus. Pants People are particular about denim, and rightly so. Finding the right pair is a years-long pursuit for some, involving far too many fitting rooms and the occasional regrettable purchase. Vuori, however, has managed to get the balance right with jeans that keep the look simple while feeling exceptional. Oh, and the sweatpants are pretty great, too, for when denim just isn't on the agenda. Highsnobiety has affiliate marketing partnerships, which means we may receive a commission from your purchase. articles.title: Stephen A. Smith drops head-turning Carson Wentz declaration ahead of Vikings’ Josh Allen, Bills matchup
articles.summary: Coach Kevin O’Connell’s Minnesota Vikings are 6-1 following a division loss to the Detroit Lions that led to the elevation of Carson Wentz over Kyler Murray as starting quarterback. Wentz made comments on disgruntled receiver Justin Jefferson that showed his leadership skills ahead of
articles._body: Coach Kevin O’Connell’s Minnesota Vikings are 6-1 following a division loss to the Detroit Lions that led to the elevation of Carson Wentz over Kyler Murray as starting quarterback. Wentz made comments on disgruntled receiver Justin Jefferson that showed his leadership skills ahead of a Monday Night Football matchup with Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills. ESPN pundit Stephen A. Smith is keeping a close eye on the Vikings, making a declaration that rocked the set of the First Take TV show on Wentz. “If Wentz wins this game, because Wentz comes close to matching Josh Allen, Wentz is gonna be the new starting quarterback for the Minnesota Vikings, that’s what’s gonna happen,” Smith said. Wentz, 33, hasn’t had his best seasons in recent years, passing for just over 1,200 yards with six touchdowns and five interceptions for the Vikings last season. His last truly outstanding season came in 2021, when he passed for over 3,500 yards with 27 touchdowns and seven interceptions with the Indianapolis Colts. Murray is dealing with a hamstring injury but hasn’t gone on injured reserve. He passed for 210 yards with two touchdowns and one interception against the Lions but has just five touchdown passes on the season against three interceptions. He hasn’t made the most of a world-class defense led by defensive coordinator Brian Flores, a rising star in the coaching ranks. O’Connell sounded confident in his backup QB Wentz in comments made prior to Monday night’s game. Beating the Bills is a tall task, but Wentz has gone toe-to-toe with some of the NFL’s best over the course of his career and come out on top, making Monday Night Football an intriguing matchup to say the least.
