articles.title: Country Up-and-Comer Greylan James Talks Viral Hit ‘Water at a Wedding,’ His New Album, And the Kenny Chesney Advice That Sparked His Career
articles.summary: Greylan James, who just scored his first Billboard Hot 100 hit, is Billboard’s Country Up-and-Comer Artist of the Month for November.
articles._body: East Tennessee native Greylan James grew up immersed in country music, watching as another East Tennessee native, Kenny Chesney, amassed scores of hit songs and headlined Knoxville’s Neyland Stadium. “I met him briefly when I was in a bluegrass band when I was 11,” James recalls. “He showed up where we were playing at and I talked with him for a couple of seconds. I told him, ‘Hey, I want to drop out of school and move to Nashville. How do I do it?’ He was like, ‘Well, hold on, stay in school. But learn how to write songs. A lot of country singers don’t write songs.’ And that always stuck with me. From that moment on, I started writing.” That advice is paying off in more ways than one. James just earned his Billboard Hot 100 chart debut with his viral hit “Water at a Wedding,” which he wrote with Matt Dragstrem and Chase McGill. View this post on Instagram The song’s ripped-from-real-life vibe and roller-coaster storyline about a guy attending his ex’s wedding, and noticing that she’s drinking water rather than wine, got the internet buzzing — and is now inside the top 20 on Billboard ’s Country Airplay chart as well. And James keeps piling up new accolades seemingly every month; he made his Grand Ole Opry debut in October and on Nov. 13, will release his self-titled debut album. He’s set to hit the road as an opener on Chesney’s Original Vibe Room Stadium Tour next year. He’s also launching his own headlining trek, Wedding Season: The Tour, on Nov. 6. “I’m just trying to hold onto my seat,” James says. “It feels like this year has kind of flown by with so many milestones that I’ve worked years and years for, to almost fit into one year…I’m really grateful that it’s all coming together the way it has. I feel like my whole dream is coming true all at once.” He points to his Opry debut as another unbelievable watershed career moment. “The Opry is one of those stages I’ve dreamed about since I was a kid,” James told Billboard shortly before his Opry debut. “My papa always told me that if I got into music, you’ll know you made it when you play the Grand Ole Opry. And to know that I”m finally doing that, just thinking about my boots stepping into the circle, it’s a surreal feeling.” He may be just now coming into prominence as an artist, but he’s been building a reputation as a solid songwriter for the past several years in Nashville’s songwriting community. James is a co-writer on Jordan Davis’s ACM song of the year-winning “Next Thing You Know,” as well as songs recorded by Chesney (“Born,” “Come Here, Go Away”), Morgan Wallen (“Nothing Left”) and BRELAND (“For What It’s Worth”), among others. Now, with a debut album filled with songs he contributed to — and a tribute song to another East Tennessee-born country music icon — James aims to continue putting his own stamp on the genre. James, Billboard’s Country Up-and-Comer artist of the month for November, joins previously highlighted artists including Colton Dawson , Mack Geiger and Kaitlin Butts in our Up-and-Comer series. Below, James talks about the success of “Water at a Wedding,” his Kenny Chesney connection and why he hopes his debut album showcases fuller depths of his songwriting and artistic talent. You started singing at a very early age, and taking part in singing competitions. What were some of the songs you performed early on? One I sang was Toby Keith’s “Who’s Your Daddy” — which is a crazy song for a six-year-old to be singing, but I was. And one of the first songs I learned to sing was “Young” by Kenny Chesney. I asked my parents to take me to the Grand Ole Opry for my fifth or sixth birthday. They were like, ‘We can’t do that, but we can take you to a karaoke cafe and let you sing.” And now, it’s very full-circle. You have not only co-written songs that Kenny – who is also from the Knoxville area — has recorded, but you are touring with him next year. I remember everybody talking about the hometown boy Kenny Chesney, who made it and was from the high school down the road. I remember I dressed up as him for Halloween one year. My mom would cut the sleeves off my t-shirts, and she had a puka shell necklace that I got from her closet. Kenny’s mom worked at a hair salon, and my parents took me to get my hair cut there. Now, he’s become kind of a mentor, and it’s crazy that my childhood idol is now my tourmate and also a really good friend. “Water at a Wedding” has become your breakthrough song. What was it about that song that kind of raised its hand as a standout initially? I had another single at radio that was the exact opposite of the subject of “Water at a Wedding.” It was a very wholesome song, and it also wasn’t what I’d gone through on a personal level, wasn’t even remotely close. I was struggling with that at the time, having to promote something that I wasn’t super connected to. And so when I had this song, and I wanted to tease it, I made a fake account — because my label and friends, family, management were all like, “You got to stick to this other song.” And I was like, “But I want to post other stuff.” I made a fake account on TikTok and just called it Grayson Jones, which is just what people accidentally call me when they don’t know my name. The first song I posted was “Water at a Wedding,” and I just said, “Wrote this about going to my ex-girlfriend’s wedding.” I had zero followers, but a few hours later, I had like 400 views, and the next morning it was like thousands and thousands of views. It was funny, because some artists were reaching out to me on that page, like, “You need to move to Nashville,” and I wanted to be like, “It’s me, bro,” but I couldn’t really tell them. Then I went to the label and was like, “I think this song needs to come out, and I think I have proof that people are going to like it.” On your album, you have a new version of “Water At A Wedding” with Gabriella Rose. Why was she the right artist for this new version? S

articles.title: Nvidia hardware worth $11.4M vanished between Oakland and Texas
articles.summary: 6 pallets of hardware vanished en route to Texas, with no arrests 2 months later.
articles._body: A shipment of Nvidia hardware valued at $11.4 million vanished in transport between Oakland and Texas over the summer, and more than two months later, police have announced no arrests or recovery of the cargo. As reported by The Mercury News , six pallets of unknown Nvidia equipment left Oakland on August 29 on a truck bound for Fort Worth, Texas. The hardware was reportedly picked up as scheduled by a truck bearing the logo of a food transportation company before vanishing off the grid. The theft wasn't noticed until early September, when the buyers realized that the shipment had never been received. Police attempting to trace the truck's route found it had made several multi-hour stops after picking up the hardware before losing the truck somewhere in San Bernardino County, California. Oakland police confirmed that there was a grand theft report filed on September 13 and that the investigation remains ongoing. Authorities have not said what Nvidia hardware was stolen or exactly how the theft was carried out. Read full article Comments

Rumors suggest that teams are already monitoring the 27-year-old’s availability come the trade deadline, according to NBA insider Brett Siegel. You can then let it go and it will float over a world map using live wind data from NOAA's public wind forecast. Other users can then catch them in a timed window as they float by overhead and add on
articles._body: I created a web/mobile app that lets you write a story/secret/encouragement/etc... on a lantern. You can then let it go and it will float over a world map using live wind data from NOAA's public wind forecast. Other users can then catch them in a timed window as they float by overhead and add on to the message chain. Then they release them to continue on. It's just a fun thing I was trying - kind of like a message in a bottle but in the sky. I thought it sounded like a cool idea and after playing with it, I really like it but was curious if other people also thought it was cool or just seemed lame. lol If you'd be willing to check it out you can view lanterns without any signup or anything. But to launch one yourself, it requires an account (all free of course and Google and Apple OAuth supported). Only cities are shown for locations (never addresses). Does the idea of watching your own lanterns float around the world in real-time and seeing others catch them interest you enough to come back to, or does it need more? I welcome any feedback but would really appreciate creative ideas to enhance it. Thanks for any help! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50397561 Points: 3 # Comments: 0

It won’t be the first time that Badgers fans have seen Hopkins, as Joseph was benched in the second half after throwing for 90 yards, though the freshman recorded 93 yards and an interception. At any rate, it remains to be seen how Hopkins fares against Rutgers on Saturday and what the quarterback situation will look like with Joseph next week. He, however, can still enter the NFL draft with his new contract, sources tell On3. In his first year at Mizzou, Simmons has led the Tigers to a 6-2 record. He currently
articles._body: Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons has signed a deal to return to the program in 2027, On3’s Pete Nakos and Hayes Fawcett report. He, however, can still enter the NFL draft with his new contract, sources tell On3. In his first year at Mizzou , Simmons has led the Tigers to a 6-2 record. He currently ranks fourth in the SEC in both passing yards (1,952) and passing touchdowns (16). $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Simmons spent the first two seasons of his collegiate career at Ole Miss , where he played under former head coach Lane Kiffin . He entered the 2025 season as the Rebels’ starter, but was soon passed up by backup Trinidad Chambliss after suffering an injury in their second game of the season. Simmons finished out the season as Ole Miss ‘ backup, and hit the Transfer Portal in the offseason. The Miami native opted to remain in the SEC, winding up at Missouri to succeed quarterback Beau Pribula (who transferred to Virginia ) in Columbia. Simmons has more than lived up to his expectations, and has the Tigers in the thick of the College Football Playoff race heading down the final stretch of the season. Austin Simmons has excelled for Missouri this season Simmons has passed for multiple touchdowns in five of his eight games played this season. That includes a stellar performance against No. 8 Florida on Oct. 3, in which he totaled 340 yards passing and two passing touchdowns with no interceptions. Missouri ‘s 45-17 win over the Gators marked its first over a top-10 ranked SEC opponent since Oct. 12, 2013 (No. 7 Georgia ). “I’m very excited. I think the best thing about Austin is his communication skills,” head coach Eli Drinkwitz said about Simmons prior to the season. “He can communicate at a high level about what he’s seeing, what he understands, how routes are similar to what he’s done in the past that he really liked. That’s accelerated the growth between Coach [Chip] Lindsey , Coach [Garrett] Riley and what we’re doing. The thing that has been really cool to watch on the offensive side of the ball, we have a lot of flexibility in scheme. It’s about we can take this concept and this concept and marry it to what Austin really likes. I think that’s what great coaches do.” Missouri slotted in at No. 18 in the first College Football Playoff Rankings of the 2026 season. The Tigers are set to close out the regular season against No. 7 Texas , No. 2 Georgia , No. 6 Kentucky , and Oklahoma . It is certainly quite the gauntlet for a Missouri team looking to clinch its fourth-consecutive eight-plus win campaign.

articles.summary: The Louisville rapper is back with sequel to his 2020 EP.
articles._body: Jack Harlow has tapped back into his R&B bag once again. Related Jack Harlow’s Birthday Present Is the New Album ‘Monica’: Stream It Now Jack Harlow Preps Second Release of 2026 With ‘Sweet Action II’ EP Jack Harlow’s Hats, Ranked The Louisville rapper delivered the sequel to his 2020 Sweet Action EP, which featured his breakout hit “What’s Poppin,” on Friday (Nov. 6). However, this time around, he’s focusing less on braggadocious raps and more on the ladies as this project takes a more smoother tone. That’s immediately apparent with the lead single “ Too Soon ” featuring the legendary Babyface . Sweet Action II is seven tracks long and comes eight months after his divisive Monica album, on which he switched up his wardrobe and aesthetic while leaning into neo soul. The album dropped March 13, on his 28th birthday. There’s less singing on this go-round, but some of the same themes surrounding love, relationships and maturity are still there as he deals with navigating the things that come with success, fame and romance at such a young age. “Across its seven tracks, Sweet Action II finds Jack exploring the messy contradictions of modern romance, from new attraction and old attachments to jealousy and commitment,” read the press release for the set. “Blending sharp humor, conversational storytelling and vulnerability, the EP captures the tension between wanting love and holding on to freedom.” The project features samples and interpolations that reference R&B acts such as Marques Houston , Lalah Hathaway , Peter Collins, Tank , Huey and Ideal. Producers Hollywood Cole, Angel Lopez, Jenius, Kid Culture, Aksel Arvid, Clay Harlow and Rogét Chahayed helped bring Jack’s vision to life. Stream Sweet Action II below.

articles._body: While many analysts have their own bold predictions for the 2026-27 Denver Nuggets , NBA insider Zach Lowe made his about All-Star Jamal Murray’s future. Nuggets’ Murray scored a game-high 35 points in a 118-110 loss to the Portland Blazers on Monday. Denver bounced back with a 128-109 win against the Toronto Raptors on Wednesday to improve to 4-3. While it’s still early in the regular season, if the Nuggets remain a middle-of-the-pack team in the Western Conference standings, they could seek a trade in exchange for Murray, according to Lowe. “I said Jamal Murray just because if this team isn’t good, I think something is gonna crack here. I’m not closing the door,” Lowe said. “I took the under on them at 48 and a half, which was startling- maybe 49 and a half; I don’t remember what it was- but I was the only one who took the under, which startled me cause I just have that much faith in Jokic. If they’re a run-of-the-mill team, I’m not closing the door on anything.” Zach Lowe says Jamal Murray could be a surprise trade candidate if the Nuggets struggle this season “I said Jamal Murray just because if this team isn’t good, I think something is gonna crack here. I’m not closing the door.” pic.twitter.com/CdUHGNHXzn — NBABase (@TheNBABase) November 5, 2026 Nuggets’ Jamal Murray is in the second year of a four-year $207.8 million contract, worth $50.1 million for the 2026-27 season. Denver has surrendered losses to the Oklahoma City Thunder, the Golden State Warriors, and the Blazers two weeks into the regular season. If they stay healthy, the Nuggets have a great chance to finish as one of the better teams in the Western Conference standings. Since winning the 2023 Finals, the Nuggets have failed to reach as far as the Western Conference Finals over the past three seasons, with teams such as the Thunder and the Minnesota Timberwolves, who eliminated them from the 2026 playoffs, standing in their way in recent years. Brian Bell, Scott Shriner and Patrick Wilson share how the tour came together, what life on the road is really like and how fans make songs such as “Say It Ain’t So” and “El Scorcho” special every night. Plus, Karl Koch takes Billboard inside Weezer’s VIP experience, with a look at the band’s instruments and history. Brian Bell: I’ve never once opened the treat, the cheese tray. Brian Bell: Hi, it’s Brian Bell from Weezer. Scott Shriner: It’s Scott. Patrick Wilson: And Patrick from Weezer. Scott Shriner and Patrick Wilson: Come with us on our tour in Billboard All Access. Scott Shriner: We got together and had Zoom calls and looked at pictures. I was just thinking this the other day, ’cause we looked at some other sets and they were, they were so different. It was such a different vibe. And I was like, so glad we didn’t do that, ’cause this turned out to be very fun and open and inclusive. Kind of puts us right in the mix with the audience. Brian Bell: The Gathering Tour was created, the creative of the creation of the being creative was a joint effort between all four members. It started with the title of the tour. That was The Gathering. That was possibly going to be the name of the record when we were in the studio making what is now known as the “Gold Album.” We had to come up with a backstory. Who’s gathering? Why are we gathering? Our in-house director, Brendan Walters, who came up with this idea of this kid, Nicholas, who summons us to play at the gathering by drawing the symbols that we came up with on a piece of paper, and they enchant us with golden eyes, and everybody else who comes to see us, and we decide to play a house party at the house where the band first originated, in the garage of, in the garage, is that garage. articles._body: After going public with their relationship last year, Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd have broken up, but it happened even before they became teammates on the Dallas Wings . On Fudd’s podcast, Fudd Around and Find Out, they announced that they have broken up. However, they called it off “over a year” ago, as Bueckers explained, “We were not together before she got drafted. Bueckers led the Wings in scoring during the 2026 season in her second year in the WNBA (like Fudd, she was selected first overall in the Draft). articles._body: Hi there :) Around a month ago, I released LDraw Nova, an agentic toolset for assembling LEGO CAD models by generating LDraw source code files. For more details, here's the Show HN post: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49937916 From the comments, I got the impression that there was quite an interest in seeing not only AI-generated LEGO models, but also AI-animated LEGO ones. I took a look at results from past experiments, and found it feasible to use agentic LLMs for: - analyzing the LDraw source code for LEGO models - reverse-engineer! the mechanisms present by reading the descriptions and sequence for the parts there - and then, animate them via Blender! This new project I'm presenting, LDraw Mecha, is the end result and proof that can be done: - Read specially annotated LDraw LEGO models .mpd source files - Infer the model structure in terms of submodels - Select from those the ones that are mechanisms - Plan animations - Execute them in Blender In summary, from an initial .mpd source file, get a rigged and animated version for the model as a Blender (.blend) file. See the results here: - Repo (v0.5.0): https://github.com/anteloc/ldraw-mecha/tree/v0.5.0 - Gallery: https://github.com/anteloc/ldraw-mecha/blob/v0.5.0/GALLERY.m... - Process: https://github.com/anteloc/ldraw-mecha/blob/v0.5.0/PROCESS.m... This project is very unusual, I'd really appreciate some feedback from the community. Cheers! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50397325 Points: 22 # Comments: 1

articles._body: As the highly anticipated matchup between the Alabama football team and the LSU Tigers is on Saturday afternoon, the injury status of star wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams has been on every fan’s mind. With Coleman-Williams looking to return for the Alabama football team against LSU , the latest update is consequential. According to college football insiders Pete Nakos and Chris Low of On3 Sports, Coleman-Williams is “currently expected to play” for the Crimson Tide against the Tigers. “NEW: Alabama WR Ryan Coleman-Williams is currently expected to play against LSU on Saturday, [Pete Nakos] and [Chris Low] report,” On3 Sports wrote on X, formerly Twitter. One person who predicted Coleman-Williams was actually LSU head coach and former Alabama football offensive coordinator Lane Kiffin. “LSU coach Lane Kiffin, on his radio show, makes a prediction on Alabama receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams. ‘I would expect him to play.’ Says Alabama has a track record of getting athletes back on the field super fast,” Jon Blau wrote on X, formerly Twitter. So far this season, the junior has caught 23 passes for 415 yards and four touchdowns, as head coach Kalen DeBoer spoke earlier this week about how Coleman-Williams is “working” to get back. “A lot of these guys from Zabien Brown to Ryan Coleman-Williams, EJ [Crowell], Racin [Delgatty], Terrance Green in particular — those guys are all working on the football field,” DeBoer said, via ESPN’s Alex Scarborough. “They’re not all in the exact same spot, but they’re all out there going through workouts. articles.title: From Mötley Crüe & Turnstile to Milo J & Residente, This Is What Vive Latino’s 2027 Lineup Will Look Like
articles.summary: The legendary Mexican festival has announced its lineup for March.
articles._body: The Vive Latino festival will celebrate its 27th edition with the highly anticipated return of Mexican rock band Zurdok and the participation of international acts such as Mötley Crüe, Turnstile, Residente, Milo J, Placebo, Latin Mafia and Los Auténticos Decadentes. These artists will take the stage at the rock celebration on March 13 and 14 at the Estadio GNP Seguros in Mexico City, promoter Ocesa announced on Friday (Nov. 6). The eclectic lineup includes more than 50 Spanish- and English-speaking groups and solo artists, such as Los Tres, Paloma Murphy, La Santa Cecilia, Carla Morrison, Ed Maverick, Kasabian, Bacilos, Attaque 77, Mi Banda El Mexicano, Polymarchs, Andrés Cepeda, Amandititita and veteran Argentine rocker Laureano Brizuela. Also on the list are Adanowsky, Ozomatli, Ximena Sariñana, Skatalites, Cuca, Cultura Profética, Inspector and La Gusana Ciega. Thanks to a partnership with Amazon Music, for the fourth consecutive year, performances from Mexico’s longest running music festival will be streamed on the digital platform in uninterrupted broadcasts. Since its inception in 1998, the Ibero-American Festival of Musical Culture, better known as Vive Latino, has maintained its reputation as an event that challenges expectations. It was the first to include pop, reggaeton, cumbia and Mexican regional music artists in its lineup; it has hosted a four-day edition; incorporated English-language bands to the biggest rock en español celebration; and became the first Latin American festival to have its own edition in Spain. Affectionately called El Vive by its fans, the festival debuted on Nov. 28-29, 1998, at the Foro Sol (now Estadio GNP Seguros) in Mexico City. Since then, it has taken place every year except in 1999, 2002 and 2021, the latter due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Check out the official lineup for the 2027 Vive Latino below. But there are still questions around the offense, which ranks 12th in the SEC in total yards per game. It’s been an up-and-down go for Arch Manning and the Longhorns this year. There has been speculation about what could lie ahead for him, whether it’s in the NFL Draft or another year in college, but ESPN’s Desmond Howard also raised questions about head coach Steve Sarkisian’s future. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Howard rekindled the rumor around Sarkisian and the NFL, alluding to comments he made last year about the subject saying he might not have been “wrong, but may have been a little too early.” He also predicted Manning likely would not be in Austin in 2027, whether that means he goes to the draft or into the transfer portal. “I’m not sure if he’s going to be there a year from now,” Howard said of Manning on The Pat McAfee Show . “I think he may transfer if he’s not, what guys would say, ‘draft-eligible,’ as far as going high up in the draft. If he doesn’t like his draft status, then he’ll probably come back to college football. I would assume that after four years with Sarkisian, they would probably need to part ways. Watch on Fubo (Try for Free) “Now, I’m not sure how that’s going to happen. Is Sark going to take an NFL job? Is he going to stay in Austin and Arch is going to transfer? But I do not see these two together in the 2027 season.” Through eight games heading into Saturday’s game against Missouri, Manning has completed 64.8% of his passes for 1,727 yards and 15 touchdowns, to seven interceptions. It’s been another up-and-down year for Manning, who threw for 3,163 yards and 26 touchdowns, to seven picks, last year. But Desmond Howard also noted the reason why there are so many questions about Manning’s inconsistency this year. It’s his fourth year in Sarkisian’s system, and his second as the starter. Still, Howard said he’s not quite sure why Manning is making some of the mistakes he has. “It’s a big game,” Howard said. “It’s a big game for Sarkisian, it’s a big game for Arch. I think people don’t understand, they’ve kind of forgotten that Arch has been there, this is his fourth year there. “Like, four years in the same program, which we all know that’s unheard of nowadays with NIL and the transfer portal. And we’re still seeing him make these mistakes that, really, he has us scratching our heads, like, ‘Why did he throw that ball? Why did he put the ball there, that interception?’ Stuff like that.”

articles.title: LIV Golf Creditors Face $100M in Claims, Just $2M to Split
articles.summary: Henry Romero-Reuters
articles._body: The prospects for unpaid vendors and contractors in LIV Golf’s Chapter 11 bankruptcy case are not good after the league announced plans to initiate the process of winding down operations . “The outlook for unsecured creditors is likely quite bleak,” bankruptcy attorney John J. Sparacino, a principal at McKool Smith, tells Front Office Sports . There are more than $100 million in claims from LIV’s unsecured creditors, but currently just $2 million set aside for recovery of those claims. “Depending on the size of the claim pool, that money would be allocated to those parties,” LIV’s chief restructuring officer David Orlofsky said during a creditors meeting on Oct. 15. “Obviously, that number may change over time, but that’s kind of what’s on the table at the moment.” LIV’s unsecured creditors committee is hopeful that $2 million turns into much more, sources familiar with the committee’s thinking tell FOS , even if it’s an uphill battle. “It’s safe to say that’s not a number they’re comfortable with,” one source says. Potential sources of recovery for those extra funds could come from more claims against the Saudi PIF (LIV’s former financial backer), third parties, and LIV employees, among others. The creditors committee is represented by New York-based law firm Willkie Farr & Gallagher and New Jersey-based Fox Rothschild. LIV players accounted for 14 of the 30 largest unsecured creditors when the league filed for bankruptcy on Sept. 8. But many other individuals and companies were listed, too, including agencies like IMG Media ($3.2 million) and GSE Worldwide ($1.28 million), golf influencer Rick Shiels ($1.39 million), the state of Louisiana ($1.22 million), and production company Fresh Tape Media ($1.2 million). The goal of the creditors committee is to maximize value for the group as a whole, sources say. The Saudi PIF is LIV’s largest creditor, since the nearly $500 million of funding it gave the league to finish the 2026 season came in the form of a secured loan. That gave the PIF control of LIV’s bankruptcy, and the sovereign wealth fund put up $49.6 million in debtor-in-possession (DIP) financing to fund the bankruptcy process. The PIF could theoretically choose to increase the $2 million “pot plan” for unsecured claims, but most experts agree that’s unlikely. “With where this case is going, it’s hard to imagine that there will be any material recoveries to really anyone,” Joe Bain, co-chair of law firm Jones Walker’s bankruptcy and restructuring team, tells FOS . Sparacino says “there is likely to be virtually nothing to distribute to unsecured creditors” and that he suspects “trade vendors will get little or no recovery.” LIV is set to file its new Chapter 11 wind-down plan on Monday, which could have more details about paying out unsecured claims. The creditors committee is scheduled to meet next on Nov. 20. One outside-the-box option for creditors could be trying to claw back money from the seven LIV executives who received more than $15.6 million in retention bonuses in June and August, since those payments were paid within the 90 days before LIV filed for bankruptcy. Brooklyn Law School professor Jodi Balsam, a former counsel for the NFL, outlined this idea on The Trey Wingo Show . articles.title: SpaceX to Get Under 10% of Revenue From US Government, Musk Says
A WhatsApp channel called Lula’s Army grew from 50,000 to more than 10 million subscribers as Brazil’s president staged a historic comeback
articles.summary: He erased the deficit and won the all-important runoff election by more than 3.5 percentage points – more than 4 million votes.
articles._body: A leader who stood up to U.S. President Donald Trump just won an election in Latin America’s biggest country, reversing a trend of new right-wing governments in the region over the past two years. Incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, having narrowly lost to Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round of voting on Oct. 5, 2026, staged a remarkable comeback on Oct. 25. He erased the deficit and won the all-important runoff election by more than 3.5 percentage points – more than 4 million votes. It was a stunning result for the leader who proved to be the first Brazilian candidate to win a presidential election after not winning the first round, and who had been all but written off for a possible win. As a professor of Latin American politics , I believe the result offers a number of key political lessons for Brazil, Latin America – and even the United States. A contest of worldviews — and social media The choice in the second-round election was stark. Lula offered measures to ameliorate steep income inequalities and an economy built on a transition to clean energy, environmental protection and increased access to higher education and technical training. On international matters, Lula balanced defending Brazilian sovereignty from a Trump administration keen on meddling in Latin America , and maintaining good relations with an array of nations and blocs, including the European Union and China. Bolsonaro, meanwhile, promised sweeping cuts to government spending, more militarized policing and eager support for the Trump administration’s campaign against drug violence . His pitch also came with offers to U.S. investors of access to critical minerals in Brazil. Such right-wing populism has been ascendant in Latin America of late, and Lula also had to overcome an anti-incumbent mood, brought on by high prices, stagnant salaries, steep interest rates and a massive corruption scandal involving Brazilian elites. That banking probe directly ensnared Bolsonaro himself , as well as powerful Supreme Court justice Alexandre de Moraes, whom Bolsonaro’s supporters had tried to link to Lula. Lula also had to neuter a social media landscape that has been dominated by images and narratives disparaging the president and his Workers’ Party. Right-wing dominance of that online ecosystem helped carry Jair Bolsonaro, the 2026 hopeful’s father, to power in 2018 and got him close to reelection in 2022. Especially after the first-round results in the 2026 vote, many analysts assumed the same pro-Bolsonaro social media presence would once again be hegemonic. Instead, after the first round, a network of young, tech-savvy pro-Lula communicators created and shared effective, often amusing videos on WhatsApp and Instagram. And they appealed to the center and even some of the right. All told, Lula easily made up more than 2 million votes by which he lost in the first round. He didn’t just increase turnout by millions and lower abstention rates; he also saw the state with the country’s second-largest electorate, Minas Gerais, flip to his side entirely – a swing of nearly 700,000 votes. Emblematic of the strength of the campaign was the growth in subscribers to the WhatsApp channel Lula’s Army , which grew from 50,000 on Oct. 5 to more than 10 million by the night of the historic election. The creator of the channel, André Janones, is a federal deputy for the Rede Party, an ally of the Workers’ Party, and a rising star in the circle around Lula. Likewise, Ana Elisa Santos Silva, a 21-year-old digital influencer and law student in the Workers’ Party, got the most votes of any federal deputy in the swing state of Minas Gerais. Cracks in the ‘Americanization’ theory of politics A prevalent narrative of Brazilian politics has held that the country’s divisions increasingly mirror those of the United States. Part of that idea is due to Trump’s loss in the 2020 election and the resulting attack on the U.S. Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021, which eerily presaged events following Jair Bolsanaro’s 2022 loss. Like in the U.S., there has also been a rapid rise of a politically active evangelical right in Brazil. More fundamentally, proponents of the Americanization thesis hold that U.S.-style deindustrialization and “Uberization” of the Brazilian economy have led to a decline of the unionized working class – a core support base for the left – and its replacement by an army of gig employees dreaming of owning their own businesses and throwing off the shackles of the taxing and regulating state. Yet similarities between the two countries shouldn’t be confused for politics always moving on parallel tracks. Survey research suggests that many Brazilians see the state as responsible for the realization of their constitutionally protected social rights, including healthcare, education and pensions. Many also regard government employment as inherently more stable and dignified than the harsh labor markets of the private sector, especially for the relatively unskilled. For all of the apparent rise in American-style libertarian politics in Brazil, the reality is that such a viewpoint remains much smaller in the country. Flávio Bolsonaro’s bet, like his father’s before him, was that this strain of libertarian right-wing politics could nonetheless propel him to victory, much as it apparently had for Javier Milei in Argentina in 2023. But it was not enough. One election can’t fix deep polarization Even with Lula’s win, Flávio Bolsonaro’s Liberal Party did exceptionally well at the legislative level. When the next Brazilian Congress convenes on Feb. 1, 2027, the Liberal Party will control 28 seats in the Senate – 35% of the total; and 121 seats in the lower house – 24% of the total (as well as five governorships, which are 19% of the total). When factoring in expected Liberal Party allies, it is clear that the right will have bigger majorities in both houses for Lula’s next administration. That will help Congress solidify control vis-a-vis the executive branch in ter

articles.title: Ferrari’s Luce was ridiculed as a ‘Magic Mouse on wheels.’ Now the EV is sold out for 2027, and buyers haven’t even driven it yet
articles.summary: Even Ferrari’s former chairman warned the EV risked destroying the reputation of the brand.
articles._body: Ferrari’s first electric car sparked ridicule when it was unveiled on May 25. It was called any and everything from a ‘Magic Mouse on wheels’ to a dishwasher or microwave , and even considered a late April Fool’s joke by some fans. Even a former Ferrari president and chairman hoped the company would take off the prancing horse emblem from the Luce, saying Ferrari was “risking the destruction of a myth.” It looks like that ridicule hasn’t stopped buyers: Ferrari’s Luce, with a $560,800 starting price, has a buyer for every car Ferrari plans to build in 2027, and wealthy buyers are lining up for the glass-roofed EV before they even get the chance to test drive it. CEO Benedetto Vigna told analysts on Ferrari’s Q3 earnings call on Tuesday that Luce deliveries for 2027 are all spoken for despite client test drives being planned for early next year. “All the Luces that we plan to sell next year, basically, are all allocated, so if someone comes, he has to wait one year to get the cars,” Vigna said, though he didn’t mention how many units were sold.  Vigna also said Ferrari holding more than 50 local premieres and private viewings across the U.S., Europe, Middle East, and Asia Pacific has helped express Luce’s “uniqueness better than any digital experience.”  The early interest for Luce is a reversal from its rocky debut, when Ferrari shares fell by as much as 8% and analysts wondered whether the car’s unconventional design– larger wheels, more rounded surfaces, and four doors –rattled investors who valued Ferrari for its luxurious visual identity. “While the vehicle promises performance consistent with Ferrari’s standards, investors appeared underwhelmed by its exterior design,” Rella Suskin, an equity analyst at Morningstar, wrote in a note after the release. “Ferrari’s design identity is an important component of its brand equity, supporting scarcity, pricing power, and aspirational desirability.”  But Vigna, who enlisted LoveFrom, the firm founded by former Apple design chief Jony Ive, to build Luce, has defended his breakaway from tradition. He told analysts on the Feb. 10 Q4 2025 earnings call that Luce wouldn’t please everyone, but that it’s still a Ferrari car first and EV second.  “What I can tell you, I can guarantee you is that we will not sell this car to people that do not want the car,” he said. “Because this is a car, Ferrari Luce, that is also electric. It’s not an electric car.” Ferrari is also taking a gamble with Luce as its competitors are reconsidering their EV ambitions because of weaker demand. Lamborghini scrapped its plan to roll out its first fully electric car in 2028, and Porsche—which announced its first electric sports car Taycan seven years before Ferrari –is reportedly planning to end Taycan’s production by 2030. But Ferrari is pressing ahead with Luce—Italian for “light”—which Vigna described as “ illuminating the path ahead ” for the brand.  This innovation also comes as Ferrari’s core business continues to grow. The carmaker reported €1.9 billion in Q3 revenue, up 7% from a year earlier, and €563 million in operating profit, fueled partly by buyers spending more to customize their cars. CFO Antonio Picca Piccon told analysts personalization made up more than 21% of total revenues from cars and spare parts, which he said “exceeded our expectations.” Ferrari did not respond to Fortune ’s request for comment. articles.title: My Chemical Romance’s ‘The Black Parade’ Was a No. 1 Album 20 Years in the Making: Inside the Campaign
articles.summary: “I think a great record is always relevant, one year, five years, 20 years or even 50 years after its original release,” says Warner Records’ Jesse Ervin.
articles._body: When My Chemical Romance released its landmark third album The Black Parade in 2006, it was met with widespread acclaim and hailed as the group’s greatest — and yet, despite it becoming the biggest album of the iconic New Jersey group’s career, it peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard 200, blocked from the top spot by Hannah Montana . Related My Chemical Romance Earns First No. 1 Album on Billboard 200 After ‘The Black Parade’ Reissue Kenny MacPherson, Veteran Music Publisher and Big Deal Music Co-Founder, Dies at 71 Diddy Moved From New Jersey Prison to Similar Facility in Pennsylvania Now, 20 years later, The Black Parade has finally achieved that No. 1 position, following a reissue on the album’s 20th anniversary that propelled the reunited rockers to the best chart peak of their career — and set a record for the longest wait for an album between its release and it hitting No. 1 in the chart’s history. But that milestone didn’t just occur in a vacuum — the reissue came on the heels of an extended tour in celebration of the album that began last year, as well as a five-night run at The Hollywood Bowl last month. It also benefitted from a full-court press by the band’s label, Warner Records, that involved 20 different vinyl variants, digital exclusives, the resurrection of the group’s old fan army and an exclusive release on an iPod Nano, harkening back to the era when the album first came into the world, all of which helped The Black Parade finally reach its rightful place as a chart-topping epic. And that helps Warner Records senior vp of marketing and digital Jesse Ervin earn the title of Billboard ’s Executive of the Week. Here, Ervin talks about the buildup to the new release, why several reissues have made it to the top 10 of the charts this year and what will come next for My Chemical Romance after this huge success. “There’s no doubt we’ll be talking about My Chemical Romance for years to come,” he says. This week, My Chemical Romance’s The Black Parade reached No. 1 on the Billboard 200, 20 years after its initial release — the longest such wait before reaching the top spot in the chart’s history. What key decision did you make to help make that happen? It really is an incredible milestone having the album reach No. 1 after 20 years. This was a true collaboration between the band, the band’s manager Brian Schechter , me, Tom Corson , Aaron Bay-Schuck , Mike Chester and the core team [at Warner Records]. We started with the reissue of Danger Days: The True Lives of the Fabulous Killjoys earlier in the year and planned to time The Black Parade ‘s 20th anniversary release around the actual album’s anniversary on October 23, ensuring it coincided with MCR performing their five historic sold-out shows at the Hollywood Bowl. Having the Bowl shows and the anniversary at the same time allowed us to lay out our marketing campaign well in advance and have tentpoles along the way to get the fans really excited about a full October and beyond of My Chemical Romance. Related How Big a Deal Is My Chemical Romance Scoring Its First No. 1 Album With a 20-Year-Old LP? How did the idea for this reissue come about? The idea centered on the actual 20th anniversary on October 23, which just happened to be a release date — so the stars really aligned. The band and our team wanted to celebrate the album’s anniversary, and this would be the third anniversary edition we had done in the past 18 months while the band has been on the road touring The Black Parade . It is also something the fans really wanted. So we pitched a few concepts, including a 2LP version that had six bonus tracks, including the long-awaited live version of “Someone Out There Loves You,” which we knew the fans would be super excited about. The band also had the idea of creating a new art concept with the very talented James Jean that would act as a slipcase for the original album and original art. The reissue came about with 20 different physical variants, as well as digital exclusives, and was driven by 42,000 vinyl sales. What was the strategy there? The idea was to create unique versions of the album that really spoke to the fans and not just creating colorways for the sake of it. This was really all fan-driven. For the first time, fans got the chance to get an album, CD or cassette signed by the band, a unique hologram version of the album featuring the incredible art and also the very first one-step audiophile vinyl, which offers the highest audio listening experience a fan can get on vinyl for The Black Parade . We also wanted to celebrate every show on the tour, and we created very limited versions of the original album for each tour date, including two for the Hollywood Bowl. Related My Chemical Romance’s ‘The Black Parade’ at 20: Every Track Ranked Those variants included a hologram vinyl, a first for Warner Records, which sold 14,000 copies. How did that idea come together, and how difficult was that to pull off? That idea came from us at Warner Records. Brian and the band are particularly proud of the hologram. We had done picture discs and Zoetropes on previous releases, and we wanted to give the fans something different that hadn’t been done before. We found an amazing vendor who could make them, and once we received the first prototype, I think every single person working on the core team was blown away. Frank Iero from the band posted about it immediately and thought it was the coolest version of the album he had ever seen. The fans shared the same sentiment, and we actually just did a re-press of the hologram so even more fans can enjoy how cool it is. How did you lean into 2006 nostalgia, and the band’s two-decade-plus history in general, to help push the reissue? One thing we did was re-launch the MCRMY, the band’s core fan group. This group was extremely active in the 2000s, and Brian and the band really wanted to reactivate it. The MCRMY

articles.title: What Republicans Can Do Before Democrats Take Control of Congress
A dead French philosopher who lived through World War II and the Cold War offers an eerie warning about the age of AI
articles.summary: In a safety test run by the company Anthropic, its own AI agent blackmailed an engineer to avoid being shut down.
articles._body: With the race to build artificial intelligence systems smarter than any human has come a boom in “accidents.” In a safety test run by the company Anthropic , its own AI agent blackmailed an engineer to avoid being shut down. Criminals have used AI agents for data-extortion campaigns and to hack government agencies , banks and technology companies. In other tests, models have escaped from test environments into real organizational systems . Several researchers who resigned from leading AI companies in 2026 have accused their employers of not taking the dangers seriously enough . In September, Bill Gates told “Meet the Press” that AI is “ powerful enough to drive events that can cause a billion deaths .” Paul Virilio, a French philosopher, spent his career analyzing the relationships between technology, speed and power . He died in 2018 , well before generative AI and the fears about it reached their present pitch. But I doubt much would have surprised him. As a researcher who studies AI-generated media and how people make sense of it, I find that three of Virilio’s ideas explain today’s AI moment better than anything written since. He argued that every new technology brings a new kind of accident into the world ; that speed takes away our time to think ; and that globally connected systems can fail everywhere at once. Technology of speed Virilio was born in Paris in 1932. When World War II began, his family moved to Nantes, a port city near the Atlantic. During the Nazi occupation of France, Germany began building the Atlantic Wall , a series of defensive fortifications stretching along the coast from Spain to Norway. But in September 1943, when he was 11, Virilio saw what the wall could not keep out. American bombers aiming for Nantes’ port hit the city center instead , killing about 1,400 people and destroying more than 700 buildings in two raids. “War was my university,” he told an interviewer . “Everything has proceeded from there.” As a young man, Virilio spent years photographing the abandoned bunkers of the Atlantic Wall. The lesson he drew from them was about speed: The Germans had built a massive military fortification, yet the Allies had gone over and around it; the wall barely slowed them. Walls were a technology of space, and the bombers were a technology of speed – inspiring his philosophical approach to understanding the world. The ship and the shipwreck As an adult, Virilio studied many more examples of technological failures, such as the Chernobyl power plant meltdown of 1986, the worst nuclear accident in history. In his 2005 book “ The Original Accident ,” Virilio summed up his main idea in a simple sentence: “To invent the sailing ship or steamer is to invent the shipwreck.” The train invents derailment; the airplane, the crash; the nuclear plant, the meltdown. Every invention, not just dangerous ones, carries a specific kind of failure that did not exist before it. In Virilio’s telling, the “accident” is not the result of bad luck added afterward. It is born at the moment of invention, even if the inventor cannot see it, because the invention will be used in ways they never imagined. Virilio did not think such accidents could be avoided. But by carefully watching, he believed, people could contain failure and prevent catastrophe. He argued that societies tend to treat each disaster as a one-off, grieve it on television, and forget it, so that the next technology’s accident arrives as a surprise. In 2002, he staged a Paris exhibition as a trial run for his plan to build a “Museum of Accidents.” Collecting information about shipwrecks, plane crashes, industrial disasters and financial crashes side by side, he argued, would show the pattern: that every invention has its failure and that failure can be anticipated . AI has invented not one accident but several . Tech companies’ own incident reports form a sort of “museum” – but not an objective one. Rule of the fastest Virilio’s second key idea came from the Cold War. In 1977, he published “ Speed and Politics ,” written in a world where nuclear missiles could cross the planet in minutes. He named the idea “dromology,” derived from the Greek word for a racecourse: “dromos .” Every age runs at the pace of its fastest machine, Virilio wrote, and whatever cannot keep up – including law, deliberation and conscience – drops out of the picture. There is “no democracy, only dromocracy”: the rule of the fastest. AI can squeeze months of work into hours. In September 2026, Open AI announced that 10,000 of its AI agents had produced a proof of a math problem that had stood for a century – a problem two human mathematicians had spent a year trying to solve . Virilio’s deepest fear about speed was not that people would fall behind machines, but that they would be absent from decision-making. Even when people attempt to stay in the loop, AI agents execute so quickly that human workers often fail to spot problems or malicious requests . Everywhere at once Virilio’s third idea is the “integral accident”: a failure that, because the same technology runs everywhere, happens everywhere at once . During the 1990s, Virilio watched how satellite television, the internet and electronic markets let an event anywhere, such as a financial crash, be felt everywhere. He later predicted that in a networked world, integral accidents, not war, would be “ the continuation of politics by other means .” AI has intensified how tightly connected the world is. It’s being used to help balance power grids , manage ships and harbors , and write hospital patient records . Consider Anthropic’s Claude Mythos model, which finds security flaws in banking software faster than banks can fix them. Many financial institutions use the same software, so a criminal with such a model could break into multiple banks at the same time. Hand on the lever Virilio wrote that a society that lives only in the present makes accidents more likely . A society too busy to keep records

articles.title: Hermès Makes Birkin Bags. It Also Makes Stage Plays
articles.summary: French luxury label Hermès sells more than expensive, exclusive bags. It also manages a cultural program that includes art, illustration, and theater.
articles._body: A curious stage play has taken over Hong Kong’s West Kowloon Cultural District. Its set is decorated with silk scarves, orange boxes, and luxury handbags, and its central character, an equestrian squire, wanders through the historic Rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré boutique of a little brand known as Hermès. You read that right. One of the world’s oldest luxury houses has gone theatrical, translating the brand’s long history into Hermèstories — a surrealist odyssey written by Pauline Bayle and directed by Joe Hufton that runs through November 8. It’s all very in line with Hermès’ crafty reputation, down to the sound effects, which are made live on stage with materials used by the house. We’re in a peak era of fashion brands using art to build their fantasies, but it usually stops at slick ads (see: the very Akira spot for Our Legacy, or Dior’s hand-drawn holiday film). Animation is just one tool in the toolbox. Only Hermès, craft-focused king, seems savvy enough to use all of them — art and illustration and stage plays, too. This isn’t the first time the luxury brand has dipped into the theatrical, though — it isn’t even the first time this play has been put on stage. Hermèstories was first seen at Milan’s Teatro Franco Parenti in 2025, and Fondation d’entreprise Hermès has commissioned performance works through its New Setting program for years. Still, with its Hong Kong edition, the luxury brand has offered a whimsical reminder of what sets Hermès apart in the industry. While other brands are content to hire illustrators for ads or throw their money behind major art institutions, the French luxury house does a bit of everything — casting its creative net wide. Take animation, the artistic flex of the moment for fashion brands. Scroll through the Instagram pages of many a major fashion label right now, and you’d be forgiven for thinking you’d stumbled onto Disney’s. Handmade visuals have never been hotter, as we noted at the start of the year . Illustration has been infiltrating advertising and seasonal campaign teasers at everything from Chanel to Prada — the latter of which literally used former Disney animators to bring its Holiday 2026 campaign ads to life. It makes sense as a brand strategy: when we’re this deep in the sludgy trenches of AI slop, hiring an illustrator to zhush up your ads is low-hanging fruit. It fits that a house this old would have perfected its formula by now, but it’s still impressive to see Hermès flex its artistic output. Its social feed regularly features animations by a rotating cast of international artists. Seoul-based illustrator Oyow's kaleidoscopic visuals sit next to a film from Argentinian artist Juan R. Lage , whose trio of cartoon characters strolls into a Hermès store, looking like something out of an Adventure Time offshoot. Over 50 artists were commissioned by the brand last year for social content, and for many other labels that’d be enough. But zoom out and a constellation of other creative endeavors are in orbit: the Hermès website recently added a series of paper illustrations drawn by Sarah Martinon and animated by Armand Béraud, and it's tapped major artists to contribute patterns and prints for decades. Add a touring stage play to the mix, and you start to see just why nobody is doing it like fashion’s elder giant. Plenty of brands put serious money behind art, be it through physical institutions like the Fondation Cartier or Fondazione Prada or through funding schemes like Louis Vuitton’s recent sponsorship of the Frick Collection in New York. This kind of patronage ensures the fashion house’s name is tied to exhibitions. Hermès, though, is doing something far quieter: folding art into the very fabric of its brand identity, tying craft to how it sells its products and tells its story. articles.title: Browns’ Carson Schwesinger addresses Jared Verse’s frustration after getting body-slammed
articles.summary: There has been lingering attention about Cleveland Browns star Jared Verse getting flipped in a game. And Mason McCormick tried to defend his actions. Furthermore, Carson Schwesinger addressed Verse’s frustration after getting body-slammed by McCormick, according to a post on X by Camryn Justice.
articles._body: There has been lingering attention about Cleveland Browns star Jared Verse getting flipped in a game. And Mason McCormick tried to defend his actions. Furthermore, Carson Schwesinger addressed Verse’s frustration after getting body-slammed by McCormick, according to a post on X by Camryn Justice. “#Browns LB Carson Schwesinger on Jared Verse’s comments about being upset that no one came to his defense on the body-slam play: ‘Well, I mean, a lot of times there’s a lot of stuff that goes on in the field that you don’t see. I mean, you asked me about it after the game, and I still hadn’t seen it at that point. ‘So obviously it’s something if you see it, you go to his defense. And something that you don’t want to see in the game of football at all. And so yeah, like I said, if that’s something that I had seen, definitely would’ve been going to his defense.’ ” That seems like a very reasonable explanation from Schwesinger. We will see if Verse accepts the olive branch. Browns edge rusher Jared Verse wanted more support Verse said he expected more from his teammates, according to ESPN. “The lack of reaction by those around me upset me a lot,” Verse said. “A similar play happened to Derek Barnett on, I think, the next field goal, and I lost it because it was my brothers and my teammates. And when you do something like that to him, it upsets me very deeply. “That’s a conversation that we’ve had and spoken about. I’ve made my issues known about the situation, but also I didn’t put them in a position to let them know beforehand I was going to talk the way I talked to the Steelers and Steelers Nation or whatever they are. I got to be better than that. I didn’t do enough on my part. We all got to pick it up.” Verse was the player sent from the Rams to the Browns in the Myles Garrett blockbuster trade. It’s interesting to note that Verse has the same number of sacks this season as Garrett. The problem for Verse? He’s played in eight games and hasn’t recorded a sack. Garrett played in one game. articles.title: FAA to finally ditch floppy disks in what it calls "historic" tech upgrade
articles.summary: FAA information display systems to be floppy-free at 435 sites by end of 2028.
articles._body: While you might be pondering whether to replace a smartphone with one that has a slightly better camera or a second screen, the Federal Aviation Administration is planning a much bigger leap in technology for the country's air traffic control system. The FAA said yesterday that it will stop using floppy disks as part of a long-awaited upgrade that will give air traffic controllers faster access to data needed for crucial safety alerts. The new Enterprise Information Display System (E-IDS) will be installed in 435 facilities, replacing several information display systems dating to the 1980s. The FAA "is continuing its historic modernization of America’s air traffic control system by replacing outdated floppy disks that contain vital weather and other critical information with a streamlined, 21st-century system," the agency said. E-IDS will be "deployed to operational control positions at more than 400 facilities across all air traffic control domains," and "provide operationally essential information for controlling aircraft," the FAA said . The Colts also have little reason to rush into a deal. If they are going to move on from Taylor, they need to make sure the return justifies giving up one of their most valuable offensive players. A first-round pick should be the starting point in negotiations, and Indianapolis could be holding out for even more than that. The trade speculation has been building for weeks, and the recent decisions to move Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner have only intensified the attention surrounding Taylor. With two major pieces already moved, teams are naturally wondering whether the Colts are prepared to continue reshaping their roster. Taylor is now one of the biggest names to watch as the deadline approaches. His talent makes him an attractive target for any contender looking to upgrade its backfield, but the Colts are in a position to demand a premium return. If Indianapolis is willing to part ways with its star running back, it should take a substantial offer to make that happen. Here is the Commanders’ Week 9 injury report versus the Rams, with QB Jayden Daniels working with a makeshift wide receiver room. With a record of 2-4-1, the Commanders are techn
articles._body: The Washington Commanders have a big problem with injuries . And the dreaded Brandon Aiyuk question has surfaced again . Here is the Commanders’ Week 9 injury report versus the Rams, with QB Jayden Daniels working with a makeshift wide receiver room. With a record of 2-4-1, the Commanders are technically still alive in the NFC East title chase. However, that seems very unlikely to stay realistic. And it’s especially thin if the Commanders lose to the Rams. Given their WR room, it’s hard to imagine an upset is on the horizon. Maybe the Commanders can lean on the West Coast teams’ struggle with 1 p.m. kickoffs on the East Coast. And the Rams have already proven they don’t know how to travel after Sean McVay’s laughable Australia travel itinerary that likely led to an embarrassing blowout loss to the 49ers. Commanders injury woes hit front and center It starts with Treylon Burks not being able to practice yet this week. But that alone tells you where the Commanders are with their receivers. Imagine if someone told you in the preseason that the Commanders would have major concerns about Burks being out of the lineup. You’d have known instantly the team was in dire straits. Also, Dyami Brown has been limited. Again, this is not something that would have crossed the radar with Terry McLaurin on the field. But McLaurin is gone for the season. So Jayden Daniels will have Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams as reasonable receiver targets. After that it’s Van Jefferson and, gasp, Luke McCaffrey. Let’s pause for a moment. The Commanders spent most of the offseason and preseason with McCaffrey listed as WR2 on the depth chart. This shows this clear inability of GM Adam Peters to build a roster. McCaffrey isn’t even a good WR4. That’s what he will be Sunday against the Rams. Peters deserves a grade of F for the way he constructed this offense. He gets a better mark for the defense. But he has killed his team’s playoff chances in a year where it may only take nine wins to capture the NFC East title. What does Jayden Daniels have to work with against Rams? First, Daniels is committed to doing the best he can to save this sinking ship , according to a post on X by Brandon. “Jayden Daniels postgame after the win vs the Eagles: ‘I’ma give it my all for this city, for this team, make sure I do whatever I can to help this team win. You know, get back to the winning ways but it starts here. We can’t get content, we got a big tough matchup next week vs the Rams so we gotta get prepared’ ” And there’s good news. Williams is emerging as a true NFL WR2. Chemistry is building between Daniels and Williams, according to commanderswire.com via Yahoo. “I think every week, it’s getting better,” Williams said. “But that comes with time. Every time the ball comes my way, I want to make sure I’m in the right spot. Trust is earned. I’m just trying to earn that.” And their connection includes Daniels finding Williams when he scrambles. “You light up,” Williams said. “The ball finds energy. So, just working to get open. A lot of big plays happen on scrambles. And when you got a quarterback like him … that scramble drill is really important to just get open and [have] energy so the ball [finds] you.” WIll Jayden Daniels be able to lift the Commanders? However, Daniels will miss Burks if he can’t make a go of it, according to commanderswire.com. “One, he’s super fast, but just his confidence,” Daniels said. “You can see his confidence continue to grow. I know, just having conversations with him early on in his career, it was rough for him. And obviously it’s, where he was drafted, when he was drafted is, he has the ability to, but coming here is like a fresh start. You can just see his confidence continue to grow from OTAs until up to this point. “His stride length. He eats up ground so quickly. (And)He has a long stride and he’s, like I said, he’s frequently athletic. It’s like, he puts a lot of stress on the DB. So that kind of works on his advantage. And you gotta get the ball up and down for him or get the ball up early because he can probably outrun the football.” The post Commanders Week 9 injury report vs. Rams: Jayden Daniels working with makeshift WR room due to injuries appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.summary: After Draymond Green and the Golden State Warriors’ 120-100 win against the Miami Heat, the veteran big man mediated a tense moment between Bobby Portis and his teammate, Georges Niang. In Green’s veteran role as the Warriors’ starting center this season, he says Niang makes thi
articles._body: After Draymond Green and the Golden State Warriors’ 120-100 win against the Miami Heat , the veteran big man mediated a tense moment between Bobby Portis and his teammate, Georges Niang. In Green’s veteran role as the Warriors’ starting center this season, he says Niang makes things easier for him on both ends of the floor, and he didn’t mind the chippiness. Green discussed Niang’s role in his first season with the Warriors during his postgame media availability, per ESPN’s Anthony Slater. “I love that type of energy, by the way. Did you see me walk up to Bobby Portis and put my shoulder on his chest, or did I do like this? It was a de-escalation, right? So it looked a little different. Alright, well at least we got an understanding there,” Green said. “Georges has been incredible for us. The way he shoots the basketball. Crazy thing is: he hasn’t even shot it at the level that he shoots the ball at. “Yet, the impact that he’s had on this team on every aspect of the game; he’s so smart. And he’s fiery. He’s been great for us. What an addition. That’s one of those signings that people look at, like aww man, then, you look up, and you can’t keep him off the floor.” Warriors veteran Draymond Green appreciates Georges Niang’s approach in his first season with Golden State. “He’s been absolutely incredible for us. I love being his teammate,” Green added. “I’ll be honest, at times, I do some random s*** out there, especially on the defensive end. But even on the offensive end, I do some random s*** at times, and he just picks up on it. He’ll fill the spot. He’ll plug. I’m looking to do some wild s*** and he’ll cut. He just knows what to do. So, really fun player to play with.” Draymond Green raves about Georges Niang: “What an addition.” “Can’t keep him off the floor.” He likes the attitude Niang has injected. Green has already broken up two Niang arguments with opponents (Collin Sexton and Bobby Portis). pic.twitter.com/gdRWDAsc0F — Anthony Slater (@anthonyVslater) November 6, 2026 When a reporter asked Georges Niang what was said between him and Bobby Portis, he gave an interesting response , per 95.7 The Game. “He actually said that his outfit looked better than mine. And then I was like, ‘Well, no mine looks better than yours.’ And we went back and forth,” Niang said. “I mean, do you really want to know what we said to each other?” "He actually said that his outfit looked better than mine. And then I was like, ‘Well, no mine looks better than yours.’ And we went back and forth. I mean, do you really want to know what we said to each other?" Georges Niang on him and Bobby Portis chirpin’ tonight pic.twitter.com/hEjm2iegUu — 95.7 The Game (@957thegame) November 6, 2026 Niang is averaging 7.9 points and 3.1 rebounds this season. The Warriors are on a six-game winning streak. articles.title: Nebraska voters block measures to legalize online sports betting, rejecting a campaign’s promise of $166 million in property tax relief
articles.summary: Nebraska voters narrowly rejected to legalize mobile sports betting in the state.
articles._body: Nebraska voters rejected two ballot measures that would have legalized online sports betting across the state, dealing a setback to gambling companies that spent $22.5 million campaigning for the expansion and promising voters a new source of property tax relief. According to the Nebraska Secretary of State, voters rejected Measure 440, which would legalize online sports betting, by approximately 55% to 45%, while Measure 441, which would regulate the business if passed, lost by approximately 54% to 46%. Both measures needed to pass for mobile sports betting to become legal in Nebraska. The defeat came as scrutiny grew across the sports betting industry, which has expanded rapidly across the U.S. since the Supreme Court opened the door to state-level legalization in 2018. The initiatives The two initiatives were designed to work together, but they addressed different parts of the legalization process. Initiative 440 was a proposed constitutional amendment. It would have amended the state’s constitution to authorize legislation allowing people to place sports wagers through internet-based platforms operated by authorized gaming operators connected to licensed racetrack casinos. Initiative 441 was the accompanying statutory initiative. It would have established the legal framework for online sports wagering and authorized the Nebraska Racing and Gaming Commission to regulate operators and adopt rules governing the industry. Under the proposals, sports betting companies could have offered mobile betting platforms in partnership with Nebraska’s licensed racetrack casinos. The platforms would also have been required to operate gaming servers within the state. DraftKings and FanDuel each gave $10.4 million to the campaign. The property tax relief promise And property tax relief was one of the central selling points of the campaign. Supporters of the measures wrote in the Nebraska secretary of state’s informational pamphlet that Nebraska was missing out on millions of dollars in tax revenue by allowing residents to place mobile wagers in neighboring states instead. The initiatives would have directed 70% of the state’s tax proceeds from sports betting into the Nebraska Property Tax Credit Cash Fund, following the same allocation used for revenue from existing casino gambling. But the amount of relief projected by supporters is relatively modest compared with the state’s property tax burden. A report commissioned by Tax Relief Nebraska—the committee that backed the measures— estimated that legalizing online sports betting could generate nearly $87 million in additional state tax revenue over five years, and $166 million in direct property tax relief over the next 10. But that would represent a small fraction of the state’s approximately $25 billion property tax burden over the next five years, according to Nebraska Family Alliance—a nonprofit policy research organization. State senator Brad von Gillern, who opposed the expansion, argued the additional revenue wouldn’t meaningfully change property tax bills. “If people are voting for the online gambling initiative believing that it’s going to substantially change their property tax bill, they’re going to be sadly disappointed,” von Gillern said, according to the Nebraska Examiner . No bets on the phone for Nebraska And for Nebraska voters, the central question was whether the potential tax revenue from online sports betting justified making gambling more accessible—especially as research found that sports betting is an overall losing game for bettors. A 2024 working paper from the National Bureau of Economic Research found that legalization led to increased sports betting participation and frequency, but also significantly reduced household savings. The effects were particularly pronounced among financially constrained households—where researchers observed increases in credit card debt, reductions in available credit and more frequent overdrafts. And a September Bank of America Institute study found that one in five Americans view sports betting as an investment—with the number doubling to four in five for Gen Z respondents. The study also found that customers recover less than 75 cents for every dollar they send to betting platforms—and even Gen Z, the best-performing generation, falls short of breaking even. Taking it physical But Nebraska already permits in-person sports wagering at its five licensed racetrack casinos, following voters’ approval of casino gambling in 2020—the caveat being that mobile betting remains prohibited, meaning residents had to be at the physical casino or cross state lines to place legal wagers through an app. And cross state lines Nebraska residents did. According to cybersecurity and geolocation compliance software company GeoComply, there were approximately 3.4 million attempts to access regulated sportsbook applications from Nebraska during the 2024-25 NFL regular season—which involved nearly 76,000 accounts. The company also recorded more than 326,000 geolocation checks at a single cornfield just across the border in Iowa. “Thousands of bettors from Omaha cross the border into Iowa to place wagers this NFL season, driven by Iowa’s legal sports betting framework,” a GeoComply press release read. “This phenomenon has earned the nickname ‘The Busiest Cornfield in Iowa’ due to the sheer volume of geolocation checks observed in this rural area just over the state line.” A version of this story was published on Fortune.com on November 3, 2026. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Klay Thompson reveals why Heat will ‘turn it around’ amid ugly 3-6 start
articles.summary: With the Miami Heat (3-6) losing to the Golden State Warriors on Thursday night, 120-100, it marked another step back for the team that came into the season with high expectations. After Heat star Klay Thompson hit the game-winner the previous night against the Los Angeles Clippers, he would spea
articles._body: With the Miami Heat (3-6) losing to the Golden State Warriors on Thursday night , 120-100, it marked another step back for the team that came into the season with high expectations. After Heat star Klay Thompson hit the game-winner the previous night against the Los Angeles Clippers, he would speak after facing his former team about how he still has the utmost confidence in the team turning it around. In the loss to Golden State, Thompson would record 11 points on three of 10 shooting from the field, two of seven from three-point range, to go along with three assists and two blocks. While the new-look Miami team, led by Giannis Antetokounmpo, continues to figure out how to play with one another, Thompson says that the Heat will “absolutely turn it around,” having gone through these types of starts before. “I’ve been through moments like this before, where you start the season 3-7 or under .500 in your first 15 games, and you can absolutely turn it around, and I know we will. It’s just about staying together,” Thompson said. Klay Thompson says the Miami Heat will turn it around this season: “I’ve been through moments like this before where you start the season 3-7…you can absolutely turn it around and I know we will. It’s just about staying together.” pic.twitter.com/LCcht3hEA5 — The HEAT Realm (@WadexFlash) November 6, 2026 It was another pedestrian and surprising low defensive effort from Miami, as they are of the belief that the offense will follow once the defense gets better. “If we don’t commit to that side, we’re gonna keep scoring 100 points,” Adebayo said after recording 18 points and 10 rebounds. The Heat “didn’t have a lot of juice” against the Warriors The Heat shot 41 percent from the field and 30 percent from beyond the arc, while the Warriors, led by Stephen Curry’s 29 points, shot 53 percent from the field and 39 percent from deep. While the team started fast on a 14-4 run, Golden State made it a tie game at halftime, leading to Miami being unable to get anything consistently going on either side of the ball. Head coach Erik Spoelstra said that the team “didn’t have a lot of juice” on the second night of a back-to-back, though he emphasized that he’s not making excuses. Coach Spo on the 2nd half collapse tonight: "We didn't have a lot of juice" pic.twitter.com/nJLQt6RAmj — Heat Central (@TheHeatCentral) November 6, 2026 Antetokounmpo would finish with 20 points, 14 rebounds, and four assists, as he and the rest of the Heat look to start the turnaround on Sunday against the Sacramento Kings. The post Klay Thompson reveals why Heat will ‘turn it around’ amid ugly 3-6 start appeared first on ClutchPoints .
