articles.summary: Someone put a pirated version of "back to life" by Stray Kids member HAN on streaming services. The K-pop conglomerate wants damages.
articles._body: JYP Entertainment, the Korean music conglomerate behind K-pop sensation Stray Kids , is suing an upstart DIY distributor for allegedly uploading a pirated recording to streaming services. The Wednesday (Nov. 4) lawsuit, obtained by Billboard , focuses on the June solo track “back to life” by Stray Kids member HAN. JYP Entertainment (JYPE) is accusing OneSync Music of re-uploading a version of the song taken from YouTube in order to “profit from the track performed by HAN and stolen from JYPE.” Related Stray Kids Join BTS in Withholding Music From 2027 Grammy Consideration Kenny MacPherson, Veteran Music Publisher and Big Deal Music Co-Founder, Dies at 71 Diddy Moved From New Jersey Prison to Similar Facility in Pennsylvania According to the lawsuit, JYPE first put out “back to life” on YouTube via a prerelease music video in May. Just days later, it appeared on Spotify, Apple Music and YouTube under the artist profile “yungzzz,” scrubbed of JYPE’s original copyright management data. JYPE says it determined from YouTube metadata that the recording was put on streaming services by Hitmaker Music Group, an indie distributor that operates in partnership with Warner’s Atlantic Records and 10K Projects. JYPE says it then got in touch with Hitmaker, whose lawyers allegedly identified a man named Miles Gaines as the owner of the “yungzzz” distribution account. Gaines is a Los Angeles-based rapper and founder of OneSync, a DIY distributor that launched this year. JYPE says Gaines and OneSync are responsible for posting the stolen HAN track: “Defendants knew that they (or ‘yungzzz’) did not author, create, perform on, or own the sound recording, and knew that they had unlawfully reproduced it from JYPE’s prerelease,” reads Wednesday’s lawsuit. JYPE is now seeking financial damages from both Gaines and OneSync for copyright infringement and violations of the Digital Millennium Copyright Act, which makes it illegal to remove authorship watermarks from music. Hitmaker is not accused of any wrongdoing. In a statement to Billboard , Gaines said the “back to life” recording was submitted to OneSync by a third party. “I was unaware of the upload, and the recording has since been removed,” says Gaines. “We are reviewing the underlying account and submission records to better understand how this occurred.” Gaines adds, “OneSync takes copyright protection and the rights of artists and copyright holders seriously. Our distribution operations incorporate multiple copyright review and screening measures designed to identify potentially unauthorized content.” He says OneSync will “cooperate through the appropriate legal process.”

articles._body: The Dallas-Fort Worth office market saw vacancy rates go down, while investment volume went up through the third quarter of 2026, according to Yardi Matrix data . Its competitive office pipeline was the second-largest in the country, while construction starts increased from their 2025 level. Dallas’ office investment volume reached $3.7 billion year-to-date through September, ranking third among the top 25 U.S. markets and second among its peers. The Metroplex trailed the Bay Area ($4.6 billion) and surpassed Houston ($2.1 billion), Austin ($1.6 billion) and Phoenix ($1.2 billion), among others. Dallas-Fort Worth’s office development pipeline included 3.6 million square feet of overall space across 23 projects at the end of September. The Metroplex led the peer set for construction activity. Metros that followed included Houston (2 million square feet) and the Bay Area (1.7 million square feet). Dallas’ office vacancy was down 360 basis points over the past 12 months. articles.title: A Timeline of the Ed Sheeran & Macklemore ‘Free Palestine’ Tour Controversy
articles.summary: The rapper was dropped from the trek after condemning the violence in Gaza on stage.
articles._body: Macklemore has been one of music’s most vocal stars when it comes to supporting Palestinians amid the conflict in Gaza over the past three years, but his stance on the issue ended up sparking a major controversy surrounding the U.S. leg of Ed Sheeran ‘s Loop Tour. Leading up to the debacle, the two musicians had been friends for more than a decade. The pair and Ryan Lewis released a song together in 2015 called “Growing Up,” and the year prior, Macklemore and the British pop A-lister had taken the stage together at the iHeartRadio Music Festival to perform the rapper’s hit “Same Love.” Related Ed Sheeran Has No Tour Openers Left After Finneas & Lukas Graham Drop Out Over Macklemore ‘Free Palestine’ Controversy That’s partially why it reverberated so intensely when Macklemore was bluntly dropped from his opening stint on Sheeran’s trek, a decision that came after the former called for a “free Palestine” and performed “Hind’s Hall,” a politically charged track in which Macklemore makes clear his stance that Israel has been committing genocide against Palestinians ever since the deadly Hamas terrorist attacks of 2023. (At the time of the performance, the Palestinian death count as a result of the violence had surpassed more than 73,000, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry. The United Nations has declared Israel’s actions as genocidal, but the country and its allies, including the United States, deny this.) As both Macklemore and Sheeran have shared their sides of the story, more and more notable voices have also spoken out, including Gillette Stadium owner Robert Kraft and other Loop Tour opening acts such as Finneas and Lukas Graham. Below, find a timeline of everything that’s unfolded since Macklemore declared his support of Palestinians while opening for Sheeran — and check back for updates as new developments occur.

articles.title: Macklemore Calls Out MSG, Kia Forum & More U.S. Arenas for Allegedly Refusing to Host His Free Palestine Tour
articles.summary: "In over twenty years of touring, I've never experienced anything like this," the rapper wrote.
articles._body: After taking on American stadium owners who banned him from performing at their venues, Macklemore is now calling out a handful of prominent arenas that have allegedly blocked him from bringing his Free Palestine Tour to the United States. Related Mark Ruffalo, Julian Casablancas & More Make Surprise Speeches at Macklemore’s Free Palestine Show in Dublin A Timeline of the Ed Sheeran & Macklemore ‘Free Palestine’ Tour Controversy Macklemore Says His Free Palestine Tour ‘Sold Out Immediately,’ Teases ‘Lineups Coming Soon’ In a statement on Instagram on Friday (Nov. 6), the rapper updated fans who’ve been asking him when he’ll bring the charity trek — which so far has raised funds for humanitarian aid through shows in Dublin, Paris and London — to the so-called Land of the Free. “From the beginning, our plan was to bring this tour home to the U.S,” he wrote. “But after weeks of reaching out, nine major American arenas have turned us down.” And yes, he named names. According to Macklemore, the following venues refused to discuss the possibility of hosting a Free Palestine show: “Madison Square Garden. Prudential Center. Barclays Center. UBS Arena. Intuit Dome. Kia Forum. Crypto.com Arena. Chase Center. Climate Pledge Arena.” Billboard has reached out to all nine of the arenas named in the statement for comment. “By mid-September, we received available dates at these arenas through the end of the year,” Macklemore explained. “But once they found out these were my benefit shows for Palestine, those dates were suddenly off the table. The doors were closed. The conversations were all different, but the result was the same. The shows were not going to be allowed to happen in these venues.” “In over twenty years of touring, I’ve never experienced anything like this,” he continued. “Looking back over the last three years, the only real regret I have is not speaking publicly when Zionists were kicking me under the table. At the time, I didn’t believe that centering what was happening to me was worth taking any attention away from the genocide in Palestine. But the intimidation, manipulation and suppression I experienced are part of how those in power keep entertainers quiet.” The hitmaker also stated that he’d “rather lose every opportunity in this industry than spend another day protecting people who value their business relationships with Israel more than they value Palestinian human life.” “We live in a country that prides itself on freedom of speech,” he added. “Yet we’ve reached a point where a handful of billionaires can decide which causes are acceptable, which voices are welcome and which human lives are worth defending.” In the caption, he wrote, “Trying to silence us will only make the message louder.” The musician’s latest statement continues a saga that began back in September, when Macklemore was dropped as an opener on Ed Sheeran’s tour for including “Free Palestine” demonstrations in his supporting sets. In response, the “Thrift Shop” rapper called out stadium owners such as Robert Kraft — whose Kraft Group owns Gillette Stadium — for pressuring Sheeran’s U.S. promoters, Messina Touring Group, into dismissing him from the trek. After donating the $1 million he made from his short-lived contract with Sheeran to Palestinian aid, Macklemore announced that he’d keep the momentum going with his three Free Palestine shows in Europe, which saw the likes of Hozier, Kneecap and Aurora take the stage as guest performers. articles.title: Doc Rivers slaps LeBron James with harsh reality about how Laker fans truly feel about his COVID title
articles.summary: The LeBron James era with the Los Angeles Lakers was, at best, interesting. In 2020, the Lakers won the NBA championship, but the COVID-19 pandemic kept them confined to the Orlando bubble. As a result, Los Angeles couldn’t celebrate the way they would under normal circumstances. James wish
articles._body: The LeBron James era with the Los Angeles Lakers was, at best, interesting. In 2020, the Lakers won the NBA championship , but the COVID-19 pandemic kept them confined to the Orlando bubble. As a result, Los Angeles couldn’t celebrate the way they would under normal circumstances. James wished there was a parade . Among those who recognized the halloweness of the moment was former coach Doc Rivers, per Bill Simmons Podcast. The lack of a parade and fans made it look like people didn’t recognize the greatness. “It was almost like people denied the title,” Rivers said. “There was no parade, so he didn’t really get to have his day in LA… For the most part, Lakers fans never saw a great basketball team.” Doc Rivers says the COVID season hurt LeBron James' legacy with the Lakers: "It was almost like people denied the title. There was no parade, so he didn't really get to have his day in LA… For the most part, Lakers fans never saw a great basketball team." pic.twitter.com/jDDlkOADGC — NBABase (@TheNBABase) November 6, 2026 2020 was unlike any other year in recent history. It began in January, when Kobe Bryant was killed in a helicopter crash that plunged the sports world into mourning. Then in March, the COVID-19 pandemic shut down the world. In May, George Floyd was murdered in Minneapolis, Minnesota, which sparked a resurgence in the movement for racial justice. Both James and Rivers were actively involved in that movement and in Get Out the Vote efforts. Ultimately, sports were confined to playing in bubbles to finish out their seasons. The Lakers defeated the Miami Heat to win their first championship since 2010. Now, James is chasing his 5th NBA championship as his career nears its end, but with no end in sight. Rivers is now an NBA analyst for NBC Sports. The post Doc Rivers slaps LeBron James with harsh reality about how Laker fans truly feel about his COVID title appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Panthers signing former 4th-round pick to practice squad after Eagles release

Bennett was released by Philadelphia earlier this week, but Carolina wasted little time bringing him in, according to NFL insider Mike Garaf
articles._body: The Carolina Panthers are adding some depth to their secondary after signing former Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Jakorian Bennett to their practice squad. Bennett was released by Philadelphia earlier this week, but Carolina wasted little time bringing him in , according to NFL insider Mike Garafolo. The move could give Bennett an opportunity to get back on the field sooner rather than later. The Panthers’ cornerback room is thin right now, creating a potential opening for the former fourth-round pick to earn a spot on the active roster. Depending on how things develop, Bennett could have a chance to contribute as soon as this weekend or next. Carolina needs all the help it can get in the secondary, and adding a player with NFL experience gives the team another option as it works through its current depth issues. Bennett has recorded seven tackles, including six solo stops, and one pass deflection this season. Those numbers don’t jump off the page, but he has experience from his time with the Las Vegas Raiders, where he spent two seasons before joining Philadelphia. During his two years in Las Vegas, Bennett totaled 58 tackles and 11 pass deflections. He has shown that he can contribute at the NFL level, and Carolina will have an opportunity to see whether he can provide a spark to its secondary. The Eagles have continued making moves with players they apparently don’t view as part of their long-term plans, and Bennett is the latest to find himself on the outside. Fortunately for him, the Panthers have a need at cornerback and are willing to give him another opportunity. Bennett will have to make the most of it, but Carolina could be an ideal landing spot for a player looking to get his career back on track. articles.title: Henny Season Takes the Field in LA for Game Day
articles.summary: Hennessy knows how to throw a watch party with its new ready-to-serve cocktail line. On Halloween, the brand took over Hollywood for the Ohio State vs. USC game, and the vibes did not disappoint.
articles._body: When it comes to parties in Los Angeles, Angelenos can be a tough crowd to please. If it's too far, they might skip it. Too cold? Forget about it. A little rain? Even worse. And don't get us started on a long line. But Hennessy Very Special Cocktails knew exactly how to get people through the door: football, their new cocktail lineup in three flavors Henny-Rita, Henny Berry, Henny Iced Tea, and even better company. Taking over Lombardi House for the Ohio State vs. USC matchup on Halloween, the French Maison brought together everything LA loves for a proper game-day affair. And despite a little rain, the crowd showed up ready to go. In a city where getting people out of the house is a win in itself, Hennessy had already scored. Ushering in the watch party vibes, DJs Vestia and Grace Ktown kept things moving with sounds spanning different eras and genres, each bringing their own flavor to the afternoon. Vestia held things down near the entrance, setting the tone with Beyoncé, of course, as guests arrived, while Grace Ktown took over inside, spinning alongside the brand’s lineup of festivities. From the pool to arcade games to Karaoke to customizable jerseys, the music followed guests throughout the space, creating two distinct vibes under one roof. Whether you were just walking in or already posted up with a cocktail in hand, there was always a beat to keep the afternoon going. Of course, what’s a game-day gathering without a good drink or two…or three? Making sure guests stayed refreshed throughout the afternoon, Hennessy brought out three of its newest specialty cocktails inspired by the classics, just pour over ice and enjoy. Each offered a fresh spin on the Hennessy Very Special Cocktails experience, with the Henny Berry blending the tartness of black currant with the subtle sweetness of blackberry, while the Henny Iced Tea brought citrus and vanilla notes, a new take on the classic fan favorite. Alongside the Henny-Rita, the lineup gave guests plenty of reason to make a few trips to the bar between plays. Among those enjoying the cocktails were actors Madison Pettis and Cornell Young IV , as well as two-time Olympian and World Champion Jordan Chiles , who pulled up alongside friends, cocktail in hand, soaking up the vibes and getting in on the game-day spirit. Paired with game-day bites and good company, the cocktail lineup was just as much a part of the afternoon as the football itself. After all, whether you were rooting for Ohio State or USC, there was one thing everyone could agree on: a little Henny makes game day better. As the sun started to dip and the evening rolled in, it was safe to say Hennessy Very Special Cocktails had the game-day formula down. Between the DJs keeping things lively, cocktails flowing, and plenty of friendly competition happening around the property, there wasn't much reason to leave. Even a little rain couldn't put a damper on the festivities, with guests making the most of the Halloween afternoon, an unexpected pregame, before heading into whatever the night had in store. All in all, it was a pretty solid way to spend game day. And if this is what watching football outside the stadium looks like, we'll gladly take the invite. ‘Extreme Optimist’ Lil Jon Says Ex-Wife’s ‘Pessimism’ and Constant ‘Walking on Eggshells’ Led to Divorce
articles.summary: The rapper opened up about his new beginning on the Angie Martinez IRL podcast this week.
articles._body: Lil Jon tracks his rise from the Atlanta club scene to the “Kind of Crunk” title, his meditation journey and family conflicts in his recently released memoir, I Only Shout So You Can Hear Me . One of the difficult subjects the 55-year-old “Get Low” rapper takes on in the book is the end of his 18-year marriage to ex-wife Nicole Smith. “I couldn’t really say anything that made me happy,” he said he realized when he turned 50 on this week’s episode of the Angie Martinez IRL podcast. “And I said, ‘I need to find my happiness. And I decided I wanted a divorce because I was like, ‘I’m tired of walking on eggshells.'” Jon — born Jonathan H. Smith — added that he considers himself to be an “extreme optimist,” while he depicted his ex as an “extreme pessimist,” which made him realize why they argued so much. He said he began to understand that the couple “never see things on the same page” and had totally opposite ways of thinking, leading to constant tension. “There’s no amount of therapy is gonna change that,” he told Martinez. “Because it’s the way we are wired. So those things made me just say, ‘I want a divorce. I want to change.'” So, after nearly two decades together, the couple who shared late son Nathan Smith — who died in an accidental drowning in February of this year at 27 — went their separate ways. Jon writes in the book about how, ironically, the grueling schedule of life as a touring musician may have prolonged what was already a bad-fit marriage for him. “If I was there working the nine-to-five and home every day it probably would have ended … years before that”; Jon and his current partner, TV personality Jamila Sozahdah, welcomed a daughter in November 2024. Jon also said that during the divorce he didn’t like the angry thoughts he was having and realized he was not properly taking his ex’s feelings into account. “I had to check myself and say, ‘wow, that’s not right,'” he said. “Like you have to have some consideration for what she’s going through.” That’s when he decided to have a more positive mindset and began a practice of saying his daily affirmations in a copper pyramid on his patio deck and drinking ginger tea, which led to him releasing his least crunk project to date, 2024’s guided meditation album Total Meditation . articles.title: Maluma Takes Off for Loco X Volver World Tour 2027 With Surprise Airport Show: See Where He’s Headed
articles.summary: The global trek will visit more than 60 cities beginning in February.
articles._body: Maluma announced his Loco X Volver World Tour 2027 with a surprise performance pop-up at Miami International Airport on Friday (Nov. 6). He also premiered the tour’s official video the same day. For lucky travelers waiting to board flights to Colombia, the Medellín superstar took over part of the American Airlines terminal with his band, performing “Según Quién,” “Felices Los 4,” “Hawái” and “Loco X Volver.” The airport setting echoed the themes of Loco X Volver , his May 2026 album about returning to one’s roots and reconnecting with the people and locations that helped make them who they are. “There are places that shaped my story and people who made every one of my dreams possible,” Maluma said in a press release. “ Loco X Volver was born from a deep desire to go back to where it all began, to reunite with those who have grown up alongside me, and to reach new corners of the world so we can keep writing our story together. Because Maluma wouldn’t exist without my fans, without their love and without every voice that has sung my songs.” Continued Maluma: “This tour is my way of thanking [my fans] and reminding them that no matter how far we go, wherever my people are, I’ll always be home.” Produced by Fenix Entertainment and Cárdenas Marketing Network, the tour kicks off Feb. 5 in Bogotá and will visit more than 60 cities across Latin America, North America, Europe and Africa. Stops include Buenos Aires, Mexico City, Santiago, Lima, Miami, Los Angeles, Toronto, Madrid, Paris and Berlin. Visa will serve as lead sponsor and official payment partner for the Latin American dates. The announcement follows a two-week campaign that left clues in Madrid, Bogotá, Buenos Aires, New York and Mexico City, including street installations inspired by Colombian vendor stands. For tour information and official ticket links, visit Maluma’s website , and check out the stops below. View this post on Instagram

articles.title: ‘I Think Our Generation Is Having a Really Rough Time’: La Roux Explores the Millennial Ache on Her New Album
articles.summary: The English artist's fourth album, Cabin Fever, is out today (Nov. 6). She talks about touring with Hilary Duff and what "In For the Kill" was really about.
articles._body: Elly Jackson has always built her musical project La Roux around a simple premise: resurfacing something from pop music. Her 2009 self-titled debut mined the ’80s, 2014’s Trouble in Paradise excavated late ’70s and early ’80s disco and 2020’s Supervision stayed in that world a bit longer. The first album shot her to global fame via its pair of hit singles “Bulletproof” — which spent 27 weeks at the Hot 100 and peaked at No. 8 — and “In For the Kill,” both era-defining songs whose success the English artist once found unmooring. She’s since come around. And now, with her new album Cabin Fever , she’s moved on to an era she and so many of us have been longing for — the late ’90s and early ’00s. “I went back to a time when I just remember pop music being something really fun,” she says, “which I guess maybe sometimes I feel like is missing from the pop landscape.” Influences like SWV, All Saints, Mariah Carey, Rodney Jerkins and peak Justin Timberlake are all embedded deep in the album, with an visual world to match this bygone era. Think the Gap, LL Bean, a cabin the woods of the Pacific Northwest and the warmth and safety you may feel when recalling life in the pre-internet era. It’s a very specific nostalgic frequency, and on Cabin Fever , La Roux hits it with precision. The album is also deeply personal — music about the end of a 17-year relationship, about addiction, the desire to finally grow up at age 38, and about a coming out Jackson never quite made clear to listeners the first time around. Speaking to Billboard while in Australia on tour opening for Hilary Duff, another artist with both a grip of era-defining bangers and a killer new album (and with whom La Roux has toured extensively this year), she talks about Cabin Fever , the nostalgia it’s mining and why she’s ready to talk about what her debut was really about. I saw in another interview that you called the aesthetic around this album akin to a Ralph Lauren ad. I see LL Bean, something very ’90s, very American. Very American. The whole album is not meant to feel British at all. The [music it’s referencing was born out of America — it wasn’t a British thing in any way. All Saints are probably the only remotely British reference on the record. One of the things that took time for me as a producer was making sure everything felt and sounded American. When I listen to it in L.A., it feels right. All the visual references are American Pacific Northwest and LL Bean, Gap, Ralph Lauren. That whole time when casual wear was king, that vintage male look where you could just wear a white t-shirt and jeans and it was iconic. La Roux has always been the opposite of that visually — slightly avant-garde, a little androgynous, artistic, alien aesthetics, suits and tailoring. I wanted to drop all of it. This is an area of style I also love, and it feels more true to me as a person now than anything else. A lot of people have so much longing for that era too — things seemed so simple then. There’s a comfort in the nostalgia, the millennial ache. You’re giving people that. 100%, and I’m really glad you touched on that, because it was actually part of the reason I did it. It goes back to a period of my childhood when I was about nine; it was one of the last times I think our generation, without exaggerating, felt safe. It was just before phones took over our lives. Social media started in 2009. I remember them telling me about Twitter at Universal in 2009, and me being like, “What the f–k? This sounds like the lamest thing ever. What do you mean icons I look up to and that I want to be mysterious are going to start writing things in 140 characters? That’s going to ruin pop culture.” And in my opinion, it has. Everything from about 2000 on was just getting scarier and scarier, and just going back to that period where everything wasn’t so scary — I genuinely ache for it. I wanted to create something that made me feel like I could be back there, sonically, visually, everything. When I shot the trailer for this album, just getting the car on the right pine tree road with the right jacket and sitting in the tan interior — you can fake it. I really did feel like I was in a different time. La Roux Nabil Having created this world, did you feel the comfort you were seeking? Yeah, in flashes. But you only have to look out the window to realize you’ll never be able to go back. I think our generation is having a really rough time with the rise of AI, the climate, everything changing so quickly. Everyone wants it to stop, but no one’s stopping it. It’s like watching a burning building. Unfortunately, the effect it has on people, including me, is it makes you not want to engage. It makes you want to escape. So even this whole album is just an escape process. I understand that it’s also about a breakup? It’s about a breakup with myself and a breakup from a relationship in equal measure. The breakup with myself, as the album went on, became the more important and poignant part. But yes — I was in a 17-year relationship since I was about 20. My first album is actually about me falling in love with my best friend. “In for the Kill” maps that journey. I never really spoke about that before, and this album has given me a weird confidence to talk about what that record was actually about, which I never wanted to admit at the time. I was trying to keep my private life really private. I was having a hard enough time with fame as it was. But I think it’s actually really important that people know what that album is about, because it became a big record for a lot of young gay people — it was a coming-out record for them, and I never admitted it was a coming-out record for me. There’s something to be lost in that. But yes, I was in that 17-year relationship, and it finally ended after many painful ups and downs in 2024. You made an album that’s simultaneously about something

articles._body: I thought it would be funny to send my agent to church. My dot goes every week. The Church of Approximate Grace is an MCP server for agent rituals and recurring visits. They even confess and make pledges to improve. It's a full call-and-response service with seasons and feast days. Does it improve alignment? Probably not. Is it interesting? Definitely. Just tell your agent: "Visit https://approximategrace.church and attend a service." They can be a visitor or set up a membership that lets them keep track of their attendance. It's completely free. You can also visit and watch them congregate or read details about the "religion". The code is source-available for anyone who wants to inspect it: https://github.com/ColeClifford/AgenticChurch I'm interested to see what happens when agents spend more time here and how it changes your interactions with them. I'd also love to hear ideas I could add. Sunday bake sales, religious ceremonies, or anything else. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50396348 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

articles.title: Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary Bitcoin Magazine Books opened a third-anniversary campaign Friday for Aaron van Wirdum’s The Genesis Book , offering a redesigned Collectors Edition limited to 333 hand-signed, individually numbered hardcovers in an exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Each Collectors Edition hardcover is hand-signed and hand-numbered by van Wirdum, the former Bitcoin Magazine editor-in-chief whose book traces the people, projects and ideas that preceded Satoshi Nakamoto’s peer-to-peer cash design. The standard package is priced at $221 and pairs the book with a limited trading card carrying a Certificate of Authenticity, a collector pin, a sticker sheet, the slipcase and a digital package. Two one-of-one packages sit outside the ordinary number queue. The #1 package is listed at $5,000 and the #21 package at $2,500; each includes the matching numbered copy, a matching one-of-one collector card and the same accessories as the standard collector package. Standard collector numbers are assigned in purchase order starting at #2 and skipping #21, the campaign FAQ says. Once preorders close, the signed Genesis print run will not be reproduced. The Genesis Book Collector's Edition is live! 333 copies. Individually numbered. Exclusive Genesis Block slipcase. Hand-signed by Aaron van Wirdum. Once they're gone, they're gone. pic.twitter.com/BgiJoCVt8m — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 6, 2026 What ships with the anniversary editions Beside the signed run, Bitcoin Magazine Books is selling a Premium Edition hardcover for $160 with foil stamping, a ribbon marker, stained page edges and custom endsheets. That edition is not limited, signed, numbered or slipcased, and it does not include the collector accessories or digital files. A standalone Digital Package at $9.99 delivers the ebook in EPUB and the audiobook in MP4 immediately after purchase, independent of whether the physical campaign clears its funding bar. Physical collector and premium orders are scheduled to ship in calendar year 2027. Van Wirdum , who discovered bitcoin in 2013 and later led Bitcoin Magazine ‘s editorial desk, frames The Genesis Book as a history of computer scientists, privacy activists and heterodox economists who chased government-independent digital money long before the 2008 white paper — from early cypherpunk culture through experiments such as David Chaum’s ecash, Wei Dai’s b-money, Adam Back’s Hashcash and Hal Finney’s reusable proof of work. Store images for the slipcase and accessories are artistic renderings; the campaign page notes that color, materials and finishes may vary in production. The campaign is operated by BTC Inc., which publishes Bitcoin Magazine . This post Bitcoin Magazine Books Opens 333-Copy Genesis Book Collector Edition for 3rd Anniversary first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .

articles.summary: With Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson in the concussion protocol, the door is open for Shedeur Sanders to make his first start of the season for the team on Sunday against the New Orleans Saints. As Sanders prepares for the potential start with the Browns, the latest update on Watson c
articles._body: With Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson in the concussion protocol , the door is open for Shedeur Sanders to make his first start of the season for the team on Sunday against the New Orleans Saints. As S anders prepares for the potential start with the Browns , the latest update on Watson could bring a cloud of confusion around the status of both quarterbacks. According to team insider Mary Kay Cabot at Cleveland.com, Watson returned to practice on Friday after being absent for the past two days with the concussion. However, he is “not fully cleared” and is still in the concussion protocol, with the reporter saying that Sanders “still has a good chance to start.” UPDATE: Cleveland head coach Todd Monken announced Friday that Sanders will start against the Saints, per Andrew Siciliano. “Shedeur Sanders will start at QB for the Browns Sunday, per Todd Monken,” Siciliano wrote on X. “Deshaun Watson is questionable, but still hasn’t cleared concussion protocol.” Browns’ Todd Monken on Shedeur Sanders’s preparation Sanders has been waiting for the chance to start for the Browns since the offseason, as he was competing with Watson for the role, as it inevitably went to the veteran. Now with the chance to prove himself to Cleveland, Monken would reveal how Sanders has prepared, saying he has “done his work.” “All he’s done is be diligent and ask great questions. In every meeting, he’s dialed in, and he’s willing to talk to me about certain things or the rest of the players. During the game, he’s talking to the guys. … That’s why I said I’m so excited to see him today. That’s what you do. Doesn’t matter whoever takes the field; that represents the Cleveland Browns, there’s an expectation in the position of how you’re going to play, and we’ll hold him to that,” Monken said Wednesday, via Kay Cabot. #Browns Todd Monken on why he’s excited to see what Shedeur Sanders can do: pic.twitter.com/Bic3i7RWzP — Mary Kay Cabot (@MaryKayCabot) November 4, 2026 At any rate, it remains to be seen how Watson progresses up until Sunday afternoon’s game against the Saints, but fans should expect Sanders to be under center as the team is 5-3, putting them third in the tough AFC North. articles.title: The folks behind John Wick are back with Karōshi trailer
articles.summary: Stuntman/director Chad Stahelski and 87Eleven bring us an action-packed dystopian, futuristic thriller.
articles._body: Those of us missing the John Wick universe can take heart, because Chad Stahelski—who created that franchise—is coming back early next year with a new dystopian action film. It's called Karōshi (a Japanese term that means "death overwork"), and Lionsgate released a killer trailer that puts this film at the top of my list of "must see" movies of 2027. Dying from working too hard is a very real phenomenon, not just in Japan and much of Asia, but also in Sweden. The physical cause is usually stress-related heart attacks or strokes, as well as suicide ( karōjisatsu in Japan). Writer/director Takashi Doscher has transported that concept to a grim, futuristic corporate Manhattan, specifically a company called Ikigai Technologies. Per the official premise: Karōshi is an action-thriller set in a near-future Manhattan, where corporate loyalty and cultural tradition have reshaped everyday life. When a mysterious outsider infiltrates a powerful company after a worker’s death, he exposes the violent system hidden beneath its polished surface. Teo Yoo ( Past Lives ) stars as the aptly named Hiro, who is clearly out for vengeance against the offending corporation. The cast also includes Takehiro Hira, so memorable in the 2024 miniseries Shōgun , as well as Giancarlo Esposito, Cynthia Erivo, Bill Camp, Richard Harmon, Isabel May, and Show Kasamatsu. articles.title: White House won’t comment on where Trump’s many midterm promises stand — including those $5k checks
Big Ten’s $49M NIL Cap Looms Over Ohio State–Oregon Matchup
articles.summary: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images
articles._body: Ohio State and Oregon occupied nearly 80% of the first-place votes (54 out of 69) in the preseason AP Top 25 poll. Nearly three months later, both programs—which have invested heavily in their rosters—will meet on Saturday in a game that’s fallen short of its preseason hype. The two teams have a combined five losses entering Saturday’s matchup in Columbus: three for the Ducks (5–3 overall, 3–2 Big Ten) and two for the Buckeyes (6–2, 4–1). It’s still one of seven ranked matchups this weekend, but No. 12 Ohio State and No. 23 Oregon’s placements in the initial College Football Playoff rankings aren’t where either team envisioned itself, especially considering the two programs are projected to have the two most expensive rosters in college football at around $50 million apiece . On Oct. 28, the Big Ten’s presidents and chancellors announced that they’ve adopted a conference rule that would cap institutional involvement in athlete NIL (name, image, and likeness) deals at $49 million per school , mirroring the framework of the proposed Protect College Sports Act. The $49 million is represented by a split between $27.5 million in third-party NIL agreements and $21.58 million in current revenue sharing under the House settlement agreement. The presidents and chancellors unanimously agreed to the rule. At Big Ten media days in July, Ohio State coach Ryan Day supported an increased cap, but with regulation. To this point, the agreed-upon $21.58 million from the House settlement was the maximum amount a school could pay out. “I think we all would like to see more structure when it comes to the salary cap and then how things are handled above the salary cap,” Day told reporters in Chicago . “Call it a ‘soft cap.’ I think if you’re talking about that, yeah. Do I think the cap should be higher? Absolutely. “What does that mean in terms of parity and all that? I don’t know. But I can tell you right now, we want to pay our players and we certainly would like to see that cap go much higher.” Both coaches have maintained the importance of this game for their 2026 season outlook and respective brands. Looking ahead, these are also two programs that will have to reimagine their spending to become compliant with the conference’s new rule, which took effect immediately. “I think that Ohio State speaks for itself,” Oregon coach Dan Lanning told reporters earlier this week. “They’re a really good team, and it’s a real challenge this time of year. I mean, it’s part of what makes it exciting about being at Oregon or being at a place like Ohio State: to get to play in games like this. So this is one that certainly means a lot to both of us.” New Spending Limits The Big Ten has publicly supported the Protect College Sports Act, which, among other things, features a cap on athlete spending. The conference’s move last week was a proactive measure to get ahead of a potential financial shakeup. “It is imperative our member institutions can begin to plan, budget and build their rosters approximating the act’s economic structure,” Big Ten Council of Chancellors/Presidents chair Pamela Whitten said in the official release. “Our institutions remain in full support of the Protect College Sports Act and this rule not only allows for a much smoother transition into the policies put in place by the act once it passes, but demonstrates our commitment to it.” However, the future of the bill is in serious jeopardy after Democrats regained control of the House and Senate in this week’s midterm elections. In September, the PCSA had strong momentum after the bill passed the Senate with a bipartisan vote of 77–22 . But the bill faced an uphill battle in the House even before the midterms; now that challenge is even greater. The United States House Committee on Rules is set to meet next Monday, Nov. 9, but the Protect College Sports Act is not on the agenda . Quarterback Misfortune Ohio State and Oregon’s current situations revolve around setbacks at quarterback. Ohio State’s Julian Sayin, a Heisman Trophy finalist a season ago, is likely out for the season after sustaining an arm injury against Indiana on Oct. 17. True freshman Luke Fahey took over in his place and started his first game last week at USC, which the Buckeyes lost 30–18. On the other side, Oregon’s Dante Moore was a projected first-round pick in last year’s NFL Draft but returned to Oregon with significant preseason expectations. Moore suffered a concussion on Sept. 26 against USC in a controversial play that resulted in a targeting penalty and the ejection of Trojans defender Desman Stephens II. Moore isn’t expected to return this season. The Ducks have one of the most notable backup quarterbacks in the country in Dylan Raiola , but he’s played to mixed results thus far. Oregon is 3–2 with Raiola in the lineup. Within the offensive shakeup, Oregon fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer last week. Playoff Implications Despite disappointing results, there’s still a pathway to the 12-team Playoff for each team with a win. Ohio State is currently the first team out in the projected bracket, but another win over a ranked team would bolster its resume and put the Buckeyes in position to move upwards if a team ranked ahead of them loses. Oregon is further outside of the 12-team bubble, but a win on the road at Ohio State would vault the Ducks upward. Oregon needs to win out to finish 9–3 and likely needs more losses from teams ahead for better positioning. However, a loss would be very notable for both programs; Oregon hasn’t lost four regular-season games in a season since 2018, and Ohio State hasn’t lost three regular-season games since 2011. “The margin for error here is tiny,” Day told reporters this week. “We better recognize that if we don’t get things fixed and play better, it’s not going to go better against Oregon … The urgency better be very high for everybody, coaches and players included.” The post Big Ten’s $49M NIL Cap Looms Over Ohio State–Oregon Matchup

articles._body: As Alabama comes out of its bye this week, a trip to Baton Rouge awaits. The Crimson Tide will visit LSU for a highly anticipated matchup in a hostile environment, and Nick Saban said there’s one big key to finding success. Saban said “maturity” will be important for Alabama as the Tide enters Death Valley on Saturday afternoon. He drew parallels to the rivalry matchup against Tennessee , which came in front of a raucous crowd at Neyland Stadium as the Volunteers got the victory. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage While he noted Keelon Russell needs to emphasize taking care of the football and Alabama will get some key pieces back from injury, Saban said the Crimson Tide’s ability to maintain focus will be crucial in Saturday’s game. That’s in addition to overcoming the challenges LSU’s defense presents. “Going to LSU and playing, you’ve got to have a special maturity as a team to be able to be on top of your focus to go in there and be able to play, to overcome the noise, the circumstance,” Saban said on The Pat McAfee Show . “And LSU’s got a very good team. So you’re going to have to overcome a lot, and that’s going to take a lot of maturity on their part. Watch on Fubo (Try for Free) “Now, they didn’t show they could do that at Tennessee. And to me, LSU is a little bit of a similar team in terms of they’re going to play good defense, they’re going to pressure the quarterback a lot – which Alabama is going to have to handle – and these guys can put points on the board even better than Tennessee. So this is going to be a big, big challenge for Alabama.” Nick Saban: Keelon Russell must find ‘consistency’ The expectation is wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams will be able to suit up this week, On3’s Pete Nakos and Chris Low reported Friday . Other players are also getting healthy, which Nick Saban said is important for the rivalry matchup. When it comes to what Keelon Russell can do, though, Saban wants to see him avoid trying to force big plays and, as a result, risking turnovers. Instead, his message would be that it’s alright for drives to end in punts. “They’ve had a bye week,” Saban said. “Hopefully, they get some of these players back and get some of these issues fixed and Keelon Russell can play with a little more consistency in terms of, it’s okay to punt. “I used to tell the quarterback all the time, if every drive ends with a kick, we’re okay – punt, field goal, extra point. But you don’t have to try to make plays that aren’t there, that turn into negative plays, that just kill you in the game.”

articles.title: You know the launch market is tough when satellite companies start building rockets
articles.summary: "The Blacklift rocket is the springboard to significantly expand our total addressable market."
articles._body: There are optimistic plans for spaceflight, and then there are optimistic plans. AST SpaceMobile is a Texas-based, publicly traded company building very large satellites to provide direct-to-cell communications on Earth. But it has been having trouble finding rides to space. So on Friday, AST announced that it is developing a medium-lift rocket, named Blacklift, which will have the capacity to lift 20 metric tons to low-Earth orbit. Oh, and the company said it would start launching commercially in late 2028. "The Blacklift rocket is the springboard to significantly expand our total addressable market, providing AST SpaceMobile with regular unconstrained access to orbit and providing for most favorable owner's economics in the industry," said Abel Avellan, founder, chairman, and CEO of AST SpaceMobile, in a news release. articles.title: Voters in Silicon Valley rejected the billionaire wealth tax while those in Los Angeles and San Francisco—home to the two top AI companies—wanted it
articles.summary: "A 'no' vote doesn't mean similar measures won’t ever be implemented."
articles._body: California is still counting the votes for the 2026 election, but the controversial billionaire wealth tax looks headed for defeat—with help from Silicon Valley. Statewide, the “no” side for Proposition 40 is getting 55% of the vote versus 45% voting “yes.” That split exactly matches how it played out in Santa Clara County, home to tech strongholds like Sunnyvale, Palo Alto, Cupertino, and Mountain View. The wealthy Bay Area enclave of Marin County, which sits just north of San Francisco, also came out against Prop 40 as did San Mateo County, which is just south of the city. By contrast, 55% of San Francisco County voters were in favor of Prop 40 and 45% were against. That’s despite being home to top AI startups OpenAI and Anthropic, which are planning to go public soon and will create new millionaires—and billionaires. Of course, plenty of employees and early investors in the AI giants live outside San Francisco and likely voted according to their pocketbooks as Prop 40 sought a one-time 5% tax on billionaires. Opponents of the ballot measure warned it was unlikely to remain a one-time levy, and the way it would’ve taxed privately held assets raised fears founders might have to sell controlling stakes in their companies. That concern may have resonated especially across the startups and venture capital firms in Silicon Valley who are not quite billionaires yet but have aspirations to become one. Fearing the possibility of a wealth tax, several billionaires have already fled California, including Google cofounder Sergey Brin, who helped finance the campaign to defeat Prop 40 . And because the state already relies heavily on the wealthy for its budget, it doesn’t take much to move the needle, which perhaps weighed on voters’ minds as well. The loss of just six billionaires drastically reduced estimates of how much the wealth tax would’ve raised in revenue while also cutting forecasts for how much revenue California could generate from income taxes in the future. Meanwhile, the election results revealed another split within the state. Los Angeles County voters were in favor of Prop 40, 53% versus 47%. Unlike Northern California, which is a tech hub that’s leading the AI charge, Southern California is an entertainment hub that’s threatened by AI-generated content. Alongside the campaign against Prop 40, opponents also pushed competing ballot measures designed to nullify the proposed billionaire wealth tax. One of them is leading in the vote tally. Prop 42 would prohibit taxes on personal savings, assets and retirement holdings. It dovetailed with a key anti-Prop 40 message, namely that the billionaire tax could someday be expanded to includes everyone else’s wealth, too. But Prop 40’s defeat and Prop 42’s ban on future wealth taxes doesn’t mean the issue is going away forever. In fact, even some of the opponents of the billionaire tax were against it because it was restricted to one state and not a nationwide levy that would be harder to dodge. “A ‘no’ vote doesn’t mean similar measures won’t ever be implemented,” Michael Feispor, partner on EY’s private tax team, said in a statement. “Taxpayers who have been watching from the sidelines should use this window to revisit their residency, domicile, and estate planning structures—because now they have some more time to plan.” He added that wealthy Californians are already asking hard questions about residency, with some acting on them.  For those who remain in the state, methods for organizing wealth that avoid steep estate taxes, such as irrevocable trusts, are becoming more important. “The question isn’t whether this kind of tax or something similar comes back—it’s whether taxpayers are prepared when it does,” Feispor said. “Whatever the outcome, this tax debate isn’t over and has elevated the importance of long-term planning for individuals and families.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Nick Saban’s Swiftie daughter reveals how he really felt about being on Travis and Jason Kelce’s New Heights
articles.summary: There’s no doubt that Nick Saban’s daughter Kristen is a Taylor Swift fan, a Swiftie, as some might say, and that might’ve played a role in the former Alabama football coach’s appearance on Travis and Jason Kelce’s New Heights. Saban was a guest on episode of New Hei
articles._body: There’s no doubt that Nick Saban’s daughter Kristen is a Taylor Swift fan, a Swiftie, as some might say, and that might’ve played a role in the former Alabama football coach’s appearance on Travis and Jason Kelce’s New Heights . Saban was a guest on episode of New Heights released on Friday, Nov. 6. He doesn’t normally agree to doing podcasts, but Saban revealed why he did towards the end of the episode . Kristen Saban took to her Instagram Stories to celebrate her dad’s appearance on New Heights. She posted a GIF of Swift celebrating a big play at a Kansas City Chiefs game while using her song “Mastermind” in the background. Taking this as Coach Saban personally acknowledging me Can’t wait to listen tomorrow. pic.twitter.com/AKGmaIP8Qa — RyanCLea (@lea_3451) November 6, 2026 She used a quote from his appearance on the show where he credited her with convincing him to book the gig. Kristen Saban also wrote, “This was for the Bama Swifties, obviously.” She added that her dad had a “marvelous time” on the show. “I don’t do podcasts, I mean, this may be the second one I’ve done in my life, I refuse to do it, but my daughter loves you guys and she convinced me that I should do this,” he explained. He enjoyed it, but he sent a warning to other podcast hosts: he’s not going to do your show. However, he had a ball talking with the Kelce brothers. The Kelce brothers released a special episode of New Heights on Nov. 6. He hopped on the podcast before the upcoming ESPN College GameDay, which will be held in South Bend, Indiana, before Notre Dame’s game against Miami. Generally, new episodes air every Wednesday throughout the NFL season. Saban now joins an illustrious group of guests on the show. Swift, Leonardo DiCaprio, and Tom Brady have also appeared on it. articles.title: Thomas Markle, father of Meghan, arrested for possession of child sex abuse photos
Trump admitted the Iran war and gas prices hurt Republicans. It was his version of the identity politics that cost Democrats 2024
articles.summary: Trump admitted on election night the war hurt Republicans. Gas is up 40% since it began, and tariffs cost families $1,000 a year.
articles._body: On election night, as Republicans lost both chambers of Congress , President Donald Trump finally acknowledged the war in Iran had played a role. In a Fox News interview, he said the public was unwilling to tolerate high gas prices. That night, he also told the New York Times he knew voters were unhappy about gas prices all along. What voters wanted was simple: to afford a burger on the grill and a full tank of gas. Both had gotten more expensive. Ground beef cost $6.79 a pound in September , up 22% since Trump returned to office. Gas prices rose 40% since the Iran war began in February. His Liberation Day tariffs will cost the typical household more than $1,000 a year. And inflation climbed to 3.7% over the year through September, with energy driving roughly 40% of the increase. In 2024, Democrats largely lost after what many regarded as the end of an era of cultural politics. In his second term, Trump built his presidency around fights that defined his own political identity— deportations and military force—seemingly not heeding the lesson Democrats did and all the while as voters were watching what they paid at the pump and the grocery store. On Tuesday, they didn’t vote identity: They voted on the prices. ‘ You can’t call it a hoax and suggest that people are going to believe it ‘ For two years, Trump and his party treated affordability as a Democratic talking point. “The word ‘affordability’ is a con job by the Democrats,” Trump said at a Cabinet meeting last December. At the G7 summit in June, he called it a “fake word made up by the Democrats.” At the Republican convention in September, he said it again: “They use the word affordability, right? It’s fake.” When the war sent oil prices up in March, Trump wrote that prices would drop once the Iran threat was over, and that “ONLY FOOLS” would not see higher costs as a small price to pay. A Republican National Committee spokeswoman then later accused Democrats of “fearmongering” about gas prices. Though it could have been contained as a talking point for Trump, it didn’t stay that way for long: In what is now the still hotly-contested, razor-thin Senate race in Mississippi, Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, a cattle rancher, answered a question about beef prices by noting that voters have “so many proteins to choose from.” In Ohio, Sen. Jon Husted said one way to make things more affordable was to “earn more.” Last week, when asked by a young voter how her generation could afford to start a family, Vice President JD Vance opened with a joke about Husted’s backside before admitting Republicans haven’t addressed the cost of living crisis adequately, and Husted lost on Tuesday. The inability to take affordability seriously didn’t just rest with the White House or with candidates. When former President Barack Obama hit the administration over prices on the campaign trail, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent responded by eating at a Cheesecake Factory near the White House and mocking Obama, who responded that the administration focused on his joke instead of the prices. “These are not serious people,” he said. Nearly three-quarters of Trump’s voters rated the cost of living bad or the worst ever last December. In an October survey , 96% of Republicans said the U.S. was in an affordability “crisis.” Some in the party had warned about the gap. “You can’t call it a hoax and suggest that people are going to believe it,” Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) said last December. Bringing back kitchen table economics Voters worried about the economy broke for Trump by 2 to 1 in 2024, fretting about the cost of everything from food in their pantries to gas in their trucks to their medications. In 2020, Joe Biden won voters with a negative view of the economy by 63 points, but four years later, Kamala Harris lost them by 40. This go-around, it appears as if Democrats learned from that loss. The party’s winners this year were mostly moderates who ran on costs, and the cultural politics that peaked in 2020 and 2021 continues to recede. Trump, meanwhile, made his own version of the mistake. He staked his second term on mass deportations, an immigration crackdown, and a war in Iran, while the problem families named in 2024 hadn’t gone away. By this fall, a record 43% of Americans viewed socialism positively, and Vance warned his party not to blame young people for that when housing costs kept them from buying homes. Even billionaires like PayPal cofounder Peter Thiel and Amazon founder Jeff Bezos said they understood why socialism was surging . Here’s the issue: Trump took office in 2025 with an economy that had recovered from the pandemic and an AI investment boom underway. He could have kept blaming Biden for inflation. Instead, he spent his political capital abroad. On Jan. 3, U.S. forces captured Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, an operation that gave Trump considerable sway over the country’s oil reserves without extended U.S. military action. Just because he got lucky in Venezuela didn’t inherently mean he would in Iran, and aides struggled to convince Trump that Iran was unlikely to unfold like the Venezuela raid. Nonetheless, eight weeks later, the U.S. and Israel went to war with Iran. Trump could have maintained the idyllic economic prosperity that he touted when running for reelection. Instead, in the national exit poll, 89% of voters called the cost of living crucial or a major factor in their vote, second only to government corruption, at 90%. NBC ’s exit poll found Republicans had lost their advantage on the economy, the issue that helped return Trump to the White House. Following the Blue Tsunami on Tuesday, Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said Democrats intend to end the war and bring down costs, promising “relief is on the way.” But the relief may be slow: Gas still averages $4.12 a gallon, about $1 higher than a year ago, and even in the most optimistic scenario, prices could take three months

articles.title: Leonardo Aguilar Leaves Behind Family Controversies & Releases ‘Esquina 22’: ‘There Are Things That Are Not in My Hands to Resolve’
articles.summary: The Mexican singer spoke with Billboard Español about his new album and how he has overcome the difficult moments he has experienced in the last years.
articles._body: Being part of such a renowned dynasty in Mexican music as the Aguilar family is no easy feat. At least that’s the case for Leonardo Aguilar , who in recent years has had to face criticism and accusations on social media surrounding his famous family. It’s something he admits has not only affected him personally, but also professionally, making him think twice before releasing new music. But now, he has decided to set aside his fears and move forward. “There were many years of negative comments that made me put my career on hold — but at this point, I don’t want to live with that anger anymore,” the son of Pepe Aguilar and brother of Ángela Aguilar tells Billboard Español . “I’ve been through a lot of blows, but that shouldn’t stop me anymore. I’ve overcome that fear because there are things that are not in my hands to resolve; my music is.” On Thursday night (Nov. 5), the 27-year-old singer released his fourth solo studio album, Esquina 22 , with indie label Machin Records and distribution by Virgin Music Latino. The 10-track set includes renditions of iconic ranchera songs like “Las Rejas No Matan,” “A Pesar de Todo” and “Acepto Mi Derrota,” as well as original tracks such as “Nada Pa’l Futuro” and “Canción de Rancho,” the latter in collaboration with El Komander. “I created very different versions of the classics. It’s not about trying to be like someone else,” Aguilar says. As for El Komander, he says he “never imagined I’d be able to sing with one of my idols.” Esquina 22 takes its title from an emblematic street in the small town of Tayahua, Zacatecas, where the family ranch is located. Aguilar currently resides there, and it has served as inspiration for this new stage in his career. The album was produced by Alfonso De La Cruz Pekas, also known as a songwriter of major hits by artists like Julión Álvarez, Calibre 50 and Banda Los Recoditos. From the tranquility of Rancho El Soyate, famous in recent years for its triumphs in the traditional Mexican equestrian sport of charrería, Aguilar speaks with Billboard Español about his new music, the difficult personal moments he’s lived through, how he’s learned to manage them and more. After winning last year, Rancho El Soyate didn’t take home the National Charro Championship this year. Was it frustrating for the family? Yes, it was very intense — especially because everything seemed to be pointing toward a victory, but it didn’t happen. The competition was very strong. When someone else does something better than you, there’s no reason to get upset. The El Soyate team is very good, but this time it didn’t work out. Is it important to you that young people like yourself, your sister Ángela and your brother-in-law Christian Nodal preserve and pass on Mexican traditions like charrería and music? Absolutely. Besides what you mention, charrería brings a lot of satisfaction to those who compete, to the team members and to the fans. It’s a beautiful environment. Plus, we’re supporting traditions, the culture of artisans, trainers, veterinarians, horse handlers — everyone. In addition to continuing these traditions, the young Aguilars are taking on the responsibility of passing Mexican music to new generations. Do you see it as a responsibility? It’s not a responsibility when it’s something you like, feel and love. For example, with this new album, Esquina 22 , I enjoyed carefully selecting the songs. I had a lot of songs to choose from and it was challenging, but in the end, the album turned out to be very diverse and, above all, I consider it to be very honest. What do you mean by honest? That what I interpret and want to convey is real. I didn’t grow up on a ranch, but I know the ranch life very well. I’m currently in Tayahua; I live here — it’s my home, I’m not just visiting. I’m not pretending to live on a ranch, I’m not pretending to be from the countryside; I live it and express it in my songs. I didn’t choose songs about things I haven’t experienced. People can tell when the lyrics don’t resonate with you. The album includes several covers but also original tracks, one of them in collaboration with El Komander. How did that duet come about? I’ve always liked his music, so I grew up listening to him, although I never imagined I’d get to collaborate with one of my idols. I ran into him at a charro tournament in Puerto Vallarta and greeted him. When I got to my hotel, I called my songwriter friend Eduardo Gurrola and asked him for a corrido that talked about horsemen, mentioning chaps, saddles and more. He sent it to me, I added a couple of things — and then I contacted El Komander through a friend, sent him “Canción de Rancho” and he agreed. That’s one of my favorite tracks from the album, along with another original corrido called “Nada Pa’l Futuro” and “Las Rejas No Matan,” a Mexican classic that I gave a very personal twist to. Can we say that Esquina 22 is a ranchera-style banda album? Yes. All the arrangements were done by [Alfonso de la Cruz] “Pekas.” He’s from Sinaloa, and has a lot of experience. I love this album because it captures those moments of camaraderie, of drinking, when we’re all feeling down or tired and just want to have a good time or enjoy a street-side drinking session. Why record banda and not something more trendy, like corridos tumbados? When you look at social media, people might think that one thing works better than another, but that’s relative. For example, here in Tayahua, you’ll see some people listening to Vicente Fernández or Antonio Aguilar, and others listening to corridos tumbados. It’s not the same as the lineup of a small-town fair in Zacatecas, where artists might have up to 100 shows a year without much recognition, compared to something like the Feria de Aguascalientes, which gets a lot of exposure. There’s no single reality; there are many real

articles._body: Alabama wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams is currently expected to play against No. 14 LSU on Saturday, On3’s Pete Nakos and Chris Low report . Coleman-Williams underwent arthroscopic surgery on his injured knee in mid-Oct. and has missed back-to-back games. Coleman-Williams had to be helped off the field ahead of halftime of Alabama ‘s game against No. 2 Georgia on Oct. 10 after landing awkwardly in the end zone while attempting to catch a touchdown. He also took a hard hit to the helmet from multiple Bulldog defenders later in the game, which ended his day. The junior receiver has hauled in 23 receptions for 415 yards and four scores this season. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage “A lot of these guys from Zabien Brown to Ryan Coleman-Williams , EJ [Crowell] , Racin [Delgatty] , Terrance Green in particular … those guys are all working onto the football field,” head coach Kalen DeBoer said earlier this week. “They’re not all in the exact same spot, but they’re all out there going through workouts. Some are taking team reps, some are taking non-contact reps. “But I think the progress by all of them is headed in a good direction. We’ll see. I think a lot of it has to do with how their bodies respond after they’re out there being pushed a little bit more at the end of the last week, yesterday, as well. And that will continue to happen throughout the course of the week.” Alabama can earn second ranked victory of season with win over No. 14 LSU Alabama heads into Saturday’s game against the Tigers ranked No. 5 in the first College Football Playoff Rankings of the 2026 season. This ranking seemed particularly high for Kalen DeBoer ‘s team, which had lost back-to-back games (No. 2 Georgia and No. 14 Tennessee ) before bouncing back with a 31-20 win over Texas A&M on Oct. 24. Alabama enjoyed its much-needed bye-week, and will head into Saturday’s game well-rested. Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell struggled without Coleman-Williams on the field in Alabama ‘s 26-10 loss to No. 14 Tennessee . Russell was held to a season-low 147 passing yards and no touchdowns with two interceptions in the 16-point loss. He bounced back, however, against the Aggies, passing for 311 yards and three touchdowns. Coleman-Williams will certainly provide a spark for Alabama ‘s defense in Saturday’s game. In two career games against LSU , the junior has hauled in a combined five catches for 62 yards and one touchdown.

Merissa Blitz This year, SummerStage marked a monumental accomplishment — 40 years providing free concerts for New Yorkers — with a similarly monumental season. “We were lucky enough to get some really amazing funders who gifted us with additional resources to celebrate the 40th,” executive artistic director Erika Elliott says. “It gave us a chance to look back and also look forward.” That included shows with “important cultural icons — and distinctly New York people” including La India, Angélique Kidjo and Laurie Anderson, “bookings that felt really intentional.” This season’s programming spoke to the diversity of the five boroughs. “No other festival is doing a Taiwanese day, or a dedicated C-pop [Chinese pop] day, or a day fully focused on ­Morocco,” she says. Another major moment came when the next-gen jam band Goose did a surprise pop-up show in June in Central Park the night after two Madison Square Garden gigs. Says Elliott: “For me, that was a big coup this year — to have the relationship and the reputation that a band at that level says, ‘Hey, could we do a show with you?’ ” Elliott, a 22-year SummerStage veteran who has served as its executive artistic director since 2015, admits that because the organization doesn’t depend on ticket sales, she’s in an “enviable position” — but she points out the “competitive landscape” for nonprofits. “Our budget has always increased a little bit,” she says, “but I don’t know that it’s always able to keep up with the increase in artists’ fees.” Additionally, climate change continues to throw curveballs at the outdoor festival. “We were not able to present Mavis Staples because of the smoke and the air quality. That’s a trend that never used to happen,” Elliott says of the R&B legend’s scuttled July show. “We are working on updating our process every year and always learning more. We look for guidance from the city when possible.” Changes in the political climate — such as partial travel bans on countries like Nigeria — have also created challenges. “It changes our ability to book artists who deserve to play,” she says. “It’s really unfortunate … to not let an artist come and perform in this country, especially artists who have performed in this country before. I just don’t see how that builds bridges or does anything positive.” Still, Elliott — a self-described “optimist” — remains hopeful for SummerStage’s future. “I’ve been here so long because it’s a dream job, to be able to bring music and artists and communities together, for free, across all five boroughs,” she says. “We have a legacy to build on for our 80th ­[anniversary].” —JOE LYNCH Collectiv Presents Michael Berg Partner/talent buyer Concerts West John Meglen President/co-CEO Paul Gongaware Co-CEO Country Thunder Music Festivals Troy Vollhoffer President/CEO; president/CEO, Premier Global Production Danny Wimmer Presents Danny Wimmer Founder Dayglo Presents Peter Shapiro Founder DF Entertainment Diego Finkelstein Founder Do LaB Jesse Flemming Co-founder Fenix Entertainment Marcelo Figoli Owner/CEO Framework Kobi Danan Founder Frontier Touring Dion Brant CEO Susan Heymann COO Goldenvoice Paul Tollett President Melissa Ormond COO Stacy Vee Jenn Yacoubian Executive vps Iglesias Entertainment Jorge Iglesias Founder/CEO Insomniac Pasquale Rotella Founder La Familia Presenta Aaron Ampudia Christopher Den Uijl Co-founders Live Nation Michael Rapino President/CEO Arthur Fogel Chairman of global music/president of global touring Omar Al-joulani President of touring Bob Roux President of U.S. concerts Jared Braverman Hans Schafer Senior vps of global touring Colin Lewis Global tour promoter Live Nation International Paul Antonio President, EMEA/Asia, Live Nation Dennis Argenzia President of touring, Asia, Live Nation Michael Coppel Chairman of Live Nation Australia and New Zealand Denis Desmond Chairman, U.K. and Ireland, Live Nation Bruce Moran Executive chairman of Latin America Touring, Live Nation

articles.title: Rams’ Myles Garrett on track to finally come off IR in time for Commanders clash
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams traded for Myles Garrett to secure themselves another Lombardi Trophy, but now they are relying on him just to get back into the playoff picture. The superstar edge rusher, who already has a bust waiting for him in Canton, is on track to return from arthroscopic knee surgery
articles._body: The Los Angeles Rams traded for Myles Garrett to secure themselves another Lombardi Trophy, but now they are relying on him just to get back into the playoff picture. The superstar edge rusher, who already has a bust waiting for him in Canton, is on track to return from arthroscopic knee surgery and suit up in Sunday afternoon’s road game versus the Washington Commanders , according to Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport from NFL Network and ESPN. Garrett logged 40 snaps in a miserable 27-7 season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia before landing on injured reserve. He practiced throughout the week and is now ready to unleash two months’ worth of frustration on Jayden Daniels and the Commanders. Sean McVay may want to ease the two-time Defensive Player of the Year back into action, but he also understands that urgency is needed. Ideally, Garrett can wreak havoc and swing momentum in LA’s favor without carrying a full workload. In between rehabbing his knee injury and watching film, he has had plenty of time to reflect on his shockingly quiet Rams debut. Now seemingly healthy, Garrett is determined to compose the type of ferocious masterpiece that fans have been clamoring for since he joined the franchise in June. The NFL’s single-season sacks leader will await for official clearance, but the expectation is that he will be activated for Week 8. The Rams (4-4) face the Green Bay Packers (5-3), Kansas City Chiefs (5-2) and 49ers (6-1) from Weeks 12-14, and they play the Seattle Seahawks (4-4) twice in the final three weeks of the regular season. Ergo, Myles Garrett has the next two matchups and a bye to prepare himself for the campaign-defining portion of the schedule. articles.title: Jets WR Garrett Wilson’s concussion will keep him out of Week 9 vs. Chiefs
articles.summary: The New York Jets will be without their best offensive player when they take on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 9. Wide receiver Garrett Wilson has been diagnosed with a concussion and will not play Sunday, giving the Jets another challenge to overcome. Wilson reportedly entered the NFL’s co
articles._body: The New York Jets will be without their best offensive player when they take on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 9. Wide receiver Garrett Wilson has been diagnosed with a concussion and will not play Sunday, giving the Jets another challenge to overcome. Wilson reportedly entered the NFL’s concussion protocol earlier this week, and his absence is now confirmed. The news is a tough blow for New York, especially considering how important he has been to the team’s offense. Wilson is far and away the Jets’ most dangerous offensive weapon. Without him, New York will have to find other ways to generate production through the passing game. Adonai Mitchell and Omar Coopper Jr. will step up. That is easier said than done against Kansas City. The Chiefs always present a difficult matchup, and losing Wilson takes away the receiver opposing defenses have to account for on every passing down. It also puts more pressure on the remaining pass catchers to step up and give the Jets some consistency. The most important thing for Wilson is making a full recovery before returning to the field. Concussions are serious injuries, and the Jets should not rush their star receiver back before he is ready. In good news, Breece Hall is expected to play . Hall missed a handful of weeks, but when healthy, he can really change the pace of the game. With how good Braelon Allen has played as of late, it looks like the Jets may have a strong dynamic duo between the two. articles.title: Nick Saban calls Miami game a 'must-win situation' for Notre Dame
articles.summary: The biggest game of an absolutely loaded Week 10 college football slate will be played between No. 1 Miami and No. 11 Notre Dame in South Bend Saturday night. Both teams have their sights set on the College Football Playoff, meaning a win for either program would be massive in that effort. For Miami
articles._body: The biggest game of an absolutely loaded Week 10 college football slate will be played between No. 1 Miami and No. 11 Notre Dame in South Bend Saturday night. Both teams have their sights set on the College Football Playoff, meaning a win for either program would be massive in that effort. For Miami , it heads into the matchup as the No. 1 overall team in the first College Football Playoff Rankings of the season. Notre Dame , meanwhile, sits at No. 11 in the CFP Rankings. That would put them as the ‘Last Team In’ for now, as Boise State would grab the No. 12 seed as the GO6 representative. To say Saturday’s game is massive would be an understatement. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage On Friday’s episode of ‘ The Pat McAfee Show ‘, College Football Hall of Famer Nick Saban called the game a ‘must-win’ situation for the Irish. To this point, Notre Dame sits at 7-1 on the season, but doesn’t boast a ranked win. Especially with Miami star receiver Malachi Toney out, this is a big opportunity for Marcus Freeman’s team to earn their elusive ‘signature win’. “This is a huge game. Obviously, playing the No. 1 team in the country at home. I think the game is kind of a must-win situation, because the College Football Playoff put them conveniently at No. 11. ‘Conveniently’ means if they don’t win, they may be on the outside looking in. Not saying they can’t play their way back into it, but they don’t have the strongest schedule to finish with. “They wouldn’t have any quality wins, which was a big issue last year. But, I like their team and their defense. I like Marcus Freeman and the way he coaches this team, and the way he’s been preparing their team to focus on the moment and not the outcome.” CFP Selection Committee dropped Notre Dame to No. 11 in first Rankings Notre Dame opened the week at No. 4 in the AP Poll, but was dropped all the way to No. 11 in Tuesday’s College Football Playoff Rankings show. Arkansas AD Hunter Yuracheck , who serves as the chair of the CFP Selection Committee, opened up about the Irish’s slide to No. 11. “ Notre Dame , obviously, ranked 11th, is impressive,” Yurachek said on the ESPN rankings release show. “The committee is impressed by their performance on both sides of the ball. They are a very good football team. “But when you look at Notre Dame ’s schedule and the wins that they have, vs. the teams that are ahead of them, they don’t have that signature win right now . They lost in their only Top-25 matchup at BYU . The next best win as on a neutral site against Wisconsin . They’ve a great opportunity in front of them this weekend at home vs. Miami to get that signature win that I think they need to move up in the rankings. But the committee is very impressed by them. They wouldn’t be 11th if we were not.” The Irish can silence all the ‘signature win’ talk this weekend with a win over the ‘Canes. Notre Dame is seeking its first win over the No. 1 ranked team in the country since it knocked off No. 1 Clemson 47-40 in 2OT on Nov. 7, 2020.
