articles.title: OpenAI wants to win over data-center opponents by calling them ‘compute campuses’ and promising local benefits
articles.summary: “A campus implies a university, not a warehouse,” says veteran brand strategist Allen Adamson of OpenAI’s new pitch to communities.
articles._body: OpenAI has a new name for the loud, dull, gray buildings Americans don’t really want as their next-door neighbors, and it’s calling them “compute campuses.” Along with the rebrand comes a list of promises. On Thursday, the company published a National Community Compact, pledging to pay its own energy costs, disclose what its facilities do to the places around them, and give residents a say in how future sites it owns and operates are built. The announcement came just two days after voters backed restrictions or rejected pro-development proposals in all but one of the 41 local data-center ballot measures across 10 states, according to Ballotpedia . “Voters made their concerns about data centers clear in this week’s elections, and we need to listen and respond with concrete action,” OpenAI Chief Global Affairs Officer Chris Lehane wrote on LinkedIn Thursday, while also acknowledging that data centers had become a proxy for concerns about affordability, corporate power, and communities losing control over their futures. OpenAI is banking on this pitch working because, for the company, it’s about more than image. Its very growth depends on putting up enormous facilities in towns where people are asking, with growing suspicion, what’s in it for them and what they could lose.  The ChatGPT maker argues that “compute campuses” captures an economic role extending beyond the buildings themselves. In a policy blueprint released alongside the compact, it says specialized equipment and recurring hardware upgrades can generate sustained demand for skilled workers and local suppliers.  “The goal is for these campuses to support lasting local jobs and economic development beyond our facilities, with communities having a say in how they’re built,” an OpenAI spokesperson told Fortune in an email statement. Allen Adamson, a veteran brand strategist, is skeptical that the data center rebrand will help. “You can’t rename your way out of a problem,” he told Fortune . He pointed to Facebook’s change to Meta , which he saw partly as an attempt to escape the backlash against social media. But a new name didn’t change the fact that it was still a social media company, he said—just as calling a data center a “compute campus” doesn’t change what’s next door. Rebranding works best when it follows improvements to the product, he said, giving consumers a reason to reconsider the company along with its name. He also questioned what the term “campus” will evoke for residents when the facilities merely house servers and power equipment, rather than an actual OpenAI campus where people research AI and think about how to build it. “A campus implies a university, not a warehouse,” Adamson said. “If you pick a name, you don’t want to overpromise. You want to try to realistically reflect what it is.” Brendan Steinhauser, a Republican strategist and CEO of the Alliance for Secure AI who is working to get his party on board the AI safeguards train, suggested the terminology might initially confuse residents without changing how they feel once they understand what’s being built. They would still see, in his words, “a big ugly thing in my neighborhood that uses a bunch of water and drives up my energy costs.” What’s on offer OpenAI’s compact outlines changes to how it develops and operates its facilities, including publishing construction plans, commissioning independent noise studies, and reporting water and electricity use. It says it will not require public officials to sign nondisclosure agreements as a condition of discussions or negotiations, while allowing narrow protections for security, trade secrets, and other sensitive information.  The company also pledges to pay for the electricity and additional infrastructure needed to serve its sites, with financial assurances to protect other customers if a project is delayed, reduced, or canceled. Other commitments reach beyond the facilities’ immediate impacts. OpenAI says it has committed $80 million beyond tax payments in Effingham County, Georgia, including a $4.8 million grant to provide free school meals for all 14,000 county students. In Pike County, Ohio, it says families identified childcare as a priority, leading to a joint $6 million commitment from OpenAI and SB Energy. OpenAI says that it’s building on commitments announced in January, and its latest blueprint was in development before the election, according to CNBC. Other companies are also making similar offers. Amazon last month announced a $1 billion investment in data-center communities , including community college access and home energy upgrades, with the program spanning five years. Microsoft’s Datacenter Academy works with local colleges to train people for data-center jobs, offering scholarships that can cover tuition, fees, and certification costs.  Steinhauser said sustained investment could help companies build goodwill over time, pointing to youth centers, libraries, infrastructure, and jobs that last beyond construction. He cited Andrew Carnegie and Andrew Mellon, whose spending on museums and libraries helped soften their reputations as robber barons.  But broader distrust of technology companies, he expects, remains an obstacle. “I think it’s just that sort of skepticism of big tech is just going to outweigh any rebranding effort,” he said. Who protects ratepayers OpenAI is also asking policymakers to establish industry-wide rules. While its compact covers future facilities it owns and operates, its blueprint proposes broader requirements for large electricity users to cover the costs they add to the grid, alongside public reporting on facilities’ local impacts. Mark MacCarthy, a technology policy expert and nonresident senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, said that it’s up to state lawmakers and regulators to ensure households aren’t left paying for data centers’ energy needs. “I don’t think there’s anything tech companies can do to reassure the pu

articles.title: Oklahoma football makes final John Mateer decision after Ben Arbuckle firing
articles.summary: With the Oklahoma football program firing offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle, the team will look to keep the ship afloat as the Sooners take on the Florida Gators on Saturday. As the Oklahoma football team has moved on from Arbuckle, there were some questions about what that could mean for quarte
articles._body: With the Oklahoma football program firing offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle , the team will look to keep the ship afloat as the Sooners take on the Florida Gators on Saturday. As the Oklahoma football team has moved on from Arbuckle , there were some questions about what that could mean for quarterback John Mateer, as his status for Saturday has been revealed. According to college football insider Pete Nakos and George Stoia at On3 Sports, Mateer is “expected to start” for the Sooners against the Gators, as the senior “took most of the first-team quarterback reps” this past week. With how underwhelming the offense has been, there was speculation about whether Mateer would be benched. “Oklahoma is expected to start quarterback John Mateer at Florida on Saturday night, sources tell Sooner Scoop’s George Stoia and On3’s Pete Nakos. The Sooners fired offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle earlier this week, prompting questions about whether Oklahoma would make a change at quarterback,” Nakos wrote. “But sources tell On3 that Mateer took most of the first-team quarterback reps in practice this week, and the plan remains for him to start. In eight games this season, Mateer has thrown seven interceptions,” Nakos continued. “The Sooners currently rank 108th in scoring offense and 111th in total offense. Mateer’s struggles have been coupled with a running game averaging just 3.17 yards per carry, which ranks 128th in the nation.” Oklahoma football’s Brent Venables speaks on Ben Arbuckle firing So far this season with the Oklahoma football team, Mateer has thrown for 1,835 yards with 13 touchdowns and seven interceptions. As tight ends coach Jason Witten is the interim offensive coordinator for the Sooners, head coach Brett Venables said in a statement Monday that he believed the team needed a “change” in firing Arbuckle. “I believe we still have meaningful opportunities ahead and a responsibility to maximize them. Our expectations remain high, and our commitment to meeting them is unwavering,” Venables said. articles.title: DraftKings Cut More Jobs Ahead of Q3 Earnings
articles.summary: DraftKings
articles._body: DraftKings underwent layoffs this week, marking at least the third round of job cuts the company has made this year. It represents the latest in a broader wave of 2026 gambling industry layoffs from companies including FanDuel, Underdog, and PrizePicks. The exact scope of the layoffs was not clear, although more than a handful of people have posted on social media about their jobs being eliminated. Front Office Sports spoke with two of the employees who were part of this week’s cuts, as well as one employee who was laid off in a prior round. “DraftKings is not going to comment on personnel decisions,” a spokesperson for the company told FOS . Affected employees in this week’s cuts worked in a range of areas, including customer experience, engineering, and legal. That’s not unusual for a company the size of DraftKings, which at the end of fiscal 2025 reported it had more than 5,500 employees. That was up from over 5,100 employees as of the end of fiscal 2024 , and well above the more than 4,400 employees DraftKings reported at the end of fiscal 2023 (in 2023, it cut 3.5% of its workforce , with affected employees being primarily based outside the U.S.). “As businesses build year over year, they take on extra fat, and at a certain point you need to cut,” said one gaming industry source who asked not to be identified due to the nature of their work. “It’s fair to assume layoffs will be one of the first levers they’d pull.” There are likely more cuts on the horizon. Citizens analyst Jordan Bender has previously estimated DraftKings could stand to cut up to 20% of its workforce. He said that in a research note from several quarters ago. The people let go this week were informed on Monday, according to two of the laid-off employees. DraftKings also cut jobs over the summer and in the spring, according to multiple sources and social media posts from affected employees. This has been a year of significant layoffs in the gambling industry. In May, Penn Entertainment and Gambling.com Group had cuts (the latter has since changed its name to Grandstand). Underdog , PrizePicks, and FanDuel also had layoffs this year. Analysts told FOS in May that the trend of job cuts in the industry could be attributed to the adoption of artificial intelligence and financial pressure from investors amid increasing competition from prediction markets. ‘Firmly focused on managing our cost structure’ The DraftKings cuts came ahead of the company releasing its third quarter results on Thursday. The company noted it remains “firmly focused on managing our cost structure.” DraftKings also said that in the third quarter, its adjusted operating expenses—excluding prediction markets—declined year-over-year. “In 2027, we expect significant operating leverage in our core business driven by national marketing efficiencies as states mature and cost programs designed to optimize how we work.” DraftKings lowered its fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to between $6.35 billion and $6.55 billion, from a range of $6.5 billion to $6.9 billion. But CEO Jason Robins expressed confidence moving forward, saying he expects an “exceptional” 2027. The company said it added more than one million prediction-market customers in the third quarter, and that it is now the “clear” number three exchange (behind Kalshi and Polymarket). DraftKings said it expects its prediction-market business to generate hundreds of millions of dollars in gross revenue this year, although new customer promotions could offset roughly 90% of that amount, leaving net revenue close to neutral. On Friday’s earnings call, Robins said the focus on growing DraftKings Predictions hasn’t come at the cost of its core business of traditional sports betting. “I don’t think we’re giving up an inch anywhere. We are laser focused on the core.” DraftKings stock was trading down more than 29% Friday morning. Year-to-date, shares are down over 52%. The post DraftKings Cut More Jobs Ahead of Q3 Earnings appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: Warriors’ Stephen Curry reveals his only trash talk with Klay Thompson these days, and it’s not what you think

Following the Golden State Warriors’ 120-100 victory over the Miami Heat, Curry revealed that his recent trash talk with his former Splash Brothers partner had nothing to do w
articles._body: Stephen Curry and Klay Thompson may no longer share the same locker room, but their friendly rivalry remains alive. Following the Golden State Warriors’ 120-100 victory over the Miami Heat, Curry revealed that his recent trash talk with his former Splash Brothers partner had nothing to do with basketball, despite their emotional reunion at Chase Center. During his postgame media availability, Curry was asked whether Thompson’s previous comments about enjoying victories over old friends provided extra motivation. Instead, the Warriors superstar revealed that their conversations centered on a college basketball wager. “No, the only conversations we’ve had are the Davidson Wildcats beating the Washington State Cougars and me getting the best end of that bet,” Curry said with a laugh . “So that was cool.” The exchange offered a hilarious glimpse into how Curry and Thompson maintain their friendship despite representing different NBA franchises. Curry played college basketball at Davidson, while Thompson starred at Washington State before both eventually became Warriors legends. The two spent 13 seasons together in Golden State, winning four NBA championships and establishing themselves as one of the greatest shooting duos in league history. Curry explained that their shared accomplishments make it easy to separate their friendship from their competitive battles on the court. He added that their competitive instincts naturally emerge whenever they face each other, making additional trash talk unnecessary. The Warriors superstar also delivered an impressive second-half performance against Miami, finishing with 29 points as Golden State secured its sixth consecutive victory. For Curry and Thompson, their rivalry now extends beyond NBA matchups, with college basketball bragging rights providing another reason to compete. articles.title: Nike's Answer to the Winter Boot? A Rugged Basketball Shoe
articles.summary: Nike's Jordan Winterized 6 Rings looks like a basketball shoe that picked up a winter job, complete with chunky soles and boot-style lacing.
articles._body: At some point, someone at Jordan decided that the Air Jordan needed to get itself a winter job. And honestly, we're not mad about it. The Jordan 6 Rings has always been a bit of a greatest-hits situation, borrowing details from the six sneakers MJ wore during his championship-winning seasons. Now, it's getting the cold-weather treatment. The Jordan Winterized 6 Rings is what happens when an Air Jordan and a winter boot meet somewhere in the middle. The familiar basketball-inspired shape is still there, but chunky tread and boot-style lacing give it a considerably tougher disposition . This particular version also comes in a rather punchy mix of blue, grey, and hits of yellow, just in case the boot-like silhouette wasn't already doing enough. Winter footwear has a habit of disappearing i nto a sea of black and brown, so it's nice to see something with a little more life to it. The bright accents give the otherwise rugged design some much-needed personality, without making it feel like you've raided the kids' shoe section. It's certainly not the sort of Jordan you'd wear to recreate MJ's greatest moments on the court. But that's kind of the fun of it. Consider it an off-duty Jordan, ready for whatever winter has planned. The Jordan Winterized 6 Rings is available for $200 on Nike's website now. articles.title: Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block Thailand’s Securities and Exchange Commission filed a criminal complaint Thursday against BG Limited, the operator of cryptocurrency exchange Bitget, alleging it ran an unlicensed digital-asset exchange for Thai users from 2022 to 2025, and notified the government to block the platform from Dec. 5. The complaint, lodged with the Economic Crime Suppression Division, also names Mr. Kritsana Kritsananuwat as an alleged supporter who promoted Bitget through Facebook and YouTube channels, the SEC said in statement No. 241/2026. From 2022 through 2025, the regulator found, Bitget offered a trading system in the ordinary course of business, charged fees, ran a Thai-language website that could show values in baht, and solicited Thai users on social channels including “Bitget Thailand” on X, “BGB Thai Holder” on Telegram and “bitgetthailand” on TikTok. That conduct amounts to operating a digital-asset exchange under Section 3 of the Emergency Decree on Digital Asset Businesses B.E. 2561 (2018) without a license, a violation of Section 26 punishable under Section 66, the SEC said. The case now moves to an inquiry official, then prosecutors and the courts. Separately, the SEC submitted Bitget’s website, other domains and its app to the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society under a 2025 royal decree that authorizes access blocks on unlicensed trading platforms. From Dec. 5, the public “will be unable to access the platform,” the statement said, and investors still holding assets there were told to consider acting before the cutoff. A licensed path that now sits next to a criminal case The enforcement push lands weeks after Bitget announced a planned acquisition of GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics (Thailand), a Bangkok digital-asset exchange and brokerage that already holds Thai licenses, through its interest in BTGT Management (Thailand) Ltd. Under that deal, GMO Internet and its Thai holding company would transfer their entire stake in GMO-Z — about 49% and 50.94%, respectively — to BTGT or a designee at completion, a Sept. 24 GMO Internet filing showed. Bitget said completion remains subject to regulatory approval and, after a change-of-control nod, it intends to introduce its trading platform to Thai users under local rules. “Thailand is an important part of Southeast Asia’s digital asset landscape, and this acquisition gives us a great opportunity to establish local operations,” Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said in the Oct. 20 release. The timetable has already slipped. GMO Internet Group pushed the effective date of the share transfer from Oct. 31 to Nov. 30, citing careful work on Thai regulatory applications and closing procedures. That revised date sits five days before the planned Bitget access block. CoinDesk reported that Bitget’s own terms of use, updated in October, already list Thailand among jurisdictions where its services are prohibited, and that the SEC has not said whether the criminal complaint will weigh on the GMO-Z change of control. What the block does and does not settle Thailand has used the same access-blocking tool before. In mid-2025 the SEC referred Bybit, OKX and three other unlicensed platforms for a June 28 cutoff, telling users to move assets first. The Bitget action follows that template — and adds a criminal complaint against the exchange operator and a named promoter. Licensed venues still sit at the center of Bangkok’s policy mix. Thailand has approved a multi-year capital-gains tax break only for trades on SEC-regulated platforms, and has been expanding regulated crypto products in derivatives and capital markets. Unlicensed platforms get the opposite treatment: investor alerts, access blocks and, now for Bitget, a police referral. What is not yet clear is whether a criminal case against BG Limited for the 2022–2025 period bars, slows or leaves untouched BTGT’s bid to take over a licensed local operator. The SEC statement does not mention GMO-Z. Bitget has not publicly answered the complaint in a statement posted with the acquisition release. For Thai users still on Bitget, the practical clock is Dec. 5. For Bitget, the test is whether Nov. 30 closes a regulated door into Thailand — or whether the complaint filed Thursday makes that licensed path the next question the ECD and the SEC have to answer. This post Thailand SEC Files Criminal Complaint Against Bitget Ahead of Dec. 5 Access Block first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .

articles.title: Cardinals hire first general manager in Chaim Bloom era
articles.summary: The St. Louis Cardinals have promoted Rob Cerfolio to the general manager position, the team announced Friday. Cerfolio is set to serve as the Cardinals’ first general manager since Chaim Bloom became the president of baseball operations in 2025. The announcement comes not long after Cardin
articles._body: The St. Louis Cardinals have promoted Rob Cerfolio to the general manager position, the team announced Friday. Cerfolio is set to serve as the Cardinals’ first general manager since Chaim Bloom became the president of baseball operations in 2025. The announcement comes not long after Cardinals former assistant GM Randy Flores was hired as the Houston Astros’ new general manager . Cerfolio and Flores were both linked to different teams early in the offseason. It seemed as if either of them could have ended up being promoted to the GM role if St. Louis indeed wanted to hire a general manager. Flores ended up taking the role in Houston, and now Cerfolio has landed the position in St. Louis. The promotion will likely ensure that Cerfolio stays with the Cardinals. At just 34 years old, Cerfolio is set to handle no shortage of responsibility. He earned the promotion, however. Cerfolio worked in the Cleveland Guardians’ front office from 2015-2024, making it as high as director of player development. Cleveland is a small market team that excels at developing talent, and Cerfolio played a role in that success. He has since impacted the Cardinals in a similar manner. St. Louis clearly appreciates the work he’s done for the organization. Cerfolio takes the reins at a key time. The Cardinals are still in a rebuild , but they outperformed expectations in 2026. The idea of St. Louis competing within the next couple of years is not out of the question. Cerfolio, along with Bloom, will need to find a way to continue rebuilding while also navigating moves around a potential contender in 2027 and/or 2028. articles._body: With the Los Angeles Dodgers in the midst of an intriguing offseason after the disappointing ALCS exit to the Milwaukee Brewers, the crux of the conversation surrounds how the team will address starting pitching. As Tarik Skubal has been linked to the Dodgers and the rest of MLB in rumors, this insider discusses how the team will operate this winter. Katie Woo of The Athletic would say in a column that Los Angeles will be “all in” on Skubal, but in a world where the team strikes out on the pitcher, would they go after the next best player? To Woo, she doesn’t “think it’s as simple” in that scenario, with players that fit in that category being Freddy Peralta and Michael King, expressing that the ball club could take a “flier on some depth options.” “The Dodgers will be in on Skubal,” Woo wrote. “If he goes elsewhere, I don’t think it’s as simple as the Dodgers going after the next highest-ranked starter on the market, such as a Freddy Peralta or a Michael King. I could see them taking a flier on some depth options to soak up innings in anticipation of a quick ramp-up post-lockout, sort of like they did when they signed Tyler Anderson in the run-up to the 2022 season.” More on who the Dodgers could target if they miss out on Tarik Skubal Woo would continue speculating what the Dodgers could do if they miss out on Skubal, saying that she could see the team go after “durable veterans” like Eric Lauer and Kris Bubic. “Could we see that again if they miss on Skubal? I say yes, though I agree…that the Dodgers won’t necessarily take the next best starter,” Woo wrote. “It’s too early in the offseason to know any legitimate options — especially because this potential addition likely wouldn’t come until after the new CBA. Still, pitching depth is vital, as the Dodgers know well. The Dodgers could consider an assortment of middle-tier starters to address that need.” At any rate, it remains to be seen who the Dodgers will pick up this offseason. articles.title: Lakers’ Luka Doncic or peak James Harden? Doc Rivers, Bill Simmons make their picks
articles.summary: Luka Doncic and James Harden have often drawn comparisons because of their scoring, playmaking, and control of the offense. Both have built their games around creating opportunities with the ball in their hands. However, Doc Rivers believes there are important differences between the two. During
articles._body: Luka Doncic and James Harden have often drawn comparisons because of their scoring, playmaking, and control of the offense. Both have built their games around creating opportunities with the ball in their hands. However, Doc Rivers believes there are important differences between the two . During an appearance on Bill Simmons’ podcast, Rivers pushed back against the idea that the Lakers star and Harden play the same way. The former Philadelphia 76ers coach acknowledged one major similarity, though. “They’re different. They are different. Even though they both hold the ball forever,” Rivers said. Doc Rivers and Bill Simmons say Luka Dončić is a better scorer than James Harden. pic.twitter.com/kN3Pxi38gc — NBABase (@TheNBABase) November 6, 2026 Rivers also argued that Harden received more criticism for his ball-dominant style during his prime, despite Doncic holding the ball for longer stretches during his time in Dallas. “Even in Luka’s heyday in Dallas, people never talked about it, but they killed James Harden for having the ball,” Rivers said. “Luka actually had the ball more in his hands, and no one ever said that, which is really interesting.” However, Rivers explained that Doncic tends to execute offensive actions more quickly. He also praised both players as exceptional passers. The discussion comes as Doncic continues to make an early case for the MVP award with the Lakers. NBA analyst Zach Lowe recently named him his leading candidate , pointing to the team’s strong performance with Doncic on the floor. “+21 with Luka on the floor, -17 per 100 with Luka off the floor. What else can you say about Luka? MVP favorite as of now, and just unguardable, completely unguardable,” Lowe said. Zach Lowe calls Luka Doncic his MVP favorite right now: "MVP favorite as of now, and just unguardable, completely unguardable." pic.twitter.com/hSPGQePu52 — NBABase (@TheNBABase) November 5, 2026 Doncic is also competing with Victor Wembanyama and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander in the early MVP conversation. Harden, meanwhile, is now playing for the Cleveland Cavaliers . Although their roles and teams have changed, the comparison between the two offensive stars remains a popular NBA debate. articles.title: Nearly two-thirds of 2021’s top 100 altcoins have lost more than 90%, CoinMarketCap data shows
articles.summary: Research CoinMarketCap shared with Fortune shows the median losing altcoin issued about 50% more tokens while the market cut its value by 95%.
articles._body: For anyone in crypto in 2021, the main risk felt like not owning any. The biggest altcoins looked like serious long-term bets: That November, Solana and Cardano were each worth roughly $70 billion, with functioning networks, full-time development teams, and ambitious roadmaps. If prices fell, you held—the same buy-and-hold logic traditional investors had long applied to quality assets. Nearly five years later, almost two-thirds of the 100 largest altcoins from that moment have lost more than 90% of their value, according to CoinMarketCap research I received, based on prices as of Oct. 21. Almost half are down more than 95%, and 70 hit their lowest price since the 2021 peak at some point this year. Over the same period, Bitcoin is up about 30% . Good projects did not reliably make good investments. Five years of data now let investors ask sharper questions than they could in 2021: whether a network is useful, whether its growth creates demand for its token and how much future growth its valuation already assumes. “That was one of the things investors often missed in 2021,” Jim Ferraioli , director of digital currencies research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research, said in an email to Fortune . “A strong team, useful technology and growing network can all be positive, but they don’t necessarily mean the token itself will capture the economic value being created.” To be sure, not every 2021 altcoin collapsed. Seven of the 100 are worth more today than at the November 2021 peak, including Zcash, up about 646% after a late-2025 rally in privacy coins, and TRON, up 212%. Familiar names XRP and BNB are up 16% and 22%, respectively. BNB also shows how supply can work in holders’ favor. Its market cap is about 4% lower than in 2021, but its price is higher because token burns cut supply by 21%. Why the old leaders stayed down Among the 81 tokens that lost at least 70%, circulating supply increased by a median of about 50%, while median market cap fell by roughly 95%. Even without additional tokens entering circulation, 77 of the 81 would still have lost at least 70%. “The popular explanation is token unlocks, but the data says demand,” Alice Liu, head of research at CoinMarketCap, said in an email to Fortune . “The median losing coin issued about 50% more tokens since 2021 while the market cut what it would pay for the whole project by 95%.” When money returned to altcoins, it didn’t necessarily return to the same ones. Crypto excluding bitcoin briefly reached a new market-cap high in October 2025, but 39 of today’s 100 largest altcoins weren’t even listed on CoinMarketCap in November 2021. “The altcoin market did not die, it changed hands,” Liu said. Ferraioli also points to the sheer number of competing tokens. “The average cryptocurrency has little fundamental value, and new ones are created every day,” he said. A 90% decline from a previous high doesn’t tell you whether the current price is cheap if the old valuation was hard to justify. Why a 95% discount isn’t a bargain Supply makes the comparison even harder. Solana’s market value , for instance, is only about 10% below its November 2021 level, but with supply nearly doubling, SOL’s price is down 54%. NEAR’s market cap rose about 20%; its price still fell 51% as circulating supply more than doubled. In both cases, the project’s market cap held up far better than its token price, and investors should watch that gap. Another question is where a network’s economic value ends up. A blockchain can process more transactions and collect more fees while token holders receive none of that income—the fees may go to validators, application developers or a treasury. Staking rewards can work against holders more quietly. If they’re paid in newly created tokens, an investor’s balance grows while their share of the total supply shrinks. “Substantial network activity does not automatically translate into value for the protocol,” Eric Lu, lead economist at the Avalanche Foundation , a nonprofit that supports the Avalanche blockchain ecosystem, said in written comments to Fortune . For investors, what matters is whether network growth can translate into token value: through fees that are burned or shared with holders, supply that is capped or shrinking, or demand that requires users to buy and hold the token. How to tell a comeback from a value trap Ferraioli, a former equity portfolio manager, said the framework he uses for crypto is similar to the one he used for stocks. “As a growth equity investor, I looked for companies that were leaders in their markets, had recurring revenue, benefited from network effects and could achieve economies of scale.” For a token to accrue value, he looks for utility, scarcity and network effects. Then he asks what the token’s use case is, whether it leads that market and whether that use case is growing or shrinking relative to the broader crypto ecosystem. “You still need a clear mechanism connecting growth of the network to demand for the token,” Ferraioli said. Stock-style fundamental analysis still has value in crypto, but it does not go far enough on its own. Investors have to understand how value flows to the token, how quickly supply is changing and what expectations are already embedded in the price. Five years from now, some of today’s leading altcoins may have stronger products, more users and larger markets. The better investment will be the one where that growth creates durable demand for the token, supply stays under control and the price does not already assume years of future success. articles.summary: The Houston Astros are set to interview Albert Pujols about being their next manager. Pujols’ legendary playing career speaks for itself, but can he translate that greatness to the dugout? Podcaster Tyler Stafford isn’t entirely sure, per Crush City Territory. Essentially, Stafford sa
articles._body: The Houston Astros are set to interview Albert Pujols about being their next manager. Pujols’ legendary playing career speaks for itself, but can he translate that greatness to the dugout? Podcaster Tyler Stafford isn’t entirely sure , per Crush City Territory. Essentially, Stafford said Pujols may be “too good” at the game, which could hurt him. In other words, explaining the game well isn’t the same as playing well. “My only concern with Albert Pujols is that he is too good at baseball,” Stafford said. “I think that sometimes when you’re too good naturally, it’s difficult to explain to mortals what you’re doing. ” Stafford then cited other legendary players, such as Barry Bonds, who took coaching positions, but it didn’t pan out. “We saw Barry Bonds take a hitting coach job with the Marlins, and they struggled. There’s not a ton of really good managers who are also the best player in baseball. Now part of that is because there’s just not a lot of guys who are the best players in baseball who also want to become managers. Maybe Albert Pujols really wants to manage for the next 30 years and knows how to do it. Of course managers differ from hitting coach, you’re not in the weeds as much. Your more kind of setting the tone of the locker room and the people in there. Albert Pujols’ first coaching tip? “Just hit 700 home runs…” @tylercstafford wonders if Pujols is too naturally gifted to manage the Astros, arguing “it is difficult to explain to mortals what you’re doing.” pic.twitter.com/Qbb8Lzd5wD — Crush City Territory (@CrushCityShow) November 6, 2026 A handful of great players became great managers. John McGraw, Roger Hornsby, Lou Boudreau, Frank Robinson, Dusty Baker, and Joe Torre are among them. The Astros fired manager Joe Espada after the Chicago White Sox eliminated them in the AL Wild Card series. Pujols finished his playing career with 3,384 hits, 703 home runs, and 2,218 RBIs. articles.title: Wisconsin reports measles death of a baby, first death in over 35 years
articles.summary: Next week, experts will determine if the US has lost its measles elimination status.
articles._body: An infant in Wisconsin has died of measles, the first measles death in the state since 1990, officials reported Thursday . The death comes amid an outbreak in the Badger State that has stricken over 430 people across 13 counties this year. "Any death of a child is a tragedy, and even more so when it is related to a vaccine-preventable disease," Wisconsin Health Secretary Kirsten Johnson said in a statement. "Measles can cause serious illness and death, and it is important for all Wisconsinites to evaluate their risk and take steps to protect themselves and their family." The baby's death is the third measles fatality nationally just this week, following the death of a New York child reported on Monday and another death in Pennsylvania reported on Wednesday . The Pennsylvania death was of an unvaccinated person in Jefferson County; the state health department did not provide additional details, such as the age of the person. The state's explosive, ongoing measles outbreak has led to 1,467 cases so far this year. Read full article Comments

Former FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing $2.47 Million in Crypto From Investigations
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Former FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing $2.47 Million in Crypto From Investigations A former FBI agent pleaded guilty Thursday to stealing about $2.47 million in cryptocurrency with wallet credentials the bureau had collected in its own cases, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia announced . Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, of Ashburn, Virginia, entered pleas to wire fraud and money laundering in federal court in Alexandria. U.S. District Judge Patricia Tolliver Giles accepted the plea. He faces up to 20 years in prison and is scheduled for sentencing on March 4, 2027. Court papers put the illicit haul at $2,474,380.66. Prosecutors say Yaroch made roughly 100 fraudulent transfers using credentials tied to 35 separate FBI investigations, drawing on wallets controlled by investigation subjects, adversarial nation-state actors and at least one wallet the FBI itself had created for an operation. The Justice Department Office of the Inspector General had flagged the case in August after Yaroch’s arrest on a criminal complaint. That earlier account described a smaller set of transfers — about 10 moves totaling roughly $1 million — and noted that Yaroch self-reported the activity to two department employees on July 29, 2026. The plea figures are larger. From 2017 through early 2025, Yaroch worked in the FBI Boston Division on a squad focused on an adversarial nation-state. From February 2025 through July 31, 2026, he served in the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division at headquarters, with access to systems that stored cryptocurrency credentials gathered in investigations. How the FBI credentials turned into cash Beginning no later than December 2024, Yaroch used that access to move coins out of those wallets and into ones he controlled. After the transfers, he swapped the stolen cryptocurrency into other digital assets and ran further transactions meant to obscure its source, nature and ownership. Between Nov. 25, 2025, and Jan. 13, 2026, he moved about $93,082 into one of his accounts, then shuffled funds among other accounts to cover debts, including credit cards, car payments and loans, the office said. FOX 5 DC , citing the same U.S. Attorney’s Office release , noted the Portugal planning that appears in the plea papers. Yaroch asked ChatGPT how to maximize investment returns and where to live in the European Union. After the chatbot suggested buying a vineyard in Portugal, he gave Portuguese lawyers a power of attorney on June 15, 2026, to register him with the Portuguese Tax and Customs Authority, obtain a tax identification number and collect the password to his finance portal. He arranged travel to Portugal for September 2026. What the plea says the FBI lost The agreed statement of facts goes beyond the dollar figure. Yaroch’s conduct compromised multiple FBI investigations into criminal groups and nation-state adversaries, the office said, and it compromised FBI sources and methods used in foreign intelligence collection and criminal cases. It also “deprived FBI employees of their ability to carry out their functions to protect public safety and national security.” First Assistant U.S. Attorney Theophani K. Stamos and Daniel S. Wierzbicki, special agent in charge of the FBI Washington Field Office’s Counterintelligence Division, announced the plea. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kathleen Robeson and Russell Carlberg are prosecuting, with help from the National Security Cyber Section of the Justice Department’s National Security Division and the DOJ inspector general’s Mid-Atlantic region. The case is 1:26-CR-208 in the Eastern District of Virginia. The admission lands in a week when federal crypto-crime stories keep stacking up — from a failed bitcoin kidnapping plot that produced its own guilty plea last month to FBI tallies putting U.S. crypto fraud losses above $11 billion in 2025, a figure the White House has used to frame a wider crackdown. What sentencing will do with the gap between Yaroch’s July self-report and the $2.47 million plea figure is still open. So is how many of the 35 FBI cases can be repaired after an insider treated the bureau’s own wallet credentials as a personal ATM. March 4, 2027, is when Judge Giles gets to answer the first question. This post Former FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing $2.47 Million in Crypto From Investigations first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .

articles.title: Anuel AA Talks Corridos Era, Fuerza Regida Collab & Posts About Ex Karol G: ‘Maybe She’ll Unblock Me’
articles.summary: The Puerto Rican superstar previews Real Hasta la Muerte 2 and Cartel Real Hasta la Muerte. Watch the full interview here.
articles._body: Anuel AA has plenty to talk about, from the recent changes he’s made in his life to his move into Mexican corridos — and his playful jokes about his ex, Colombian superstar Karol G . In an interview with Billboard ‘s co-chief content officer Leila Cobo, released Friday (Nov. 6), aboard a yacht in Miami, he also explains why he’s fallen in love with music all over again. The Puerto Rican trap star says he decided about six months ago to stop smoking and drinking, and that he feels more alert now. “You mature over time, you know what I mean? And life teaches you things,” he admits. “Drugs don’t fulfill you, fame doesn’t fulfill you, money doesn’t fulfill you.” Related Anuel AA Reveals He’s Dropping an All-Corridos Album Along With ‘RHLM 2’: Everything We Know Anuel AA Asks Karol G to Unblock Him While Promoting ‘Vuelve’: ‘I Fall Deeply in Love’ Queens of the Stone Age Crowned on ARIA Chart With 'Perfecth' That change comes amid a busy stretch for his music. Anuel says Real Hasta la Muerte 2 is coming Nov. 19, and he may also release Cartel Real Hasta la Muerte — a Mexican corridos album he’s still finishing — on the same day. Exploring the genre has meant learning a different way to sing and working with Mexican musicians. “I fell in love with music all over again — with something new, not the same old thing,” he says. “There are going to be songs produced by Fuerza Regida. I’m talking with Jesús [Ortiz Paz] — he’s my brother, and he’s helping me with a few songs,” he adds. The conversation also touches on his kids, business ventures and relationships with his exes. When Cobo asks if he asked Karol G to unblock him on social media, Anuel laughs: “No, I’m just messing with her. But maybe she’ll unblock me.” “Do you want all your exes to be at peace with you?” Cobo asks. “Well, not all of them — not my ex… We should live in peace, right?” he replies. The exchange stays playful, and Anuel jokes that a movie about his love life would be called Los Amores perros de Anuel (or Anuel’s Love’s a B–ch ): “It’ll sell a lot. It’ll be incredible.” Between news about his upcoming projects and personal revelations, the interview offers a look at Anuel as he rethinks his life and music. Watch the full conversation above.

articles._body: In his first in-depth interview in several years, Anuel AA talks about how, after hitting rock bottom with drugs and alcohol, he found the strength to return to music — not with one album, but two. On Nov. 19, Anuel AA will release Real Hasta la Muerte 2 , a tribute to the original Real Hasta la Muerte , alongside his first corridos album, Cartel Real Hasta la Muerte . The rapper also shares that Karol G still hasn’t unblocked him on social media and how he made peace with fellow rapper Cosculluela. He opens up about his sobriety, and how during his darkest moments, he couldn’t recognize himself in the mirror. Today, he’s celebrating new collaborations with Fuerza Regida and Luis R Conriquez, as well as his love for Mexican culture. He also talks about how much he loves his children, why De La Rose is like “Anuel in a woman’s body,” Puerto Rico, and the new music festival he’ll launch in 2027. Leila Cobo: That you asked Karol to unblock you. Anuel AA: Yes. And did she unblock you? No. Hello, everyone. I’m Leila Cobo. I’m here with Anuel, and we’re here chatting on a small boat, on a yacht, here in the city of Miami, where you live, right, Anuel? Yes. This is your home. Yes, this is my home. First of all, let’s see, they’re two guns. I thought it was a cross, but no. No, they’re two guns, and they have lasers too here. Well, and where did you get them? Honestly, I’d never seen them. A jeweler that I’m working with now. He’s called Limitless. He’s very good. Here in Miami? Yes, here in Miami. OK. You’re doing a lot of new things, right? Yes, I’m working a lot. Many different things. In music and outside of music? Yes, yes. In music and outside of music. Let’s see, but first let’s talk about you. New jeweler. Yes, 100 percent. New habits. You told me you’re not smoking anything anymore. Right, yes, no, I don’t smoke anymore. You’re not drinking alcohol anymore. That either. Are you exercising every day? No. Almost every day. No, no— Not either? I’m not exercising. I’m working, eating healthy and working — pure music and pure business always. Well, and eating healthy. Yes. And when did this lifestyle change start? It started about six months ago. And why? Because one matures with time, if you understand me. Through life situations, one learns, and I don’t know, I started to feel like I already wanted — I wanted it, I wanted a change in me already. Keep watching for more!

articles.title: Olivia Dean, Kehlani, Juanes & More to Announce 2027 Grammy Nominations
articles.summary: And heads-up: The 2027 Grammys will air/stream at 4 p.m. PT, one hour earlier than before.
articles._body: Olivia Dean , the reigning Grammy winner for best new artist, is widely expected to receive multiple Grammy nominations, including album, record and song of the year, on Monday Nov. 16. She’s also set to help announce the nominations on a livestream bright and early that morning, along with Kehlani , who won two Grammys earlier this year and could be in line for more awards for her eponymous album; Amy Allen , who has won songwriter of the year, non-classical the last two years; and Pharrell Williams , a past three-time winner of producer of the year, non-classical. Related Don Toliver, Megan Moroney & ADÉLA — Who Made the Entry List for Best New Artist at the 2027 Grammys & Who Didn’t? Harvey Mason jr. on 2,300 New Grammy Voting Members, the Asian Pop Category Uproar & More: ‘We Want To Bring More People Into the Tent’ Categories With the Most & Fewest Entries for 2027 Grammys Other artists set for the nominations livestream include Alan Menken, Carly Pearce, David Guetta, FYÜTCH & Aura V, Herbie Hancock, Israel Houghton, Juanes, Linda Perry, Meghan Foley & Michelle Holme, Renée Fleming, YUNGBLUD and Ziggy Marley, as well as Harvey Mason jr., Grammys CEO, and Dr. Chelsey Green, chair of the Recording Academy Board of Trustees. Nominees across all 100 categories for the 2027 Grammys will be revealed during a special presentation on Grammy.com and the Grammys YouTube channel, with special live coverage on Good Morning America . The nominations livestream begins on Monday, Nov. 16 at 7:45 a.m. ET / 4:45 a.m. PT. There will be a wrap-up show at 9 a.m. ET/6 a.m. PT (times approximate). For the first time, the Grammy Nominations special presentation will be broadcast live at The Square in Times Square, presented by Hilton. The complete nominations list will be published on Grammy.com and at Billboard.com at 9:00 a.m. ET / 6:00 a.m. PT. The Grammys also made an important announcement about the 2027 Grammys, which will air one hour earlier than in the past. The 69th annual Grammy Awards will air/stream live on Sunday Feb. 7, 2027 at 7:00 p.m. ET / 4:00 p.m. PT on ABC, and stream on Disney+ and Hulu. This follows the lead of the Oscars, which first moved up their show to start at 4 p.m. PT for the 96th Academy Awards in 2024. The move is designed to allow viewers on the East Coast to remain with the show for the top awards without having to stay up to midnight. 2024 was Raj Kapoor’s first year as an executive producer of the Oscars. Kapoor is also an executive producer of the Grammys. The 2027 Grammys will again be held at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.

articles.summary: The six-piece say they're ready to BLOW UP with a new hyperpop single after navigating compromise, career pressures and getting their label to listen.
articles._body: During P1Harmony ‘s first six years together, there was a stretch when members couldn’t articulate why they were working so hard. “What I felt was hardest in this process was when I couldn’t find a reason for running,” Intak tells Billboard during a sit-down in their downtown Los Angeles hotel hours before they fly home to Seoul. “There were times the company just had us run without a clear purpose or a point to reach and I think I got a little worn out the moment I realized that. ‘What is our purpose in this moment? What are we running this hard for? Is it even true that running like this will get us there?’ Every time I had moments like that, I’d suddenly feel drained and it was hard. But even if our steps were really small, we always climbed little by little.” Six years into their career, the six-piece of Intak, Keeho, Theo, Jiung, Soul and Jongseob has a much clearer view of where all that running is taking them. The K-pop act’s newest EP BLOW UP arrived Friday (Nov. 6), and its title doubles as a mantra for where the group stands today. After years of steady gains on the charts, in album sales, in concert audiences and in hard-won lessons inside the boy band, they’re ready to break through in a bigger way. P1Harmony’s performance at 82WORLD: LA , their first headlining slot at a U.S. festival the previous weekend, felt like proof. “The last time we did an outdoor thing was the first time we came to L.A.,” leader Keeho recollects. “It’s been like almost four to five years and that’s a really big, full-circle moment.” Numbers show how far that gratitude goes, with Intak saying he can track the group’s progress in chart positions. “Before, our goal was just to get onto Billboard ,” he says. “Just the other day we were at No. 60, then we’re getting into the top 20 and now the top 5. Because we achieved these things one by one, I feel reassured now and I think it’s good that we can show our fans we’re artists who can do at least this much.” P1H’s six albums’ worth of Billboard 200 history — all EPs — show just that: After first entering the chart at No. 51 with HARMONY : ALL IN during the summer of 2023, P1Harmony earned their first top 40 album with 2024’s Killin’ It (No. 39 peak), followed by SAD SONG (No. 16 in 2024), DUH! (No. 23 in 2025) and their debut English-language EP, EX (No. 9, their first Top 10 in fall 2025). Earlier this year, UNIQUE debuted at No. 4 on the Billboard 200 , the group’s best showing yet, earning 58,000 equivalent album units in its first week. While they’re aiming even higher with BLOW UP , bigger shifts have been happening behind the scenes. “Because K-pop seems very exotic, people think it’s like, ‘Whoa, these guys have no control over their careers and whatnot,'” Toronto native Keeho says of outside perceptions. “That is the case for some people, I will not lie, but I feel like even labels out here [in the U.S.] are really controlling with the creatives you work with, the people you’re allowed to talk to, the visuals and stuff like that — they won’t listen to you unless you make it big. It’s the same thing with us.” What changed the conversation with P1Harmony’s Korean label and agency, FNC Entertainment, was evidence, perhaps best seen when the Keeho-composed album track “Pretty Boy” off DUH! became an unexpected breakout streaming hit, earning 12 million more listens on Spotify than the album’s title track single despite no promotion tied to it. “The company sees successes like ‘Pretty Boy’ and the fans liking the music that the members are making, taking direction in, [creating] choreo for, the stage direction that Theo takes,” explains Keeho. “It’s not just, ‘Hey, listen to us’ without any evidence; it’s the company saying, ‘Hey, actually the members are taking directions in their own fields and the fans are loving it — maybe we should listen to them more.’ I think it’s that buildup that now, finally, in [year six], they’re like, ‘Hey, maybe y’all actually know what you guys are talking about.'” For UNIQUE this year, the group thought ahead about what other songs might connect with audiences. “We really communicated to the company that something might hit differently, so let’s prepare,” Keeho continues, sharing that the sextet landed on using their budget to make visuals for “L.O.Y.L.” (because “artistically, that’s something we’ve never done”) and “ICE (VVS)” (“‘UNIQUE’ is gonna have this moment, but people at the end of the day are gonna listen to ‘ICE’ — it’s going to be the one”). True to their vision: the most-listened songs from the record on Spotify are “UNIQUE” (15.5 million streams), “ICE (VVS)” (14.5 million) and “L.O.Y.L.” (6.9 million). That track record carried into the choice of “BLOW UP” as P1H’s pick for a new single. “We don’t get to call the shots in everything by any means, especially with our lead single,” Keeho says. “But I think it’s more like we can manipulate the system a little bit better now. It’d be more like, ‘Actually, I think this song’s a little better’ and we can really communicate our thoughts and ideas. But after that, it’s kind of up in the air.” “We’ve never done [anything] this rhythmical,” Jongseob, the group’s youngest, adds. “I get more of a youthful [feeling]. This time is for a new chapter and challenging something new. That’s why we especially think ‘BLOW UP’ is better than the other options. We love ‘BLOW UP.'&#82

articles.title: 5 Best Moments of the 2026 HEAT Latin Music Awards: Olga Tañón, Gloria Trevi & More
articles.summary: The gala, which took place in Mexico for the first time, was held on Thursday (Nov. 5) in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco.
articles._body: The HEAT Latin Music Awards, popularly known as Premios HEAT, were held for the first time in Puerto Vallarta, Mexico, on Thursday (Nov. 5). The ceremony attracted a slew of stars, including Gloria Trevi, Olga Tañón, Los Ángeles Azules, Jessi Uribe, Arthur Hanlon, La Arrolladora Banda El Limón de René Camacho and Piso 21. Related Carlos Rivera Wins Big at 2026 Heat Latin Music Awards: Complete Winners List The event, which took place at the Puerto Vallarta International Convention Center and was broadcast live on LosHeat.tv and Jalisco TV, celebrated a variety of genres, including regional Mexican music, pop, urbano, cumbia, reparto and reggaetón. Joining the event were artists such as Ha*Ash, Majo Aguilar, Mar Solís, Dayanara, Paola Jara, Pututi & Nesty, Grupo 5 and Corridos Del Rey. One standout performances of the evening was a segment titled “Los que siempre viven” (“Those Who Live On”), where various artists sang timeless classics in tribute to late legends such as Selena, Vicente Fernández, José José, Paquita la del Barrio, Antonio Aguilar and Flor Silvestre, creating an emotional and heartfelt moment. Another highlight was the tribute to Puerto Rican merengue icon Olga Tañón’s career. Also known as “La Mujer de Fuego” (Woman of Fire), Tañon shared the stage with Mar Solís and Grupo 5, performing “Contigo o Sin Ti” with the former and the classic “Ya Me Cansé” with the latter. The Mexican-American sister duo Ha*Ash delivered a live performance of its new single “Antes Que Te Cases,” originally recorded with Cristian Castro, taking its pop music to new heights. Meanwhile, Gloria Trevi, who was honored this year as Artista Oro (Golden Artist) at the HEAT Latin Music Awards al Estilo Jalisco, closed the show with a vibrant medley of her greatest hits, including “Todos Me Miran,” “Me Lloras,” “Pelo Suelto” and “Con Los Ojos Cerrados.” The awards ceremony capped off HEAT Week, which ran from Oct. 31 to Nov. 5 in the state of Jalisco, coinciding with the traditional Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead). Carlos Rivera emerged as the night’s biggest winner, taking home three awards. Other notable winners included Karol G, Grupo Firme and Ovy on the Drums. For the full list of winners, click here . Here are five standout moments from the HEAT Latin Music Awards al Estilo Jalisco, organized in collaboration with the government of Jalisco and the municipality of Puerto Vallarta, in alphabetical order of the artists involved.

articles.title: Show HN: Self-Annotating Stock Charts
articles.summary:
Most stock charts work in a similar way - they give you a bunch of tools to draw lines and patterns on a chart. This is fine, and I assume that advanced traders enjoy drawing on the chart. But it's also annoying, and seems arbitrary sometimes.

So I created stock charts that annotate themselves.
articles._body: Most stock charts work in a similar way - they give you a bunch of tools to draw lines and patterns on a chart. This is fine, and I assume that advanced traders enjoy drawing on the chart. But it's also annoying, and seems arbitrary sometimes. So I created stock charts that annotate themselves. The process has two stages: First, the algorithm goes through the daily candles and identifies the structure: support and resistance zones, trendlines, volume spikes, etc. Then, an LLM models understands the relative importance of the structure components, decides which ones to include, and annotates them. Finally, it lays out the possible future moves: base case, bull and bear cases. It's included in Portfolio Genius, the AI investment manager I'm building, and it's available free without signup here: https://portfoliogenius.ai/features/ai-annotated-charts Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50394931 Points: 2 # Comments: 0

Kristaps Porzingis and Domantas Sabonis were two elite frontcourt talents, and before his ACL i
articles._body: About three or four years ago, the players on the cover art of this NBA intel column would’ve made up a very formidable team, one that could contend for a title with the right talent around them. Kristaps Porzingis and Domantas Sabonis were two elite frontcourt talents, and before his ACL injury, Kyrie Irving was playing like one of the best point guards in the NBA. Now in the midst of the 2026-27 NBA season, all three aging stars face major questions with the trade season creeping closer. Of course, nobody faces more questions than Porzingis, whose future is no longer with the Golden State Warriors and may not even be in the NBA. Porzingis has been away from the Warriors since training camp started due to his ongoing health issues, only visiting the team facility once to meet with the team’s head of medicine, Rick Celebrini, and GM Mike Dunleavy Jr. Since then, little has been said of Porzingis’ future… other than the fact that he is not currently being paid and he is seriously contemplating retirement. Once thought to be a key addition for the Warriors, especially after signing his two-year, $40 million contract extension in the offseason, Porzingis is now a dead contract that the team is looking to trade for value. Despite the complications surrounding Porzingis, this situation may have actually played right into the Warriors’ insurance plan they created for themselves with the 31-year-old. Sabonis has been available for the Sacramento Kings and is once again proving to be one of the best rebounders in the league. But with the Kings struggling to remain relevant and the 30-year-old under contract through the 2027-28 season, he will find himself as the best center available on the market before the Feb. 11 trade deadline. And then there is Kyrie, a star guard various teams have attempted to trade for since the offseason began this past summer. Will Irving remain with the Dallas Mavericks, or will the team look to sell high on the 34-year-old guard now that he’s proving to be the same player he was before the ACL injury? Let’s kick things off with how we’ve started most of the intel stories recently: Discussing what the Warriors plan to do with Porzingis and what is essentially now a $20 million trade exception with a favorable twist. Interest in Kristaps Porzingis trade growing? Bob Kupbens-Imagn Images After losing the first three games of the season, all hope seemed lost for the Warriors, and many were writing off Stephen Curry and this team. Well, flash-forward to a couple of weeks later, and all of a sudden, this group is now 6-3 on the season and on a six-game win streak after taking down the Miami Heat 120-100 on Thursday night. All seems to be right for Golden State except the fact that this Porzingis situation is still at the forefront of conversations, especially since it’s a chance for Dunleavy and this front office to really push their chips in on this season and the final years of Curry’s career. Making trades in the NBA is all about waiting for the right opportunity. If you get overanxious and make deals too soon, things tend to go in a different direction than you may have thought. The Warriors know this better than any team in the league, and this front office has been very opportunistic when it comes to operating with patience and exploring all avenues. That is what has happened with Porzingis so far, as the Warriors have held conversations with many teams around the league about Porzingis and his current contract, which is basically operating as a $20 million expiring salary in a way. Before diving into the latest rumors and intel we are hearing about a potential Porzingis trade, it’s worth mentioning and explaining the finer details about why the Warriors believe they are in a very strong position in terms of trading the big man. For starters, Porzingis’ time with the Warriors is over. He will not be playing another game for this franchise, as ClutchPoints reported on Oct. 23 before the team’s first game of the season, and it’s almost a given he will be traded, likely within the next 30-40 days. Why 30-40 days? Well, that takes us to the week before and right at December 15, which is when many around the NBA who just signed contracts this offseason become trade-eligible. Much like how the Warriors traded for Dennis Schroder in the middle of December during the 2024-25 season, only to re-aggregate him in a bigger deal for Jimmy Butler at the trade deadline, league sources are anticipating a similar strategy this time around with Porzingis. If the Warriors time it right, and they certainly have specific dates in December circled on their calendar in terms of potential trades, they can deal Porzingis before the holidays, acquire a player to contribute now, and possibly look to flip said asset into more before February 11. Another key piece of information that is essential to the Warriors’ trade plans is the fact that Porzingis is not currently being paid since he is away from the team , and he is at peace with this. Not is Porzingis fine with not being paid right now, but there will be no challenge on his behalf from the NBPA, and the Warriors have no plans to entertain the idea of a buyout, sources said. Doesn’t it seem like there is more in play here behind the scenes? One league source close to the situation who spoke to ClutchPoints on the grounds of anonymity claims that Porzingis is prepared to take a massive buyout agreement upon being traded by the Warriors, with the same source stating Porzingis would give up over 60% of his salary. If true, not only does this make the idea of trading for Porzingis easier for the Warriors in discussions with other teams, but those other teams will have great interest in freeing up immediate cap space in the form of his $20 million contract. articles._body: Guys - OpenAI Decisions, Jev, World Models are interesting. We ran some tests for the C-suite to decide between OpenAI Decisions vs. their own existing models vs. training their proprietary Financial World Model. Sharing the results of our sample tests. If you like a walkthrough with video of results - see this video - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UN1LIF01uHQ We are also trying to reach OpenAI team & community to collaborate on running various tests to help the C-suite to make decisions. Which involves which business cases, they wish to map on which Decision models. Summary: Small Financial World Model compared to OpenAI Decisions. This test is not to build a better model. But to help C-suites make informed choices. There are various considerations viz Latency Cost per decision On-premises or Hosted APIs Regulatory & Compliance Mapping to use cases Financial modelling or LLM-based reasoning as underlying architecture We ran tests to: Predict credit defaults Cross-sell propensity Churn Risk Future cash flows Future state of customers & causal impacts of interventions like no-action, Payment reminders etc. These tests are specific to banking use cases. Why Benchmark & comparison: Small on-prem Decision Models are needed due to latency, cost, regulatory or protecting the proprietary data for Enterprises. This benchmarking helps C-suite executives to decide which option - their in-house models or other options are better. Vaayu FinBench also includes some specific banking-related business cases as examples. World Model also has action-conditioning. Thus, it predicts which decision optimizes the future outcomes. Eg Risk weighted return or prevent default. Core ask from Banks Small Financial World Model is trained on-premesis on proprietary data for enterprises. Scope - This is only for demonstration purposes to give a glimpse of how to compare various options. The dataset & model size is way too small yet. On a larger proprietary dataset, the results need to be benchmarked. Results: Latency - A co-located Small Financial World Model way improves latency. Major part may be coming due to network latency. So this is one area where we would like to discuss alternatives with OpenAI team & community. Is there a smaller on-premesis version for Decision Model avaialble for co-location. Credit Defaults - Our Small Financial World model worked worse than Decision API. Cash Churn & Cross Sell propensity - Our Small Financial World model improved marginally. It’s obvious that since Decision API hasnt seen the propreitary data. The marginal improvement shows model is learning..but our model is very very small (Few 100 thousand parameters) trained on small dataset.. But test demonstrates - architecture is capable of learning better. Action conditions outcomes - This is available in World Model …but we aren’t aware of this in Decision API yet. Financial Modelling - Model is trained finance native can handle temporal & causal scenarios If you like a walkthrough - see this video - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UN1LIF01uHQ Disclaimer: This is quick tests results & has some know issues. This is only for demonstration purpose. We have included OpenAI Decisions for now...Including Jev in next releases. At the moment talking to C-suite & Banks for what they wish. We find Decision API & World Models interesting developments especially in finance & enterprises space. Looking forward to collaborate with OpenAI team & community how to enable C-suite to make choices…which are underway right now at enterprises. Prediction markets had a great election night: Now bettors are turning to which Trump officials could leave first
articles.summary: Pete Hegseth leads Polymarket’s odds for the next Cabinet departure, followed by Susie Wiles and Marco Rubio.
articles._body: Traders on prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket correctly favored Democrats to win both chambers of Congress, and proved highly accurate in forecasting several key Senate races, helping boost the platforms’ reputation for accuracy. Now, with the midterms behind them, prediction market traders have shifted their attention toward what comes next. At a time when the incoming Democratic majorities are promising to investigate many aspects of the Trump Administration—from the war in Iran to allegations of corruption—traders are placing bets on who could be the next to leave Trump’s Cabinet. A market on Polymarket has drawn nearly $190,000 in trading volume, with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, White House chief of staff Susie Wiles and Secretary of State Marco Rubio among the leading contenders. As of Friday morning, Hegseth led at roughly 31%, followed by Wiles at 24% and Rubio at 8%. But traders also put the odds of no Cabinet departure before 2027 at about 27%. Hegseth’s lead in the market comes as his role in the Iran war fuels calls for his ouster. The House could vote as early as next week on articles of impeachment that accuse him of waging the war without congressional approval, an effort Republican Rep. Thomas Massie plans to revive after the GOP’s midterm losses. Wiles has also become a target as Republicans search for someone to blame for their midterm losses. Among her critics is former Trump aide Caroline Sunshine, who called for her resignation in an interview with Fox News on Wednesday. “Her campaign skills have not translated into governing,” Sunshine said. Rubio, meanwhile, has faced questions about both his future in the administration and a possible 2028 presidential bid. He has discussed stepping down with White House officials, who asked him to stay, Bloomberg reported. But he publicly rejected the exit speculation this week, telling The New York Times that serving through the end of Trump’s term has “always been my plan.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Red Sox rumors: Boston’s offseason ‘priority’ could lead to signing star outfielder
articles.summary: The Boston Red Sox are expected to add a bat or two this offseason. While Boston would benefit from bringing in a starting pitcher with Sonny Gray entering free agency, the team’s “priority” will be to add a hitter to the middle of the lineup, Jen McCaffrey of The Athletic repor
articles._body: The Boston Red Sox are expected to add a bat or two this offseason. While Boston would benefit from bringing in a starting pitcher with Sonny Gray entering free agency , the team’s “priority” will be to add a hitter to the middle of the lineup, Jen McCaffrey of The Athletic reports. McCaffrey mentioned outfielders Randy Arozarena and Seiya Suzuki as possible MLB free agency targets for the Red Sox. Both sluggers would make sense for this Boston team. While the Sox already feature a number of right-handed hitters in the order, their overall power from the right side is a bit questionable. Of course, Willson Contreras is a slugger, and Trevor Story still has some pop in his bat. Nevertheless, having someone such as Suzuki or Arozarena join the lineup would only help the ball club. Arozarena, 31, hit .281 with an .865 OPS and 26 home runs in 2026. He added 26 stolen bases. The veteran earned his third career All-Star selection as well. While Arozarena’s strong season got overlooked at times due to the Seattle Mariners’ extremely disappointing campaign, he still certainly had a big year. Suzuki, 32, hit .270 with an .841 OPS and 26 home runs as well. He played a crucial role for a Chicago Cubs team that reached the postseason. The Red Sox play in a big market and have money to spend. Signing at least one of Arozarena or Contreras should be a feasible goal. Of course, it remains to be seen if either player is open to signing with Boston. If there is any level of mutual interest, it wouldn’t be difficult to imagine a deal coming to fruition. articles.summary: Finding reliable wide receiver production on the waiver wire can be challenging, especially as the fantasy football season enters its second half. Changing target distributions and emerging playmakers create opportunities for managers willing to look beyond the usual stars. Week 9 offers several
articles._body: Finding reliable wide receiver production on the waiver wire can be challenging, especially as the fantasy football season enters its second half. Changing target distributions and emerging playmakers create opportunities for managers willing to look beyond the usual stars. Week 9 offers several intriguing options , of course. Whether you need an immediate starter or a dependable alternative for your flex spot, these four receivers deserve a closer look before kickoff. Matthew Golden, GB (@ NE) Matthew Golden is making a strong case as one of the most appealing wide receiver options available to fantasy managers heading into Week 9 . He caught seven of 13 targets for 79 yards and a touchdown in Green Bay’s 27-19 victory over Carolina on Thursday. What makes the outing even more impressive is that Golden entered the game questionable with shoulder and foot injuries. Neither issue appeared to significantly affect his performance. He established a new career high with seven receptions against Carolina’s depleted secondary. Golden has now surpassed 75 receiving yards in five of his first eight games. His 13 targets against the Panthers also highlight the trust Green Bay has placed in him as a passing option. The upcoming matchup against New England gives Golden another opportunity to build on that momentum. Managers should feel comfortable considering him for their starting lineups, particularly in PPR formats. Just keep an eye on his injury status after Thursday’s game. Luther Burden III, CHI (vs. TB) Luther Burden III is quickly becoming one of the more intriguing wide receiver options in fantasy football. He delivered an impressive performance in Chicago’s Monday-night victory over Seattle. Burden caught seven of nine targets for 56 yards and a touchdown. Although his yardage total was relatively modest, Burden made the most of his opportunities. Seven receptions provided a useful PPR foundation, while his touchdown gave fantasy managers an additional scoring boost. More importantly, his involvement in the passing game suggests that his role is continuing to grow. Burden has been heating up recently. That makes him an increasingly attractive option for managers searching for production outside the usual top-tier receivers. His ability to turn targets into receptions gives him a reasonable weekly floor. Meanwhile, his scoring potential provides additional upside. Chicago faces Tampa Bay in Week 9, and Burden should remain firmly in the fantasy conversation. Given his recent momentum and growing involvement, he deserves consideration in all league formats. Rashee Rice, KC (vs. NYJ) Rashee Rice remains one of Patrick Mahomes’ most trusted receiving options. That makes him an appealing fantasy football target despite some uncertainty surrounding his health. He caught seven of eight targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in Kansas City’s 28-24 loss to Denver. Rice led the Chiefs in both targets and receptions. His 11-yard touchdown reception in the first quarter also provided a valuable fantasy boost. That’s even though his average of 7.6 yards per reception limited his overall yardage production. The most important takeaway is his usage. Rice continues to receive consistent opportunities from Mahomes. That involvement gives him a strong foundation for future fantasy production. However, managers need to monitor his injury situation closely. Rice is dealing with two injuries and was limited during Wednesday’s practice. If cleared to play, Rice should be considered a strong starting option against the New York Jets. Tetairoa McMillan, CAR (vs. DEN) Tetairoa McMillan continues to offer dependable target volume, even when the yardage and touchdown production are not particularly impressive. He caught six of 11 targets for 58 yards in Carolina’s 27-19 loss to Green Bay on Thursday, providing a respectable performance for managers in PPR formats. The Packers did a good job limiting his ability to generate significant yardage, but McMillan’s involvement remained encouraging. He has now caught 30 passes over his last four games, averaging six receptions per contest across the season. The biggest concern is his recent lack of touchdowns. McMillan scored twice against Detroit in Week 4 but has not found the end zone since. That has limited his fantasy ceiling, particularly in standard scoring formats where receptions carry less value. Still, his consistent target volume makes him difficult to overlook. Carolina continues to feature him prominently in the passing game, giving him opportunities to produce even when opposing defenses limit his explosive plays. The Week 9 matchup against Denver will present another challenge. Still, McMillan remains a high-end WR2 in most formats. Managers should continue starting him, especially in PPR leagues, where his reception volume provides a dependable foundation. Final Takeaway Golden and Burden are attractive streaming options after encouraging performances, while Rice offers substantial upside if he is cleared to play. McMillan remains a dependable target-volume option despite his recent touchdown drought. Check the final injury reports, prioritize consistent involvement, and make your receiver decisions before these opportunities disappear.
