articles.title: Taylor Swift Called the ‘Fakest’ New York Knicks Fan by 2 of Team’s Players: ‘It’s a Little Performative’
articles.summary: "I'm gonna get some hate from the Swifties," Tyler Kolek acknowledged.
articles._body: After drawing ire from disgruntled football fans in 2023 who felt she was present at too many games, Taylor Swift has managed to irk men in another sport for apparently attending too few. New York Knicks point guards Tyler Kolek and Miles “Deuce” McBride recently criticized the pop star as the “fakest” fan of the 2026 NBA champions, accusing her and other celebrity row visitors of being “performative.” Related Travis Kelce ‘Can’t Wait’ to Make New Traditions With Taylor Swift on His First Christmas ‘As a Married Man’ Taylor Swift Made Sure She Didn’t ‘Kick Somebody Off’ of ‘Toy Story 5’ by Agreeing to Write the End Credits Song Seattle Seahawks Shade Taylor Swift & Travis Kelce After Ending Kansas City’s Undefeated Streak In a clip from an NBA 2K TikTok livestream Deflected posted Thursday (Nov. 5), the two men fiddled with game controllers while debating who they believe is the least authentic celebrity Knicks fan. “Maybe Taylor Swift,” Kolek said, to which McBride offered, “I would agree.” What defines a “fake” Knicks fan, in their eyes? “They just want to be seen at the game, they’re not necessarily fans,” Kolek noted. “I don’t know if I’ve seen her at any other games. I’m gonna get some hate from the Swifties. I guess she’s got a lot going on, so she can’t come all the time. But it’s a little performative.” “Swifties not gonna like that answer,” McBride said with a laugh as the two players shouted out Ben Stiller and Tracy Morgan for showing up consistently at Knicks games. “Everybody else [but Swift] is usually solid.” Billboard has reached out to Swift’s rep for comment. The 14-time Grammy winner was present at Game 4 of the NBA Finals, cheering on the Knicks alongside Mariska Hargitay and Este and Alana Haim in custom Knicks T-shirts. Before that, she also traveled with now-husband Travis Kelce to watch an away game against the Cleveland Cavaliers. It’s ironic that Swift — who, as Kolek generously pointed out, might’ve been a little busy this season, having been gearing up to release Billboard Hot 100 -topping song “I Knew It, I Knew You” for Toy Story 5 the same month of the NBA Finals, among other projects — is now getting flack for this reason. It wasn’t long ago that football fans expressed upset over the amount that she was seen at NFL games when she first started showing up to support Kelce. “I think we all know that if there’s one thing that male sports fans want to see in their spaces and on their screens,” Swift later sarcastically joked about the outrage in her 2025 cameo on New Heights , “it’s more of me.”

articles.title: Lil Baby’s ‘FRESH’: All 17 Tracks Ranked
articles.summary: See how Billboard ranks the new songs from Lil Baby's new album, FRESH.
articles._body: Lil Baby finds himself at an interesting point in his career. On one hand, he’s six years removed from his star-making My Turn era, and hasn’t had the same kind of hit records or released a critically acclaimed album since. Conversely, he has also amassed 160 Billboard Hot 100 entries (including 13 top 10s) throughout his career, as well as four consecutive Billboard 200 No. 1 albums, showing that his core audience and beyond have remained invested in what he puts out. In the music game, though, narratives are often just as impactful as numbers. So while one person may feel he is still highly successful, another may rightfully say he has lost steam since the massive “We Paid” with 42 Dugg, and his politically-charged anthem “The Bigger Picture.” As for Baby himself — per his recent comments on Popcast — he doesn’t even view what could be perceived as a “cold streak” as a slump. This year’s “Dead Fresh”, a top 20 song on the Billboard Hot 100, showed some people that even if he can’t catch lightning in a bottle again, he still has a little electricity in his arsenal. The true intrigue, for many, is: How can he evolve his style? What new stories does he have to tell? Was 2020-2022 just a run, or is he as good as he established himself then to be? His new album FRESH isn’t a major shift in his sound, and doesn’t reveal much new about him. But it is a reminder that he can rap well, and is among the best of this era within his tier of artists. There are some fun, inspired production choices, but, for the most part, Lil Baby remains who we have always known him to be. Check out our ranked list of the 17 tracks on FRESH below.

articles.summary: Stephen Curry couldn’t resist showing off his biggest smile when he found himself next to Klay Thompson during the Golden State Warriors’ matchup against the Miami Heat on Thursday night. The former Splash Brothers, who reunited at Chase Center for Thompson’s return, shared a hi
articles._body: Stephen Curry couldn’t resist showing off his biggest smile when he found himself next to Klay Thompson during the Golden State Warriors’ matchup against the Miami Heat on Thursday night. The former Splash Brothers, who reunited at Chase Center for Thompson’s return, shared a hilarious moment that quickly caught fans’ attention. With 6:03 remaining in the first quarter, Curry noticed a fan apparently trying to capture a photo of him alongside Thompson. The Warriors superstar immediately flashed a wide grin, pointed toward his former teammate, and gave an enthusiastic thumbs-up. The lighthearted interaction shared on X showed Curry happily posing while Thompson appeared focused on the action around him. The contrast between Curry’s exaggerated smile and Thompson’s serious expression made the moment even funnier. Steph Curry posed with Klay Thompson for a fan pic.twitter.com/3U27O09zcy — Fullcourtpass (@Fullcourtpass) November 6, 2026 The scene offered a nostalgic reminder of their legendary partnership in Golden State. Curry and Thompson spent 13 seasons together, winning four NBA championships and establishing themselves as one of basketball’s greatest shooting duos. Their reunion carried additional significance after Thompson joined Miami, giving fans another opportunity to see the former teammates share the court as opponents. The Warriors eventually secured a 120-100 victory, with Curry scoring 29 points to help Golden State extend its winning streak to six games. The matchup also produced plenty of entertaining moments, including Jimmy Butler’s playful Instagram post featuring Thompson after the win. For Curry, however, the brief photo opportunity showed that even competing against his longtime teammate couldn’t erase their familiar chemistry. The spontaneous exchange also reminded fans of the friendship Curry and Thompson built over the years, even as they now represent opposing teams. articles.title: State of the Art: Fashion Spent Its Holiday Budget on Animators
articles.summary: Fashion's holiday ads are going all in on animation, with Dior teaming up with Oscar-nominated director Sylvain Chomet and Prada tapping an ex-Disney artist.
articles._body: In State of the Art , a column for Highsnobiety, Chris Erik Thomas untangles the crossover between fashion and art. “Josh O’Connor as The Chair” and “Rihanna as The Lucky Star” are two sets of words I never thought I’d see flash before my eyes. Especially not within the opening credits of a fashion brand’s holiday ad. Yet this is no hallucination. Josh O’Connor really is Chair; Rihanna, a Lucky Star. (Or maybe we’re the lucky ones, for her agreeing to this?) Both have lent their vocal talents to an animated short film narrated by Robert Pattinson that also includes Greta Lee as one of the seamstress Bees, Camille Cottin as Marlene Dietrich, and Louis Garrel as… the inimitable Christian Dior. This level of stacked talent makes Christian Dior’s Night in Color the fashion film equivalent of The Odyssey , and that extends to the person behind the lens: French animator Sylvain Chomet, best known for his Oscar-nominated films The Triplets of Belleville and The Illusionist . It helps that nearly the entire cast happen to be Dior brand ambassadors, but there’s no denying that Jonathan Anderson — and, of course, Dior’s parent company LVMH — has popped off for the holidays. Or has it? In the days since the ad debuted, animators in the field have alleged that hand-drawn illustrations were brought to life using AI, noting hands with one too many fingers and other wonky details. Coming so soon after Prada's own holiday ad, which recruited veteran Disney animator John Pomeroy and included an extensive behind-the-scenes companion video of the animation process, Dior's effort feels disingenuous to those who believe it's AI-assisted. Whatever becomes of the short film, the fact that we're even debating it is a major step forward. Misstep or not, the idea that one of the world’s biggest luxury labels would blow its budget on an animated film would’ve felt like an aberration a few years ago. When Balenciaga partnered with The Simpsons in 2021 on a 10-minute “episode,” who could’ve guessed Marge pairing her blue ‘do with a bit of Demna couture would be the bellwether for a coming wave? The times, they have a-changed: Rimowa went stop-motion for its newest ads (with short films reportedly set to release later this month) and LOEWE announced a Nightmare Before Christmas collection, plus Our Legacy teased its first standalone Tokyo flagship store via a very Akira- coded anime . Every day our January declaration that this would be the year of the fashion illustrator feels more and more prescient. Animation and illustration have never been more prized in the industry, becoming key weapons in a brand’s “we love craft” arsenal — a repository that now includes everything from artisan awards like the Loewe Craft Prize and artist-fronted capsules like Lemaire’s Roland Topor collection to brand-backed print publications and sponsoring art shows, as Bottega Veneta has done for a Peggy Guggenheim exhibition opening this month in London. In this kind of climate, a stunty animated film feels like a slam-dunk return on investment. It helps that these campaigns tend to look great (and sometimes even better than the wonky visuals we’d get from actual animated features). And, in the case of Christian Dior’s Night in Color , the pairing is a perfect fit. Hand-drawing is a couture-level process in its own right, and the storyline draws on Dior’s very real history and lore: the designer really did call his atelier staff his bees, and he really did dress Dietrich for the silver screen. Fashion has always sold a fantasy, and few visual mediums are more fantastical than animation. This might be the closest we get to Dior becoming our next Disney, or Prada our Pixar. But either way, fashion ads have never felt more alive. Highsnobiety has affiliate marketing partnerships, which means we may receive a commission from your purchase. Want to shop the products our editors actually love? Visit our SHOPPER page and subscribe to the newsletter for recs on all things fashion, footwear, and beauty.

articles.title: Patriots’ TreVeyon Henderson releases statement detailing ‘unexpected’ medical emergency

Henderson released an official statement detailing the situation, explaining that he experienced a series of une
articles._body: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson shared a concerning health update after experiencing an unexpected medical emergency that required several days of hospitalization. Henderson released an official statement detailing the situation, explaining that he experienced a series of unexplained neurological symptoms. He underwent extensive medical testing and evaluation during his hospitalization, but doctors have not yet determined what caused the emergency. “While the results of my comprehensive medical testing have come back positive and reassuring, the cause of this remains unknown and unexplainable,” Henderson said. Although the test results have provided some reassurance, Henderson explained that the symptoms have affected his strength, coordination and other physical functions. He will continue working with specialists and physical therapists as he focuses on his recovery. “My health and long-term well-being remain my foremost priorities,” Henderson added. This is a scary situation for Henderson, his family, and everyone around the Patriots organization. The running back is still working through an unknown medical issue, and there are understandably more important things to focus on than football right now. The hope is that Henderson can make a full recovery and get back to feeling like himself. It is also important that doctors eventually identify what caused the symptoms so he and his medical team can better understand what happened and determine the best path forward. For now, Henderson’s health needs to come first. The positive test results are encouraging, but there is still uncertainty surrounding his condition. Hopefully, he gets the answers he needs and can focus on returning to full strength. articles.title: The killer mistake Lions must avoid at 2026 NFL trade deadline
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions are finally looking like an NFC juggernaut in 2026. Detroit is on a three-game winning streak after handing Minnesota their first loss of the season in Week 8. Now the Lions are in control of their own destiny at 5-2 and right in the thick of the NFC North division race. But [&#
articles._body: The Detroit Lions are finally looking like an NFC juggernaut in 2026. Detroit is on a three-game winning streak after handing Minnesota their first loss of the season in Week 8. Now the Lions are in control of their own destiny at 5-2 and right in the thick of the NFC North division race. But not everything is going in Detroit’s favor so far this season. Unfortunately, the defense is still a big issue in Detroit despite a handful of good performances. The Lions lost Jack Campbell to a scary injury last week and there’s no telling when he’ll be able to return. On top of that, DJ Reed and DJ Wonnum both picked up injuries last week and have not practiced this week. If there’s any good news, Brian Branch practiced on Thursday and Kerby Joseph was limited for two days in a row. The headline here is that defensive talent is still a problem for the Lions. Now that the team is looking competitive, it could make sense for GM Brad Holmes to hunt for some defensive players ahead of the NFL trade deadline. Should Detroit make a big move to add more players? Or should they take a more cautious approach to the trade deadline? There is one big mistake that the Lions need to avoid making at the trade deadline no matter what. Detroit cannot sacrifice their future to bring in a star at the trade deadline It may be tempting for the Lions to make a big move at the deadline. But they need to avoid sending away significant draft capital that could impact the organization’s future. One important factor here is Detroit’s salary cap situation. They do have some cap space next season with $62.08 million currently available . That does not account for potential extensions for Branch and Sam LaPorta, who are both on expiring contracts. Fortunately, the Lions are projected to have 10 picks in the 2027 NFL Draft and their full complement of picks in future drafts. That puts them in a strong position where they could swing one or two trades while still leaving enough picks to solidify their future. However, they’ll need to be bargain trades instead of blockbuster deals for star players. The reality is that star players often cost a lot and come with massive contracts. So adding another talented player like that doesn’t make a lot of sense for Detroit. If the Lions can find some bargain bin players to patch up the defense, they should be just fine. Ultimately, Detroit should not be willing to give up more than a third-round pick in any trade deadline move. Which players could be trade targets for the Lions? The Lions could actually do some last-minute scouting on a few Dolphins players in Week 9. Miami is one team that should feel comfortable selling players as they are in the middle of a complete rebuild. Their young talent may not be for sale, but they have plenty of veterans who could give the Lions a boost. Jordyn Brooks is arguably the tempting option for Detroit. The Lions may need linebacker help with Campbell sidelined, and Brooks is a tackling machine. However, he is under contract for multiple seasons so the Lions would need to really fall in love with him to bring him in. Another option is cornerback JuJu Brents . The fourth-year cornerback is on the final year of his rookie contract. That’s a good thing for Detroit, as it gives them the flexibility to only bring him on as a one-year patch. But if he proves himself to the coaching staff, Detroit could sign him to an extension. Perhaps more importantly, it means that Brents would likely be a cheap acquisition. Other players Lions fans should keep an eye on include Chargers cornerback Donte Jackson and Commanders cornerback Mike Sainristil. Chiefs’ Rashee Rice claims he owes nearly $3.5 million in debts stemming largely from car crash, assault allegations
articles.summary: The effects of Rashee Rice’s car crash and assault allegations have resulted in the Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver filing for bankruptcy due to his debts. Rice filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy (which is for “individuals who have financial difficulty preventing them from paying their d
articles._body: The effects of Rashee Rice’s car crash and assault allegations have resulted in the Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver filing for bankruptcy due to his debts. Rice filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy (which is for “individuals who have financial difficulty preventing them from paying their debts and who are willing to allow their non-exempt property to be used to pay their creditors”) on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. He claims to have more than $3.45 million in debts (via ESPN). He filed in the Northern District of Texas bankruptcy court. He alleges that over $2.1 million of his debts are from various plaintiffs suing him in civil litigations, which have either been settled or are still waiting on a trail. His role in a 2024 high-speed multi-car crash has resulted in him being sued by several individuals. Additionally, one of his ex-girlfriends has sued him for allegedly repeatedly assaulting her from 2023 to 2025. The Chiefs star claims to have $677,054 in personal assets (he claimed $39,241 of it to be nonexempt). Among the “personal assets” is $421,825 in “deferred compensation.” He also has $13,640 in his checking accounts and rents a residence (though he claims to not own any property). However, he still owes his largest creditor $979,837. This is tied to the civil settlement reached related to the crash in 2025. Rice is also disputing potential debts in some of the civil trials. He is reportedly using his Super Bowl championship ring as collateral with his attorney in the pending civil litigation, Thomas McMurray. The ring is valued at $160,000. Rice has missed two of the Chiefs’ games this year. He has 20 receptions for 243 yards and two touchdowns in the five games he has played. The Chiefs lost their last game to the Denver Broncos. They are hoping to rebound in Week 9 when they host the New York Jets. Gang Green is coming off a heartbreaking loss to the Las Vegas Raiders last week. articles._body: Adria Petty says an anniversary, to her, is “a very uncool marketing thing.” But this year’s 50th anniversary of the self-titled debut album by her father, the late Tom Petty, and his band the Heartbreakers was too good of a storytelling opportunity to pass up. “I really want to acknowledge the Heartbreakers this year, ’cause they’re all alive and have achieved so much and are still going strong now,” Petty — who co-produced the new box set Origins 1971-78 — tells Billboard via Zoom from California. “This anniversary is really important to us. It’s really important to us that everybody gets their flowers when they’re still alive…. ( Origins ) is the musical diagram to how Tom became Tom and the Heartbreakers and how they found their way to this music.” Out Friday (Nov. 6), Origins represents a two-year undertaking that dove deep into Petty and the Heartbreakers’ vaults, primarily conducted by the Petty Legacy LLC brain trust which also includes longtime producer/engineer Ryan Ulyate and managers Will Botwin and Scott Greer. The multi-disc set includes new mixes of Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers and 1978’s You’re Gonna Get It! (with extended versions of some of the tracks), an unreleased Live From the Record Plant 1977 performance and videos from the BBC’s Old Grey Whistle Test in 1978. The focal point, however, is No Sleep Til L.A ., which features a dozen early tracks from 1971-77 — recorded by the pre-Heartbreakers band Mudcrutch and Petty solo in addition to the Heartbreakers — as well as five more included on an EP dubbed The Cut Out Bin . Those will also be issued as a separate, individual album as well as on the box set. “This body of work, to me, is sort of a Rosetta Stone for rock ‘n’ roll in a weird way,” explains Adria Petty, a music video and commercial director in addition to her Petty Legacy role. Since Tom Petty’s death in 2017 at the age of 66, she’s also co-produced archival projects. “They could take it to reggae, they could take it to disco, they could take it to soul, they could really take it to country rock — this, that or the other. They went their own way and became an amalgam of all that. They were just experimenting, making noise together that they liked. My responsibility here is to point out the cultural importance, that during disco, during their aftermath of Vietnam, these guys blazed their own trail and kept it going for 50 years.” Heartbreakers keyboardist Benmont Tench, who was also part of Mudcrutch along with Petty and guitarist Mike Campbell, confirms via Zoom from his home that before the first Heartbreakers album, “We were searching. I think ( No Sleep Til L.A./The Cut Out Bin ) is nice because you can hear where Tom is listening to some country stuff and also listening to R&B and to Van Morrison. And the rest of us are just going, ‘Oh, this fits around what he’s saying’ and playing it. Mudcrutch and the Heartbreakers were both great bands,” he says. “From the first minute of the Heartbreakers it was really natural and easy, and the first couple of records are the sound of us finding out what we could do. You can hear the excitement, us going, ‘Oh, this is good!'” Stan Lynch, the Heartbreakers’ drummer from 1976-94, adds that the material provides an accurate snapshot of the band at that time. “What I hear as I listen now is those are some old souls, boys doing men’s work,” he says. “We were driven. We were desperate. We were hungry — and we were good. We weren’t messing around. We didn’t care about anything but the music. We were just feral in those days, and you can hear that.” Rocking Around With You Ulyate, who met Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers via Jeff Lynne and began working full-time with 2008’s Mudcrutch reunion album, says that once he got the word about the Origins project from Adria Petty, “My job was just to go through every tape that we had — and there’s a lot.” That meant cataloging “every multi-track tape they made from 1971-78,” which he says was probably more than 100. Ulyate was also insistent that “I wanted to make sure people heard this in the best way possible, so we didn’t find a bunch of cassettes or bootlegs.” That was a slight disappointment for Tench, who had a set of Mudcrutch demos recorded in his family’s living room back in Gainesville, Fla., that he offered for consideration. “It sounded like a 45 from a band in Detroit in 1968 to me,” he says. “I was told the fidelity wasn’t good enough, and I’m like, ‘That’s the point!’” But Tench adds, “I still love it. I always like it if we can find something good and we can put out something good. I don’t want to ever get to the point where we put out unreleased stuff that’s like, ‘Oh, I can see why this wasn’t released.'” Adria Petty says that “five or six times” more than the 17 unreleased tracks were considered for Origins , with a good deal of discussion and debate among the production team. She herself was outvoted on the inclusion of the yacht-rock-style track “Save Me,” but there was great consensus about others, including “Parade of Loons,” which the Heartbreakers recorded between the first two albums, the goofy “Sin City,” the reggae-tinged “You’re Gonna Learn” and Tom Petty’s solo acoustic rendition of “Unheard of Kind of Hero,” which dates back to 1976. No Sleep Til L.A . also includes original recordings of Mudcrutch songs such as “I Can’t Fight It,” “Depot Street” and “Up in Mississippi Tonight” that were included on the 1995 compilation Playba

College Football’s Loaded Saturday Sets Up Huge Day for ABC, ESPN
articles.summary: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images
articles._body: Multiview will be a necessity for college football fans on Saturday. The highly anticipated Week 10 slate marks the first time in nine years that seven matchups on the same day all feature both teams ranked in the top 25 of the College Football Playoff rankings . The biggest winners among the TV networks are the Disney-owned ABC and ESPN, which together will broadcast five of those games. Here’s the lineup of Saturday’s marquee games: Noon: No. 9 BYU at No. 3 Utah (ABC) Noon: No. 7 Texas–No. 18 Missouri (ESPN) Noon: No. 8 UCLA–Minnesota (Fox) 3:30: No. 5 Alabama–No. 14 LSU (ABC) 3:30: No. 23 Oregon–No. 12 Ohio State (CBS) 6:15: No. 6 Kentucky–No. 13 Tennessee (ESPN) 7:30: No. 1 Miami–No. 11 Notre Dame (NBC) 7:30: No. 2 Georgia–No. 10 Ole Miss (ABC) “It just sort of all came together perfectly,” ESPN senior director of programming and acquisitions Kurt Dargis tells Front Office Sports . ESPN knew its platforms would likely have multiple strong Week 10 matchups from the time the SEC’s schedule came out in December. It then acquired the top pick for this week’s Big 12 matchups in its TV draft with Fox back in the spring—but wasn’t exactly counting on BYU-Utah having the relevance it does. “For it to turn out to be a top-10 matchup, I think that might have been a little bit of a stretch to think that we were going to get that,” Dargis says. BYU-Utah was slotted into the noon ET window (which means a 10 a.m. local kickoff) last week, but wasn’t put on ABC until after both teams won in Week 9. Had both or even either lost last weekend, Dargis says, then Texas-Missouri very likely could have gotten the prime network slot. Meanwhile, Fox’s Big Noon Saturday window will feature undefeated UCLA looking to keep its position atop the Big Ten playing at Minnesota. Head-to-Head Battles In the spring, CBS used its first pick in its Big Ten TV draft on Oregon–Ohio State, which initially looked like it could be the matchup of the season as the Buckeyes were the No. 1–ranked team in the preseason AP Top 25 poll and the Ducks were No. 2. But Oregon (5–3) is all but out of the CFP picture and Ohio State (6–2) is on the bubble. With the dampened hype around that Big Ten matchup, even more eyes should be on Alabama-LSU at 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC, which will lead into the network’s primetime clash with NBC, featuring Georgia–Ole Miss going head-to-head with Miami–Notre Dame. “We liked the idea of hopefully getting—even starting back with BYU-Utah in the moon window—just building, building, building throughout the day,” Dargis says. “Alabama-LSU in the middle is as good a matchup of brands and high rankings that you could get—hopefully get a really, really big number there—and just let that flow right into the Georgia–Ole Miss game in primetime.” NBC’s pregame College Countdown show that typically airs at 7 p.m. ET ahead of Notre Dame and other major 7:30 kickoffs on the network will start 30 minutes early at 6:30 p.m. on Peacock with expanded coverage ahead of the Fighting Irish’s primetime telecast. ESPN’s College GameDay pregame show is airing from South Bend, Ind., on Saturday, after already traveling to five SEC locations and both BYU and Utah this season. The big day of matchups arrives as college football viewership this season is down 11% across all Nielsen-rated networks. The post College Football’s Loaded Saturday Sets Up Huge Day for ABC, ESPN appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.summary:
Hello HN, I'm Nik. I built Infinity for myself because I tend to love to rabbit-hole on various subjects.

I usually have 3-4 windows open for ChatGPT desktop + Claude + Ollama. Typically, I'd ask a question, see something interesting in the answer, and then keep expanding on it. The mental chai
articles._body: Hello HN, I'm Nik. I built Infinity for myself because I tend to love to rabbit-hole on various subjects. I usually have 3-4 windows open for ChatGPT desktop + Claude + Ollama. Typically, I'd ask a question, see something interesting in the answer, and then keep expanding on it. The mental chain of thought eventually gets lost and I would start from scratch again. Second, I also wanted to compare answers across multiple models. From there, pick and use the best one and continue. So I built Infinity for myself. Multiple windows, multiple chats. Projects all aligned in one place. But the best part is when you start highlighting any part of the response - you can branch off and fork into new chat sessions from there without losing your original chain of thought. It's a native Mac app written in Swift. You can use all the popular cloud models that you already pay for but on top of that, you can use local models as well. You can even set out what each model's job is and assign certain models for certain jobs. It's free, there's no account, no analytics on the actual app. Everything is stored locally. Just download, connect up, and get going. Still extremely early but if there is interest, would love to hear what works and what doesn't! It’s too early to tell if it will hold, but so far, so good. One of those giving
articles._body: No one is surprised: the Philadelphia 76ers are on an absolute roll . They are off to an 8-1 start led by a superstar lineup that includes LeBron James, Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, and VJ Edgecombe. It’s too early to tell if it will hold, but so far, so good. One of those giving credit where credit is due is former 76ers coach Doc Rivers, per The Bill Simmons Podcast. He told Simmons he believed no one could stop them, at least for now. “They’re the best team in the NBA,” Rivers said. “They’re gonna be hard to beat.” Doc Rivers says the Sixers are the best team in the NBA right now. “They're the best team in the NBA. They're gonna be hard to beat.” pic.twitter.com/B31EWx3tEo — NBABase (@TheNBABase) November 6, 2026 Rivers coached in Philadelphia from 2020 to 2023. During that time, Rivers finished 154-82 with a 20-15 playoff record. However, the 76ers suffered three straight first-round losses, leading to Rivers being fired in 2023 . Afterward, Rivers coached the Milwaukee Bucks from 2024 to 2026. It ultimately led to a losing record and two early playoff exits in 2024 and 2025. In 2026, Rivers stepped down as the Bucks finished 32-50. At the same time, the Miami Heat snatched up Giannis Antetokounmpo. Meanwhile, the 76ers are dominating not only on offense, but also on defense. They allow opponents only 105.1 points per game and have a defensive rating of 105.4. Furthermore, Maxey has emerged as their clutch performer during crunch time. James, Brown, and Embiid’s veteran leadership and presence have gelled well. It also helps that head coach Nick Nurse is facilitating such an elaborate operation. On Friday, the 76ers will face the Cleveland Cavaliers on the road at 6:30pm CST/7:30pm EST. articles.title: Could potential AI clones of GTA VI force a quicker official port?
articles.summary: A former Rockstar tech director thinks the developer is facing new time pressures.
articles._body: Yesterday, when reporting on emerging efforts to pipe the console version of GTA VI through a PC's DLSS-powered Nvidia GPU , we mentioned in passing that PC players could instead just wait for the AI-assisted decompilation port that will no doubt be coming in short order. Now, a former Rockstar tech director says he thinks that exact threat could cause the developer to work faster on the official PC version of its soon-to-release crime/lifestyle simulator. Obbe Vermeij hasn't worked at Rockstar since 2009 , but in a new interview with Rock Paper Shotgun , he recalled how artists for the PC version of the original top-down Grand Theft Auto were incensed when the console version squashed the game's 256-color textures down to 16 colors for the PS1 release. "So it always has been that sort of awkward relationship between PC and the console," Vermeij said. "So in those days, it was like PC first and then console second, even though that didn't really make much sense for the sales, because the PlayStation versions sold way better." articles._body: UFC Vegas 124: Cortes-Acosta vs. Walker headlines the card with a five-round heavyweight fight between Waldo Cortes-Acosta and Johnny Walker. Check out our UFC Vegas 124 odds series for our Cortes-Acosta-Walker prediction and pick. Waldo Cortes-Acosta (17-4) steps into the Octagon looking to snap consecutive decision losses to Alexander Volkov and Curtis Blaydes that followed his second-round stoppage of Derrick Lewis, as he comes into his fight this weekend against Johnny Walker. Johnny Walker (23-10) recently made a explosive heavyweight debut by knocking out Mick Parkin with a clinch knee at UFC 332. That win followed a split decision loss to Dominick Reyes at light heavyweight as he comes into his fight this weekend against Waldo Cortes-Acosta. UFC Vegas 124 Odds, courtesy of DraftKings UFC Vegas 124 Odds: Waldo Cortes-Acosta-Johnny Walker Odds Waldo Cortes-Acosta: -230 Johnny Walker: +190 Over 1.5 rounds: -220 Under 1.5 rounds: +170 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Why Waldo Cortes-Acosta Will Win Waldo Cortes-Acosta holds the more reliable path to victory over Johnny Walker at UFC Vegas 124 this weekend. His durable frame and heavier punches should make the early exchanges far more dangerous for Walker. Walker enters with a questionable chin and a reputation for fading when pressure builds. Cortes-Acosta has absorbed huge shots from top heavyweights and kept walking forward. The Dominican fighter also owns a clear volume advantage, landing over five significant strikes per minute. Walker’s longer reach helps, but he often leaves his chin elevated when throwing his looping offense. If Walker rushes forward, Cortes-Acosta can counter with straight rights and shoves against the fence. His clinch control should blunt the Brazilian’s knees and make every exchange feel physically taxing. Five rounds also favor the heavier man in a short-notice contest. Expect Cortes-Acosta to wear down Walker with patient pressure and body work, then take a decision or late stoppage. Why Johnny Walker Will Win Johnny Walker has the kind of explosive creativity that can end a heavyweight fight in one moment. His 82-inch reach and unpredictable angles give Cortes-Acosta problems he rarely sees. Walker looked sharper and more comfortable at heavyweight against Mick Parkin. That clinch knee showed his speed remains dangerous against larger opponents. Cortes-Acosta has dropped two straight decisions and appears to have lost some of his earlier momentum. Walker can exploit that hesitation by throwing first and using lateral movement. The Brazilian does not need to win every minute because a single spinning shot or knee can change the fight. He is also more accurate on the feet, landing roughly 59 percent of significant strikes. Walker should avoid long fence battles and punish Cortes-Acosta whenever he reaches in with the jab. Expect an early blast that wobbles the favorite and produces a first-round knockout. Final Cortes-Acosta-Walker Prediction & Pick Waldo Cortes-Acosta has the stronger chin, better pace, and clearer plan for a five-round heavyweight fight. He also has the more repeatable offense against a short-notice opponent who has only one heavyweight fight. Walker remains the biggest danger because he can find a finish from nowhere. Even so, Cortes-Acosta has shown he can survive huge shots and keep walking forward. The best outcome is a measured fight where Cortes-Acosta uses clinch work and body shots to slow Walker. That should drain the Brazilian’s explosiveness and reduce the chances of a lucky knockout. Cortes-Acosta has gone the distance often in the UFC, so the fight should not collapse into a quick finish. Expect him to control the middle rounds, absorb Walker’s early bursts, and take a clear decision. Grant remains tough, but his experience may not be enough against a young fighter with this much athleticism. The main danger for Smith is falling into a long striking exchange with a pressure fighter. Grant’s volume and toughness can steal rounds if Smith loses patience. Smith’s wrestling gives him a cleaner path. He can mix takedown threats with punches and keep Grant from settling into his rhythm. A finish looks likelier than a long decision because Smith has proven finishing instincts and Grant has been vulnerable to sharp striking. Expect Smith to land the cleaner shots, pressure the veteran, and stop him late. articles.title: Over a quarter of Gen Z say they’d choose their dream home over their dream job—and they’re moving back in with mom and dad to make it happen
articles.summary: Gen Z is willing to put career ambitions on the back burner to achieve the American Dream of homeownership.
articles._body: Gen Zers are so desperate to get a home of their own they’re increasingly willing to make trade-offs—even if it means putting opportunities on the back burner and moving back in with mom and dad. Around 28% of Gen Z adults say they would choose their dream home over their dream job, according to new Harris Poll data commissioned by Coldwell Banker Real Estate. About 92% of the young generation who aren’t homeowners want to buy one day—even if it means setting aside other big life goals. And to make it happen amid a stifling cost-of-living crisis, many are settling down in their childhood bedrooms; more than three-quarters of Gen Zers have moved in or considered living with their parents or in-laws to save up for a home.  They’re part of a growing number of young Americans putting off traditional milestones of adulthood, as living with family becomes a more practical and increasingly culturally accepted way to get ahead financially. “Gen Z is telling us loud and clear that owning a home is still the milestone that says you’ve made it,” Mary Lee Blaylock, president of Coldwell Banker Affiliates, tells Fortune in a written comment . “Many are moving back in with family and making real sacrifices now because they see homeownership as the foundation for the life they want to build.” Despite how out-of-reach homeownership can look, it’s still an integral achievement for people to feel like they’ve made it; around 85% surveyed said owning a home is part of the American Dream for most Americans, unchanged from 2025, according to the Coldwell report. Knowing how difficult it is to buy, some young families are already planning ahead so their kids don’t face the same hurdles. Around 85% of Gen Z and 82% of millennial parents have started saving for a child’s home down-payment, or at least considered it. Why Gen Z and young millennials are delaying their move-out A record 25.2 million U.S. adults under the age of 35 lived with their parents in 2025—representing about one in three young adults—according to a 2026 report from Realtor.com. It was even higher than the pandemic-era surge, when many budding professionals returned home to ride out the pandemic with their loved ones. However, it doesn’t mean that Gen Zers and young millennials are jobless and mooching off their family resources.  In fact, around 70% of 25 to 34-year-olds who still live at home with their parents are actually employed, according to the report. Plus, around 72% of young adults who live with their parents say they contribute financially to the household in some sort of way, according to 2024 data from Pew Research. About 46% contribute toward rent or the mortgage, while 65% put in money towards the family groceries, utilities, or other household expenses. But many have found they can’t fly the coop just yet, as pay increases have failed to keep pace with skyrocketing housing costs.  In 2025, the median American home price was $430,000, up 34.4% from 2019, according to the Realtor.com report. Meanwhile, average monthly rent shot up by 17.9% to $1,673. And a housing shortage of roughly 4 million homes is only exacerbating the issue. Instead of kicking back, most workers are postponing their move-out plans thanks to an affordability crisis pinching the wallets of everyday Americans. And as professionals on the lowest rung of the corporate totem pole, their rock-bottom salaries, job instability, and lack of savings may be keeping them home. The American Dream has changed: ‘We are going to start looking a lot more like Europe’ For younger Americans, moving back in with their parents is no longer necessarily a temporary detour on the path to independence. Instead, it may be a longer-term lifestyle shift, as the financial and cultural barriers to multigenerational living continue to fall. “Now since rates have been going up and affordability remains very stretched, we’re seeing [multigenerational living] increase,” Ivy Zelman, cofounder and executive vice president at housing research firm Zelman, a Walker & Dunlop Company, said during a roundtable discussion Fortune attended earlier this year. “We assume that it’s going to stay fairly stable as we continue into the second half of the decade.” The proportion of adults in their twenties and thirties living at home has continued to rise in recent years, and shows no sign of letting up. Back in 1980, only around 15% of these younger adults opted to live with their parents.  Now, around 22.4% of Gen Zers and millennials are bunkering down with their families, according to recent data from Zelman. And the real estate firm predicts that number won’t budge by 2030. Echoing the Realtor.com data, Zelman also found that young adults face a cost-of-living crisis and lackluster salary increases; only 44% of 20- to 39-year-olds could afford their median local rent. And beyond affordability, the firm noted that a cultural change is underway.  “We also believe that there’s a secular shift in how people are living,” Zelman continued, explaining that when you look “at young adults today that are happy or content living with their parents, the negative stigma is really no longer prevalent. We are going to start looking a lot more like Europe: multigenerational living.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Strive (ASST) Posts $474.8 Million Common Net Income as Bitcoin Yield Hits 63.2%
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Strive (ASST) Posts $474.8 Million Common Net Income as Bitcoin Yield Hits 63.2% Strive reported $474.8 million of net income attributable to common stockholders for the third quarter ended Sept. 30, a print that arrived Friday alongside a company claim that Class A total return had outperformed bitcoin by 103.7% year to date through the same date. GAAP net income was $509.0 million, or $5.24 a share on a fully diluted basis. Almost all of that came from a $533.7 million unrealized gain on digital assets marked to fair value. Operating revenue for the quarter was just $2.7 million, so the earnings line is a treasury mark, not a fee business. In a post on X that led with the outperformance figure, Strive also highlighted a year-to-date bitcoin yield of 63.2% and a bitcoin dollar gain of $9.00 per assumed diluted share outstanding, both measured through Sept. 30. Chairman and CEO Matthew Cole tied those metrics to the stock’s relative showing against the asset. “Strive has continued to successfully execute on its treasury management strategy, delivering a strong bitcoin yield year to date in 2026, which I believe is the primary driver of our common equity’s outperformance relative to Bitcoin so far this year,” Cole said in the earnings release. Bitcoin yield, buys and the preferred stack Bitcoin yield, as Strive defines it, is the percentage change in bitcoin per share over a period — not a cash yield. On that measure the company posted 18.5% in the third quarter alone and 19.3% from Oct. 1 through Oct. 30, after the SATS preferred debut. Strive acquired 8,136 bitcoin in the third quarter at an average cost of about $78,885 and 20,373 bitcoin over the nine months ended Sept. 30. Another 15,124 coins followed between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30. Holdings stood at 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 and 43,124 by Oct. 30, keeping Strive among the largest public corporate stacks after recent multi-thousand-coin buys and smaller weekly adds that still trailed Strategy . Digital assets at fair value were $2.34 billion on the Sept. 30 balance sheet. Cash had risen to $490.4 million by Oct. 30, and Strive still held Strategy’s variable-rate STRC preferred with a fair value of about $50.1 million. The capital stack that funded the buys is mostly perpetual preferreds. On Oct. 20 Strive closed a registered offering of 7 million shares of its 15% Series A perpetual preferred (SATS) for about $609 million in net proceeds. Preferred dividends of $34.2 million in the quarter are what turned the $509.0 million GAAP profit into the $474.8 million common figure. Strip the story to nine-month GAAP and the picture flips. For the nine months ended Sept. 30, Strive posted a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $88.4 million. The third-quarter profit is real under fair-value accounting, but it is concentrated in one mark-to-market line. What ASST stock has done over the past year ASST itself has not moved in a straight line with the company’s bitcoin-yield scoreboard. Shares closed at $20.59 on Thursday, down about 10% on the day, and traded near $20.70 early Friday. That leaves the stock roughly 29% below its level a year earlier, when Yahoo Finance data put the close near $29, and about 33% under its Oct. 21 local high of $30.75. The 52-week range on Yahoo Finance runs from $7.02 to $34.40. Year to date, the price path from the Jan. 2 close near $17.30 into the mid-$20s is a gain of roughly 20%, with a February low near the 52-week floor and a September push back toward $30. Through Sept. 30 — the cutoff on Strive’s outperformance claim — ASST had risen about 70% from that January close while bitcoin was down roughly 7% over the same window on Yahoo Finance data, a wide gap even before the company’s own total-return methodology. The longer chart still carries the scar of 2025, when Asset Entities became the public shell for Strive’s bitcoin-treasury reverse merger and the share price spiked into triple digits on weekly closes before collapsing. Investors who held through that conversion saw a different ride than the tidy year-to-date relative-return figure Strive put at the top of Friday’s note. Cole said the recent SATS issuance leaves Strive “never been in a better position to generate long-term returns in excess of Bitcoin for our common equity shareholders.” The test for ASST from here is whether another quarter of bitcoin yield and preferred-funded buys can reopen the gap to bitcoin after a year in which the stock still sits well below where it traded twelve months ago, even as the treasury has climbed past 30,000 then 40,000 bitcoin . This post Strive (ASST) Posts $474.8 Million Common Net Income as Bitcoin Yield Hits 63.2% first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .

articles.title: Some Gen Z Trump voters switched sides over what one calls an ‘egregious betrayal’ on the economy and war
articles.summary: Home prices rose 30% while young households’ income grew 9%. Gen Z voters explain their midterm votes that drove a "blue wave."
articles._body: Ryan Wharton normally doesn’t vote. But at a low point last year, the 28-year-old PR professional and freelance journalist found himself cashing in his pennies and quarters at a Coinstar machine for dollars he could spend on medication and groceries. This time, the Texas resident voted for Democrats up and down the ticket. He told Fortune the economy under President Donald Trump had left him feeling completely hopeless. He struggles to imagine a future in which Gen Zers like him can live what he considers a “normal life.” Texas delivered one of the biggest upsets of a wave election for Democrats. State Rep. James Talarico beat Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton by double digits , becoming the first Democrat to win a U.S. Senate race in Texas since 1988. Democrat Gina Hinojosa unseated Gov. Greg Abbott . Across the country, Democrats flipped seven Republican-held Senate seats, including in Iowa, Ohio, and South Carolina, to take control of the chamber. In Kansas, Methodist pastor Adam Hamilton defeated Sen. Roger Marshall , the first time Kansans have sent a Democrat to the Senate since 1932. Young voters led the shift. About 7 in 10 voters under 30 backed the Democrat in their local House race, according to The AP Voter Poll , a survey of more than 100,000 voters, after many in their generation supported Trump in 2024. The economy was at the center. About 4 in 10 voters overall named it the top issue facing the country. Gen Z has borne the brunt of the affordability crisis, squeezed by inflation and rising costs just as they’re trying to build their lives. In October, 91% of young registered voters told the Harvard Youth Poll that the cost of living mattered in their vote. Fortune spoke to six young people across the country and across the political spectrum and heard the same core frustration: the future they were promised feels like it’s slipping further away, replaced by deep disillusionment with how the economy works today. Polling suggests that anger isn’t aimed only at Washington; young voters across party lines also say they’re worried about corporate power. Prices are outrunning paychecks For many Gen Z voters, affording even the essentials has become nearly impossible. Between 2019 and 2024, the median home price rose 30%, while the median income of households headed by adults under 40 grew just 9%, according to the Pew Research Center . This year, the war with Iran pushed gasoline prices higher and fed inflation . Entry-level work is harder to find, too. The unemployment rate for recent college graduates held at 5.6% this summer, above the rate for all workers, according to Federal Reserve Bank of New York data cited in Fortune ’s reporting on Gen Z graduates . Wharton told Fortune he’s been in “survival mode 24/7.” “I’m always having to handle a new crisis. If it’s not groceries, it’s medication, and then God forbid, an unexpected expense like my dog’s vet bill comes up,” he said. “It just feels like I’m running out of time.” A protest vote, not an endorsement Wharton leans liberal. But even some Republican voters crossed party lines, citing the economy and the war in Iran. Peter, a 26-year-old from Ohio who asked to be identified only by his first name, said he voted for Trump in 2024 but switched to Democrats in this year’s midterms because of what he called Trump’s “betrayal” on the economy and war. “I genuinely cannot think of a more direct and egregious betrayal by a political candidate than running on a campaign of ‘no new wars’ and ‘fixing the economy,’ then destroying the economy for a foreign war,” he wrote to Fortune . He made clear he didn’t switch because he prefers Democrats. He wanted to send Republicans a message. “To be honest, I don’t actually think Democrats are the better choice. I voted because I wanted this midterm to send a message: if you, as a U.S. president, get us into another foreign war, your presidency is DONE,” Peter wrote. He isn’t alone in his ambivalence. The AP Voter Poll found the Democratic Party only modestly more popular than the GOP . Sophia Robertson, student chair of the Harvard Public Opinion Project, which conducts the Harvard Youth Poll, told Fortune that Democrats should be cautious about reading the results as a mandate. “A lot of people are angry about the state of the economy, about disruption, about all of these top issues, about international conflicts,” Robertson says. “But that doesn’t mean they’re affirmatively excited about the Democratic Party.” “The system that was set up may not be supporting Gen Z” The biggest takeaway from the young people who spoke to Fortune : they don’t believe the system is set up for them to succeed. Amrita Bhasin, a 25-year-old sustainability startup founder from California, believes the status quo wasn’t built for her generation to thrive. “I think Gen Z is realizing that the system that was set up may not be supporting Gen Z, and the question is, what are our politicians going to do about that?” Megan, a 27-year-old personal trainer from Texas, feels none of her representatives, including the president, have offered a solution to the cost of living, which squeezes her even on a $70,000 salary. Alex, a 28-year-old budtender at a dispensary in Alaska, still can’t afford health insurance, doesn’t qualify for Medicaid yet, and feels trapped by the cost of living. Both women asked to be identified only by their first names. “I live with my boyfriend and his mom because, at 28, even with his good-paying job, we can’t quite save up enough for a place that’s decent,” she told Fortune . She ties those costs to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, the tax-and-spending law Trump signed in July 2025, and to the state’s Republican leaders. “Most of all, I don’t want to see Dan Sullivan and Mike Dunleavy come into power again; they cut state funding all across the board from Medicaid to schools, and I’m sick of it.” As of Thursday,

articles.summary: Trademark Property Company and Morgan broke ground yesterday on a 362-unit Class A multifamily community at 3900 Lemmon Avenue in Dallas’ Oak Lawn neighborhood, adjacent to Turtle Creek. The first re
articles._body: Trademark Property Company and Morgan broke ground yesterday on a 362-unit Class A multifamily community at 3900 Lemmon Avenue in Dallas’ Oak Lawn neighborhood, adjacent to Turtle Creek. The first residences are expected to be completed in fall 2028, with full delivery in the second quarter of 2029. Costs for the project are estimated at $100 million. The land was previously owned by H-E-B. The community will feature a rooftop pool and outdoor spa; a fitness center with a private studio, sauna and cold plunge; a pocket park with preserved trees; two additional courtyards; a clubroom and coffee bar; coworking areas; a golf simulator and virtual gaming area. Residences will offer dens, balconies, or large private patios, and select ground-level homes will have street-facing stoops and private yards. Morgan will serve as the project’s developer, general contractor and property manager. The project team also includes GFF as architect. articles.title: Men’s College Soccer Calendar Change Roundly Rejected by Schools
articles.summary: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images
articles._body: The NCAA’s latest attempt to move Division-I men’s soccer to a fall-to-spring calendar has failed after hundreds of schools rejected the proposal. Goal first reported Thursday evening that at least 241 schools had voted against the proposal, but the news didn’t become official until 5 p.m. ET on Friday. On Friday, Goal reported that a total of 247 D-1 schools voted to rescind the proposal, with 106 of them not having men’s soccer teams. The NCAA confirmed shortly afterward that enough schools voted to rescind the proposal, and D-1 men’s soccer would remain a fall sport. Men’s college soccer currently plays in the fall from August to December. Advocates for the new calendar argue that the current schedule doesn’t give players enough time to rest between matches and travel. On Oct. 7, the DI Cabinet approved a plan that beginning in 2027–28 would see games run from August through Thanksgiving, then, after a winter break, resume in February, culminating in a spring championship. This calendar would align with European soccer as well as the new MLS format coming next year. On the day of the vote, U.S. Soccer CEO JT Batson celebrated the decision, calling it “exciting news for the future of the American soccer pathway.” The DI Cabinet didn’t reach enough support internally—it needed 75% approval—to pass the new proposal outright. That sparked a 30-day window for all D-I schools to vote against the plan, even schools that don’t sponsor a men’s varsity soccer team. The opposition needed two-thirds of D-I institutions, or 241 schools, to overturn the change. It hit that number Thursday night, according to multiple outlets, and climbed to 242 schools by Friday morning, The Athletic reported. Maryland head coach Sasho Cirovski, who has strongly backed the proposal, said on Thursday afternoon that 41 of the then–most recent 50 votes against the plan came from schools without a varsity men’s soccer program. Florida Gulf Coast athletic director Brian Barrio, who oversees a men’s soccer team, posted on Thursday that the “half-baked” proposal, which he says came from coaches, happened “without any consideration of the impact on our other student-athletes who share facilities and support staff” with men’s soccer. “Without any consideration of the impact on those already overworked support staffs,” Barrio wrote , “ADs need to think about 15-30 other sports, not just soccer.” Top Coaches Want Two-Semester Plan Despite the overwhelming vote against the change, schools with strong men’s soccer programs are largely in support of the new calendar. On Thursday, several top-ranked schools gave Front Office Sports favorable opinions on the NCAA’s proposal, including No. 7 Portland, No. 8 Louisville, No. 9 West Virginia, No. 11 Maryland, No. 15 Wake Forest, and No. 17 North Carolina. “The data clearly shows that the current model is not serving the best interests of student-athlete wellness or development,” No. 3 Clemson head coach Mike Noonan told FOS . “At the end of the day, aren’t our student athletes the reason we have jobs in the first place?” No. 12 University of Missouri-Kansas City coach Ryan Pore said he “strongly” supports the proposal because he believes “it is the right step forward for our student-athletes and the future” of soccer. “We need to continue evolving the college game, putting our student-athletes first, and creating an environment that allows the sport to reach its full potential nationally,” Pore said. No. 5 Akron head coach Jared Embick, who told FOS he supports the plan, acknowledged that it could be rescinded. “I know the coaches will keep trying to move Men’s college soccer forward in the future and hopefully find a model that works for the student athletes, universities and the support staff that has supported our game,” Embick said. Terrapins coach Cirovski has suggested a possible solution, where schools that want the fall-to-spring calendar could form their own tier, similar to FBS and FCS in college football. The post Men’s College Soccer Calendar Change Roundly Rejected by Schools appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: 25th Anniversary Edition of Britney Spears’ Self-Titled Third LP Features 11 Bonus Tracks: Listen
articles.summary: Among the additions to the 2001 album are five songs being released for the first time.
articles._body: Britney Spears ‘ third studio album, 2001’s Britney , was reissued in an expanded edition on Friday (Nov. 6) featuring the entire original album along with 11 bonus tracks. The digital version of the LP is available now, with a physical package due out on Jan. 22 available for pre-order now here . Related Queens of the Stone Age Crowned on ARIA Chart With 'Perfecth' Britney Spears Seemingly Calls Out Stars Copying Her Image: ‘At Least Mine Was Real’ Lil Baby Brings 'Fresh' to Life: Stream It Now The expanded edition also includes five songs that are being officially released for the first time: the 2022 Pepsi commercial track “Right Now (Taste The Victory),” “She’ll Never Be Me,” “Am I A Sinner,” “When I Say So” and “My Big Secret,” as well as two remixes, “Overprotected (Darkchild Remix),” and “Boys (feat. Pharrell Williams) (The Co-Ed Remix).” The vinyl version of the album will be pressed on Bombastic Blue Splatter, with the package for the physical version including unreleased photos from the period when the singer recorded the LP, according to a press release. Another vinyl variant, a liquid-filled version from Bad World, is also available for pre-order today. Britney was originally released on Nov. 6, 2001 and debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, cementing Spears’ place in music history as the first female artist ever to have their first three studio albums debut at No. 1. It spawned the Billboard Hot 100 No. 27 hit “I’m a Slave 4 U” and the Nov. 86 hit “Overprotected,” and featured the fan-favorite songs “I’m Not a Girl, Not Yet a Woman,” as well as “Boys,” and a cover of Joan Jett’s “I Love Rock ‘n’ Roll.” The original album ends with “What It’s Like to Be Me,” a track co-written and co-produced by Spears’ then boyfriend, *NSYNC’s Justin Timberlake, and choreographer Wade Robson. Spears, who has said she is effectively retired from the music business, has not released a new album since 2016’s Glory and does not appear to be involved in the promotion of the anniversary edition. She did, however, preview the classic Britney pop banger “ She’ll Never Be Me ,” last month, giving fans a listen to the song she co-wrote with Timberlake along with Bradley Daymond (*NSYNC) and Alex Greggs (*NSYNC, Paris Hilton) and which was co-produced by Riprock ‘n’ Alex G. The resurfaced unreleased songs are the first “new” music from Spears since she teamed with will.i.am on 2023’s one-off “Mind Your Business.” In January, Spears vowed that she would “ never perform in the U.S. again ,” seven years after wrapping her global Piece of Me tour. Listen to the 25th anniversary edition of Britney below.

articles.title: Billionaires Ray Dalio and Richard Branson hate workplace gossip—but men who do it could face a steeper career penalty than women, study finds
articles.summary: New research found that men who gossip are perceived as less competent and less qualified for leadership roles than women who engage in the same behavior.
articles._body: Men who gossip around the office watercooler could be hurting their chances of climbing the corporate ladder. That’s according to a new study by researchers at the University of Iowa and the University of New Mexico, which found that men who gossip are perceived as less competent and less qualified for leadership roles than women who engage in the same behavior. “Men when they engage in gossip, they tend to be judged a lot more harshly than women,” Trevor Spoelma, an associate professor of management and entrepreneurship at the University of Iowa’s Tippie College of Business, told Fortune . The researchers reached that conclusion through three studies: an observation of 272 undergraduate students working in five-person teams on a class project, followed by two online experiments involving roughly 450 U.S. workers.  Across the studies, people who gossiped received lower competence ratings, but men faced a steeper penalty than women. Gossip has existed as a social practice for centuries, but the word itself took on a more negative connotation around the 16th century, when it became increasingly associated with women spreading rumors. That history may help explain the gender double standard. When men gossip about a third party, they can be seen as violating traditional expectations of how men should behave, Spoelma said. For women, the behavior may be viewed as more consistent with longstanding gender stereotypes. Gossip can foster a sense of belonging—but men are penalized in their career more Negative gossip, Spoelma added, can involve questioning a colleague’s abilities, criticizing their work, or sharing an unflattering story about them. But gossip isn’t always necessarily malicious. It can also mean complimenting a colleague or sharing a harmless anecdote about someone who isn’t in the room. In some cases, both forms of gossip can have benefits to employees by fostering trust and a sense of belonging. “You’re suddenly in on something that supposedly not everyone’s in on. You become part of that inner circle,” psychologist Scott Lyons previously told Fortune . “You feel special. You feel like you matter.”  That sense of connection could be particularly valuable as hybrid work enables employees to collaborate less face-to-face. And amid a broader loneliness crisis among men , informal workplace interactions can offer another way to build meaningful relationships with colleagues. But while men tend to receive more leniency than women when their behavior violates social norms or is perceived as unusual, gossip appears to be an exception, Spoelma said. “A lot of times, men receive a pass compared to women for different norm-violating behaviors,” he told Fortune . “But specifically, when it comes to gossip, that’s an instance where we see this penalty.” Richard Branson and Ray Dalio hate workplace gossip. Dave Ramey says he’ll even fire you Despite employees enjoying gossip, some of the world’s most prominent business leaders have made clear they don’t think it has a place in the workplace. Billionaire co-founder of Virgin Group Richard Branson , for example, has long championed a philosophy of avoiding speaking poorly of others. “If I ever hear anybody gossiping, I will walk away because it’s just not good,” he told LinkedIn in 2024. “Everything comes back to people, people, people.“Are you good with people? Are you good at drawing out the best in people?”  Ray Dalio , the billionaire founder of hedge fund Bridgewater Associates, has echoed that talking about people behind their backs in the workplace is counterproductive.  “You shouldn’t talk behind somebody’s back or gossip,” he said in an interview with the Academy of Achievement in 2012. “Too many people talk about the other people, what they’re doing wrong,” Dalio explained. “Except they don’t talk to those people about what they’re doing wrong. So they don’t know whether they’re actually doing them wrong or not. They haven’t heard the other side and they’re not being productive. So that’s terrible.” Personal finance radio show host Dave Ramsey has gone so far to make “No Gossip” one of the 14 values of his company, Ramsey Solutions. “One of our core values is, I will fire you for being a gossip. I just did it and I’ll do it again,” he said on his EntreLeadership show in 2024. Workplace disagreements and frustrations are inevitable, Ramsey acknowledged, but employees have a responsibility not to make them worse by spreading negativity among colleagues. “You have one option at Ramsey. You must hand your negatives up to someone in leadership who can do something about it,” he said. “But if you hand your negatives down or sideways, that’s called gossip. I’ll warn you once maybe, but we’ll probably just fire you.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Bill Gates believes a billionaire’s tax is the only option in the age of AI—and ‘whatever’s left over’ can be used as a philanthropic safety net
articles.summary: "The primary responsibility of dealing with inequality will always rest with governments."
articles._body: The stock rout of the past 24 hours may have wiped billions from the net worths of the world’s wealthiest people. Still, the hiccup will do little to dissuade economists from believing that artificial intelligence will be a major driver of wealth gains in the coming years. And while proposals for a billionaire’s tax have proved divisive in states like California, Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates suggests a similar policy is likely the best way forward in the age of AI. Already, the fortunes of individuals who have founded AI or AI-adjacent companies have boomed, and the wealth effects for families invested in those companies promise to be significant. But with massive wealth gains comes the question of inequality, and particularly in the case of AI, whether it might further exacerbate the current K-shaped economy. The K-shaped economy refers to the divergence between higher and lower earners and their economic prospects. Philanthropic initiatives from the wealthy cannot be relied upon to address this gap, Gates said in a recent interview with The Financial Times . Rather, policymakers must move to tax wealth progressively, and then individuals can choose to donate accordingly from their earnings. “The primary responsibility of dealing with inequality will always rest with governments,” Gates said. “We can’t expect philanthropy, which is voluntary in nature, to be the safety net.” Gates, the founder of the Gates Foundation, decided to give “virtually all my wealth”—about $100 billion—to the organization early last year. The only catch was that it all had to be spent within the next 20 years. Yet even these sums won’t go far enough to offset the inequality AI is likely to cause. According to Fed data , the top 1% of the wealthiest people in the U.S. own more than 50% of the nation’s stock market, meaning the gains experienced this year—and in the future—disproportionately flow to them. “So, in a world of AI, there will have to be changes in tax systems, including the ability to tax people with huge wealth, the ability to tax billionaires,” added Gates. “But whatever’s left over after those new taxes are put in place, I do think we’re seeing a very enlightened group that in both areas, here in the United States and for global good, they’re at a very young age already asking the questions about, ‘OK, what’s the most impact I can have?’ and ‘How do we be complementary to whatever government aid there is?'” Gates’s other suggestion Gates’s suggestion to tax the super-rich is—unsurprisingly—not universally popular among his tech-founder peers. Google co-founder Sergey Brin and former CEO Eric Schmidt have both flocked to tax-friendly states amid California’s proposed billionaire tax. Other entrepreneurs, like Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, say they understand why they may need to be taxed more . But where Huang and Gates disagree is on the latter’s suggestion that robots should be taxed . In an essay shared in August , the entrepreneur and philanthropist wrote: “Right now, if you’re an employer and you hire someone, you pay payroll taxes on their earnings. But if you buy a robot, you can usually write it off right away as a business expense. The tax system nudges you toward replacing people with machines.” As a result, Gates suggests taxing AI tokens and robots. Huang disagrees. In an interview with  Fox  Business’s  The Claman Countdown , the chipmaker boss said a few days later: “I love the heck out of Bill … but I don’t see what he sees. I see something very, very different. And so my remedies will be a little different.” Huang added: “I’m in favor of taxes. And I think that … for anybody who is productive, it’s a great way for us to contribute back to society and the economy. But the fact of the matter is, there are probably lots of different ways to approach this.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles._body: Oklahoma is expected to start quarterback John Mateer at Florida on Saturday night, sources tell Sooner Scoop’s George Stoia and On3’s Pete Nakos. The Sooners fired offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle earlier this week, prompting questions about whether Oklahoma would make a change at quarterback. But sources tell On3 that Mateer took most of the first-team quarterback reps in practice this week, and the plan remains for him to start. In eight games this season, Mateer has thrown seven interceptions. The Sooners currently rank 108th in scoring offense and 111th in total offense. Mateer’s struggles have been coupled with a running game averaging just 3.17 yards per carry, which ranks 128th in the nation. Mateer has a 65.6% completion percentage. In six games against power conference competition, Oklahoma is averaging 18.5 points per game. Tight ends coach Jason Witten has been tabbed as interim offensive coordinator for the remainder of Oklahoma’s season. “I have decided to make a change at offensive coordinator,” Oklahoma head coach Brent Venables said in a statement on Monday afternoon. “My responsibility is to the whole team and what I believe is best for us right now. We need a change. “I believe we still have meaningful opportunities ahead and a responsibility to maximize them. Our expectations remain high and our commitment to meeting them is unwavering.” Oklahoma at Florida kicks off at 7:45 p.m. ET on SEC Network.

articles.title: Tenth Circuit rules in favor of NCAA in Wisne eligibility lawsuit, overturns injunction
articles.summary: In a landmark legal win for the NCAA, the Tenth Circuit ruled in the governing body’s favor in the Wisne eligibility lawsuit on Friday. As a result, the injunction has been overturned as athletes sought a fifth year. The suit was filed in Colorado over the summer in light of the NCAA’s age-based, fi
articles._body: In a landmark legal win for the NCAA, the Tenth Circuit ruled in the governing body’s favor in the Wisne eligibility lawsuit on Friday. As a result, the injunction has been overturned as athletes sought a fifth year. The suit was filed in Colorado over the summer in light of the NCAA’s age-based, five-year eligibility model. Upon implementation, the new rule was not retroactive to members of the class of 2022, and a number of legal challenges followed. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Judge Charlotte Sweeney of the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Colorado ruled in favor of the class by granting a nationwide injunction. In August, though, the Tenth Circuit granted the NCAA’s request for a stay of the injunction, which meant it was on pause pending a ruling from the court. Attorneys for both the plaintiffs and the NCAA argued before the three-judge panel Oct. 13. During oral arguments, the judges said one of the central parts of the case was figuring out how the athletes would be harmed if they were not declared eligible. SUBSCRIBE to the On3 NIL and Sports Business Newsletter “It doesn’t seem there’s been a definition of the market from a huge, huge division – golf, everything,” U.S. Circuit Judge Paul Kelly said during the hearing, via the AP . “And you’re lumping them all together and you never looked at commonality and interchangeability of the various buyers.” While the court stayed the Wisne injunction, more lawsuits were filed at the state level. The NCAA won out in some of those cases, including in Kentucky, Arizona and Ohio. As a result, athletes in those cases would not be eligible pending a final ruling. In light of Friday’s ruling, NCAA chief legal officer Scott Bearby sent a memo regarding the decision. He cited the consistency of the Tenth Circuit’s decision with federal appeals courts and criticized the number of lawsuits around the age-based eligibility model. “While we are appreciative of the Tenth Circuit’s decision, injunctions like the one entered by the district court have created chaos for the 2026-27 season,” the memo reads . “The NCAA membership’s decision about the implementation of the age-based eligibility rule was clear and unanimous. It is disappointing that a minority of schools continue to support efforts to flout rules they agreed to follow. “The serial lawsuits and forum shopping by former student-athletes who repeatedly file suit in different jurisdictions in search of any judge willing to enter an injunction on a limited record is unacceptable.” The Kentucky case notably includes Thomas Castellanos , who played four games for the Red Raiders after securing a preliminary injunction. However, after the Kentucky Court of Appeals dissolved the temporary injunction, his availability came into question while awaiting a hearing. A judge then granted a motion for a new injunction , and Castellanos suited up for Texas Tech vs. Arizona State . The NCAA announced implementation of its five-year, age-based eligibility model this summer. Athletes will now get five years to play five seasons, with their eligibility “clock” starting at their 19th birthday or the date they enroll at a university, whichever happens first. The Tenth Circuit’s ruling also comes as the Protect College Sports Act heads to the U.S. House of Representatives. It advanced out of the Senate by a 77-22 margin in late September and addresses eligibility, among many other issues. The House is due back in session Monday, but as Ross Dellenger detailed for On3, the bill’s future is very much in question .
