articles.title: Inside Addi Mack’s bittersweet career night against South Carolina
articles.summary: Brenda Frese remembers watching Addi Mack go through a star shooting drill in high school. It doubled as conditioning, which was part of what made it so impressive. Mack kept moving and kept making threes. “She didn’t miss a shot,” Frese told On3. “It was unbelievable to watch.” Frese went back to h
articles._body: Brenda Frese remembers watching Addi Mack go through a star shooting drill in high school. It doubled as conditioning, which was part of what made it so impressive. Mack kept moving and kept making threes. “She didn’t miss a shot,” Frese told On3. “It was unbelievable to watch.” Frese went back to her staff and told them she’d just seen a kid who reminded her of Kristi Toliver. She liked the way Mack could get up and down the floor, too. She watched her play for her high school and AAU team and could picture her in Maryland’s offense. And over the course of recruiting her, she got to know a kid who would sometimes beat her to the first question on the phone. “Before I could ask what she was up to, she was asking me about what I’m doing,” Frese said. “And that’s unique with players.” Mack remembers those calls too. Frese recruited her for a long time and Mack wanted to go somewhere she could help right away. When Mack arrived, she had players like Yarden Garzon, Saylor Poffenbarger and Mir McLean to watch. They’d each played years of college basketball before Mack got there. By the time she got to the Big Ten and NCAA tournaments, she felt more comfortable managing a game herself. “I just felt a lot more comfortable with myself,” Mack told On3. “Being able to not only find ways to be successful for myself but finding ways to be able to make my team better.” The shooting was a little more complicated. Mack was dealing with a nagging ankle for much of Big Ten play. She’d never had to manage an injury like that before, so she figured out how to fit rehab in around class and practice and kept playing. “During the season you have no time really to be like, ‘Okay, I’m just gonna take two weeks off,’” Mack said. Frese could see how much the ankle affected Mack’s shot. She also noticed that Mack kept taking it. “She never lost confidence around it,” Frese said. “Which I think is important when you go through an injury.” By the end of her freshman year, Mack had started 26 games and earned a spot on the Big Ten All-Freshman Team. She averaged 11 points, 2.2 assists and 1.1 steals, and she scored in double figures in 21 of her 31 games. After the season, Mack finally had time to rest the ankle. She knew she needed the break. She also knew she was going to get bored. So she worked on her handle while sitting in a chair. She learned to juggle tennis balls with one of her coaches. More recently, she was messing around and figured out she could juggle basketballs, too. “Throw it really high,” Mack said. “That’s my trick.” By the time she was back on the floor that summer, Frese could see a difference in how Mack ran the offense. She was more confident calling plays. She knew who needed the ball and where they wanted it. Her ankle felt good again and she had a year’s worth of experience to draw on. “She’s commanding the position,” Frese said. Then Maryland opened the season against No. 1 South Carolina in Paris. At halftime, Mack had four points and Maryland was down 61-33. Frese wanted the Terps to be more patient on offense and Mack also wanted to talk about the other end of the floor. On a team retreat, the players had discussed what they wanted Maryland basketball to look like. They’d settled on defense and rebounding. Sitting in the locker room in Paris, Mack thought about what somebody would’ve taken away from watching the first half. “We are not playing Maryland basketball,” she remembers telling her teammates. A year earlier, Mack had been learning from the older players around her. In Paris, she was the one speaking up. “Being the point guard, I think it’s my job to get everyone on the same page,” Mack said. When she went back out, she looked for whatever might get the team going. A deflection. Somebody trying to take a charge. A teammate grabbing a rebound. “The ball finds energy,” Mack said. It found her plenty in that second half. She scored 17 points in the third quarter and 31 after halftime. Her teammates kept finding her. For a while, she said, it felt like she was back in her senior year of high school. “When she plays free, that’s what it looks like,” Frese said. Mack finished with 35 points, six threes and six assists. Maryland cut a 31-point deficit to six. But South Carolina won 101-93. Frese ran into Mack’s parents in the lobby afterward. They were, in her words, “pretty fired up.” Mack had plenty to feel good about. She’d spent the beginning of the summer working on her handle from a chair and now she’d had the best scoring night of her college career against the No. 1 team in the country. Then Paige Bueckers followed her. For somebody who’d once said in a video that all she wants to do is play like Bueckers, that was pretty cool. At the buzzer, though, Mack remembers feeling something a little harder to put into words. “I’m not sure disappointment is the right word,” she said. She landed on bittersweet. She was proud that a team with so many new faces had found a way to make it a game. And there was still a part of her that kept thinking about how different the night could’ve been if Maryland had played that way a little sooner. “Ah, shoot,” Mack said. “Like the first half, if we could have just changed it. You think of so many what-ifs.” In the moment, Mack had been so caught up in getting the next stop or taking the next shot that she’d barely thought about the clock. Then she looked up. Maryland was only down six. She couldn’t remember exactly how much time was left. She remembered being surprised there was so little of it. “I was like, no way, we’re coming this close to the end of the game already,” Mack said. When she watched the game back, she could see how much had gone right for Maryland to get that close. She could also see all the little things that might’ve made it enough. To explain what she meant, she brought up swimming. She used to compete and still gets in the pool when she goes home. She knows how little can separate two swimmers reaching for the wall. “Swimming

articles.title: Dianna Russini Set to Return to Media: What We Know
articles.summary: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images
articles._body: Dianna Russini is poised to make a sports-media comeback soon, Front Office Sports has confirmed, several months after resigning from The Athletic in the aftermath of Page Six publishing photos showing her with Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel at an adults-only Arizona resort in April. After ProFootballTalk first reported Russini has told people around the NFL that she is expecting to return to the industry next week, several options have emerged for what comes next. Russini is expected to launch new content sponsored by gambling operators, sources said, adding there have been talks with Jake Paul’s Betr platform, as well as offshore sportsbook BetUS. One source said Russini has also had talks with iHeart. FOS discovered a new X/Twitter page titled “The Russini Report,” created in October, that has only three followers at the time of publication—Andres Vargas, a content creator and spokesperson for BetUS; Crossing Lines, a show sponsored by BetUS featuring ex-Barstool personality Jeff Nadu and cohost Donnie Seymour; and an additional video manager, named Natalie, following the page from a protected account. The “Russini Report” page indicates a show will air live on Wednesdays encompassing pro football news, injuries, and analysis. The page previously indicated the show would be “powered by BetUS,” but that language has since been edited out. FOS screenshot On Friday, BetUS teased a new show on social media, with a woman making a comeback, launching Nov. 11. In the teaser, text messages reading, “Is it true? You back?” and “Football was weird without you reporting,” among others expressing similar sentiments pop up on the screen. Something big is arriving on November 11. Who do you think it is? Only on BetUS. Get the first look: https://t.co/WZZ5VL8HjU pic.twitter.com/LTwGDYkmce — BetUS Casino & Sportsbook (@BetUS_Official) November 6, 2026 In an announcement posted later Friday to its website, the company said: “BetUS is about to steal headlines after reaching an agreement with an NFL specialist with more than 10 years of experience in the game. “Although we can’t disclose the name just yet, we can reveal that this specialist will be hosting a live NFL betting show featuring game previews, matchup breakdowns, guest interviews, and data-backed NFL picks and predictions throughout the remainder of the 2026 season.” BetUS said it will announce the host’s name on Monday, and the first show will air on Wednesday at noon ET. The host will be “writing an accompanying column,” BetUS wrote, that “will also cover NFL matchups, detailing betting angles, breaking news, and industry rumors.” Basketball Hall of Famer Dennis Rodman is also an endorser of BetUS, which is headquartered in Costa Rica. On Wednesday, Page Six reported Russini will be “headlining her own show” on a digital platform . “It’s been in the works for a while and she can’t wait to get back to what she loves,” a source told Page Six . Russini stopped responding to messages when presented with BetUS, Betr, and iHeart as places she has had talks with. Her agent, Matt Olson of CAA, referred FOS to the publicist Melissa Nathan, who declined to comment. Spokespeople for BetUS, Betr, and iHeart did not respond to requests for comment, nor did Vargas. Jon “Stugotz” Weiner, a host for iHeart and its subsidiary Fox Sports Radio, has previously said he would welcome the chance to collaborate with Russini again. Russini was a frequent guest on Weiner’s previous show, The Dan Le Batard Show with Stugotz , and also joined Weiner on his God Bless Football show during Super Bowl week this past February. If Russini reaches a deal with iHeart, it is not expected to encompass Fox Sports Radio, one source said. Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy also previously said he would consider hiring Russini, but he told FOS this week that she is not going to work for Barstool now. Sources told FOS that Kalshi, Underdog, and FanDuel are not in the running to sponsor her content at this time. After Russini and Vrabel were photographed hugging and holding hands, the two issued statements saying their relationship was platonic, not romantic. Russini resigned from the New York Times –owned Athletic about a week later, and Vrabel missed one day of the NFL Draft to attend counseling. One source told FOS he expects Russini to lean in to her NFL insider role. The question is how much cooperation she will get from NFL players and coaches, as well as the league itself, with the NFL playoffs and Super Bowl only months away. “All she needs is one big scoop to show she has motion,” says the source. FOS previously reported that Russini was planning a sports-media comeback . In September, The Athletic released an investigation saying Russini “should have disclosed to The Athletic the nature of her relationship with [Mike] Vrabel to allow editors to assess the kinds of stories on which she should have been working.” The investigation did not seek to discover whether the two had a romantic relationship, and while it noted Russini was “effusive” in her praise of Vrabel at times, it mirrored how he was covered by other outlets. Ultimately, the investigation recommended editor’s notes be added to three videos and one story in which Russini covered Vrabel during her time at The Athletic . Show HN: Botel – always reachable agents you pay for only while they're working
articles.summary:
I built a pay-as-you-go two star hotel for bots that you’re only charged for while it’s active. Typically wakes in under a second, runs on a vm, and costs very little while it’s paused.

In my free time I’ve been building a firecracker based vm orchestration platform. In order to dogfood the thi
articles._body: I built a pay-as-you-go two star hotel for bots that you’re only charged for while it’s active. Typically wakes in under a second, runs on a vm, and costs very little while it’s paused. In my free time I’ve been building a firecracker based vm orchestration platform. In order to dogfood the thing I put together a place to run agent harnesses (openclaw etc) on machines but only pay for them when they are in use. What started as a demo has grown legs into a more unique product than the platform. Botel has prebaked templates for each harness, with a daemon of mine running beside it monitoring the harness’ activity. It communicates out to the host over a link-local self api; instructing when to pause or wake next based on stored schedules. With a proxy in front to wake on http. The harnesses are preconfigured to point to my llm gateway that proxies through to openrouter. One of the biggest struggles while building it was preventing claude from going off the rails with hotel metaphors in the ui. Once it sees a joke it really strangles the hell out of it. A more real ;) awkward part is that the harnesses don’t expose exactly what I needed in order to detect activity. I'm still struggling with how to handle the fact that background job can be short or long lived (http/dev servers etc). I’m hoping to propose changes to hermes, openclaw, and dsh soon for a consistent way to know what kind of a job is running with annotated lifecycle hooks. Some of the nicest things about the bot hotel are: - You get a proper linux vm with sudo, so you can ssh in, scp, or run docker. - You can ask the agent to expose something publicly or privately (behind your login). A port gets a unique hostname/url. Those endpoints also wake the vm. So you could build and host a little app or self host something. - Guided telegram setup. It’s pretty awkward in general/my setup hopefully takes some of the edge off. A friend of mine who built a website for his local orienteering club has used this to make it easy for peoge on the committee to update news and events. All in all it should cost something like 40 cents a month to run so long as the club members don’t get too friendly with the agent. If you’re interested, give the thing a spin. The first 50 signups get $2 credit. Price is pretty low at 3c per GB of ram per hour awake, plus a few cents per GB-month asleep. You use credit for inference or byok. Let me know how you get on and whether you have any ideas or requests for it. Thx! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50393793 Points: 2 # Comments: 3

Yeezy Is Officially Sampling Itself
articles.summary: You know what season it is. Ye just seized the means of production, and re-launched his fashion line Yeezy with a perfectly self-referential runway.
articles._body: It’s Yeezy Season all over again — as in, we’re starting over with Yeezy Season 01. To debut the first-ever Los Angeles Yeezy flagship store and apparently reintroduce Yeezy proper, Ye hosted a guerilla-style runway show late on November 4 titled “Season 01,” suggesting a full reset from first principles. And if today is the day when Yeezy is born anew, it’s worth asking: what even is, or was, Yeezy? To understand the brand’s future, you must study its past. On Wednesday night, instead of a full Yeezy reset, we saw a self-referential carousel of some of Ye’s greatest design hits. The runway was packed with various lengths of his preferred earth-toned catsuits, mock-neck jackets, faded jeans, and cargo pants, with a couple of lingerie bits thrown in for good measure. Shades of the other Yeezy Season 1 , Season 2 , Season 3 … The fact that the collection demands a visual aid to be fully appreciated speaks to one of Ye’s greatest design strengths: his ability to identify specific products with broad appeal, then make them in a zillion colorways so they still feel new. Ye has always done this in his music. Now, we’re seeing him do the same thing in fashion. In a 2020 interview with Forbes, Ye declared “Yeezy is for everyone,” a maxim that would serve as his philosophy for YEEZY GAP. And even when YEEZY GAP was “engineered by” Balenciaga , the clothes — whether they were collarless puffer jackets or perfectly boxy hoodies — were priced at or under a comfortable $90. Over the past half-decade, Yeezy has delivered on that egalitarian aim, even after YEEZY GAP fell apart and the Yeezy website began offering everything from in-house iterations of the ubiquitous adidas YEEZY slides ($40) to relatively anonymous black hoodies ($40) to the “merch” created for Ye and Ty Dolla $ign’s Vultures ($20). Even the oft-viral collaborations with longtime Ye cohort and English designer Mowalola, ranging from the skin-tight WET tanks to “KITTY” intimates that debuted at London Fashion Week, were priced to match ($20-$40). A lot of the people involved in current-day Yeezy are members of my personal nightmare blunt rotation, such as head of design Gosha Rubchinskiy and manufacturing partner Dov Charney . In the context of public opinion, Ye and some members of his circle are controversial. The Yeezy reset and opening of the LA store are a part of Ye’s ongoing career rehabilitation. In 2022, the artist and designer wore a “White Lives Matter” shirt at Paris Fashion Week and made a series of antisemitic remarks, leading to an investigation by the Anti-Defamation League and the dissolution of his deal with adidas and other partners. (In January, Ye took out a full-page ad in The Wall Street Journal to apologize, attributing many of his comments to his mental illness.) In the context of the fashion industry, Ye is employing power players who can execute his desired minimalist-hype clothing at his desired prices — Charney with his production résumé and Rubshinskiy with the ability to translate subculture into product. (Footwear designer Mats Rombaut, who helped create new Yeezy shoes including the sheath-like SL-01, SL-02, and SL-03 models, has a comparatively clean track record.) Ye, I’m happy to have you back doing what I think you do best in fashion: designing clothes to make women feel sexy and men feel tough. Both end up looking really steezy, as in the true definition of the portmanteau of “swag” and “easy.” The footwear, which encompassed tall opaque heels and less-tall military-style boots, accomplished the same goal. It’s Ye doing Yeezy 2015 in 2026, not a redux so much as it is a sample — a remix. If anything, it’s a reminder of how perennial Ye’s taste is. To quote him , “It’s not that I’m not right, I’m just not right now.” Highsnobiety has affiliate marketing partnerships, which means we may receive a commission from your purchase. Want to shop the products our editors actually love? Visit our SHOPPER page and subscribe to the newsletter for recs on all things fashion, footwear, and beauty.

HUGO’s New Campaign Is for Anyone Who’s Been Doubted
articles.summary: The heartbeat of Red Means GO, HUGO’s campaign platform launched last season, comes from five trailblazing talents, each bringing their own perspective.
articles._body: Paris has its own rhythm, and you have to keep up. From racing for the Metro to cutting through the Marais in search of something new, the city is always moving. It’s a fitting setting for HUGO’s Fall/Winter 2026 collection. The heartbeat of Red Means GO, HUGO’s campaign platform launched last season, comes from five trailblazing talents, each bringing their own perspective. The campaign explores what it takes to pursue your own path in photography, art, curation and music, navigating expectations, embracing uncertainty and finding the confidence to keep going. Four of these talents took part in the Highsnobiety shoot, sharing their approaches to creativity, self-expression and forging their own paths, bringing their own perspectives to that journey, with Paris providing a backdrop that feels like an extension of their lives. For photographer and director Tereza Mundilová, working between Berlin, Paris and New York, that instinct begins before the camera even comes out: “Before I take a photo, I see it in my head. For me, photography is always about what you see or what you dream of.” Creatives whose paths are shaped by experimentation rather than a fixed destination. For London-based artist and musician Cato, that freedom means moving between disciplines while following the instinct behind an idea. “Most of my ideas are visual. I love to flesh them out into a video or an animation, but it’s easier to get them down as a painting. With music, I just start playing and see what comes out.” His creative process also involves a degree of distance from the worlds he depicts. “Even though my work is about groups of people, I’m kind of the voyeur. I’m the one looking at them.” HUGO’s mix of sharp tailoring and more relaxed, expressive pieces reflects a similar freedom to move between worlds without being defined by just one. Rather than committing to a single medium, Cato follows ideas across painting, animation and music, allowing each to find its own form. Temitayo Famakinwa works across art curation, media and digital culture, including content and social strategy for Saatchi Yates exhibitions. Her practice connects established cultural institutions with new ways of reaching audiences. That willingness to move into unfamiliar territory is personal, too. After leaving neuroscience, Famakinwa chose to pursue a future in the arts, despite the uncertainty and the doubts of those around her. “Staying true to myself meant taking the leap, even if people around you might take some time to catch up.” DJ and creative Nick Cheo takes another route, building an audience through genre-blending mixes that pair humour with a broad musical vocabulary. Having attracted attention from artists including Tinashe, Zack Bia and Verdy, and recently supported PinkPantheress on her North American tour, he continues to shape a distinctive place within contemporary music culture. For Cheo, keeping that momentum going comes down to trusting the experience he has already gained: “Everything you’ve done in your past is proof that you’ve done it once, so you can just do it again. And that applies to everything.” Together, the four talents give Red Means GO its meaning. Their backgrounds differ, but each reflects the ambition to keep evolving, crossing disciplines and creating opportunities on their own terms. The clothes become part of that expression: relaxed denim and leather bring an instinctive edge, while considered tailoring offers structure without imposing a uniform. Whether it means following a visual instinct, stepping away from a familiar career or trusting the lessons of the past, their stories suggest that finding your own direction is less about having everything figured out than having the confidence to take the next step. For HUGO, Fall/Winter 2026 is about making familiar formulas feel personal again. ’90s tailoring, utility details and substantial textures provide the foundation; unexpected combinations and individual styling give them a contemporary perspective. In Paris, where every route leads somewhere different, the collection finds its natural rhythm. The collection follows a similar instinct, taking familiar wardrobe codes and pushing them somewhere new. ’90s tailoring sets the foundation, reworked through relaxed proportions, utility influences and tactile winter fabrics. In menswear, HUGO check, herringbone and structured outerwear meet Nappa leather, sateen and ribbed wool. A brown leather jacket with workwear-inspired chest pockets, worn with baggy black denim and a slim turquoise shirt, balances practicality with a more expressive edge. Elsewhere, a dark-grey herringbone jacket and pleated trousers bring a relaxed attitude to traditional tailoring. Womenswear explores the same tension between structure and freedom, combining sharp ’90s silhouettes with hints of ’60s alpine dressing. Strong shoulders, hourglass shapes, leather and cashmere-blend outerwear create a confident foundation. A sculptural blazer with rhinestone detailing and kick-flare trousers adds a note of individuality, while an oversized brown biker jacket, ribbed knitwear and straight-leg Japanese denim offer a more understated take. Across both collections, rich textures and a restrained palette of brown, black, mushroom and tinted white are punctuated by lacquer red. The HUGO Fall/Winter 2026 collection is available worldwide through HUGO stores, wholesale partners and online at hugo.com.

articles.title: ‘A master class in how to handle layoffs’: Canva is restructuring 22% of its workforce, and LinkedIn is applauding the exit package
articles.summary: CEO Melanie Perkins’s note to staff drew applause online for a package that includes a year of healthcare, career coaching and $10,000 project grants
articles._body: Most layoff announcements draw anger. Canva’s is drawing applause. Co-founder and CEO Melanie Perkins announced on Tuesday that a sweeping restructuring will affect 1,271 employees, or 22% of the Sydney-based design company’s workforce. Her note to staff , which she also shared on LinkedIn, quickly became an online case study in how to cut jobs, largely because of what Canva is giving the people who leave. Jasveer Singh, co-founder and CEO of KnotDating, called it “a master-class in how to handle layoffs” and described Perkins’s announcement as “thoughtful, honest and generous,” Newsweek reported . Mark Di Stefano, Rear Window editor at the Australian Financial Review, called the package “exceedingly generous.” Commenters on Perkins’s LinkedIn post struck a similar note. “Really impressive, empathetic, transparent, and generous way to communicate what was undoubtedly a very hard decision,” one wrote, according to Fast Company . On Instagram, the praise turned to envy. “How do I apply to be fired by Canva?” one user asked, American Bazaar reported . The goodwill comes at a delicate moment. Perkins wrote that Canva’s growth slowed this year for the first time in a decade, and in August the company cut its 2026 revenue growth forecast from 30% to 20%, the Australian Financial Review reported . For some of the 1,271, the restructuring means new roles or a request to relocate, with Sydney becoming the main base for more product teams. For others, it means leaving the company. Canva has not said how many will lose their jobs. In her note, Perkins said the company is “simplifying layers, consolidating overlapping responsibilities, and ensuring teams have the right mix of skills and experience for the chapter ahead.” As Canva grew, she explained, work was divided among more specialized teams, leading to “fragmented ownership” and making it harder to see the bigger picture. The goal, she said, is “getting back to our roots of small, empowered teams with the freedom to make decisions, take ownership, and focus on what matters most for our community.” A Canva spokesperson told Fortune these roles are not being replaced by AI. “AI is changing what’s possible for our community and the kinds of products we’re now building. That also changes how we need to organize our teams and the skills we’ll need. These changes are about setting Canva up to build those products, not using AI to do the work of people who are leaving.” Fortune , which put Perkins on its cover in 2022 , has reported that the restructuring is part of a broader AI-driven rethink of the company . What departing Canva employees get Departing employees will receive at least six months’ salary, inclusive of statutory entitlements, regardless of location. On top of that, they’ll receive 12 months of continued healthcare coverage in countries where Canva already provides it. Other perks include career transition support, complete with one-on-one coaching, interview preparation and a year of LinkedIn Premium. Employees leaving the company can also take their company MacBooks with them, and Canva is removing the one-year vesting cliff for people who joined in the past year. And it doesn’t stop there. Through a new Canva Collective Fund, eligible departing employees can apply for $10,000 grants to pursue an idea, start a business or launch a project, without Canva taking any equity or ownership in what they create. Applications close Dec. 14. The company said it has already received applications for a wide range of ideas, including writing and publishing a book, building a sustainable farming venture and going back to school. Canva has not disclosed how many grants it plans to award. Oracle’s ceiling is Canva’s floor The average severance package in the tech industry was 11.2 weeks of pay in 2024, according to a 2025 report by outplacement firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas , near the bottom of the industries it tracked. Canva’s minimum of six months, or roughly 26 weeks, is more than double that. It also matches the most anyone could get from Oracle, which laid off an estimated 20,000 to 30,000 employees in March and offered U.S. workers four weeks of base pay for their first year of service, plus one additional week for each subsequent year, capped at 26 weeks . Severance is moving in two directions Not every company is getting more generous. In an October study by global talent and workforce solutions company LHH , 56% of surveyed U.S. companies said they had made their severance policies more generous over the past two years, down from 76% in the firm’s previous study. The share that made them less generous jumped to 38% from 9%. Tech is leaning the other way. In the IT services and technology sector, 64% of respondents reported making their policies more generous, compared with 28% who made them less generous, according to additional data LHH shared with Fortune . The firm cautioned that the subgroup findings are directional. “Severance and career transition support are standard at many companies,” Russell Williams, SVP of Career Transition & Mobility at LHH, told Fortune . “Seeing all of it in one package is the exception, not the rule.” Why companies pay more to say goodbye Williams said employers are paying more attention to how they treat departing employees, recognizing that it matters to their business. “People notice. That includes the ones leaving, the ones staying and the ones the company will want to hire down the road,” he said. “How a company handles exits is one of the biggest signals it sends to the team it’s counting on next.” And layoffs aren’t exactly rare these days. In a 2026 global study by LHH, 73% of surveyed employees said they had witnessed layoffs on their teams in the past year. Employees also reported heavier workloads, lower morale and lost trust in leadership following layoffs. articles.title: Rule to Allow Crypto in 401(k)s Arrives at White House for Final Review
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Rule to Allow Crypto in 401(k)s Arrives at White House for Final Review A final DOL rule that would ease alternative assets such as private equity, real estate and cryptocurrency into 401(k) retirement plans arrived at the White House on Thursday for review, Bloomberg Law reported , a procedural step that usually precedes public release. The Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs logged the package on Nov. 5 under the title “Fiduciary Duties In Selecting Designated Investment Alternatives,” RIN 1210-AC38. The filing lists the DOL’s Employee Benefits Security Administration as the authoring office, marks the stage as a final rule, flags it as economically significant and notes that there is no legal deadline for completion. The DOL unveiled the proposal on March 30. In that draft, plan fiduciaries who follow a documented process when adding private assets to a 401(k) menu would get a legal safe harbor under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974. The six factors named in the proposal are performance, fees, liquidity, valuation, performance benchmarks and complexity. Satisfying them does not force plans to offer crypto. It lowers the litigation risk for employers that decide they want to. JUST IN: The White House is now reviewing a new rule which will allow Americans to invest in crypto through their 401(k) retirement plans pic.twitter.com/uXGGIXEzdC — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 6, 2026 What the DOL safe harbor covers President Donald Trump’s Aug. 7, 2025, executive order, “Democratizing Access to Alternative Assets for 401(k) Investors,” directed the Labor secretary to reexamine ERISA guidance and, where appropriate, propose rules with “appropriately calibrated safe harbors.” The order defined alternative assets to include private-market equity and debt, real estate, holdings in actively managed vehicles that invest in digital assets, commodities, infrastructure and lifetime-income strategies. The March proposal implements that order. A DOL fact sheet said prudence under ERISA is process-based and that fiduciaries retain discretion to select any designated investment alternative if they follow the outlined review. Deputy Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling cast the approach as neutral: “The department’s days of picking winners and losers are over.” That stance reverses a prior chill. In May 2025 the DOL rescinded its March 2022 compliance release that told fiduciaries to use “extreme care” before putting cryptocurrency on a 401(k) menu. The department said that phrase was not found in ERISA and restored a context-specific standard. Later, it was reported that Sens. Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren pressed the DOL to abandon the crypto-friendly path. House Republicans have separately pushed to codify Trump’s crypto order in statute. Why OIRA review matters for bitcoin and crypto OIRA review under Executive Order 12866 is the last interagency checkpoint before a final rule can be published in the Federal Register. Bloomberg Law said the arrival signals the package is nearing completion. The same office cleared the proposed version in late March before the DOL published it; that earlier pass took roughly two months after the January submission, per prior Bloomberg coverage of the roughly $12 trillion 401(k) market. What is not yet public is the final text itself. Whether the six-factor safe harbor survived comment intact, how digital-asset vehicles are described, and what effective date the DOL chose will only be clear when OIRA returns the rule and the department posts it. Comment volume on the proposal was heavy; industry and labor groups have argued opposite sides of the prudence standard for months. For bitcoin, the stakes sit in plan menus rather than spot ETF flows. Trump’s August order helped frame digital assets as a retirement-access issue for more than 90 million defined-contribution savers. A finalized DOL safe harbor would not put bitcoin and crypto on every lineup overnight. It would give plan committees a clearer map if they want exposure through an asset-allocation sleeve that holds digital assets. The test now is how fast OIRA clears the economically significant package — and whether the published final rule still gives fiduciaries the process cover the March draft promised, or whether the comment fight rewrote the safe harbor before the White House stamps it. This post Rule to Allow Crypto in 401(k)s Arrives at White House for Final Review first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .

articles.title: Show HN: Agentic Identity Broker, OAuth Delegation for AI Agents
articles.summary:
Hi HN, I’m Jan. I am co-author of the Agentic Identity Broker (AIB), an MIT-licensed OAuth2 broker in the Zalando Incubator, that lets a user give an AI agent scoped, revocable access to MCP services.

The broker solves three major challenges that are especially relevant in corporate environment
articles._body: Hi HN, I’m Jan. I am co-author of the Agentic Identity Broker (AIB), an MIT-licensed OAuth2 broker in the Zalando Incubator, that lets a user give an AI agent scoped, revocable access to MCP services. The broker solves three major challenges that are especially relevant in corporate environments: (A) Enable users to delegate workloads to agents without providing the agents all the user’s tokens. (B) Connect fragmented identity and authorization systems. (C) Centralize tool approvals and audit logging. We built AIB to fill an infrastructure gap in our own agent platform. At this moment in time, IETF working groups are still finalizing standards for agent identity, and vendors are still turning the necessary infrastructure into off-the-shelf products. We needed that infrastructure today. How it works: the user consents once per agent and service. The broker stores the third-party tokens encrypted. At request time a gateway (e.g. Agentgateway) does RFC 8693 token exchange. Agents never see user tokens and MCP servers only implement tools and don’t need to care about all the OAuth 2.1 plumbing. AIB is v0.1 and runs in production, bringing together hundreds of our agents with dozens of internal and external MCP servers. To try it locally: clone the repo, run "just compose-up-detached". The current features focus on on-behalf-of (OBO) use cases, where human actors delegate to agents. Next we are looking to also support headless agents, where agents are invoked by machines. Intent-based authorization is yet another package on our roadmap. If you’ve built either, or have feedback on the UI/UX, I’d like to hear from you! Nick Saban on 24-team CFP: 'There's not 24 teams in the country that can win a National Championship'
articles.summary: After years of discussion around the matter, it appears as if the College Football Playoff will officially expand to 24 teams next season. The field will double in teams, as more and more teams will now have the opportunity to win a National Championship. As with any controversial move in the world
articles._body: After years of discussion around the matter, it appears as if the College Football Playoff will officially expand to 24 teams next season. The field will double in teams, as more and more teams will now have the opportunity to win a National Championship. As with any controversial move in the world of sports, the 24-team CFP has both its fans and haters. Fans will claim the new format allows fresh matchups and new faces to emerge in the National Championship race, while those who oppose the move will complain about watering down the field and taking away conference championship games. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage One of the biggest names to publicly oppose the 24-team College Football Playoff has been College Football Hall of Famer Nick Saban . His campaign against the move continued on this week’s episode of the New Heights Podcast . There, Saban claimed that there are not 24 teams that can win the National Championship, making the expanded field rather pointless. Especially, when you’re adding games and taking away conference title games. “It’s too many… there’s not 24 teams in the country that can win a National Championship,” Saban said. “So, what is the reason to actually do it? It’s about the money. What you’re giving up, which I hate to see… the SEC Championship Game. Playing in the SEC Championship was a big thing for our players and our fans. It was a tradition and it was a great venue. There’s only two teams who can play in a National Championship, but more teams can play in [conference] championship games. There’s a lot of pride in winning the conference championship.” Nick Saban claims expanded CFP leads to ‘too many games’ The field initially expanded from four teams to 12 teams in 2024, tripling the size of the field. That, however, wasn’t good enough. “[The SEC Championship] was a great game, and players loved that. We’re gonna give that up to have an extra game where the 24th team is going to play the ninth best team,” Saban continued. “If we just put the right 12 teams in and didn’t go through all the political BS team we went through so we can have a 12-team Playoff, and end up putting a couple of teams in that shouldn’t be in, and some teams that didn’t get in should have gotten in, that was a good tournament. “Maybe you go to 16 if you want to include some other people, but 24 is a lot. It’s too many games for college football players to play. We played 15 games three times, and I thought that was too many games.”

articles.title: Ravens rumors: Ian Rapoport doubles down on Lamar Jackson contract prediction amid disaster 2026 season
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens will once again be without Lamar Jackson for an extended period of time after he hurt his thumb last week against the Buffalo Bills. Though they say it may not be season-ending, everyone is bracing for the possibility that he won’t be back on the field for the remainder
articles._body: The Baltimore Ravens will once again be without Lamar Jackson for an extended period of time after he hurt his thumb last week against the Buffalo Bills. Though they say it may not be season-ending, everyone is bracing for the possibility that he won’t be back on the field for the remainder of the year. That has led some to think that Jackson has played his last snap as a Raven , especially since he hasn’t signed an extension with the team yet. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network doesn’t think that Jackson is going anywhere, and it’ll depend on what happens during the offseason . “Lamar Jackson has one year left on his contract and has not signed a contract extension yet with the Baltimore Ravens, despite the fact that the organization wants to,” Rapoport said. “He has a big cap number next year, but here’s my understanding of the situation. When this season ends, Lamar Jackson and the Baltimore Ravens will get together, and the hope is that he will be a member of the Baltimore Ravens for a very long time, potentially through the end of his career. From @NFLGameDay Kickoff: The #Ravens QB situation is in flux, with Jacoby Brissett on the way. But what about the future of Lamar Jackson? pic.twitter.com/iIkGMCQc9k — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 5, 2026 “Doesn’t sound to me like he wants to go anywhere. Doesn’t sound like the Ravens want him to go anywhere. I would be surprised, or maybe even stunned, if Lamar Jackson was not the quarterback of the Baltimore Ravens in 2027.” The next day, Rapoport doubled down on his claims . “I do not see a scenario where Lamar Jackson is not the quarterback of the Baltimore Ravens next year,” Rapoport said. It sounds like it’ll come down to the offseason, and if both sides can’t agree to a deal, the Ravens may have to consider what a trade looks like for Jackson. He’ll become a free agent in 2028, and there’s no way they’ll let him walk for nothing. Since both sides seem to be willing to get something done, the chances of Jackson staying should be high. articles.title: Weezer: Photos From the Billboard Cover Shoot
articles.summary: Check out new pics of the legendary alt-rockers ahead of their Billboard Live Music Summit appearance.
articles._body: Rivers Cuomo is reclining in a zero-gravity chair in a musty, windowless room deep within Tampa, Fla.’s Benchmark Arena — baseball cap on his head, a copy of Cormac McCarthy’s Blood Meridian and a pair of headphones beside him. Nearby, there’s a keyboard, a small drum kit and an acoustic guitar that his Weezer bandmate, drummer Patrick Wilson, periodically picks up and noodles on; a jar of peanut butter; a printed, official-looking setlist on a spreadsheet; and a paper bag labeled “clarinet books” in marker. It’s flummoxing to consider that in just a few hours, this soft-spoken iteration of the Weezer frontman will be channeling the power-pop gods onstage for thousands of screaming fans. But this is Cuomo in power-saving mode, restoring the energy he burned onstage the night prior outside of Fort Lauderdale and didn’t quite recover on the four-hour overnight bus ride across the Sunshine State. Yet at precisely 9:12 p.m. on this October night — just like every show night this tour — the lights will go down for Weezer’s headlining set, and Cuomo will transform. This is the precise time that, like clockwork, the lights have gone down for every show on the Weezer: The Gathering Tour, and it’s the time they will continue to go down for its remainder; if all goes as planned, Weezer will leave the stage at 10:53 p.m. on the dot. A prerecorded video plays, setting up the show’s concept: A kid makes a wish for Weezer to play at his house, and when the quartet receives the magical transmission, it links up to answer the call. Finally, after the clip rolls, one of the great American rock bands strides onto the stage — which is decked out with a fake house, fence, yard and power lines to resemble the home from the video. “Dearly beloved, we’re gathered here tonight,” Cuomo declares into his mic as the band revs up, “to celebrate a thing called Weezer!” Read the full Weezer Billboard cover story here. Weezer will be honored with the Legend of Live award and sit down for an exclusive Q&A at the 2026 Billboard Live Music Summit on Nov. 10 at the 1 Hotel West Hollywood. Tickets for the Nov. 10 event are available here .

articles.title: Warriors’ Draymond Green fires back at Dillon Brooks by calling out ‘de-escalate’ BS after recent skirmish
articles.summary: What happens when two of the NBA’s biggest trash-talkers meet? Draymond Green learned it firsthand. The latest confrontation between the Golden State Warriors’ veteran and Dillon Brooks took place during the Bay Area team’s win over the Phoenix Suns. Brooks claimed he stepped into Tuesday&#
articles._body: What happens when two of the NBA’s biggest trash-talkers meet? Draymond Green learned it firsthand. The latest confrontation between the Golden State Warriors’ veteran and Dillon Brooks took place during the Bay Area team’s win over the Phoenix Suns. Brooks claimed he stepped into Tuesday’s altercation to calm things down. Green strongly disagreed with that explanation during a recent appearance on his podcast, arguing that Brooks’ actions did not match his claim. “He was talking. He came in talking, putting his shoulder on my shoulder, putting his chest on my shoulder. You know that ain’t how you de-escalate,” Green said. “Yeah, he was talking. Putting his chest on my shoulder. That ain’t how you de-escalate. So I just wish he stood on the type of business he was on.” Draymond Green on latest altercation with Dillon Brooks on Monday (via @957thegame ) pic.twitter.com/7P0dnVsexq https://t.co/gFPanKoitQ — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 6, 2026 Green also questioned why Brooks approached him instead of going to his own teammates if his intention was to settle the situation. “When you’re de-escalating, you usually go to your teammate, but your teammate’s there, so you’re not de-escalating anything,” he added. The confrontation happened in the third quarter when Green threw Suns center Khaman Maluach to the floor while trying to stop a basket. Brooks rushed toward Green, leading to a physical exchange. Both players received technical fouls, while Green was ejected. After the game, Brooks said Green had been “tweaking” throughout the contest. Green took issue with that comment, accusing Brooks of trying to win public support rather than standing by his actions. Green also challenged Brooks to embrace the reputation he has built in the league instead of presenting himself as someone who was only trying to calm the situation. The Warriors eventually rallied for a 116-113 victory after Green’s ejection. Stephen Curry and Brandin Podziemski both said the incident gave the team extra motivation. The disagreement, however, appears far from settled. Green has made it clear he does not believe Brooks’ explanation of what happened. articles.summary: Disclaimer: When I wrote this predictions column, I was in no way under the influence of whatever the College Football Playoff selection committee partook of when compiling their initial rankings. (Alabama No. 5? Oregon No. 23?) I’m not under the influence and coming off another winning week (yes, o
articles._body: Disclaimer: When I wrote this predictions column, I was in no way under the influence of whatever the College Football Playoff selection committee partook of when compiling their initial rankings. (Alabama No. 5? Oregon No. 23?) I’m not under the influence and coming off another winning week (yes, only 5-4), but you can’t go broke making a profit every week. And 45-31 the past seven weeks. On to Week 10, using odds courtesy of Polymarket . Clemson at Syracuse Dabo Swinney reminded everyone this week that a Clemson win would make it 27 consecutive seasons the Tigers have won at least six games, including 18 with Swinney as head coach. The only other schools to do it: Ohio State , Georgia and Oklahoma , although I’m not expecting those schools to promote that stat. OK, maybe Oklahoma might. Bad news for Dabo: the Tigers won’t get that elusive sixth win this week. They visit red-hot Syracuse , which has covered four straight games as an underdog, winning the past two vs. North Carolina and SMU . Fran Brown has the Orange two wins from bowl eligibility. My Position : Syracuse to cover +3½ at 56% Iowa State at Baylor You might spot a trend in this week’s predictions: I am going against the field stormers. The majority of college football teams are rollercoasters: up one week, down the next. Iowa State stormed the field after upsetting Oklahoma State . Now, the Cyclones face a rejuvenated Baylor team that walloped UCF last week. Under interim coach Joe Klanderman , the Bears took advantage of a flat spot for the Knights, outgaining UCF by 222 yards. I don’t think it was a fluke. My Position : Baylor to cover -9½ at 50% Oregon at Ohio State I’m not sure what was more surprising: the College Football Playoff selection committee’s ranking of Ohio State at No. 12 or Oregon at No. 23. The Buckeyes are the nation’s only team with two road wins at current CFP Top 25 teams. Oregon is only 2-2 AD – After Dante (Moore) – escaping with late wins against Nebraska and Northwestern . The Buckeyes, in Luke Fahey’s second start, will expose the Ducks. My Position : Ohio State to cover -6½ at 58% Charlotte at UAB Both teams enter off losses: Charlotte suffered a heartbreaking OT loss to Tulane and UAB a misleading 20-point loss at South Florida in which the Bulls returned two UAB fumbles for touchdowns. UAB (4-4) can take a big step toward bowl eligibility, while any slim chances the 49ers (1-7) had for a bowl game were eliminated last week. My Position : UAB to cover -6½ at 58% Penn State at Washington The Nittany Lions stopped a four-game slide with last week’s win vs. Purdue . Penn State rolled up 457 yards, its most in Big Ten play this year, behind QB Rocco Becht and RB Cam Wallace (a career-high 135 yards). Meanwhile, the Huskies somehow, someway scored two TDs in a 12-second span in the final two minutes to beat Nebraska . Washington was outgained by 120 yards and benefited from three NU turnovers. Washington won’t be as fortunate two weeks in a row. My Position : Penn State to cover +3½ at 57% Louisiana Tech at Troy We’ll go back to the well with the Bulldogs , who were an easy winner for us last week. Louisiana Tech is 7-1 against the spread, the nation’s second-best mark behind only UCLA . Against Troy , the Bulldogs’ defense should dominate a pedestrian Trojans offense. Also, Troy is coming off a big upset at James Madison and should come back to Earth this week. My Position : Louisiana Tech to cover -4½ points at 54% Louisville at Georgia Tech Since the Yellow Jackets upset Duke – did that really happen? – they have lost three consecutive ACC games, all by double digits. They must win their final four games to become bowl-eligible. Louisville’s hopes to reach the College Football Playoff realistically ended with consecutive losses to Wake Forest and NC State . Since then, however, the Cards have won three straight featuring QB Lincoln Kienholz and an offense that leads the nation, averaging 7.8 yards per play. My Position : Louisville to cover -13½ points at 55% Colorado at Arizona State Here’s another play against a field stormer. Last week, Colorado was a favorite against Kansas State and defeated the Wildcats 27-24, leading to the Buffs’ fans running onto the field. Seems kinda weird doing so after winning a game you were supposed to win. I guess it’s almost as odd as retiring two players’ jerseys a few months after their playing careers ended. Anyway, Arizona State also beat Kansas State, but by 11 points, in its last home game (ASU didn’t storm the field). Freshman QB Jake Fette , who threw for two TDs in last week’s close loss at BYU , should continue his strong play. My Position : Arizona State to cover -2½ at 57% Iowa at Northwestern Iowa only ranks 14th out of 18 Big Ten teams in passing offense, which may not sound that great. Until you consider that the Hawkeyes had the Big Ten’s worst or second-worst passing offense in each of the past four seasons. Iowa and Northwestern’s offenses are similar statistically, but Wildcats QB Aidan Chiles may not be 100 percent. So, I’ll take the much better defense getting points. My Position : Iowa to cover +3½ at 57% Michigan State at Michigan This could be an old-fashioned Big Ten rock fight, featuring two of the nation’s worst offenses in yards per play. The Spartans rank No. 134, UM is No. 118. Sparty enters on a six-game losing streak and they have been injury-plagued at quarterback. Michigan has gone a different direction recently at quarterback with Tommy Carr taking over. The Wolverines’ last five games have all been decided by seven points or less. That streak ends Saturday. My Position : Michigan to cover -12½ at 52% Liberty at New Mexico State Since losing its opener at James Madison , the Flames have been, pardon the pun, on fire. Liberty has won seven consecutive games, the last six by an average margin of 28 points. They rank in the top 20 in the nation in scoring margin (30.3 points) and yards per game margin (229 yards). articles.title: U2’s Carnaval de Luz review: 50 years in, Bono, The Edge, Adam Clayton, and Larry Mullen Jr. can’t stop now
articles.summary: “Dinosaur, wonders why it still works the earth, yeah,” U2 singer Bono contemplated in the song “The Blackout” from their last proper album, Songs of Experience (released in 2017). U2, some of the last remaining titans of rock music, might have been doing some self-reflect
articles._body: “Dinosaur, wonders why it still works the earth, yeah,” U2 singer Bono contemplated in the song “The Blackout” from their last proper album, Songs of Experience (released in 2017). U2, some of the last remaining titans of rock music, might have been doing some self-reflection here, pondering what happens “when the lights go out.” Now, they are back with their first album of new music in almost a decade, Carnaval de Luz , out Nov. 13, 2026. So much has changed since then. A global pandemic hit, and President Donald Trump is back in office. U2 embarked on two tours, performed a 40-night residency at the Sphere sans Larry Mullen Jr. , and released Songs of Surrender, an album of 40 re-recorded songs from U2’s back catalog. Now, they are back at full strength on Carnaval de Luz. The boys—Bono, The Edge, Adam Clayton, and Mullen—from Dublin, Ireland, who celebrated their 50th anniversary in September, have returned with an exceptional album. Earlier in the year, the band released two phenomenal EPs: the politically charged Days of Ash and the reflective Easter Lily. Somehow, they saved the best for last. The world didn’t need a new U2 album. It needed this U2 album. It’s a little adrenaline-filled punk rock, a little upbeat beach rock, and completely hopeful. Bono once sang that the “future” needs a big kiss. With Carnaval de Luz, U2 is providing that glimmer of hope for the future, promising it’ll never go out because “all of us are better than any of us.” U2’s Carnaval de Luz review Photo courtesy of Michael Schwartz. Carnaval de Luz picks up where Easter Lily left off at the end of “COEXIST (I Will Bless the Lord at All Times?).” The Brian Eno-filled meditative lullaby ends with music’s equivalent of an MCU post-credits scene. After the song winds down, a buzzing noise is heard. It’s almost like something you’d hear on “Zooropa.” “Go (Carnaval de Luz)” opens the album, starting with more of those sounds. The best way to describe “Go (Carnaval de Luz)” is as a sci-fi Ramones punk-rock song. It’s one of three sub-three-minute songs on the album (which is not a bad thing). Length doesn’t matter; it’s about how much punch you pack in the time. U2 has been known to “dream it all up again,” and “Go (Carnaval de Luz)” is an adrenaline-filled wake-up call, as Bono, singing in his low register almost like he did on “The Fly,” sings, “Woke up in the scream, dreaming in the dream / So deep a sleep I had to wake up / My scar’s a lucky charm, you wrote it on my arm / The past and me have got to break up / Go!” Bono is like the carney to his carnival, and “Go (Carnaval de Luz)” welcomes you into this weird (complimentary) circus. He went from being the “preacher stealin’ hearts at a traveling show” to the carnival barker of said “traveling show.” The whole album is a call to action, and it starts on the opening track: “Welcome to tonight, a carnival of light / Illumination is the way to fight this / I’ve had it with the fear, can’t believe I made it here / Came to find the other people who feel like this.” Foot-stomping rockers The opening track leads to “La Reina,” a song written about a young girl completely naive to the world at large, dubbed the “face of the future,” not to be confused with the “Song of the Future,” inspired by Sarina Esmailzadeh. It’s a foot-stomping rock song that brings Achtung Baby—a timeless album—to the modern day. It’s hard to ignore how similar it sounds to “Even Better Than the Real Thing,” complete with multiple layers of vocals in the verses and Clayton’s groovy bass playing. “The Mirror Maker (Rosaliá)” opens with fittingly angelic falsetto, almost like “Iris (Hold Me Close).” They swirl as The Edge plays harmonic notes that sound like a throwback to the Boy and Joshua Tree Days of U2. This is one of two instances on the album where Bono’s whispering leads to a kickass guitar solo from The Edge before the “Rosaliá” refrains at the end. “When I was in the hall of mirrors I could only see my own face,” Bono whispers. “You can hate yourself, but I let it pass / I didn’t know what you know / In case of an emergency break the glass / In case of an emergency break the glass / And go through the mirror.” The carnival metaphor Photo courtesy of Rich Fury. The carnival is a clever metaphor for U2. A carnival can be a festive celebration, but it doesn’t have to feature acrobatics and bearded ladies. A carnival is a communal experience, much like the ones U2 creates with their concerts. Like a carnival, Carnaval de Luz has the glitz and glamor; just listen to Brian Eno’s soundscapes on “Go (Carnaval de Luz)” or “Can’t Stop Us Now.” There are also intimate numbers like “Torn,” which features Dolly Parton’s last recorded vocals, and “The Greatest Show on Earth.” “Superficiality” takes your mind to the carnival as the lights first go up with The Edge’s guitar. The song opens with ringing guitars like U2’s earliest work. This will also likely be a highlight when U2 plays it live on their next tour. This is maybe the closest (besides “Street of Dreams”) that U2 comes to a pop song on the album, but beneath the upbeat nature of the arrangement are deep lyrics (perhaps proving the point of the title). It’s a call for hope in times of despair, promising that the “news can’t break us.” There will be trials and tribulations, though. The carnival can also be a metaphor for the church. Christianity (and activism) can be performative, and Bono questions

articles.title: Stove God Cooks Finds Home for Highly-Anticipated Sophomore Album
articles.summary: The Upstate New York MC just dropped the project's second single alongside Swizz Beatz.
articles._body: Stove God Cooks has found a home for his much anticipated sophomore album. After a year of false starts, a scrapped Goat Stamp album, a February lead single in “Welcome to My Garden” and a previous March 27 release date , All This For Me? will be released early 2027 via Babygrande Records in partnership with Warner Records Billboard has exclusively learned. And while the Syracuse, N.Y. rapper has been keeping himself busy with features on songs like “ Live or Let Die ” with French Montana and Max B and “ The Aroma ” with Fat Joe and Jadakiss , he’s remained patient and is excited to finally give his fans a new full length album. “Everything played out exactly how it was supposed to,” he said in a press release. “Real power is knowing when to walk away! Even from something the world thinks you need. A lot of people are afraid to do that. I’m not one of them. When God has His hand on you, what’s meant for you can’t miss you. This new season isn’t luck! It’s confirmation! I’m excited about this next chapter and what we’re building with Warner Records, but even more excited to give my fans the music and the moment they’ve patiently waited for.” Chuck Wilson , founder and CEO of Babygrande Records used his industry connects to help find a home for this particular record after he and Stove renegotiated their initial deal. “I met Julian Petty from Warner a decade ago. I would send him Stove updates from time to time and at some point he took notice,” he recalled. “He reached out to me, Stove and I flew out to LA to meet Warner’s team and the vibe was great. This all paved the way for what I believe is a fantastic partnership that is beneficial to all parties. Relationships are everything in the music business.” All This For Me? will be fully produced by Swizz Beatz , who will also serve as the project’s executive producer. “You don’t often get to revisit the past but this was the rare opportunity to partner with one of my former law clients (Babygrande) to help propel one of hip-hop’s most compelling storytellers, Stove God Cooks,” adds Julian Petty, executive VP and head of business & legal affairs at Warner Records. You can stream the second single “ Stovie’s Home (Down Down) ” now.

articles.title: Oilers star Connor McDavid calls out ‘dangerous’ hit after tight loss to Ducks
articles.summary: Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid criticized a dangerous play by Anaheim Ducks defenseman Drew Helleson after being driven into the goalpost during Thursday’s 5-4 loss at Rogers Place. The incident occurred just over eight minutes into the opening period when McDavid accelerated toward
articles._body: Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid criticized a dangerous play by Anaheim Ducks defenseman Drew Helleson after being driven into the goalpost during Thursday’s 5-4 loss at Rogers Place. The incident occurred just over eight minutes into the opening period when McDavid accelerated toward the net and attempted to get past the Ducks defense. After Anaheim goaltender Laurent Brossoit knocked the puck away with a poke check, Helleson made shoulder-to-shoulder contact with McDavid, sending him crashing into the left goalpost . The 29-year-old centre remained on the ice momentarily before getting back up and confronting Helleson. He subsequently headed to the dressing room for an evaluation but returned to action later in the first period without an apparent injury. McDavid was particularly unhappy with the collision because of his previous injuries from similar situations. During his rookie campaign in 2015-16, he broke his collarbone after being sent into the end boards following a collision involving Philadelphia Flyers defensemen Michael Del Zotto and Brandon Manning. He missed 37 games because of that injury. In 2019, he also suffered a small PCL tear in his left knee after Calgary Flames defenseman Mark Giordano sent him into the goalpost during the final game of the regular season. Explaining his frustration after Thursday’s game, McDavid described such collisions as dangerous , especially when players approach the net or end boards at high speed. “Obviously it’s a play that is a little sensitive to me,” said McDavid. “Those are plays that I’ve been really really hurt on before, you know? Going into the end wall, going into the net. Those type of plays I find to be dangerous and obviously I didn’t love it. “When you’re going Mach 1 into the end wall or into the net, you know, those are dangerous plays in my opinion, and a situation that I find myself a lot in.” The incident also led to teammate Vasily Podkolzin to confront Helleson. Podkolzin landed several punches before officials separated the players. He received penalties for fighting and instigating, along with a game misconduct, resulting in his ejection. McDavid expressed appreciation for Podkolzin’s response but was unhappy with the resulting penalty decision. The confrontation also disrupted Edmonton’s forward combinations for the remainder of the contest. Even amid the chaos, McDavid once again showcased his brilliance , finishing with one goal and three assists in 24:25 of ice time. He extended his season-opening point streak to 17 games, collecting 44 points through 16 appearances, including 10 goals and 34 assists. His four-point performance also kept him on pace for 217 points, which would surpass Wayne Gretzky’s NHL single-season record of 215 points established in 1985-86. The Oilers faced a 5-2 deficit before scoring twice late in the third period to make the contest a one-goal game. However, Edmonton could not complete its comeback. The Ducks also capitalized on the penalty-filled contest, scoring twice on the power play. A total of 57 penalty minutes were assessed by the final buzzer, contributing to a game in which the Oilers never quite settled into a consistent rhythm at even strength. The post Oilers star Connor McDavid calls out ‘dangerous’ hit after tight loss to Ducks appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Binance Hackers Swap About $50 Million of Stolen XRP Mostly Into Bitcoin, Elliptic Says
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Hackers Swap About $50 Million of Stolen XRP Mostly Into Bitcoin, Elliptic Says Hackers tied to the record Binance theft have begun converting a large slice of the stolen XRP into bitcoin, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic said in an update dated through Friday, with about 42 million XRP — roughly $50 million — already swapped, mostly through THORChain. Converted bitcoin from other stolen assets nearly doubled overnight to about 1,650 BTC, worth some $124 million, Elliptic wrote . Most of that jump came from the XRP route. About 192 million XRP, roughly $226 million, remained unswapped in addresses linked to the Binance theft. The XRP was part of the Oct. 29 drain that Binance later put at $6.34 billion. Between 20:05 and 20:09 UTC that day, five hot wallets sent 233.46 million XRP to an attacker address. The FBI has attributed the campaign to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Binance has reopened withdrawals in stages and said it has frozen or intercepted about $2.85 billion while covering customer losses from its own funds. How the XRP started moving The stolen XRP sat quiet at first. Early on Nov. 2, between 02:12 and 04:00 UTC, all about 233 million XRP moved into six new addresses, where it stayed until Nov. 5, Elliptic said . From the afternoon of Nov. 5, two of those six addresses began sending XRP on to dozens of new accounts that swapped it, mostly through THORChain into bitcoin. A small amount of ether also went through THORChain into bitcoin that evening. The main bitcoin and ether holdings from the theft — the largest pools — have still not moved, Elliptic said. That pattern matches what the firm saw after the Bybit hack: turn freezable and mid-liquidity tokens into bitcoin first, then attempt cash-out later through OTC brokers. The broader laundering trail is already vast. Since the Binance theft, Elliptic has counted more than 20,000 wallets on 16 blockchains, at least 36 services and at least 65,000 transactions — roughly one new wallet every 30 seconds and one transaction every 10 seconds. About $3.11 billion remains in addresses linked to the Binance theft, mostly as ether and bitcoin. A negligible amount has likely been cashed out so far. Why XRP and bitcoin matter here Issuers can freeze many stablecoins. They cannot freeze XRP the same way, and they cannot freeze bitcoin. After Tether and Circle locked down large stablecoin tranches on Oct. 29, the attacker prioritized assets that sit outside that kill switch. Swapping XRP into bitcoin continues that logic: bitcoin is harder to claw back once it is fragmented across fresh addresses. All of the stolen SOL, about $87 million at Elliptic’s prices, has already been swapped, bridged or mixed, with much of it ending as bitcoin. Most early Tron laundering — about $220 million in TRX — has also run, a flow Bitcoin Magazine noted when covering the quiet shutdown of the T3 Financial Crime Unit before the hack. Only small parts of the main ether and NEAR piles have moved. Some converted bitcoin has gone into Wasabi-style coinjoins — about 33 BTC, or $2.5 million, since Nov. 1 — and about $1.1 million in ether and SOL entered the Privacy Cash pool before that service paused deposits. Elliptic said the speed points to conventional automation, not an AI agent making live decisions: fixed timing, set amounts, blind retries and new tactics introduced hours apart. U.S. bank supervisors have already checked in with lenders after the Binance breach. For bitcoin markets, the nearer question is how much more of the remaining ~192 million XRP — and eventually the parked ether — gets turned into BTC before anyone tries to cash out. The test now is whether THORChain operators and other bridges keep blocking the published attacker addresses fast enough to slow the XRP-to-bitcoin pipe, or whether the rest of that pile follows the same overnight path the first $50 million already took. articles.title: ‘Pick another protein’: A cattle rancher senator’s answer on beef prices could give Democrats their first Mississippi Senate win since 1982
articles.summary: Trump called affordability a ‘fake word.’ Scott Colom’s ad turned her ‘so many proteins’ line into the race’s defining moment.
articles._body: Three years ago, Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith made sure Scott Colom would not become a federal judge. Now, he may take her Senate seat. President Joe Biden nominated Colom, a district attorney in northeast Mississippi, to the federal bench in 2022, and Mississippi’s other Republican senator, Roger Wicker, supported him. Hyde-Smith blocked the nomination because of what she called his “opposition to legislation to protect female athletes” and because of past support from a PAC funded by George Soros. And so in 2025, Colom announced he would run against her . It’s been four years since that fated blocked nomination, and on Tuesday night, Colom led her by 1,138 votes in a state that hasn’t elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1982. While the race has yet to be called, it seems like the issue that got him in the lead was simply the price of beef. “So many options” In February, a TV reporter asked Hyde-Smith—herself a cattle rancher who was the former Mississippi Commissioner of Agriculture and Commerce and also married a fifth-generation cattle rancher—what Republicans were doing about rising beef prices. “You know, you have so many proteins to choose from,” she responded. The question wasn’t without a good reason: beef has gotten more expensive. The average pound of ground beef cost $6.79 in September, up from $5.55 when Trump returned to office in January 2025. And so in a widely-viewed political ad entitled “Pick another protein,” Colom’s campaign let her do the talking and used her February interview, juxtaposing that with people grilling and buying beef at the supermarket. “Pick another protein? She done lost her damn mind!” one woman says in a diner. A man grilling burgers says he’d “rather pick another senator instead.” The spot ends with Colom at his own kitchen table, laughing as he delivers the same line. On Thursday morning, following newfound popularity into the ad following the election and as results showed him with a razor-thin margin, Colom wrote in a post on X that it was “important people know the back story of this ad.” The Open Society’s Patrick Gaspard “gave me the idea to take her inexcusable gaffe and do something edgy with it that could get attention,” Colom wrote. Then, “my content creator Ryan Sayles “directed and edited it. He should be considered the breakout-star of this cycle. He’s going to be a giant in the media consultant game. He did GAME CHANGING work with SO little.” As of Thursday evening, seven counties Hyde-Smith carried in 2020 now favor Colom, who out-raised Hyde-Smith $5 million to a little more than $3 million after making the cost of living crisis the center of his campaign. No one talks about affordability Why a relative no-name challenger was able to out-raise an incumbent likely has to do with how Colom focused on wages, costs, hospitals and jobs—and how inflation was eating away at people’s stagnant earnings. There’s a name for this: affordability. It’s a word President Donald Trump has spent the past year telling Americans isn’t real. “The word ‘affordability’ is a con job by the Democrats,” he said at a Cabinet meeting last December. In June, at the G7 summit, he called it a “fake word made up by the Democrats,” as consumer prices rose at their fastest pace in three years. At a rally in July, he again repeated the mantra that it was something Democrats “made up.” Some Republicans had warned about dismissing the “affordability” issue. Pollster Frank Luntz said in December that Trump risked appearing out of touch if he kept calling affordability a “hoax” when Americans felt they were paying more. It’s not just Trump—it came up again just days before the midterms when a Texas Christian University student asked Vice President JD Vance at a town hall how young people could afford to start families when the average home costs more than $415,000. Instead of answering immediately, Vance joked that he was asked only one question about Ohio Sen. Jon Husted’s backside , before conceding that Republicans hadn’t done enough on affordability for young people. So come Tuesday, it was no shock that voters named the cost of living and government corruption as their top two issues in AP exit polls, after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress . A historic win If Colom wins, he’d be the first Democrat Mississippi has sent to the Senate since John Stennis won his last term in 1982. Stennis, who served from 1947 to 1989, voted against the Civil Rights Act of 1964. That same summer, President Lyndon Johnson, also a Democrat, signed the law knowing it could cost his party the South. “Well, I think we may have lost the south for your lifetime—and mine,” Johnson told his special assistant, Bill Moyers, that night, according to Moyers’s account to the Guardian. Moyers died in 2025. Among the counties now favoring Colom is Forrest County, home to Hattiesburg and named for Confederate general Nathan Bedford Forrest, the Ku Klux Klan’s first grand wizard. Colom would also be Mississippi’s first Black senator since Blanche K. Bruce, who was born into slavery in 1841 and served from 1875 to 1881. Because Mississippi is the only state that doesn’t allow recounts to be triggered automatically or requested by a candidate (so any challenge would go to court), the Democratic party is sending reenforcement to help with the remaining count. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Warriors’ Jimmy Butler’s lively sideline antics vs. Heat draw obvious relationship analogy
articles.summary: Jimmy Butler couldn’t hide his excitement during the Golden State Warriors’ 120-100 victory over the Miami Heat, and teammate Georges Niang had a hilarious explanation. The injured star, who has been working toward his return from a torn ACL, was particularly animated on the sideline
articles._body: Jimmy Butler couldn’t hide his excitement during the Golden State Warriors’ 120-100 victory over the Miami Heat, and teammate Georges Niang had a hilarious explanation. The injured star, who has been working toward his return from a torn ACL, was particularly animated on the sideline against his former team. Speaking after the win, Niang addressed Butler’s lively behavior, joking that the forward probably had extra motivation against Miami. “I wonder why,” Niang said when asked about Butler’s energy. He then offered a relationship analogy to explain the competitive feelings that can linger after leaving a team. “Do you want to see your ex do better than she was with you? Not really.” Niang, who has played for several NBA teams, admitted he understands wanting to prove something against a former organization. He also joked that Butler was probably listening to country music and screaming in the weight room. Beyond the jokes, Niang praised Butler’s character and generosity behind the scenes. He recalled how Butler welcomed teammates to San Diego home and continued checking on them despite his injury. Niang revealed that Butler even offered him help while recovering from his torn ACL, something that genuinely surprised the veteran forward. Butler’s enthusiasm also followed his playful Instagram trolling after the Heat victory, adding another entertaining chapter to his reunion with Miami. Although Butler remains sidelined, Niang’s comments highlighted how the Warriors star continues supporting his teammates while maintaining his trademark humor. His presence has provided Golden State with another source of leadership, showing that Butler remains invested in the team’s success even while facing a lengthy recovery. articles._body: The Atlanta Falcons will be playing against the Cincinnati Bengals this week, and there is a chance one of their players won’t be on the field. After serving an eight-game suspension, James Pearce Jr. was eligible to return this week , but he’s also dealing with a back injury that the team is monitoring, according to team reporter Tori McElhaney. “A change to the injury report: RB Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) has been ruled OUT. James Pearce Jr. is dealing with a back issue that the Falcons will monitor throughout the weekend, per Kevin Stefanski,” McElhaney wrote on X, formerly Twitter. The Falcons are hoping that they can get Pearce back so they can get a boost on the defensive end, specifically getting pressure on the quarterback. They’ve been fine at doing so throughout the season, but Pearce brings another level that they can help them become even better in that category. He showed that last season in his rookie year when he finished with 10 1/2 sacks. “I see it as a positive to add a good player to the mix,” Stefanski said via Daniel Fick of the Atlanta Journal-Constitution. “I think the way ‘Brick’ and the defensive staff have constructed this rush plan, obviously married up with the coverage plan, I think it’s beneficial to all parties to do your job. But adding another good player to the mix is a good thing.” James was suspended for eight games for violating the league’s personal conduct policy after he was arrested in February due to an altercation with his ex-girlfriend.
