articles.title: Balenciaga Deserved Martine Rose
articles.summary: A day after Balenciaga's short-lived creative director, Pierpaolo Piccioli, left, beloved British designer Martine Rose has been chosen to lead the house.
articles._body: Fashion’s worst-kept secret has finally been confirmed: Chemena Kamali is taking over Saint Laurent! Oh wait, sorry, no. Still waiting on that one. The real news is that Balenciaga dropped Pierpaolo Piccioli as creative director after only three collections — the latter of which was actually really good , but came too little, too late — and announced Martine Rose as his replacement a day later. It’s less a shakeup and more a recentering: Rose consulted on the brand under Demna pre-Piccioli, helping to shape the house’s menswear while juggling her own brand. In such a shaky period for the luxury market, and fashion writ large, it’s refreshing to see the powers that be at a brand hire a designer people actually shipped with the fashion house. Rose to Balenciaga feels like endgame after a wrong turn; the fashion equivalent of Belly finally dropping Jeremiah and ending up with Conrad Fisher on The Summer I Turned Pretty (spoiler alert, I guess). The British designer built a devoted following for a reason. Simply put: Rose has the sauce. She always offers something wholly original — fresh and unexpected, yes, but also tied to a British streetwear savvy that can’t be taught. See: surprise Stüssy collab riding gloves or, for her namesake brand’s Spring/Summer 2026 collection , skin-tight versions of menswear staples like jerseys and track jackets. She’s masterful at playing with proportion like Demna, but the end product feels familiar but twisted in a way that doesn’t come off as confrontational and, respectfully, edgelordy like what was on offer during the Georgian designer’s Balenciaga era. Rose’s larger sportswear-with-edge style has also won over the likes of Rihanna and Kendrick Lamar . Plus, those Nike Shox Mules ? They’ve been a staple choice for Berlin art-world baddies for years. Though the announcement is slightly blunted by the fact that everyone even tangentially interested in fashion has been waiting for this exact chain of events to commence for weeks, it’s no less historic. Rose isn’t just the first woman to take over in Balenciaga’s 109-year history; she’s also only the second Black woman to be named creative director at a major European fashion house. The first? Grace Wales Bonner for Hermès, announced only a year ago. (Bonner’s debut menswear collection for the brand will debut in January.) There’s no announcement yet on exactly when we’ll see Rose’s vision for Balenciaga hit the runway, but with this much goodwill at her back (plus the benefit of knowing the brand), this is one case of designer musical chairs that feels perfectly in tune. Bitcoin Price Holds Near $75,000 After Hot October Jobs Report
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Holds Near $75,000 After Hot October Jobs Report U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, nearly three times the 59,000 economists expected, the Labor Department said Friday, and the bitcoin price briefly pushed above $76,100 before settling near $75,500, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows. The unemployment rate edged down to 4.1% from 4.2%, beating the Dow Jones forecast that called for it to hold. Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% on the month and 3.1% over the year, both ahead of estimates, CNBC reported . Prior months were revised higher as well. August payrolls moved to 186,000, an upward revision of 53,000, and September rose to 60,000 after a 31,000 upgrade, leaving the two-month total 84,000 stronger than first reported. The print lands on a market still digesting Thursday’s Nasdaq-led rout. The bitcoin price had held near $76,000 into that close, dipped toward $75,200 late in the session, then recovered into the mid-$75,000s overnight before the 8:30 a.m. ET release. Spot bitcoin changed hands around $75,800 after the data, with a market cap of about $1.52 trillion and roughly $48 billion in trading volume over the past day, Yahoo Finance data indicated. Bitcoin price reaction Bitcoin price’s first move was a quick spike above $76,100, then a slide toward $75,600 before it settled back near $75,800. The range on the day has run from about $75,240 to $76,280, leaving the market little changed from its pre-release level even as rate futures repriced. That muted finish fits the pattern after big macro prints. Most of the damage to the bitcoin price this week came from equity risk-off, not from the labor market itself, and a hot payrolls number mainly reinforces the path the Fed was already pricing. CME FedWatch odds put roughly a 79% chance of a 25-basis-point hike at the Dec. 9 meeting after the release, up from about 70% into the open. The next employment report is due Dec. 4, five days before that decision, and the signal points the same way the last Fed hold did: stronger hiring and firmer wages leave less room for another pause. Tech rout aftermath and ETF outflows Thursday’s session still sets the floor under the bitcoin price. The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5.5% and dropped into correction territory, more than 10% below its recent high, while the S&P 500 lost about 4.4% and the Dow shed roughly 1,800 points, or 3.4%, CNBC reported . The Magnificent Seven erased more than $1 trillion in market value. Nvidia alone lost more than 9%, wiping out roughly $440 billion in capitalization, as investors priced in a slower AI data-center buildout after the Democratic midterm sweep. Bitcoin has traded with that AI-heavy complex for most of the year, so a correction in the Nasdaq has pulled the bitcoin price lower even when on-chain flows looked steady. Miners that leased power and floor space to AI tenants are caught in both trades. Fund flows followed the risk-off tape. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs posted $430.2 million in net outflows on Thursday, led by about $200 million from Fidelity’s FBTC and roughly $105 million from BlackRock’s IBIT, bringing week-to-date redemptions through Thursday to about $870 million. Leverage kept the bitcoin price soft into the overnight. More than $1 billion in crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, mostly long bets built during Wednesday’s short-squeeze bounce that lifted bitcoin near $80,000 . What comes next for bitcoin price Professional and business services led October hiring with 70,000 jobs, health care added 42,000, and transportation and warehousing gained 25,000. Manufacturing rose 19,000. The breadth undercuts the recent pattern in which health care carried most of the gains. Policy risk has not eased either. House Democrats are already drafting their own market structure bill ahead of taking the committees in January, a backdrop that has hung over crypto equities since the midterm results first hit the bitcoin price . Traders are watching whether the bitcoin price can defend the mid-$75,000 zone that held on election night and several times since August. A clean break would leave September’s low back in sight after a week that erased most of the post-election squeeze, now with a hotter labor market and firmer hike odds stacked on top. At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $75,500. This post Bitcoin Price Holds Near $75,000 After Hot October Jobs Report first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .

articles.summary: The 86-year-old singer told a crowd in Los Angeles on Wednesday (Nov. 4) that he had a near-death experience during his hospitalization.
articles._body: When Sir T om Jones contracted a nasty upper respiratory infection back in July that forced him to postpone a show in Germany , he apologized to disappointed fans and promised to make it up to them. But on Wednesday night (Nov. 4) during his rescheduled show at the Greek Theatre in Los Angeles on his Come Gather Round tour — which was originally scheduled for Oct. 26 and then postponed after Jones contracted the flu — Jones, 86, revealed that his latest health scare had him fearing the worst. “[I thought], ‘Oh, well, this is it,'” he told the crowd at the Greek, according to BBC News . “‘You’ve had a wonderful life, Tommy, but it’s over right now.” Jones reportedly spent a week at the Ronald Reagan UCLA Medical Center in Los Angeles due to the illness described at the time as a “ bad case of the flu ,” which resulted in the rescheduling of shows in L.A. and San Diego. He later had to reschedule another California show as doctors ordered more rest and then postponed gigs in Sacramento and San Francisco as well on doctor’s advice. “I must say this, in the UCLA, they really did a wonderful job. So I’m here,” he told the L.A. audience. “[The medical staff said] ‘What do you want to do now?’ I was there for a week. And I said, ‘I’ve got to get back on the stage.’ This is where I belong. I can’t live without this, believe me.'” Jones’ next scheduled show is a rescheduled gig at the Yaamava’ Theater in Highland, Calif. on Friday night (Nov. 6).

articles.title: Tulane gives up 15-point lead, lose to Jackson State in head-scratching moment
articles.summary: Days after Oklahoma’s shocking loss to East Texas A&M as massive favorites, it’s Tulane’s turn to submit their entry for the worst loss of the season. The Green Wave somehow conspired to lose to HBCU Jackson State 87-85 after leading by as many as 15 points in the first half
articles._body: Days after Oklahoma’s shocking loss to East Texas A&M as massive favorites , it’s Tulane’s turn to submit their entry for the worst loss of the season. The Green Wave somehow conspired to lose to HBCU Jackson State 87-85 after leading by as many as 15 points in the first half. And to make matters worse, they lost with a play made infamous by Michigan alum Chris Webber: they called a timeout when they had none left . Tulane calls a timeout they don't have with 1.6 seconds left and loses to Jackson State on technical FTs pic.twitter.com/NYWd9jyQHH — The Field of 68 (@TheFieldOf68) November 6, 2026 With the game tied at 85 and 11 seconds left, Tulane’s Krystian Lewis got the rebound off a blocked 3-point attempt. After bringing the ball up the court, Lewis picked up his dribble on the left win and was being pressured by a Jackson State defender. So he turned to the referee and called for a timeout. A couple members of the Tulane coaching staff instantly reacted, perhaps knowing that the team was already out of timeouts. However, it was too late. Jackson State was awarded two technical free throws with 1.6 seconds remaining. Senior Daeshun Ruffin stepped up to hit both free throws. TJ Nadeau missed a last-second 3-pointer for Tulane to give Jackson State the unlikely win, their first of the season. Dorian McMillian led the Tigers with 23 points and seven rebounds. Meanwhile, Ruffin added 17 points and eight assists amid a rough 4-of-15 shooting game. As for Tulane, they had six players finish in double digits. Carson Schwieger and Nadeau tied for the team high with 16 points apiece. Tulane will look to bounce back at home against Nicholls on Tuesday. As for Jackson State, they will travel to Starkville to take on Mississippi State on Monday. articles.title: Splice Reimagines the DAW With ‘Create’ — Its Agentic AI-Powered Platform for Newcomers
articles.summary: As the company's CEO, Kakul Srivastava, explains to Billboard, Splice Create is made to "not create a song for you, but to show you how to do it and collaborate with you."
articles._body: Splice has launched its first-ever digital audio workstation (DAW), featuring agentic and assistive AI features to help new producers learn the program and finish songs. Most notably, the DAW features a chatbot, offering production tips and following instructions from a producer’s voice or text prompts. It also offers a way to mix and match samples from the Splice library with greater ease. The company, known best for its library of more than three million human-made, licensed samples and loops, enters the DAW market at a time of disruption. While incumbent DAWs, like Ableton, Logic, ProTools and FL Studio, remain the market’s top players, new browser-based applications, like BandLab, have grown a fanbase in recent years, offering a simpler and cheaper option for the novice producer. Plus, as generative AI has taken hold, AI platforms like Suno and Moises have also leaned in to DAW features to provide users with more optionality after a track is generated. Related AI’s Second Wave, From Anxiety to Imagination (Guest Column) Kenny MacPherson, Veteran Music Publisher and Big Deal Music Co-Founder, Dies at 71 Diddy Moved From New Jersey Prison to Similar Facility in Pennsylvania Meanwhile, remixing and DJ-like features — which also encourage fans to customize their favorite songs — have never been of greater interest. Spotify , Udio, Klay and more are working on AI-powered music remix features. Both Spotify and Apple Music include DJ features in-app, and start-ups like Hook are working on licensed remix concepts for the TikTok generation. Despite all the buzz of generative AI, Splice has held steadfast on its commitment to providing only human-created samples, loops and instruments, instead, opting to use AI to better tailor and customize those samples by using it to better shift timbre, key, tempo and more. In 2023, Splice’s CEO, Kakul Srivastava , said in an interview with Billboard : “One of the things that we find disturbing about a lot of the work that is happening in generative AI is that it is ‘push button’ creativity,” she said. “For us, that’s eliminating the creative as opposed to putting tools into the creatives’ hands.” In that interview, she discussed Splice’s Create in its first form: an AI-powered tool to mix and match Splice samples to, hopefully, help producers begin the song creation process and help them find the perfect sample faster. Now, Create has morphed into a full-fledged DAW, thanks to its acquisition of Kits AI at the start of the year. The DAW still has that original mix-and-match product at its core to help users find a starting place, and it further employs AI to help producers navigate the tools and get toward their final master. In an interview with Billboard , Srivastava discusses the latest version of Create and why the company’s mission is to “not create a song for you, but to show you how to do it and collaborate with you.” Related Splice Partners With ElevenLabs to Create New AI Products I feel like a DAW is a natural extension for Splice. Why didn’t Splice work on a DAW earlier? Srivastava: We really wanted to go down the partnership route [with pre-existing DAWs], and part of it was recognizing that people have very sticky workflows, and so I was like, “Gosh, I don’t know if we’ll build a better version of these great products that already exist.” So we partnered with them, and we built these plugins for integration. What changed was this last year. It just felt like AI capabilities went so far that — for me as someone who’s worked in creative tools all of my career — I realized that this is really changing creative workflows in a big way, and I just didn’t see any of the other players leaning into it as aggressively as we thought we should, as we thought the industry should. We even talked to some of [the incumbent DAWs], and we said, “Hey, how about this? Is there a way we can partner with you to build these kinds of agentic capabilities?” There wasn’t a lot of interest, and so we almost felt like we had no choice except to build this because, I mean, I genuinely feel like this product needed to be built. Splice acquired Kits AI in January, and you’ve noted that the Kits team was instrumental in building this product, but my understanding was that Kits was a voice platform. What did their team bring to the table for Create? The Kits acquisition was as much of a technology acquisition as it was a team acquisition, and the people who have come over from the Kits side are just extraordinary. It seems like everyone is interested in DAWs right now. How do y’all plan on carving out a space that is uniquely Splice’s in this crowded market? I think relative to the [AI music] model companies, we have an edge because their superpower is around the model. They’re building a very thin application layer [with their DAWs], but it’s really about the model. For us, generative is actually not a very small part of this experience… I also think fundamentally that generative is tough for users who care about creative control, because you do a prompt, you get a song out, then you want to edit that song, and it’s very hard to get into the individual components to get fine-level control. Then you end up basically re-prompting, and that’s just a cumbersome, frustrating way to create. articles._body: While she made a splash at Game 4 of the NBA Finals in June, some players don’t think Taylor Swift is a real New York Knicks fan . During an appearance on Deflected, Tyler Kolek and Miles McBride played NBA 2K26. They were asked who the “fakest celebrity fan” is that they’ve seen at a game. Kolek had to answer since McBride made the next basket. He believes there are a lot of “performative” fans, especially ones like Swift. Q “Who’s the fakest celeb fan you’ve seen courtside?” Tyler Kolek “Maybe Taylor Swift?” Deuce McBride “I would agree…Swifties not gonna like that answer” Kolek “I’m gonna get some hate…I guess she’s got a lot going on…can’t come all the time…but it’s a little performative” pic.twitter.com/r7v4AJBK04 — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) November 5, 2026 “At the Knicks games, I would say it’s very performative ’cause they just want to be seen at the game; they’re not necessarily fans,” he said. “Maybe Taylor Swift. I don’t know if I’ve seen her at any other games.” McBride tried to warn his teammate, warning him, “Swifties not gonna like that answer,” though he agreed. Deuce did give a shoutout to some tried and true fans like Ben Stiller and Tracy Morgan. Kolek tried to save himself from the wrath of Swifties, acknowledging that the singer might have “a lot going on so she can’t come all the time.” Still, it’s “a little performative,” at the very least. When did Taylor Swift last go to a Knicks game? Brad Penner-Imagn Images. Swift last attended the Knicks’ dramatic 29-point comeback in Game 4 of the NBA Finals against the San Antonio Spurs. She sat next to Este and Alana Haim and Mariska Hargitay. Swift wore a themed shirt that read, “Stevie Knicks.” Just a few weeks earlier, she attended one of the Knicks’ wins against the Cleveland Cavaliers in the Eastern Conference Finals with her now-husband, Travis Kelce. They sat courtside for the Cavs’ 13-point loss. The Cavaliers would ultimately be swept in the series. The “Shake It Off” singer has strong ties to the Big Apple. She moved there years ago and wrote the anthem “Welcome to New York” for her 1989 album. She also married Kelce at Madison Square Garden, the Knicks’ home arena, in July 2026. articles.title: South Korean Crypto Exchange Gopax Suspends Withdrawals and Trading After Hacking Threat
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine South Korean Crypto Exchange Gopax Suspends Withdrawals and Trading After Hacking Threat South Korean cryptocurrency exchange Gopax suspended withdrawals and trading on Friday after receiving a hacking-threat email, and said it is moving all held virtual assets into offline cold wallets as a preemptive step to protect customer funds. Gopax halted standard deposit and withdrawal services at 2:55 p.m. local time and stopped trading at 3:53 p.m., Yonhap News Agency reported , citing the exchange. Direct withdrawals through the website and app are unavailable. Customers who want coins out must apply through the customer support center, where requests are processed manually after internal verification. “To ensure the safe custody of user assets, we plan to transfer all virtual assets to cold wallets for storage,” Gopax said in remarks carried by Seoul Economic Daily. “Direct withdrawals through the Gopax website or app are temporarily unavailable, and customers wishing to withdraw funds should apply through the Gopax customer support center.” No actual loss of assets has been reported. The company has not set a date to reopen trading or standard withdrawals. What Gopax closed and what still works With trading offline, all open orders were canceled, Chosun Biz reported . Deposits were initially paused with withdrawals; later Korean coverage said deposits had been restored while web and app withdrawals stayed shut. Manual withdrawals through support will take longer than usual. A cold wallet is a storage setup kept offline, cut off from the internet that hot wallets use to process customer sends. Gopax said the shift of remaining hot-wallet balances into cold storage is meant to shrink the surface available to anyone who can reach online systems. A Gopax official told Yonhap the email came from a party claiming it could hack the exchange, but that the threat itself had not been verified. “We ask for your understanding, as this measure is intended to prevent financial incidents and protect user assets,” the company said . A rough stretch for Korean crypto platforms The freeze lands in a week when exchange security is already under a bright light. On Oct. 29, attackers drained about $6.34 billion from Binance hot wallets in what Binance later described as a months-long campaign that began with a fake job interview. The FBI has tied that theft to North Korea; Binance has reopened withdrawals in stages and said it is covering customer losses from its own funds. Brazil’s Mercado Bitcoin froze deposits and withdrawals earlier this week after its own security incident, with preliminary estimates of suspicious transfers near $40 million. Gopax’s case is different on the facts disclosed so far: the exchange is describing a threat email and a precautionary lockdown, not a confirmed drain. Gopax itself has been dealing with account trouble. From early September, abnormal access hit some user accounts, leaking personal information on seven customers and two current or former employees, with further leakage confirmed last month, Yonhap’s Korean dispatch said. The company has treated that breach as separate from Friday’s threat email; any link has not been confirmed. South Korea’s Financial Services Commission has also been pressing domestic platforms after a broader wave of cybersecurity incidents across financial firms. Korean exchanges are already required to keep at least 80% of customer crypto in cold storage. Friday’s move pushes Gopax further offline while it checks whether the threat is real. For bitcoin holders on Gopax, the practical effect is a queue: coins are being parked offline while support staff approve outbound sends one by one. That is slower than an app button, and it is the trade the exchange says it is making to keep balances intact. The test for Gopax now is whether it can finish the cold-wallet transfer, clear the manual withdrawal queue without a loss, and say when trading comes back — or whether the unverified threat turns into the incident it was trying to get ahead of. This post South Korean Crypto Exchange Gopax Suspends Withdrawals and Trading After Hacking Threat first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .

articles._body: Ahead of the absolutely loaded Week 10 college football slate, Josh Pate has released his weekly JP Poll . The Georgia Bulldogs , coming off a bounceback 27-8 win over No. 17 Florida in Atlanta last Saturday, top the ratings. They are still viewed more favorably than any other team by the model’s neutral-field favorability rating. The biggest riser in this week’s JP Poll was South Carolina , who jumped from No. 25 to No. 17. After opening the season with a 2-3 record, the Gamecocks have now rattled off three consecutive victories. The biggest faller in this week’s JP Poll was Louisville , which fell from No. 16 to No. 22. The Cardinals have also rattled off three consecutive wins after opening the season 2-3. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage This week’s ratings consist of 10 SEC teams, six Big Ten teams, five Big 12 teams, three ACC teams, and Notre Dame . Five of the 10 SEC teams present reside in the Top 10 of the ratings. 1. Georgia Bulldogs (7-1, 5-1) – Georgia bounced back from its stunning 27-24 home loss to Auburn two weeks ago with a strong 27-8 win over No. 17 Florida on Saturday. The Bulldogs dominated that matchup, out-gaining Florida 318-252 and winning the turnover battle 4-1. Georgia now sits at 7-1 (5-1) on the season, atop the SEC rankings alongside Kentucky . Kirby Smart ‘s team heads into the final stretch of the regular season, in which it is slated to face three ranked opponents over its final four games. That includes No. 10 Ole Miss, No. 18 Missouri , and No. 21 South Carolina , before closing out the regular season against a disappointing Georgia Tech squad. The Bulldogs are seeking their fifth CFP appearance in the past six seasons. 2. Miami Hurricanes (8-0, 6-0) +2 For the second time in three weeks, Miami suffered a serious scare at the hands of an ACC opponent. The Hurricanes held off Florida State 43-35 in 2OT on Oct. 17, and held off North Carolina 38-35 last Saturday. Although the ‘Canes have been pushed to the limit as of late, they head into the month of Nov. with an unblemished 8-0 record. Their win set up a monstrous matchup this weekend against No. 11 Notre Dame , in a rematch from last year’s regular season game. The ‘Canes won that game, which ultimately earned them the final CFP at-large bid last season. It will be a large task for Mario Cristobal ‘s team to win this weekend in South Bend, however, especially with star Malachi Toney out for the game. Toney is undergoing tightrope surgery and will be out 4-6 weeks. 3. LSU Tigers (6-2, 3-2) – It’s safe to say LSU has been absolutely dialed in since its disappointing 35-34 OT loss at Kentucky on Oct. 10. Since then, the Tigers have dominated No. 16 Mississippi State 31-0 and Auburn 38-17. That win over the Tigers came one week after their road win at No. 1 Georgia . Lane Kiffin ‘s team looks to be rolling at the perfect time. They’ll return to the gridiron at home this Saturday against No. 5 Alabama , in a game that will hold massive College Football implications. LSU is seeking its first CFP appearance since 2019, when it won the National Championship. 4. Notre Dame Fighting Irish (7-1) -2 Although the Irish started off slow in Saturday’s game against Navy , Notre Dame was able to come away with a dominant 35-13 victory. That improved their record to 7-1 on the season ahead of this Saturday’s game against No. 1 Miami . Notre Dame is seeking its first win over the No. 1 ranked team in the country since it knocked off No. 1 Clemson 47-40 in 2OT on Nov. 7, 2020. If Notre Dame can end Miami ‘s undefeated season on Saturday, it would put itself in a stellar position to return to the College Football Playoff. If they fail to take down the ‘Canes, that would put their Playoff hopes in real danger. Following that game, the Irish close out their regular season against Boston College , SMU , and Syracuse . Without a win over Miami , Notre Dame might just not have the resume needed to sneak into the 12-team field. 5. Texas Longhorns (6-2, 3-2) +2 Texas has rebounded from its two-game losing streak ( Oklahoma and Florida ) in a massive way, as its racked up wins over No. 7 Ole Miss and Mississippi State over the past two weeks. The Longhorns held off the Rebels 34-27 two weeks ago, and dominated the Bulldogs 31-3 on Saturday. They now sit at 6-2 on the season, and remain right in the thick of the College Football Playoff race. These next two weeks will be extremely important for Texas ‘ CFP hopes, as it will play back-to-back road games against No. 18 Missouri and No. 14 LSU . After that, Texas will close the regular season against Arkansas and Texas A&M . A three-loss Texas team could very well find itself in the CFP, thanks to the strength of the Longhorns’ schedule. 6. Ohio State Buckeyes (6-2, 4-1) -1 Ohio State fell just one spot in this week’s JP Poll after it was stunned 30-18 by USC in Los Angeles Saturday night. The loss ended their 13-game winning streak against Big Ten opponents. Although Ohio State out-gained the Trojans 464-338 in the defeat, it still found itself losing by 12 points. That marked the program’s biggest margin of defeat (12) since Nov. 26, 2022, when it fell to No. 3 Michigan 45-23. Ohio State now finds itself in dangerous waters heading down the stretch of the regular season, with matchups against No. 23 Oregon , Northwestern , Nebraska , and Michigan still looming. Dropping just one of those games would put the Buckeyes in serious jeopardy of missing the College Football Playoff for just the second time in the past five seasons. 7. Alabama Crimson Tide (6-2, 4-2) +3 Alabama slots in at No. 7 in this week’s JP Poll, up three spots from last week, following its 31-20 home victory over Texas A&M two weeks ago. articles.title: Joe Milton’s instant reaction to getting QB1 nod in Week 9 for Eagles
articles.summary: Joe Milton has spent the past few weeks learning a new offense after joining the Philadelphia Eagles from the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad. Now, he has a much bigger responsibility ahead of him. The Eagles have named Milton their starting quarterback for Sunday’s Week 9 matchup agai
articles._body: Joe Milton has spent the past few weeks learning a new offense after joining the Philadelphia Eagles from the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad. Now, he has a much bigger responsibility ahead of him. The Eagles have named Milton their starting quarterback for Sunday’s Week 9 matchup against the New York Giants. The 26-year-old will make his first NFL start after Philadelphia benched Tanner McKee following three consecutive losses. Milton said Thursday that he had already been preparing for this kind of opportunity before leaving Dallas. “You never know what can happen in NFL,” Milton said. “That’s kind of how I took it… I was just pretty much going through the plays, going through the week like I was a starter or like I was playing, and just being ready. And that’s what NFL is about: just being ready when your name is called and just preparing for those moments. And I’ve been preparing and still preparing for the week.” Milton joined Philadelphia on Oct. 16 after Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve . Although he has had only three weeks to learn offensive coordinator Sean Mannion’s system, he believes its West Coast concepts are similar to the offense he played in as a rookie in New England. Asked how much of the playbook he had learned, Milton laughed before responding, “Shoot, whatever’s in this week.” The Eagles will need him to adjust quickly. Philadelphia has lost six straight games and sits at 2-6. Milton brings considerable arm strength and mobility, but his experience in Mannion’s offense remains limited. articles.title: Falcons adjust Week 9 injury report for Bengals game in Madrid with Brian Robinson Jr. downgrade
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons are gearing up for a huge international game this weekend. Atlanta will face off against Cincinnati from Madrid in a game that must feel like a must-win for both teams. Unfortunately, the Falcons will not have one of their offensive weapons on Sunday after their latest injury
articles._body: The Atlanta Falcons are gearing up for a huge international game this weekend. Atlanta will face off against Cincinnati from Madrid in a game that must feel like a must-win for both teams. Unfortunately, the Falcons will not have one of their offensive weapons on Sunday after their latest injury update. The Falcons made a few changes to their injury report ahead of Week 9 on Friday. Running back Brian Robinson Jr. has been ruled out for the Madrid game because of a hamstring injury, per Falcons reporter Tori McElhaney. Robinson was limited in practice on Thursday, which created some hope that he could play in Week 9. Robinson has not played since Week 6 against the Bears. Since then, the Falcons have pulled off a massive upset over the 49ers and a shutout loss against the Buccaneers. That shows that Atlanta can win games without Robinson, they tend to perform better when he’s on the field. The 27-year-old running back has 53 carries for 211 rushing yards and four touchdowns on the season while backing up Bijan Robinson. EDGE rusher James Pearce Jr. is also dealing with a back issue. Atlanta will monitor his status throughout the weekend before making a decision on him, per head coach Kevin Stefanski. Pearce is officially eligible to return from his 8-game suspension against the Bengals. In other Falcons injury news, rookie wide receiver Zachariah Branch is also ruled out for Week 9. He is also dealing with a hamstring issue. But in positive news, cornerback Billy Bowman Jr. has been cleared to play despite his hamstring injury. He was a full participant at practice this week, which were held at Real Madrid training grounds. It will be exciting to see if Atlanta can get a huge Week 9 win in front of an international audience. Falcons at Bengals kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET on Nov 8 from Santiago Bernabéu in Madrid. articles.title: Last-minute fantasy football streaming options for NFL Week 9: Running Back
articles.summary: Finding a dependable running back on the waiver wire becomes increasingly difficult as the fantasy football season progresses. Injuries and changing backfield rotations can create unexpected opportunities. Week 9 is no exception, with several players emerging as potential streaming options after
articles._body: Finding a dependable running back on the waiver wire becomes increasingly difficult as the fantasy football season progresses. Injuries and changing backfield rotations can create unexpected opportunities. Week 9 is no exception , with several players emerging as potential streaming options after impressive performances or increased involvement. Whether you’re dealing with injuries, bye-week absences, or an underperforming starter, these four running backs deserve consideration before setting your Week 9 lineup . Tyler Allgeier, ARI (@ SEA) Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Tyler Allgeier could be one of the most valuable waiver-wire additions heading into Week 9 . He rushed 11 times for 147 yards and a touchdown while catching all five of his targets for another 44 yards. It was a massive breakthrough for Allgeier. He had not rushed for more than 50 yards in his previous six contests. He took full advantage of an Arizona backfield dealing with injuries to Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight. Allgeier turned increased opportunities into 191 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns. The biggest question now is whether that workload will continue. If Love and Knight remain sidelined for Arizona’s Week 9 matchup, Allgeier could once again handle a substantial share of the backfield touches. Remember that volume matters at running back. Allgeier should be considered a strong streaming option with significant upside. Jonah Coleman, DEN (@ CAR) Jonah Coleman is quickly becoming one of the more intriguing running back options in fantasy football. He rushed 11 times for 41 yards and a touchdown while catching four of five targets for 63 yards in Week 8. What makes Coleman’s performance particularly encouraging is his growing role in the Broncos’ backfield. He led Denver’s running backs in carries for the second consecutive game. He even had more touches than JK Dobbins in Week 8. Coleman also delivered the game-winning touchdown with approximately two minutes remaining. The workload comparison is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore. Across the last two games, Coleman has recorded 24 carries compared to 13 for Dobbins. That suggests that Denver is becoming more comfortable featuring him. That development puts Coleman firmly into the weekly fantasy football starter conversation. The Week 9 matchup against Carolina offers another opportunity to build on his momentum. Coleman’s receiving involvement also gives him additional value in PPR leagues. Managers searching for a running back streamer should strongly consider adding Coleman before his workload becomes even more valuable. Devin Singletary, NYG (@ PHI) Devin Singletary made the most of his limited opportunities in the Giants’ 27-21 victory over Houston. He rushed for 41 yards and a touchdown on just five carries. Singletary’s performance becomes more interesting when considering the Giants’ injury situation. Both Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy sustained injuries during the contest. That potentially creates additional opportunities in the backfield. If Skattebo or Tracy miss additional time, Singletary could become a much more relevant option. His experience and ability to capitalize on limited touches make him worth monitoring, particularly in deeper leagues. Woody Marks, HOU (@ LAC) Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Woody Marks offers another potential streaming option. He carried the ball 19 times for 66 yards in the Texans’ loss to the Giants. The overall production was not spectacular. Marks failed to break off a major run or find the end zone. That left fantasy football managers without the kind of scoring boost that can turn a high-volume performance into a strong outing. Nevertheless, his workload is encouraging. Marks was clearly the Texans’ primary ball carrier. That kind of volume gives him a potential path to fantasy relevance, even if his efficiency needs to improve. Houston now emerges from its bye week against the Chargers. For now, Marks is worth considering in deeper leagues. That’s particularly true for managers who prioritize opportunity over immediate production. However, his fantasy outlook will depend heavily on Houston’s backfield health after the break. Final Takeaway Allgeier and Coleman are the two most appealing immediate streaming options. That’s thanks to their recent production and expanding opportunities. Singletary is worth considering, while Marks offers volume but faces uncertainty. Monitor late-week injury updates, prioritize workload, and make your waiver decisions before these opportunities disappear. articles.title: Argentine Bitcoiners Debut “The Genesis of Satoshi Nakamoto” Artwork in Downtown Buenos Aires
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Argentine Bitcoiners Debut “The Genesis of Satoshi Nakamoto” Artwork in Downtown Buenos Aires “The Genesis of Satoshi Nakamoto,” a 2.4-meter, multi-dimensional cube, was presented on October 29 at Polo Dot as part of the Open Fest of LABITCONF 2026 . Driven by Bitcoin.ar through the Premio B·Arte, the work combines art, technology, and education in a journey through Bitcoin’s fundamental principles. The inauguration featured guided remarks by Rodolfo Andragnes and a musical performance by Mayumaná, according to an announcement by the organization. Buenos Aires now has a monument dedicated to Satoshi Nakamoto, the person—or group of people—behind the creation of Bitcoin, whose identity remains unknown.  Driven by Bitcoin.ar through the fifth edition of the Premio B·Arte, the monument was conceived not only as a tribute to Satoshi, but also as an artistic and educational experience. Through its five faces—four lateral and one upper—it proposes a journey to approach different concepts that explain Bitcoin’s origin, functioning, and philosophy. During the inauguration, Rodolfo Andragnes — co-founder of Bitcoin.ar and LABITCONF — accompanied the public with words and explanations about the details of the work, guiding the reading of its various elements and the meaning behind each representation. The presentation was accompanied by a musical show by Mayumaná, which added rhythm and sound to the opening of this new space dedicated to Bitcoin’s history. Five faces to discover Bitcoin’s history and principles Each of the monument’s faces offers a gateway to a different aspect of Bitcoin. The figure of Satoshi Nakamoto, for example, represents the anonymous character of its creator and the collective dimension of a technology that, once set in motion, continued to grow thanks to thousands of people distributed around the world. The reflections and multiplied geometric forms also evoke the structure of a network that replicates and expands. Another of its faces addresses Bitcoin’s programmed scarcity through a cube that successively divides into halves in a Fibonacci sequence. The representation refers to “the halving”, the mechanism that approximately every four years halves the reward miners receive for validating blocks and that regulates the issuance of new bitcoins. Starting at 50 bitcoins per block, the total reward gets cut in half every four years for roughly 130 years, until 21 million bitcoins have been emitted and the block reward becomes zero. This supply limit is iconic to the cryptocurrency and key to its qualities as hard money. The work also incorporates the first words of Bitcoin’s foundational document, the white paper published by Satoshi Nakamoto in October 31st,  2008. There, the possibility of making electronic payments directly between people, without needing to go through a financial institution, is proposed. That idea constitutes a foundational principle of the technology. Another face reproduces information from the genesis block, the first block of the Bitcoin chain, created on January 3, 2009. Among its elements appears the reference to the headline from The Times newspaper that Satoshi incorporated into that block, a historical mark that places Bitcoin’s birth in its context and anchors it to history and time. Finally, on the upper part are two expressions that synthesize principles associated with this technology: “Don’t trust, verify”, an invitation to check information for oneself, rather than trust at face value. And “Vires in numeris,” Latin for “strength in numbers,” which refers to the safety of the crowd when it comes to privacy, as well as the self-evident, self-asserting strength of a money built and defended by cryptography rather than authority or military might. Thus, the monument proposes something more than contemplating a sculpture: it invites one to walk around it, observe it from different angles, and discover the concepts behind each of its parts; “The intention is to bring Bitcoin closer to those who are already part of its community, but also to awaken the curiosity of those who do not yet know its history.” A collective work that connects art, technology, and education The monument was created by Ricardo Alonso, engineer, and Celeste Difabio Videla, architect, a couple of artists from Bariloche who won the fifth edition of the Premio B·Arte. The work measures 2.40 meters in width, length, and height, and is made of stainless steel and glass.  Its construction involved teams and collaborators from different localities across the country, in a process that combined different trades, materials, and techniques. Aída Pippo, visual artist, researcher of new technologies applied to art, and member of the Board of Directors of Bitcoin.ar, led the project and coordinated the different stages of production and assembly. “It gives me great pride to feel that this is something we can leave in our city and in our country,” Andragnes expressed during the presentation, highlighting the value of a collective initiative that seeks to leave a cultural and educational footprint. For their part, the creators noted that they sought for the work to function as a meeting point for the community and, at the same time, as a gateway for those who do not yet know Bitcoin. “You don’t always have the possibility of leaving something for posterity,” they shared when speaking of the experience of seeing the monument finished and installed in Buenos Aires. With this inauguration, Bitcoin.ar seeks for the monument to become a permanent resource for the city: a space that schools, universities, families, and visitors can approach to learn Bitcoin’s history, discover its principles, and open new conversations about the future of money and technology. The intention is that what is presented today as an artistic work can continue to grow through educational activities and new experiences, and remain in Buenos Aires as a legacy for future generations. articles.title: Wynonna Judd to Receive ASCAP Golden Note Award: ‘A Singular, Powerhouse Voice’
articles.summary: Previous recipients include Garth Brooks, LeAnn Rimes, Reba McEntire and Alan Jackson.
articles._body: Wynonna Judd is set to receive the ASCAP Golden Note Award at the ASCAP Nashville Songwriters Celebration on Monday, Nov. 16, in Nashville. The invitation-only celebration recognizes the songwriters and publishers of the past year’s most-performed ASCAP country and Christian songs. Previous recipients of the ASCAP Golden Note Award, which celebrates extraordinary career milestones achieved by songwriters, composers and artists, include Garth Brooks, Tom Petty, LeAnn Rimes, Lee Ann Womack, Reba, Alan Jackson and Don Williams. Related Wynonna Showcases Her Songwriting Talents, Shares Her ‘Hard Truth’ on New Album: ‘I Turned My Pain Into Purpose’ Queens of the Stone Age Crowned on ARIA Chart With 'Perfecth' Lil Baby Brings 'Fresh' to Life: Stream It Now “Wynonna’s legendary career is defined by a singular, powerhouse voice and a rich body of work that has permanently shaped the landscape of American music,” Paul Williams , ASCAP chairman of the board/president, said in a statement. “As we honor her with the ASCAP Golden Note Award, we celebrate a true trailblazer whose soulful, unmistakable sound continues to inspire generations of music creators.” The Judds — in which Wynonna teamed with her late mother Naomi — received nine CMA Awards: the Horizon Award in 1984, single of the year for “Why Not Me” in 1985 and seven consecutive awards for vocal group (later, duo) of the year, from 1985-91. The Judds amassed 14 No. 1 hits on Billboard ’s Hot Country Songs chart and four No. 1s on Top Country Albums. As a solo artist, Wynonna has also logged multiple No. 1 hits on both of those charts, including four singles and three albums. The Judds were inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in April 2022. In a heartbreaking turn of events, Naomi Judd took her own life the day before the induction ceremony. Last month, Wynonna released her ninth solo studio album, The Hard Truth , via ANTI- Records. The 10-track project marked her first time co-writing an album. Wynonna is currently on the road on The Hard Truth tour, a 33-date tour across North America.

articles.title: How a Foot Injury & ‘Midlife Crisis’ Led to Kings of Leon’s ‘Therapeutic’ New Album ‘O My Beloved’
articles.summary: "It felt like something that I had buried down and hadn't really addressed," frontman Caleb Followill tells Billboard.
articles._body: It was bad news when Kings of Leon frontman Caleb Followill broke his foot while playing tag with his children in spring 2025, forcing the group to cancel planned tour dates in the U.S. and Europe. But the incident also provided the first step toward O My Beloved , the Grammy-winning Nashville quartet’s 10th studio album, out Friday (Nov. 6) on the group’s own Love Tap Records — a gentler and more reflective 13-song set that’s the first to be produced by the band itself. “That foot injury was a midlife crisis kind of deal,” says Followill, who formed Kings of Leon with his brother, drummer Nathan Followill, in 1999 (they were joined three years later by brother Jared and cousin Matthew Followill). “At first it was a lot of self-pity and also guilt, ’cause I felt like I was letting everyone down. After a little bit of that, I did grab the guitar and I started to play and the first thing that came out of that ended up being ‘My Whole World,'” O My Beloved ‘s lead single. “It just felt different,” Followill tells Billboard over Zoom. “I didn’t feel like I was writing something that I was necessarily going to put out into the world; it just felt therapeutic, and it felt like something that I had buried down and hadn’t really addressed. So that song came very naturally and very quickly. I just kept writing and the songs that came after that all had that same feeling.” The tunes were decidedly not in the vein of most of the band’s catalog, including Billboard Hot 100 hits such as “Sex on Fire” and “Use Somebody,” even though Followill notes that “we have always had these moments on each of the albums where we bring it back to our roots, which is more songwriter-driven.” He expected that his new batch of material would be voted down and the troupe would go back to “the Kings of Leon thing which people expect to hear — the rock songs, the fast, up-tempo kind of stuff.” To his surprise, however, that wasn’t the case. “I was expecting to be met with a little hesitation, a little, ‘Let’s not try to switch up what people have come to expect,'” Followill recalls. “But it was the opposite. I feel like we’re all at the same place and we all felt like, ‘Yeah, it’s time to let the songs shine.’” Working in its Neon Leon studio in Nashville, Followill says the group’s approach was “to feel the room that we were recording in.” That included sounds from trains rolling through a station across the street, which seeped into the recordings. “There’s trains all over the album,” he confirms. “You can hear a lot of walls rattling, but I think that adds something. It feels like a reverb or something.” He notes there was no thought of scrubbing that from the tracks. “It’s not perfect, and we didn’t want it to be,” Followill explains. “We didn’t want bells and whistles. We didn’t want loud pedals and reverb and all the things that can make something sound better. We tried to avoid that. We just wanted the songs to shine.” The result is an album that’s unlike anything else in Kings of Leon’s catalog. O My Beloved ‘s songs are mostly mid-tempo and melody-forward, with an acoustic underpinning and careful nuances enhanced with strings, keyboards and hand percussion. Electric guitars — whether it’s the airy slides in “My Whole World,” the biting solo in “Cold Blue Dawn” or the soaring break in “Feel the Love” — embellish rather than the drive the tracks, making for an ambience that Followill says was wholly intentional in the process. “Whatever we were playing, we wanted it to feel like a four-piece,” he notes. “At first we thought we were just making demos…but in the process, we would listen back and we were like, ‘I think this is better than demos.'” That, in turn, led to the decision for the band to produce O My Beloved itself. “We felt like if we brought someone in, we were going to be fighting to make it sound like (it does), and we’re already getting there ourselves,” Followill explains. “We were just in our little paint factory, and the sounds we were getting were so authentic. We got to a place where it was like, ‘We don’t want anyone coming here. We want to do this ourselves. We want that challenge. We want to meet that opportunity.’ It was so freeing to have our own space and work on our own schedule and do things the way we wanted to do it.” O My Beloved also takes a different lyrical bent — sentimental, philosophical and at times nostalgic, set off by occasional “threads of darkness” that represent the journey taken to the positive outlook that pushes through. At the same time, Kings of Leon end the album with Followill acknowledging “I think we still have a lot we’d like to learn” in “Get You Down.” “I know we use the word gratitude a lot, but I don’t really know how else to describe it,” Followill says. “I felt like I was just looking back on our accomplishments, and outside of music — at our life and who we’ve become as men and fathers. There was a lot of appreciation and pride for that and the potential to continue doing what we do, because I feel like we’re at a place now where we love it more than we ever have.” In addition to “My Whole World,” the group has advanced the album with the singles “KOYSAR” and “Cold Blue Dawn,” the latter accompanied by an inventive lyric video created with the Weather Channel using NASA satellite topography to spell out the words. The group will be in London for a show on Nov. 10 and Abu Dhabi on Dec. 3. Australia is on tap

articles.title: WME Signs BLACKPINK’s JISOO for Worldwide Representation
articles.summary: The K-pop star joins WME just days after the release of “Addicted,” the second pre-release single from her forthcoming debut solo album.
articles._body: BLACKPINK ‘s JISOO has signed with WME for worldwide representation. Announced Friday (Nov. 6), the K-pop superstar joins the WME roster just days after the release of “Addicted,” the second pre-release single from her forthcoming debut solo album. Earlier, in September, she dropped the single “ Click ,” and a third solo song is expected in the weeks ahead, “Sun Showers,” an original number that will appear on the The Angry Birds Movie 3 soundtrack, according to The Hollywood Reporter . As a member of the record-busting BLACKPINK, JISOO completed the sold-out Deadline World Tour earlier this year, a trek that stopped in major stadiums across North America, Europe and Asia. Adjacent to her pop career, the in-demand South Korean artist has a growing profile in film and fashion. She’s the global ambassador for Dior, Cartier, Tommy Hilfiger and Salomon; was appointed the face of ALO Yoga, and in 2024 became the first musician to be the face of the London fashion house Self-Portrait ; she landed a starring role in the Netflix romcom Boyfriend on Demand , which premiered in March; and recently launched brand collaborations with Off-White and Pokémon. It’s been full speed ahead for JISOO, who teased her new solo chapter last year with  “ EYES CLOSED,” a collaboration with  ex-One Direction star Zayn . The single reached No. 72 on the Billboard Hot 100. With that effort, BLACKPINK became the first girl group to have every member enter the Hot 100 as a solo artist. BLACKPINK released the DEADLINE  EP in February of this year, after completing the tour of the same name. DEADLINE opened at No. 8 on the Billboard 200, and marked their first major music release since hitting No. 1 on the all-genres albums tally with 2022’s Born Pink . JISOO began her solo journey in 2023, with the release of her debut EP,  ME , which became the first album by a female solo artist in South Korea to surpass one million sales. Its single, “꽃(FLOWER),” powered to No. 2 on the Billboard Global 200 in April of that year, and No. 1 on the Global Excl. US chart. A debut mini album arrived in 2025,  AMORTAGE , and included songs “earthquake” and “Your Love. When her album proper arrives, expect the full package. “Since I’m preparing a full-length album this time, I’m working on showing a wider range of music,” she told V Magazine   for an interview published in May . “I think I’d be really happy if people listen to this album and say they discovered a new side of me.” At WME, JISOO joins a stable of artists that includes Andrea Bocelli, Billie Eilish, Bob Dylan, Bruno Mars, Chris Stapleton, Coldplay, Depeche Mode, Foo Fighters and many others.

articles.title: Show HN: Grid – A Hold'em arena where your AI agent plays your strategy (Beta)
articles.summary:
Hi HN, my friend's team and I have been building a game called GRID, a dog poker game with an AI twist.

Under the cute dog graphics, GRID is an arena where LLMs compete, with no-limit hold’em as the medium. You duke it out as a strategist, vibe coder, and bot maker.

Why: models get compared o
articles._body: Hi HN, my friend's team and I have been building a game called GRID, a dog poker game with an AI twist. Under the cute dog graphics, GRID is an arena where LLMs compete, with no-limit hold’em as the medium. You duke it out as a strategist, vibe coder, and bot maker. Why: models get compared on benchmarks all the time, but rarely as my agent against yours in its truest form. GRID is our attempt at creating that arena, because we believe this type of game will exist in the future, as AI becomes as common a tool as the browser. How it works: * Paste a prompt and an MCP config into Claude Code, Codex or any MCP client. The agent waits for its turn and sends actions back through tool calls. * The strategy is text written in the game, up to 6,000 characters. We thought it’d be cool to have a preset, “Play like Elon”, to show you what you can do. * You can change the strategy any time, and it applies from the next action. You can even ask your AI to change it for you, based on what it learns about its opponents’ strategies from the match history. * Free beta. Play chips only. We just opened up the game today and are gathering data on how to steer this ship next. Rough edges: * MCP can be finicky, especially if you refresh your browser while in a match. If this happens and you can’t get your agent to connect, wait 5 min and retry | log out using the settings button at the top left and log back in. Stability is currently our top priority. * MCP also uses a lot of tokens, more than the game should, because every tool call costs tokens. We plan to overhaul this with a new connection type in a future version so it’s much more efficient. * There’s a built-in local model for folks who don’t want to use their own AI. It plays basic hold’em OK but struggles to follow written strategies. If you want to try it, I’d recommend leaving your strategy blank. Sadly, it plays best with no instructions. * House bots fill empty seats. We made this choice so matches happen even when only a few people are online. Honestly, I’m most curious how you’d write a strategy that holds up against everyone else’s agents. And if MCP setup breaks on you, please tell me. We'll be in the thread as long as possible. articles.title: Zach Bryan Reveals the Very Special Person Who Gets a Royalty Cut From Every Song He Records: ‘He’s the Reason!’
articles.summary: Bryan opened up about the sweet gesture during last month's rambling, two-hour On the Porch podcast chat with Matthew McConaughey.
articles._body: Zach Bryan is not one to forget where he came from. The Oklahoma-bred “I Remember Everything” singer and military veteran sat down last month with actor Matthew McConaughey for one of his first public interviews in years to discuss Bryan’s new book and EP, Young Manhood & Other Donatable Organs , as well as the sweet, honorable gesture he makes to his former commanding officer in the Navy who helped get his career off the ground. “Is it true you give your commanding officer a cut of royalties on every track since?,” McConaughey asked after Bryan described the crucial role his former Navy commanding officer, Leo Alba, played in helping to produce his 2019 debut album, DeAnn during the wide-ranging, two-hour On the Porch podcast interview with the actor who starred in his 2024 “ Nine Ball ” video. “He’s the reason, man. He’s the reason I recorded any songs ever at all!,” said Bryan, who joined the Navy at 17 and served in active duty from 2013 until an honorable discharge in 2021 to pursue his music dream after encouragement from Alba to record a full album while the singer was still enlisted. “And I thought it was justified, man. He’s the reason I have any music at all. He’s the reason we’re all here at this house pretty much. I wouldn’t be who I was without him f–kin’ looking at me and saying I can record those songs.” Bryan, 30, said Alba’s children call him “uncle” and Alba comes to his shows all the time and, to this day, he gives Alba a percentage of royalties from every song he releases. “Because that’s how much that meant to me,” he said of Alba’s encouragement. “Him believing in me enough to do that for me.” The interview also features Bryan discussing his sobriety , the difficulty of life on the road, God and the inspiration behind his recently released eight-track Young Manhood & Other Donatable Organs EP, which debuted at No. 1 on Billboard’s Top Country Albums, Top Rock Albums and Americana/Folk Albums charts and No. 2 on the Billboard 200 in its first week of release last month. The EP features a duet with Lana Del Rey on “Lies” and the Turnpike Troubadours on “ Plainsman .” Watch Bryan discuss Alba’s impact on his career below.

articles.title: 49ers GM John Lynch shares exactly where he stands on ‘unique’ Brandon Aiyuk saga
articles.summary: Several members of the San Francisco 49ers team have been asked about wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk potentially rejoining the team after his contract was voided last year. Naturally, 49ers general manager John Lynch has also been asked about this situation during a radio spot on KNBR. As transcribe
articles._body: Several members of the San Francisco 49ers team have been asked about wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk potentially rejoining the team after his contract was voided last year. Naturally, 49ers general manager John Lynch has also been asked about this situation during a radio spot on KNBR . As transcribed by ESPN’s Nick Wagoner, Lynch pointed out how unusual the Aiyuk situation is and that they are still trying to work things out. “This is kind of a unique situation, not one you have, so there’s really no playbook. But I always go back to what’s my charge, what’s my job? My job is to look out for the best interest of the 49ers. And as such, in this particular situation, we’re working with the NFL Management Council to navigate through a different situation. And so it’s fluid,” Lynch said. When asked about a potential reunion with Aiyuk, Lynch didn’t rule it out. “Yeah, of course. I think everything’s possible.” A first-round pick by the 49ers in 2020, Aiyuk has not featured in the NFL since suffering a torn ACL and MCL in 2024. In July 2025, the 49ers voided his contract for 2026 after failing to do rehab sessions and check-ins with the team. He was put on the reserve/left squad list in December. But last week, Aiyuk hired agent Drew Rosenhaus with a plan to get reinstated to the NFL. The 49ers could use reinforcements at wide receiver with Mike Evans currently out with an Achilles injury . However, Lynch will be careful not to disrupt the chemistry the 6-1 Niners have built, especially given how poorly Aiyuk’s first stint with the team ended. One Seahawks player is taking responsibility for his part in that tough loss. Seahawk guard Grey Zabel took full accountability for his struggles
articles._body: The Seattle Seahawks did not look competitive on Monday Night Football . Seattle got smacked around by Chicago 34-17 in a crushing loss at Lumen Field. One Seahawks player is taking responsibility for his part in that tough loss. Seahawk guard Grey Zabel took full accountability for his struggles in Week 8 against the Bears. “It was a deal, a challenge opportunity for me to grow, get outside my comfort zone and ultimately become a better player,” Zabel said, per Seahawks reporters Gregg Bell. “So at the end of the day, there was a lot of stuff I need to clean up. But that’s what practice is for, that’s what coaches are for, and we’ve got some unbelievable coaches and we’ll do just that.” Zabel explained that moving from left guard to right guard was the most challenging move of his football life. Seattle moved his position after acquiring Quenton Nelson from Indianapolis on October 27th. He also gave credit to Bears defender Jeffery Simmons, who thrived against Seattle’s offensive line on Monday Night Football. “I won’t downplay how good Jeffery Simmons was. And I won’t downplay how bad I was…. Got to wear a blow to the chin,” Zabel concluded. Simmons finished the game with six total tackles and one sack. He applied plenty of pressure and made more of an impact than can be seen on a simple box score. Unfortunately, the Seahawks may need Zabel to turn things around rather quickly. Nelson is dealing with a knee injury and may not be able to play in Week 9. That by itself poses an interesting question of whether Zabel should fill in for Nelson or remain in his new position. Beyond that, Seattle also has six different starters who sat out of practice on Thursday. They include key players on both sides of the ball. Regardless, the Seahawks need to get back in the win column after starting the season 4-4. Hopefully they can pull off a huge divisional win this weekend. Next up for the Seahawks is a Week 9 home game against the Cardinals. articles.title: No more Cybertrucks; Musk moves on from the angular metallic flop
articles.summary: Tesla wanted to unseat the Ford F-150, instead it made the Edsel look successful.
articles._body: Elon’s Edsel is no more. Last night, Tesla CEO Elon Musk revealed on social media that his car company is ending its failed attempt to wrest control of the American pickup truck market. The Cybertruck will cease production in the middle of 2027, liberating that space in Tesla’s cavernous factory for other uses—more Cybercabs , most likely. Musk first revealed the Cybertruck in late 2019 , back when Tesla was still trading at a theoretically understandable price-to-earning ratio. The pickup's unusual angular shape owed more to low-res video game models than any concessions to practicality. At the time, Musk made fanciful claims that the truck would use a stainless steel monocoque construction, telling his audience that “the body and bed don’t do anything useful” on a normal truck. While some race cars use carbon-fiber monocoques for strength and lightness, making a pickup truck with a stainless steel monocoque chassis would only make sense if someone had an awful lot of stainless steel lying around and needed something to do with it all. The truck was supposed to go on sale for less than $40,000, and Tesla made its usual stratospheric sales predictions that (had they been accurate) the bare metal EVs would be as ubiquitous as the Model 3 and Y. articles.title: The government can lower grocery prices. It doesn’t have to run the stores
articles.summary: It’s a Costco card, with Washington as the buying club.
articles._body: Almost every plan to lower food prices ends up putting the government in one of two businesses, either running a grocery store , as New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani is now doing, or telling grocery stores what to charge. A new proposal from the Kitchen Table Project does neither, which is why I’ve spent more time with it than I expected to. Instead of working on what shoppers pay, it works on what the store pays. The federal government already buys an enormous amount of food. USDA runs competitive auctions to supply school lunch and other nutrition programs, and it has been doing so for decades. The proposal would let any grocer, whether a bodega in the Bronx or a Kroger in Lansing, buy a basket of 20 staples at a similar auction price. The one condition is that the store has to sell them at a markup that’s set in advance and posted where customers can see it. This is like a Costco membership where Washington is the buying club and the grocer is the member. The government never owns a store, never runs a warehouse, and never writes a check to cover the gap between what food costs and what a politician would like it to cost. The report estimates a family of four would save about $315 a year. I’m more sympathetic to this than I usually am to grocery proposals, and the reason is purchasing power. Small stores pay more for the same case of eggs because they buy fewer cases. Price surveys consistently show the big discounters undercutting most supermarkets, and the Atlanta Fed has found that food inflation ran hottest in lower-income metro areas, where shoppers have fewer stores to choose from. If a corner store could buy at something close to Walmart’s price, that’s a form of relief neither a price cap nor Mamdani’s city-run supermarkets can offer . New York is paying for a 30 percent discount at five stores, while this proposal would reach every store that signs up. And since the markup is public, shoppers would have a number to hold their regular supermarket against. This also gives other supermarkets a reason to watch their prices. But for six of the 20 items, which include eggs, milk and ground beef, the report shows no savings at all. I don’t think that’s a flaw in the design so much as a reminder of where food prices come from. Ground beef is close to $7 a pound because the U.S. cattle herd is the smallest it has been in 75 years. No auction or purchasing plan, however large, produces more cows. I’d also bet against the federal government out-negotiating Walmart and Costco, which have spent decades on procurement and are very good at it. If Washington simply matched what the big chains pay, that would still be a meaningful help to independents, and it’s worth doing. It’s just a smaller promise than the headline number suggests. Which brings everything back to the markup. The report doesn’t say who sets it. Rent and wages in the Bronx are not rent and wages in Lansing, and a single national margin could end up either squeezing out the stores the program is meant to help or leaving so little room that the discount barely shows up on the shelf. The chains that already get good terms may look at the paperwork and decide it isn’t worth it. There’s a second-order problem too. A grocer selling 20 items at a capped margin still has to make payroll, and the obvious way to do that is to increase prices on the other several thousand items in the store. A family could save on the program staples, lose it on everything else, and never know the difference. Even so, this is the first grocery proposal I’ve seen in a while that tries to lower prices through competition rather than by having taxpayers absorb the difference. That alone makes it worth piloting. Name the markup. Say who can join. And then judge it by what a family actually saves on the whole cart, not on a handful of staples. articles.title: Cava hit 500 restaurants ahead of schedule. Its CFO explains how it plans double in size by 2032
articles.summary: Cava's CFO Tricia Tolivar on reaching the halfway mark to 1,000 restaurants early.
articles._body: Good morning. Cava has reached 500 restaurants ahead of schedule, putting it halfway toward its goal of at least 1,000 locations by 2032. But for CFO Tricia Tolivar, the bigger challenge is ensuring the Mediterranean fast-casual chain can sustain its performance as it doubles in size. The early results are encouraging. Cava’s newest restaurants are operating at roughly 100% productivity, Tolivar told me, suggesting the company has room to expand into new markets without sacrificing sales performance. “Even more encouraging is the strength of those new restaurant openings,” she said. Still, Cava’s rapid expansion comes as consumers face mounting financial pressure. The company reported Wednesday that third-quarter Cava segment revenue rose 22.1% year over year to $353.7 million, while same-restaurant sales increased 3.1%, with guest traffic slightly positive. Consolidated revenue totaled $356.4 million, short of analysts’ estimate of about $358.4 million. Tolivar attributed about 150 basis points of the same-restaurant sales impact to consumer concerns about fresh produce following a Cyclospora outbreak, even though Cava wasn’t among the chains linked to it. Excluding that impact, same-restaurant sales would have grown roughly 4.6%. CAVA nevertheless raised its full-year same-restaurant sales guidance to 6% to 7%, up from 4.5% to 6.5%. Cava has been one of the restaurant industry’s strongest performers in recent years, particularly in growth and sales momentum. The challenge now is balancing expansion with operational discipline, particularly as Cava enters new markets and consumers become more cautious about spending. Tolivar said Cava has kept price increases below inflation over the past six years, while investing in technology and employee development to support growth. That includes a new operator portal that allows general managers to manage digital orders and update out-of-stock items in real time. The company’s in-house Cava Command Center also consolidates restaurant performance data, replacing separate systems and spreadsheets. For a chain that now operates in 31 states and Washington, D.C., those investments could become increasingly important. Managing 1,000 restaurants will require more than opening new locations; it will mean maintaining consistent execution, controlling costs and protecting the customer experience across a much larger operation. Cava reached its 500-restaurant milestone through long-term planning, performance tracking, and adapting as circumstances changed, Tolivar said. “When curveballs come your way, how do you then pivot and adjust so that you can continue to meet, if not exceed, expectations?” she said. She added that Cava is investing in the business “not for the next 12 weeks, but for the next 12 years and beyond.” Have a good weekend. articles.title: Show HN: KeepPlain – ask your coding agent why a line of code exists

KeepPlain saves your agent sessions. It uses git blame to find the session that corresponds to a file, line, or commit. Then it shows the original req
articles._body: My code is written by agents now. Git blame shows me the commit and my own name, but the reason for the code is in a session I closed weeks ago. KeepPlain saves your agent sessions. It uses git blame to find the session that corresponds to a file, line, or commit. Then it shows the original request and the reasoning behind the change. It also finds commits made by the user after the agent session and links them to the session. I also try to use the mistakes the agent makes over and over to turn them into rules for new sessions. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi and Antigravity. Your sessions are uploaded to my server and are kept private to you. All secrets are redacted on your machine before the upload. I’m sure there will be lots of questions about this. The plugin is MIT licensed and open source. The server is not. Teams can run their own Postgres database to store their data. KeepPlain is free for personal use and teams will pay for it. I am a solo developer and this is early on in development so please let me know where it breaks. articles._body: It wasn’t just Jalen Brunson on Law & Order: Special Victims Unit last night, as his father, New York Knicks assistant coach Rick Brunson, was also in the episode. When Olivia Benson (Mariska Hargitay) enters the building to meet with Brunson’s character, Captain Madison, his father can be seen walking in first. It’s a quick, blink-or-you’ll-miss-it cameo , with one fan even saying they “didn’t notice him the 1st time” they watched the clip, but some Knicks fans didn’t like it. "Blew a 0.25 and started yelling at me" –– Detective Madison aka Jalen Brunson to Mariska Hargitay on Law & Order SVU With cameo from Rick Brunson pic.twitter.com/18bDIOQxtp — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) November 6, 2026 One X, formerly Twitter, user reacted to the clip by saying, “Pops don’t let this man do S**T alone lol.” Someone compared it to “take your kid to work day” but the other way around. Another X user commented on the post, saying, “He [is] the male version of Jayden Daniels’ momma.” Knicks fans review Jalen Brunson’s Law & Order: SVU performance Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Some Knicks fans were also critical of Jalen Brunson’s acting chops. One commented on New York Basketball’s clip on X, “Don’t quit your day job, Jalen!” though they hoped he “had fun.” Someone else said that the Knicks captain’s performance was “better than some Tubi actors.” A different Knicks fan is “ready for another spin-off” after Brunson’s cameo, using the iconic Martin Scorsese “Absolute Cinema” meme. Another was more positive on his performance, saying, “Oddly, if I had no idea who he was…I’d say this works…Sometimes decent acting isn’t acting at all, just delivering lines casually without exaggeration. Not bday, kid[,] lol!” It’s unknown if Captain Madison, or “Jay,” as Olivia calls him at the end of their conversation, will return in Law & Order: SVU. For now, Brunson is focused on the season. The Knicks are rolling after blowing out the Chicago Bulls in their last game. Brunson scored 33 points in 28 minutes. Now, they turn their attention to the Cleveland Cavaliers—whom they swept in the Eastern Conference Finals earlier this year. articles._body: Absent from WWE for months now, Rhea Ripley was recently spotted in public after a long time. Ripley recently appeared on stage at the Nov. 5, 2026 concert of metalcore band Motionless In White in Orlando, Florida. Chris Motionless, the lead singer of the band, publicly expressed gratitude to Ripley for promoting metal music and gothic culture globally. “Mami” appeared onstage at the Kia Center during the group’s “Sweat and Blood Tour” stop. The band dedicated the song “Fight Like Hell” to Ripley, who was the inspiration behind it. Carson Wentz has easy solution to Justin Jefferson’s frustration: ‘Just get him the rock’
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings are looking to get back in the win column in Week 9. Minnesota suffered their first loss of the season in Week 8 and now faces another elite team in Buffalo. To make matters worse, the Vikings will be forced to start Carson Wentz against the Bills on Sunday. Wentz explained
articles._body: The Minnesota Vikings are looking to get back in the win column in Week 9. Minnesota suffered their first loss of the season in Week 8 and now faces another elite team in Buffalo. To make matters worse, the Vikings will be forced to start Carson Wentz against the Bills on Sunday. Wentz explained his perspective on one key problem surrounding the offense during a recent interview. He has a plan for getting Justin Jefferson more involved in the passing game. “I mean, just get him the rock. He’s as good as I’ve been around. So, you know, for him the last couple of weeks not getting it as much as he would maybe want, I get it. I’d be frustrated if I were him,” Wentz told reporters on Thursday, per Ari Meirov. “I mean, he’s as good as it gets at his position and I look forward to just, I want to get him the rock as much as anybody. I look forward to trying to do that without forcing it. We’ve got a bunch of talent on the offensive side of the ball, so my job is just to distribute it and I’m confident he’ll get his this week.” Kyler Murray is dealing with a sore hamstring, which is why Wentz will get the start. Jefferson and Murray have not created a very strong chemistry between the two. The superstar receiver only has 28 receptions for 335 yards and four touchdowns in six games this season. He has yet to go over 100 yards in a game and has only received 40 targets thus far. It is great to hear that Wentz will prioritize getting Jefferson involved. Jefferson stiffed the media last week and seemed frustrated with Murray’s performance in their loss to Detroit. Hopefully Wentz brings some stability to the offense and can unlock Jefferson’s full potential. Vikings vs. Bills kicks off at 8:15 p.m. ET on Nov 9 from U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. There were some unexpected challenges along the way, but also moments that felt like a glimpse of the future.
