articles.title: Queens of the Stone Age Crowned on ARIA Chart With ‘Perfecth’
articles.summary: It’s the seventh top 10 appearance, and third leader, for Josh Homme and Co.
articles._body: It’s a perfecth start for Queens of the Stone Age (via Matador/Remote Control) on the ARIA Albums Chart , as the U.S. rock act debuts at No. 1. QOTSA leads the latest chart with Perfecth , their ninth studio album . It’s the seventh top 10 appearance for Josh Homme and Co., and their third leader after 2013’s … Like Clockwork and 2017’s Villains . Perfecth is the best seller on wax for the week, earning top spot on ARIA’s Vinyl Chart. Canadian rock favorites Nickelback start on the chart podium with Everything Under The Sun (Virgin Music Group/Inertia), their 11 th studio album. It’s new at No. 3. Nickelback now have 10 ARIA top 10 albums, including a best-seller with 2011’s Here And Now , which logged one week at No. 1. Australian actor, singer and comedian Eddie Perfect enjoys a career-best result with Beetlejuice (Live At The Regent Theatre Melbourne) , which opens its account at No. 5 on the latest chart, published Friday, Nov. 6. Indeed, it’s a first-ever appearance in the top 50 for Perfect, who reprised the title role last year in the Australian production of Beetlejuice The Musical . Close behind is Aussie country artist Fanny Lumsden , whose new album Traditions debuts at No. 6 on the ARIA Chart. That’s Lumsden’s third consecutive top 10 appearance and a new career high. Traditions is the fifth studio album for Lumsden, a two-time ARIA Award winner. Gretta Ray has her own career high with Heartsong (EMI), the Melbourne-born singer and songwriter’s third studio album. It’s new at No. 11, besting the peak of her 2021 debut Begin To Love Around , and the No. 17 best for 2023’s Positive Spin. It’s an uplifting comeback for Ray, who endured a five-week hospital stay in 2024 after falling ill with “severe” cardiac disease — infective endocarditis, a rare and life-threatening ailment that can cause damage to the heart. Also new to the chart is U.S. singer Dominic Fike ’s third LP How To Quit Smoking (Columbia/Sony), new No. 22. That bests the No. 34 for his 2020 collection What Could Possibly Go Wrong and the No. 25 peak for 2023’s Sunburn . Moog, one of the Australian creators of the popular Mighty Car Mods YouTube channel, sneaks into the top 40 with Shift. It’s new at No. 40. The automotive series, launched by Marty and Moog, boasts almost 4 million subscribers on YT. Over on the ARIA Singles Chart , Tate McRae enters a third consecutive week at No. 1 with “Housewife,” and there’s a post-Halloween bump for Tame Impala ’s “Dracula” (Columbia/Sony), which rises 20-13.

articles.title: Watch Arizona’s Bryce James sink corner 3 for first college bucket
articles.summary: Aside from Ivan Kharchenkov, Arizona basketball posted an underwhelming offensive effort in Monday’s 84-75 loss versus UCLA. Bryce James had a particularly tough night. Despite starting at guard, the son of all-time NBA great LeBron James only logged six minutes of action. He missed all thr
articles._body: Aside from Ivan Kharchenkov, Arizona basketball posted an underwhelming offensive effort in Monday’s 84-75 loss versus UCLA . Bryce James had a particularly tough night. Despite starting at guard, the son of all-time NBA great LeBron James only logged six minutes of action. He missed all three of his field goal attempts and finished with one assist in the season opener. The Wildcats showed more life on Thursday, however, and so did the 19-year-old. Less than three minutes into a home matchup against Cal Poly, James scored the first points of his collegiate career. He knocked down a corner 3-pointer off an assist from freshman guard Caleb Holt, via the Oh No He Didn’t X account. Bryce James first college bucket! pic.twitter.com/o25tNiwMfF — Oh No He Didn't (@ohnohedidnt24) November 6, 2026 The 6-foot-5 talent, who redshirted in his first year at Tuscon, recorded five points on 3-of-5 shooting to go with two assists, two steals and one rebound in the Wildcats’ 104-84 win over the Mustangs. There is still obviously room for improvement following this 17-minute performance, but James made gradual progress in game number two. Arizona head coach Tommy Lloyd is trusting this young player to help set the tone, but he does not expect him to fill up the stat sheet on a consistent basis. There are several members of this team who can carry the load. The 7-foot-2 Motiejus Krivas did so versus Cal Poly. He dropped 30 points on 10-of-13 shooting and added eight rebounds and two blocks. Holt posted 21 points, eight boards and two steals. Kharchenkov had a double-double and also tallied seven assists and four steals. The Wildcats’ core showed up against the inferior Mustangs, as they should. Ideally, Bryce James gained confidence after seeing the ball go through the net. He was also active on the defensive end, exploiting a Cal Poly squad that committed 19 turnovers. Arizona basketball got the straightforward W, and James exhibited growth. Lloyd will expect the same result when his team hosts Northern Arizona on Tuesday. The post Watch Arizona’s Bryce James sink corner 3 for first college bucket appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Southeast Asia shouldn’t copy the U.S. healthcare model, says Walgreens Boots Alliance’s APAC head: ‘It saves your life, but it’s not very healthy’
articles.summary: Southeast Asia is building out its systems of care amid rising healthcare costs and a shortage of specialist doctors.
articles._body: The U.S. is the world’s largest healthcare spender , pouring roughly 17% of its GDP—or $5.6 trillion—into treatments and care. Yet, according to Li Zhong, the APAC president of the Walgreens Boots Alliance (WBA), while Americans generally have a long lifespan, they have a shorter healthspan than their counterparts in Vietnam, despite the latter devoting just 4.6% of its GDP to health spending. “Everyone loves to reference the U.S., since it has been able to come up with the most advanced therapies to extend life,” Li said at Fortune’s Southeast Asia 500 Summit in Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh City on Nov. 3. “It saves your life, but it’s not very healthy. That’s not what I would suggest for Southeast Asia.” Li’s comments come as Southeast Asia builds out its systems of care amid rising healthcare costs and a shortage of specialist doctors. “Every country is different and has to find its own route,” he explained. “What’s not right is to automatically reference the U.S. model.” Many Southeast Asian countries, like Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia, are also rapidly greying . And with that demographic trend comes a rise in chronic disease incidence. “The scarcity of specialists is becoming a burden,” admits David Utama, the president director of Indonesia’s largest private hospital chain, Siloam Hospitals. “In Indonesia, the ratio of specialists is about 0.2 per 1,000 people. Neighboring Malaysia and Thailand are about 0.5, while Singapore sits at 1.2 [specialists per 1,000 people].” More patient-centric To serve patient needs, Asia’s healthcare operators are increasingly looking to community-based care. Singapore and Malaysia-headquartered IHH Healthcare, for instance, operates over fifty primary care clinics under their Parkway Shenton network, while offering ambulatory care, diagnostic and rehabilitative care facilities within residential neighborhoods.  Siloam Hospitals, too, is building more community health facilities in Indonesia. “We have about 41 hospitals across Indonesia, but we’re now building an ecosystem of primary care clinics.” (The firm’s website shows that it currently has 25 clinics , spread across the cities of Palembang, Jakarta, Bali and Surabaya.) Pharmacies can also play a larger role, Li argued. He points to the UK’s NHS Pharmacy First scheme , which allows patients in England to walk into participating Boots pharmacies for clinical assessments and treatment for seven common conditions, without needing a GP appointment. “It’s more cost-efficient to utilize community healthcare centers and pharmacies to help with everyday healthcare,” Li explained. “But that’s on the condition that we have to get our [pharmacists] well-trained.” Ultimately, both experts agreed that public-private partnerships and emerging technology like AI are countries’ best bets at enabling affordable, high-quality healthcare for its populace. “Patient-centric healthcare requires a collaboration between governments and the private sector,” said Utama. “Who has access, who has scale, [it’s] obviously the government… but the private sector helps to build capability, innovation and speed.” Since late-2025, Utama and Siloam Hospitals have also been investing in enterprise AI. He says the team will finish building the foundational layer of its AI platform by this year, and is now looking to build digital twins for its patients, doctors and hospitals. “For us to leapfrog, we need to adopt technology,” Utama concluded. “Today, in our ICUs, because of the data analysis we do, we can predict 30 minutes before a patient drops. Previously, we could only react 30 minutes after a patient dropped.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: The 1 Jaguars’ thing Trevor Lawrence laments from beatdown of Ravens on TNF
articles.summary: Trevor Lawrence has every reason to celebrate after the Jacksonville Jaguars dismantled the Baltimore Ravens 33-10 on Thursday Night Football. However, the franchise quarterback was quick to identify one area that still needs improvement. They need to finish offensive drives with touchdowns inste
articles._body: Trevor Lawrence has every reason to celebrate after the Jacksonville Jaguars dismantled the Baltimore Ravens 33-10 on Thursday Night Football. However, the franchise quarterback was quick to identify one area that still needs improvement. They need to finish offensive drives with touchdowns instead of settling for field goals. Despite another dominant performance that pushed Jacksonville to 6-2 and sole possession of first place in the AFC South, Lawrence believes his team left valuable points on the field. “We were ready to go from the jump… but we should have had more [points],” Lawrence said, according to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. His frustration centered on Jacksonville’s inability to consistently capitalize on favorable field position created by its aggressive defense. Kicker Cam Little converted four field goals. However, the Jaguars could have made the final margin even more commanding with better red-zone execution. Jacksonville’s defense forced three turnovers. It repeatedly gave Lawrence and the offense opportunities to extend their advantage. Yet several promising drives stalled before reaching the end zone, an issue that could become more costly against tougher playoff competition. Lawrence’s 2026 campaign has been defined by improved efficiency and leadership under head coach Liam Coen. Through eight games, he has distributed the football effectively to targets such as Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers while benefiting from a productive ground attack. His 242-yard performance against Baltimore, highlighted by a 50-yard touchdown strike, further strengthened his growing MVP case. The Jaguars have now outscored their last two opponents by a combined 75-17. They have established themselves as legitimate AFC contenders. Still, Lawrence’s postgame assessment reflects a quarterback unwilling to settle for comfortable victories. If Jacksonville wants to become a genuine Super Bowl threat, turning more scoring opportunities into touchdowns will be essential. Zillennials are spending 5 hours a week self-promoting themselves—it’s called ‘loud working’ and colleagues are getting so annoyed they’re quitting
articles.summary: One in four workers have considered quitting over colleagues who won’t stop shouting about their wins—and zillennials are the loudest.
articles._body: So you’ve heard of the trend quiet quitting, and its sister, loud quitting —but now workers are doing the complete opposite: “loud working.” Instead of doing the bare minimum to get by or turning their anger on their employers, they’re pouring all their energy into making their work more visible. Think of the colleague who posts every win on LinkedIn or pings the whole team on Slack the second a task is done. New research from Tide, a finance platform, found that the average U.K. worker spends 131 hours a year—more than 17 working days or 2.8 hours a week—making their work visible. That includes singing their own praises on social media, posting updates on Slack or Teams, speaking up in meetings, and vocalizing their wins to anyone who will listen. And the loudest of all are younger workers: In fact, nearly 70% of 25- to 34-year-olds are “loud working.” They’re spending about 5 hours every week self-promoting. And it’s drawing attention from management, clients and even angry coworkers. Does ‘loud working’ actually work? Yes. Perhaps unsurprisingly, it’s not always the most competent worker who gets rewarded—it’s the one who makes the most noise about it. According to the research, 77% of “loud workers” have had at least one career opportunity in the past year alone, including new customers or clients, pay rises and promotions. For 15% of respondents, getting vocal about their wins has even gotten them awards. And all the new noise around their success is attracting the attention of other employers; In fact, 17% say they’ve not only been poached, but they’ve actually landed a new job because they’ve been more vocal about their work.  But worryingly, it’s not just “loud workers” who are at risk of being snapped up and leaving the business. Colleagues are sick of ‘loud workers’—and even quitting over the trend Not everyone’s cheering. More than one in four (27%) workers have considered leaving a job because of a loud working culture, or because colleagues are too vocal about their own achievements.  One in 10 have already walked out. Zillennials are both most likely to be guilty of “loud working,” as well as the ones walking off.  They’re posting about their success at more than three times the rate of over-55s. Yet nearly half of 25 to 34-year-olds have considered quitting a job because of it—and one in five already have.  Some industries are more forgiving of office braggers than others: Workers in IT, telecoms, and finance are the most likely to have had enough of performative culture. Meanwhile, men are more likely than women to have already quit over it. “Loudworking has mixed reactions in the workplace and it’s easy to understand that a colleague who turns every small win into an announcement might be off-putting,” said George Schmidt, Tide’s CEO for the U.K. and Europe. “But our research shows there’s a difference between being performative and backing yourself.” He said that for small business owners, sharing their work, wins and expertise is often the most effective marketing they have. And the same goes for anyone who has left their employer to go solo or who is eyeing up the exit.  Ultimately, though, many workers want to be at a business that rewards people for actually doing the hard work—not just shouting the most about it.  Do you ‘loud work’—or have you quit over a colleague who does? articles.title: Zillennials are ‘loud working ’: They’re spending 5 hours a week self-promoting themselves—and colleagues are getting so annoyed they’re quitting
articles.summary: One in four workers have considered quitting over colleagues who won’t stop shouting about their wins—and zillennials are the loudest.
articles._body: So you’ve heard of the trend quiet quitting, and its sister, loud quitting —but now workers are doing the complete opposite: “loud working.” Instead of doing the bare minimum to get by or turning their anger on their employers, they’re pouring all their energy into making their work more visible. Think of the colleague who posts every win on LinkedIn or pings the whole team on Slack the second a task is done. New research from Tide, a finance platform, found that the average U.K. worker spends 131 hours a year—more than 17 working days or 2.8 hours a week—making their work visible. That includes singing their own praises on social media, posting updates on Slack or Teams, speaking up in meetings, and vocalizing their wins to anyone who will listen. And the loudest of all are younger workers: In fact, nearly 70% of 25- to 34-year-olds are “loud working.” They’re spending about 5 hours every week self-promoting. articles.title: In a contentious North Carolina House race, it was $59,000 against an incumbent’s $3 million warchest—and the challenger won
articles.summary: Democrats in several races overcame fundraising disadvantages to flip races in Republican strongholds.
articles._body: In a blue wave midterm that swept Democrats into power in previously Republican strongholds, even major money couldn’t make the difference, and one race in North Carolina is the perfect example. In North Carolina’s 14th Congressional District, which stretches from the suburbs of Charlotte to the Western North Carolina mountains, Democratic political newcomer LaKesha Womack unseated Rep. Tim Moore , the influential former state House speaker who helped draw the district and dominated it in 2024. Moore outraised Womack more than 50 to 1, with a war chest of $3 million compared to $59,000 raised by his Democratic opponent, according to Axios . Even still, Womack narrowly beat out Moore in the midterm election Tuesday by about 6,400 votes, ending the Republican’s time in Congress after just one term. The win was particularly striking because Moore, who served for more than two decades in the North Carolina House—and served the longest ever stint as speaker of the state House—helped redraw the district in 2023, and the following year, he won it by about 16 percentage points, according to the Washington Post . Womack, an entrepreneur and the founder of Womack Consulting Group , said despite being outspent, she used her limited funds to attend between five and seven events per week in the district she aimed to represent, according to an interview with Spectrum News . “A lot of that money was spent on gas,” she said. “I made sure that I showed up everywhere across this district.” Rep. Moore did not immediately respond to Fortune ’s request for comment. In a statement to Fortune , Womack said this week’s victory was “a testament to the power of ordinary people who believe that their voices matter and that leadership should be rooted in service, accountability, and opportunity for all.” Womack’s unlikely success helped propel Democrats to their strongest performance in North Carolina in years. In the U.S. Senate race, former Gov. Roy Cooper trounced former Republican National Committee chair Michael Whatley in a win that helped his party secure a majority in the Senate. Despite the Republican-controlled state legislature’s recent effort to skew congressional districts in their party’s favor, Democrats also flipped at least five, and potentially six Republican-held seats, potentially reversing the state’s 10-to-four Republican majority in Congress to favor Democrats. Democrats also won a majority of seats in the state’s House of Representatives for the first time since 2010, while Republicans lost their veto-proof supermajority in the state Senate. “It’s a total wipeout across the board,” National Republican Congressional Committee spokesman Mike Marinelli told the Washington Post , adding that the Republicans’ midterm losses could be chalked up to “a total referendum on the president and voters being livid about the prices, the war and immigration.” Courtesy of LaKesha Womack Money’s limits Womack’s success in North Carolina was part of a larger trend across the U.S. that saw Democratic challengers win despite being outraised by Republican opponents. In the end, money and favorable election maps were seemingly overwhelmed by voters’ frustrations with President Trump, affordability, and other issues. An exit poll conducted by NBC News found that three-fourths of voters rated the economy as “poor” or “not so good” and 65% said President Trump’s policies had made the economy worse. Beyond North Carolina, these issues boosted Democrats in races nationwide where they were heavily outraised by their Republican opponents. That includes Democrat Victoria Broderick’s unlikely edge over longtime Republican Rep. Scott DesJarlais in Tennessee. Broderick raised $94,000 compared with DesJarlais’ $660,000 through mid-October, according to Axios . Just two years earlier, DesJarlais defeated Broderick by 40 percentage points. Yet, as of Wednesday, Broderick was beating DesJarlais by 280 votes, according to the New York Times . A recount will only be called if a candidate challenges the outcome. In Alabama, Democrat Allison Montgomery won a state House race after raising about $23,000. That’s about a tenth of the $215,000 raised by the Republican incumbent Phillip Rigsby. Another Democrat in a state race, Nell Brown, won a seat in the Alabama House of Representatives despite raising just $11,000 to her opponent’s $185,000. In the governor’s race in Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms also defeated billionaire Republican Rick Jackson, who poured more than $200 million of his own fortune into the race. Pro-Jackson groups spent or reserved nearly $76 million in TV airtime, as compared with about $8 million for Bottoms and her allies. Even the world’s richest man couldn’t always make the difference. Elon Musk put at least $447 million toward electing Republicans . Just three of the 37 Republican House candidates Musk supported had won as of Thursday, and 33 had lost, Reuters reported . Another race in which a Republican candidate backed by Musk for the House was leading, was yet to be decided, according to the outlet. Six of the seven Senate candidates Musk backed also lost, with one race, the Senate race in Alaska still undecided, though Democrat Mary Peltola was slightly ahead with nearly three-fourths of the votes counted as of Thursday, according to the New York Times . The most expensive election ever While greater spending in midterm races didn’t guarantee victories for either party, more money has been shown to increase a candidate’s likelihood of getting elected. A 2022 study by Danielle Thomsen, a professor of political science at the University of California—Irvine found that top fundraisers win their primaries 92% of the time .  The 2026 midterm election was the most expensive election in U.S. history , with about $12

articles.title: ‘The nail that sticks out gets hammered first’: Elon Musk’s net worth falls $113 billion from Tesla and SpaceX drops
articles.summary: Tesla and SpaceX bucked the market rally as investors worried about political retaliation.
articles._body: Wall Street had a historic moment the day after Democrats swept the midterms, with the Dow rising 3% on Wednesday, its best performance after a midterm in 44 years . But on Thursday, it erased those gains, dropping 2.9% as investors dumped AI-related stocks like AMD and Micron . But for Elon Musk, who spent an estimated $427.5 million to $483 million on backing Republicans , the losses started on the same day as the rally, and then accelerated. Tesla shares fell by 3.3% and SpaceX shares fell by 3.8% on Wednesday’s market close, erasing tens of billions from Musk’s fortune as they also underperformed against the S&P 500’s 1.6% growth and stocks like Amazon and Apple , which jumped 6.1% and 5.3%, per Fortune’s analysis. He lost $33.5 billion of his paper wealth that day, and another $79.7 billion in Thursday’s selloff , bringing his two-day loss to about $113 billion as of market close on Nov. 5, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index . In short, in 48 hours, Tesla and SpaceX went from having a combined market cap of about $3.5 trillion on Tuesday night, to a combined $3.04 trillion on Thursday night, wiping out about $456 billion in total . As of Thursday night, SpaceX’s market cap is $1.68 trillion , about 87% of what it was on midterms night, and Tesla’s market cap is $1.36 trillion, about 86% of its value from then. Investors are worried the two companies and their founder will face increased scrutiny from the new Congress. Democrats have signaled they want to investigate Musk’s involvement with DOGE gutting federal agencies and his potential conflicts of interests, since SpaceX has earned billions from federal contracts. The incoming House Oversight Committee chair Rep. Robert Garcia has vowed to investigate “corporate corruption,” and his spokesperson told Politico on Oct. 20 that Musk’s role in DOGE “is something we plan to investigate.” “The nail that sticks out gets hammered first, and Musk has certainly stuck out, especially in government, whether it be donations, the election, and any of the feathers he ruffled while he was at DOGE,” Keith Snyder, senior equity analyst at CFRA Research, told Fortune. The scrutiny could extend to SpaceX’s satellite business, its most consistently profitable segment. Sen. Richard Blumenthal from Connecticut sent a letter to Musk asking about SpaceX’s contracts with the Department of Defense and its ability to restrict Starlink after reports circulated that Ukraine’s military lost access to Starlink without notice. But Snyder said the brief SpaceX and Tesla selloff was investors having a “knee-jerk reaction” to the election and overestimating the impact Democrats can have on the companies. After all, President Donald Trump still has veto power over any major AI restrictions they can pass, and is still friendly toward Musk. “Reigning in AI has been a stated goal of theirs, but you have to remember Trump seems to still be backing Musk and has veto power,” Snyder said. For investors hanging their hopes on a SpaceX and Tesla merger and worried about Democrats’ interference there, Snyder said that because the Federal Communications Commission has a Republican majority, he doesn’t expect major actions there except Democrats’ power to “dramatically slow things down.” Fortune has reported that the merger math doesn’t add up for SpaceX shareholders. “There’s too many pieces that are already in place for Musk, for Tesla, for SpaceX that will allow him to continue without having to worry about any kind of Democratic action,” he said. Some analysts take a more bearish stance. Dan Ives wrote in a note on Thursday that a Tesla SpaceX merger “faces a much tougher regulatory roadmap” because of Texas turning blue. This new political reality partially made possible by voters angry over data centers coincides with investors’ long-running concerns about the AI buildout being unsustainable. Snyder said that anxiety could’ve contributed to the SpaceX selloff, but that SpaceX has an advantage in already having broken ground on data centers. On its Q3 earnings call before the midterms, Musk said he was confident the company can bring 10 gigawatts of compute online by 2027 on top of the 2.5 to 3 gigawatts SpaceX will have by the end of 2026, a total number that AI and semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis quantified as equivalent to all of Google’s data center capacity from 1999 to 2026 in just one and a half years. “Even if they’re able to achieve 25% to 50% of that goal, that would be incredible in terms of capacity build out,” Snyder said. He said where he sees more risk for SpaceX and for AI in general is if there’s a Democrat win in the White House in two years, since for now there will be a political gridlock with a Republican president and a Democrat-controlled Congress. “The fears to these AI companies are real now,” he said. “[Democrats’] agenda has clearly stated they want to rein in AI, and so, ‘27, ‘28 is gonna be a stalemate, but it then becomes what happens in ‘29.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: First-time buyers have ‘no low-rate mortgage to surrender’—and with rates back above 7%, one-quarter are leaning on family for the down payment
articles.summary: For first-time buyers, saving for a down payment can take years, and a record share are now relying on inheritances.
articles._body: It’s hard to believe just a few years ago potential homebuyers were staring down sub-3% mortgages during the pandemic era. That’s because new homebuyers today face mortgage rates back in the 7% range , making it feel impossible for many to break into the housing market. Meanwhile, many current homeowners are holding on to the low rates they locked in during the pandemic, but first-time buyers don’t have that option. As Odeta Kushi, deputy chief economist at First American Financial Corporation, recently put it , they have “no low-rate mortgage to surrender,” so they’re facing today’s rates head-on. “For many younger buyers, mortgage rates below 3% became their reference point, even though those rates were historically exceptional,” Kushi told Fortune . “So today’s rates can feel expensive by comparison, particularly when home prices are also significantly higher.” Mortgage rates peaked in the early 1980s in the 18% range. But today’s new homebuyers are unlikely to remember that time, leaving them frustrated by how unaffordable today’s housing market feels. But for most first-time buyers, the 3% era isn’t really the sore spot anymore. Several real estate agents told Fortune their clients have largely accepted that those rates aren’t coming back. What stings more is how this year played out—and how stubbornly high home prices are. Mortgage rates fell to a low of 5.98% on Feb. 26, according to Freddie Mac . Then they climbed back, averaging 7.40% the weeks of Oct. 8 and Oct. 15, the highest since November 2023. Meanwhile, the average existing home price is still about 25% higher than it was when the pandemic first started, National Association of Realtors data shows.  “It’s almost as if just as first-time homebuyers were accepting the 6% rate and hoping for 5’s, the mortgage rates decidedly took another leg up,” Ken Sisson , an associate broker with Christie’s International Real Estate Southern California in Los Angeles, told Fortune . Most of what he hears from first-time buyers now, he said, is disappointment that they aren’t being quoted rates in the low 6s. But more recently, affordability has been a “significant challenge,” Sisson added. “The mortgage rates obviously are half of the story related to that affordability challenge,” he said. “The other half of the story is the home prices. My first-timers are well aware that the local prices were driven up significantly by the pandemic-era low rates.” But even buyers who can handle the monthly payment face a bigger hurdle: the down payment. Unlike repeat buyers, first-timers don’t have equity from a home sale to put toward their next purchase. “Even when someone earns enough to comfortably afford a monthly mortgage payment, saving tens of thousands of dollars for a down payment and closing costs can take years,” Kushi said. Her research identified nearly 1.3 million “shadow homeowners,” or young adults living with family whose characteristics suggest they could be future homeowners. “Many are older and further along in their careers,” she said. “They’ve delayed forming their own households, and accumulated savings may help some of them eventually make the leap.” So for a growing number of first-time buyers, the cash they need to buy their first home is coming from their parents. “There is currently a massive transfer of wealth from boomers going on,” Veronique Perrin, a real estate agent at Christie’s International Real Estate New York, told Fortune . “I am working more and more with buyers who are doing this with their parents’ help. There is a lot of gifting happening, and most of the deals I have worked on lately involved one.” Perrin, who said she is a baby boomer herself, said she’s having those conversations “more and more” with her peers. Nationally, 25% of first-time buyers used a gift or loan from family or friends toward their down payment, according to the National Association of Realtors’ 2026 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers, released Thursday . Still, Kushi said first-time buyers who feel they missed out should remember what buying a home actually looked like when rates were below 3%. “Multiple-offer bidding wars were everywhere, buyers routinely waived contingencies, and fierce competition helped push home prices up at double-digit annual rates,” she said. “Getting a low mortgage rate often meant competing in an extremely difficult market.” Today’s buyers face higher borrowing costs and prices that remain elevated, but in many markets the balance has shifted in their favor in other ways, Kushi said. Homes are sitting on the market longer, buyers have more choices, and sellers are more willing to negotiate on price or offer concessions, such as help with closing costs or mortgage rate buydowns. “There’s something to be said for having the time and negotiating power to find the right home at the right price,” she said. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Should Ravens sell at trade deadline after getting crushed by Jaguars to fall below .500?
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens are running out of time. A fourth consecutive loss, a growing injury list, and an impaired offense have turned this campaign into a fight for survival. Thursday night’s 33-10 humiliation against the Jacksonville Jaguars exposed a roster struggling to compete on multiple
articles._body: The Baltimore Ravens are running out of time. A fourth consecutive loss , a growing injury list, and an impaired offense have turned this campaign into a fight for survival. Thursday night’s 33-10 humiliation against the Jacksonville Jaguars exposed a roster struggling to compete on multiple fronts. The Ravens now have precious little time left to make meaningful corrections. With the NFL trade deadline approaching, general manager Eric DeCosta faces an uncomfortable question: Should Baltimore keep pushing for a playoff spot, or finally acknowledge that selling is the smarter move? Season unraveling Mark Konezny-Imagn Images The Week 9 home showdown against Jacksonville was supposed to be Baltimore’s opportunity to arrest a three-game slide. Instead, it devolved into a blowout that laid bare just how thin the margin for error has become without Lamar Jackson. The superstar quarterback is on injured reserve after suffering a serious right thumb injury against Buffalo. Backup Tyler Huntley is also sidelined with a toe injury. That left third-stringer Joe Fagnano to make his first NFL start . Sadly, the passing attack managed just 60 yards through the air. Jacksonville methodically controlled the contest behind Trevor Lawrence’s 242 passing yards and a touchdown. Baltimore struggled to generate any meaningful response. Derrick Henry battled for 57 rushing yards. Justice Hill provided a late spark with a spectacular 65-yard touchdown run. However, the rest of the operation crumbled. The Ravens failed to record a sack. All-Pro safety Kyle Hamilton exited with a hip injury. Baltimore is now 4-5 after starting 4-1. The urgency surrounding its season has become impossible to ignore. Cold arithmetic The AFC will show little mercy to a battered roster trying to tread water. Baltimore has surrendered valuable ground to its divisional rivals and wild-card competitors. The latest defeat suggests the problems extend well beyond quarterback availability. Jackson’s absence is obviously enormous. The Ravens, though, have also struggled to generate consistent pressure, protect their defensive weaknesses and sustain drives. Their offensive line has been dealing with injuries. Theur defense has not delivered. Waiting for everyone to get healthy is a dangerous gamble when Jackson’s recovery timeline remains uncertain. The trade deadline arrives on November 10, giving DeCosta only a narrow window to make decisions that could benefit the franchise beyond this campaign. Selling does not mean abandoning Jackson, Henry, or the team’s long-term ambitions. It just means recognizing that a championship window is sustained through smart asset management and timely recalibration. They have to do it now. Cashing in expiring capital The most sensible approach is selective selling rather than a full-scale teardown. Baltimore should examine offers for veteran contributors whose contracts are nearing expiration. Veterans such as defensive linemen and secondary pieces could attract interest from contenders looking for experienced depth. There is a cost to that strategy, of course. Trading away experienced defenders could make an already struggling unit even more vulnerable. Removing too much veteran leadership could undermine the locker room. DeCosta must therefore establish a clear asking price and refuse to move players simply for the sake of making transactions. Baltimore should prioritize assets that are unlikely to be part of its long-term plans. The front office must also weigh potential draft returns against the possibility of receiving compensatory selections if certain pending free agents leave next offseason. Just as importantly, the Ravens should avoid touching the pillars of their offense. Jackson remains the franchise’s defining player. Henry’s physical presence still gives Baltimore an identity worth preserving. Trading either would be an overreaction to a season derailed by injuries. Hamilton, meanwhile, should remain a cornerstone of the defense. Protect the championship window Kirby Lee-Imagn Images There is still a case for waiting. If Jackson can return sooner than expected and the defense rediscovers its identity, the Ravens could make a late push in a competitive AFC. That said, building a deadline strategy around best-case injury scenarios is not sound roster management. Baltimore needs to evaluate what it can realistically accomplish now. Ultimately, the Ravens do not need to dismantle the roster or concede the entire Jackson era. They need to turn expendable veteran value into resources that can address their structural weaknesses. Holding onto every pending free agent in pursuit of a possible seventh seed would be short-sighted. A difficult decision now could give Baltimore a healthier and more balanced roster next season. The loss to Jacksonville should force the organization to confront the possibility that its best move is to start preparing for the next one. articles.title: Schools blocking AI from student computers will now lose access to Google’s search feature, leaving edtech experts scratching their heads
articles.summary: “From a business angle, they're just doubling down as much as they can to try and force people to use AI,” one edtech critic said. “But from a pure learning angle, why?”
articles._body: Google’s updated policy on how schools access its AI tools has raised questions among educational technology experts about the rationale behind the decision. The tech company on Tuesday announced plans to turn off AI tools in its software for students, which can be reversed by a school administrator’s decision. Google said the change would enable K-12 classrooms to have more control over how students engage with AI. But if a school restricts AI entirely, its students will no longer be able to use Google’s Search feature.  A social media post from Google clarifying the changes, which will be implemented early next year, explained the feature was meant to provide schools with “more choice, not less” by creating the option for administrators to enable Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search. However, Google’s Search function is embedded with AI Mode and AI Overview that cannot be disabled, meaning schools with AI bans are unable to grant students access to the tool. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who issued a one-year moratorium on generative AI for public schools through eighth grade, was among politicians and policy experts criticizing the inextricable integration of Google Search with AI tools. The move, critics said, was a means of taking advantage of its monopoly to push use of its AI features. “Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools,” he wrote on social media on Wednesday. “No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children. Our public schools exist to serve students, not to grow the profit margins of Big Tech.” Experts who study technology use in classrooms had slightly different responses, suggesting that Google’s AI-laden Search feature could actually have an adverse impact on its goal of being used in classrooms in the first place. “I’m guessing from a business angle, they’re just doubling down as much as they can to try and force people to use AI,” neuroscientist and former teacher Jared Cooney Horvath, told Fortune . “But from a pure learning angle, why?” What are the potential unintended consequences of Google’s AI Search? U.S. schools have spent more than $30 billion as of 2024 to provide laptops to students, with Google’s Chromebooks being among the most ubiquitous. By 2017, the low-cost computers accounted for more than half of digital devices sent to classrooms. More classrooms using Chromebooks was lucrative for Google, too, and as of 2025, education represented 60% of Chromebook’s global market share , which totals $14 billion. An internal presentation from the company in November 2020 said exposing students to Google’s interface would create future customers (“You get that loyalty early, and potentially for life.”) A Google spokesperson said at the time the documents “mischaracterized our work.” But the reality of how AI is being used—or rather limited—in the classroom could threaten Google’s classroom presence to begin with. Jose Antonio Bowen, a consultant on technology in the classroom and a former president of Goucher College, explained in an email to Fortune that AI subverts the process of learning—which requires working hard—so many teachers are encouraged to use it sparingly , such as for teachers to create lesson plans, not for students to look up information. “What Google and other companies seem to be doing is streamlining and integrating AI (surely reducing internal costs) and that might work in other realms of AI use,” Bowen said. “But this makes AI an outlier in use: Yes, most people will find AI search useful for most cases, but in education it can’t be unfettered access.” Horvath, a longtime critic of the unchecked use of technology in classrooms, suggested Google’s decision not to allow users to turn off AI Mode or AI Overview from Search could actually incentivize more classrooms to turn back to analog research tools. “I guess maybe this is a good thing in the sense that now it will force schools to think twice before just going to Google when it comes time to do research: Maybe go to a book. Maybe go to the library,” he said. Bowen noted Google Search’s structure could also open doors for companies like DuckDuckGo, which has positioned itself as an AI-free search engine because it can automatically turn off AI summaries and filter out AI-generated images in private searches. DuckDuckGO founder and CEO Gabriel Weinberg told Fortune in an email he’s seeing more companies putting AI into features “making it increasingly impossible to turn off.” Weinberg said that after Google announced in May it would overhaul Search and integrate it with Gemini 3.5 Flash, DuckDuckGo saw a tripling in traffic to its no-AI search page, which has since remained elevated. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Warriors star Stephen Curry reveals Steve Kerr’s message after 0-3 start that sparked win streak
articles.summary: Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors have flipped the script on their season, and the superstar guard revealed that a message from head coach Steve Kerr after an 0-3 start helped spark the turnaround. Speaking after Thursday’s 120-100 win over the Miami Heat, which extended Golden State’s
articles._body: Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors have flipped the script on their season , and the superstar guard revealed that a message from head coach Steve Kerr after an 0-3 start helped spark the turnaround. Speaking after Thursday’s 120-100 win over the Miami Heat , which extended Golden State’s winning streak to six games, Curry looked back at what Kerr told the team after a loss to the Phoenix Suns on Oct. 24. “It was in Phoenix, I think he was talking about after that game, I know a lot of guys didn’t play, but he just mentioned sticking with the process and the things that he’d noticed on film and just the feel in games, like we were really close to being able to put together, you know, winning performances,” Curry said after the game. “He just mentioned sticking with the process, the things he noticed on film, and just the feeling games, like we were really close to being able to put together winning performances.” Steph Curry on what Steve Kerr told the team after their 0-3 start (via @kenzofuku ) pic.twitter.com/xoRCMEb07J — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 6, 2026 Curry pointed to some encouraging signs even during the losses, including the closing minutes of a narrow defeat to the Memphis Grizzlies . “And the Memphis game, again, inside the last four minutes, the way that those guys played in Phoenix and then how we’ve been playing since, it’s just small building blocks of an identity of how this team is supposed to compete,” Curry said. “And I think the biggest part is he just was proud of how hard we were playing. And everybody’s taking on that challenge as well when they come in the game.” Kerr’s patience has paid off. The Warriors opened the season with a 127-105 loss to the Los Angeles Lakers, followed by a 111-108 defeat to Memphis and a 131-122 loss to the Suns. They have not lost since. Golden State has rattled off wins over the Denver Nuggets, Minnesota Timberwolves, Lakers, LA Clippers, Suns and Heat. That stretch included a 116-113 win over Phoenix on Monday, with Curry pouring in 34 points against the team that handed Golden State its third loss. In the latest victory, Curry scored 29 points in just 28 minutes, while rookie Yaxel Lendeborg added 17 points, eight rebounds, six assists and three steals. Nine Warriors finished with at least eight points, a sign of the depth Kerr has been able to lean on. The Warriors, now 6-3, will look to keep the momentum going when they host the Orlando Magic on Saturday before closing their homestand against the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday. articles.summary: "Fresh" is the followup to 2025's "WHAM," which arrived at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, one of his four leaders on the all-genres albums chart.
articles._body: Baby’s back.   Two weeks after his big reveal , Lil Baby goes and drops Fresh , the followup to WHAM which arrived at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 following its release in February 2025. The Atlanta native packs it in with 17 Fresh tracks. Just two of those feature guest appearances: “All My Partnas” with Future, Young Thug and 4PF running mate Rylo Rodriguez, plus “In Your Head,” on which Rodriguez gives an assist. Sadly, there’s no Sabrina Carpenter collaboration — something the rapper recently admitted he was open to. “I’m still in that box a little bit, but I’m more open to stepping out of the box,” he told The New York Times’ Popcast last month. “The box is bigger. As I step out a little bit, the box gets bigger.” He added: “Even a Sabrina Carpenter — just say, for instance, in my head, I don’t have a song on my hard drive to send to her. But if we sit there and create something, or she sends me something, I feel like I could make it work.” The hip-hop star got the wheels moving on his new project in July with “Dead Fresh,” a Pharrell -produced number that cracked the Billboard Hot 100’s top 20, peaking at No. 18. Pharrell premiered “Dead Fresh” during Louis Vuitton’s Spring-Summer 2027 Men’s Show the previous month, in June. Lil Baby has amassed a ridiculous 160 titles on the Billboard Hot 100, including 13 top 10 appearances, and a further nine titles on the Billboard 200 chart, with four No. 1s. Baby closed out the year 2025 with The Leaks, a mixtape that debuted and peaked at No. 17 on the all-genres albums tally. The Leaks proved to be a late bloomer, as it lifted 25-1 in its second week on Billboard ’s Top Rap Albums chart, for his fifth consecutive leader. Fresh is Baby’s fifth studio album. “S/o To Everyone Who Played A Role In Bringing This Album To Life,” he writes on his Instagram . Stream Fresh below.

articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings have reached the “but” phase of the Kyler Murray era. That was quick. articles._body: The Minnesota Vikings have reached the “but” phase of the Kyler Murray era. That was quick. The two-time Pro Bowl quarterback is posting paltry production for the Purple and Gold, squandering some of the momentum that a first-class defense has built over the first half of the season. Murray will miss Monday’s matchup versus the Buffalo Bills due to a hamstring strain, and many are wondering if he will start again this year. Minnesota reportedly still thinks that the former No. 1 overall draft pick possesses the necessary talent to help them contend for a championship, but….. since he has yet to prove it on the field, management is forced to keep its options open going into the Nov. 10 trade deadline. “That hamstring injury for Kyler Murray is legitimate. He is week to week,” NFL on Prime Video insider James Palmer said after Thursday’s game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Baltimore Ravens. “Now, they still believe that Kyler Murray can play the best football of his career with this coaching staff, in this offense. They understand it takes time and they’re being patient. But that does not mean that they won’t address the quarterback position before Tuesday, I’m told. “They know the market, they know what options are out there. Their general manager Nolan Teasley has been working the phones over the last several weeks on a variety of positions. I’m told keep an eye on what happens Monday night.” The Vikings are going to start Carson Wentz Monday night against the Bills. Kyler Murray is dealing with a hamstring injury and is week to week. Could Minnesota look to add a QB before the deadline? My report on our @NFLonPrime postgame show. pic.twitter.com/gQMQBvvWW7 — James Palmer (@JamesPalmerTV) November 6, 2026 Based on Palmer’s report, it sounds as if Carson Wentz could potentially cement himself as the QB1 moving forward if he succeeds against the Bills . The former Second-Team All-Pro has completed 23-of-39 passes for 276 yards (59.0 completion percentage) with three touchdowns and no interceptions in 2026. Kyler Murray owns a 64.9 percent completion rate and has thrown for 1,022 yards and five TDs in six starts for the Vikings. He has tossed three picks and rushed for 167 yards. Neither player presently seems very appealing for the playoffs. Teasley and head coach Kevin O’Connell will thoroughly evaluate the room and determine if there are attainable QBs on the trade market who can properly supplement Brian Flores’ relentless defense and help Minnesota win its first Super Bowl. At time of print, they still have more than 100 hours left to decide. The post Vikings rumors: Insider won’t rule out potential QB trade after Kyler Murray injury appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Southeast Asia needs more regulation and investments for its cultural industries to scale, says POPS Worldwide CEO Esther Nguyen
articles.summary: While listeners today embrace music from different countries, there’s still a way to go before Southeast Asia’s music industry can scale globally.
articles._body: Open your TikTok or Instagram app and you’ll likely be greeted by short-form video content soundtracked by music from across the globe.  “Social networks have really democratized music , in terms of release, promotion and marketing so that anyone anywhere in the world can consume it,” said Esther Nguyen, CEO of Vietnam-headquartered entertainment firm POPS Worldwide, during the Fortune Southeast Asia 500 Summit in Vietnam on Nov. 3. While listeners today embrace music from different genres and countries, Nguyen says there’s still a way to go before Southeast Asia’s music industry can scale globally.  “It’s a concerted effort, and South Korea has done it really well,” Nguyen explained. “[You’ll need] government regulations and policies supporting IPs, legal infrastructure and frameworks, international export support, and investments and financial incentives.” “There needs to be a more robust investment community that are experts in entertainment and music,” she added. “L.A., New York and Tokyo, for example, [have] investors who are really well-versed in entertainment… an understanding of the industry really helps it to grow as well.” The fragmented nature of Southeast Asian markets can also make scaling its music industry tough. “While I have personally invested in certain entertainment assets, including large theme parks and music streaming platforms, I think the biggest challenge is the fragmentation in Southeast Asia,” said Sujey Subramanian , the APAC head of asset manager ICG. “Our typical minimum equity check is $50 million, and it’s just hard to find assets of scale in the region.” Music, and more The panelists also discussed South Korea’s rise to become an entertainment powerhouse, debating which parts of the country’s playbook could be applicable to Southeast Asia.   “The first thing that was exported from Korea was K-culture. We’re talking about K-dramas and food, and then K-pop came up on the back of that,” said Kenny Ong, the managing director of Sony Music for Malaysia, Singapore and Vietnam. “For Vietnam and any other Southeast Asian countries, we can’t just push content, but [also] have to create demand for the culture.” Parallel offerings, such as merchandise and live experiences like meet-and-greets and concerts, are also bumping up profit margins for artists. “ Physical music [products] are also growing [in popularity],” Ong added. “We’re talking about CDs, physical vinyls and box sets… In the past couple of years, they’re growing [in the] double digits.” Southeast Asia can also further capitalize on the rising popularity of concert-going by upgrading its physical infrastructure. “We need venues which can host different sizes of tours… It’s not just venues which host 50,000 , we need mid-sized venues that hold 4,000 to 5,000, and smaller venues holding around 2,000, in order for artists in each country to grow and perform.” Ultimately, the panelists were optimistic about the direction in which Southeast Asia’s music industry is headed. “We’ve seen a lot, especially in the past year, of the [Vietnamese] government really trying to clean up pirated sites and go after bad actors. We saw an eight-year IP case finally get fast-forwarded and be heard, and we got a positive result,” Nguyen concluded. “That being said, the enforcement and interpretation of IP laws still needs some work, but at least it’s going in the right direction.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.summary: Justin Verlander’s illustrious career came to an end in 2026, and he had his swan song with the team he started his big-league journey with, the Detroit Tigers. He also reunited with manager AJ Hinch, whom he spent three seasons with (2017 to 2019) on the Houston Astros, winning a World Ser
articles._body: Justin Verlander’s illustrious career came to an end in 2026, and he had his swan song with the team he started his big-league journey with, the Detroit Tigers. He also reunited with manager AJ Hinch , whom he spent three seasons with (2017 to 2019) on the Houston Astros, winning a World Series (albeit a controversial one) during their time together in the Lone Star State. But not even a player of Verlander’s stature is above the managerial authority of Hinch. The current Tigers manager recalled a time where he had to make the future Hall of Fame starting pitcher redo a drill in Spring Training, which speaks volumes to the moxie he possesses. “I remember the first time I ever had Justin Verlander on the mound in a PFP (pitcher’s fielding practice) in Spring Training, and that rep that gets messed up between pitcher and first baseman. And I’ve got to reset them. And I’ve got to send Verlander back to the mound. I’m in my late 30s, early 40s as a manager, and I’ve got this future Hall of Famer and he screwed up a play and I got to make him do it again,” Hinch recalled in an appearance on the “Dirt From the Dugout” podcast. “That was learned in Midwest City, Oklahoma as a 16-year-old kid throwing the ball away in infield practice and my dad and my head coach making me reset and do it again until I did it right. That’s something I think that everybody can learn from. It’s not a punishment. It’s a standard.” A.J. Hinch once had to send Justin Verlander back to the mound to redo a botched spring training rep. Where’d he learn that? His dad, when he was 16. “It’s not a punishment. It’s a standard.” pic.twitter.com/lN6OISJgzN — Dirt From the Dugout (@dirtfromthedug) November 5, 2026 Verlander did not get to where he was at his best by ignoring the instructions of his coaches, and it’s a testament as well to his teachability that he listened even when he could have been a prima donna. The Tigers believe that Hinch is the man for the job given the way he handles the clubhouse, as evidenced by the way he got Verlander to listen, and it will be interesting to see if it pays off in the future in the form of postseason success. articles.title: Warriors star Stephen Curry makes confident declaration after huge 2nd half vs. Heat helps extend win streak
articles.summary: Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors are rolling, and after a dominant second half carried them past the Miami Heat on Thursday night, the superstar guard sounded like a man who believes in this group. The Warriors pulled away for a 120-100 win at Chase Center, extending their winning stre
articles._body: Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors are rolling, and after a dominant second half carried them past the Miami Heat on Thursday night , the superstar guard sounded like a man who believes in this group. The Warriors pulled away for a 120-100 win at Chase Center, extending their winning streak to six games. Curry made it clear the hot stretch is doing wonders for the team’s belief. “This run that we are on is building a lot of confidence,” Curry said, via Anthony Slater of ESPN . It is easy to see why. After the game was tied 53-53 at halftime, Golden State blew it open in the third quarter, outscoring Miami 38-23. The Warriors won the second half 67-47 and led by as many as 20 points. Curry led the way with 29 points in just 28 minutes, shooting 9-of-19 from the field, 6-of-12 from deep and a perfect 5-of-5 from the free-throw line. He was able to rest down the stretch while the team’s younger players closed things out. It came on the heels of a 34-point outing in Monday’s win over the Phoenix Suns . Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg stuffed the stat sheet once again , finishing with 17 points, eight rebounds, six assists and three steals. Draymond Green dished out 11 assists, while nine Warriors scored at least eight points in a balanced effort. Will Richard and Brandon Williams each added 10 points, and Al Horford went a perfect 3-of-3 from the field for eight points. Golden State’s defense also feasted, forcing 22 Miami turnovers and turning them into 28 points. For Miami, Davion Mitchell scored 22 points and Giannis Antetokounmpo posted 20 points and 14 rebounds. Former Warriors star Klay Thompson, playing in his first game at Chase Center as a member of the Heat , finished with 11 points on 3-of-10 shooting, one night after hitting the game-winner against the LA Clippers . The win improved Golden State to 6-3 after an 0-3 start to the season. The Warriors have not lost since falling to the Phoenix Suns on Oct. 24. Miami, playing on the second night of a back-to-back, fell to 3-6. The Warriors will look to keep the streak alive when they wrap up their homestand against the Orlando Magic on Saturday and the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday. articles.title: Canadiens star Cole Caufield makes NHL history with more OT heroics to beat Mammoth
articles.summary: Cole Caufield and the Montreal Canadiens bounced back from a wild collapse in a big way, and the sniper made NHL history in the process. Caufield scored 30 seconds into overtime to lift Montreal to a 5-4 win over the Utah Mammoth at Bell Centre on Thursday night. The game-winner was Caufield’s 15
articles._body: Cole Caufield and the Montreal Canadiens bounced back from a wild collapse in a big way , and the sniper made NHL history in the process. Caufield scored 30 seconds into overtime to lift Montreal to a 5-4 win over the Utah Mammoth at Bell Centre on Thursday night. The game-winner was Caufield’s 15th career overtime goal, and he got there faster than anyone in league history. The 25-year-old reached the mark in just 384 career games, beating Connor McDavid, who needed 559 games to get to 15. Overtime has long been Caufield’s specialty. Last season, he scored back-to-back overtime winners against the Seattle Kraken and Nashville Predators in October, and he reached 40 goals for the first time in his career with an overtime winner against the Boston Bruins in March . Thursday’s goal was vintage Caufield. On a 2-on-1, the Canadiens forward faked a slap shot before ripping a wrist shot over the right shoulder of Mammoth goaltender Sebastian Cossa to send the Bell Centre crowd home happy. COLE CAUFIELD WINS IT IN OVERTIME pic.twitter.com/JAuuHUaQyW — B/R Open Ice (@BR_OpenIce) November 6, 2026 Montreal had to work for it. Utah’s Logan Cooley put on a show with three goals and an assist, recording his second hat trick in four games. Nick Schmaltz’s power-play goal gave the Mammoth a 4-3 lead early in the third period, but Adam Engstrom tied the game with 5:06 left in regulation to force overtime. Nick Suzuki made a strong return to the lineup after missing six games with an upper-body injury, finishing with a goal and two assists. Arber Xhekaj and Kirby Dach also scored for Montreal, and Jakub Dobes made 16 saves. The win was a much-needed response for the Canadiens. Just two nights earlier, Montreal blew a 4-0 lead in the final 2:39 of regulation and lost 5-4 in overtime to the Winnipeg Jets, marking the latest four-goal comeback in NHL history. Caufield had scored in that game, too. This time, he made sure the Canadiens came out on top in the extra period. Montreal improved to 10-3-3 on the season and has now won six of its last seven games. Utah, meanwhile, fell to 10-6-1. The Canadiens will look to keep the momentum going when they visit the Toronto Maple Leafs on Saturday. articles.title: Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence’s ‘relentless’ Liam Coen take that shows how he turned Jacksonville into a juggernaut
articles.summary: Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars kept rolling on Thursday night with a dominant 33-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens, and the star quarterback made sure head coach Liam Coen got his share of the credit. Speaking with the “Thursday Night Football” crew on Prime Video after the game, Law
articles._body: Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars kept rolling on Thursday night with a dominant 33-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens , and the star quarterback made sure head coach Liam Coen got his share of the credit. Speaking with the “Thursday Night Football” crew on Prime Video after the game , Lawrence was asked about Coen’s impact on the organization. Jacksonville is now 19-6 in the regular season since Coen took over. “Yeah, he’s great. I mean, he’s relentless the way he, you know, prepares, just the way he thinks. I think he’s a great leader for our team. You know, guys respond really well to, you know, how he leads. He’s got a lot of energy, a lot of enthusiasm, brings the juice every day. And then you see the things that we’re able to do offensively,” he said. "He's relentless the way he prepares." Trevor Lawrence on how Liam Coen has improved this Jaguars team #TNFonPrime pic.twitter.com/gHhqykOj0M — NFL on Prime Video (@NFLonPrime) November 6, 2026 “He’s also really smart, has a great staff that he’s put together, and guys that are great coaches around us. And then I think, you know, the players are all bought into it,” Lawrence added. The 27-year-old also shared a funny story about his head coach. After settling for three second-half field goals, the Jaguars finally found the end zone again late in the fourth quarter on a Chris Rodriguez touchdown run. Lawrence joked that the team “might have to take a commercial flight home” if they had not scored. “He wanted that 700,” he said with a laugh. That late touchdown pushed Coen’s offense to 702 points through 25 games together. The turnaround under Coen has been impressive. Coen arrived in 2025 from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, where he was offensive coordinator, and guided Jacksonville to a 13-4 record and an AFC South title . Lawrence finished fifth in MVP voting that year. This season, the Jaguars are 6-2 and look like one of the best teams in the AFC. Lawrence threw for 242 yards and a 50-yard touchdown to Parker Washington against the Ravens, and he now has 17 touchdowns to just four turnovers on the year. Traveling Jaguars fans even serenaded him with “MVP” chants in Baltimore. Jacksonville’s defense was just as impressive, holding Baltimore to 227 total yards and forcing three takeaways . With Lawrence and Coen clicking, the Jaguars have every reason to believe they can make a deep run this season. articles.title: Ravens RB Derrick Henry instantly shuts down trade noise after Jaguars rout
articles.summary: Derrick Henry and the Baltimore Ravens suffered another ugly loss on Thursday night, this time falling 33-10 to the Jacksonville Jaguars at M&T Bank Stadium. Amid growing chatter about his future, the star running back made it clear he is not thinking about going anywhere. Henry was asked aft
articles._body: Derrick Henry and the Baltimore Ravens suffered another ugly loss on Thursday night, this time falling 33-10 to the Jacksonville Jaguars at M&T Bank Stadium . Amid growing chatter about his future, the star running back made it clear he is not thinking about going anywhere . Henry was asked after the game whether he expects to remain with the team for the rest of the season, given Baltimore’s struggles. He quickly shut down the idea . “I’m not mentioning me going anywhere else. I’m saying let’s go back to work, try to get better and turn this around,” Henry said, via Cordell Woodland. The question came after ESPN’s Dan Graziano flagged Henry as “someone to keep an eye on” ahead of the trade deadline. The 32-year-old turns 33 in January and is set to earn $12 million next season, none of which is guaranteed. It has been a frustrating stretch for Henry and the Ravens. Baltimore has now lost four straight games, dropping to 4-5 and last place in the AFC North. Injuries have played a major role, with both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley landing on injured reserve. That forced undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into his first career start on just three days’ rest, and he completed 10 of 18 passes for 60 yards with two interceptions. Henry’s own struggles continued. He finished with 57 yards on 17 carries and took 10 direct snaps, marking his fourth straight game with fewer than 60 rushing yards. Justice Hill provided Baltimore’s lone touchdown with a 65-yard run in the fourth quarter, with the game already out of reach. Still, Henry made some history in the loss. He passed both Jerome Bettis and LaDainian Tomlinson to move into seventh place on the NFL’s all-time rushing list , with Curtis Martin next in his sights. Meanwhile, the Jaguars improved to 6-2 behind a balanced effort. Trevor Lawrence connected with Parker Washington on a 50-yard touchdown before halftime, and Cam Little knocked down four field goals. The Ravens will have extra time to regroup before hosting the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football on Nov. 16. Henry’s comments suggest he wants to be part of the turnaround, but Baltimore’s front office could face some tough decisions if the losing continues. articles.title: Lil Baby, JENNIE, Dove Cameron, XG, Boys Noize & More: New Music Friday Guide
articles.summary: Check out the must-hear releases of the week.
articles._body: Billboard’s Friday Music Guide serves as a handy guide to New Music Friday’s most essential releases each week — the key music that everyone will be talking about today, and that will be dominating playlists this weekend and beyond. Last week , we featured Dominic Fike, Mariah Carey and Queens of the Stone Age. This week, Lil Baby is back with his anticipated fifth album; JENNIE drops a new single for the animated Netflix film STEPS ; Dove Cameron releases her long-awaited debut album; and Boys Noize returns with his first solo studio album in five years.… plus much more. Check out all of this week’s picks below: Lil Baby, Fresh After scoring his third consecutive Billboard 200 No. 1 album with WHAM last year, Lil Baby is gunning for his fourth with Fresh . The new set arrives with a title inspired by his recent hit single “Dead Fresh,” an infectious, Pharrell-produced joint that soared to No. 18 on the Billboard Hot 100 and topped Rhythmic Airplay. Stacked with guest appearances by frequent collaborators Future, Young Thug and Rylo Rodriguez, Fresh finds Baby delivering 17 new songs that reassert his position as one of the most gifted mainstream MCs to blow up this decade. — KYLE DENIS JENNIE, “Someone To Hold” The inviting disco-colored intro of “Someone To Hold” neither sounds like a typical song for JENNIE nor a Disney princess — and that’s what makes it magic . The colorful pop song shows a new side of JENNIE’s artistry that leans more playful and vibrant than anything on her solo debut full-length, while also matching the fresh take of the movie it’s from — as the upcoming musical comedy Steps reimagines Cinderella from the perspective of the stepsisters. — L.H. Dove Cameron, Final Girl Despite launching her career over a decade ago in Disney TV and film franchises — also lending her voice to both — Final Girl is Dove Cameron’s debut full-length. At long last. The dramatic and soaring album delivers a range of tempos and emotions, from softer songs like pop ballad “Silver Screen Baby” and the raw “Immortalized” to uptempo dance-pop single “When In Rome” and the haunting and heavy “Skin On Bone.” It’s an album that was well worth the wait, and offers so much possibility and intrigue as to what sounds and styles Cameron will want to explore next. — L.H. Kings Of Leon, “Rose” Veteran rock band Kings Of Leon has released its 10th album, O My Beloved — and the first the band has ever self-produced. That decision paid off, as the gorgeous album marries thoughtful and melodic production with deeply personal storytelling about the member’s families and upbringings. Described in a press release as a “love letter” to the road that brought the band to this point, it feels just as much a love letter to the fans who have walked that road with them for more than two decades. — L.H . XG, “Depends” Since debuting in 2022, Japanese girl group XG have kept busy — especially this year. Since releasing its first full-length in January, titled THE CORE – 核 , the group has embarked on its second world tour and has now, amidst that outing, released more new music with “Depends.” The electro-pop track showcases the members vocal strengths, from hard-hitting raps to syrupy, soaring high notes — all of which are united with groovy, metallic production and making for a high-energy addition to its set. — L.H. Rex Orange County, “Elvis (featuring Brendan Yates)” British alternative artist Rex Orange County is back with his sixth album, Dream Fatigue , with featured artists including Mustafa, Daniel Ceasar and Turnstile lead singer Brendan Yates (on “Elvis”). There’s a dark beauty to the song, on which Rex sings of lover-boy nerves: “I’m not so calm, I shake my legs like I’m Elvis/ I wanna be your only friend ’cause I’m selfish/ I wanna stay here forever like it’s Vegas/ There’s no one else I wanna share this hotel with.” Yates joins for a final verse before he and Rex harmonize on an outro that lingers long after the last note. — L.H. Slayyyter, “Hey Boyyy” In just one month, on Dec. 4, Slayyyter will unveil the counterpart to this year’s acclaimed WOR$T GIRL IN AMERICA album. Aptly titled wor$t man in america , the new album will contrast the perspectives she shared and ideas she explored on its predecessor. Frenetic new single “Hey Boyyy” delivers on Slayyyter’s signature sound thought is a bit softer in its lyrics, striking a balance only she can between a chaotic nature with good intentions. “I can’t stop blushing/ I’m too old to feel, more than nothing, she sings ahead of the chorus in which she admits, “Hey, boy, I got a funny little secret/ I get so nervous when you talk to me.” Not even ascendant superstars are immune. — L.H. Boys Noize, 7LLVSION After nearly two decades as an underground hero, it feels like the world finally caught up to Boys Noize. Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross tapped him to remix their 2024 score for Challengers , then brought him on to co-produce much of their 2025 Tron: Ares soundtrack, finding clear connective tissue between their own industrial rock and the industrial electronic of the Boys Noize catalog. The Iraqi-German producer born Alex Ridha then lived out a rock ‘n’ roll fantasy, effectively becoming a member of Nine Inch Nails while opening for and playing with the band on its Peel It Back run before releasing the collaborative Nine Inch Noize album and playing a pair of Coachella shows that some called among the best in the festival’s history. articles.summary: Jonathan Taylor watched the Indianapolis Colts trade left guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner hours apart. He probably caught glimpse of a team social media post that was hyping up rookie running back Seth McGowan on that same day. He also knows that the organization is und
articles._body: Jonathan Taylor watched the Indianapolis Colts trade left guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner hours apart. He probably caught glimpse of a team social media post that was hyping up rookie running back Seth McGowan on that same day. He also knows that the organization is undergoing changes after firing general manager Chris Ballard. The franchise has done everything to signal that a rebuild is underway, except ship out No. 28. Most fans anticipate that he too will switch teams before the Nov. 10 deadline, and apparently, so does the player himself. “My understanding is Jonathan Taylor expects to be traded,” insider James Palmer said on the NFL on Prime Video postgame show Thursday night. “We’ll see if somebody gets up {to the Colts’ high asking price}.” What's the latest on Jonathan Taylor heading into the weekend? My report on our @NFLonPrime postgame show. pic.twitter.com/nmW4l3Xdcm — James Palmer (@JamesPalmerTV) November 6, 2026 Palmer listed the Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants, Green Bay Packers and Denver Broncos as suitors. There have been offers, but Indianapolis is currently not satisfied with the packages that are being presented. Nonetheless, Taylor is bracing himself for a change of scenery. The 27-year-old is a former All-Pro who has led the NFL in rushing yards once and rushing touchdowns twice. He is the Colts’ all-time leader in the latter category (77 TDs) and ranks second behind Edgerrin James in the former (8,208). The body of work is undeniably impressive, hence why Indy is seeking significant value in return. But is a decline coming? Taylor is averaging an adequate yet unspectacular 4.1 yards per rushing attempt this season. While he is still dangerous with the ball in his hands, one has to wonder if this efficiency dip is only the beginning. Back-to-back seasons with 300-plus carries are bound to take a toll on a man. Playoff-caliber squads clearly still covet his skill set, however. Taylor is preparing for Sunday’s meeting with the visiting Dallas Cowboys, but he is perfectly aware of the prominent place he occupies in the rumor mill . The No. 41 pick in the 2020 NFL Draft is exercising common sense ahead of the trade deadline. Taylor has amassed 812 scrimmage yards and eight touchdowns through eight games played. articles.title: JENNIE’s ‘Steps’ Soundtrack ‘Someone to Hold’ Is Here: Stream It Now
articles.summary: The fresh cut will appear on the soundtrack for the forthcoming Netflix animated film, "Steps."
articles._body: JENNIE strides on out with her latest solo cut “Someone to Hold,” which appears on the soundtrack for the forthcoming Netflix animated film, Steps . The BLACKPINK star shares in full her new song , written and produced by Justin Tranter. “Someone to Hold” is light on its feet, a melodic neo-disco production with strings, slapping bass, and layers of JENNIE vocals. On it, she sings: “After, after everything that we’ve been through / The ins and outs, the upside downs and good times too / You’re still the shooting star that’s in my skies / You’re still the only one I want in every life.” Tranter, who wrote and produced three more original songs for the film’s official soundtrack, has described “Someone to Hold” as “pure danceable joy inspired by vintage organic dance pop.” Directed by Alyce Tzue and John Ripa, Steps sends the tale of Cinderella in a different direction. According to a statement, Cinderella’s “evil” stepsisters Lilith (Ali Wong) steals the magic wand belonging to the Fairy Godmother (Bette Midler) and hijacks the Royal Ball with Margot (Stephanie Hsu). Enter Priscilla (Nikki Glaser), a “villainous schemer who swoops in and snatches the throne.” With Priscilla in charge, consider the party over. And the happily-ever-after ending ruined. Realizing her terrible move, Lilith must join forces with Cinderella (Amanda Seyfried) in an epic quest, with battles royale and friendships forged along the way. “We love how Jennie’s bright and spirited ‘Someone To Hold’ represents Lilith, Cinderella, and Margot’s sisterhood, giving audiences a shot of energy and positivity straight to the heart,” Tzue and Ripa comment in a statement. Steps is produced by Amy Poehler, Jane Hartwell, Kim Lessing, with Poehler and Lessing producing for Paper Kite Productions. The companion soundtrack arrives Nov. 20, the same day as Steps rolls out on Netflix. JENNIE is coming off her biggest hit as a solo artist with her guest work on Tame Impala’s “Dracula” remix, which went to No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 2 on the Official U.K. Singles Chart and enjoyed a scary Halloween streaming boost . Pre-save Steps here and stream “Someone to Hold” below.
