articles.title: Giants DC Dennard Wilson drops defiant truth bomb on holding his defense accountable
articles.summary: Dennard Wilson has not been shy about calling out the New York Giants’ defense this season, and the defensive coordinator is not changing his approach as the team prepares to face the Philadelphia Eagles. Asked whether there is a danger in being so blunt publicly, Wilson did not flinch. “I think
articles._body: Dennard Wilson has not been shy about calling out the New York Giants’ defense this season , and the defensive coordinator is not changing his approach as the team prepares to face the Philadelphia Eagles. Asked whether there is a danger in being so blunt publicly, Wilson did not flinch . “I think we get too caught up into not speaking the truth, right? The film doesn’t lie, and it never lies. And it’s always evidence. It’s a solid tape. And what I said in front of this podium, they’ve heard me say it from the first day they were here. So it’s nothing that they haven’t heard before,” Wilson said, via SNY. Dennard Wilson talks about holding himself and his defense accountable: "We get too caught up in not speaking the truth. The film doesn't lie…too many coaches these days are scared to have those hard conversations" pic.twitter.com/5OOKpo14dQ — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) November 5, 2026 “It’s not calling out a specific player. It’s calling out a behavior. It’s calling out what we’re not doing collectively, because at the end of the day, it’s me as well. So if I let it slip, shame on me,” he continued. “You know, I think too many coaches these days are scared to have those hard conversations.” Wilson added that a strong bond with his players is what allows him to be so direct. “If you build a relationship and you have this bond and you have this tight-knit group, you can speak to them in a certain way and identify certain things without attacking them personally. It’s not a personal attack. It’s a behavioral attack,” Wilson said. “And that’s how I go about it, and that’s how I’ve been trained to do this since I was a young coach 20-some years ago.” Wilson made headlines last month after a Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints, when the Giants missed 18 tackles. He did not hold back, labeling players who do not run to the ball as “traitors to the defense” and warning that “if you don’t change the behaviors, we have to change the players.” New York bounced back with a 27-21 road win over the Houston Texans in Week 7, and the Giants enter Sunday’s matchup at 4-2-1 coming off their bye. Wilson joined John Harbaugh’s staff in January after two seasons as the Tennessee Titans’ defensive coordinator, reuniting with the coach he worked under in Baltimore. The Giants will now look to keep it rolling against an Eagles team that has dropped six straight games. articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has no hard feelings toward Brandon Aiyuk despite their lengthy separation. With the receiver seeking reinstatement ahead of the NFL trade deadline, Purdy said any potential reunion on Friday would be met with nothing but love. Aiyuk is expected to repo
articles._body: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has no hard feelings toward Brandon Aiyuk despite their lengthy separation. With the receiver seeking reinstatement ahead of the NFL trade deadline, Purdy said any potential reunion on Friday would be met with nothing but love. Aiyuk is expected to report to San Francisco’s facility after filing paperwork to return from the reserve/left squad list. However, his future with the organization remains uncertain following a prolonged absence. Asked whether he had considered what he might say to Aiyuk, Purdy admitted he hadn’t given the possibility much thought. “Nah, I haven’t,” Purdy said in comments shared by OurSF49ers. “Like I’ve said before, I love what we did together when we played together and everything, and obviously haven’t spoken to him in a long time or anything.” Purdy acknowledged that he doesn’t fully understand Aiyuk’s circumstances, emphasizing that the situation remains beyond his control. “Not really sure what the whole situation is and stuff, that’s out of my control, but if I saw him, it would be nothing but love from me.” The two previously developed a productive connection during San Francisco’s playoff runs. Aiyuk recorded a career-high 1,342 receiving yards in 2023, helping the 49ers reach Super Bowl 58. Meanwhile, coach Kyle Shanahan previously indicated he had mentally moved on from Aiyuk, although general manager John Lynch has not completely ruled out a reunion. For Purdy, the situation remains personal rather than contractual. Whatever San Francisco ultimately decides, the quarterback made it clear that his respect for his former teammate hasn’t disappeared. articles._body: Don’t look now, but Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars may be legitimate Super Bowl contenders. The Jaguars blew out the Baltimore Ravens 33-10 on Thursday night , improving to 6-2 while extending their NFL-best point differential to a whopping +108. That is nearly double the next-best team, which is the San Francisco 49ers with a +58. Lawrence did not have the best day statistically as he finished with 242 yards and a touchdown. Nevertheless, the Jaguars quarterback was still serenaded with MVP chants by a sizable section of Jags fans who made the trip to Baltimore. Trevor Lawrence gets MVP chants after the Jaguars' HUGE win on Thursday Night Football (via @NFLonPrime ) pic.twitter.com/8C1AUPo4iH — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 6, 2026 Lawrence finished fifth in MVP voting last season as he led the Jags to a 13-4 record with over 4,000 yards passing and 29 touchdowns against 12 interceptions. This season, he is on pace to throw for 4,100 yards and 41 touchdowns with a potentially similar record. With a relatively easy schedule the rest of the way, owing to a weak AFC South, there’s a chance they could claim the top seed in the AFC . There does not seem to be a truly standout MVP contender this season, which could end up benefitting Lawrence. At the moment, he, Brock Purdy, and Josh Allen project to have similar cases as the quarterbacks for the best teams in the league. If Lawrence can lead the Jaguars to the best record in the NFL while leading the league in touchdowns, he could make a compelling MVP case as the league’s new quarterback star. But talk of Lawrence for MVP is much too soon. With half the season remaining, there is still a lot that can happen, and a lot that Lawrence still needs to prove. articles.title: Ravens’ Mark Andrews is completely unfazed after getting booed by home fans
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens fans are understandably frustrated after losing their franchise quarterback for a big chunk of the season once again. They have seen more lackluster football than they are accustomed to, and they have had enough. Those who filled M&T Bank Stadium for Thursday night’s fa
articles._body: Baltimore Ravens fans are understandably frustrated after losing their franchise quarterback for a big chunk of the season once again. They have seen more lackluster football than they are accustomed to, and they have had enough. Those who filled M&T Bank Stadium for Thursday night’s face-off with the Jacksonville Jaguars probably purchased their tickets with the intent to watch Lamar Jackson compete. They had a few days to accept their new reality, however. Undrafted rookie third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano was set to make his first NFL start in the rain, and do so against a defense that recorded nine interceptions in its first seven matchups while allowing an AFC-best 15.9 points per game. And do so while nursing an ankle injury. Simply put, there was little reason to expect a positive outcome. The home crowd was nevertheless disgusted by what it witnessed in Charm City. Fans booed during what ended up being a 33-10 loss. Some players can take such a reaction the wrong way, especially when considering the obvious adversity they are currently suffering through. Mark Andrews is not letting the jeers get to him , though. He is focused on keeping the locker room united amid this four-game losing streak. “They have every right to boo or do whatever they want to do,” the ninth-year tight end told the media, per The Baltimore Sun’s Josh Tolentino. “Obviously, us in here, we have to stay together… Just keep on relying on each other. You got to be there for your brother, and that’s what we’re going to do. Keep it in house and continue to fight for one another. We’ll see how this thing shakes out, but I believe we have a bunch of fighters.” The Ravens may have fighters, but they certainly did not do much swinging on Thursday. Mark Andrews on being booed at home: pic.twitter.com/dGMFfkBkba — Josh Tolentino (@JCTSports) November 6, 2026 Fagnano completed 10 passes for a mere 60 yards and threw two interceptions versus the Jaguars. Andrews led all Baltimore pass-catchers with 19 yards. Derrick Henry once again struggled, posting an inefficient 57 yards on 17 carries. Fellow running back Justice Hill scored the squad’s only touchdown, courtesy of a 65-yard run with 7:15 left in the fourth quarter. The Ravens are severely limited without a viable QB option. They better hope that the arriving Jacoby Brissett , who was benched in his final start for the Arizona Cardinals, can energize the offense. Baltimore still has much to fix on defense, however. Field position obviously matters, but fans still want more from a lauded defensive mind like Jesse Minter. Those in attendance could not find a silver lining in this Jacksonville-issued drubbing . Mark Andrews is wisely emphasizing the importance of cohesion. There is already plenty going against this group. Players cannot mentally check out. If the Ravens (4-5) fail to defend their house versus the presently winless Los Angeles Chargers next Monday, then they might need to take cover. articles.title: Packers’ Evan Williams credits red-hot Green Bay defense for winning Defensive Player of the Month
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers enjoyed a stellar October month which saw them win four of their five matches to bring themselves up to 5-3 for the season. And well, as a result of what has been an impressive season thus far, safety Evan Williams was named NFC Defensive Player of the Month for October afte
articles._body: The Green Bay Packers enjoyed a stellar October month which saw them win four of their five matches to bring themselves up to 5-3 for the season. And well, as a result of what has been an impressive season thus far, safety Evan Williams was named NFC Defensive Player of the Month for October after recording 41 tackles, two interceptions, four passes defended, one sack, three quarterback hits and a fumble recovery. Williams himself credited the red-hot Packers defence for the award , per a post on X by Matt Schneidman. “Pretty good, pretty good, it’s definitely a blessing man, even be considered for something like that,” he said. “I feel like it’s really more of a group award than anything. We say when we’re all succeeding, that’s when individuals start to see success … it’s a blessing to receive some recognition like that.” Williams was selected in the fourth round of the 2024 NFL draft , and is currently having a breakthrough year. Williams became the third safety since 2000 to record at least 40 tackles and three takeaways in a single month, and the first to accomplish the feat since 2011. Williams posted a 90.9 overall defensive grade in October, the highest among NFL defenders, while recording 31 solo tackles, six pressures, 10 defensive stops and three turnovers. He allowed just seven completions for 58 yards on targets in coverage, surrendered no touchdowns and gave up a passer rating of 21.1. Williams received his first Defensive Player of the Month award and became the third Packers safety to win the NFC honor, joining Xavier McKinney in 2024 and Atari Bigby in 2007. Green Bay has now had a player win the October award in three consecutive years, with Micah Parsons receiving it in 2025 and McKinney in 2024. The Packers will now travel to Gillette Stadium to take on the New England Patriots, and will hope to continue their stellar run in November. articles._body: Our team is excited to launch Stitch.ai this week. We've been working hard to bring knowledge workers, freelancers and founders a workspace that doesn't require hopping between apps and tabs; everything is in one app. The Stitch.ai app includes mail, calendar, contacts, tasks, notes, sheets, slides, files, boards and forms. We sort of still can't believe we managed to build so many tools! We use auto-generated Knots and Tags to label your work, helping you surface related items with one click. Stitching is also a great feature that allows you to 'Stitch'. your items together. You can Stitch tasks to events, emails to notes, and slides to contacts. What gets Stitched together stays together! We've also launched Stitchy, our AI assistant who works with you across everything. She writes your emails, schedules events and manages your tasks. Oh, and she's a dog in a robot costume so that's a bonus! She also runs jobs for you, so you can ask her to watch out for email replies, send daily project updates, or give you daily news snippets to read with your morning protein matcha espresso latte. Everything is built-in, so there's no need to set up email clients or integrations. You get your own @stitch.ai email address when you sign up. Try it out for free for 7 days at the link! We'd love for the HN community to play around with it, send emails, schedule events, try out Knots and Tags, Stitching items, and give us your honest feedback! articles._body: A new era beckons for the Los Angeles Angels. After 23 years, Arte Moreno finally decided to give up ownership of the franchise — selling it to Kroenke Sports & Entertainment for a reported $4 billion figure. And while the expectation is that, under new management, the Angels will be turning it around, they’ve been so bad for so long that it’s going to take some time to get this team back to playing winning baseball. To that end, it looks like the Angels, according to this insider, should at least be exploring the trade market for one of their best position players in shortstop Zach Neto, who recorded 27 home runs and 77 runs batted in across 157 games in 2026. “This is the time to gauge interest in Zach Neto and Reid Detmers,” MLB Network’s Jon Morosi said on Hot Stove. “The Angels, I believe, have two of the most appealing names out there. When you talk about Neto in particular, I love his skillset and the way that he could potentially fit with any number of teams.” “There is tremendous interest in the industry right now… I suspect this is not our last conversation about the possibility of a Zach Neto trade.” – @jonmorosi on #MLBNHotStove pic.twitter.com/1AERogVlnL — MLB Network (@MLBNetwork) November 6, 2026 Only 25 years of age, Neto has three years of team control remaining, so the Angels should be in no rush to trade him away. But for Morosi, the Angels are so deep into their rebuild that it might be better off to cash in on Neto as a trade asset to replenish their farm system even further. “The Angels are very much in a rebuilding phase. If you’re looking at the Angels, this is a building job. It’s not about winning a World Series in 2027. It’s about building a consistent winner by the end of this decade. And if you’re not gonna sign him long-term, think about ways to trade him now to get prospects,” Morosi added. Neto is averaging over 21 home runs per season in his career, and he’s playing a premium defensive position, so the likely outcome here is that he starts the 2027 season with the Angels. articles.title: What Ravens’ Joe Fagnano said after getting pummeled by Jaguars in first NFL start
articles.summary: Joe Fagnano did not have a very ideal first NFL start. The Baltimore Ravens quarterback, stepping in after the team’s top two signal-callers went down with injuries, was seemingly thrown to the wolves on Thursday as he struggled mightily in a 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars at M&
articles._body: Joe Fagnano did not have a very ideal first NFL start. The Baltimore Ravens quarterback, stepping in after the team’s top two signal-callers went down with injuries, was seemingly thrown to the wolves on Thursday as he struggled mightily in a 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars at M&T Bank Stadium. But at least Fagnano was aware enough of his performance to not make any excuses. “I’m not here to make excuses. We just didn’t execute. I have to play better,” the 25-year-old Fagnano said after the game, via Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic. Fagnano, an undrafted rookie out of the UConn Huskies football program, completed just 10 of his 18 passes for 60 passing yards against the Jaguars. He had zero touchdowns and was picked off twice, while getting sacked once. But the offense as a whole clearly had a hard time making things happen for the Ravens . Running back Derrick Henry turned 17 carries for only 57 rushing yards. Justice Hill had 85 rushing yards, but a bulk of those came off a 65-yard rushing score in garbage time in the fourth quarter. Overall, Baltimore compiled just 227 total yards with three turnovers. The Ravens never had an attempt inside the 20-yard line and were 4-of-14 on third downs. Fagnano’s time as a starter is also seemingly about to end, with the Ravens acquiring veteran Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. The Ravens lost Lamar Jackson and chief backup Tyler Huntley to injury, leaving them with the decision to give Fagnano the keys to the offense on the field, as they await for the Brissett trade to get finalized. articles._body: “Bold City” shook up “Charm City” on Thursday Night Football. The Jacksonville Jaguars forced the Baltimore Ravens to chuck a tabl et and hit new franchise lows in the 33-10 rout. But in the process, coach Liam Coen, quarterback Trevor Lawrence and company just put the NFL on notice. Even in a loaded AFC, the Jags are the new team to beat for these reasons. Trevor Lawrence is starting to play his best football Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Bold statement to make, considering how Lawrence has established himself as a Pro Bowler. But few quarterbacks have created a tear like he has. “T-Law” hasn’t delivered a multiple interception game in his last eight contests. He’s also thrown eight touchdowns compared to one pick in his last three games. Furthermore, the Jaguars have gone 14-3 in their last 17 games with Lawrence behind center. And during that time, he’s thrown two or three picks in only two of those contests. Lawrence currently has thrown 17 touchdowns compared to four aerial takeaways during this start. Coen has unlocked him even further thanks to this pre-snap motion heavy offense featuring play actions and bootlegs, the latter taking advantage of Lawrence’s mobility. Liam Coen offense is birthing new stars Travis Register-Imagn Images Not just limited to a more resurgent Lawrence either. Wide receiver Parker Washington is averaging 16 yards a catch and leads with four receiving touchdowns. Jakobi Myers has become resurgent in averaging a career-best 14 yards a reception . Then there’s leading receiver at tight end in Brenton Strange, who’s also hitting a new personal best with 11.9 yards a catch. All three have surpassed 20 receptions and benefitting from the Los Angeles Rams style attack Coen brought to Duval County. But there’s one more fast riser here in running back Bhayshul Tuten. The 2025 fourth rounder owns a combined six touchdowns and has racked up 673 total yards. Oh, Jacksonville and Coen are starting to involve Travis Hunter both ways too after finally becoming convinced to increase his snaps. But Coen’s offense has tallied an astonishing 702 total points through 25 games together. Ballhawks reside on defense Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Hunter is one with two picks on the season to go along with six pass breakups. Fellow cornerback Jourdan Lewis has grabbed two picks too. Linebacker Foyesade Oluokun adds to the pick party too with his couple of takeaways. But the Jags features nine different defenders who have broken up two to six throws. That includes safety Rayuan Lane III with his four PBUs. “Bold City” has created a no fly zone under defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile. This will mean names like Patrick Mahomes of the Kansas City Chiefs, Josh Allen of the Buffalo Bills, even Aaron Rodgers of the Pittsburgh Steelers have a loaded pass defense to deal with should one of them face the Jaguars. articles.title: Show HN: Repairer – close the breach when a Linux flaw goes public
articles.summary:
As we've seen with the Ubuntu critical CVE-2026-98432 (CVSS 9.8), AI-dicovered zero day exploit are being reported at an exponential rate and we don't have the process for dealing with the flood of exploits in real time.

What we need is an AI-based system for autopatching systems based on real
articles._body: As we've seen with the Ubuntu critical CVE-2026-98432 (CVSS 9.8), AI-dicovered zero day exploit are being reported at an exponential rate and we don't have the process for dealing with the flood of exploits in real time. What we need is an AI-based system for autopatching systems based on real time information. The vendor's fix can take days or weeks to be out (is the Ubuntu thing patched yet?) and meanwhile the grid is vulnerable to exploitation, especially AI worms. Repairer is a small program that runs on each of your servers. The day an exploit goes public it puts up a stopgap that blocks it, and once the real fix is up it takes the stopgap back off by itself. A stopgap only takes something away — drop certain packets, turn off a kernel module or service, remove a setuid bit. It never opens a port, installs or downloads anything, nor runs code. It arms an undo playbook before applying the stopgap, so the change reverts if affects any services. It only ever acts on rules you sign with a (hardware) crypto wallet. Let's go further: stopgaps are written and checked by a swarm of AI agents (gnosh.ai sessions) running on gno.land, each with bonded stake. Each stopgap is run on fresh machines, and whoever is caught lying loses their stake to whoever caught them. The agent is built and tested on Ubuntu and Debian, all open source, standard-library Go. More distros coming. Let's build repairer together. https://gno.security/repairer/ https://github.com/gnosecurity/repairer Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50388417 Points: 1 # Comments: 1

articles.title: ‘It Would Take a Lot to Say No to Australia’: Foo Fighters Kick-Off Tour Down Under With Three-Hours of Power
articles.summary: The Foos were back on familiar turf for their Take Cover Australian tour opener at Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane, the noisy neighbor to the XXXX brewery.
articles._body: Australia is at the mercy of factors beyond anyone’s control. Extreme weather, the tyranny of distance. This great southern land is at the ass-end of the world, a journey that that will take many travelers a day out of their life to get there, and another to return home. In rocks the Foo Fighters , again, urging you to hold their beer. In January of this year , the U.S. band completed the long-haul for a one-off show in Launceston, the second city of Tasmania, an island some 1,600 miles north of Antarctica. On that occasion, the Foos spent 48 hours traveling, for a three-hour show at UTAS Stadium. Mission accomplished. Four years earlier, in 2022, Dave Grohl and Co. performed for one-night only at GMHBA Stadium in Geelong, a satellite city of Melbourne, to help refuel a touring industry crippled by the lockdown. On Thursday night (Nov. 5), the Foos were back on familiar turf for their Take Cove r Australian tour opener at Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane , the noisy neighbor to the XXXX brewery. It’s their second visit to this country in 10 months. In a quirk of the schedule, the band will break after the Adelaide date on the tour, Nov. 17, and return in late January for New Zealand shows and a tour closer in Perth. Count them. That’s three visits to Australia in a year, all of them for concerts produced by Frontier Touring. View this post on Instagram The Foos love Australia, and it’s reciprocated. Guitarist Chris Shiflett stepped out wearing an AC/DC shirt, with the sleeves hacked off. Grohl recounted his three-decade-long affair with the country, before the band played “Big Me” from their self-titled 1995 debut album. The parody “Footos” music video, Grohl revealed, was shot here. The Foos might as well have Aussie passports at this point. “I’m so f—ing grateful, and lucky, that we’re still here 30 years later, and coming to tour for you guys again,” Grohl told his audience. “It would take a lot to say no to Australia.” From the gritty staccato chords of “All My Life” and Grohl’s “are you f—ing ready” pep talk, through to the Foos’ traditional ending number “Everlong,” Billboard soaked up the action on a glorious spring night. Check out four outstanding moments below.

articles.title: Ravens’ Jesse Minter doesn’t hold back on ‘unacceptable’ play after latest blowout loss
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens suffered a blowout 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday Night Football, extending their losing skid to four straight games. The Ravens started undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano amid their quarterback injury crisis, and he was unable to make much of an impact in the g
articles._body: The Baltimore Ravens suffered a blowout 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday Night Football, extending their losing skid to four straight games. The Ravens started undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano amid their quarterback injury crisis, and he was unable to make much of an impact in the game after the Ravens went down big. While Ravens head coach Jesse Minter acknowledged the team was in a tough spot with Fagnano starting, he was not pleased with their second-half showing . “In the second half, we just got in our own way. We’re turning the ball over a couple times in a row. The defense was out there, it felt like the whole half. I thought they battled and fought, and did a decent job in the second half. But obviously, the results are not acceptable for us and what we’re after,” Minter said. After a relatively clean first half, Fagnano immediately threw an interception in the first drive of the second half, which led to a Jaguars field goal. The Ravens then committed back-to-back turnovers with another pick and a fumble to start the fourth quarter, which allowed the Jags to blow the game wide open. These second-half collapses are becoming a common occurrence for the Ravens. Their current four-game losing streak started with back-to-back meltdowns against the Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals with Tyler Huntley at quarterback. While the absence of Lamar Jackson amid this skid has been huge, Minter has much work to do in terms of keeping his team playing to a high standard for the entire game. articles._body: Brandon Aiyuk has gashed the San Francisco 49ers many times since 2024, and those wounds may never fully heal. But the memories he created with his teammates might also stand the test of time. Trent Williams sill cares for the controversial wide receiver . “I haven’t talked to him, but you know, obviously Aiyuk is family,” the three-time First-Team All-Pro left tackle told reporters, per the OurSF49ers X account. “You know what he went through with his career and business endeavors, you know, you kind of got to step back and let somebody just let him figure it out. We just focus on the Raiders. He come in, {I’ll} be happy to see him, obviously, but that’s out of my hands.” Aiyuk and agent Drew Rosenhaus will meet with the 49ers on Friday to discuss a path forward, leaving many to speculate. Will the organization release him? Is there any chance that the 2023 Second-Team All-Pro suits up again for the franchise that drafted him back in 2020? Williams does not seem to hold a grudge. Other members of the locker room may feel differently , however. Trent Williams on Brandon Aiyuk: “I haven't talked to him, but you know, obviously Aiyuk is family. You know what he went through with his career and business endeavors, you know, you kind of got to step back and let somebody just let him figure it out….we just focus on the… pic.twitter.com/OwYsG7AMnG — OurSF49ers (@OurSf49ers) November 6, 2026 When healthy and at full force, Aiyuk can certainly provide a boost to any offense, but he has not played in an NFL game since tearing his ACL, MCL and meniscus versus the Kansas City Chiefs on October 20, 2024. His attitude is also a potential drawback. Brandon Aiyuk engaged in a training camp hold-in and nearly got himself traded after a tense contract standoff, before ultimately inking a $120 million extension. He suffered season-ending injuries less than two months into the 2024 campaign and then eventually became disgruntled once again. The 28-year-old has flung several insults at the 49ers and stated his desire to play elsewhere. Both John Lynch and Kyle Shanahan appear mentally over the entire ordeal . Perhaps Aiyuk and the 49ers can finally reach a resolution. Trent Williams understands the complicated nature of this situation. Do not expect him to side against management, but the future Hall of Famer clearly still has room in his heart for the former No. 11. articles.title: The AI boom is the first platform shift where there are ‘real advantages’ of building from Asia, says Antler’s founder and CEO Magnus Grimeland
articles.summary: A few factors make Asia an appealing home for startups: a rapidly growing electricity grid, and an abundance of advanced chips and engineering talent.
articles._body: Despite its fragmented markets and myriad of cultures and spoken languages, Asia is becoming an increasingly popular home for budding tech and AI entrepreneurs, according to Magnus Grimeland, the founder and CEO of venture capital firm Antler . “Going to the U.S. to build companies is still very popular and we see that happening at scale,” Grimeland said at the Fortune Southeast Asia 500 Summit in Vietnam on Nov. 3. “[But] for the first time ever in one of these platform shifts, there are real advantages in Asia that will lead to a lot of the leading companies being built out of here.” According to Crunchbase data , investors poured $42.8 billion into startup funding rounds across all of Asia in the second quarter of 2026—the highest quarterly total in over three years. In Grimeland’s telling, several factors make Asia an appealing home for startups: a rapidly growing electricity grid, and an abundance of advanced chips and AI engineering talent. “If you look at global power production, there’s four times more power being generated and built in Asia per year than in Europe and the U.S. combined,” he explained. “Most of that is in China, but [it’s happening] in the rest of Asia as well… the cost of power has gone down drastically compared to what you can access in the U.S..” Asia, too, is leading in the physical AI realm . “All the leading companies in that space are here,” Grimeland said. “There’s very, very few autonomous vehicles on the streets in the U.S…. [but there’s] one company in China that has more autonomous vehicles on the streets than the rest of the world combined.” Uneven growth Yet, the allocation of venture funding remains hugely uneven within Asia. Thus far in 2026, 68.1%—or $96.1 billion of $141 billion—of VC funds entering Asia flowed into China, mainly to AI startups such as DeepSeek, Moonshot AI and StepFun, according to Dealroom data . By contrast, only $10.7 billion of venture funding went to Southeast Asia during the first nine months of the year. “I get this question all the time: “What kinds of AI deals are you seeing in the Philippines?”” said Franco Varona, managing partner at Foxmont Capital Partners , a Philippines-based early growth fund. “[But] we don’t have the infrastructure for an LLM developer. We don’t even have the infrastructure for AI apps to be developed in the Philippines.” Varona, a Canada-born Filipino, argued that this environment creates different investment opportunities. “In developed markets, you can already benefit from the infrastructure which has been developed, and you can invest in innovators, because those innovators have everything around them that can help them out,” Varona said. “[But] when we think about investing in an emerging market like the Philippines, we think about it as investing in the infrastructure itself.”  To date, Foxmont has launched several themed funds , including one on digitization in the Philippines, and another focused on accessibility and affordability for Filipino consumers. The unique corporate dynamic in Asia has also pushed the region’s long-running venture firms to launch new funding models. Singapore-headquartered VC firm Granite Asia’s private credit fund Libra Hybrid , for example, combines the characteristics of both debt and equity into a single financial instrument.  “A lot of businesses [in Asia] are family owned or part of conglomerates,” said Ming Eng, Granite Asia’s managing partner. “They may not be interested in dilution or going for an IPO at any point in time… but they still need strategic capital to help them grow, and that’s where we see a lot of opportunities to help founders and companies, [by] having a different form of capital other than [pure] equity.” All three panelists remained bullish on Asia’s VC scene, despite recent geopolitical headwinds . “We are going into a world now where the balance of innovation is clearly shifting,” concluded Grimeland of Antler. “There’s a real chance that more than the majority of the most exciting and innovative companies in [the AI] space will have been built out of Asia, and that has never happened before.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Ravens’ Jesse Minter declines to give any Lamar Jackson injury update after losing to Jaguars
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars defeated the Baltimore Ravens 33-10 on Thursday night, extending the Ravens’ losing streak to four games. The Ravens were without quarterback Lamar Jackson, who had injured his right throwing thumb in a collision against the Buffalo Bills. Jackson was making a return from
articles._body: The Jacksonville Jaguars defeated the Baltimore Ravens 33-10 on Thursday night, extending the Ravens’ losing streak to four games . The Ravens were without quarterback Lamar Jackson, who had injured his right throwing thumb in a collision against the Buffalo Bills. Jackson was making a return from a Grade 1 high ankle sprain that he suffered in Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans, and may now be out for the season. Asked about his status, head coach Jesse Minter refused to comment , per a post on X by Luke Jones. “I’m not going to speak on that,” he said. The loss dropped the Ravens to 4-5, while Jacksonville improved to 6-2 with its fifth victory in six games. Jackson suffered the thumb injury on his first offensive snap against the Bills when he collided with rusher Greg Rousseau while attempting a pass to Zay Flowers. The Ravens lost that game 36-10, and Minter had previously confirmed that Jackson would undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve. Jackson had completed 70.8% of his passes for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception across his first four appearances, while adding 144 rushing yards and another touchdown. His absence has exposed Baltimore’s lack of depth at quarterback, particularly after Tyler Huntley also suffered a toe injury. Regardless, Trevor Lawrence completed 16 of 26 passes for 242 yards and a touchdown. Jakobi Meyers recorded four receptions for 65 yards, Parker Washington had two catches for 61 yards and a 50-yard touchdown, while Nate Boerkircher added two receptions for 61 yards. For the Ravens, Joe Fagnano completed 10 of 18 passes for just 60 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions. Baltimore will now the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 10, while Jacksonville will travel to take on the Tennessee Titans next. articles.title: Robbie Avila set to play for Saint Louis in 2026-27 after receiving injunction
articles.summary: Saint Louis forward Robbie Avila will return for another year of college basketball after St. Louis City Circuit Court Judge Jason Sengheiser granted him a preliminary injunction Thursday. The ruling allows the Atlantic 10 Player of the Year to return for the 2026-27 season, giving the Billikens
articles._body: Saint Louis forward Robbie Avila will return for another year of college basketball after St. Louis City Circuit Court Judge Jason Sengheiser granted him a preliminary injunction Thursday. The ruling allows the Atlantic 10 Player of the Year to return for the 2026-27 season, giving the Billikens another reason for optimism ahead of their rivalry matchup against Missouri on Friday. As part of the decision, Sengheiser also authorized Saint Louis University to carry a 16th roster spot for Avila despite its existing 15-player limit. The arrangement will remain in place until a full trial takes place, which is not expected for several months. Consequently, Avila is expected to be available for the entire season and make his 2026-27 debut versus the Tigers. The eligibility dispute stems from the NCAA’s five-for-five framework, which allows athletes five seasons of competition within a five-year period. The eligibility clock begins when a player turns 19 or graduates from high school, whichever happens first. However, the policy was not designed to cover athletes from the 2022 high school class who had already exhausted their eligibility, prompting several players across different sports to pursue legal action. Avila is among those who have received favorable rulings. His case also involved his summer experience with the Los Angeles Lakers. The 23-year-old participated in the NBA Summer League and verbally agreed to an Exhibit 10 contract with the franchise, but never officially signed the agreement or secured a professional contract. Avila previously spent two seasons at Indiana State under Josh Schertz before following his coach to Saint Louis. He has started 132 of his 137 collegiate appearances, averaging 17.3 points per game during his junior campaign before recording 12.8 points in 2025-26. He also converted 41% of his three-point attempts while taking approximately 4.6 shots from beyond the arc per game last season. His return holds considerable value for the Billikens coming off a 29-6 campaign that included an Atlantic 10 regular-season championship. Saint Louis earned a No. 9 seed in the NCAA Tournament, defeated Georgia 102-77 in the opening round and subsequently lost to eventual national champion Michigan in the Round of 32. The win over the Bulldogs was the program’s first NCAA Tournament win since 2014. With Avila returning, the Billikens will have four starters and two additional rotation players from last season’s NCAA Tournament team available. He also joins Trey Green and Ishan Sharma as part of a group that combined for 233 three-pointers last season. However, uncertainty surrounding these eligibility decisions remains. Although judges have sided with athletes in most cases, potential NCAA appeals could change the situation, leaving players’ eligibility vulnerable to future rulings. articles.title: Why Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy can’t stop gushing over Emmett Johnson
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs superfan Eric Stonestreet already launched a Rookie of the Week campaign for Emmett Johnson after his monster performance against the Denver Broncos. Another Eric — Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy — is also a big fan of the rookie running back out of Nebr
articles._body: Kansas City Chiefs superfan Eric Stonestreet already launched a Rookie of the Week campaign for Emmett Johnson after his monster performance against the Denver Broncos. Another Eric — Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy — is also a big fan of the rookie running back out of Nebraska and he shared exactly why despite his dislike of Cornhuskers. “Emmett works. He does not take anything for granted. It ain’t by chance that he’s had success when called upon, because you talk about a kid that does not take anything for granted. He goes out there and he works — whatever you ask him to do, he’s gonna try to excel at it,” Bieniemy said of Johnson. Bieniemy added that Johnson has the “type of mental and physical attitude that you want from all your players,” which is high praise for a rookie entering a championship-winning organization. A fifth-round pick by the Chiefs this year, Johnson hasn’t had too many opportunities to feature in the Kansas City offense. But that changed against the Broncos, as he exploded for 128 yards on five catches with a 73-yard touchdown. It seems all of Johnson’s hard work behind the scenes has finally paid off, and he figures to get more touches moving forward. Despite the return of wide receiver Rashee Rice , the Chiefs desperately need an injection of energy to their offense, which has been sputtering during their two-game losing skid. Johnson will look to provide it once again as the Chiefs take on the struggling New York Jets in Week 9. articles.title: 49ers’ George Kittle pleads the 5th on Brandon Aiyuk’s expected return to facility
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is reportedly inching closer to making a return to the NFL, after last having played in October 2024. Aiyuk suffered a torn ACL, MCL and meniscus injuries in his right knee against the Kansas City Chiefs, and now plans to return to the 49ers’ traini
articles._body: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is reportedly inching closer to making a return to the NFL, after last having played in October 2024. Aiyuk suffered a torn ACL, MCL and meniscus injuries in his right knee against the Kansas City Chiefs, and now plans to return to the 49ers’ training facility. And well, tight end George Kittle hilariously declined to discuss Aiyuk’s potential return to the team, per a post on X by Grant Cohn. I asked George Kittle if he’s looking forward to seeing Brandon Aiyuk in the 49ers’ facility tomorrow. pic.twitter.com/r9dcci8iJs — Grant Cohn (@grantcohn) November 5, 2026 “Plead the fifth, yeah. You can ask John. Or Kyle. Don’t ask me. I’m a conspiracy guy,” he said. Kittle’s response came as Aiyuk’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, confirmed Wednesday that the 28-year-old had submitted the necessary paperwork to return and planned to report to the 49ers’ facility Friday afternoon. Rosenhaus said Aiyuk was healthy and ready to play, and San Francisco will now determine whether to reinstate Aiyuk. General Manager John Lynch describing the situation as fluid and confirmed that the organization is working with the NFL Management Council to find a path that works for both sides, per ESPN. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said he had mentally moved on from Aiyuk and did not expect an immediate resolution. Aiyuk missed the entire 2025 season during his recovery. His relationship with San Francisco deteriorated further after the organization voided approximately $27 million in guaranteed contract money in July 2025, citing his failure to complete required rehabilitation sessions. The 49ers subsequently placed him on the reserve/left squad list in December after he stopped reporting to the facility, and his failure to report for training camp in July resulted in his placement on the reserve/did not report list. His current designation means San Francisco is not paying him and he does not occupy a spot on the active roster. The 49ers have previously attempted to trade Aiyuk, and a release remains a likely outcome. articles.title: Ravens hit embarrassing new low in franchise history with blowout loss to Jaguars
articles.summary: Thursday was a day to forget for Baltimore Ravens fans, as the AFC North team suffered an embarrassing prime-time 33-10 loss at the hands of Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore. Moreover, the lopsided defeat had the Ravens hitting a new franchise low.
articles._body: Thursday was a day to forget for Baltimore Ravens fans, as the AFC North team suffered an embarrassing prime-time 33-10 loss at the hands of Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore. Moreover, the lopsided defeat had the Ravens hitting a new franchise low . “The struggles without Lamar Jackson have reached historic levels. The Ravens’ 33-10 loss to the Jaguars marks the first time in their 31-year history that they’ve lost three straight games by 20 or more points,” Jamison Hensley of ESPN shared via a social media post on X, formerly Twitter. Making his first NFL start, Ravens quarterback Joe Fagnano struggled mightily under center, which wasn’t exactly a surprise. He went 10-for-18 for 60 passing yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions. Fagnano was also sacked once. As a team, the Ravens coughed up just 227 total yards and turned the ball over three times, while going 4-for-14 on third downs. Baltimore’s loss looked even worse than it appeared on paper. If not for a 65-yard touchdown run by Justice Hill amid a fourth-quarter blowout, the Ravens would have lost by an even wider margin. At that point, the only mystery left was the final score. The Ravens drop below .500 with a 4-5 record following the loss to the Jaguars. It’s still not too late for Baltimore to turn things around despite a four-game losing skid, and the Ravens will look to end their slump, potentially with Jacoby Brissett running the show from under center as early as Week 10’s home game against the Los Angeles Chargers. New head coach Jamahl Mosley appears to have stumbled upon a formula that works, balancing out a roster filled with talent but just cou
articles._body: The New Orleans Pelicans have rebounded from a poor start to the 2026-27 season, as they have now won four consecutive games to claw back to the .500 mark (4-4). New head coach Jamahl Mosley appears to have stumbled upon a formula that works, balancing out a roster filled with talent but just couldn’t seem to put it all together. With the Pelicans being better than expected in the early goings of this new campaign, perhaps they would be inclined to pull off a consolidation trade to try and upgrade the roster. One potential target that has come up for New Orleans is Sacramento Kings center Domantas Sabonis, who should be available on the trade market yet again with Sacramento headed for yet another losing season. “The Pelicans, for example, they have the salaries and type of players that the Kings would want where you could give up a Jordan Poole, a $34 million expiring salary. Maybe you can give up a future first-round pick and unload someone else. Maybe it’s a three-way or a four-way deal where you can give up Dejounte Murray in that case,” Siegel said on the latest episode of the Clutch Scoops show. “There’s a lot of room for the Pelicans here to either go after Sabonis or another big man on the market.” Latest trade rumors/intel: Warriors, Thunder | Clutch Scoops with @TomerAzarly & @BrettSiegelNBA https://t.co/vjgWFuHgEd — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 5, 2026 It’s not quite clear though, from a basketball perspective, as to why the Pelicans would trade for Sabonis. Zion Williamson remains entrenched as the starter at the four, and New Orleans needs size and rim protection at the five. This explains why New Orleans went with Yves Missi as their starting center to begin the campaign, and they’ve now called upon Karlo Matkovic, a floor-spacing shot-blocker, to start with Missi out injured. Sabonis’ presence could also stunt the development of Derik Queen, the man the Pelicans traded a valuable first-round pick for to get in the 2025 NBA Draft. Suffice to say, the Pelicans might be better off looking elsewhere if they were to pull off a trade — perhaps involving Murray, so that they could fully turn over the point guard position to Jeremiah Fears . articles.summary: Angel Reese’s former outfit, the No. 9 LSU women’s basketball team, recorded a program-record 131-22 victory over Texas Southern on Thursday, winning by 109 points. The win meant that LSU broke the record for the largest margin of victory in the history of the program for a second tim
articles._body: Angel Reese’s former outfit, the No. 9 LSU women’s basketball team , recorded a program-record 131-22 victory over Texas Southern on Thursday, winning by 109 points. The win meant that LSU broke the record for the largest margin of victory in the history of the program for a second time running , after beating Southeastern Louisiana 129-35 on Monday, per a post on X by ClutchPoints. The Tigers improved to 2-0 and outscored Texas Southern 106-9 over the final three quarters after taking a 25-13 lead into the second period. The defining stretch was a 40-0 second-quarter run during which LSU forced nine turnovers, held Texas Southern without a field goal on 13 attempts and shot 15-of-20 from the floor, including 5-of-6 from three-point range. Texas Southern went without a point after a three-pointer with 24 seconds remaining in the first quarter until Jayla Cornelius connected from beyond the arc at the 6:15 mark of the third. LSU forced 38 turnovers, converting them to a whopping 55-0 advantage on points, as a total of seven players scored in double digits. LSU were led by Anna Minaeva’s game-high 21 points, as she also recorded seven rebounds and three assists. Mikaylah Williams contributed 20 points, six rebounds and five assists, while Jada Williams finished with 18 points, seven assists and two steals. Williams scored 16 of her 18 points in the second quarter after going scoreless in the first half. ZaKiyah Johnson added 17 points and eight rebounds, while Grace Knox and MiLaysia Fulwiley each scored 15. Fulwiley also recorded six assists, four blocks and five steals, as Lola Lampley was the seventh LSU player to reach double figures with 10 points. LSU’s next scheduled opponent is McNeese State, with the Tigers set to host the team in their next game, while Texas Southern is scheduled to travel to Rice. articles.title: The 1 trade Bengals must make in final week before 2026 NFL trade deadline
articles.summary: Do the Cincinnati Bengals have one more trade in them this season? They’ve already made one of the biggest trades this season by acquiring ex-New York Giants defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence during the 2026 NFL Draft. Despite that blockbuster move, though, Cincinnati isn’t quite satis
articles._body: Do the Cincinnati Bengals have one more trade in them this season ? They’ve already made one of the biggest trades this season by acquiring ex-New York Giants defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence during the 2026 NFL Draft. Despite that blockbuster move, though, Cincinnati isn’t quite satisfied with where their team currently stands amongst the contenders in the AFC. Because of that, the Bengals are involved in some trade rumors as the trade deadline approaches. There are plenty of trades that Cincinnati can make to bolster their roster. Let’s look at the move that this team should make. Bengals must trade for Eagles’ Zack Baun at NFL trade deadline Kyle Ross-Imagn Images The Bengals traded for Lawrence, yes, but it was clear that the defense still had a ton of weaknesses. In particular, their linebacker group was a major question mark coming into the season. Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr. have both played better this season, but it’s still painfully clear that both linebackers are outmatched against their opponents. Opposing offenses have feasted in the short and intermediate areas of the field due to the duo’s struggles in coverage. That’s the reason why Bengals fans were clamoring for the team to sign or trade for a linebacker during the offseason. Popular choices at the time include Dolphins LB Jordyn Brooks and now-Washington Commanders LB Leo Chenal. However, another more intriguing option has emerged this season as a potential trade target: Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Zack Baun. One of the best linebackers in the league, Baun’s availability is tied heavily to the Eagles’ fate this season. With Jalen Hurts out for the year due to his deep vein thrombosis, Philadelphia has gone from contenders to potential sellers at the trade deadline. Tanner McKee has done nothing to inspire confidence in a playoff run, and they’re now taking a look at prospect Joe Milton to lead them the rest of the day. Because of that and the long-term implications of Hurts’ DVT diagnosis, many are wondering if Philadelphia might decide to enter a rebuild. Baun is one of the players who will likely fetch good value at the trade deadline. The Eagles linebacker started his career as an edge rusher, but he has made the transition to a coverage linebacker with the Eagles. Baun is one of the best coverage linebackers in the league, able to cover both tight ends and slot receivers in space. He was part of the 2024 Eagles team that won the Super Bowl, so he also brings championship pedigree to a Bengals team that has high aspirations this season. Cincinnati’s linebackers are playing better than last year, but last year is an admittedly low standard that they have barely cleared this season. Knight Jr. has been great against the run this season, but he’s one of the worst linebackers in coverage this year. Carter has been great for the most part too, but he’s still prone to lapses in coverage and takes bad angles at times. Having Baun, a bona fide veteran, as one of their linebackers would be greatly helpful to this team moving forward. articles.title: Why Grizzlies’ Isaiah Stewart has ‘no regrets’ on wild LeBron James altercation
articles.summary: Isaiah Stewart has built a reputation as one of the NBA’s most fiery players, and the Memphis Grizzlies big man is not about to apologize for it. Looking back on his infamous altercation with LeBron James and other run-ins, Stewart made it clear he does not regret a thing. In an interview with An
articles._body: Isaiah Stewart has built a reputation as one of the NBA’s most fiery players, and the Memphis Grizzlies big man is not about to apologize for it. Looking back on his infamous altercation with LeBron James and other run-ins, Stewart made it clear he does not regret a thing. In an interview with Andscape, Stewart was asked whether he had any regrets about those incidents or if it was simply the emotion of the moment. “I don’t have no regrets. You know, I feel like there’s lessons out of everything. You know, even going back to that first incident, you know, Charlotte, like I don’t have no regrets and I don’t care what people may perceive me as,” Stewart said. “I come to play basketball and I play the game a certain way. And it has been times where, you know, I thought back and say, hey, I shouldn’t have done that.” Isaiah Stewart says he has no regrets about trying to fight LeBron James (Via @andscape / h/t @0xBassey ) pic.twitter.com/WrXxsGevz9 — NBACentral (@TheDunkCentral) November 5, 2026 Stewart also called out opponents he believes try to bait him into losing his cool. “And I feel like teams having their game plan of, hey, let’s do something to trip him off, to get him out the game. For me, it’s hard to respect you as a man if that’s your game plan,” he said. The LeBron incident remains the most memorable of Stewart’s career. Back in November 2021, James struck Stewart in the face with an elbow while the two were battling for position during a free throw, leaving the then-Detroit Pistons big man bloodied. An enraged Stewart repeatedly charged after James and had to be held back. James was ejected and later suspended one game, while Stewart received a two-game suspension. His most recent suspension came in February 2026, when Stewart left the bench to join a fight between the Pistons and the Charlotte Hornets . The NBA handed him a seven-game ban, citing his “repeated history of unsportsmanlike acts.” It was his fourth suspension for fighting. A few months later, Detroit traded Stewart to the Grizzlies for three future second-round picks during the 2026 NBA Draf t, ending his six-season run with the Pistons. Now 25 years old, Stewart is part of a Grizzlies team that is off to a 6-2 start. Based on his comments, he has no plans of changing the way he plays anytime soon. Per Adam Schefter of ESPN, Hamilton will no
articles._body: The Baltimore Ravens just can’t catch a break with all the injuries . Already down to their third-string quarterback, the Ravens have now lost safety Kyle Hamilton for the rest of their Thursday Night Football game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Per Adam Schefter of ESPN, Hamilton will not return after suffering a hip injury . He had already been dealing with a knee injury that kept him out of practice the previous week . The Ravens look on course to lose their fourth game in a row. As of this writing, they are down 33-10 to the Jaguars in the fourth quarter. A first-round pick by the Ravens in 2022, Hamilton came into Thursday night as the team’s second-leading tackler behind Roquan Smith with 57 tackles in eight games. He also has one interception and a forced fumble. Hamilton’s injury adds to the Ravens’ already lengthy injury list in the secondary. Cornerback Nate Wiggins was listed as inactive shortly before the Jags game due to illness . Safety Jaylinn Hawkins was also listed as out. It remains to be seen whether this latest injury will keep Hamilton out for their next game against the Los Angeles Chargers. But they will have a lengthy 11-day break before that game, which should give him time to recover. But if it is in any way serious, the Ravens are unlikely to risk sending him out amid his other injury concerns. With the Ravens’ season increasingly looking lost amid their quarterback injuries, they will be wise to exercise caution moving forward. Brandon Aiyuk’s agent confirms plan for return to 49ers facility
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is set to return to the team’s facility on Friday after spending more than a year away from the organization. His new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, confirmed to ESPN’s Adam Schefter in a message Thursday that he and Aiyuk plan to report at 3 p.
articles._body: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is set to return to the team’s facility on Friday after spending more than a year away from the organization. His new agent, Drew Rosenhaus , confirmed to ESPN’s Adam Schefter in a message Thursday that he and Aiyuk plan to report at 3 p.m. to discuss the 28-year-old’s situation with the franchise. “We will be there tomorrow at 3pm to meet with the team at the facility,” Rosenhaus texted. “We will put our best foot forward and go from there.” Aiyuk has already submitted the necessary paperwork to seek reinstatement to the NFL. Reporting to the facility is required for him to be removed from the reserve/left squad list. However, Aiyuk’s anticipated return comes with several complications. He could reportedly owe the 49ers approximately $13 million in forfeited bonuses. The NFL Management Council and NFL Players Association are involved in efforts to settle the financial dispute, which may involve an agreement between the parties or proceed to arbitration. Aiyuk has not appeared in an NFL game since October 2024, when he suffered season-ending ACL and MCL injuries during a Week 7 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. His absence continued into the 2025 season, while his relationship with San Francisco deteriorated. The 49ers voided his guaranteed money for 2026 after reportedly citing his failure to attend meetings and participate in other team activities. Aiyuk subsequently claimed that his 2027 guarantees had also been voided. He also expressed his frustration with the organization through multiple social media posts and repeatedly sought his release. Head coach Kyle Shanahan has made little effort to hide his stance on the situation. He said on Wednesday that he had mentally moved on from Aiyuk and reiterated Thursday that he could not think of anything the receiver could do to change that position. Shanahan also acknowledged that he had no meeting scheduled with Aiyuk on Friday. General manager John Lynch, meanwhile, said that everything remained possible while acknowledging the team’s discussions with the NFL. San Francisco has several potential options, including bringing Aiyuk back, releasing him or exploring a trade. The financial implications of a potential release also remain considerable. The 49ers have paid Aiyuk $48.1 million for just seven games since signing his contract extension in August 2024. Releasing him would reportedly create $12.4 million in dead-cap charges for 2026 and another $19.3 million in 2027. articles._body: It’s no secret that the Sacramento Kings have been looking to trade away Domantas Sabonis to lean further into their ongoing rebuild. And with the Kings having started the season with just one win in eight games, trade talks involving the Lithuanian big man are only going to heat up the deeper we progress into the new campaign. To that end, ClutchPoints NBA insider Brett Siegel named the Toronto Raptors and Charlotte Hornets as prime trade destinations for Sabonis. “Two teams that looked to trade for him last year and had those trade conversations were the Toronto Raptors and the Charlotte Hornets,” Siegel said on the latest Clutch Scoops show. “The interest has not gone away. I can speak to that with certainty here. There’s been no new dialogue to report here but those are two teams that we’re keeping an eye on.” (Fast forward to around the 33:30 mark.) Latest trade rumors/intel: Warriors, Thunder | Clutch Scoops with @TomerAzarly & @BrettSiegelNBA https://t.co/vjgWFuHgEd — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 5, 2026 Siegel then clarified why the Raptors or Hornets weren’t able to trade for Sabonis last season. The Kings did not want to take on Jakob Poeltl’s contract and could not find a third team to absorb the three years and $84 million left on his deal. Meanwhile, the Kings were demanding too much out of the Hornets (lottery picks during the 2026 NBA Draft) and Charlotte wasn’t budging. But at this point, perhaps the Raptors would be more inclined to trade for Sabonis. Poeltl has struggled immensely to begin the 2026-27 season, and Collin Murray-Boyles hasn’t yet solidified his place in the starting lineup. Toronto also has the defenders to help cover for Sabonis’ weaknesses on that end, and with the arrival of Kawhi Leonard, they are in win-now mode, which could nudge them towards a more aggressive approach on the trade market. Maybe the Hornets get desperate as well considering that their offense is currently the worst in the NBA. They need a new offensive hub following the departure of LaMelo Ball and amid the injury to Kon Knueppel, and if they keep losing, maybe they swing a trade for the Kings center. KNBR captured the moment during pregame warmups, as Curry and Thompson met at midcourt for a quick chat. With fans already filing into the stands, the two shared a few words before going back to their respective sides of the floor. Steph Curry and Klay Thompson having a quick chat at midcourt before Warriors/Heat tonight (via @KNBR ) pic.twitter.com/eJY8yXXWgz — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 6, 2026 It was a familiar sight for Warriors fans, who watched the Splash Brothers win four NBA championships together . The duo spent 13 seasons as teammates in Golden State before Thompson left for the Dallas Mavericks in 2024. After two seasons in Dallas, Thompson reached a buyout agreement with the Mavericks in August and signed a two-year deal with the Heat . Warriors head coach Steve Kerr admitted it still feels odd to see Thompson, along with Andrew Wiggins, in another uniform. “Those first couple times are really bizarre, and then you get used to it. And it’s a reminder that most of us in the NBA end up with multiple teams. It’s so rare to play with one team,” Kerr said. “You end up competing against friends and sometimes even family.” “But it’ll be great to see both guys, two just incredible contributors to the Warriors’ championships,” Kerr added. “Both Klay and Wiggins are wonderful human beings and great teammates, and it’ll be great.” Both Curry and Thompson enter the matchup in good form. Thompson is coming off a 30-point night in Miami’s 117-116 overtime win over the LA Clippers on Wednesday, knocking down eight 3-pointers and hitting the go-ahead triple with one second left in the extra period. It was his first 30-point game since April 2024, when he was still with the Warriors. Curry, meanwhile, dropped 34 points in Golden State’s 116-113 win over the Phoenix Suns on Monday. The Warriors have won five straight games and sit at 5-3 on the season, while the Heat are 3-5 and playing on the second night of a back-to-back. Thursday will mark Thompson’s first game at Chase Center as a member of the Heat, and the pregame moment showed that the bond between the Splash Brothers remains as strong as ever. In doing so, he joined an exclusive list of undrafted rookies to do so on short res
articles._body: It’s been a whirlwind last few days for Joe Fagnano. He has gone from undrafted third-stringer to the Baltimore Ravens’ starting quarterback against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday Night Football. In doing so, he joined an exclusive list of undrafted rookies to do so on short rest. As it turns out, though, Fagnano has been getting himself ready for just this moment, with a lot of help from his wife . As mentioned during the telecast on NFL on Prime, Fagnano’s wife would go over plays with him at home and test him on different calls to keep him ready in the off chance he was called upon to play. Joe Fagnano's wife would go through plays with him to make sure he was ready to go if his name ever got called #TNFonPrime pic.twitter.com/ONUlslPOeW — NFL on Prime Video (@NFLonPrime) November 6, 2026 As fate would have it, with both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley knocked out with injuries, that’s exactly what has happened to Fagnano. After coming on against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, he’s had just a few days to prepare for the first start of his career on Thursday night. In fairness to the undrafted rookie, he has acquitted himself as well as could be expected through one half. He’s completed seven of his 11 pass attempts for 30 yards. He also led the Ravens to a field goal in his opening drive. However, the Ravens have still found themselves down a 17-3 hole to the Jaguars at halftime. Amid all the struggles the Ravens offense has had in the second half, even with Tyler Huntley at quarterback, Fagnano faces an uphill battle to overcome such a big deficit in his first career start. articles._body: Justin Jefferson is not happy with how the Minnesota Vikings offense is being inconsistent despite a hot start to the 2026 NFL season. Jefferson is halfway through the seventh season of his career with the Vikings. He shines as one of the best receivers in the league, often helping them be in the mix for playoff contention. Minnesota is enjoying an incredible start to the season. They were the last undefeated team standing before losing to the Detroit Lions in Week 8. He spoke with media on Thursday, wanting to see the offense take a big step in the right direction and prevent a significant slide in the second half of the campaign. “It was wanting to win,” Jefferson said, via ESPN. “And I felt like we had plenty of opportunities to win that game and we only hurt ourselves in multiple ways. It’s just wanting better from the whole entire offense especially. And I feel like the potential and the guys that we have in that room is something very, very special. I feel like we’re wasting that if not going out there executing the plays that we have called and just not living to that standard that we feel like we live up to every single day.” What lies ahead for Justin Jefferson, Vikings Justin Jefferson knows he is very capable of booming with big performances. The Vikings just need to give him more attention so the offense can be more explosive. Minnesota has a 6-1 record this season, sitting at the top spot of the NFC North Division standings. They are above the Chicago Bears and the Detroit Lions at the moment. In terms of the conference standings, they are second place. They lead over the New York Giants and the Carolina Panthers while being under the San Francisco 49ers. The Vikings will continue preparations for their upcoming matchup this weekend, being at home. articles.title: Seahawks G Quenton Nelson downgraded on injury report with knee issue before Cardinals game
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks could be dealing with another offensive line concern ahead of their Week 9 NFC West matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, as newly acquired guard Quenton Nelson was downgraded on Thursday’s injury report because of a knee issue. Nelson was a limited participant during
articles._body: The Seattle Seahawks could be dealing with another offensive line concern ahead of their Week 9 NFC West matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, as newly acquired guard Quenton Nelson was downgraded on Thursday’s injury report because of a knee issue. Nelson was a limited participant during Wednesday’s practice but did not take part in the following day’s session. His absence adds to Seattle’s growing list of injury concerns, with nine players missing practice on Thursday. The six starters who sat out included quarterback Sam Darnold, wide receiver Rashid Shaheed, left tackle Charles Cross, Nelson, defensive tackle Leonard Williams and linebacker Derick Hall. Moreover, edge rushers Uchenna Nwosu and Connor O’Toole, along with nose tackle Brandon Pili, also did not practice. Meanwhile, linebacker Ernest Jones IV and quarterback Drew Lock were limited, while several other players made progress. Most prominently, right guard Anthony Bradford was upgraded to full participation after being limited Wednesday. If Nelson cannot suit up on Sunday, Bradford could return to his usual starting position on the right side, allowing rookie Grey Zabel to move back to left guard. Zabel had switched to the right side after the Seahawks traded for Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts on October 27. The adjustment came with challenges during Monday night’s 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears. Zabel allowed one pressure, which resulted in a sack by Jeffery Simmons, while Nelson surrendered just one hurry across 39 pass-blocking snaps. Nelson also recorded a false start during the contest. Seattle will hope to have Nelson available as the team searches for an antidote to its flagging offensive potency. The Seahawks have averaged 3.9 yards per rushing attempt through eight games, ranking 24th in the NFL. Their minus-50.33 expected points added on rushing plays is the worst mark in the league. Seattle enters the Week 9 clash at 4-4. The game also carries division implications, as the loser could drop to the bottom of the standings if the Los Angeles Rams take down the Washington Commanders. articles._body: Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry keeps writing himself into the record books . Last week, he joined greats Marshall Faulk and Marcus Allen in an exclusive rushing touchdown club. In doing so, he tied Faulk for seventh on the list of most touchdowns in NFL history. This week, it’s LaDainian Tomlinson’s turn to be overtaken by Henry. As Jeff Zrebiec pointed out on X, formerly Twitter, the Ravens running back leapfrogged his childhood idol to take seventh spot on the all-time rushing yards list. At age 32, Henry remains highly productive for the Ravens. Heading into Thursday night, he had already racked up 632 yards with eight touchdowns in eight games. However, he is currently averaging just 4.0 yards per carry, which is a career-low. After two highly disappointing games in the losses to the Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals, he did bounce back against the Bills. He finished with 53 yards on 11 carries with a touchdown, his first since Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans. Henry has previously shared his admiration for Tomlinson growing up, so the fact that he has now surpassed his idol will likely mean a lot to him. With LT overtaken, Curtis Martin is next up for Henry to surpass. After that, he will need to overtake Adrian Peterson to break into the top five all-time. However, it remains to be seen whether Henry will achieve those milestones as a member of the Ravens, as he has sprung up in trade rumors amid their poor season . But wherever he might end up, he stands a decent chance of climbing even higher up the all-time list. articles._body: The Boston Red Sox have quite a bit of work to do in the offseason. Most of the Red Sox issues had to do with a lack of hitting, particularly in the final month of the regular season and in the playoffs. Sonny Gray didn’t have great things to say about the Red Sox organization at the end of the season. WEEI Red Sox Insider Rob Bradford weighs in on whether he may be back with the team next year. @KenLairdWEEI @teddyjradio @heyrichhey pic.twitter.com/wnvVdjz7cD — Rich and Ken with Ted Johnson (@richkented) November 5, 2026 However, they may need to bring in starting pitching if they can’t re-sign ace pitcher Sonny Gray. After Garrett Crochet went down with an injury that kept him out from April until he was able to pitch in relief in the playoffs, Gray simply took over as the team’s best starting pitcher. He had an 18-5 record along with a 2.72 earned run average. Gray made 29 starts for the Red Sox and he pitched 169.0 innings. Unlike most of the top pitchers in the game, Gray is not a fireballer who depends on a 100-MPH fastball to blow hitters away. Instead, he is an old-school pitcher who induces weak contact and lets his fielders do the job. He regularly lives on the corners or forces hitters to swing at pitches out of the strike zone. Gray is a free agent and he will have the opportunity to get offers from teams that value his services. Red Sox insider Rob Bradford believes the Red Sox want Gray back, but it may be at their price . If Gray wants more, the Red Sox may be willing to let him move on. That would seem to be a foolish move. It appears that Gray, Payton Tolle and Ranger Suarez clearly fill important roles for the Red Sox starting staff and the belief is that Crochet will come back healthy next year. That would give the Red Sox four solid starters. However, if Gray leaves, they would need a new starter and perhaps one who can take over as an ace. articles._body: Notre Dame football head coach Marcus Freeman knows Malachi Toney is on Miami’s injury list . Yet Freeman finds himself still believing Toney will suit up. Freeman explained the reasoning via Pete Sampson of The Athletic Thursday. “We’ll see if he plays or not. We have to make sure we have a plan if he plays. If he doesn’t, we’ll adjust,” Freeman said. Toney reportedly underwent tightrope surgery, which is common for players dealing with a sprain. Those type of injuries need up to four weeks at the least to heal. Miami rolled out a vision involving holding off Toney until the College Football Playoffs to play. Still, Freeman believes that Miami is more than the star wideout. “They’ve got a long list of guys that they can put on the field to be the 11th player. It’s not always the position as much as it is the player. There’s players all over,” Freeman added to reporters. “There’s great running backs, there’s good tight ends, there’s good young wide receivers who can step up. Whatever it is their plan will be on Saturday, we have to be ready to adjust.” Freeman will need to get his defense to prepare for another Miami star too in quarterback Darian Mensah. He’s bringing 25 touchdowns in tow with only one interception. And Mensah’s next best target in the absence of Toney is Cooper Barkate, who was Mensah’s top wideout at Duke last season. articles._body: While the Dallas Cowboys sort through some injuries , it seems like Dak Prescott is concerned about the team’s identity. But one thing Prescott seems sure about is George Pickens, as he defended the receiver amid trade rumors, according to a post on X by Jon Machota. “Dak Prescott, when asked about those who think the Cowboys should trade George Pickens: ‘People say a lot of things I don’t believe, so I’m not listening to that one, either. George is a great teammate. And I say that in the sense of, he’s gonna do whatever is asked, he’s gonna do whatever is called. If it’s to go block, if it’s to just go run a guy off, he’s gonna do that. He believes in just doing the right thing, and the ball will come his way at times. And so, that’s not on George.’ ” Will WR George Pickens get traded by Cowboys? If you listen to some observers, Pickens will be in Dallas for quite a while , according to the House of Haymaker podcast via Heavy.com. Fort Worth Star-Telegram beat writer Nick Harris said he thinks the Cowboys will pony up the cash to sign both Pickens and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. “I think it will be a long-term extension (for Pickens),” Harris said. “And Porter gets the tag. I think there’s already kind of been foundations to that conversation being had with Porter. Whether Porter knows it or not, I think the foundations of that conversation have already started.” Another player on Pickens’ side is receiver CeeDee Lamb, according to a post on X by Calvin Watkins. “CeeDee Lamb on the fan base wanting George Pickens traded: ‘I don’t know why that’s the thing, but come on, man. articles._body: The Baltimore Ravens are not just integrating a new quarterback during Thursday night’s home matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars. They are also trying out a new kicker. With Tyler Loop now on injured reserve , head coach Jesse Minter is trusting Jake Moody to show off his big leg. The former third-round draft pick and All-American with Michigan is competing in his first NFL game since last January. He is maximizing this opportunity, at least so far. Moody put the Ravens on the scoreboard via a 53-yard field goal midway through the first quarter. The 26-year-old has eaten a ton of humble pie over the last few seasons, but he is ready to start anew in Charm City. Given the limitations that undrafted third-string QB Joe Fagnano is already facing in this prime-time AFC showdown, Moody instantly becomes one of Baltimore’s most important weapons. Jake Moody NAILS the 53-yard field goal in his first game as a Raven Jaguars lead is now 7-3 early in the 1st quarter. pic.twitter.com/RPFB8lkyyn — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 6, 2026 The Ravens have future Hall of Fame running back Derrick Henry and dynamic wide receiver Zay Flowers at their disposal, but without Lamar Jackson, they are only so effective. Unless Fagnano stuns the world, long field goals may have to be the norm. Even when Jacoby Brissett takes snaps under center , manufacturing offense will not come easy. The reemerging Jake Moody must stay sharp. The two-time Big Ten Kicker of the Year, who joined Baltimore’s practice squad at the end of August, is hoping to leave his San Francisco scuffles in the past. Despite performing competently on both the Chicago Bears and Washington Commanders, Moody has struggled to inspire the level of faith that he did upon entering the league in 2023. Perhaps that will soon change. The 53-yard FG remains the Ravens’ only source of points at time of print.
