articles._body: Rob Gronkowski and Julian Edelman are showcasing a new talent that Tom Brady couldn’t help but jokingly throw a jab at. It’s been years since Brady, Gronkowski, and Edelman walked out onto a field together, but their post-career choices have them right back at their old antics. In an ad to promote their new Fox Sports digital series “The Gronk & Jules Show,” the former tight end and wide receiver began singing their new track, “Talkin’ Football” — and it’s everything you think a Gronk and Edelman song would sound like. In the song, Edelman and Gronkowski sing about wanting careers talking about football. Brady reposted the video and threw some shade their way, writing, “They used to walk out to practice like this.. same turtlenecks and everything.” They used to walk out to practice like this.. same turtlenecks and everything https://t.co/erDedrDGPk — Tom Brady (@TomBrady) November 5, 2026 Despite the intention being a funny song, the retired NFL players’ track sounded did hit some notes during their promo. “Me and Gronk have been keeping our singing talent a secret for so many years, so getting a real chance to showcase that and doing it about a topic we love so much was really just a lot of fun,” Edelman said in a statement per Variety. Senior VP of on-air promotions for Fox Sports, Bill Battin, commented on the NFL stars linking up for the promo sharing that, “we had a ton of fun on this one.” “Gronk and Jules made the song their own, bringing their personalities to a great concept from Clay and the team at The San Clemente Experiment,” Battin added. The twice-weekly digital series will have the Super Bowl champions discuss all things football. “On Mondays, Gronkowski and Edelman break down the weekend’s biggest games, reacting to on-field action versus what the box score says. On Thursdays, Edelman sits down with a rotating cast of players, coaches and insiders for deeper conversations,” the logline reads. Gronkowski, Edelman, and Brady won three Super Bowls together when they were teammates on the New England Patriots. They have since all scored jobs with Fox Sports with Gronkowski being a full-time studio analyst on FOX NFL Sunday, Edelman a studio analyst for FOX NFL Kickoff, and Brady the lead NFL color commentator who calls games calling games alongside play-by-play announcer Kevin Burkhardt. articles._body: Kiah Stokes made sure the Golden State Valkyries’ championship parade came with a little extra message for ESPN , and the veteran center is now opening up about what was behind it. Stokes turned heads at Wednesday’s parade by wearing a T-shirt featuring a printout of ESPN’s analytics, which had not exactly been kind to Golden State’s title chances during the season. Appearing on “In Case You Missed It with Khristina Williams,” Stokes explained exactly where the idea came from. “I just remember during the season, right before All-Star, ESPN released whatever that was, and we were second at the time in the standings. And I was like, okay, we’re second, but like, you can’t even give us any type of shot to win a championship,” Stokes said. “So I just felt like a type of way. So at the time, I took a screenshot. You never know, you may or may not need it, depending on how the season ends up.” Four-time WNBA champion Kiah Stokes ( @kstokes41 ) breaks down the story behind her championship parade t-shirt. pic.twitter.com/9dJSm8Ujip — In Case You Missed It with Khristina Williams (@ICYMIwithKW) November 6, 2026 “And then when we won, I was like, yeah, let me just throw it on the shirt. Talk a little mess here and there, but I just, I gotta be a little bit petty,” she added. Williams compared the move to A’ja Wilson’s famous parade shirt from 2023, when the Las Vegas Aces star trolled MVP voters by wearing a shirt that displayed her voting numbers. Stokes, who was Wilson’s teammate in Las Vegas, admitted she picked up some of that pettiness during her time with the Aces. ESPN, for its part, took the jab in stride. The network responded with a new chart showing the Valkyries at 100% odds, while also noting that it had given Golden State the top title odds as of Aug. 10. Stokes certainly earned the right to have some fun. The Valkyries center was a defensive force throughout the WNBA Finals, setting a record for the most blocks in a single Finals series . She also tied Lisa Leslie for the longest streak of games with three or more blocks in a single postseason. Golden State went on to beat the Atlanta Dream in seven games to claim the first championship in franchise history, in just its second season. For Stokes, it marked her fourth WNBA title, after winning three with the Aces. articles.title: Cloudflare’s appeal won’t fix what’s broken in Delaware’s Chancery Court
articles.summary: A vice chancellor, Travis Laster, sent his own ruling to the state Supreme Court. Boards shouldn’t read that as reassurance.
articles._body: The morning after we wrote in Fortune about a controversial Chancery Court decision involving Cloudflare, Vice Chancellor J. Travis Laster moved with uncommon speed to certify an interlocutory appeal of his ruling to the Delaware Supreme Court. Corporate boards might read that as a sign the system is correcting itself. They shouldn’t, at least not yet. The appeal was necessary because Laster used an unusually expansive reading of “good faith” to enjoin the Cloudflare board’s decision about its capital structure. A vague standard With corporate anchoring fees rivaling personal income taxes as Delaware’s primary source of revenue, Delaware’s wise leaders, including its governor and its legislature, saw this exodus coming, and tried to stem its root cause. In March 2025, Delaware passed Senate Bill 21 (SB 21) , the most significant rewrite of its corporate code in a generation, to stop the flow of companies out of the state. SB 21 was generally recognized to have been a direct response to a run of activist rulings from the Court of Chancery, which were widely seen as blatant judicial overreach. The spirit of SB 21 is simple: if a board routes a possibly “conflicted” deal through a committee of independent directors with real power to reject it, the deal is considered “kosher.” This means no injunctions, no damages, no trial. Indeed, Laster’s 142-page opinion concedes the legitimacy of SB 21 and its applicability to this case. He held the directors were independent. He held they were not negligent. He wrote that their process showed “ all the outward signs of diligent and careful effort .” By his own account, virtually every requirement the legislature wrote was met by the Cloudflare board. He enjoined the transaction anyway, on a novel basis. SB 21 does require that the committee act “in good faith,” but Laster’s route was to re-define what good faith entails – even though the legislative intent of SB 21 and the surrounding debate in the legislature, clearly shows that the Delaware legislature intended SB 21 to be more deferential to independent boards, not less. The term “good faith” was not a third level of diligence beyond the duty of care and duty of loyalty, but merely presumed to be the spirit of board actions. Before this, good faith had been previously generally assumed, in deference to independent boards, with nary any heightened review threshold, much less any invocation to enjoin a transaction. Instead, he pointed in part to the fact that the board used Signal to communicate about sensitive strategic information they presumably did not want competitors obtaining, irrespective of litigation, and to a CEO who was known to have a hot temper, even though the temperament of the entrepreneur is irrelevant to good faith and typical of creative businesses in technology, media, fashion and the like. From those disconnected scraps, the court inferred that the committee was serving the founders rather than bargaining against them, or what Laster, borrowing from the 2011 Southern Peru case, called “a controlled mindset”, as proof of possible lack of good faith by the committee. In analyzing Laster’s novel interpretation of what “good faith” means, readers might ask whether Laster was merely applying the statute, SB 21, rather than inventing a new standard. But that flies in the face of the legislative history of SB 21, which clearly suggests the intent of the Delaware legislature was to try to drive greater predictability and greater deference to independent boards, rather than drive more elevated scrutiny of those same boards. Against that backdrop, Laster’s idiosyncratic, broader reading of ‘good faith’ substantively guts the protections SB21 was meant to provide. But even more importantly, and legally salient; Laster’s interpretation of ‘good faith’ is far from what “good faith” has always historically meant in Delaware, from a legal perspective. The existing Delaware definition of bad faith is grounded in scienter, the requirement of showing that individuals acted with knowledge and intent of wrongdoing, together with the requirement that each board member be assessed individually to determine whether a majority intentionally acted in bad faith. That is the Disney line of cases.  In 2006, the Delaware Supreme Court defined bad faith as “intentional dereliction of duty, a conscious disregard for one’s responsibilities,” and held that gross negligence, “without more, cannot constitute bad faith.” Stone v. Ritter that same year made good faith a “subsidiary element” of the duty of loyalty rather than a freestanding duty. And Lyondell in 2009 held that directors who merely “failed to do all that they should have” breached only their duty of care, while “only if they knowingly and completely failed to undertake their responsibilities” could they be found disloyal. Startlingly, Laster largely set aside that definition in practice. A board’s understandable use of Signal to communicate about sensitive strategic information, or a CEO known to have a hot temper, amounts to nothing even remotely resembling scienter, which is knowing or willful misconduct. The opinion likewise faults the committee for not obtaining a fairness opinion while conceding, in its own footnote, that “Delaware courts have stated that there is no duty to obtain a fairness opinion.” Under Lyondell , a process that could have been better is a question of care, not loyalty, and Laster found no failure of care. Most tellingly, he acknowledged that without what he called the defendants’ “credibility problems,” he “could have concluded” the safe harbor applied. In other words, the statute’s protection now turns on whether a trial judge likes the witnesses. If a board can be independent, informed, and diligent and still be found to have acted in bad faith, directors are left without a clear rule to follow. That uncertainty is exactly what is pushing companies to reincorporate elsewhere. A disputed record, headed to the Supreme

Ex-Angels GM joins Braves for 2027 season
articles.summary: The Atlanta Braves are continuing to reshape their front office ahead of the 2027 season, with Alex Anthopoulos reconnecting with executives who previously worked in the organization. Former Houston Astros general manager Dana Brown recently rejoined the Braves as a senior advisor to the amateur
articles._body: The Atlanta Braves are continuing to reshape their front office ahead of the 2027 season, with Alex Anthopoulos reconnecting with executives who previously worked in the organization. Former Houston Astros general manager Dana Brown recently rejoined the Braves as a senior advisor to the amateur scouting department. His addition brought a familiar evaluator back into the organization’s operation early in the offseason. Perry Minasian also has longstanding ties to Anthopoulos and Atlanta. He served as the Braves’ assistant general manager from 2017 through 2020, helping build the club into a perennial contender before leaving to run the Los Angeles Angels. That experience followed scouting work with the Texas Rangers and nine years with the Toronto Blue Jays. USA Today’s Bob Nightengale shared an update Thursday on X, formerly Twitter, addressing Minasian’s next step following his departure from the Angels. “Former Angels VP Perry Minasian now rejoins Atlanta front office staff” The move reunites Minasian with Anthopoulos for the 2027 season after six seasons overseeing the Angels’ baseball operations. Los Angeles relieved Minasian of his general manager duties on June 26 with the team at 34-48 and last in the American League West. The Angels named John Mozeliak interim general manager following the change. Minasian’s tenure began ahead of the 2021 season, but Los Angeles never finished with a winning record during his time leading the front office. His dismissal came a little over four months before Thursday’s report. Rumors earlier in the offseason suggested Anthopoulos could reunite with Minasian and Brown. Both executives have now returned to Atlanta after serving as general managers elsewhere. Brown’s advisory position centers on amateur scouting. Nightengale’s announcement confirms Minasian’s return but does not identify his job title, outline his responsibilities or specify how his duties will differ from those of his former colleague. articles.title: The Iran war has cost U.S. households nearly $2,000 each. New strikes could keep the bill climbing
articles.summary: Pentagon data puts U.S. war costs above $47 billion, and Moody’s estimates households have paid nearly $2,000 each. Oil’s post-election drop may not last.
articles._body: On Oct. 8, President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that “we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd.” On Nov. 2, the day before Americans voted, U.S. forces struck Iran’s Qeshm Island. U.S. officials told CNN the Qeshm attack was a defensive response to Iranian forces using surface-to-air missiles against U.S. assets. In a Fox News interview that aired that night, Trump suggested there had been no recent fighting. The Qeshm attack was not an isolated event. Officials told ABC News that limited “defensive strikes” had been carried out in recent weeks and not publicized to avoid signaling a return to major combat operations. The strikes are small next to earlier phases of the war. But they come at a fragile moment for energy markets, which had just priced in hopes of a diplomatic exit, and as the U.S. heads into heating season. Gilbert Metcalf, a visiting professor at the MIT Sloan School of Management and a former deputy assistant secretary for environment and energy at the U.S. Treasury Department, says the strikes raise the odds of the outcome markets fear most. “The risk to global oil markets and, by extension, the global economy as we head into winter is the potential for Iranian strikes against shipping in the Strait of Hormuz or against oil and gas infrastructure in the region,” Metcalf tells Fortune . “Continued strikes against Iran, albeit so-called ‘defensive strikes,’ only increase the likelihood of their undertaking those attacks.” Even restraint from Tehran may not help much. “Even if the Iranians hold back, any increased military activity in the region heightens the risk of retaliation, which adversely affects markets,” he says. “Oil prices will remain persistently high in the face of these risks, and this is particularly concerning as we move into winter and the need for oil and gas for home heating.” What the war has cost so far U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran that began Feb. 28 set off a regional war, according to the Congressional Research Service . Iran has retaliated against targets across the Middle East, including a pumping station on Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline , and has used attacks on commercial shipping to assert control over the Strait of Hormuz. The two sides agreed to a ceasefire in April and signed a memorandum of understanding on June 17. The agreement collapsed within weeks amid renewed fighting and formally expired in August. By September, the CRS described the conflict as a war of attrition. The price tag keeps rising. The U.S. military has spent more than $47 billion on the war, Reuters reported on Oct. 27, citing Pentagon data. That is up from the $37.5 billion Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth estimated in July, and more than $29 billion of it goes to replacing expended munitions. Households are paying, too. Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moody’s Analytics, estimates the war has cost the average U.S. household nearly $2,000, CNN reported . About $1,100 of that comes from higher energy and transportation costs, with higher interest rates and a share of military spending making up the rest. “Nationwide, that adds up to $265 billion,” Zandi wrote on X on Oct. 12. Much of the pain runs through the Strait of Hormuz, which carried about 20 million barrels of oil a day before the war. Qeshm Island, about 14 miles from the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas, is central to Iran’s ability to control traffic through it, and Iran has stepped up attacks on commercial ships transiting the strait in recent weeks, according to ABC News. There is no easy workaround. Metcalf told Fortune last month that even Saudi Arabia’s plan to send 10 million barrels of oil a day around Hormuz may barely move prices. The midterm relief rally may not hold Energy costs hung over the campaign. Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate on Nov. 3, and Vice President JD Vance put it bluntly : “The reason we lost is the war.” Oil reacted quickly. Brent crude fell more than 9% on Nov. 4 as traders bet the results would push the White House toward a deal, CNBC reported , and Trump said he had no immediate plans to strike Iran. Iran has long been expected to wait out the vote. In September, Fortune ’s Jordan Blum reported that Tehran was unlikely to let the war end until after the midterms. Mediators were awaiting U.S. and Iranian responses to their latest proposal as of Nov. 2, CNN reported. Metcalf isn’t convinced the relief will last. “The blue wave sparked hopes that the Iran war might be resolved diplomatically and, not surprisingly, oil prices fell sharply,” he says. “That optimism may be short-sighted if Trump decides that, with the election behind him, he can increase military pressure on Iran.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Warriors’ Brandin Podziemski flexes a sweet but unexpected ride to Heat game
articles.summary: Brandin Podziemski and the Golden State Warriors are set to host the Miami Heat on Thursday night, and the young guard made sure his arrival at Chase Center did not go unnoticed. The NBA shared a clip of Podziemski rolling into the arena’s underground parking garage on an electric scooter. The 23
articles._body: Brandin Podziemski and the Golden State Warriors are set to host the Miami Heat on Thursday night, and the young guard made sure his arrival at Chase Center did not go unnoticed . The NBA shared a clip of Podziemski rolling into the arena’s underground parking garage on an electric scooter . The 23-year-old kept it casual for the ride, rocking a black beanie, a puffer jacket over a gray hoodie and a pair of red patterned pants as he cruised past the Warriors’ signage. Brandin Podziemski slides in on the scooter ahead of Warriors-Heat (via @NBA ) pic.twitter.com/2wicdNvS4k — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 6, 2026 It was certainly not the kind of entrance fans are used to seeing from an NBA player, especially one who just landed a big payday. Podziemski agreed to a five-year, $110 million rookie-scale extension with Golden State in October, a deal that includes a mutual option in the fifth year and a trade kicker. He later thanked the organization for taking a “leap with faith” on him . Podziemski, the 19th overall pick in the 2023 NBA Draft, is now in his fourth season with the Warriors. Podziemski’s season did not get off to the smoothest start. He was ruled out of the season opener against the Los Angeles Lakers with lower back soreness. Since returning, though, he has been a key part of a Warriors team that has caught fire. Golden State has won five straight games after dropping its first three, improving to 5-3 on the season. Podziemski chipped in 20 points on 7-of-15 shooting, including 3-of-8 from deep, in Monday’s 116-113 win over the Phoenix Suns. Stephen Curry led the way with 34 points in that one, while rookie Yaxel Lendeborg added 16 points and five assists. The Warriors will now look to extend their winning streak against a Heat team playing on the second night of a back-to-back. Miami is 3-5 on the season but is coming off a thrilling 117-116 overtime win over the LA Clippers on Wednesday, thanks to a go-ahead 3-pointer from former Warriors star Klay Thompson . Thompson, who won four championships in Golden State, is making his first trip back to Chase Center as a member of the Heat . Andrew Wiggins, another former Warrior, is also on Miami’s roster. Podziemski will hope his performance on the court is as smooth as his ride to the arena. articles.title: Ravens’ Jacoby Brissett expected to start Week 10 vs. Chargers after Cardinals trade
articles.summary: Jacoby Brissett got major news about his latest situation after the Baltimore Ravens acquired him in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals. Brissett is going through the 11th season of his NFL career, his first with the Ravens. He started the 2026 campaign with the Cardinals, starting in the first e
articles._body: Jacoby Brissett got major news about his latest situation after the Baltimore Ravens acquired him in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals. Brissett is going through the 11th season of his NFL career, his first with the Ravens. He started the 2026 campaign with the Cardinals, starting in the first eight games before the team benched him for Gardner Minshew. Demoting him down to QB3, Arizona ultimately decided to send him to Baltimore this week. Brissett enters an intriguing situation with his new chapter in Baltimore. The Ravens are dealing with injuries at quarterback, seeing Lamar Jackson on injured reserve and Tyler Huntley being out for the season. NFL insider Ian Rapoport provided his thoughts on Brissett’s status, seeing him to be on pace to be the starter in Week 10. “Jacoby Brissett would have a couple extra days to study and get used to this Ravens offensive, learn a little bit, and then make the start next week. Yeah, a very unusual situation,” Rapoport said on NFL GameDay Kickoff. “Remember, Brissett was benched in Arizona, making him expendable. If he comes over at about $5 million, a little more in salary, the Arizona Cardinals and the Ravens will basically split that. It still should be done tomorrow, and then once again, the Ravens will have a new starting quarterback one that has familiarity with the system because Brissett and Israel Wilfork, the quarterback’s coach, were together in Arizona. We will see if the Ravens can keep things afloat.” From @NFLGameDay Kickoff: The #Ravens QB situation is in flux, with Jacoby Brissett on the way. But what about the future of Lamar Jackson? pic.twitter.com/iIkGMCQc9k — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 5, 2026 What lies ahead for Ravens after Jacoby Brissett trade Jacoby Brissett provides valuable experience and wins under his belt. The Ravens should benefit with his production, especially with his ability to keep running backs and receivers active. Baltimore has a 4-4 record this season, sitting at the bottom of the AFC North Division standings. They are behind the Cleveland Browns, Cincinnati Bengals and the Pittsburgh Steelers at the moment. In terms of the conference standings, they are 10th place. They lead over the Houston Texans and the New York Jets while being under the Las Vegas Raiders and the Browns. Following their Week 9 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars at home, the Ravens will gear up for their next home contest. They host the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 10 as kickoff commences on Nov. 16 at 8:15 p.m. ET. articles.title: Steelers’ 7-round 2027 NFL Draft according to PFF mock draft simulator during bye week
articles.summary: It seems weird to consider the Pittsburgh Steelers a Super Bowl contender. They still have things to fix. But with their bye week, it’s time to look ahead to the 2027 NFL Draft. And here is the Pro Football Focus mock draft simulator for the Steelers. Sitting on top of the AFC North, the Steelers
articles._body: It seems weird to consider the Pittsburgh Steelers a Super Bowl contender . They still have things to fix . But with their bye week, it’s time to look ahead to the 2027 NFL Draft. And here is the Pro Football Focus mock draft simulator for the Steelers. Sitting on top of the AFC North, the Steelers stood strong in the first half of the season. But can they continue their winning ways? And if not, what does 2027 look like? Round 1, Pick 27: CJ Carr, Notre Dame The Steelers set their future on the highly regarded Fighting Irish standout. Carr has gained strength, which was one question mark in consideration for his NFL future. But even without the great physical attributes , Carr is a quality quarterback, according to theringer.com. “The foundation of Carr’s game is his football intelligence,” Todd McShay wrote. “As the grandson of legendary Michigan head coach Lloyd Carr, he’s been immersed in the game his entire life, and it shows. Carr processes information at an advanced level, working through progressions more quickly than most college quarterbacks while demonstrating an impressive understanding of route concepts and defensive coverages. He plays with decisiveness and rarely appears overwhelmed by what defenses present before or after the snap.” Also, Carr succeeds with top-level mechanics. That’s always a bonus for NFL quarterbacks. “Carr has a compact throwing motion and an exceptionally quick release, and he consistently generates good velocity without wasted movement,” McShay wrote. “His ball placement is one of his biggest strengths, particularly on layered throws between the numbers and along the boundary, where he routinely drops passes into tight windows with excellent touch.” Carr would be an excellent fit for head coach Mike McCarthy and the Steelers. Round 2, Pick 60: T Lance Heard, Kentucky Heard has made a name for himself with the Wildcats, who are having a surprisingly good season after forking over the cash to get Heard. And head coach Will Stein thinks Heard will get a good NFL payday. “The people in the NFL that get paid the most are the quarterbacks, left tackles, edge players, corners,” Stein said. “I mean, that’s the market. And, so, we needed to do what was necessary. But also, show him why he needs to be at Kentucky, why he needs to play for me and Cutter Leftwich … in this offense. “He’s like a fun toy to play with. I mean, the guy’s big, physical, can run. He loves it. He’s smart. And so I think anytime we can get players that are that talented in different spots, I think it’s advantage us.” Heard is expected to go in the second round. And that’s exactly where the Steelers get him. One downside is penalties, according to NFL Draft Buzz. “Penalties have followed him, with seven in each of his two Tennessee seasons and three more this year,” NFL Draft Buzz wrote. “And his balance and punch timing can desert him mid-rep. His run blocking is less forceful than his size suggests. And ESPN’s Jordan Reid has reported that some scouts view him as a guard. He is also on his third SEC program in four seasons, and teams will ask about the moves. Round 3, Pick 76: LB Tony Rojas, Penn State It’s possible Rojas might not last this long. So this would be a good pick for the Steelers. The Nittany Lions are struggling to find wins, but Rojas is having a good year , according to post-gazette.com. “I think I’ve been playing at a good level,” Rojas said. “I’m kind of hard on myself, so I know I have a lot to improve on, a lot of things to work on. During the bye week and going forward, just watching film, I know I could be better at things, like getting off blocks against the O-line.” Mel Kiper recently had Rojas as his fourth-best linebacker. And The Athletic has mentioned Rojas as one of the top draft-eligible linebackers. Round 3, Pick 91: T Samson Okunlola, Miami The Steelers continue to build their offensive line with Okunlola in the fold. He can move quite well for a tackle, according to NFL Draft Buzz. “His pass protection is still uneven,” NFL Draft Buzz wrote. “He has allowed 15 pressures in eight games, including five in the double-overtime win over Florida State. This is his first season as a full-time starter, so teams have only half a season of tape at tackle to judge him on, and they will want to see his sets become more consistent against quicker edge rushers. “Overall, Okunlola is a high-upside tackle with five-star tools, positional flexibility and a strong finish to 2025 behind him. He projects as a fourth-round tackle with the ceiling of a starting left tackle if his pass sets keep improving and the floor of a valuable swing lineman. His experience at guard also gives him a fallback position, which adds to his value for a team that wants to develop him behind a veteran line.” Round 4, Pick 130: WR Evan Stewart, Oregon It has been a solid season for Stewart thus far, but not outstanding. He has 31 catches for 423 yards and four touchdowns. But the NFL skills are there. Still, an injury clouds his future. A significant knee injury cost him the entire 2025 season. And since he isn’t the biggest receiver at 6-foot and 178 pounds, those question marks will follow him to the NFL level. Stewart has rare speed. Also, he has shown good separation in his college career. Round 6, Pick 192: DI CJ Mims, Texas A&M This is somewhat of a questionable pick. The 6-foot-2, 312-pound Mims might have to make his way onto an NFL roster by way of being an undrafted free agent. The fifth-year senior is considered a late bloomer. So perhaps that will continue at the next level. Round 6, Pick 200: DI Justin Scott, Miami It’s hard to imagine Scott being available this late in the draft. If the Steelers like him, they would have grabbed him at pick No. 192 instead of Mims. But the draft is a long way off, so who knows how it will play out. articles.title: Ravens’ Joe Fagnano pulls off extremely rare NFL feat in first career start vs. Jaguars
articles.summary: Joe Fagnano is the Baltimore Ravens’ starting quarterback against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday Night Football on Week 9. With this feat, he has joined quite an exclusive club. As the NFL Plus account shared on X, formerly Twitter, Fagnano has become just the eighth rookie quarterbac
articles._body: Joe Fagnano is the Baltimore Ravens’ starting quarterback against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday Night Football on Week 9. With this feat, he has joined quite an exclusive club. As the NFL Plus account shared on X, formerly Twitter, Fagnano has become just the eighth rookie quarterback since 1950 to make his first career start on only three days’ rest . Of those eight, only he and David Blough went undrafted. Undrafted out of UConn, Fagnano is making his first career start in less-than-ideal circumstances. With both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley out injured, Fagnano was suddenly thrust into the spotlight against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. Fagnano went 10-of-21 for 91 yards with no touchdown and an interception in his first career NFL appearance against the Bills. And after getting a bit banged up during that 36-10 loss, he’s now playing again on Thursday night. The Ravens have since acquired Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals amid their quarterback injury crisis. But while he was unable to play on Thursday night, the veteran quarterback is widely expected to take over from Fagnano as the Ravens’ starter in Week 10 against the Los Angeles Chargers. Fagnano’s first quarter as a starter finished with him going 2-of-2 for seven yards. Running back Derrick Henry also got a pass attempt out, but it went for -3 yards. Fagnano is still searching for his first career touchdown pass. But he did lead the Ravens to a field goal during their first drive of the game to answer the Jaguars’ touchdown. Looks like fellow pitcher Blake Snell helped answer that on Thursday. Snell dropped this response when asked about Skubal’s pending status via SportsNet LA. “I’ve done my pitch. I hear the Dodger fans hitting me up all the time to get lil’ bro to stay here. We’ll see what he does, but I think we have a good shot,” Snell said while breaking ground new baseball fields in Altadena, California. "I've done my pitch. I hear the Dodger fans hitting me up all the time to get lil' bro to stay here. We'll see what he does, but I think we have a good shot." @THEREAL_DV chats with Blake Snell in Altadena, where the @DodgersFdn broke ground on Dodgers Dreamfields 69 & 70,… pic.twitter.com/r4PhHRuLVV — SportsNet LA (@SportsNetLA) November 6, 2026 So Snell is optimistic that the former Detroit Tigers MLB All-Star will keep LA as his home. Skubal emerged as a pivotal MLB trade deadline deal for manager Dave Roberts and LA. The move also came amid two-way star Shohei Ohtani dealing with an injury that limited his pitching. Skubal, however, endured a rough National League Championship Series against the Brewers along with the rest of the Dodgers. He took the loss after standing on the mound for five innings and allowing five hits, including one home run to Brice Turang. Los Angeles and Skubal eventually took the 2-1 loss in game one of the NLCS. Los Angeles never recovered from there. Even Snell endured his own rough outing against the eventual WS champs . Snell surrendered four hits in six innings while allowing three different home runs to Jake Bauers, Garrett Mitchell and Jackson Chourio. The Dodgers pitcher did strike out nine batters, but took the game three defeat. articles.title: Heat star Klay Thompson has that look on his face ahead of Warriors showdown
articles.summary: Klay Thompson is back in the Bay Area, and the Miami Heat sharpshooter looks locked in ahead of Thursday night’s showdown with the Golden State Warriors at Chase Center. The NBA shared a clip of Thompson arriving at the arena, headphones on and wearing a calm, focused expression as he made his wa
articles._body: Klay Thompson is back in the Bay Area, and the Miami Heat sharpshooter looks locked in ahead of Thursday night’s showdown with the Golden State Warriors at Chase Center. The NBA shared a clip of Thompson arriving at the arena, headphones on and wearing a calm, focused expression as he made his way inside. The timing could not be better for Miami, as Thompson is coming off one of his best performances in years. Klay Thompson returns to the Bay after dropping 30 points, knocking down 8 threes and hitting the game-winner in last night's OT win, now as a member of the Heat (via @NBA ) pic.twitter.com/TQrJiCB5Kg — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 6, 2026 Thompson erupted for 30 points in Wednesday’s 117-116 overtime win over the LA Clippers, knocking down eight 3-pointers on 17 attempts. He also capped the night with a go-ahead triple with one second left in the extra period, lifting the Heat to a thrilling road victory. It was his first 30-point game since April 2024, back when he was still suiting up for the Warriors. Afterward, Thompson admitted he savored the moment . “I can’t lie to you. It felt really good,” Thompson said. Next up, he heads back to the place where he made his name. Thompson won four NBA championships with Golden State alongside Stephen Curry and Draymond Green before leaving for the Dallas Mavericks in 2024. After two seasons in Dallas, he reached a buyout agreement with the Mavericks in August and signed a two-year deal with Miami. Green even came to his former teammate’s defense shortly after the move, urging people not to expect the Thompson of old. “Don’t try to set my brother up like you getting the 2018 version so when you don’t, you can bash him,” Green said on “The Draymond Green Show.” Now playing in the Eastern Conference for the first time in his career, Thompson has teamed up with Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo in South Beach. He is also reunited in Miami with former Warriors teammate Andrew Wiggins. The Heat will have to dig deep to pull off another win, though. Thursday’s game is the second night of a back-to-back, and Miami enters at 3-5 on the season, while the Warriors sit at 5-3. Golden State also has rookie Yaxel Lendeborg off to a hot start . If Wednesday was any indication, Thompson could be ready for another big night against his old team. Amy Winehouse’s ‘Back to Black’ Reissue Sparks Top 10 Chart Return
articles.summary: The late singer’s sophomore set makes a top 10 splash on four charts.
articles._body: Amy Winehouse ’s Grammy-winning Back to Black album impacts the top 10 of four Billboard charts, following its 20th-anniversary reissue. The album re-enters the top 10 of Indie Store Album Sales (No. 3), Vinyl Albums (No. 4), Top Album Sales (No. 7) and Top R&B Albums (No. 7) (all charts dated Nov. 7). The project also jumps back onto the overall all-genre Billboard 200 at No. 42. Related Amy Winehouse’s ‘Back to Black’ at 20, an Oral History: ‘It Was Just Like Magic’ Ozzfest Announces 2027 Return With Three-Date U.K./North American Run Rush Bringing Reunion Tour to Sphere With 'Elevate From the Norm' Residency Back to Black peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 in 2008, following its big night at that year’s Grammy Awards, where Winehouse won record of the year, song of the year, best female pop vocal performance (for the album’s “Rehab”), best new artist and best pop vocal album (for Back to Black ). For its 20th anniversary, the album was reissued in a variety of options on Oct. 23, including an expanded version with previously unreleased b-sides, demos and a live concert. Back to Black marked the second and final studio album from Winehouse before her death in 2011, and spun off the Billboard Hot 100-charting singles “You Know I’m No Good” and the No. 9 hit “Rehab.” In the tracking week ending Oct. 29, Back to Black earned 16,000 equivalent album units (up 185%) in the United States, according to Luminate. Of that figure, 11,000 was in pure album sales (up 885%), with the remainder driven by streaming activity and track sales. (All versions of the album, old and new, are combined for tracking and charting purposes.) Back to Black is among seven debuts or reentries in the top 10 of the latest Top Album Sales chart. The highest debut of the week belongs to Anderson .Paak and Cordae’s collaborative project Heavy Is the Crown (No. 2), while My Chemical Romance’s The Black Parade jumps 29-1 following its own 20th anniversary reissue.

articles._body: The Ohio State Buckeyes are struggling to keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive as they prepare to host Oregon in a key Big Ten game Saturday. Ryan Day said Thursday that Sayin’s recovery will “take some time, but I think certainly for the long term, we feel like we're on a good track here.” https://t.co/mX3Dp7wnp5 pic.twitter.com/tb2fm5FVdn — Eleven Warriors (@11W) November 5, 2026 The Buckeyes (6-2) dropped their second game of the season last week against USC, struggling to move the ball on offense throughout the game in the 30-18 defeat. It was Ohio State’s first game started by backup quarterback Luke Fahey after the elbow injury suffered by QB1 Julian Sayin during the October 17 victory over Indiana. Sayin reported suffered an elbow fracture, according to reporting by Ohio State beat reporter Bill Rabinowitz. Prior to this report, which Ohio State head coach Ryan Day neither confirmed nor denied, the team had merely referred to the issue as an elbow injury. The Buckeyes ranked 11th in the CFP rankings that was released earlier this week. Ohio State lost an early-season game to the Texas Longhorns in addition to last week’s game against the Trojans. articles.title: The Strokes Better Look Out: Druski Is Coming for Their Musical Guest Gig in New ‘SNL’ Promos
articles.summary: "Can they do this?" the first-time host asks the rock band while ripping an electric guitar solo. (Yes, they can.)
articles._body: Druski is looking to follow in the footsteps of Olivia Rodrigo, Sabrina Carpenter, Harry Styles and more hosts who pulled double duty as the musical guest on Saturday Night Live . There’s only one problem: The Strokes were already booked as this weekend’s musical guest. In new promos for Saturday Night Live , the first-time host — surrounded by cast member Sarah Sherman and The Strokes — proudly announces, “Hi, I’m Druski, and I’ll be the host and musical guest on SNL this week!” Related Watch Druski Get Down to This Viral Latin Hit With Marcello Hernandez Ahead of ‘SNL’ Hosting Debut The Strokes Send Off Stephen Colbert With Late Night ‘Falling Out of Love’ Performance: Watch The Best Phone Plans for Frequent Concertgoers That Offer VIP Access, Ticket Discounts & Festival Lounges “Druski, we already have a musical guest — The Strokes,” Sherman replies, to which the band’s Fabrizio Moretti just waves at the viral comedian and says, “Hi!” “Can they do this ?” Druski asks before ripping a totally sick (and obviously pantomimed) electric guitar solo. “Wow, that’s really great!” Strokes frontman Julian Casablancas tells Druski. “But yes, yes we can.” The promos begin with Druski singing a song and playing air guitar and then asking, “That’s you guys, right?” When Moretti politely shakes his head, “No,” Sherman urges the host: “Just do the promo, Druski!” Watch the full promos below: Druski is hosting Saturday Night Live for the first time this weekend, while The Strokes will be the musical guest for a fourth time. They made their SNL debut in January 2002 and also performed in 2006 and 2011. The band is promoting their most recently released album, July’s Reality Awaits , which debuted at No. 13 on the all-genre Billboard 200 and at No. 5 on the Top Rock & Alternative Albums chart. articles.title: Pusha T Thinks Today’s Rap Landscape Lacks Originality: ‘People Try to Do Different Versions of What’s Hot’
articles.summary: The Virginia rapper also spoke on Jay-Z's stance on rap battles.
articles._body: Pusha T isn’t the biggest fan of biters. During a conversation with The Wall Street Journal about his daily routine, the Virginia rapper had some thoughts on the rap landscape in 2026 and feels like the game lacks originality. “It started off with a lot more individuality. Everybody wanted to be different,” he explained. “They wanted to be great, and they wanted to set themselves apart. You can’t look like me, you can’t do what I do.” He added, “Now people try to do different versions of what’s hot. Everyone can just be good and be the same. I feel like people don’t mind being like other people these days.” Push, who’s found himself in a rap battle or two during his career, was also asked about his thoughts on Jay-Z telling GQ that he thinks maybe rap battles should be avoided these days because stan culture and social media can blow things out of proportion, while using the Drake and Kendrick fallout as an example. He played coy on the recent battle Jigga was referencing and essentially disagreed with the Brooklyn rapper’s point-of-view, but did say that things should be kept on wax. “I don’t see a world in which artists are just going to get along at all times. This is a very competitive sport,” he said. “I don’t what instances Jay-Z was talking about — I’m sure that things have gotten out of hand, but they never need to go that far. As long as it’s music, it’s fine. Anything outside of that realm, it’s overboard.” Elsewhere in the interview, he revealed that he and Pharrell often talk at 5:30 a.m. and treat their studio time like jobs, usually working a 12-hour shift starting at 6 a.m. to 6 p.m.

articles.title: The AI backlash needs a plan
articles.summary: Democrats have a mandate to rein in frontier labs, data centers, and more. Can they deliver without repeating their mistakes from the social-media era?
articles._body: This is a column about AI. My fiancé works at Anthropic. See my full ethics disclosure here . On Tuesday, America voted to give Democrats control over both houses of Congress , punishing Republicans for the abandoned promises of the second Trump administration and raising hopes that a decade of MAGA misery might be coming to an end. In exit polls, voters were fed up with high prices for gas and groceries, the chaotic conflict with Iran, and the endemic corruption of the Trump administration, which they seemed to have noticed in large numbers for the first time. But another powerful thread of discontent ran through the voting on Tuesday, and it lay in the administration’s full-throated endorsement of Big Tech oligarchy and the AI accelerationism it has pushed for in the White House.   In Texas, Gina Hinojosa unseated Gov. Greg Abbott after campaigning on an immediate moratorium on new data centers . In Ohio, Sherrod Brown beat Sen. Jon Husted, whom he called “the face of data centers” after Husted recruited and gave tax breaks to the facilities during his time as lieutenant governor. Voters approved bans or restrictions on data centers in at least 38 jurisdictions . The efforts of pro-AI super PACs mostly went nowhere , as did those of Elon Musk, who spent nearly half a billion dollars this cycle and got almost nothing in return . The incoming majority in Congress is already promising to take a stronger hand in regulating tech companies. Rep. Greg Casar, who chairs the Congressional Progressive Caucus, called the results an "early tremor of a much bigger AI earthquake." Sen. Ed Markey joked that Democrats would be issuing so many subpoenas they'd need new forests. At Transformer , Shakeel Hashim predicted that a bill regulating frontier models will pass in the first months of 2027, and that President Trump might even sign it. It’s clear that Democrats won a strong mandate against something: data centers and their various externalities, billionaires buying elections, and the AI industry’s ongoing promise to take your job and also maybe kill you. But properly regulating AI isn’t as simple as banning data centers — which the labs will simply move to other states, countries, or even into space. It may not even be as simple as pausing frontier AI development — even if the United States could coordinate a global pause, we would still be left with the question of how technology development could safely continue. The uncertainty over what to do next feels familiar. It’s an uncertainty that plagued the entire debate over what to do about social media in the aftermath of the 2016 US presidential election — a debate that never resulted in any meaningful regulation from Congress. Social media is now being regulated primarily by judges and juries. AI regulation can’t afford to take the same path. One, the stakes are even higher than they were in social media. (TikTok and Instagram might scramble your brain, or the brain of someone you love, but there was never any risk that they might automate your job or invent a novel bioweapon.) And two, the technology is developing much faster : most industry leaders believe that hugely powerful AI systems may arrive within the next two years. Congress will not have a decade to debate which approach to regulation is the right one. And in particular, it does not have a decade for a debate that goes nowhere. Beginning in 2018, Congress spent roughly four years being performatively furious at social media companies. Mark Zuckerberg was dragged in to testify about Cambridge Analytica and a host of other issues. Frances Haugen brought tens of thousands of pages of internal Meta documents with her to Capitol Hill. Antitrust subcommittees produced a 450-page report and a package of bills aimed at dismantling the oligarchy.  All America got in return was a ban on TikTok that, in the end, no one bothered to enforce. The country still has no comprehensive privacy law, no Section 230 reform, and no new antitrust legislation. The Kids Online Safety Act, first introduced four years ago, appears stuck in a kind of perpetual limbo. It took juries in Los Angeles and New Mexico accepting the argument that addictive product design can cause harm to get around Section 230 and punish the platforms for their recklessness. State attorneys general got a settlement from Meta worth roughly $17 billion , plus some of the time limits and notification curfews for teens that Congress never managed to pass.  There was once bipartisan momentum to regulate social media, too. But America got nowhere, I think, because of a handful of mistakes that it may be on the verge of making again when it comes to AI.  With that in mind, then, here are three things to watch out for as the new Congress is seated in January. Mistake No. 1: no coherent goal. Maybe the biggest problem with the movement to “make social media safer” was that no one could agree on what “safe” meant.  Is social media “safe” if it can’t send push notifications? If the feed is not personalized to your interests? If it is scrubbed of all bullying, harassment, hate speech, violence, and self-harm?  Should platforms be able to rent your personal data to advertisers, or show you ads for scams without much penalty? What obligations should they have to label and remove propaganda? How far should a sitting president be able to go in overturning the results of an election and keep his account?  Each of these questions demands a separate answer. But Congress largely treated “regulating social media” as one thing — go look at the range of questions Zuckerberg would get whenever he went before lawmakers, even if the hearing had been organized around a more coherent set of subjects. Falcons’ Bijan Robinson shoots down notion that he is NFL’s best RB, for now
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons decimated the Green Bay Packers in Lambeau Field and upset the San Francisco 49ers in Mercedes-Benz Stadium, demonstrating the capacity to compete at a playoff-caliber level on a given night. They are still not a consistently good football team, though, hence their 3-5 record.
articles._body: The Atlanta Falcons decimated the Green Bay Packers in Lambeau Field and upset the San Francisco 49ers in Mercedes-Benz Stadium, demonstrating the capacity to compete at a playoff-caliber level on a given night. They are still not a consistently good football team, though, hence their 3-5 record. Kevin Stefanski’s team is about to enter a strenuous stretch that features games against the Cincinnati Bengals, Kansas City Chiefs, Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions (Week 11 bye sandwiched in between). If Atlanta is going to be competitive by Christmas, Bijan Robinson will need to perform like the NFL’s best running back . Many people believe he currently carries that title, but the player himself is not convinced. “I don’t feel like I am playing like that right now,” Robinson said, per reporter Tori McElhaney. While the All-Pro certainly believes he has what it takes to reclaim top status, he does not think his recent play warrants such a label at this time. Robinson rushed for 139 yards in his last two games combined, averaging 3.2 yards per carry versus the 49ers and 4.0 yards per attempt in Sunday’s 16-0 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He did not score in either week. Even so, the two-time Pro Bowler unquestionably remains in the discussion for best back in the league. He is closing in on 1,000 scrimmage yards and is gaining an elite 5.2 yards per run. Jahmyr Gibbs, Kenneth Walker III and James Cook could all surpass him in rushing yards once they play the same amount of games, but it should not be long before Bijan Robinson amazes everyone again with his lethal combination of power and elusiveness. No. 7 will try to channel his inner beast versus the Bengals in Madrid , as the Falcons do their best to keep pace in an uninspiring NFC South. articles._body: New Orleans Pelicans star Trey Murphy III is dealing with an injury at the moment. He is listed on the injury report for Friday night’s game against the Minnesota Timberwolves as probable with bilateral patella tendinopathy. Barring unforeseen circumstances, it seems as if Murphy should have a good chance of playing. Murphy, 26, is averaging 14.9 points, 4.6 rebounds and 3.4 assists per outing so far in the 2026-27 NBA season. The forward is also shooting 45.5 percent from the field and 38.5 percent from beyond the arc. He’s certainly made a big impact through his seven games played up to this point. Julian Reese (G League two-way) is also probable to play. Jaron Pierre Jr. (G League two-way) and Malik Dia (G league two-way) are both doubtful for the game. Yves Missi (left knee contusion/bone bruise) is out. For the Timberwolves, Terrence Shannon Jr. (left hip contusion) is questionable to play. Anthony Edwards (right knee arthroscopy) and Donte DiVincenzo (right Achilles tendon repair/surgery) both remain out for the game. New Orleans has been inconsistent so far this season. The Pelicans are 4-4 overall following their 120-113 win over the Utah Jazz on Wednesday night. The Timberwolves most recently earned a 117-107 victory over the Houston Rockets on the road. Minnesota is looking to perform well despite Edwards’ injury absence. They are 6-3 overall. The Pelicans will enter play on Friday in 10th place in the Western Conference, while the Timberwolves are in seventh place. Tip-off for Friday night’s game between the Western Conference opponents is scheduled for 8 PM ET in New Orleans. articles._body: The San Francisco 49ers received an encouraging injury update Thursday as star running back Christian McCaffrey returned to practice ahead of Sunday’s Week 9 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders. McCaffrey participated on a limited basis after sitting out Wednesday’s session with a hamstring injury. His return represents progress for the 49ers , who are preparing for their first game following a Week 8 bye. The 49ers running back is working his way back from a mild left hamstring strain that raised concerns about his availability for Sunday’s matchup. The Athletic’s Sam Warren shared the Raiders’ updated injury report Thursday on X, formerly Twitter, confirming McCaffrey’s change in participation. Raiders CB Darien Porter was a limited participant in his return to practice on Thursday. WR Dont’e Thornton Jr. was limited with a back injury. pic.twitter.com/UMdzDuVOjE — Sam Warren (@samwarren83) November 5, 2026 The report listed the former Stanford standout as a nonparticipant Wednesday before he returned to practice in a limited capacity Thursday. McCaffrey sustained the injury during San Francisco’s lone loss of the season against the Falcons, playing just 52 percent of the 49ers’ offensive snaps. Despite the setback, he totaled 100 scrimmage yards and a rushing touchdown on 13 touches. Friday’s practice and final injury report will help determine whether McCaffrey carries an injury designation into Sunday’s matchup. His return is particularly important given the 49ers’ mounting injuries at wide receiver and his elite ability to generate yards after the catch out of the backfield. Christian Kirk missed Thursday’s practice with a knee injury, joining Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) on the sidelines. The absences could leave the 49ers shorthanded offensively against Las Vegas. The 49ers (6-1) host the Raiders (4-4) at Levi’s Stadium on Sunday. Kickoff is scheduled for 1:25 p.m. PT (4:25 p.m. ET). articles.title: 76ers’ Joe Embiid retroactively slapped with Flagrant 1 for kicking Cade Cunningham
articles.summary: The NBA has assessed Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid a Flagrant 1 foul for kicking Detroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham during Wednesday’s 112-106 win, ClutchPoints’ Kris Pursiainen reported on Thursday. The incident occurred with 5:32 remaining in the first quarter. Cunningham
articles._body: The NBA has assessed Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid a Flagrant 1 foul for kicking Detroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham during Wednesday’s 112-106 win, ClutchPoints’ Kris Pursiainen reported on Thursday. The incident occurred with 5:32 remaining in the first quarter. Cunningham was defending Embiid near the three-point line when the 32-year-old extended his right leg during an initial shooting attempt. Embiid subsequently passed the ball to LeBron James, but his kick struck Cunningham in the groin , leaving the 25-year-old bent over in pain. No foul was called during the sequence. Cunningham was slow to recover as Embiid moved past him for a dunk and later continued grabbing the area where he was struck. The incident was not Embiid’s only disciplinary issue during the contest. He also received a technical foul after pushing Pistons forward Tolu Smith underneath the basket with 1:25 remaining in the first half, leading to a brief confrontation. Both the technical and the retroactively assessed Flagrant 1 were Embiid’s first infractions of their respective types this season. Under league regulations, a Flagrant 1 carries one point, and reaching six points during the regular season results in a one-game suspension. A player also faces ejection after receiving two Flagrant 1 fouls in the same game, while a Flagrant 2 results in an automatic ejection. Despite the incident, Embiid finished with 26 points and a season-high 15 rebounds against Detroit . He is averaging 19.6 points and 10 rebounds through his first seven appearances this season. The victory improved Philadelphia’s record to 8-1 . Jaylen Brown led the 76ers with 30 points and seven rebounds, while Cunningham recorded 26 points and 11 assists for the Pistons. The two teams will not face each other again until February. The post 76ers’ Joe Embiid retroactively slapped with Flagrant 1 for kicking Cade Cunningham appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Upset Alerts: Josh Pate reveals concern level in notable Week 10 games
articles.summary: We haven’t even seen what is going to happen in Week 10, but it’s likely to go down as the best weekend of the college football regular season. Before the action gets underway, Josh Pate has unveiled his weekly upset alerts, identifying teams that he has at least some level of concern in. There are
articles._body: We haven’t even seen what is going to happen in Week 10, but it’s likely to go down as the best weekend of the college football regular season. Before the action gets underway, Josh Pate has unveiled his weekly upset alerts, identifying teams that he has at least some level of concern in. There are seven games between two College Football Playoff-ranked teams this weekend. No. 3 Utah hosts No. 9 BYU , No. 10 Ole Miss hosts No. 2 Georgia , No. 11 Notre Dame hosts No. 1 Miami , No. 12 Ohio State hosts No. 23 Oregon , No. 13 Tennessee hosts No. 6 Kentucky , No. 14 LSU hosts No. 5 Alabama , and No. 18 Missouri hosts No. 7 Texas . $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Of course, on Tuesday night, the first CFP rankings of the season were unveiled. The 12-team bracket , as of today, features five SEC teams, two Big Ten teams, two Big 12 teams, one ACC team, plus Notre Dame and Boise State . There was a lot of criticism with the rankings, notably surrounding Alabama, Notre Dame, Ohio State and others. This weekend, those initial rankings might not matter much. Now, it’s time for Week 10, a do-or-die week for many teams. Here’s who Pate has on upset alert. Watch on Fubo (Try for Free) No. 8 UCLA at Minnesota UCLA is 8-0 on the season, 5-0 in the Big Ten, and ranked No. 8 in the first College Football Playoff rankings. Being at No. 8 while undefeated shows that the strength of schedule is holding the Bruins back at least a little bit. They’ll go on the road to Minnesota, who is 5-3 overall and 3-2 in the Big Ten. The Golden Gophers took Indiana to overtime last week. Can they give another top ten team a run for their money? “The long November theory is if you’re a contender for the first time in a long time, it’s one thing to do it in September, it’s one thing to do it in October,” Pate said. “It’s a fact that November is the longest month of the year for new contenders.” Concern Meter: 7/10 Texas A&M at No. 21 South Carolina Texas A&M has struggled this season, currently 4-4 overall, 1-4 in the SEC and having lost four of its last six games. No. 21 South Carolina lost three in a row in the middle of its season, but now has three straight wins to sit at 5-3 overall and 3-3 in the SEC. The Gamecocks are surging, and find themselves in the first CFP rankings. Can they stave off the upset in Week 10? “I don’t care how big a lead South Carolina gets in this game, I will white knuckle this thing for four quarters,” said Pate. “I will white knuckle this thing until Shane Beamer is at the postgame press conference podium going, look at that, four wins in a row. Look at that, it wasn’t just ‘Cocktober’ magic.” Concern Meter: 7/10 No. 19 Iowa at Northwestern Iowa cracks the top 20 in the first CFP rankings, and they’re 6-2 on the season and 3-2 in Big Ten play. The Hawkeyes are 2-2 in their last four games. They’ll go on the road to take on a Northwestern team that just recently fell out of the AP Poll. The Wildcats fell to Oregon last week, dropping to 6-2 on the season and 3-2 in the Big Ten. “Chip Kelly versus Phillip Parker is like a pay-per-view banner,” Pate said. “I could see that on a late 90s WWF pay-per-view promotional poster. That is irresistable force and immovable object type stuff, Chip Kelly and Phil Parker. … This is a coin flip game, so it’s a 10.” Concern Meter: 10/10 Michigan State at Michigan This game is between two rivals, and two teams that have questions at quarterback. Michigan State starter Alessio Milivojevic entered the week questionable, while Michigan just named Tommy Carr its starter for the foreseeable future over Bryce Underwood . The Spartans have lost six games in a row after a 2-0 start, sitting at 2-6 overall and 0-5 in the Big Ten. The Wolverines are 5-3 overall and 2-3 in the Big Ten after Carr’s big performance last week against Rutgers. “I am not counting on Michigan to get margin on anyone this year,” said Pate. “So even the games they win, they are close games. That means I’ve got to put at least a 6 on the upset alert concern meter for all Michigan games.” Concern Meter: 6/10 Oklahoma at No. 24 Florida Jason Witten is set to make his debut as Oklahoma’s interim offensive coordinator on Saturday after the team fired Ben Arbuckle this week. Can he unlock John Mateer and the offense again after falling to 4-4 on the season and 2-3 in the SEC last week? As for No. 24 Florida, they’re rolling with Tramell Jones Jr. as their starter this weekend. The Gators have lost three of their last four, falling to 5-3 on the season and 3-3 against the SEC. “There are changes everywhere for both of these teams,” Pate said… “Yeah, I think it could be sloppy. I’m gonna put a 7 on the upset alert concern meter because I have no idea what to expect.” Concern Meter: 7/10 West Virginia at No. 15 Texas Tech If there’s one thing to know about West Virginia, it’s that they can score. Defense has been a struggle, but the duo of quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. and running back Cam Cook can beat you even though they had a quieter day last weekend in a win over TCU . The Mountaineers are 5-3 overall and 2-3 in the Big 12. No. 15 Texas Tech recently turned to Thomas Castellanos at QB, and he led the Red Raiders to a win over Arizona last weekend to reach 7-1 on the season and 4-1 in the Big 12. “Texas Tech has a top 15 run defense. West Virginia does not have a top 100 run defense,” Pate said. “Both teams want to run the ball, one of them will far more effectively, and that’s the home team.” Concern Meter: 2/10

The cornerback Wiggins is a surprising inactive for the Jaguars game. Apart from Wiggins, the Ravens also announced wide receiver Elij
articles._body: The Baltimore Ravens face Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 9 on Thursday Night Football, but they will be without defensive back Nate Wiggins. The cornerback Wiggins is a surprising inactive for the Jaguars game. Apart from Wiggins, the Ravens also announced wide receiver Elijah Stewart, safety Jaylin Hawkins, guard Emery Jones, defensive tackle Aeneas Peebles, and quarterback Kedon Slovis as among those unavailable to play for this game at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore. Wiggins is reportedly dealing with an “illness/stinger,” which is why he’s been ruled out for the assignment versus Jacksonville, according to Jamison Hensley of ESPN. The former Clemson Tigers defensive back was a full participant in the first two days of practice this week. That was before he sat out Wednesday’s practice, prompting concerns about his availability for the Week 9 contest in Baltimore. For now, the Ravens will have to find a way to contain the high-flying offense of the Jaguars without Wiggins. Jacksonville enters Thursday fifth in the league with an average of 28.0 points per game and 16th with 227.4 passing yards per outing. So far in his third season in the NFL, Wiggins has four passes defended and 24 combined tackles in eight games. Wiggins’ absence adds a headache for the Ravens, who are already dealing with other injuries to key players, including their top two quarterbacks, Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. The Ravens selected Wiggins, who had an injury scare as well in the offseason , in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft and signed him to a four-year, $12.81 million contract. Siegel would say that he is “buying” the scenario of Memphis trading Jerome at the trade deadline, saying that he will be “one of the top trade candidates on the market.” With the prospect of getting back draft picks, Siegel mentions how Grizzlies general manager Zach Kleiman values draft capital, predicting that Jerome will be “moved to a team that is going to be making the playoffs and is going to be in the championship mix.” “He’s [Jerome] going to be pretty much entering the final year of his contract near the trade deadline because he has that player option that he can decide on in the offseason,” Siegel said. “He’s going to be declining that to get a major payday for what he’s done with Memphis…And now there’s going to be teams out there that need key point guards, he’s on a very team-friendly contract. articles.summary: LEGO's latest holiday ad encourages families to spend more quality time together through hands-on play.
articles._body: All products and services featured are independently chosen by editors. However, Billboard may receive a commission on orders placed through its retail links, and the retailer may receive certain auditable data for accounting purposes. LEGO brings some familiar faces — and helmets — together for its 2026 holiday commercial . Directed by The Greatest Showman filmmaker Michael Gracey, the ad brings together Daft Punk , E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, Derpy Tiger from KPop Demon Hunters , Thor, Doctor Doom, the Ninjago Twin Titans and more in an action-packed video set to Daft Punk’s “One More Time.” In the ad, one humble brick becomes the lead character in a fast-moving journey through a workshop full of familiar faces from film, music, sports and the wider LEGO universe, with a message about the simple pleasure of play. shop sets featured in 2026 holiday ad At the heart of this year’s campaign is interactive play with family and friends, and builds on last year’s holiday ad, which featured a child distracted by doomscrolling before LEGO characters inspired him to put down his phone and join his sister in building. This year, the message is all about starting with a single brick and the endless possibilities that come from hands-on creativity, working together and quality time. Lego According to research shared in LEGO’s press release, 89% of people wish they spent more time playing together as a family, while 24% of parents admit they’ve purchased a LEGO set as a gift knowing they would enjoy playing with it themselves. The findings give the campaign a timely angle, particularly for families looking for ways to spend more meaningful time together during the holidays. LEGO is extending the campaign beyond the screen, too. Brick-and-mortar stores worldwide have been transformed into holiday workshops, offering festive experiences through Pick a Brick, Build A Mini, Minifigure Factory and the LEGO #BuildToGive initiative, which donates sets to children every year during the holidays. Shop the Sets from LEGO’s 2026 Holiday Ad shop sets featured in 2026 holiday ad For shoppers looking to recreate moments from the commercial, several featured sets are available to add to a holiday wish list , such as the Ferrari F2004 & Michael Schumacher build, which includes 735 pieces and costs $89.99. E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial , who made a memorable cameo in the ad, is made up of 1,226 pieces and is selling for $139.99, while the Avengers: Doomsday Quinjet is a 433-piece set priced at $59.99. Lego KPop Demon Hunters ‘ Derpy Tiger and Sussie Bird made a brief appearance and together make up an 825-piece build for $69.99. Among the stars was also Lionel Messi , whose LEGO set comprises 958 pieces for $79.99. Together, these builds bring the commercial’s mix of entertainment, sports and nostalgia into the home. LEGO’s holiday message is ultimately about more than what’s underneath the Christmas tree. It’s about making time to build, play and connect. As the ad’s outro reads: “Give the joy of bricks.”

Jordan Love and his wife were blind referees for Halloween pic.twitter.com/aKp85sVeWA — Jomboy Media (@JomboyMedia) November 4, 2026 The Packers are p
articles._body: The Green Bay Packers have the serious business of trying to chase down their three NFC North rivals. It may be the toughest job in the NFL. Jordan Love and his wife were blind referees for Halloween pic.twitter.com/aKp85sVeWA — Jomboy Media (@JomboyMedia) November 4, 2026 The Packers are playing quite well as they have won four of their last five games and own a 5-3 record. However, in the brutal NFC North, that has left them in fourth place in the division. The Packers have a pair of tough games coming up as they face the New England Patriots in Week 9 before hosting the Vikings in Week 10. The Packers have been hit hard by penalty calls in recent weeks, and quarterback Jordan Love and his wife dressed up as blind NFL referees for the recently concluded Halloween celebration. The Halloween costumes were designed as a joke, but NFL officials don’t take kindly to criticism of its officials by players or coaches. If the NFL looks at this as tongue-in-cheek criticism, there could be a rebuke or a fine. Love sent the video of the costumes to Packers head coach Matt LaFleur, and the head coach thought the quarterback’s take was quite funny but didn’t go much further. “He did send me the clip and I thought it was pretty hilarious,” LaFleur said , per Matt Schneidman of The Athletic . “But I should probably refrain from commenting on that.” Love is regularly viewed as one of the most talented quarterbacks in the NFL because of his ability to throw deep passes to his receivers. Love has completed 192 of 312 passes for a league-high 2,246 yards. articles.summary: Through the new collaboration, ASCAP members will be connected with mental health providers offering talk therapy, psychiatric services and more.
articles._body: ASCAP and Project Healthy Minds are collaborating on an initiative to provide the PRO’s songwriter, composer and music publisher members with access to a comprehensive ecosystem of mental health services, therapy options and wellness tools, it was announced Thursday (Nov. 5). The effort is meant to support creators at every stage of their careers and is an outgrowth of ASCAP’s wellness initiative launched in 2019 , which earlier this year expanded to include a telehealth benefit through MD Live for urgent care consultations, plus dermatology and additional health services. Related Therapy on the Road: Inside the Touring Mental Health Service Used by Olivia Rodrigo, Ed Sheeran & More Kenny MacPherson, Veteran Music Publisher and Big Deal Music Co-Founder, Dies at 71 Diddy Moved From New Jersey Prison to Similar Facility in Pennsylvania “Creativity thrives when creators are supported — in mind, body, and spirit,” Nick Lehman , ASCAP executive vp/chief strategy and digital officer, said in a statement. “Music creators put their everything into the music we love, yet trying to find quality, affordable support shouldn’t feel like everything is stacked against them in an opaque healthcare system. By teaming up with Project Healthy Minds, we are delivering direct access to vetted care — removing friction so our members get meaningful support, whenever and however they need it.” According to the announcement, the initiative will allow ASCAP members to privately connect with mental health providers that offer such services as talk therapy and psychiatry; peer-led and expert-moderated support groups; and self-care apps and digital tools. “Songwriters have helped millions of people feel less alone, and this partnership makes sure they have that same support in return,” Project Healthy Minds founder/CEO Phillip Schermer said in a statement. “We are thrilled to give ASCAP’s members a simple way to find care, whether that’s a therapist, a support group or a tool they can use on the road.” Information on how to access the program is available on the ASCAP member access portal .

Colman Domingo Reveals He & Will Smith Went to High School Together: ‘He Was the Cool Kid & I Was the Nerd’
articles.summary: Which director will reunite these two West Philly legends?
articles._body: Colman Domingo and The Fresh Prince go way back. Sort of. The actor recently dropped by Benny Blanco , Lil Dicky and Kristin Batalucco‘s Friends Keep Secrets YouTube show, and while he and Dicky bonded over being from the Philadelphia area, Domingo revealed that he and Will Smith went to high school together. “I went to high school with Will,” he said after referencing The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air ‘s theme song. “He was in the class before me, we had gym class and science class together.” However, they weren’t really that close back in those days as Smith was beginning his rap career as one-half of DJ Jazzy Jeff & The Fresh Prince . “We were never friends,” Domingo continued. “He was the cool kid and I was like ‘The Nerd.’ I was trying not to get beat up the whole time.” He added that the future multi-platinum rapper and Oscar winner “really was the most popular kid in high school.“ “He was a local rapper and he and Jazzy Jeff , they would do shows at The Wynne Ballroom, and all the cool kids went. I didn’t go because I wasn’t a cool kid. I heard about it, but I was too busy doing schoolwork.” The weird thing, though, is the two actors haven’t run into each other in Hollywood yet. The last time they saw each other was when Colman waited on him at a restaurant back home after Smith had become a huge star. “The last interaction I had with him, I was working at El Torito restaurant in Philadelphia as a waiter,” he recalled. “This is after he became very successful, moved to L.A., came back, and he had a big table with a bunch of friends and stuff like that.” Domingo said as he was taking the table’s order, Will eventually recognized him and the two “hugged and that was it.“ “The weirdest thing is throughout our careers now, I’ve never run into him. I’m sure we’ll see each other at some point. And there’ll be warmth and a shared history from Philadelphia,” he concluded. You can watch the full episode below.

articles.title: Dolly Parton Estate Drops Lawsuit Against Late Star’s Nephew Over Alleged Threats
articles.summary: Last week, lawyers for Bryan Seaver said they and the Parton estate had been "engaged in good faith discussions in an attempt to resolve this matter."
articles._body: Dolly Parton ’s estate has ended its lawsuit against Bryan Seaver , the late country star’s nephew and longtime head of security. A Thursday (Nov. 5) court filing, obtained by Billboard , voluntarily dismisses the Parton estate’s claims against Seaver without prejudice, meaning they could be refiled again in the future. Lawyers for both sides did not immediately return inquiries as to whether the dismissal reflects a settlement, though Seaver’s attorneys wrote in a court filing last week that they had recently been “engaged in good faith discussions in an attempt to resolve this matter.” Related Dolly Parton Carefully Planned Her Estate to Avoid Family ‘Mess.’ A Legal Fight Is Brewing Anyway Kenny MacPherson, Veteran Music Publisher and Big Deal Music Co-Founder, Dies at 71 Diddy Moved From New Jersey Prison to Similar Facility in Pennsylvania She’s Alive LLC, the entity managing Parton’s posthumous affairs under the leadership of her longtime manager Danny Nozell , sued Seaver in September. The estate alleged Seaver had been trying to extort money since Parton’s death a month earlier by sending violent threats like “I’m a killer” and “all I do is warfare.” Seaver denied this , saying Nozell had taken his text messages out of context and “turned a private, profane and ultimately friendly exchange between two longtime friends into a claim of terror.” Parton’s estate had been seeking an injunction to bar Seaver from interfering with the business (Seaver’s financial inheritance was never at issue in the legal case). A hearing on the injunction request was delayed numerous times and had been set to finally begin this coming Tuesday (Nov. 10) in Nashville. That court proceeding is now canceled. When Parton was alive, she was intentional about planning her estate to avoid the type of infighting that’s roiled grieving families of so many famous artists before her. But as the Seaver matter demonstrated, all the organization in the world still does not guarantee peace. “It only takes one to upset the apple cart,” estate attorney Scott Rahn told Billboard when the lawsuit was filed. But Rahn said the fact that Parton’s estate brought the matter to court so quickly was a sign that she had put the right people in place to take care of things. “You cannot plan for every possible eventuality,” said Rahn at the time. “Your documents would fill libraries talking about every single thing. At the end of the day, what you need to do, which is I think what Dolly did, is pick a capable team for managing your affairs. And that’s what’s happening here.”
