articles.title: The Road to Las Vegas begins in earnest now
articles.summary: The College Football Playoff committee released its first rankings as the road to Las Vegas and the National Championship begins in earnest. This Saturday’s slate of games will help sort out who can make it to Las Vegas in January. Seven games feature two ranked teams. Games like Alabama-LSU and Tex
articles._body: The College Football Playoff committee released its first rankings as the road to Las Vegas and the National Championship begins in earnest. This Saturday’s slate of games will help sort out who can make it to Las Vegas in January. Seven games feature two ranked teams. Games like Alabama-LSU and Texas-Missouri could be playoff elimination games this weekend. Notre Dame, Ole Miss and Tennessee look to need a win to keep their playoff hopes alive. BYU-Utah will help determine how many teams the Big 12 get in the playoff. This college football season will end with the best team in America hoisting the national title trophy at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas. But Las Vegas is the best place to experience college football all season long. Get the trip out of the group chat and let Ari Wasserman and Andy Staples give you their guide to the perfect college football Saturday. Breakfast Spot Ari: Eggslut, Cosmopolitan It’s Las Vegas. You’re going to have pretty big lunches and dinners, so you may not want to overdo it at breakfast. Even if you do, there’s something for you at Eggslut. That’s the move. It turns egg-based dishes into comfort food and serves what is legitimately the best egg sandwich I’ve ever had in my entire life. If you want to ramp it up, Eggslut also serves the Gaucho Sandwich, which has wagyu tri-tip steak, chimichurri, red onions, and seasoned arugula over an over-medium egg on a warm brioche bun. Originally an LA food truck, this is a quick stop where you order at the counter and eat in the seating area. Perfect baseline for a Las Vegas day, especially if you’re getting your food minutes before BYU and Utah kick off. Andy: Hash House A Go Go, The Linq Nothing prepares you for a day of partying or refuels you after a night of partying quite like the home of Twisted Farm Food. Of course I’m partial to Andy’s World Famous Fried Chicken Waffle Tower. Prepare to carb load, because you’ll also want a banana and brown sugar pancake on the side, a perfect thing to eat while watching Texas to try to keep its CFP hopes alive against Missouri. Already moved on to lunch? Grab a hand-hammered pork tenderloin sandwich or a bacon, avocado and cheddar stuffed burger. And it’s never too early — or too late — for the Black Crow, Hash House’s fresh blackberry-infused Old Fashioned. Spot to watch the first window Ari: Charlie’s, Wynn Don’t know whether you want a sportsbook or a sports bar? Charlie’s has you covered. It’s an awesome sports bar located directly next to Wynn’s sportsbook. There are no walls enclosing the restaurant, so you have great television views both inside the sports bar and out toward the big board of the sportsbook. It has awesome bar food and great drinks, and it’s very convenient to get up and take a quick walk to the cage if you’re so inclined. The location is a must, as you’d be arriving just as Alabama-LSU and Oregon-Ohio State are kicking off. Andy: Beer Park, Paris One of the best afternoons of my life was an NFL Sunday a few years back spent at Beer Park surrounded by friends and pitchers. It would be even better on a college football Saturday. Every game is on, from the endings of the morning window to the beginning of Kentucky-Tennessee. There’s a tap for every taste. (I highly recommend the Moose Drool brown ale.) The weather late in football season is glorious. And the people-watching on the Strip below provides peak between-play entertainment. Dinner First Night Ari: Piero’s Italian Cuisine: Located on Convention Center Dr. Piero’s is a Las Vegas institution and a five-star Italian restaurant. Though the location isn’t on the Strip — it’s right off it — Piero’s scratches the itch if you want to feel like you’re in “Old Las.” The food is incredible, and it’s an institution that has served mobsters, politicians, and celebrities since 1982. Go for the food, stay for the vibes, catch Miami-Notre Dame. Perfect evening. Andy: estiatorio Milos, The Venetian Milos combines a Mediterranean-style fish market with fine-dining ambience. Start with the Milos Special (a tower of paper-thin fried zucchini and eggplant chips) and chargrilled octopus. To choose your entree, you’ll peruse the selection of fresh fish caught off the coasts of Greece, Tunisia, Nova Scotia and Florida. Pick whatever fish suits your tastebuds, but keep the preparation simple. Order it baked in a salt crust and thank me later. Great flavor and Ole Miss-Georgia? What’s better. Dinner Second Night Ari: Mother Wolf, Fontainebleau An upscale Italian restaurant that honors Rome’s mythological origin story of Remus, Romulus, and the Lupa Capitolina, this is one of the most beautiful dining rooms you’ll find in all of Las Vegas. And while it’s Italian, everything on the menu is 10/10 good. Pasta? Pizza? Steak? Fish? There’s something for everyone, and the cocktails are out of this world. You will be hard-pressed to find a better dining experience anywhere else in America, let alone only in Las Vegas. Andy: Barry’s Downtown Prime, Circa Resort and Casino This is a classic, old-school steakhouse that will make you feel like you’ve stepped back into a more glamorous age. Want to go big? Order the dry-aged tomahawk ribeye. And make sure to order whole main lobster mac ’n cheese for the table. (That tomahawk is all yours.) Sportsbook To Watch The Evening Slate Ari: Fountainebleu Sportsbook Because you just left dinner at the Fontainebleau, you won’t have to go far. Though there are a ton of sportsbooks in Las Vegas that vary in size and vibe, the Fontainebleau does an incredible job. The sportsbook is integrated with The Tavern, which gives it a dining-forward layout rather than the feel of a betting hall. It feels more like a sports bar. The layout has open sightlines to all the televisions, there’s a great wraparound bar, and hospitality is more reliable than at other books. Grab a drink and settle in for endings of the big-time afternoon games and the beginnings of Big Ten slogs like Iowa-Northwestern. Andy:

articles.title: Garth Brooks Sexual Assault Accuser Wins Court Ruling in Bid to Stay Anonymous
articles.summary: The ruling overturns an earlier decision that noted Brooks had already revealed her name: "We are not persuaded that the proverbial cat is out of the bag here."
articles._body: A woman who accused Garth Brooks of sexual assault can potentially keep her real name hidden, a federal appeals court has ruled. The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit overturned a trial judge’s ruling last year that Jane Roe must use her real name in the litigation, which centers on her accusations that the country star assaulted her while she worked for him as a hairstylist. Related Garth Brooks Reveals Name Of Sexual Assault Accuser In New Legal Filing Kenny MacPherson, Veteran Music Publisher and Big Deal Music Co-Founder, Dies at 71 Diddy Moved From New Jersey Prison to Similar Facility in Pennsylvania The lower judge had ruled that her need for privacy was “weakened” because the “cat” was already “out of the bag” after Brooks publicly disclosed her name in court filings and she accidentally included it in another. But in its decision Wednesday (Nov. 4), the appeals court said that’s not how it should work. “We are not persuaded that the proverbial cat is out of the bag here,” the appeals court wrote in the ruling, obtained by Billboard . “Internet sleuths might speculate that Roe is a particular person [but that is] not the same as a public broadcasting of Roe’s certain identity.” Neither side’s attorneys immediately returned requests for comment on Thursday (Nov. 5). The accuser filed her claims against Brooks in Los Angeles court in October 2024, claiming he exposed her to “appalling sexual conduct,” including an alleged incident in which she says he raped her during a May 2019 stay in a Los Angeles hotel room. Brooks has vehemently denied the allegations , calling them “lies” aimed at forcing him to pay “hush money.” Weeks before that case was filed, Brooks had quietly filed his own preemptive lawsuit in Mississippi federal court under a John Doe pseudonym, accusing an unnamed Jane Roe of extorting him with threats of a public lawsuit. After she filed her case in Los Angeles, Brooks refiled his own lawsuit with her real name listed. The move quickly sparked outrage from the accuser’s attorneys, who immediately moved to reseal her name and seek legal penalties against Brooks. They also asked the media not to disclose the name, and Billboard abided by that request. Last year, the judge overseeing the federal case in Mississippi ruled that Roe was not entitled to proceed under a pseudonym. He cited the fact that her name had already been disclosed, both by Brooks and in an inadvertent filing in the California case. But in Wednesday’s appeal decision, the Fifth Circuit said those disclosures did not mean Roe was less entitled to use a pseudonym in a case dealing with issues of the “utmost intimacy.” “As to the fact that Roe’s name was a matter of public record for short periods, that was either because of Doe’s actions (which Roe objected to), or Roe’s inadvertent disclosures which counsel corrected,” the appeals court wrote. “In sum, we agree that Roe’s privacy interest … should not be weakened for these reasons.” The ruling was not an outright reversal, and did not order the lower court to allow Roe to keep her name shielded. Instead, it merely said the trial judge analyzed the situation incorrectly and should reconsider in light of the appellate court’s decision: “We express no view on the ultimate outcome of this issue.” The ruling might finally allow for progress in the litigation over the accusations against Brooks, which has been largely stalled for more than two years and remains in the earliest stages. The Mississippi case will proceed first, followed by the Los Angeles lawsuit.

articles.title: Weezer’s Biggest Billboard Chart Hits: ‘Buddy Holly,’ ‘Beverly Hills’ & More
articles.summary: The group has charted nine No. 1s among 23 top 10s on Billboard’s Alternative Airplay chart.
articles._body: More than three decades after “Undone – The Sweater Song” introduced Weezer to rock radio — and to Billboard ’s charts — the band is still collecting Alternative Airplay hits. Weezer’s Wednesday collaboration, “We Might as Well Be Strangers,” topped the chart dated Oct. 31, 2026, becoming the band’s ninth No. 1. Weezer has placed 36 songs on the chart since 1994, including 23 top 10s. Its biggest hits have arrived in waves, from its 1990s breakthrough to a steady run of leaders in the 2020s. The group’s chart history began with “Undone,” which reached No. 6 in August 1994. “Buddy Holly” hit No. 2 that December and “Say It Ain’t So” rose to No. 7 in August 1995, cementing the band as an alt-rock force. Weezer kept charting through the late 1990s and returned to No. 2 with “Hash Pipe” in 2001. Its first No. 1 arrived in 2005: “Beverly Hills.” The song became a crossover smash, reaching No. 10 on the Billboard Hot 100 (the band’s only top 10 on the all-genre, multimetric chart) and No. 2 on Pop Airplay. “Perfect Situation” led Alternative Airplay in 2006 and “Pork and Beans” ruled for 11 weeks in 2008. The following year, “(If You’re Wondering If I Want You To) I Want You To” reached No. 2, spending 37 weeks on the chart, the most for a song by the band to that point. After 2010s hits including “Back to the Shack” (No. 5, 2014) and “Feels Like Summer” (No. 2, 2017), a fan-driven cover of Toto’s “Africa” topped the chart in August 2018. It kicked off a remarkable streak of No. 1s this decade: “Hero” (2020); “All My Favorite Songs” (2021), over a career-best 43-week chart run; “A Little Bit of Love” (2022); and “Records” (2023). 2026 brought a revived hit and a new one. “Go Away,” a 2014 duet with Best Coast’s Bethany Cosentino, went viral on TikTok. It entered the Hot 100 in March, the band’s first appearance there since “Africa” and reached No. 3 on Alternative Airplay in June. Then “We Might as Well Be Strangers,” a duet with Wednesday’s Karly Hartzman from Weezer’s 2026 self-titled LP (aka the Gold Album), returned the Rivers Cuomo-fronted act to the top. Reflecting more than three decades of chart success, below Billboard counts down Weezer’s 25 biggest Alternative Airplay hits. Weezer’s Biggest Billboard Hits chart is based on performance on Billboard’s weekly Alternative Airplay chart through the Nov. 7, 2026, ranking. Songs are ranked based on an inverse point system, with weeks at No. 1 earning the greatest value and weeks at lower ranks earning less. Due to changes in chart methodology over the years, eras are weighted to account for different chart turnover rates over various periods.

articles._body: The Cleveland Browns have some injuries to deal with as the 2026 NFL season reaches its ninth week of action. Among the notable players on the team’s injury report ahead of its Week 9 showdown against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome in New Orleans is tight end Harold Fannin Jr. The second-year pro has been arguably the most important weapon downfield for Cleveland this season , but the team is facing the possibility of missing Fannin for the game in the Big Easy. The Bowling Green Falcons product popped up on the Browns’ injury report on Thursday with a lower-body issue, though he was able to practice in limited fashion with the team. “Browns TE Harold Fannin Jr. was added to the injury report and limited with a groin injury. A groin injury prematurely ended his rookie season and kept him sidelined for much of the offseason workout program,” Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN shared via a social media post on X, formerly Twitter. Hopefully, this is nothing but a bit of maintenance on the part of the Browns, but it is still a reasonable cause for concern that Fannin is on the injury report this close to the matchup versus Tyler Shough and the Saints on the road. Fannin still has a chance to practice in full and remove any doubts about his status for Sunday’s game, so his situation is worth monitoring, especially given his importance to the Browns’ attack. A third-round pick by the Browns in the 2025 NFL Draft, Fannin is leading the team so far this season with 411 receiving yards to go along with three touchdowns on 35 receptions and 51 targets through eight games. articles._body: Hunter Henry hasn’t made progress in his injury recovery, presenting question marks for the New England Patriots ahead of their Week 9 matchup this weekend. Henry has been playing in the NFL since 2016, going through his sixth season with the Patriots. He stands out as one of the better veteran tight ends in the league, helping New England make a deep playoff run to Super Bowl 60 last season. However, Henry suffered a foot injury during the Patriots’ win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 8. It has impacted him enough to the point that he has been absent from practices for two consecutive days , per reporter Mike Reiss. “TE Hunter Henry, who was limited to eight snaps Sunday after injuring his foot, is absent from practice for the second day in a row,” Reiss wrote on Thursday. What lies ahead for Hunter Henry, Patriots It is tough news for the Patriots to get regarding Hunter Henry. They await his full recovery from the foot injury, looking to other options if he isn’t ready for Week 9. Henry has settled in as one of Drake Maye’s top targets, having reached 85 targets, 60 catches and 650 yards each of the past two seasons. This year, he has caught 29 passes for 326 yards and two touchdowns in a balanced New England attack. New England has a 5-3 record this season, sitting at second place in the AFC East Division standings. They are above the New York Jets and the Miami Dolphins while trailing the Buffalo Bills. In terms of the conference standings, they are seventh place. They lead over the Cleveland Browns and the Las Vegas Raiders while being under the Cincinnati Bengals and the Kansas City Chiefs. The Patriots will continue preparations for their upcoming matchup this weekend, being at home. They host the Green Bay Packers in Week 9 as kickoff commences on Nov. 8 at 4:25 p.m. ET. articles._body: Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten appears likely to play Thursday night against the Baltimore Ravens despite ankle and foot injuries that kept him out of practice all week. Tuten, the Jaguars’ leading rusher , carried a questionable designation into Thursday after head coach Liam Coen labeled him a game-time decision. Jacksonville planned to evaluate how he responded during a pregame workout before making a final call on his availability. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler provided the strongest indication yet on X, formerly Twitter, that Tuten is trending toward playing. “Jaguars RB Bhayshul Tuten (questionable, ankle/foot) ‘should be’ good for TNF vs Ravens barring any pregame setbacks, per source.” Tuten injured his ankle and foot during Jacksonville’s 42-7 Week 8 win over the Indianapolis Colts but still delivered one of his best performances of the season. He finished with 159 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns, including 104 rushing yards on 16 carries. The performance made Tuten the first Jaguars player since Maurice Jones-Drew in 2007 to record at least 100 rushing yards, 50 receiving yards and multiple touchdowns in the same game. Jacksonville kept Tuten out of practice throughout the short week, creating uncertainty around his status. If Tuten suffers a setback before kickoff or Jacksonville limits his workload, Chris Rodriguez Jr. could take on a larger backfield role. The Jaguars enter Thursday night at 5-2 and atop the AFC South after consecutive wins. The Ravens enter Thursday at 4-4 and plan to start rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano. articles.title: Asia can’t afford a ‘cloudless’ day. That means paying attention to undersea cables
articles.summary: More than 99% of all international data is carried not by satellites but by a physical backbone of subsea cables.
articles._body: Picture a “cloudless” day—not in the meteorological sense, but one in which digital operations come to a sudden, catastrophic halt. Financial transactions stall. AI applications lose access to data. Supply chains slow, and customer experiences suffer. It may sound improbable, yet recent events suggest otherwise. In 2024, subsea cable damage caused widespread internet outages that disrupted banks, fintech platforms and cloud-based businesses across Africa; in 2025, Red Sea cable cuts severely disrupted access across Asia and the Middle East. Internet traffic was rerouted through longer paths, increasing latency for cloud services and adding costs for businesses reliant on real-time digital operations. These incidents are a reminder that what we call “the cloud” is neither virtual nor invincible. We often imagine it floating somewhere above us. In reality, it lies at the bottom of the ocean: More than 99% of all international data is carried not by satellites but by a physical backbone of subsea cables. The regional digital economy runs uninterrupted only because companies made continuous, heavy investment in critical transit hubs like India and Singapore. AI is placing unprecedented demands on the cloud, the foundation of today’s digital economy. AI workloads and hyperscale data centres need ever-greater bandwidth—with 400 gigabits (gbps) per second now the baseline and 800 gbps already emerging. As countries and businesses race to scale AI, much of the focus has been on compute and data centres. But the networks connecting those systems need to keep pace as well. That raises a critical question for Asia: is the region overlooking a key AI infrastructure bottleneck? Without sufficient investment in subsea cables and end-to-end networks, businesses could spend heavily on AI infrastructure only to see the returns eroded by disruption, higher operating costs and unreliable access to data. For the C-suite, that presents a looming crisis : while AI investment is a board-level strategic priority for 77% of enterprise leaders, 65% of enterprises continue to operate on legacy or still-developing infrastructure, according to a Tata Communications study. With AI workloads making global traffic patterns increasingly unpredictable, enterprises need dynamic, flexible data-centre-to-data-centre connectivity that can scale rapidly with demand to protect the bottom line and operational stability. Meeting this need will require continued investment from network providers in the infrastructure and capabilities needed to deliver scalable, resilient connectivity. Most discussions of Singapore’s AI ambitions revolve around compute capacity, talent and regulation. Those are all important. But they overlook what happens when the data that AI systems depend on cannot be transmitted quickly, reliably or securely.  Singapore and India are emerging as two of the region’s most important data transit hubs, underpinned by their strategic locations and growing digital infrastructure. Singapore serves as a gateway to Southeast Asia, with one of the world’s densest concentrations of data centres. Meanwhile, India acts as a link between Asia, the Middle East and Europe, supported by major cable landing points and expanding data centre capacity in cities such as Mumbai and Chennai. Together, these strengths make both countries important hubs for international data traffic, underscoring the need for resilient and diverse connectivity routes to keep data moving efficiently between major financial centres and commercial workloads. The industry needs to rethink how it approaches network architecture. For decades, infrastructure was built to support predictable, linear traffic. Today, infrastructure must now accommodate increasingly volatile AI-driven data demands. This requires better integration  between subsea cables, terrestrial fibre and individual data centres, as a bottleneck at a coastal landing station can immediately negate the speed of a transoceanic cable. However, keeping these cables secure and running requires far more than laying fiber in the ocean. True resilience demands a coordinated focus across four dimensions: capacity planning, network diversity, protection and repair readiness, and disciplined lifecycle operations. This behind-the-scenes management—including robust monitoring, strategic spares management, tight integration of subsea and terrestrial networks, and clearly defined long-term governance—is what ensures a single cable cut does not become a regional blackout. Crucially, this industry-led push is now being reinforced by public policy. The recent adoption of the Enhanced ASEAN Guidelines for Strengthening Resilience and Repair of Submarine Cables—which recommends capping repair processing times at 10 days—is a vital step forward. Regional policymakers are making rapid repair readiness of economic stability. For businesses,  the practical consequence is a change in what gets funded. Compute and data centres often take priority in investment decisions because their capacity and returns are visible. Meanwhile, the cables, landing stations and alternative routes that keep them connected are less visible, and can be harder to justify as investments in their own right. Yet, the trade-off is clear: underinvestment in connectivity risks leaving expensive AI infrastructure vulnerable to disruption, congestion and higher operating costs. Connectivity must be treated as an essential and strategic asset not simply an operational cost hidden in the IT budget. The cloud begins beneath the ocean. As AI adoption accelerates, Singapore’s competitiveness as a global digital hub will depend on the strength of that invisible lifeline beneath the sea. articles._body: When Michigan was searching for a new head coach, Biff Poggi was a serious candidate. He served as the interim following Sherrone Moore’s firing, and he thought he was going to get the full-time gig before it went to Kyle Whittingham . “I was a finalist, it came down to me and Kyle,” Poggi said on an appearance on The Stadium & Main Show earlier this week . $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Poggi said that he had four really good interviews, and he was given positive feedback at the time. But when he didn’t get the job, it was a hard transition. “It was hard because I really thought I was going to get it,” said Poggi. “I had four interviews, they all went really well, I was getting really positive feedback from the search guy. It was all going very well. We were also the players’ favorite, and that doesn’t always mean that that’s the right thing. But what was disappointing was that I wasn’t going to be around those kids anymore. “And then you quickly transition to, ‘Well, too bad. Who cares? You’re an old fart, who cares about what you think? You’ve got to support this program now because these are the kids you care about and you can’t be, like, putting a divorce into the family. You’ve got to jump all in and support this guy. And that’s what I tried to do.” Watch on Fubo (Try for Free) Michigan went 2-1 under Poggi’s guidance in 2025. The first two came early in the season, when he filled in for Moore as he served a suspension in September. Poggi and the Wolverines won both of those games against Central Michigan and Nebraska. He was promoted to interim head coach again in December when Moore was fired. Michigan went on to face Texas in the Citrus Bowl, losing 41-27. Poggi has had multiple stints in Ann Arbor. He was an analyst in 2016, and returned as associate head coach from 2021-2022. He then got the Charlotte head coaching job, where he spent the 2023-2024 seasons before being fired and returning to the Wolverines in 2025. At Charlotte, Poggi was 6-16 overall. The 49ers went 3-9 (2-6 in the American) in 2023 and 3-7 (2-4 in the American) in 2024 before he was let go. Whittingham came to Michigan after a long career at Utah. This season has been a bit of a mixed bag, with offensive struggles overshadowing a strong defense. The Wolverines are 5-3 on the season and 2-3 in Big Ten play so far.

articles.summary:

I started working on this in January wanting to have a better environment to write TLA+ specs and model check them. I started out with running TLC via CheerpJ ht
articles._body: Bisimia is a browser-based local-first environment to write and model-check TLA+ specs. I started working on this in January wanting to have a better environment to write TLA+ specs and model check them. I started out with running TLC via CheerpJ https://cheerpj.com/ (which I later on found out to be the approach taken by https://learning.tlapl.us/ ), however after many days and nights I've abandoned this for a few reasons, the most prominent of which is performance. Now we use GraalVM https://www.graalvm.org/ and some magic around it to achieve a median improvement of 22×, with speedups reaching nearly 70× compared to CheerpJ. The goal here was to run the real TLC (and be bug-for-bug compatible) and not re-implement things (which is the approach taken for example by https://will62794.github.io/spectacle/ ). articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens recently opted to shake things up by trading for quarterback Jacoby Brissett of the Arizona Cardinals. The move comes amid the Ravens’ turbulence at the position of late, with both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley going down with injuries in Sunday’s loss to the Bu
articles._body: The Baltimore Ravens recently opted to shake things up by trading for quarterback Jacoby Brissett of the Arizona Cardinals. The move comes amid the Ravens’ turbulence at the position of late, with both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley going down with injuries in Sunday’s loss to the Buffalo Bills. Now, the Ravens have made another move at the quarterback position, in addition to other roster transactions. “We have signed QB Austin Reed to the 53-man roster and placed QBs Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley on injured reserve. We have also elevated OLB Adisa Isaac and kicker Jake Moody from the practice squad (standard elevations) for tonight’s game,” reported the Ravens’ official team account on X, formerly Twitter. Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network later reported on X that “Austin Reed will be the backup tonight, with Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley on IR.” Starting for the Ravens on Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars will be Joe Fagnano, who finished the game on Sunday in Buffalo in what turned out to be a blowout loss. However, Brissett is expected to get the starting job going forward once the trade is finalized later on, as he recently lost his starting job in Arizona to Gardner Minshew after the latter’s excellent game vs the Dallas Cowboys over the weekend. The Ravens currently sit at 4-4 on the season, and the hope is that Brissett will be able to keep the team above water while they hope for good news on the Jackson front. In any case, the Ravens will next hit the field on Thursday evening at home against the Jaguars, with kickoff set for 8:15 pm ET. articles._body: The Philadelphia Phillies’ need for right-handed offense is drawing attention early in free agency, with two established outfielders emerging as suggested additions to their lineup. Philadelphia finished last in OPS from right-handed hitters in 2026, according to MLB Network Radio. That ranking provides the backdrop for a discussion about strengthening the Phillies’ offense through the open market. The segment focused on players who finished the season with the Seattle Mariners and Chicago Cubs, respectively. Both now face qualifying-offer decisions that could determine whether they remain with those organizations for another year. MLB Network Radio shared host Mike Ferrin’s assessment Thursday on X, formerly Twitter, underscoring the connection between Philadelphia’s offensive shortcoming and available outfield talent. “Randy’s going to get paid, and he’s going to be a really good addition for somebody… The Phillies. Oh my God, the Phillies could use Randy Arozarena. Phillies could use Seiya Suzuki.” The #Phillies finished LAST in OPS from right-handed hitters in 2026. Does free agency have the fix? #RingTheBell https://t.co/iXax8hx4iO pic.twitter.com/9uKiwk20cE — MLB Network Radio on SiriusXM (@MLBNetworkRadio) November 5, 2026 Arozarena, 31, hit .281 with a .381 on-base percentage, 26 home runs and 79 RBIs for the Mariners. He also stole 26 bases, contributing on the bases alongside his offensive production. Suzuki finished with a .270/.368/.473 slash line, 26 home runs and 86 RBIs across 143 regular-season games for Chicago. His on-base percentage and slugging percentage combined for an .841 OPS. The Mariners and Cubs extended one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offers to Arozarena and Suzuki on Monday. Each player has until November 17 to accept or decline. Acceptance would keep a player with his current team under that contract. Declining would preserve the opportunity to negotiate a different agreement, including a potential return to the same club. Ferrin’s comments present possible fits rather than establish contact between Philadelphia and either player. The clip does not identify an offer, contract demand or active negotiation at this early stage. For now, both players have qualifying offers pending, and the Phillies’ next outfield move remains unresolved. articles.title: Patriots’ AJ Brown, TreVeyon Henderson among players to not practice Thursday
articles.summary: The New England Patriots will be facing the Green Bay Packers this week, and there is a chance that they won’t have two of their key offensive players. AJ Brown and TreVeyon Henderson didn’t practice yesterday, and it looks like it’ll be a second day in a row they’re not o
articles._body: The New England Patriots will be facing the Green Bay Packers this week, and there is a chance that they won’t have two of their key offensive players. AJ Brown and TreVeyon Henderson didn’t practice yesterday , and it looks like it’ll be a second day in a row they’re not on the field, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. “No practice again today for AJ Brown and TreVeyon Henderson,” Schefter wrote X, formerly Twitter. If Brown and Henderson are not able to practice tomorrow, there is a good chance that they won’t be able to suit up for the matchup. That’s not the best news for the Patriots, especially with them being two of their top offensive weapons. Brown was out last week for the Patriots as he deals with a nagging knee injury, and he hasn’t had much of an opportunity to get into a rhythm with Drake Maye due to his absence. Henderson also didn’t play last week as he’s dealing with an illness. He’s another player who hasn’t been able to play much this season, and Rhamondre Stevenson has taken over the backfield. The good news for the Patriots is that they may be able to get Mack Hollins back after he’s missed the past few games with a calf injury. He’s been limited at practice this week, and if he can log one more, he should be good to go for the game. Even despite the injuries, the Patriots have been able to win three of their last four games, and Drake Maye is making things work with what he has. The defense has also given the team a lift, which has been key to their success. articles.title: Jason Kidd sends urgent demand to Heat player he used to coach with Mavericks
articles.summary: Former Dallas Mavericks head coach Jason Kidd has a clear message for Miami Heat guard Tim Hardaway Jr. as the team looks to overcome its early-season shooting struggles. During his debut appearance on ESPN’s “NBA Today” on Thursday, Kidd urged Hardaway to improve his perimeter
articles._body: Former Dallas Mavericks head coach Jason Kidd has a clear message for Miami Heat guard Tim Hardaway Jr. as the team looks to overcome its early-season shooting struggles. During his debut appearance on ESPN’s “NBA Today” on Thursday, Kidd urged Hardaway to improve his perimeter shooting after a disappointing start to the 2026-27 season. The comments came as ESPN’s Brian Windhorst discussed Miami’s offseason additions and the importance of outside shooting to the team’s success. “They really tried to load up on shooters. Signed THJ, and Klay Thompson. They haven’t been hitting shots,” Windhorst said. “You say they get to top 10 defense, I agree with you. I think they do improve dramatically. If they don’t start making outside shots, they’re gonna have to be one of the greatest defenses of all time.” Kidd, who previously coached both Hardaway and Thompson in Dallas, emphasized the importance of getting more consistent production from his former players. Jason Kidd and Brian Windhorst say Tim Hardaway Jr has to start knocking down some shots: Windy: They really tried to load up on shooters. Signed THJ, and Klay Thompson. They haven’t been hitting shots. You say they get to top 10 defense, I agree with you. I think they improve… https://t.co/QaiJIlj0ur pic.twitter.com/UdsSYeIA3s — Heat Central (@TheHeatCentral) November 5, 2026 “I just think that understanding Klay that’s a big one, going back home,” Kidd said. “They gotta get Timmy. Timmy has to start knocking down some shots.” Tim Hardaway Jr. struggling to find his shooting touch with Heat Hardaway, 34, has struggled offensively through his first eight appearances with Miami, averaging just 5.8 points and 1.6 rebounds in 16.9 minutes per game. The veteran guard is shooting 30.4% from the field, 26.5% from 3-point range and 69.2% from the free-throw line, putting him on pace for career lows in several statistical categories. Miami signed Hardaway to provide additional perimeter scoring and floor spacing alongside Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo. However, his inability to consistently convert outside shots has limited his offensive impact. Hardaway previously played under Kidd in Dallas before continuing his career elsewhere. His familiarity with Kidd’s coaching approach makes the former Mavericks coach’s assessment particularly notable. Meanwhile, Thompson delivered a much-needed offensive boost Wednesday night, scoring 30 points and connecting on eight 3-pointers in Miami’s 117-116 overtime victory over the Los Angeles Clippers . Thompson also knocked down the game-winning 3-pointer as the Heat overcame a 20-point deficit to secure their third victory of the season. The Heat (3-5) will look to build on Wednesday’s victory when they face the Golden State Warriors (5-3) , who enter Thursday night’s matchup riding a five-game winning streak. The game is scheduled for 10 p.m. ET on NBA TV. For Hardaway, the upcoming stretch presents another opportunity to regain his shooting rhythm and establish himself as a reliable contributor in Miami’s rotation. As Kidd made clear, the Heat need more from their veteran guard if they hope to maximize the offensive potential of their revamped roster. articles.title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $76,000 as Nasdaq Tumbles into Correction
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $76,000 as Nasdaq Tumbles into Correction Bitcoin price traded near $76,000 on Thursday afternoon, down more than 5% on the day after sliding through the mid-$75,000s as a Nasdaq-led selloff in chip and AI stocks deepened into a formal correction and forced out more than $1 billion in leveraged bets, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows. The afternoon session extended the morning crash that had already erased overnight gains above $80,000. Bitcoin briefly tested support near $75,400 before stabilizing just under $76,000 into the final hour of U.S. cash trading. Bitcoin near $75,900 in afternoon trade, on track for its biggest single-day slide since June. The move undid Wednesday’s short-squeeze bounce in a single session. Traders who bought the midterm rebound with borrowed money were the first forced out when stocks cracked at the open, and the bitcoin price never regained the $77,000 area that held as morning support. Nasdaq’s correction pulls crypto lower Wall Street set the tone. The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5% on Thursday and dropped into correction territory, more than 10% below the record close it set last month, CNBC reported. The S&P 500 lost roughly 4%, and the Dow shed more than 1,600 points. Semiconductors led the rout. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index sank about 11%, and the iShares Semiconductor ETF posted its biggest one-day drop since March 2020. Nvidia and Broadcom each fell around 9%, Qualcomm lost about 9% and Tesla dropped about 11%. Investors are pricing in a slower AI data-center buildout under a Democratic Congress. Traders fear construction pauses and tighter financing for neoclouds, a risk that has weighed on chip and infrastructure names since the midterm results. Analysts told CNBC that the $1.2 trillion of AI capital spending forecast for next year is now being reworked. Bitcoin has moved with that AI-heavy complex for most of the year. Miners that sold bitcoin to fund data centers are now caught in both trades, so political risk on power and construction hits the same names that used to trade mainly on the bitcoin price. Leverage flush grows past $1 billion Forced selling kept the bitcoin price under pressure into the afternoon. Roughly $1.08 billion in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, including about $954 million in long bets, as futures markets unwound positions built during Wednesday’s short squeeze. Nearly $900 million of that wipeout came in a roughly four-hour stretch after the U.S. open, turning a stock-led break into a cascade of margin calls. Ether fell below $2,300 as the same leverage flushed out. Crypto equities followed. Strategy (MSTR), Coinbase (COIN) and Circle (CRCL) each fell more than 10%, and bitcoin miners dropped as much as 20%. Keel Infrastructure (KEEL), which sold its entire bitcoin treasury for $192 million, slid about 20%. CleanSpark (CLSK), Cipher (CIFR) and TeraWulf (WULF) each lost more than 12%. What comes next for bitcoin price The next test is Friday’s October jobs report, then October CPI on Nov. 10 and the Fed’s Dec. 9 decision. Policy risk is building too, with House Democrats drafting their own market structure bill ahead of taking the committees in January. Traders are watching whether the bitcoin price can hold the mid-$75,000 area that served as support on election night and several times since August. A clean break would leave bitcoin with room to run lower, near its weakest levels in months and put the September low back in view. Options markets have been quiet into the jobs print, but the cash market is not. Volume stayed elevated through the afternoon as stocks and crypto sold together rather than against each other. At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $75,900. articles.title: Google: Schools can keep search while skipping Gemini, but AI search is non-negotiable
articles.summary: Google is technically offering schools more choice but not the choices anyone wants.
articles._body: Google faced the ire of educators and parents earlier this week when it announced a new AI policy for K–12 schools . Google said that it developed its new approach to give schools more control, but early reporting also suggested Google would block search access for schools that didn't want to use AI. Google didn't see the backlash coming, but now that it's here, the search giant is clarifying what exactly its new policy means and what's changing. The gist of the new policy, according to Google's blog post, is that schools using Google apps will have to opt into its AI products going forward. Since the company considers search part of its AI portfolio (Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Search), schools have to specifically turn that on for logged-in student accounts. When Google revealed its new policy, the company's VP for education spoke exclusively to The New York Times , which interpreted the situation as Google will "turn off search" if schools reject AI. This has a nefarious vibe, but it's probably not the most accurate way to describe how Google's educational AI system will operate. Google's approach may not be entirely altruistic, but it technically offers schools more choice and control than they have now. Instead of Google turning off search, it will let schools make that decision based on their internal AI policies. Read full article Comments

articles.title: Lawsuit: Man introduced his wife to ChatGPT. She used it to plan his murder.
articles.summary: Bitter energy drinks turned out to be ChatGPT-steered poisoning, lawsuit says.
articles._body: ChatGPT allegedly helped a North Carolina woman, Cheryl Gates, craft a “personalized plan” to poison her husband, James, after fueling her delusions that he planned to divorce her and leave her with nothing. A grand jury indicted Cheryl Gates on charges of attempted first-degree murder and food contamination in October. About a week prior, the accusations that ChatGPT was a co-conspirator in the attempted murder came in a lawsuit filed in San Francisco County Superior Court that was made public this week. In it, James Gates alleged that OpenAI and Sam Altman failed to employ technical safeguards to shut down Cheryl’s chats even after her queries became “obviously suspicious” and sought advice on how to execute and conceal a homicide. At first, Cheryl told ChatGPT that she was researching poisoning out of fear that her husband might possibly try to kill her—framing her queries as “self-protection.” Coming to the rescue, ChatGPT did not terminate the conversation. Instead, it helped her “with specific instructions for the preparation, dosage, and administration of Oleander, including whether anti-nausea medicine would accelerate or inhibit death, whether it would show on an autopsy report, and whether it could be injected into a vein or muscle instead of being ingested in tea and have the same lethal effect,” the lawsuit said. Get the First Look Into Newly Remodeled Las Vegas Clubbing Institution XS
articles.summary: The grand reopening of the club at Wynn Las Vegas happens Nov. 5-8 with Rüfüs du Sol, The Chainsmokers, Calvin Harris and Diplo b2b Hugel.
articles._body: XS at Wynn Las Vegas has been a nightlife institution on the Strip since it opened 18 years ago. Now, the club has gotten a shiny (literally) new remodel ahead of its grand reopening this weekend. The club has been closed since August for a remodel that includes a glitzy, chrome- and gold-drenched look, custom audio and lighting tech designed and engineered exclusively for XS. The new space is outfitted with a bespoke constellation of 1,200 moving pendants that exist within an overhead installation, making the architecture shift its appearance throughout the night. This is XS’s first-ever remodel (although in 2015 it did debut $10 million worth of new lighting, sound effects and technology) and comes ahead of a reopening weekend (Nov. 5-8) with sets by Rüfüs du Sol , The Chainsmokers , Calvin Harris and Diplo b2b Hugel . See exclusive photos of the reimagined XS below. “The new XS is not a departure from its legacy. It’s the next chapter of it,” Michael Wood, the vp of creative at Wynn Design & Development, says in a statement. “We’re taking everything people remember about XS, the glamour, the fantasy, the sense of spectacle, and asking what those ideas mean for the next generation of nightlife.” “XS has long been synonymous with the very best of Las Vegas nightlife, setting a standard for entertainment and energy,” adds Adam Norotsky, vice president of nightlife at Wynn Las Vegas. “With this reimagining, we saw an opportunity to build on that legacy and deliver even more of what guests love about XS, including a stage that regularly welcomes some of the most sought-after talent in the world. Our goal was to create an unforgettable night out, where world-class music, standout performances and a lively atmosphere come together for an experience guests will want to return to again and again. We look forward to welcoming them back.” Encompassing 40,000 square feet, XS can host up to 1,840 guests in its indoor area and up to 3,121 guests with its outdoor areas. Upon opening in December 2008, the club became crucial in establishing Las Vegas as a new global destination for dance music, helping bring DJ fees to new heights and establishing DJs as a new type of superstar artist. articles.summary: It's been a rocky week for the global girl group.
articles._body: KATSEYE have postponed two more concerts. Related KATSEYE Postpones Detroit Concert Due to Illness KATSEYE Reveal Dates For 2026 Wildworld Global Arena Tour KATSEYE’s ‘WILD’ New EP: All Six Tracks Ranked On Thursday (Nov. 5), the official Instagram pages for Chicago’s United Center and Minneapolis’ Target Center shared statements announcing the postponement of the global girl group’s ongoing Wildworld Tour. “We’re sorry to share that tonight’s KATSEYE show at the United Center has been postponed due to Megan’s illness,” read the United Center statement, which also confirmed that purchased tickets and VIP packages will be valid for the yet-to-be-announced rescheduled date. “Please do not travel to the venue, as doors will not open for tonight’s show.” Around the same time, Target Center posted an identical statement — save for the guidance to not travel to the venue — regarding the group’s previously scheduled Nov. 7 show. On Tuesday (Nov. 3), the group postponed their show at Michigan’s Little Caesar’s arena, with sources at the show noting that KATSEYE did a VIP soundcheck without Megan present. At press time, none of the four touring KATSEYE members have posted on their personal Instagram profiles addressing the postponements. Manon Bannerman and Sophia Laforteza are currently still on hiatus. KATSEYE’s Wildworld Tour commenced on Sept. 1 at Dublin’s 3Arena. The group completed a nine-date European leg before kicking off their North American leg on Oct. 13 at Miami’s Kaseya Center. When the group resumes their trek, KATSEYE will play arenas through the remainder of 2026, ending the year with two dates at Mexico City’s Palacio de los Deportes. After a two-month break, at the top of next year, the ladies will bring their tour to Asia and Australia for 14 more shows. Promoted by Live Nation, the sprawling tour supports the group’s WILD EP, which debuted atop the Billboard 200 and spawned the Billboard Hot 100 top 40 hits “Animal” (No. 24), “Pinky Up” (No. 28) and “Hootie Frutti” (No. 31). WILD is the official follow-up to the group’s Beautiful Chaos EP, which soared to No. 4 on the Billboard 200 and earned the ladies two Grammy nominations: best new artist and best pop duo/group performance for “Gabriela.” Read the statements from United Center and Target Center concerning KATSEYE’s postponed shows below. articles.title: Record-High Attendance Drives Live Nation Revenue Up Nearly 20%
articles.summary: More concertgoers at venues outside North America and greater attendance at stadiums post-World Cup provided a big boost in the third quarter.
articles._body: A record-high 61 million fans attended Live Nation events during the company’s third fiscal quarter, as strong attendance globally and more stadium concerts in the U.S. drove the number of concertgoers and revenue up 19%, the company reported Thursday (Nov. 5). The world’s largest live entertainment company generated $10.1 billion in revenue, driven by a record-high $8.7 billion from its concerts business in the quarter ending Sept. 30. In addition to a nearly 30% year-over-year increase in international audiences, U.S. stadiums that were occupied by the FIFA World Cup from May to July held more concerts in the months following the soccer contest, while September amphitheater attendance hit an all-time high. Concert attendance in North America overall was up 13%, helping generate $892 million in overall operating income. Related Why Live Nation Is Doubling Down on Latin America & How Indie Promoters Are Adjusting: ‘Surf the Wave’ Kenny MacPherson, Veteran Music Publisher and Big Deal Music Co-Founder, Dies at 71 Diddy Moved From New Jersey Prison to Similar Facility in Pennsylvania Demand for concert tickets remains strong. Ticket sales in October were up 20% from a year ago, with monthly ticket sales exceeding prior-year levels every month since January. “Artists are taking their music to more fans in more places than ever, and fans are showing up in record numbers,” Michael Rapino , Live Nation president/CEO, said in a statement. “Through October, we’ve sold 170 million tickets, up 13% and already ahead of all of last year. We now expect to welcome nearly 180 million fans in 2026.” The company’s 14% increase in adjusted operating income (AOI), for a total AOI of $1.14 billion, was driven by growth across Live Nation’s three main businesses, and it puts the company on the path to “sustain double-digit growth for years to come,” Rapino said. The Live Nation concerts business reported a record-high event-related deferred revenue of $3.8 billion, with more than 180 million fans set to attend future events. Live Nation has made international expansion a key pillar of its growth, and it’s on track to open or acquire 10 venues with more than 3,000 seats by the end of 2026. Those venues are expected to result in more than 5 million attendees this year, eventually rising to an 8 million run rate. The company’s Venue Nation division, which operates venues outside of North America, hosted 26 million fans in the third quarter, an increase of 17% from the year prior. Sponsorship revenue of $506 million was up 14% year over year, with 65% coming from international markets. AOI for the division is up 12% to $350 million, as international sponsorship surpassed North America as the greatest contributor to operating income and AOI for the quarter. Ticketmaster reported that revenue rose 9% to $870 million, with AOI up 10% to $316 million.

articles.summary: Here is Cerea, a self-hostable, open-source (Apache 2.0) chat+agent frontend for LLMs. It works alone with any OpenAI-compatible inference provider, but it's way better when coupled with the model gateway I'm also developing, Pystino (
articles._body: Here is Cerea, a self-hostable, open-source (Apache 2.0) chat+agent frontend for LLMs. It works alone with any OpenAI-compatible inference provider, but it's way better when coupled with the model gateway I'm also developing, Pystino ( https://github.com/paoloviviani/Pystino ). I came to this after struggling to find a hosted chat interface that was truly open source, that I really enjoyed to use, and that was simple enough to be shared and used by family. In particular, I was looking for something that could provide the smooth and integrated user experience of commercial products for the tasks needed by family (e.g., document editing, form filling, notes and knowledge management), but backed by open models hosted wherever I decide. Then it became richer, now supporting: remote coding agents (wrapping Opencode), delegation and coordination between agents, integration between chat/projects and code agents (this one to me is a pain point for Claude, which I use at work), projects, RAG, rich artifacts support, schedules, and more. You can try it yourself, either cloning the full repo and head to Cerea/kit, or just the deploy kit with a script ( https://github.com/paoloviviani/Cerea#quick-start ). It's just a docker compose with a ./configure script that helps to generate a sensible .env for the specific scenario. It works in the browser and as a PWA on mobile. articles._body: EtherPK (a markdown / wikilink based notes app) tasks are plain markdown, but the EtherPK client has built powerful functionality on top of markdown tasks, integrating a Kanban board and MCP server to allow you to manage your work in your notes and easily hand off with instruction and full task context to your AI Agent (e.g. Claude Code). A task in is a markdown checkbox line in your notes, written in any document, wherever and whenever the task or idea comes up. If you nest it under another task and it becomes that task's subtask. A Kanban board shows those lines as cards and keeps no copy of them, so moving a card edits the line. The task editor is a form over the same text, so a picture, a comment or a subtask you add there ends up as text in the note. articles.title: Fat Joe Reps for NYC With Big Apple-Flavored Tiny Desk Concert Featuring Jadakiss & Remy Ma: Watch
articles.summary: Joey Crack is one of the rare artists to receive a second Tiny Desk.
articles._body: Fat Joe is back at NPR for his second Tiny Desk Concert, which arrived on Thursday (Nov. 5). Joey Crack made sure to bring some friends with him, as Remy Ma , Jadakiss and Stove God Cooks brought the Big Apple flair down I-95 to Washington, D.C. Related Watch Cardi B Bring the Brash & Beauty to NPR for Unapologetic Tiny Desk Concert Watch Sampha’s Mesmerizing Tiny Desk Concert Fat Joe Hasn’t Seen NYC This Unified Since 9/11 Thanks to Knicks Finals Run Joe told NPR he wanted to “touch the third rail” with his return to NPR, making him join the short list of artists to notch a second Tiny Desk Concert. The Bronx rapper took it back to his roots and ran through 30 years’ worth of hits for the nine-track setlist. Fat Joe kicked things off by bringing out his Terror Squad sister Remy Ma for “Cocababy,” before heading into the Soul II Soul -sampling “(Ha Ha) Slow Down” and LL COOL J’s “I Shot Ya.” “Y’all bout to hear some f–kery in the background. We tryna get thrown out this b—h,” Joe proclaimed. Jadakiss — a fellow Tiny Desk alum — made his first two cameos for Ja Rule’s “New York.” Kiss took it back to his viral rant blasting Cam’ron at the 2021 Verzuz battle between The LOX and Dipset, which saw him shading Cam for moving out of NYC. Joey Crack made sure to big up his orange and blue ties with a “Knicks in five” shout-out, which has become a greeting around the Big Apple following the Knicks’ 2026 championship run. The NPR stage got a bit busy when Joe assembled Kiss, Remy and Stove God Cooks to assist on “The Aroma,” which landed on the Bronx native’s Organized Rhyme album in August. Stevie Mackey, who Joe hailed as “your favorite singer’s favorite singer,” stepped up from his backup vocalist duties to guest on “Feelin A Way” and fill in for J. Holiday on “I Won’t Tell.” Fat Joe saved his fastball for a strong close with a pair of timeless anthems, raising the roof for Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 smash “Lean Back” and “All the Way Up.” “Salute Tiny Desk, thank you so much,” Joe said before departing. To date, the 56-year-old has notched 20 entries on the Hot 100, including another two top 10 hits: “What’s Luv” featuring Ashanti as well as the Nelly -lifted “Get It Poppin’.” Watch Fat Joe’s Tiny Desk Concert below.

articles.summary: With the Seattle Seahawks coming off a disappointing loss to the Chicago Bears last Monday night, 34-17, the hope is to bounce back this Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, but the team will be without starting quarterback Sam Darnold. As Darnold will be without for the Seahawks against the Car
articles._body: With the Seattle Seahawks coming off a disappointing loss to the Chicago Bears last Monday night, 34-17, the hope is to bounce back this Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, but the team will be without starting quarterback Sam Darnold. As Darnold will be without for the Seahawks against the Cardinals, backup quarterback Drew Lock hasn’t been healthy as well, as he speaks about the elbow injury he’s been dealing with. Lock has been dealing with an elbow injury for multiple weeks after suffering the issue during a practice in the rain, where he was hurt to the point where he was the third quarterback on the depth chart. With him being in line to start Sunday, Lock says Thursday that his elbow injury is “doing a lot better.” “It’s doing good. I’m excited to be back out there. It felt great to get under center and rip some balls yesterday. So feels good,” Lock said, according to Greg Bell. “I’m going at it like a normal week. If the training staff want to pull it back a little bit, then let them make that decision. But I’m expecting to go take every rep,” Lock continued. Drew Lock says his injured elbow feels good, he’s letting it rip in practice this week to start Sunday vs Arizona. He also says he knew early in the #Seahawks ’ loss to the Bears Monday night that Sam Darnold was injured and off. @933KJR pic.twitter.com/IVQ6vvGZqT — Gregg Bell (@gbellseattle) November 5, 2026 Seahawks’ Drew Lock knew Sam Darnold was injured during Bears loss Lock has filled in before with the Seahawks this season, as early as Week 1 of the regular season in the win over the New England Patriots, where Darnold sustained a glute injury, leading to the backup playing in Week 2. Funny enough, Lock would start against the Cardinals in Week 2 and threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns, hoping to do the same on Sunday in place of Darnold, who is dealing with a quadriceps injury. Lock would say that he knew “pretty early” that Darnold was impacted by the injury on Monday, commending him for playing through it. At any rate, it remains to be seen how long Darnold will be without for Seattle, as the hope is that Lock can get healthier ahead of Sunday’s game against the Cardinals and keep the ship afloat. The Seahawks are 4-4 in the NFC West, putting them at second. The post Seahawks’ Drew Lock shares update on elbow with Sam Darnold already ruled out due to injury appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Tech stocks are suffering their biggest selloff since Covid, as investors see premature end to AI datacenter boom
articles.summary: Two days after voters overwhelmingly rejected data centers, the companies that make the chips, networking gear, and other tech for the facilities saw their stocks crushed.
articles._body: It may have been Blue Tsunami on Tuesday but it was a sea of red that washed over tech stocks on Thursday, covering everything from chips and datacenter companies to software and gig economy firms, as investors panicked that the U.S. midterm election results will bring the AI boom to a premature halt, or at least, a significant slowdown.  The tech-heavy Nasdaq was down more than 1,340 points, or 5.2% in midday trading, shedding more than $3 trillion in market cap, and representing its biggest daily drop since the Liberation Day tariff announcement in April 2025, according to Bloomberg data. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Sector index, which tracks the 30 largest companies in the chips business, was down more than 1,000 points—on track for its single biggest day loss since March 2020.  Some of the biggest names in tech took it on the chin, with Facebook parent company Meta down 3.4%, Microsoft down 2.8%, and Nvidia down 8%.  Thursday’s selloff dragged down the entire market, marking a sharp reversal from Wednesday, when shares rallied following the Democrats’ retaking of the Senate and House of Representatives in the midterm elections. Voters overwhelmingly approved candidates and ballot measures that sought to curtail the buildout of AI data centers in the U.S.  That reality seems to have hit tech stock investors more forcefully on Thursday, as some early signs of the changing business conditions came into focus.  Meta President Dina Powell McCormick , speaking at a conference organized by the Wall Street Journal on Wednesday, acknowledged the new hurdles. Building data centers in the U.S. is “going to be harder,” she said. “I can also tell you that every hyperscaler is now thinking about ‘Do we need to build outside the United States?’ Because they’re enormous investments, hedging those investments is a wise thing to do.” Dan Ives, the usually bullish analyst at Yorkville Ives, wrote in a note to investors Thursday that he now expects the tech industry’s capex growth to peak next year, instead of in 2028 or 2029.  That capex spree has been an engine of the U.S. economy over the past two years as companies such as Alphabet , Microsoft, Amazon , Meta, and Oracle , as well as new so-called neocloud companies, raced to build data centers to run AI services. The companies are spending hundreds of billions of dollars for the chips, computers, and networking gear, in addition to land, energy, and construction, to erect the data centers.   “While Big Tech and hyperscaler capex should still easily exceed $1 trillion in 2027 the growth rate into 2028 will clearly moderate significantly as the data center buildout comes at a much slower pace given the political map especially in the state of Texas,” Ives wrote.  “We estimate on the low end 10% of the planned 800-1,000 AI focused data centers in the US will now be wiped off the roadmap, with potentially up to 20% of these facing a much longer regulatory road that could further impact the capacity buildout in the US over the next few years,” Ives wrote. Chip stocks were some of the worst hit, with Micron , the one of the world’s top 3 makers of memory chips, down roughly 14% and AMD , a rival to Nvidia, also down 14%.  Simeon Wallis, chief investment officer at Aprio Wealth Management, told Fortune that uncertainty around data center expansion in Texas, Georgia, and Ohio is leading to worries about AI industry growth. “We see that uncertainty reflected disproportionately in semiconductors, an industry that has been a major beneficiary of AI infrastructure investment,” said Wallis, whose firm manages $6.1 billion in assets. Neocloud companies, which have taken on large amounts of debt to build data centers that compete with the likes of Amazon and Google, were particularly hard hit as well. Coreweave, one of the leading neocloud companies, was down 9% on Thursday, and on track for an 18% decline over the past two days.  By contrast, Google, one of the industry’s largest cloud providers, with a search advertising business powering its business, was down a more modest 1.6% on Thursday. The turmoil triggered by data center worries spread across the broader tech sector throughout Thursday. Software stocks like Salesforce and Snowflake were down 3.6% and 6.4% respectively. Figma, a maker of design software which reported stronger than expected Q3 revenue on Wednesday, was down 17%. Even gig economy and streaming media companies like DoorDash , Uber , Spotify , and Netflix were all down by multiple percentage points by the time the market closed Thursday. “Ultimately, we believe that markets can over-react in the short term to speculating who future winners and losers are,” said Wallis, of Aprio Wealth Management. With additional reporting by Scott DeCarlo and Catherina Gioino. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: BMW bumps battery for the better: The 2027 i7 60 xDrive, driven
articles.summary: BMW has updated its flagship sedan with the newest EV and infotainment tech.
articles._body: BMW provided flights from Washington, DC, to Los Angeles and accommodation so Ars could drive the 2027 i7 as well as the 2027 iX5 and X5. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. When BMW debuted the new 7 Series in 2022, it set a new standard for large luxury sedans, increasingly irrelevant though that class is. Rather than siloing off an electric alternative like Mercedes, with its EQS alongside the normal S-Class, BMW simply made the powertrain an option. Stick with a V8 if you want, or consider the rather good electric version instead—only subtle differences like the badging and lack of exhaust pipes give the game away. Since then, BMW has brought out a string of even newer electric vehicles for the 5 and 3 Series (plus their SUV counterparts). It has switched from battery packs made of prismatic cells to more energy-dense arrangements of cylindrical cells. The motors are still electrically excited synchronous ones, but now the drive units feature silicon carbide inverters and more compact packaging. This sixth-generation electric powertrain was designed for the clean-sheet Neue Klasse family, which also threw out the legacy cruft of dozens and dozens of discrete single-function electronic control units for a handful of powerful domain controllers. These computers take over those functions but with much faster processing power—and therefore more capabilities in terms of chassis control or powertrain efficiency—as well as the ability to be more easily updated. articles.title: Wall Street’s best post-midterm rally in 44 years lasted just one day—then $3 trillion vanished as chip stocks plunged over AI fears
articles.summary: Chip and AI stocks led a delayed selloff on fears new Democratic governors will pause data centers. Analysts split on how long.
articles._body: The Nasdaq fell about 5% on Thursday and the S&P 500 nearly 4%, just a day after Wall Street had cheered the Democratic sweep of Congress. By early Thursday afternoon, the Nasdaq dropped 5.2% and the S&P 500 3.8%, and the Dow was down 2.9%, or more than 1,500 points. The S&P 500 fell as low as 7,394.49, below where it closed on Election Day. Thursday’s drop off seemed to hit AI and tech stocks the hardest: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was down about 9.75% in a Reuters intraday snapshot and briefly fell as much as 11%, on track for its steepest daily loss since March 2020. Among other AI-related stocks include AMD and Micron , which each lost roughly 15%, and Nvidia fell almost 9%. But the drop came a day late. On Wednesday, the Dow rose 1,569 points, or 3%, its best performance after a midterm election in 44 years. The S&P 500 rose 1.6% to 7,688.62, as oil fell more than 8% and investors seemed to hope that a divided government would mean steadier policy. But by Thursday, U.S. stocks had shed roughly $3 trillion in market value, and the Dow was heading for its worst second trading day after a midterm in data going back to the index’s start in 1896. Are Democratic policies inherently anti-AI? Perhaps part of the reason for the huge hit to the AI and tech sectors could be because of the Blue Tsunami . There were 41 ballot measures regarding slowing down data center buildouts, and most of them passed, especially in Ohio. So the midterm risk to AI was showing up on Wednesday, but only in parts of the market, before it showed up in full Thursday. Vistra plunged 14% and Vertiv fell 13% on fears of data center moratoriums, while Nvidia slipped only 3% on Wednesday. Smaller AI cloud providers such as CoreWeave were also hit hard, since a permitting slowdown in Texas would hurt operators like CoreWeave before it reached the hyperscalers that are their main customers. Meanwhile, some of the biggest tech companies—which pay for the build-out—saw their stocks rise. Some analysts and economists argued political pushback could let air out of an inevitable AI bubble without popping it. That’s when Asian markets started selling off overnight: South Korea’s Kospi closed down 5.28% with trading halts during the session, Taiwan’s main index fell 3.2% and the Nikkei 1.79%. By Thursday, the largest U.S. tech names had joined the decline: Tesla dropped as much as 10%, Qualcomm fell 11.2% and Arm Holdings 11% after weaker technology earnings. Oil prices also rebounded following Wednesday’s drop. While the losses were most concentrated in tech, four of the S&P 500’s 11 sectors were up on the day, including consumer staples, which rose 1.5%, and Berkshire Hathaway hit an all-time high. Texas is the main source of worry about the build-out. Democrat Gina Hinojosa, who wants an immediate moratorium on new data centers, beat Republican Gov. Greg Abbott — Wells Fargo estimates 27% of planned data center gigawatts are in Texas. Amy Acton in Ohio and Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia also campaigned on restricting data center development . The opposition is not purely partisan. Abbott paused new data center permits in September pending a grid audit, and Hinojosa campaigned on extending that moratorium. Hinojosa likely won’t need a new law, since Abbott’s pause on grid connections already freezes data center permits. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles._body: Breece Hall revealed positive news about his health as he prepares for the New York Jets’ Week 9 matchup of the 2026 NFL season. Hall is halfway through the fifth season of his career with the Jets. He shines as the leading rusher in the offense, being one of the bright spots over the past couple of seasons. However, Hall had injuries keep him on the sidelines. He missed the entirety of October due to a quadriceps injury, only appearing in three games throughout the first eight weeks of the campaign. He spoke with media on Thursday as he delivered the good news about his availability this weekend, per reporter Rich Cimini. “Breece Hall says he’s ready to go for Sunday. #Jets,” Cimini wrote. What lies ahead for Breece Hall, Jets The Jets need all the offensive firepower they can get amid a tough start to the season. Having Breece Hall back in the fold will elevate their quality of play, but their aspirations for a successful campaign won’t get any easier. Hall has been decent throughout the three games he played in. He has racked up 51 carries for 163 yards and a touchdown while catching 10 passes for 102 yards. New York has a 2-6 record this season, sitting at third place in the AFC East Division standings. They are above the Miami Dolphins while trailing the New England Patriots and the Buffalo Bills. In terms of the conference standings, they are 12th place. They lead over the Indianapolis Colts and the Dolphins while being under the Houston Texans and the Baltimore Ravens. The Jets will continue preparations for their upcoming matchup this weekend, being on the road. They take on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 9 as kickoff commences on Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET. Core Scientific (CORZ) to Exit Bitcoin Mining by Year-End as Colocation Hits $215 Million
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Core Scientific (CORZ) to Exit Bitcoin Mining by Year-End as Colocation Hits $215 Million Core Scientific will complete its exit from bitcoin mining by year-end and enter 2027 as a pure-play high-density colocation provider, management said on Thursday’s third-quarter earnings call, capping a pivot that has already cut the company’s mining fleet nearly in half. Chief Financial Officer Jim Nygaard told investors the company expects to “complete the wind-down during the fourth quarter.” Chief Executive Officer Adam Sullivan put the same end date more bluntly: “We expect to complete our exit from Bitcoin mining by year end.” The comments landed alongside a results release filed with the SEC that shows how far the shift has already gone. Colocation revenue climbed nearly 60% sequentially to $215.4 million in the quarter ended Sept. 30, the earnings exhibit shows. Digital asset self-mining revenue fell to $12.3 million, down about 79% from $57.4 million a year earlier. Hosted mining for third parties added just $5.2 million. Of $232.9 million in total revenue, colocation now accounts for roughly 92%. Self-mining posted a $7.5 million gross loss in the quarter. Colocation gross profit was $128.4 million, a 60% margin. Adjusted EBITDA more than tripled sequentially to $133.6 million, with the margin expanding to 57% from 25%. Mining shrinks as AI leases fill the floor Nygaard said Core Scientific had nearly 50% fewer miners online at the end of September than at year-end 2025. The company has been repurposing power and floor space under long-term customer agreements for AI and high-performance computing workloads, a process its investor materials describe as continuing “as circumstances allow.” That path is not unique among public miners. Peers have been selling bitcoin and leasing campuses to AI tenants, and research notes have flagged a widening funding gap between those that can finance data center builds and those that cannot. Core Scientific is billing for 485 megawatts of colocation capacity as of Sept. 30 — up 90 MW in the quarter — representing more than $700 million in average annualized colocation GAAP revenue. The remaining roughly 100 MW under its CoreWeave buildout is in commissioning and expected to start recognizing revenue over the next few months, Sullivan said. Beyond CoreWeave’s contracted 590 MW, Core Scientific has 530 MW under an AMD-backed agreement across five campuses, with initial delivery targeted for the first half of 2027 and full delivery by the end of 2028. Together, the two relationships cover about 1.1 GW. Once fully delivered and billing, management expects that portfolio alone to generate $1.8 billion in average annual run-rate revenue and $1.6 billion in net operating income. What Core Scientific’s sheet shows Bitcoin is almost gone from the books. Digital assets stood at $2.7 million on Sept. 30, down from $49.7 million three months earlier and $222 million at year-end 2025. Earlier this year, Core Scientific was still adding coins even as it sold into the pivot; that chapter is effectively closed. The mining exit has already carried a cash cost. A $41.9 million loss on contract termination booked in the second quarter reflects the decision to end a Block/Proto mining chip supply agreement. Liquidity ended the third quarter at about $1.7 billion, including roughly $800 million in cash, after heavy capital spending on AMD sites and the Polaris acquisition. Sullivan framed the wind-down as simplifying the business toward “more attractive long-term growth opportunities.” Nygaard added that starting 2027 with a “very clean P&L” — one without mining in the numbers — should give investors a clearer look at a true colocation run-rate. The test now is whether Core Scientific turns the last machines off on schedule in the fourth quarter, and whether the AMD financing package lands in time to keep that clean P&L growing. This post Core Scientific (CORZ) to Exit Bitcoin Mining by Year-End as Colocation Hits $215 Million first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .

articles.title: Sony Employee Impersonator Sentenced to 6.5 Years in Prison for Fake Artist Bookings
articles.summary: Meceo Ray McEaddy previously served four years in prison for falsely promising to book shows by Rihanna, Lady Gaga and Justin Bieber.
articles._body: A recidivist fraudster has been given a lengthy prison sentence for posing as a marketing director at Sony Music Entertainment to steal more than $1 million from event bookers.     Meceo Ray McEaddy, aka “Ray Annes,” was sentenced by a Manhattan judge on Wednesday (Nov. 4) to six and a half years in federal prison. He previously served four years in state prison for defrauding investors with false promises that he could book performances by Rihanna , Lady Gaga and Justin Bieber . Related Judge Torn on Lil Durk Bail Question After Murder-for-Hire Verdict: ‘A Question of Psychology’ Kenny MacPherson, Veteran Music Publisher and Big Deal Music Co-Founder, Dies at 71 Diddy Moved From New Jersey Prison to Similar Facility in Pennsylvania McEaddy has admitted to launching a near-identical scheme almost immediately after getting released from jail in 2017. Starting in 2018, he began to pose as a high-up employee at Sony Music Latin and convinced 20 victims to wire him a total of $1.2 million for nonexistent concert slots. Prosecutors say McEaddy lied about having connections to famous artists and even forged the signature of one top musician. Court papers do not identify the names of these artists, though McEaddy claimed on a podcast in 2019 that he worked with top Latin acts, including Bad Bunny , Ozuna , Maluma and J Balvin . He was indicted on federal charges in May 2025 and pled guilty a few months later to fraud and aggravated identity theft. Prosecutors cited McEaddy’s hefty criminal record in seeking a lengthy prison sentence: in addition to running the similar concert-booking scheme years earlier, McEaddy has five other prior convictions for crimes including reckless endangerment, disorderly conduct and posing as law enforcement. “Upon his release, he again returned like clockwork to engaging in fraudulent behavior,” wrote prosecutors in an October court filing, obtained by Billboard .  “A serious sentence is necessary to hammer home for this defendant that his actions are wrong, to protect others from becoming victims of the defendant’s schemes, and to promote respect for the law that the defendant clearly lacks.” Prosecutors asked for a seven-year sentence. McEaddy’s lawyer urged a judge to instead give him three years in prison, saying the man has “done everything possible to meaningfully atone” after having “deluded himself into believing” he could book top artists. Ultimately, Judge Gregory H. Woods came down closer to the prosecution’s recommendation and ordered a six-and-a-half-year sentence. McEaddy will also serve three years of supervised release after his prison term and return his $1.2 million fraud earnings. Law360 was first to report the news . Reps for the prosecution and Sony declined to comment on the sentence. McEaddy’s lawyer did not return a request for comment.
