articles._body: The Calgary Flames have been up and down to start the season so far, but they could be getting some big help soon. Devin Cooley had been sidelined for a few games after an injury, but it looks like the Flames are ready to bring him back into the fold, according to Pat Steinberg of Flames Now. “Calgary has activated Devin Cooley off injured reserve. Cooley is ready to return after missing four games with a lower body injury. Arsenii Sergeev was returned to the AHL Wranglers earlier Thursday,” Steinberg wrote on X, formerly Twitter. This is good news for the Flames, as they get back a player who fans have loved this season. In seven games, Cooley is 4-3-0 with a .914 SV% and 2.69 GAA. He’s also 12th-best in Goals Saved Above Expected per 60 among the 41 qualified netminders. With Cooley returning, the Flames are reassigning Sergeev. He played one game for the Flames during his call-up, in which they lost to the Colorado Avalanche. The Flames didn’t start the season the best , as they were once 1-6-0, but have since improved their record to 7-8-1. The hope is that they can continue playing at a high level so they can climb the standings. There are a few teams that they have to try to catch, but with the return of Cooley, there is a chance they could do so. After being near the bottom of the Pacific Division last season, the Flames want to make sure they’re making improvements to start this season so they don’t find themselves in the same situation. articles.title: MLB rumors: Astros, Angels may hold key to unlocking elite shortstop trade value
articles.summary: With the baseball world wondering if a fire sale will take place with the Houston Astros and Los Angeles Angels due to the differing directions of the teams, the conversation has centered around each of the franchises’ shortstops. As rumors will continue to surround the Astros and the Angel
articles._body: With the baseball world wondering if a fire sale will take place with the Houston Astros and Los Angeles Angels due to the differing directions of the teams, the conversation has centered around each of the franchises’ shortstops. As rumors will continue to surround the Astros and the Angels this offseason, this former player and analyst speaks on the shortstop market and how barren it is, leading to the higher value for Jeremy Pena and Zach Neto. Erik Kratz would speak on “Foul Territory” on the matter, saying that the “asking price” is sure to be huge if a team in need of a shortstop would go after Pena or Neto. “Two shortstops available, two shortstops that have clear upside,” Kratz said Wednesday. “Neto and Pena. Does a team pivot and go to Neto, or does a team pivot and go to Pena? I guess it’s really the asking price…it’s really if you can actually talk to somebody with the Angels. But I think there’s an inflection point with both teams, and getting rid of a shortstop is a huge, huge deal.” Shortstop help is hard enough to find. If Jeremy Peña or Zach Neto becomes available, the asking price could be MASSIVE. pic.twitter.com/7FjmK70Zc4 — Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) November 4, 2026 Having been with Houston since 2022, Pena has been one of the top shortstops in MLB, as he recorded a .277 batting average to go along with 22 home runs and 56 RBIs in 112 games. As for Neto, who has been with Los Angeles since 2022, he had a career-high 27 home runs last season to go along with a .239 batting average, 77 RBIs, and 24 stolen bases. Shortstops in the perspective of the Astros, Angels Kratz would also look at the situation from the perspective of the Astros and Angels, saying that while the return for a shortstop could be big, you’re still giving up a premium position. “You don’t find big-league shortstops at very many places. That’s why I think it’s hard to move those guys because I think they’ll probably ask the world for them,” Kratz said. It remains to be seen if either Houston or Los Angeles gives up Pena and Neto, respectively, as the former won the AL WEST with an 81-81 record and the latter was last in the division at 62-100. articles.title: Brewers rumors: Insider reveals how Jake Bauers-Milwaukee reunion could happen
articles.summary: Jake Bauers’ future with the Milwaukee Brewers remains unresolved as the first baseman weighs a qualifying offer following a career season and the franchise’s first World Series championship. The 31-year-old hit .266 with 26 home runs, 86 RBIs, and an .874 OPS in 2026. He also earned NLCS MVP hon
articles._body: Jake Bauers’ future with the Milwaukee Brewers remains unresolved as the first baseman weighs a qualifying offer following a career season and the franchise’s first World Series championship. The 31-year-old hit .266 with 26 home runs, 86 RBIs, and an .874 OPS in 2026. He also earned NLCS MVP honors during the Brewers ’ four-game sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers. Bauers faces a significant financial decision after earning $2.7 million in 2026. His experience at first base and in the outfield gives Milwaukee flexibility as it evaluates its roster for next season. Foul Territory shared a clip Thursday on X, formerly Twitter, featuring The Athletic’s Ken Rosenthal discussing the Brewers’ options during the “Grillin’ Ken” segment of “Fair Territory.” “The Milwaukee Brewers could use a first baseman. I don’t know that they want to pay Jake Bowers 23.15 million, but maybe you work out a longer deal at a lower average salary.” “He’s finally in position to hit the jackpot.” @Ken_Rosenthal says Jake Bauers could turn his breakout season into a multi-year deal if he rejects the qualifying offer. pic.twitter.com/vXhqQdXwwc — Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) November 5, 2026 Bauers is one of eight players who received qualifying offers before Monday’s deadline. He has until 4 p.m. ET/1 p.m. PT on November 17 to accept the one-year, $23.15 million contract. The amount represents a record for the qualifying offer, which MLB calculates using the average of its 125 highest salaries. Accepting would increase Bauers’ annual pay by $20.45 million compared with his 2026 earnings. Declining would leave him free to negotiate with other clubs while preserving the possibility of returning to the Brewers on different terms. If he signs elsewhere before the next amateur draft, Milwaukee would receive a compensatory draft pick. Rosenthal’s proposal describes one possible contract structure, not an agreement between the sides or confirmation of ongoing negotiations. The clip does not establish how many years either party would seek or what annual salary would make a deal possible. As of Thursday, Bauers has not announced his qualifying-offer decision, leaving his next contract and destination unsettled. articles.title: MLB rumors: Analyst says quiet part out loud about Tarik Skubal’s free agency
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers are currently in the early stages of the MLB free agency period, coming on the heels of their loss to the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLCS. The biggest priority for Los Angeles this winter is bringing back star pitcher Tarik Skubal, who is now a free agent after the team trad
articles._body: The Los Angeles Dodgers are currently in the early stages of the MLB free agency period, coming on the heels of their loss to the Milwaukee Brewers in the NLCS. The biggest priority for Los Angeles this winter is bringing back star pitcher Tarik Skubal , who is now a free agent after the team traded for him from the Detroit Tigers this past season. Now, former MLB general manager and current analyst Jim Duquette has weighed in with his thoughts on Skubal’s free agency. “When you start to narrow it down, I feel like it’s the Padres, the Mets, the Dodgers, and maybe there’s one another team. Maybe it’s the Giants possibly… when I hear the Cubs, the most that they’ve spent on a contract was Jayson Heyward and Dansby Swanson. They’re not spending that kind of money on a starting pitcher,” he said, per Foul Territory on X, formerly Twitter. Indeed, many organizations have a history of not paying premium prices for the top players, particularly pitchers, as Duquette noted there is only so much impact that a single pitcher can make on a team’s success in the MLB when compared to other sports, such as a quarterback in football. The Dodgers would certainly love to have Skubal back for the foreseeable future, and they’ve certainly shown no hesitation to shell out huge money to bring in star players throughout Mark Walter’s tenure as the team’s owner. Still, the prospect of Skubal joining one of their NL adversaries, like the Padres or Mets, could be a daunting one for Los Angeles’ chances of getting back to the MLB mountaintop. articles.title: THAT’s a Halloween Song Now?! Some Unexpected Songs Seeing Streaming Bumps This Oct. 31
articles.summary: This week's Halloween-themed Trending Up also looks at Lady Gaga's status as the new Scream Queen, and how the GOAT spooky-season song is comparing to past years.
articles._body: Welcome to Billboard Pro’s Trending Up newsletter, where we take a closer look at the songs, artists, curiosities and trends that have caught the music industry’s attention. Some have come out of nowhere, others have taken months to catch on, and all of them could become ubiquitous in the blink of a TikTok clip. This week: A Halloween post-mortem, starring “Thriller,” Lady Gaga, and a handful of songs we would not have anticipated having to talk about this time of year. Songs You Won’t Take Home to Mother? Unexpected Spooky-Season Jams Emerge From Rick James, Camila Cabello and More As we find out every year, Halloween is truly in the playlist of the beholder, as songs that seem equally at home the other 364 days of the year to many still get tabbed by some as Oct. 31 standards. One of the biggest examples this year undoubtedly comes via Rick James’ 1981 funk classic “Super Freak,” whose sense of freakiness is much more traditionally sexy than spooky. However, with the “Freak” in its title and an arguable tinge of haunted-house energy to its new-wave-y synths, it’s become an unlikely Halloween perennial — streaming in the seven-digits (1.2 million official on-demand U.S. streams, to be exact) this Oct. 31 for the second year in a row, a 328% gain over the 273,000 streams the song racked up the prior Saturday (Oct. 24). Nearly as surprising is the addition to the Halloween canon of Camila Cabello’s DaBaby-featuring 2020 hit “My Oh My,” another song about a lyrical subject more threatening to parental approval than to personal safety, but with a slight melodic eeriness and an appropriate-enough lyric or two (“He comes alive at midnight”) to slip into Halloween playlists relatively inconspicuously. (In the case of “My Oh My,” there’s also a violent-skewing music video to give it slight slasher-soundtrack cred; music video associations have also helped Backstreet Boys’ “Everybody (Backstreet’s Back)” ) — up 203% to 890,000 — become an Oct. 31 perennial.) Whatever the contributing factors, “My Oh My” also saw a huge Halloween bump, racking up 405,000 streams on Oct. 31, a 192% gain from the prior Saturday. Other emerging Oct. 31 favorites make more sense as Halloween songs, but not necessarily so much as Halloween hits. “My Girlfriend Is a Witch” would not be anyone’s normal idea of 2026 streaming-core, as a little-heard late-’60s nugget from L.A. psych-rockers October Country, who had no major chart history during its career. But whether through long-gestating virality or the whims of the Haunted Algorithm, “Witch” has become a spooky-season streaming staple, generating 493,000 Oct. 31 after posting just 82,000 the prior Saturday, a 505% gain. What other tangentially connected and/or deeply obscure songs will become fright night staples in short order? Queen’s “Death on Two Legs”? Ariana Grande’s “Ghostin”? Adina Howard’s “Freak Like Me”? We’ll be on the lookout for new twists and turns in this spooky saga in the years to come. – ANDREW UNTERBERGER Is Lady Gaga Officially Halloween’s New Music Scream Queen? Who needs screams when you’re racking up streams? Lady Gaga dominated this year’s Halloween streaming gains with a trio of songs that make a strong case for her earning the Scream Queen Crown. On Halloween (Oct. 31), Mother Monster’s catalog received 10.57 million official on-demand U.S. streams, according to Luminate, marking an impressive 65% gain from the 6.39 million streams it collected the week prior (Oct. 24). “The Dead Dance,” her Emmy-nominated synth-pop soundtrack single for Wednesday season two, posted the biggest gain from her spooky-themed tracks. “Dance” earned 1.14 million official on-demand U.S. streams, up a jaw-dropping 414% from the 222,000 streams it pulled the week before (Oct. 24). “The Dead Dance” appears on the reissue of Gaga’s 2025 Grammy-winning Mayhem album, which also houses the dance-pop smash “Abracadabra.” On Halloween, “Abracadabra” jumped 232% to over 1.04 million official streams, an impressive gain from the 313,000 streams it garnered on Oct. 24. Gaga’s relationship with the Wednesday series actually began with the show’s first season, which revived her 2011 Born This Way deep cut “Bloody Mary,” thanks to fans using a sped-up version of the song in edits and fancams celebrating the titular character’s eye-catching dance. “Bloody” soared to 1.37 million official on-demand U.S. streams this Halloween, marking a 91% jump from the 717,000 streams it earned the week prior. As a pop auteur who’s always had an eye for the macabre, it’s not too much of a surprise to see so many new-age Halloween anthems emerge from Gaga’s catalog. Let’s see if she snags another one from the upcoming third season of Wednesday . — KYLE DENIS Did “Thriller” Bring More Screams Than Usual This Year? The best-performing song basically every Halloween season is of course Michael Jackson’s “Thriller,” which was already back in the top 20 of the Billboard Hot 100 for the chart dated Oct. 31 (released last week). Given how much all things Michael Jackson were back in the mainstream this year, and how catalog titles have been proving more culturally impactful than ever across the chart, we spent a lot of last week wondering if “Thriller” might be due for its best Halloween ever this year — and, for the first time, possibly even the No. 1 spot on the Hot 100? The results: conclusive, but perhaps not so decisive. “Thriller” racked up about 10.1 million official on-demand U.S. streams this Halloween, according to Luminate, with another 4 million on Friday (Oct. 30) and 2.3 million on Sunday for a full-weekend total of about 16.4 million. That’s up about 36% from the 12.1 million streams it amassed

articles.title: The key Jordi Fernandez adjustment that unlocked Nets’ best performance of season
articles.summary: The Brooklyn Nets may have found the solution to their struggling offense on Wednesday. After failing to reach 100 points in three straight games, Jordi Fernandez’s group continued to sputter offensively early against the Charlotte Hornets. Then, a Jordi Fernandez rotation adjustment helped
articles._body: The Brooklyn Nets may have found the solution to their struggling offense on Wednesday. After failing to reach 100 points in three straight games, Jordi Fernandez’s group continued to sputter offensively early against the Charlotte Hornets. Then, a Jordi Fernandez rotation adjustment helped turn the tide. Fernandez benched Chaney Johnson and Keon Ellis for Danny Wolf and Terance Mann in the second half. Meanwhile, Noah Clowney exited early in the third quarter due to knee soreness. Those changes helped spark a 64-point second half for the Nets en route to a 114-104 victory. Wolf’s offensive punch and rookie Mikel Brown Jr.’s career-high 18 points helped Brooklyn regain the lead in the third quarter. Following the Nets’ ugly fourth-quarter collapse against the New York Knicks , Michael Porter Jr. took them home on Wednesday, scoring 17 of his 26 points in the second half. “Sometimes you see guys not having it… not having a good game. And then you want to find fresh legs and fresh energy,” Fernandez said when asked about benching Johnson and Ellis in favor of Wolf and Mann. “And I think [Danny and Terance] were hungry and ready to go, and they’ve prepared themselves so well. Otherwise, you can’t go out there and perform like this. So searching, searching. And I think we came up with a good group, and it was a great home win for us. The fans deserved it.” While Johnson, Ellis and Clowney have helped the Nets defensively , having all three in the rotation had become untenable offensively. The trio has combined to shoot 15-of-51 (29.4 percent) from the field and 5-of-29 (17.2 percent) from three, with nine assists and 11 turnovers over their last four games. That lack of production proved costly during recent losses to the Detroit Pistons and Knicks. Brooklyn had scored under 25 points in eight of its last 14 quarters before the trio exited the rotation midway through Wednesday’s win. Danny Wolf jumpstarts Nets’ sputtering offense during much-needed win over Hornets Brad Penner-Imagn Images The infusion of Wolf and Mann provided much-needed ball-handling and floor spacing alongside Julius Randle, Porter, Brown and Nolan Traore. “I think the biggest staple of our team, especially our offensive identity, is supposed to be playing fast, playing with the pass,” Wolf said following the win. “We use the terminology pace and space. And I feel like there are times when we do it great, and then I think there are times, just with my play style, that I can really help us push the ball up the floor, make simple passes to start the break. And I think you get those, and you get momentum, and momentum is what helps win you a basketball game. And I think right to start the second half when I went in, there was a big Julius and-one bucket. And after that, I think you heard Barclays shift, and you have the fans behind you, and basketball’s fun that way. It’s how it’s supposed to be played.” HAPPY WOLF WEDNESDAY https://t.co/WbaVLHbiQj pic.twitter.com/QiYgwdtWbg — Brooklyn Nets (@BrooklynNets) November 5, 2026 Despite his limited playing time through the Nets’ first seven games, Wolf said he knew his number could be called at any time. “In the NBA, there’s going to be times, especially early in your career, that you might not be in the rotation. And that was the case [for me] when we started the year. But everyone emphasizes and preaches that you’ve got to be ready, and you hear it over and over: just make sure you’re doing all your work, doing all your things to make sure that when your number gets called, you’re ready. And I tried taking advantage of all the time I had. And when coach called my name in the second half, I was ready, and I was looking forward to that opportunity and tried doing everything I could to help the team win.” Porter pointed to Wolf, Mann and Brown as the difference in the win. Brown scored a season-high 18 points on 6-of-11 shooting with four assists in 20 minutes. “I ain’t going to lie. The difference tonight was Terance Mann and Danny Wolf,” Porter said. “They haven’t been in the rotation much but came in ready to play. Terance is one of those guys where it doesn’t matter how much he scores; he impacts the game so much with his IQ, his defensive ability, his connectivity, and his communication. So he’s a pleasure to share the court with, one of my favorite teammates I’ve ever had. And Danny coming in and contributing right away, that takes a lot of readiness and a lot of discipline to not play for so many games, come in in the second half and to contribute the way he did. I always thought Danny was a special player, and I’ve said that since he got here. I think he could do so many things on the basketball court, and I’m really happy that he got the opportunity. He was a plus 17. Terrance was a plus 11. So I’ll say those two dudes, and then obviously Mikel was the other one. He had 18 points, but the shots he hit and the plays he made were big time. So yeah, those three guys really stood out for sure.” Julius Randle posted 22 points and four assists on 7-of-13 shooting during the win. However, he played only three minutes during the fourth quarter. Fernandez said he planned to put Randle back in to close the game, but the veteran told him to leave the same five in after the Nets went on a run. Nolan Traore added 16 points on 7-of-11 shooting from the field and 2-of-5 from three in 27 minutes. Day’Ron Sharpe chipped in five points on 2-of-3 shooting with a career-high eight assists, one turnover and two blocks. The Nets will return to action on Saturday against the Atlanta Hawks as they kick off a four-game road trip. The post The key Jordi Fernandez adjustment that unlocked Nets’ best performance of season appeared first on ClutchPoints .

Show HN: GitHub-like reply with "R" for Basecamp and Slack
articles.summary:
Hello HN!

I wrote a browser extension (also available as a userscript) that allows to insert quotes into site's reply message box using selected text + hitting 'r' (as it's done on Github). It targets only specific sites (basecamp.com, slack.com), because that's what we use at our company daily
articles._body: Hello HN! I wrote a browser extension (also available as a userscript) that allows to insert quotes into site's reply message box using selected text + hitting 'r' (as it's done on Github). It targets only specific sites (basecamp.com, slack.com), because that's what we use at our company daily. The idea came out of my boss (who's also a good friend of mine) frustration. He always complained that Basecamp's replies are so inconvenient compared to Github's way. You have to select the quote, copy it into clipboard, then scroll to the reply box, paste it, then select the text again, and finally format it as a quote using editor's toolbar. That's 6 steps vs 2 on Github! Last summer Basecamp rolled out a new facelift featuring a heavy usage of keyboard shortcuts. But "reply with r" was still missing, so another rant from my boss followed :) At that time I was toying with an old browser extension written long time ago as a learning project. I was rewriting it against the new extension API to see what changed/improved. Being immersed into the topic, it was obvious that a thought about "fixing" Basecamp with a browser extension came into my head. So I started working on the Dial R for Reply project during my spare time. I had two clear motivations: 1. I knew it would make someone's life better (myself included). 2. I would learn something new along the way. During the process I realised I could also "fix" Slack replies. It was a bit of trial and error (I didn't use any LLMs for reasons stated above). The hardest part was to dig into each editor's public and private APIs (Basecamp uses lexical, Slack uses Quill). I had to resort to using internals, so be warned -- it might break when site owners decided to update those libraries. On the other hand, hacking a site with an extension is a risky operation anyway (anything may be changed at any time). Key takeaways: 1. browser extensions are cool! Compared to native apps and electron wrappers, you as a customer have such a powerful tool to amend a web application as you like. 2. if you are a library writer, if possible, keep your private state and/or functions accessible to the outside world. Yes, you should clearly mark them as a private, so there's a clear boundary drawn between what can be used safely and what's not. But being able to peek into private state was the only option for me to debug and hack into the application. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50383827 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

articles.title: Colin Cowherd says quiet part out loud about Chiefs’ dynasty
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs have looked great during their comeback season in 2026. Kansas City is 5-2 headed into Week 9 despite finishing just 6-11 last season. Despite the solid turnaround, some national voices are skeptical that the Chiefs can become the greatest dynasty in NFL history. Colin Cowh
articles._body: The Kansas City Chiefs have looked great during their comeback season in 2026. Kansas City is 5-2 headed into Week 9 despite finishing just 6-11 last season. Despite the solid turnaround, some national voices are skeptical that the Chiefs can become the greatest dynasty in NFL history. Colin Cowherd was not shy when comparing the Chiefs’ dynasty to the Patriots head of Week 9. He explained that the Patriots dynasty is more prolific than many fans remember. “I spent around half of the dynasty surrounded by Patriots fans. What is remarkable about that dynasty [is] if you really look at the numbers, it’s even greater than you remember,” Cowherd said on Thursday via The Herd with Colin Cowherd. “… 19 years, 17 division titles. They won 77% of their games in the National Football League. Conference championship game 13 times, Super Bowl appearances nine.” By comparison, the Chiefs accomplished seven consecutive AFC Championship appearances from 2018-24. They turned those into five Super Bowl appearances and three Lombardi Trophies. Cowherd argued that despite all of their strengths, the Chiefs are nowhere close to accomplishing what the Patriots did during the Brady era. “The smartly owned, brilliantly coached, remarkably quarterbacked, excellent front officed Kansas City Chiefs. They’re not halfway there yet and they’re already flailing,” Cowherd added. “Until Kenneth Walker, they had no run game for Patrick Mahomes’ entire career.” Cowherd also cited Kansas City’s recent spat of special teams woes as another huge difference between the two dynasties. There’s no question that the Chiefs were a dominant force in the modern NFL for several seasons. They are still a contending team that could get the dynasty right back on track during the postseason. Still, the Chiefs have not looked as invincible as the Patriots did during their prime years. None of that puts a cap on what Kansas City can accomplish. But it does show that the Chiefs have a long way to go if they want to be remembered as the best franchise of all time. Next up for the Chiefs is a Week 9 home game against the Jets. Dončić has scored 308 total points while shooting 49.5% from the field and 43.1% from three-point range,” reported NBA Communications on X, formerly Twitter. Indeed, Doncic has been torching the competition so far this year, hitting his usual barrage of step-back triples, tough finishes at the rim, and a hefty serving of free throws en route to dominating the league’s scoring charts thus far. Many suspected that Doncic’s already astronomical scoring would take another bump this year after the departure of LeBron James in free agency, and that has definitely been the case so far. Meanwhile, the Lakers haven’t exactly faced the stiffest competition this year, but they have been taking care of business against their slate of lesser opponents, and Austin Reaves is also starting to round into form after a relatively quiet start to the year. It will be interesting to see if Doncic can continue this historic pace throughout the season, or if his scoring will dip slightly as things go on. In any case, the Lakers will next hit the floor on Friday evening at home against the Portland Trail Blazers in an NBA Cup game. articles.title: Show HN: Teach a speech model (en) a name by saying it once, on your Mac
articles.summary:
I wanted to see if a speech model could spell a name better if it heard it, not just read it.

Most STT tools handle custom words as text (keyterm list, fixing transcript after with llm, etc).

So I trained an adapter to try it, specifically a LoRA on Qwen3-ASR 1.7b (see benchmark). This LoRA t
articles._body: I wanted to see if a speech model could spell a name better if it heard it, not just read it. Most STT tools handle custom words as text (keyterm list, fixing transcript after with llm, etc). So I trained an adapter to try it, specifically a LoRA on Qwen3-ASR 1.7b (see benchmark). This LoRA transcribes words only after it hears a recording of each of your custom words. To make this model easier to use in day-to-day life, we also built Detail Keeper. It's a Mac app where you can put this adapter to use by specifying difficult-to-transcribe-correctly words and then having them picked up correctly in your recordings. We've found this helpful in two specific cases: 1. Words STT has never heard: invented characters and places, codenames, unusual surnames. 2. Your spelling of a word it does know: Kathryn and not Catherine, Jon and not John. I wasn't able to achieve both good recognition and recognizing many words (1k+) with the model alone. Detail Keeper first narrows each passage to the likeliest taught names by sound. Then the adapter writes the passage, and the app checks it against a plain transcript. On our open benchmark (audiobooks, 1,100 name mentions) it spells taught names as well as Eleven Labs Scribe with keyterms: 89.6% vs 88.2%, no measurable difference. The only downside is that it overwrites a few more untaught names and changes slightly more ordinary words. Everything, including where we lose, is at detailkeeper.com/benchmark. Note: It's free, local and nothing leaves your Mac, but it does require an Apple M series+ mac and OS 26+ currently. Also worth noting that it downloads about 3.6GB of models and only works in English right now. If you're interested, you can also find the adapter itself on HF: huggingface.co/virgil-coach/own-names-qwen3-asr Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50383785 Points: 2 # Comments: 0

articles.title: Miami’s High-Priced QB Loses Top Target Before Notre Dame Clash
articles.summary: Stan Szeto-Imagn Images
articles._body: In some ways, it’s hard for Miami’s Malachi Toney to describe how close he’s grown to Darian Mensah in a matter of months. The quarterback–wide receiver combination is one of the most potent one-two punches in college football this season and is the main reason why the Hurricanes are the No. 1 team in the initial College Football Playoff rankings released Tuesday . “It’s just been crazy,” Toney told reporters this week. “We were just in the locker room just talking about how I saw him at [Prime 112 Restaurant] right after he committed. Just him getting adapted to Miami, we’ve grown so close.” That connection was disrupted Wednesday, when Toney sustained an ankle injury in practice and underwent surgery. He’s expected back later this season, but he will miss Saturday’s much-anticipated matchup with Notre Dame, No. 11 in the Playoff rankings. But confidence remains high in Coral Gables because Miami has Mensah, who’s proved himself as a leader and competitor within Miami’s program since he arrived. “He’s eager to get the ball,” Miami head coach Mario Cristobal said this week. “Enthusiasm, excited, doesn’t flinch, very focused. Just ready, prepared. It was a preparation to give him that kind of confidence. He’s ready to roll.” Mensah has emerged as one of college football’s biggest stars this season. He’s at his third school in three years, having led Duke to a win in the ACC championship game in 2025 and Tulane to a 9–4 record in 2024. This year he’s been one of the most impactful transfer-portal additions in the sport—Mensah leads the nation in touchdown passes (25), and his 80.7% completion percentage would break the NCAA single-season record by more than three points (Bo Nix, 77.4%, 2023). Overall, Miami’s offense leads the nation in scoring at 46.7 points per game. Mensah’s ascension encapsulates how player mobility has changed the sport. Each transfer has led to a bigger on-field opportunity and higher compensation. Mensah arrived at Tulane as a consensus three-star recruit in 2023. He signed a two-year, $8 million deal with Duke in 2024 , one of the biggest in college football at that time. Today, his $6.5 million NIL valuation at Miami is the highest in men’s collegiate athletics, according to On3 . Mensah’s endorsement deals include CVS, Derby Watch Supply, Dr Pepper, and Sling TV. Saturday’s game at Notre Dame was the predetermined biggest game for Mensah and Miami this season, and Toney’s injury has scaled the challenge by a significant margin. Toney, like Mensah, is a nationwide leader in receiving; he ranks first in catches (73) and receiving touchdowns (13), and second in receiving yards (1,027). Saturday’s game is a huge opportunity for Mensah to showcase his ability without his top weapon. It’s a game that’s been circled by NFL scouts, who’ve been waiting for Mensah to perform against an elite team, and in a primetime slot. Miami has played only one ranked opponent through eight games this season: No. 16 Wake Forest. “Whether it was at Tulane, Duke, and now Miami, he’s had success at every level,” Dane Brugler, NFL Draft analyst at The Athletic, told Front Office Sports. “I don’t root for teams, but I root for players to be in big-time moments. … I want to see you go up against a more high-profile team, and I want to see you do it at that level. “But I do think if the draft were tomorrow, he would be a first-round pick.” Bob Donnan-Imagn Images Transfer Portal Impact Mensah is attempting to follow in the footsteps of former Miami quarterback Cam Ward as a multi-time transfer turned Heisman Trophy finalist and eventual first-round draft pick. Through eight games and what’s projected ahead, Mensah’s on the short list of most impactful multi-time transfers in the portal era. At the highest level of performance, it’s most common in quarterbacks. Ward (Incarnate Word, Washington State, and Miami) is the most successful to date, followed by Dillon Gabriel (UCF, Oklahoma, and Oregon) and Tyler Shough (Oregon, Texas Tech, and Louisville), who were Day 2 NFL Draft picks in their respective years. Elsewhere, offensive lineman Olu Oluwatimi (Air Force, Virginia, and Michigan) won the Rimington and Outland trophies while playing for the Wolverines in 2022. The difference between the aforementioned players and Mensah is that none played at their three schools in three consecutive seasons. He was involved in a lawsuit with Duke in January stemming from his decision to transfer. Duke claimed he violated the terms of a contract with the school. It marked the first lawsuit filed by a school against a current athlete over an NIL and/or revenue-sharing contract. Eventually, a settlement was reached. The three-year run is an unusual scenario for a quarterback, but Miami is arguably the school most equipped to handle the circumstances. This is the third straight year that the Hurricanes have a plug-and-play, experienced transfer quarterback: Ward, the No. 1 pick in the 2025 NFL Draft; Carson Beck, a Georgia transfer who led Miami to the national championship game a year ago and was a 2026 third-round pick; and now Mensah. “I think that’s the [school] that’s probably done the best job, whether they’re revitalizing somebody’s stock or just developing them,” Jordan Reid, NFL Draft analyst at ESPN , told FOS. “We’ve seen it over the past three years with Cam Ward, Carson Beck. … Now Darian didn’t really need to revive his stock, but he’s definitely unlocked the next level of his development.” USA Today Network Plenty on the Line Last season, Miami and Notre Dame were involved in CFP controversy . Miami was placed above Notre Dame in the final rankings despite consistent placement behind Notre Dame throughout the season. Miami did defeat Notre Dame in Week 1, 27–24, but it was not a data point used by the committee—until the final rankings. This Saturday’s game carries significant Playoff implications once again. articles.title: Cody Campbell’s Texas Tech Board Seat in Jeopardy After Elections
articles.summary: USA Today Network
articles._body: Since 2024, billionaire Cody Campbell has become one of the most powerful figures in college sports on multiple levels, from the football field to the halls of Congress. But after the 2026 midterm elections produced a blue wave , the Republican donor and ally of U.S. President Donald Trump could lose at least one lever of power: his seat as board chairman of Texas Tech. In Texas, the governor appoints public university board members, who are then approved by the state Senate. When Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa, a Democrat, takes office in January, she will have the power to replace a host of board members appointed by outgoing Republican Gov. Greg Abbott. Campbell, whom Abbott appointed in 2021, will complete his six-year term in January—making him one of the first Abbott appointees whom Hinojosa could replace. However, the Texas state Senate, which will remain in Republican hands, could serve as a check on Hinojosa that could help Campbell or other conservative board members. Hinojosa’s campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment regarding her plans. Campbell declined to comment on the future of his board seat. In his capacity as Texas Tech board chairman, Campbell—a Texas Tech alum and former Red Raiders football player—has wielded significant influence over the Red Raiders sports program. This past summer, for example, he led the school through the Brendan Sorsby saga . Campbell also had a say in operations at the Big 12 conference level, given that university presidents of Big 12 schools sit on the conference’s board ( and board members exercise power over presidents ). Now, Campbell could lose his formal position of power. But even if Hinojosa replaces him, he will likely continue to be an influential voice in college sports. Campbell, who became a billionaire through a successful career in the oil and gas industry and through his company Double Eagle Energy Holdings, will likely continue to support Red Raiders athletics from a financial standpoint. He and his business partner John Sellers founded the Red Raiders’ NIL collective and have continued to provide key financial support to athletics in the revenue-sharing era. Campbell will likely continue to remain involved in shaping college sports legislation, both individually and through his 501(c)(4) nonprofit organization Saving College Sports. He also remains a key advisor to Trump on college sports legislation. Campbell solidified his relationship with Trump long before he took office in 2025. He was one of the earliest members of the America First Policy Institute, a nonprofit closely associated with the Trump Administration, and has been a generous donor to Republican candidates and causes. (Just two weeks ago, Campbell spoke at a Trump rally in Lubbock . Trump praised Campbell and offered his son, Carson, a shout-out for his football aspirations.) Currently, Campbell is a member of both Trump’s Council on Sports, Fitness, and Nutrition and his college sports council, which Campbell led alongside New York Yankees president Randy Levine. He helped advise Trump on two executive orders Trump signed on college sports. And, alongside Levine and others, Campbell was also an architect of the policies in the Protect College Sports Act , which had momentum after garnering a bipartisan vote in the Senate but is in peril after the midterms. The post Cody Campbell’s Texas Tech Board Seat in Jeopardy After Elections appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: WTA Takes ‘Full Responsibility’ for Livestream of Pegula’s Hot-Mic Comments
articles.summary: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Geoff Burke
articles._body: The WTA is taking the blame for a hot-mic incident involving Jessica Pegula at the WTA Finals. Pegula, the world No. 5 and one of the most active members of the tour’s player council , was heard during a livestream of her practice Wednesday talking to her coach, Mark Knowles, about World No. 3 Mirra Andreeva. The American star said Andreeva “needs to be humbled.” “She’s always been very nice to me, but I’ve lost a little bit of respect for her because I’m just like, this girl—I mean, she’s a nice girl, but she’s a diva,” Pegula said. In a statement to Front Office Sports , the tour responded, saying: “The WTA takes full responsibility for failing to inform our players and their teams that microphones, in place to give fans a livestream of the players’ practice, were active on the courts at the WTA Finals. We sincerely apologize for failing to meet our responsibility to ensure players and coaches were properly informed.” A tour source told FOS that the microphones were not meant to capture conversations of players and coaches, but rather ambient noise during practice. Live streams will continue without audio during practices at the WTA Finals, the tour’s season finale featuring its top eight players, which starts Sunday. The hot mics picked up other comments from Pegula as well. “If I was a coach and my girl, you just played four great games, and you’re up four-zero, and you’re mad at me, hitting balls at me, I would be like, first of all, [that’s] disrespectful to the other person,” she said. “You’re up four-zero, shut the fuck up. But she just can’t.” Later, Pegula also named fellow American Coco Gauff, saying that if Andreeva “had Coco’s mentality, she’d be better than Coco.” Representatives for Pegula, Gauff, and Andreeva did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Livestreamed practices are common throughout tennis tournaments, including the US Open in New York and the BNP Paribas Open, which is also held at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden. But privacy issues have been a long standing issue in tennis, particularly at Grand Slams where cameras are present in many of the backstage areas. At the Australian Open in January, cameras caught Gauff smashing her racket after losing in the quarterfinal. Gauff admitted that she thought she was away from the view of cameras, and Pegula showed support for her. “I’m not a fan of the cameras,” Pegula said. “You’re just going about your day and feel like someone’s constantly filming you. I saw online that people were zooming in on player’s phones. Literally the only time you’re not being recorded is when you’re going into the shower and going to the bathroom.” The post WTA Takes ‘Full Responsibility’ for Livestream of Pegula’s Hot-Mic Comments appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: LIV Golf Is Shutting Down, Lawyers Confirm in Bankruptcy Hearing
articles.summary: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images
articles._body: LIV Golf is proceeding with plans to wind down its operations and will not follow through with a “LIV 2.0” of the league. The league officially announced the move shortly after its lawyers revealed the decision at a brief, 13-minute hearing in its Chapter 11 bankruptcy case in New Jersey on Thursday morning. LIV said that “despite extensive discussions, the relevant parties were ultimately unable to reach a consensual resolution of certain outstanding terms” of its $300 million rescue deal with BC Partners Credit, and as a result, the deal “has been terminated, and the transaction is not expected to move forward at this time.” BC Partners pulled out of its nine-figure deal to provide LIV with post-bankruptcy financing on Wednesday, which left the league with no other option beyond heading for liquidation of its assets. The Saudi PIF spent more than $5 billion on LIV since the league launched in 2022, but cut off its funding after the 2026 season. The PIF controlled LIV’s bankruptcy process as the largest creditor. LIV intends to file its Chapter 11 plan and disclosure statement implementing the wind-down by Monday. “BC Partners Credit supported a transaction that aligned the interests of players and investors, offering a credible path toward building a sustainable future for LIV Golf,” a spokesperson for the firm said in a statement to Front Office Sports . “While there was great support for the league, we are disappointed that mutually acceptable terms could not be reached among the various stakeholders.” Gene Davis and Jon Zinman, chairmen of LIV’s independent board of directors , said, “In light of the current circumstances, we believe shifting toward an orderly wind-down is the most responsible path forward for the league at this time.” LIV in its announcement said it “will remain open to, and continue to consider, any value-maximizing alternatives with third parties that may arise” during the wind-down process. Gibson Dunn partner Matthew Williams, one of LIV’s attorneys, said on Thursday morning’s hearing that the decision by LIV to wind down was “not for lack of a good-faith effort over the past several weeks. The debtors, BC Partners, the PIF, the players, the creditors committee—we all negotiated intensely and in good faith.” But “despite everyone’s best efforts, we just couldn’t get to the level of combined financial and player support necessary for a viable LIV 2.0 within the required timeline,” Williams said. LIV’s strategic initiatives committee “concluded that a wind down is the most likely way to maximize value for creditors at this time,” Williams added. “This was not an easy conclusion for anyone who believed in what LIV Golf built, but it is the right one for these estates and the circumstances.” LIV CEO Scott O’Neil said in a statement, “We created memories that I hope will inspire a new generation of fans to follow, play, and fall in love with this great game.” O’Neil also thanked the PIF and BC Partners for their involvement in the process. The Chapter 11 case will take several more weeks, at least, to be sorted out. The case’s creditors committee will meet on Nov. 20, and another hearing with Judge Michael Kaplan is scheduled for Nov. 24. “I do appreciate the candor and professionalism and overall the energy and effort that went into trying to make LIV 2.0 work as a viable path for this chapter 11 case,” Kaplan said Thursday. “What I [also] appreciate is that there’s still an efficient plan to move forward as far as maximizing the return to creditors through an orderly wind down.” The post LIV Golf Is Shutting Down, Lawyers Confirm in Bankruptcy Hearing appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: Julian Edelman: Foxborough ‘Will Be Rocking’ for Tom Brady’s Return
articles.summary: Brian Fluharty-Imagn Images
articles._body: Julian Edelman has a big next few days coming up with Fox Sports. On Thursday, he released a new music video, Talkin’ Football , with his former Patriots teammate and current Gronk & Jules podcast cohost Rob Gronkowski. On Sunday, Gronkowski is getting inducted into the Patriots’ Hall of Fame, the 2016 Super Bowl team will be honored, and their former teammate, Tom Brady, is calling his first New England game in two-and-a-half years with Fox when the Patriots take on the Packers. The network will also be celebrating Veteran’s Day with its programming. Ahead of this weekend’s festivities, Edelman spoke to FOS about the music video, upcoming festivities, what it will be like for Brady to return to Foxborough, which NFL quarterback he’d pick for the next five years, and whether the Rams are “overusing” Puka Nacua. Front Office Sports : You’ve got this music video with Gronk coming out. How did this project come together and what did you learn about the process of making one of these? Julian Edelman: It came together with our marketing and social team and our whole team of people thought this would be a good idea. They put us in the studio, we sang—I’ve been holding in these vocals for a long time, wanted to let them shine, and I’m excited to see what the people think about my voice. FOS : Did you ever think this was something that you would do? JE: I’ve done a lot of things, so I wouldn’t put it past me. I’ve been in so many different verticals of crazy videos—YouTube, Instagram; I’ve been in this content-making game since 2011, so did I see myself making a music video? Probably not, but does it surprise me? No. FOS : This Sunday is a pretty packed Fox event, between Gronk’s team Hall of Fame induction and Tom Brady calling his first Patriots game for the network. What’s your thoughts on all of these things coming together at once in a perfect storm? JE: We also have a huge Veteran’s Day program for all the men and women who have served our country. We have two pregame shows with Fox NFL Kickoff and Fox NFL Sunday where we’ll be on two locations with our service members. That’s going to be exciting as well. Going back to Foxborough is going to be insane. Tom calling his first game. The place will be rocking. You’ve got two really good football teams. The Packers have gotten hot the last couple weeks. The Patriots have come on the last three or four weeks. You’ve got Gronk getting into the Hall of Fame. We’re also celebrating the 2016 Super Bowl 28–3 Falcons game, so we’ll have all our teammates there. It’s just gonna be really fun to get to see guys you haven’t seen in a long time. There’s something that’s always said in the locker room when it’s your last game: “You’ll never be the 2016 football team ever again” — because there’s new coaches and players every year, so it will be a really good time to celebrate a larger-than-life character in Gronk. I don’t think people realize this guy was like a Beatle in Boston with how big his persona was. Having Tom, a man who dedicated his life to New England, brought them the most success an NFL organization will ever experience with one quarterback, probably—I would say like 98% chance—and for me being the guy who was inducted into the [Pats] Hall of Fame last year, getting to celebrate with my teammates, is going to just be a really fun, memorable weekend for us all. And, to celebrate with the fans—we all have our own lives now. We’re all away from the game, or the team, or the area, and to get to go back to where we were in our glory days—it’s just gonna be a fun experience. FOS : What does that type of celebration look like when you guys all get together? JE: It’s a bunch of guys who sit and talk war stories, going over the joys, failures, and grind that we went through. It’s just a good refresher of things you may not remember, or you bring something up that someone else didn’t remember, and it’s a good time to go over an incredible accomplishment that we did as a team. The incredible accomplishment of probably the greatest tight end ever, Rob Gronkowski, and to have Tom there calling the game is the cherry on top. FOS : How do you expect that to go for Tom? As you mentioned, he accomplished so much with the Patriots, but the ending, as endings tend to be, was not the happiest there. What type of emotions are you expecting him to experience and communicate to the viewer? JE: You’d have to ask him, but I can tell you right now he’s won more Super Bowls with that organization than any other team has won in the history of the game. So, I can’t speak for him or for the fans. The Boston people know what’s up. Tom Brady loved his time. It made him who he was to be in New England, so I think it’s gonna be a great moment. FOS : You had commented a couple times on Bill Belichick’s relationship with Jordon Hudson. What were your thoughts when you saw that relationship came to an end? JE: I don’t have really any comment on Bill’s personal life. I haven’t spoken to him in awhile, so I’m more focused on the great weekend that we’re going to celebrate with Rob Gronkowski, Tom Brady calling the game, and the 2016 Super Bowl championship Patriots along with celebrating our vets. FOS : As you look at the quarterbacks across the league, which one would you want for the next five years? JE: It would have to be either Josh Allen, Caleb Williams, or Drake Maye. They all have tremendous arm strength and talent. They’re all mobile. The contracts of Caleb and Drake are still rookie contracts, so there’s a lot of value there to build teams around them. With a guy like Josh Allen who’s getting $65 million a year, it’s harder to surround him with better players, so I’m taking everything into consideration. But he’s that good where he doesn’t need as many good players around him when he’s playing in that kind of flow. I’d maybe throw Joe Burrow in there too. articles._body: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput. Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the US and ground zero for Big Tech’s largest AI buildouts. But the blue wave that swept the Lone Star State may jeopardize that position. Democrat James Talarico won the US Senate seat, Gina Hinojosa won the race for governor, and Democrats will take control of the Texas House for the first time in 24 years. They won after making data centers a central issue on the campaign trail. The swings could spell trouble for hyperscalers with ambitious plans in the state. They also add to growing anxiety that America’s AI buildout could stall. Here’s how the election results could reshape AI’s future . —James O’Donnell What’s next for US energy policy after the midterm elections? Democrats have taken control of both the House and the Senate, but we probably won’t see major federal climate and energy legislation while Trump remains president. The midterm elections could, however, be a big deal for energy at the state and local level. The results could shape everything from the state grid and data center development to renewable energy and greenhouse gas emissions. Find out what the midterms could mean for the future of US energy . —Casey Crownhart This story is from The Spark, our weekly climate tech newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Wednesday. It’s a plan that could start an overhaul of the slow, complicated process for getting energy projects approved. But some environmental groups oppose the bill, or parts of it. ( WSJ $) + Its chipmakers are poaching engineers from foreign rivals. ( CNBC ) + A star mathematician has left the US to develop AI in China. ( SCMP ) 6 Watchdogs have sued over tech titans advising the Pentagon Musk and Palmer Luckey could profit from their advice. articles.title: A new bill could change how the US builds energy infrastructure
articles.summary: A sweeping bit of legislation designed to cut red tape could speed up the buildout of energy infrastructure in the US. With the dust barely settled on this week’s momentous midterms, the Senate is set to vote on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) on November 9. It’s a plan th
articles._body: A sweeping bit of legislation designed to cut red tape could speed up the buildout of energy infrastructure in the US. With the dust barely settled on this week’s momentous midterms, the Senate is set to vote on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) on November 9. It’s a plan that could finally start an overhaul of the slow, complicated process for getting energy projects approved, as part of something called permitting reform. People on both sides of the political aisle have been pushing for this type of change for some years. The key question is whether this will cut greenhouse-gas emissions from the US energy sector or push them higher still.   The federal permitting system is designed to protect the environment against industrial pollution from large projects like power plants, transmission lines, and natural-gas pipelines. Today, permitting is governed by a range of laws, including the National Environmental Policy Act and the Clean Water Act. And if there’s one thing you might know about the current state of permitting in the US it’s that it’s slow and incredibly complicated. So in its 417 pages, BAAJA attempts to tighten things up. The bill has provisions that narrow the sorts of projects that need to apply for federal permits and others that enact deadlines in hopes of speeding up a process that today can take years. (There are also specific provisions about transmission planning, mining, and the rest of the kitchen sink; this thing is dense .) One thing to know about this bill is that it’s largely technology neutral: It opens the doors for the buildout of projects involving both fossil fuels and renewables. So there’s a weird mishmash of legislators and outside groups supporting it. The bill’s four sponsors in the Senate are two Republicans and two Democrats. The White House has backed this permitting reform bill, with its Council of Economic Advisors finding that it would reduce review times and have economic benefits like boosting GDP. Clean energy groups like the American Clean Power Association have largely come out in favor of the bill too, with the group’s analysis finding that it could unlock 350 gigawatts of new clean energy for the grid. Some environmental groups, however, oppose the bill, or parts of it. An assessment from the Natural Resources Defense Council says the parts about transmission could have substantial benefits for the grid, but the narrowing of environmental reviews could be damaging for public and private lands. Many in the climate world have long been calling for permitting reform, arguing that renewables stand to benefit more than fossil fuels. The thinking is that solar and wind power are some of the cheapest sources available today, so if we unlock the ability to build more energy, they are likely to win out economically. A few early analyses have tried to quantify just what BAAJA would mean for emissions in the US. One, from the think tank Rhodium Group, found that in the best-case scenario, the bill would cut economy-wide emissions by 4%, reduce annual energy bills by $78 per household, and add 200 gigawatts of new clean energy by 2040. In the worst case, emissions would stay about the same. Another report , from the nonprofit research group Resources for the Future, found that the bill could cut power-sector emissions 6% by 2041 and save more than $350 billion on system costs by midcentury. But there are some concerns that this permitting bill’s real effect would be to open the floodgates for new natural-gas plants. As data centers have put more pressure on the grid, a wave of such plants have been announced. “You get down to a trade-off between essentially growing the clean electricity industry on the one hand and then, as a compromise, growing the fossil-fuel industry on the other,” says Kevin Kircher, an energy modeler and assistant professor of mechanical engineering at Purdue. To quantify that trade-off, Kircher also modeled the potential emissions effects of the bill and found that if BAAJA had been in place in 2025, energy sector emissions would have been higher than the actual baseline. Health and mortality risks associated with air pollution would also have increased. This bill is scheduled for a Senate vote on November 9, well before the next Congress takes control. It’s not clear what the dramatic victories for Democrats might mean for the legislation, which was expected to pass the Senate with largely Republican support if a few Democrats got on board. Democrats could decide to wait for next year, when they’ll have control of both chambers. But any deal would ultimately need to win Trump’s signature, limiting what a future bill might be able to change.  In a world where permitting new projects is easier, we’ll see more clean energy, but we’ll see more natural gas, too. And while prices could get lower, that could push demand for electricity higher, leading to more emissions overall. Simplifying the permitting system and cutting red tape is a worthy goal. But when it comes to emissions, it still really matters what, exactly, you want to build.

articles.title: Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput.
articles.summary: Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the US and ground zero for Big Tech’s largest AI buildouts. But the blue wave that swept the Lone Star State may jeopardize that position. Democrat James Talarico won the US Senate seat against Ken Paxton. Gina Hinojosa won the race for govern
articles._body: Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the US and ground zero for Big Tech’s largest AI buildouts. But the blue wave that swept the Lone Star State may jeopardize that position. Democrat James Talarico won the US Senate seat against Ken Paxton. Gina Hinojosa won the race for governor against the Republican incumbent, Greg Abbott. At the state level, Democrats will take control of the Texas House for the first time in 24 years. Talarico and Hinojosa made data centers a central issue, discussing them constantly on the campaign trail. Even before the polls closed, insiders in the data center industry noticed that the times were changing. At the industry’s DCD conference in Ashburn, Virginia, on Tuesday, panelists lamented that Texas had been the easiest place to build for years—until September. That’s when Abbott, perhaps seeing the increasingly bipartisan distaste for these facilities , began changing course himself.  Developers said the governor’s office had stopped responding to their emails. On September 21, Abbott directed a key state regulator to halt data center permits. Many panelists at the conference were expecting this to mean that existing projects might be slowed and new ones could be halted altogether.  The governor-elect indeed seems eager to do that. Hinojosa supported tax breaks for data centers in 2023 as a way to boost construction jobs, but during her campaign she began pushing for a full-fledged moratorium. That would be a problem for the hyperscalers of Big Tech, which have ambitious plans for AI training facilities in the state. The scale of projects already underway in Texas is massive. The Stargate Frontier data center in Shackelford County is projected to serve 1,820 megawatts—about as much as the nation’s largest data center, SpaceX’s Colossus 2 in Tennessee, and more than twice as much as the largest data center currently operating in Texas. Nexus Hubbard, also under construction and intended mostly to serve Anthropic, has a planned size of 6,400 megawatts and is the second-largest data center being built in the US, behind only Meta’s Hyperion project in Louisiana.  The potential for Democrats to order delays to these projects or moratoriums on new ones adds to growing anxiety that the AI buildout could stall. Banks and lenders are already getting pickier about the projects they back. And given the extent to which the data center buildout is underpinning growth in the economy right now, those forces combined could have ripple effects. Voters around the country, though, were unambiguous in the midterms, sending a similar message on everything from state ballot questions to national offices. Voters supported efforts to protect ratepayers from increases in their electricity bills caused by data centers, and they favored some larger bans on new data centers altogether. If we needed any more convincing that Big Tech has fumbled its effort to sell voters on the idea that AI-powered abundance will make health care better, goods cheaper, and scientific breakthroughs more common, this was it. A key question is whether the Texas counties with the largest data center presence were part of the reason these Democrats got elected, or if the anti-data-center vote came from elsewhere.  It’s complicated: The counties where much of the data center buildout is happening are around Dallas. Dallas County and others closest to it predictably went blue, but nearby Ellis County, which leads in permitting requests for data centers, went for Greg Abbott and Ken Paxton. Cameron County, near the state’s southern border, is a hot spot for data centers and voted blue in the midterms, which was a shift. But Mitchell County and Scurry County, where a bunch of projects in west Texas are located, went red.  This is a big deal, because no single office in the state decides whether a project goes ahead or is halted. Decisions often reflect an interplay between city governments, county officials, and state offices.  Local officials who have some say over data center development may resist sweeping restrictions from the state. And Democrats pushing for a moratorium might also face pushback from the construction unions that supported some of their campaigns. So while the blue wave spells a death knell for Texas data centers in theory, election winners may find that following through on their opposition once in office is much more complicated than campaigning on it.

articles.title: Houston Retail Market Strengthens
articles.summary: Houston’s retail market maintained healthy fundamentals during Q3 2026, supported by stable occupancy, continued rental growth, and positive tenant demand. Lee & Associates reports that direct
articles._body: Houston’s retail market maintained healthy fundamentals during Q3 2026, supported by stable occupancy, continued rental growth, and positive tenant demand. Lee & Associates reports that direct vacancy remained at 5.6% for the second consecutive quarter, while the average direct asking NNN rent increased to a record $22.03 per square foot, approximately 8.1% above Q3 2025. Retail demand strengthened during Q3 2026, with net absorption reaching 551,122 square feet, a significant improvement from 39,756 square feet in the previous quarter. Leasing activity totaled approximately 1.75 million square feet, bringing year-to-date leasing activity to nearly 5.9 million square feet. Through the first nine months of 2026, Houston recorded more than 1.1 million square feet of positive net absorption. Development activity emerged as one of the quarter’s most notable trends. Houston’s construction pipeline expanded to approximately 5.1 million square feet, the highest level since 2019, while quarterly deliveries moderated to approximately 449,000 square feet. New construction remains concentrated in expanding suburban growth corridors,. The post Houston Retail Market Strengthens appeared first on Connect CRE .

articles.title: What’s next for US energy policy after the midterm elections?
articles.summary: I’ve been locked in to my various screens since results from midterm elections started to roll in last night. And it didn’t take long to see the beginning of the blue wave: Democrats took control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate, a dramatic swing from Donald Trump’s victory two
articles._body: I’ve been locked in to my various screens since results from midterm elections started to roll in last night. And it didn’t take long to see the beginning of the blue wave: Democrats took control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate, a dramatic swing from Donald Trump’s victory two years ago.   While the results are striking, we probably won’t be seeing some of the big climate and energy policy shifts that have come in recent years as Congress and the presidency have changed hands. Instead, we’re entering a period of divided government, with a Congress that will likely do battle with Trump’s White House over the next two years. But even if the federal government isn’t likely to pass laws that overhaul energy and climate policy, the midterm results could be a big deal for energy, especially at the state and local level.  Let’s step back for just a moment to put these results in context. Readers might remember huge laws affecting climate and energy that were passed in just the last four years. The 2022 Inflation Reduction Act included massive support for clean energy, including tax credits and government grants and loans. Then the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act essentially slashed much of the support and financial incentives in the IRA from two years before. What those two laws had in common was a period when the government was entirely united, with the Senate, House of Representatives, and presidency all controlled by the same party—the Democrats in the first case and the Republicans in the second. Now Democrats have captured a majority in both the Senate and the House. But Donald Trump is still in the White House. And crucially, neither chamber is anywhere close to a two-thirds Democratic majority. That’s the ratio that would be needed to override a presidential veto. So even if Congress puts together new legislation to boost climate measures and clean energy, Trump will need to sign it—and that dramatically narrows the scope of what might happen legislatively between now and the next election. There could be some bipartisan compromises. One interesting bit of legislation to watch immediately after the election is what happens with permitting reform. In late September, a bipartisan group of senators put forward a bill that would overhaul how new energy projects are reviewed and approved in the US. The law aims to cut red tape and speed up the permitting process. The Senate is set to vote on that package, called the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, on November 9, before the new Congress takes control in January. The White House has supported the bill, and it could pass the Senate if just a handful of Democrats join the Republican majority. But now, we might see Democrats wait until next year to try to renegotiate a deal, though anything would still need to pass muster with Trump. With Democratic control of Congress, we’ll likely see much more scrutiny of Trump and agencies controlled by his appointees. Democratic leaders have already signaled plans to go after leaders like EPA commissioner Lee Zeldin over cuts to staff and investments. Democrats will have the power to subpoena cabinet members and open investigations. Looking beyond the national results, a major trend to watch moving forward will be local action. Democrats swept local control of Pennsylvania, and officials there have signaled plans to support renewable energy and efforts to cut greenhouse-gas emissions. Democrats also took control of the Georgia Public Service Commission for the first time in 30 years. The group regulates electric utilities, essentially controlling much of the grid’s buildout.  Among the broadest effects of these election results, though, will be for the data center industry. According to tracking from Ballotpedia, there were 41 local ballot questions related to data centers. And overwhelmingly, voters chose to restrict their development. Nearly every single one of these measures looks set to come down against data center development, as of the morning of November 4.  And AI critics fared well in their races, too. Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the governor’s seat in Texas, ousting Republican incumbent Greg Abbott. During her campaign, Hinojosa called for a law to completely pause data center development; if passed, it could have major implications for both the state’s grid and the data center industry more broadly. We might not see dramatic new climate- or energy-related federal legislation between now and the next major US election. But many voters signaled, and quite loudly, that they wanted a change. We’ll see how much will shift in the next two years, and where that leaves us.  This article is from The Spark, MIT Technology Review ’s weekly climate newsletter. To receive it in your inbox every Wednesday, sign up here .

articles._body: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. These startups hope “blended” food will cut our appetite for red meat  In the fall of 2025, Jeff Dodge served hungry students steaming marinara sauce and meatballs. The students loved them: 92% of those who tried them wanted them on the menu. Few could guess that mushrooms had been mixed into the meat. Dodge was testing a new product called 50/Cut from the company Joyn. The blend of seemingly simple ingredients—available as meatballs, burgers, and ground meat—could help solve one of the biggest challenges of the climate crisis: getting people to eat less meat, particularly beef. Joyn is among a wave of startups creating “blended meat,” which combines plant proteins with the real deal. The logic: The best meat replacement is … better meat. Get a taste of the startups betting on greener beef . —Meghan McCarron This implant can restore sight for patients with macular degeneration More than 5 million people have an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) called geographic atrophy, in which retinal cells die off. Until now, no treatment could restore their vision. A system called PRIMA changes that. It combines a retinal implant with camera-equipped eyeglasses to improve sight in patients who develop a blind spot in the middle of their vision. After training sessions, more than 80% of recipients could read, do crosswords, and use their phones. Find out how the sight-restoring implant works . —Linda Marsa MIT Technology Review Narrated: The agentic web is here In 2001, a decade after inventing the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee articulated a new vision: an internet navigated by autonomous software agents that address our every need, without requiring us to muck about with browsers and search engines ourselves. At the time, the idea seemed far-fetched. But a quarter-century on, AI agents are beginning to make it a reality. They can triage your inbox, do your grocery shopping, and even access your bank accounts. This new era is being called the agentic web, and it will inevitably transform the internet. Whether the human web survives this transition is anyone’s guess . This is our latest story to become an MIT Technology Review Narrated podcast, which we publish each week on Spotify and Apple Podcasts . Just navigate to MIT Technology Review Narrated on either platform, and follow us to get all our new content as it’s released. articles.title: Securing the agentic enterprise with data lineage
articles.summary: A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal for the sales rep. No
articles._body: A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal for the sales rep. No human checks either handoff. When it’s discovered that the proposal includes unapproved, confidential, and sensitive information, no one can trace where the problematic data entered the workflow or how it spread across systems, files, and agents. DOWNLOAD THE REPORT This scenario illustrates why AI governance needs to evolve, rapidly and dynamically. As more enterprises begin to use agentic AI in daily workflows, they’re realizing that they must manage more than static files; they must manage moving and fragmented data that is continuously ingested, copied, summarized, transformed, reused, and redistributed in new forms. In short, AI security isn’t a tool problem; it’s a data visibility problem. Consequently, traditional security approaches built solely around applications, systems, networks, or endpoints are no longer sufficient. Securing agentic AI at scale requires understanding how data moves. Teams, therefore, need to establish data lineage in order to effectively manage governance, accountability, and trust across human, agentic, and hybrid workflows. articles.title: The Download: controlling AI agents and “Super Intelligence” loyalty tests
articles.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to control powerful AI models by designing
articles._body: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to control powerful AI models by designing systems that incentivize them to stick to the rules. While game theory predicts how rational actors behave under particular rules, reverse game theory designs rules to elicit the behavior we want. Think of splitting a cake: if one person cuts it and the other gets first choice, the cutter has an incentive to make the portions equal. Researchers believe the approach could align AI more closely with our rules and instructions. But big questions remain about whether these mechanisms will work in practice. Here’s how reverse game theory could help make AI agents behave . —Amit Katwala Here’s who is falling in line for Trump’s “Super Intelligence” loyalty test At the end of September, President Trump signed an executive order with just one directive: government agencies must rebrand artificial intelligence as “Super Intelligence.” One month on, the rebrand is slowly appearing across government websites and documents, but it hasn’t caught on with everyone. Even some of the biggest names in tech still use “AI.” But the bigger concern is the new term becoming a political loyalty test: Those who use it signal allegiance to the administration. Those who don’t become targets for attacks. So one month in, who’s on board? —James O’Donnell This story is from The Algorithm, our weekly AI newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Monday. The must-reads I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology. 1 Today’s midterms will test AI’s influence on US politics Candidates are betting that AI regulation will sway voters to their side. ( Axios ) + Angry constituents could derail Elon Musk’s Republican bets. ( BI ) + Tech investors are on edge about the results. ( Reuters $) + America is divided over AI regulation. ( MIT Technology Review ) 2 Nvidia is ordering data centre clients to limit their business with China It told providers that the majority of their sales must be non-Chinese. ( FT $) + The move follows pressure from Washington. ( Bloomberg $) + Chinese AI has ruptured the White House. ( MIT Technology Review ) 3 Hackers have turned supermarket fridges into a food security risk Attacks in Europe have put US supermarket systems on alert. ( CNBC ) + They’ve also sparked concerns over other domestic appliances. ( BBC ) + It’s a good time for doing crime. ( MIT Technology Review ) 4 Scientists have detected signals at the smallest scale ever explored The discovery offers clues to a world of exotic new particles. ( BBC ) + It came via CERN’s Large Hadron Collider. ( The Times $) 5 Zapping part of the brain makes you think harder—at a cost It can both improve performance and reduce motivation. ( New Scientist $) + Neuropixels probes are transforming how we study the brain. One more thing The noise we make is hurting animals. Can we learn to shut up? As human society has expanded, animals have started struggling to hear one another. For many birds, the noise has grown so loud that they’ve begun to sing with faster trills. Now, their mating calls aren’t as effective.  The growing hubbub can also increase bird-on-bird conflict, and entire species that can’t handle urban clamor simply leave town for good. But there are technological solutions to the noises hurting animals—and they could help humans, too.
