Sellers took her talents to the UpShot League, suiting up for the Jacksonville Waves, the inaugural season runners up. While Sellers’ numbers were nothing special, her performance, plus her pedigree, was enough to encourage the Los Angeles Sparks to sign her to a late-season development contract. She ended up seeing time in two games, totaling 21 minutes, four points, two rebounds, two assists and two steals. Sellers’ Sparks stint did little to suggest she’d be back in the WNBA in 2027. Yet, playing for UMCS Lublin in the EuroLeague, Sellers might be proving that her pro potential is still there. A MASSIVE double-double and a crucial win to keep Lublin alive in #EuroLeagueWomen Group D! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/FBq4a8ikHR — EuroLeague Women (@EuroLeagueWomen) November 3, 2026 While Lublin is 1-3, currently putting them in last place in Group D and at risk of elimination from the competition, Sellers is averaging almost 18 points per game on 50 percent shooting, including 40 percent from 3. She’s adding 4.5 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game, as well as nearly two steals. She’s also shooting over 90 percent from the free throw line. The one blemish is her three turnovers per game. Nevertheless, that’s the statistical profile of the player she was thought to be coming out of Maryland. The shooting, in particular, is crucial. After never shooting better than 34.7 percent from 3 across her first three seasons at Maryland, she jumped to 40 percent as a senior. An efficient shooter from distance who also can handle the ball, drive to the basket and earn repeated trips to the line—all at 6-foot-2—is a WNBA player. However, as Sellers is not a great athlete, with those deficits appearing to doom her early attempts to stick in the W, all those offensive pieces need to be in place for her to be of value to a WNBA team. Thus far, her EuroLeague experience with Lublin has reintroduced this outcome. Aliyah Collier (KKŽ Crvena Zvezda) If Aliyah Collier gets a WNBA chance, it would be the culmination of an incredible rise for the former Clemson product who averaged less than 10 points

articles.title: 2026 WNBA season review: Injuries, ill-fated decisions and other self-inflicted issues obscured the few bright spots for the Chicago Sky
articles.summary: It was another losing season for the Sky. One where the future was discussed more than the present. And the hope for draft picks, a practice facility and players returning from injury received more attention, and rightfully so, than the product on the court. While Chicago didn’t reach the playoffs f
articles._body: The Chicago Sky. | Getty Images It was another losing season for the Sky. One where the future was discussed more than the present. And the hope for draft picks, a practice facility and players returning from injury received more attention, and rightfully so, than the product on the court. While Chicago didn’t reach the playoffs for the second-straight year, there were some positives, but still more negatives and too many unknowns. So, let’s break down that state of things in the Chicago. In the comments, let us know your thoughts on all things Sky. What went right for Chicago ? Trading Ariel Atkins to the Los Angeles Sparks for Rickea Jackson was a brilliant move by the Sky. This season, Atkins continued to decline in Los Angeles, while Jackson looked ready to become an All-Star. In Jackson’s first four games with the Sky, she was averaging 18 points and 4.8 rebounds per game. Unfortunately, she tore her left ACL, ending her season early. Rickea Jackson + Kamilla Cardoso give & go to counter switching (Carla Leite) via back-cut from Jackson Salute to Cardoso on the bounce pass Solid debut for new-look Chicago Sky pic.twitter.com/XhKHGV243w — Jackson Lloyd (@JacksonLloyd952) May 10, 2026 Despite the darkness that was Jackson’s injury, there was a ray of sunshine in the season: Sydney Taylor. The rookie guard was a walking bucket. It wasn’t long before Taylor, who averaged 13.6 points per game, became a bona fide starter for the team. Thanks to her high level of play, she earned All-Rookie honors. What went wrong for Chicago? Where should we start? (First, there was that other trade .) The Sky also ran into more delays with their practice facility . This frustrated everyone and was another example of promises the Sky organization left unkept. Besides Jackson’s major injury, other players like Azurá Stevens, DiJonai Carrington and Skylar Diggins also missed time. And when Diggins did play, it didn’t go well. Her production plummeted this year. She averaged 14.2 points per game, her worst scoring season since 2016. Then there was the losing. After Jackson went down, the Sky never looked like a serious team for long stretches. Instead, it was a lot of defeats and a struggle to find an identity among a roster full of questionably fitting players at different stages of their WNBA careers. If things ever do go right in Chicago, it certainly feels like most of the players who will be there for it aren’t part of the team now. What’s next for Chicago? There is good news in Chicago. They have a solid young player in Taylor and a superstar in the making in Jackson. Head coach Tyler Marsh also seemed to have improved as a leader, leading the team to some great wins over teams like the Las Vegas Aces, Golden State Valkyries and New York Liberty. And that practice facility should, finally, be ready by 2027. Nevertheless, improvements are needed everywhere up and down the roster and in and out of the organization. If they are serious about fixing things, their offseason should be busy, righting the ship so there are brighter days ahead for the Sky.

articles.title: Te’Yala Delfosse stepped into the star spotlight, and No. 5 Michigan took down No. 2 UConn
articles.summary: The downside of decades of dominance? It’s only news when you lose. On Thursday night in Ann Arbor, No. 2 UConn lost to No. 5 Michigan, 77-66. As Michigan head coach Kim Barnes Arico said after the game, “How many teams beat UConn? It doesn’t happen.” The loss snapped the Huskies’ 39-game regular-se
articles._body: Te’Yala Delfosse and the Michigan Wolverines. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The downside of decades of dominance? It’s only news when you lose. On Thursday night in Ann Arbor, No. 2 UConn lost to No. 5 Michigan, 77-66. As Michigan head coach Kim Barnes Arico said after the game , “How many teams beat UConn? It doesn’t happen.” The loss snapped the Huskies’ 39-game regular-season winning streak, all while sinking the prospects of another undefeated UConn campaign after just two games. Yet, UConn never beats themselves, thus demanding that Michigan receive requisite praise, and then some, for earning the highest-ranked win in program history. A 22-13 was the finishing flourish in the fourth quarter—in short, out-executing the Huskies in winning time—secured the win for the Wolverines. The Wolverine win also might have berth women’s college basketball’s newest star: Te’Yala Delfosse. Te'Yala Delfosse (11/5/26) pic.twitter.com/ghG6vb5Nhh — @balapattyszn (@balapattyvids) November 6, 2026 The 6-foot-3 junior forward led Michigan with a career-high 22 points, showing off an intriguing combination of athleticism and skill as she helped the Wolverines puncture a usually-stout Husky defense. A 32 percent 3-point shooter across her first two college seasons, Delfosse went 3-for-4 from downtown, demonstrating a quick, comfortable release on her catch-and-shoot conversions. She paired that shooting with assertive attacks to the basket, using her long strides, solid handle and finishing touch both in transition and halfcourt situations. She also added nine rebounds, two steals and a block. Even if the deep shooting doesn’t sustain, Delfosse, just a three-star recruit in the class of 2024, looks to have unlocked an new level, aided by an earned confidence, that will justify the optimism about the Wolverines that likely will reach an all-time high after this historic victory. Against UConn tonight, Te'Yala Delfosse led Michigan in points (22), rebounds (9) and FGM(8/13). Kim Barnes Arico on Delfosse's development on both ends of the floor: pic.twitter.com/LC2HQbOlfJ — Jaxson Kaplan-Rudolph (@jaxsonkr) November 6, 2026 UConn head coach Geno Auriemma endorsed such optimism, proposing after the game , “It’s one game for them, but they’ve put themselves in a position to say, ‘Why can’t we be a Final Four team?’ While Delfosse could be Michigan’s ceiling raiser, they’ve established this high floor because of fellow juniors Olivia Olson and Syla Swords. Olson, a selected to the All-America Third Team last season as a sophomore, stuffed the stat sheet for 19 points, eight rebounds, four assists and four steals. Playing all 40 minutes, Swords hit three 3s on her way to 10 points and five points. Transfer Courtney Ogden, in her first official game in Maize and Blue after spending her first three college seasons at Stanford, immediately introduced her value as a physical, efficient scorer, contributing 12 points in her 13 minutes. Earned it together 〽️ pic.twitter.com/9mEaLYgXvO — Michigan Women’s Basketball (@umichwbball) November 6, 2026 UConn, meanwhile, can believe that the outcome might have been different had Sarah Strong not experienced early foul trouble, resulting in the reigning National Player of the Year going scoreless in the first half before finishing with 13 points, eight rebounds and two assists. With Strong limited, freshman Jovana Popovic assumed star scoring duties for the Huskies, again exhibiting excellent efficiency as she scored 25 points, going 10-for-15 from the field and 3-for-5 from 3. She also added seven boards, four assists and three steals. Beyond that pair, the Huskies didn’t get much. An off night from sophomore Blanca Quiñonez robbed the UConn of an off-the-bench scoring boost. Outside of Strong, Popovic and Quiñonez, this UConn team lacks threatening self creators, making the Huskies particularly dependent on 3-point shooting. An 8-for-31, or 26 percent, performance is, obviously, insufficient. The UConn defense also was also not up to the expected standard, as the open shots and uncontested drives that the aforementioned Delfosse feasted on exemplified the Huskies’ lack of connectedness and resistance on that end. Sarah Strong: "I think we have a lot to learn from this game. When we sit down and watch film, sit with our position coaches, just watch how we just didn't play UConn basketball at all, and I think we just let Michigan do whatever they wanted to do the whole time… We just have… pic.twitter.com/I1yZkMya8r — Storrs Central (@StorrsCentral) November 6, 2026 UConn, of course, will be better. But, Michigan might be even better.

articles.title: 2026 WNBA season review: The Toronto Tempo were on track for a special expansion campaign, until injuries derailed everything
articles.summary: You can’t talk about the Toronto Tempo’s inaugural season without starting with Marina Mabrey’s WNBA-record-tying 53 points in a single game on June 25. Mabrey ended up averaging a career-high 20.8 points per game, a mark that not only was a significant increase from her previous mark of 15 points p
articles._body: Brittney Sykes and Marina Mabrey. (Photo by Tara Walton) | NBAE via Getty Images You can’t talk about the Toronto Tempo’s inaugural season without starting with Marina Mabrey’s WNBA-record-tying 53 points in a single game on June 25. MARINA MABREY TIES THE WNBA SINGLE GAME SCORING RECORD. 53 POINTS. WOW 🤯 (via @WNBA ) pic.twitter.com/b6B39X309z — Overtime (@overtime) June 26, 2026 Mabrey ended up averaging a career-high 20.8 points per game, a mark that not only was a significant increase from her previous mark of 15 points per game but also good for sixth in the WNBA. The first-time All-Star had been a great 3-point shooter in the past, but she took her ability to get on a heater and raised it to another level at 2026 Unrivaled and during the 2026 W season. You couldn’t give her any space, and she would make 3 after 3 no matter the degree of difficulty. She made 105 triples at 38.5 percent! Mabrey lived up to her million-dollar contract, as did her backcourt partner Brittney Sykes, though Sykes was limited to 17 games due to a plantar fascia injury. Mabrey also dealt with an injuries and missed 12 contests. Together, they led the Tempo to a 7-5 record to start the season. Injuries were then the main culprit in the team then going 4-28 over the remainder of the season for a final record of 11-33. Sykes was on track to be an All-Star , as she upped her career-best scoring average from 15.9 points per game to 18.6 points per game. Both she and Mabrey were empowered to take career-highs in field goal attempts per game, and they also each took the most free throws per game of their careers. A look at history as Brittney Sykes scores the first-ever bucket for @TempoBasketball 🚨 https://t.co/DIQD6Mp9lZ pic.twitter.com/eO2NP5b202 — WNBA (@WNBA) May 8, 2026 The Tempo were questioned by many for attempting to win now as an expansion team. Also, many doubted if it was the right move to pay Mabrey and Sykes as much as they did and give them the reins. But they managed to be the two best players on a team that started 7-5. Injuries up and down the rotation doomed the Tempo Canada basketball fans had been dying to get a WNBA team of their own and were treated to more than just Mabrey and Sykes. However, the injury bug bit the supporting cast as well. The No. 6 pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft, Kiki Rice earned All-Rookie honors. She was third on the team with 13.4 points per game, as her college improvement from beyond the arc translated to the W (26 makes at 35.1 percent). She also made 3.3 free throws per game at 86.9 percent. A Grade 2 ankle sprain limited her to 28 games, though. 100 CAREER POINTS FOR KIKI RICE🤩 🥹 pic.twitter.com/NLqUYTvJRM — Toronto Tempo (@TempoBasketball) May 28, 2026 Isabelle Harrison missed the first 10 games of the season with a thumb injury before experiencing a career resurgence. At age 32, she averaged double-digit scoring for the first time since 2021 (with a career-best 12.8 points per game) and a career- and team-high 6.9 rebounds per game. Nyara Sabally, the team’s second pick in the expansion draft, played in just 24 games due to various injuries. She was good when she played, though, achieving 12.3 points per game (fifth on the team) and 5.3 boards per game (third on the team).  María Conde was a solid contributor, playing the fifth-most minutes per game on the squad at 26.4, but she missed nine games (various injuries/illness/Spain national team commitments). Toronto’s first pick in the expansion draft, Julie Allemand shot better than 30 percent from 3 for the first time in her W career since 2020 with an impressive mark of 41.9 percent (39 makes). She also posted 5.5 assists per game to lead the Tempo and place 10th in the league. She played in 33 games, missing some time due to injury and Belgium national team commitments. A 29-year-old rookie revelation, Laura Juškaitė was the only key contributor to play in more than 35 games, playing in all 44 (36 starts) with averages of 25.4 minutes per game and 11.3 points per game. Toronto is set up for a potentially transformative offseason Toronto’s third million dollar woman, after Mabrey and Sykes, is Temi Fagbenle, who was never able to provide her expected impact, playing in just 25 games due to injury and registering just 5.9 points per contest. She is now an unrestricted free agent. The next-highest paid player on the Tempo is Sabally at under half a million ($436,957). So if they don’t retain Fagbenle, they’ll have some room to work with. Mabrey, Sykes and Allemand are signed to guaranteed contracts through 2027. Rice is signed to her rookie contract through 2029, while Aneesah Morrow, a midseason pickup via trade, is also on her rookie contract (through 2028). Morrow averaged a solid 9.3 points per game (seventh on the team) and 6.6 boards per game (second on the team) across her seven games with Toronto. Breaking: The Toronto Tempo have acquired Connecticut Sun forward Aneesah Morrow in a trade that’s sending the rights to Maria Kliundikova and a 2028 second-round pick to Connecticut. pic.twitter.com/T7oJ7LOOlV — Alexa Philippou (@alexaphilippou) July 31, 2026 With the Tempo’s winning percentage matching the now-Houston Comets (previously the Connecticut Sun) as the lowest in the W when counting the past two seasons combined (so only 2026 for Toronto), they are tied with Houston for the highest odds of winning the draft lottery, the results of which will be revealed on Nov. 15 (7:30 p.m. ET, ESPN). Both they and the Comets have a 32.9 percent chance of landing the No. 1 pick, which presumably would be used to draft JuJu Watkins, a generational talent out of USC, if she declares for the draft. Tempo head coach Sandy Brondello is a proven winner Tempo head coach Sandy Brondello is a two-time WNBA championship-winning head coach, having won it all with the Phoenix Mercury in her first year there (2014) and the New York Liberty in 2024. She’s been to two other Finals (2021 with the Mercury a

articles.title: NCAA gameday discussion: When No. 5 Michigan hosts No. 1 UConn, watch out for Syla Swords and Jovana Popovic
articles.summary: The early-season women’s college basketball menu is often overstuffed with a buffet of blowouts, as top-ranked teams fatten up on overmatched opponents, resulting in games that not only are uncompetitive and sometimes unwatchable, but also uninformative. (Hi, LSU!) And yet, those gluttonous games ar
articles._body: Jovana Popovic. | Getty Images The early-season women’s college basketball menu is often overstuffed with a buffet of blowouts, as top-ranked teams fatten up on overmatched opponents, resulting in games that not only are uncompetitive and sometimes unwatchable, but also uninformative. (Hi, LSU!) And yet, those gluttonous games are balanced by a few delicacies, when top teams please the palates of fans hungry for some high-level hoops. No. 2 UConn’s visit to No. 5 Michigan might be the most delicious early-season treat (6:30 p.m. ET, FS1). Last season, the Huskies and Wolverines met in Mohegan Sun Arena late November, with Michigan giving UConn their toughest regular-season test in what turned into a thriller. Michigan, down 22-5 after the first, eventually rallied, cutting UConn’s once 20-point lead all the way down to a single point before losing by three points, 72-69. This season’s top-five matchup, on Michigan’s home floor, likewise projects an early barometer for both teams. Can the Wolverines, who reached the door step of the sport’s upper echelon with a trip to the Elite Eight last season, step through with a statement win over the Huskies? Or, will UConn, as is their wont, assert their longstanding superiority with a dominant victory? Here are two players—one Wolverine and one Husky—who can swing the outcome of this top-five tilt. In the comments, let us know if you agree, or which Wolverines or Huskies you see as emerging as the X factors on Thursday evening. No one loves a big stage more than Michigan’s Syla Swords Of course, it’s Syla Swords. A top-five matchup on national television? Those are the ideal conditions for a Swords masterclass. The now-junior Canadian guard introduced herself to the wider women’s college hoops world with an epic freshman debut against No. 1-ranked South Carolina, dropping 27 points as the Wolverines sent a shiver through the Gamecocks. In last season’s aforementioned game against UConn, Swords, again, was on one, serving as the engine of Michigan’s comeback with 29 points, including eight 3-pointers. SYLA SWORDS ARE YOU MAD ?????? https://t.co/tB8r5Z1wDu pic.twitter.com/MnChgtZT4w — Shabazz 💫 (@ShowCaseShabazz) November 22, 2025 Swords’ tendency to elevate her play on the biggest stage can make her game difficult to analyze. Seemingly poised for a leap as a sophomore , her overall production remained modest, with her efficiency from the field and from 3 actually dropping from her freshman season. She also struggled with consistency, with 20-point games followed by single-digit ones. (Although, as long as the talented Wolverines win, that’s not necessarily a real problem.) But if Michigan is to not only announce themselves as a real threat with a win over UConn, but also maintain that status through a Big Ten regular-season gauntlet, a more efficient and consistent Swords will be a must. The Wolverines have yet to play this season, making Thursday’s showdown the first chance to see what Syla has in store. Jovana Popovic already looks ready to help UConn to title No. 13 Over two years ago, our Łukasz Muniowski interviewed Jovana Popvic , talking with the then-17-year-old about her play in the top women’s basketball league in Serbia, where she won Finals MVP as she helped ZKK Mega MIS Beograd win the league title. In the interview, Popovic comes off a shy and soft-spoken, humbly crediting her teammates and coaches for her success. Her game, however, can be loud, as UConn fans already have discovered. In her debut, the now-19-year-old Popovic posted 19 points in her 22 minutes, going 8-for-12 from the field, including 3-for-4 from 3. Jovana Popovic tonight: • 19 points • 3 rebounds • 3 steals • 3/4 3PM • 8/12 FG • 22 minutes played pic.twitter.com/XlGkUxn9OT — Women’s Hoops Network (@WomensHoops_USA) November 2, 2026 The jumper is pure, as she drained buckets from off the dribble and off the catch, showing comfort in the midrange and behind the arc. She also can make her way to the hoop with apparent ease, recognizing openings in the defense and gliding to the rim. Popovic profiles as the kind of point guard that the Huskies lacked last season, with her ability to run the offense and set the table for others enhanced by her own scoring prowess. The likes of Swords or Mila Holloway will provide much more resistance than Popovic saw against Cornell, as UConn romped to the 100-35 win on opening day. However, considering Popovic also scored 22 points in an exhibition game against No. 6 Texas, in addition to notching seven rebounds and five assists, it might be unwise to think she’s going to experience a “Welcome to the NCAA” moment. Rather, the pro-polished Serbian superstar might use the official top-five test to cement herself as THE piece who, wearing No. 13, is poised to help the Huskies capture title No. 13.

articles.title: Season 3 of Unrivaled is on the way. With all eight rosters now revealed, which 3×3 club is the early championship favorite?
articles.summary: While the WNBA season is over, US-based women’s professional basketball will be back soon thanks to Unrivaled. On Wednesday, the 3×3 league unveiled the full rosters for the eight clubs that will begin play for Season 3 on Jan. 8, 2027. Here is a full breakdown of all eight clubs that will be c
articles._body: Dominique Malonga and Paige Bueckers. | Getty Images While the WNBA season is over, US-based women’s professional basketball will be back soon thanks to Unrivaled. On Wednesday, the 3×3 league unveiled the full rosters for the eight clubs that will begin play for Season 3 on Jan. 8, 2027. You heard it here first on Unrivaled Radio! Season 3 teams are set – stay tuned for Tip-Off on January 8, 2027 👑 pic.twitter.com/zeLCbWMT2L — Unrivaled Basketball (@Unrivaledwbb) November 5, 2026 Here is a full breakdown of all eight clubs that will be competing for the championship. In the comments, let us know who you think the early favorites should be, as well as which new, or old, player partnerships you’re excited to watch. Rose BC Rosebuds!!! How we feelin'? 🌹 pic.twitter.com/j5z5pFQjlC — Unrivaled Basketball (@Unrivaledwbb) November 5, 2026 There’s a lot of veteran leadership on this team. Chelsea Gray is the Point Gawd and Brittney Sykes is an experienced and productive backcourt player. Aziaha James brings some youth to the guard depth, and Kayla Thornton is fresh off winning a WNBA championship with the Golden State Valkyries. In a press release, returning Rose head coach Nola Henry seemed pumped to get started with this squad, saying: I’m excited about the group we’ve put together. We have a great mix of experience, toughness, versatility, and competitiveness. My focus is on establishing our identity early, maximizing everyone’s strengths, and building the chemistry needed to compete for a championship. That’s always our standard. Hive BC Buzzinssss your ‘27 squad is locked in 🐝 Presented by @Chegg pic.twitter.com/7mNQ175k3r — Unrivaled Basketball (@Unrivaledwbb) November 5, 2026 Hive is going to be really fun to watch. Olivia Miles is one of the most electrifying guards in the game, Rae Burrell is coming off a career year with the Sparks and Cameron Brink is an elite defensive big growing as a scorer. Add in Naz Hillmon, Sonia Citron, and Natisha Hiedeman, and Hive will have plenty of fans. Breeze BC Young and Turnt with some new additions 👀 Presented by @thornehealth pic.twitter.com/Jt244MZvWx — Unrivaled Basketball (@Unrivaledwbb) November 5, 2026 Breeze is absolutely stacked. They have Paige Bueckers, who is a supernova on offense. Dominique Malonga is one of the best young bigs in basketball and Kahleah Copper is a superstar in her own right. Here’s what new head coach Jarell Christian said about his team: When I look at the 2027 Breeze, I see a group of competitors who play with passion and pride. I love the versatility throughout our roster, which will allow us to play and win in a variety of ways. I’m excited to welcome Paige and Dom back for their second season with the Breeze. Their familiarity and chemistry will be extremely valuable to our success. Adding a player of Kahleah’s caliber is special, but it’s her character, professionalism, and spirit that will help shape the culture we’re looking to build. Lunar Owls BC Can I get a Hootie Hoooooo?! 🦉 pic.twitter.com/sDXRn0lAuf — Unrivaled Basketball (@Unrivaledwbb) November 5, 2026 The Lunar Owls are an older team. They’ll have plenty of leadership with Napheesa Collier, Courtney Williams, and Skylar Diggins. But they also pack a punch. Marina Mabrey can score with the best of them, and Sydney Taylor was one of the best WNBA rookies this year. With Temi Fágbénlé returning, this will be a fun team to watch. Laces BC Solemates! Here’s your new LacesBC crew 👟 pic.twitter.com/pBLWFTVgtO — Unrivaled Basketball (@Unrivaledwbb) November 5, 2026 The Laces are oozing with championship knowledge. Gabby Williams just won it all with Golden State, and Jackie Young has starred for the Las Vegas Aces during their three title runs. Jessica Shepard took a leap in the WNBA in 2026 and will bring her top game to the Laces. Phantom BC Season 3 Phantom looking scary 👻 pic.twitter.com/D5pKv6jDrP — Unrivaled Basketball (@Unrivaledwbb) November 5, 2026 Kelsey Plum is one of the best scorers in basketball, and she’ll get plenty of buckets in Unrivaled. With Aaliyah Edwards and Kalya McBride on the team, they should have a potent offense and solid defense. Tiffany Hayes and Natasha Could will be a big reason Phantom will be tough to score on. With Li Yueru providing additional size, this will be a team to watch early on. Mist BC Mist BC ready to defend its title 😶‍🌫️ pic.twitter.com/O5HbTJH1l1 — Unrivaled Basketball (@Unrivaledwbb) November 5, 2026 Whenever Mist plays, be sure to get the popcorn ready. They are primed to have one of the most explosive offenses in the league. Arike Ogunbowale can get hot at any moment, Breanna Stewart is one of the best players ever and young players like Kiki Rice will be ready to go. Can they repeat as champs? It’ll be exciting finding out. Vinyl BC VinylBC ready to make some noise 🎶 pic.twitter.com/UfF7FmdfFQ — Unrivaled Basketball (@Unrivaledwbb) November 5, 2026 Vinyl has a great balance of elite frontcourt and backcourt players. Jordin Canada will work so well with Dearica Hamby in the pick-and-roll. Rhyne Howard is a great scorer, and Allisha Gray can shoot the ball well. When Flau’jae Johnson, who joined Renee Montgomery and Chelsea Gray on the roster reveal stream, saw the roster, she certainly was excited about what her first Unrivaled season has in store for her. Flau'jae's reaction to joining her new Unrivaled club 🤣 pic.twitter.com/SvfMS6IvNb — Bleacher Report (@BleacherReport) November 5, 2026
